product_title: Brainwavz M2 In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: It's not bad but it's not good either *Updated*
review_body:
So after using it for few days, I must say I am little bit dissapointed. First of all, as soon as I picked up the earphones, The rubber part that's covering the wire and the metal part of the body was falling apart. Left side was glued down and it stayed in place but the right rubber came out like there is no glue or what so ever. Plus the stick part of the metal is screwed onto the speaker part and it keeps being unscrewed and starts to come off. So as for the construction.. it's cheaply made. I don't really trust chinese stuff especially for electronics, but I gave it a try becasue of so many good reviews and recommendations. However, after using it for few days, I don't know what is up with all the hypes. The sound quality is mediocre, it's at the level of Panasonic RPHJE120D In-Ear Headphone which is about $8.00(they are amazing for $8.00 btw). It has slightly clearer mids and treble but the bass is actually worse. It was even worse with stock rubber tips but got little bit better with rubber tip from Panasonic RPHJE120D. stock rubber tips are really comfortable but none of the stock size rubbers gave me the tight seal as the rubber tip from RPHJE120D so the bass sounded really weak with the stock rubbers. With rubbers changed it sounded little bit better but still it wasnt up to my hopes for $50.00 headphone.They are not bad, but they are not good either. It's not like im a bass freak, I didn't expect Bose earphone style of bass. Bass is just too weak. Every earphones sound different and they have their own characteristics, but M2's sound is just...mediocre.

*Update 2/18/17* I never thought I'd be updating the review for this product.. but back then I did not know about the importance(or effectiveness) of burnining in headphones.. Now I do and after burn-in I gotta admit the headphone sounds better. Im raising my star to 4. Sound got a lot better than when it was new. The build is still somewhat fimsly. but nothing broke down and everything is still working as it should.working as it should.

review_body:
I bought this product as a gift for my mother (age 65) who is constantly misplacing important items (keys, purse, phone, etc.). She was delighted when she received the gift. She proceeded to place 5 of the 6 beepers on different household items - one on her cell phone, her key chain, in her purse, the cordless house phone (she had worn out the internal beeper in the phone from using it so much), and her coffee cup. Each time I speak with her on the phone or in person, she thanks me again and again for the beeper set because she uses them so much. It helps keep her sanity, as she loses things constantly. She used to spend much of her day looking for things, but now she doesn't! Luckily she hasn't lost the beeper remote yet. I am thinking about giving her another set so she can place a beeper on the 1st remote and have a backup remote to beep the 1st one in case she misplaces it...

Initial setup of the beeper set was a breeze. Simply remove the plastic tabs that keep the installed battery contacts separated from the devices and they are ready to use. They even come with a full replacement set of batteries for each beeper and remote, though after 6 months of pretty heavy use, the original batteries are still holding up. Three of the beepers use a key chain link to attach, and the other three use a double sided sticky pad to attach to items. The three sticky beepers have so far held their stickiness (6 months use), even attached to the back of a heavily used cell phone. The noise from the beepers could be a bit louder, but it has been sufficient for my mother to always locate the missing items in her house. I would recommend this product to anyone who has trouble keeping up with their keys or things around their home.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Around-Ear Bluetooth Headphones, Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: I was really surprised just how good these headphones really are.
review_body: I really was shocked at how good these sound.    Here's the low-down as best I can provide it.    Out of the box, I charged them with a powered 8-port USB 3.0 Hub, and it took but about 95 minutes to charge them fully (the manual says allow up to 3 hours).    I then tested them listening to Music and programming streamed Amazon Prime Instant HD Video from both an Acer Chromebook and Macbook Pro running iOS8.1.    I compared these with the Bose QC15 headphones and MiE2 ear buds.    I then used them paired with an iPhone 5s and streamed music and took calls.    I compared that with the MiE2's    1. Nothing compares to the QC15's in my book.  End of entry.    2. Sound quality (as measured in tonal and \\"spatial\\" reproduction) was definitely better with these than the MiE2s.  Again both music and HD audio reproduced beautifully balanced and rich.  These reproduce audio with a noticeable spatial-like quality to the sound (the music and audio seemed to emanate from all around my head, vice squeezed just into the space of my ears).    2a.  Phone calls, music and video audio sources all reproduced very well (I've seen before where Bose would balance sound for, say Video Audio, and thus music would need the use of equalization to sound full).  But there is no need to equalize the audio with these.  They are exceptionally balanced to especially well all the audio sources I tried them with.    3. The microphone is.. well... there's a microphone.  But that's all about all I can say.  The mic on the MiE2 earbuds works much much better than the mic on these.  I think Bose just put the mic there to make these attractive to users who are looking to use them with their mobile phones.    4.  As to fit.  These things are stupid comfortable. It's hard for me to say which was more comfortable, the QC15s or these.  They are both well engineered for comfort.  They are lighter... and I've worn them for several hours in 1 sitting, as never once experienced any discomfort whatsoever.  They'renicely padded and the leather ear cup covers sit nicely against my skull skin.    I read the reviews, and more than a few people were curious about noise cancelling.  None, nope not a bit.  But when listening to music, it's easy to forget there is ambient sound going on outside them.    Also, I saw a few questions about the bluetooth adapter itself.  It will NOT fit in the QC15 (or similar models).  The design of the BT module exculdes the user from being able to connect the mini jack into the QC 15's.  Same with the headphone cables, they are not interchangeable.    I like how the BT module has volume and player controls (the latter being multiple taps on the control button on the top of the module - e.g. 1 tap for pause, 2 taps for next, and 3 taps for previous).  Plus the +, - and buttons are very easy to find and touch identify with just the left hand.    5.  Range.  Yup, like the product specs say, 30ft. is about right.  But really, if you think about it, 30ft. is plenty.    6.  Pairing with multiple devices:  I've paired these with my iPhone and a laptop, (tried with both my Chromebook and MacBook Pro) and they work great.  When watching video on the laptop and I get a call, the video pauses, when I finish the call, then I can watch the video again.  They really handled being paired to two devices quite well.  Absolutely no complaint there.    Finally, one thing to say about Bose product support.  I've had occasions where I had Bose devices go bad years after purchase.  Bose has always had incredible support (easy to find replaceable parts) and when all else has failed, they've offered me 1/2 off the newest models if I wanted to swap them out.  This is why so many things I own for sound reproduction are Bose.

product_title: Portable Waterproof Bluetooth Speakers w/ FM Radio & LCD Display, IPX7 Water Resistant & Shockproof - Ultimate Wireless Handfree Rechargeable Shower Speakerphone
review_body:
The minute I opened the package I noticed a difference between the quality of this Bluetooth speaker and some of the others that I own. It looks and feels so much more substantial than some of the others. This speaker is very well made. If you look at the front grill you can see the two small speaker cones inside. Each of those small speakers can produce up to 4 watts of power for a total of 8 (eight!) watts of stereo power! The sound this Bluetooth speaker produces is rich and full. On the bottom (in the back) of the speaker is the bass reflex port. Turning the volume up to level 15 (the loudest it goes) it was very, VERY loud inside of our house,... for me it was a bit much, lol. Even when I had it turned up there was no distortion whatsoever,...none. I love the sound this speaker produces!

I also had no trouble pairing this up to any of my Bluetooth devices. My phone and my laptop both found the \\"Acoustix\\" name in the Bluetooth device lists quickly and pairing was fast. When connected to my laptop it didn't always auto connect like some of my other devices do, so I did have to go back into my laptops settings and click the connect button each time it failed to reconnect. You will see a fast blinking blue light through the front grill when it is ready to pair, and then it changes to a steady blue glow when paired. Once paired you will see it blink once every 10 seconds.

This speaker comes with a USB charging cable and a wall outlet adapter so you can charge this in your car or from a regular wall outlet. Also included is a lanyard and a small carabiner clip for hanging. There is a flip up folding handle on each side of the speaker for hanging up just about anywhere. The charging port, reset button access hole, and Aux. plugin are accessed through the back of the speaker, there is a thick rubber cover that helps keep dust and water out but still makes it easy to access the plugin ports when needed.

All of the controls are on the top and are simple to understand. Even the user manual is easy to use, I was happily surprised to find a manual with print that was large enough to see without having to use a magnifying glass!

English is the default language, if you prefer the LCD screen to be in French or Spanish then hold down the Play/Pause button for 5 seconds. Scroll through your choices using the volume up or down button, then press the power button again to set your choice or just let the speaker sit idle for 10 seconds to confirm your selection. I love the LCD screen, you can easily see what song is playing, what your volume level is at, your battery level, and even the number of the person that is calling you. If a call comes in and you want to reject the call, just a quick click of the power button is all it takes. The microphone is located behind the grill and this speaker works great when used as a speakerphone. I had no problem hearing callers or being heard during calls.

The mode button lets you choose between Bluetooth, Aux., and FM radio. No Aux. cable is provided, but the speaker provides you with an Aux. port in case you want to hook up a pair of headphones, or plug in a non Bluetooth device. The FM radio worked pretty good too. I was able to add my favorite stations to the preset list. It did take me a few minutes to figure it out. Go to FM mode then click the play/pause button to get into pre set mode. Then click the forward or back button to scan for your station, then click and hold the preset button again to store. After storing your favorite stations you can scroll through them by clicking the preset button.

The outside of this speaker has a rubber like finish with a stainless steel grill and is dustproof, waterproof, and impact resistant to a bit over 3 feet when dropped, so this makes a good choice for using outdoors.

*I did receive a free product sample for review purposes. After using this speaker I would recommend it 100% to anyone looking for a Bluetooth speaker that performs well and can handle the abuses of being used outside. Adding an SD slot would have made this even better, but as it is now this Bluetooth speaker sounds wonderful and looks great too!!!d can handle the abuses of being used outside. review_headline: I bought two! Considering a third!
review_body:
I purchased two of these little bad boys. A black one for me and a red one for my wife. If you look closely at the customer reviews, a lot of consumers of this product are giving their feedback as a result of receiving this speaker under a promotional discount or outright free of charge. While I'm upset that I wasn't able to receive one free of charge for my "unbiased" and honest opinion, I am happy to report that this portable wireless Bluetooth speaker does in fact rock. It's clear and loud and even produces a good amount of bass for something so tiny. My wife and I were pleasantly surprised! We use our I-Venstar speaker outside during our crossfit workouts. We've paired the Bluetooth feature with both of our phones and it works great but 99% of the time, we find ourselves using the TF CARD MODE. We had a couple of 32gb micro SD cards laying around from our old cell phones. We formatted the SD cards and viola! We added over 1000 songs to each of our SD cards and enjoy playing our music straight from this versatile little speaker. The only thing we wished it had would be the ability to play our mp3's in a random / shuffle mode. Instead, we must listen to our songs in alphabetical order. It is certainly no reason to drop this item from a 5 star rating to a 4 star rating. The speaker itself is actually very impressive!

By the way, if anyone knows if this speaker is capable of playing mp3's in random / shuffle mode, please leave your comments! We are considering the purchase of one more of these awesome little speakers to take with us on our upcoming vacation!

product_title: Panasonic ErgoFit In-Ear Earbud Headphone
review_body: I wanted an inexpensive set of earbuds to replace the awful over-the -ear headphones that came with my Sony SRF-M37W AM/FM/Weather Walkman. For less than $7, I figured I try a set of Panasonic RP-HJE-120 Ergos based on all the favorable reviews they have received.  They are certainly a great value for the price, and deliver very good performance, with satisfying, but not overwhelming bass, and clear and well-balanced mids and highs.  And they are very comfortable, thanks to their asymmetrical,ergonomic design.  And they stay securely in place while I am working out on my spinning bike.  But I had to subtract  a star because the silicone ear tips are very difficult to change.  They do not slip easily over the post on the earbud, and I struggled for more than half an hour to replace the medium tips that came already attached to the earbuds with the larger tips to get a better fit.  And it does not come with a small pouch to store the extra tips, so they can easily get lost or misplaced.  Also, the package is one of those sealed clear plastic bubble affairs which is a bitch to open, even with a strong pair of scizzors.  If you're not careful, you could lose the extra tips in the process of cutting the package open.  Why do so many companies use such consumer unfriendly packaging?  But if you can live with these minor drawbacks, then the Panasonic RP-HJE-120 Ergos are a great buy.  You won't be disappointed with the sound they deliver.

review_headline: Great for breaking audio out from Roku 3!
review_body:
I have a Denon AVR2112 receiver that controls two sets of speakers - 5+1 (Zone1) and 2 speaker stereo (Zone2). Zone1 is my family room surround sound. Zone2 is connected to speakers on my patio. I have a Roku 3 device which is connected by a HDMI cable to the "Game1" input of the Denon receiver, which until now has only been used in Zone1. The only weakness of the Denon system is that you can only connect analog inputs to Zone2. I listen to Pandora through my Roku 3 a lot, and wanted to be able to pipe it outside, but because the Roku 3 uses a digital HDMI output this could not be connected to Zone2.

This device was perfect for my needs. I hooked this device inline between the Roku and the Denon tuner, then connected the audio out connection to the "Dock" analog input of the tuner. All I have to do is switch Zone2 to use Dock input to get Pandora on the patio.

The device comes with a USB cable to power it, and a 3.5mm to dual RCA female connector. All I needed to add was an extra HDMI cable and a dual RCA male-to-male cable to hook everything up. I didn't want to waste a USB charger to power the device, so I connected the provided USB power cable into a router that sits next to my Denon tuner, which worked fine.

review_body:
I have an elderly neighbor with an old school analog tv who cannot afford cable, so when I was offered the opportunity to receive this Liger HDTV Antenna in exchange for my unbiased review, I quickly accepted with her in mind.
I do not consider myself well versed in technology, so I placed my order with some apprehension as to whether or not I would be able to install it, but I cannot express how pleased I am with how easy it was to hook up this antenna!
Liger provides a well written, easy to understand instruction sheet with diagrams that made it possible to hook up the antenna in a matter of seconds, once I located the digital receiver I had stashed in the closet after purchasing my HDTV.
I only wish I had my camera with me so I could have taken a photo of the look on her face as I set the tv to scan mode and station after station was programmed in...
When the programming had finished we found that she had her choice of 17 stations with excellent reception - ALL FREE OF CHARGE!
The picture is clear and the signal has remained uninterrupted since the installation, even on a stormy Florida day!
The antenna itself is very attractive to the eye and the thin 10' coaxial cable was easy to secure to the wall with a couple of fasteners, so I don't have to worry about her catching it in the vacuum.
My neighbor and I both give this Liger Ultra-Thin Indoor Antenna our highest recommendation!

product_title: BlackVue DR650S-2CH 16GB with Power Magic Pro, Car Black Box/Car DVR Recorder, Wi-Fi, Full HD, G Sensor, GPS, 16GB SD Card Included, Up To 128GB Support
review_headline: One of the Best Car Cams on the Market!
review_body:
Feb. 14, 2014.

I've been using GoPros in my vehicle for front and rear video and they work ok, but have to many limitations. Such as no time stamp, they keep falling out of loop or wifi mod. Then they cost $400 a piece. So I wanted something a bit more dash cam friendly. After researching 10-15 cameras I picked this one.

I just received my DR650 in the mail. I'm going to write an on going type of review since I've just received it. As far as delivery, two day free shipping really you can't beat it. Came as advertised.

Unboxing was not problem and I started to try to set it up in the vehicle but that was a bit of a pain, because if I didn't like it I didn't want to have to tear it down. So I had a 12 volt power supply in the house, works a lot better especially if you have to get on the internet to figure the crap out of their very very very limited in box manual!

Right off the bat a problem formatting the 16g SD card provided. The nice annoying voice keep repeating please check SD card, please check SD card, etc... Your supposed to insert the card and hold the button for 7-10 seconds and BAM it's formatted. That didn't work. Had to read other's experiences about the same issue and ended up downloading a program for FAT32 formatting and formatted my 64g card and it worked fine.

Then the WIFI, just make sure you look at all the paper work in the box, the Easy Tip for Wi-Fi gives you the PW, it's easy just the name of the company. Once you download the program on your phone you can change it to a secure PW.

That's another thing. Went to the website to see if their was an update, yep there is a firmware update, from 1.000 to 1.003. Yet when I followed their instructions to a T, it will not update the firmware no matter which way I try to do it.

As for the iPhone interface with the WIFI connection to the camera, it's ok, but needs to be more user friendly. Now the Configure button takes you to the Firmware Settings. I would be nice if the manual and the PDF you can down load would mirror the phone interface and explain each setting. But no it doesn't, so you have to guess at some of them! I believe the firmware update would have taken care of some of this if I had been able to update it. (Hoping these people are reading our reviews) Would also be nice if they had a 800 U.S. tech support number to call instead of Korea!

Now onto the camera, one of the main reasons I got it was after watching the video reviews on Youtube, the picture clarity on both day and night were better than my GoPro. Well, that doesn't seem to be the case with mine. Took it out for a spin at twilight and it was disappointing compared to those reviews I watched. Maybe the lens was dirty or smuggled because oncoming head lights worry terrible, they halo'd/star'd out the video till the vehicle passed. Even then it was still not the best I've seen. So tomorrow I'll mount the camera and drive it during the day.

Before I used my GoPros I used MUVI cameras, for front and rear, they had a standby on mod and you could link them both with one wifi control. They also had a time stamp on the video for evidence in court if you need that, where the GoPro doesn't. The only problem I had with the MUVI's, they would overheat (same with GoPro, unless you turn wifi off and use a lower resolution setting), the MUVI's battery would also swell to the point it wouldn't recharge or some of the control functions would not work till it cooled down. But when it did work it was great.

The only concern I have is that others report some overheating and shutting down. I know with windows up and sun shining on a black camera they get HOT! I measured my MUVI's and Gopro at over 145 degrees and they shut down. This is rated at 20c - 60c (-4F to 140F). So I'll have to wait for summer to know if it will take the heat of the cab.

Now onto what I really, really, really, like about this camera. First of, it not only has a time stamp, but GPS stamp and speed stamp, all of which you can turn off. I turned off the speed stamp because if you're in an accident that can and will be used against you in a court of law! Even though they could recreate your speed it would still be harder to prove it than if they just look at your video. BTW, officer can not by law take your video without a warrant. If is your property and your evidence. So tell them either get a subpoena or a warrant for a copy of the video. It has a parking mod with motion sensor that you can set. You can also turn the parking mod off since it defaults to that when the vehicle isn't moving for any length of time. I prefer a continuous recording so I turned off the parking mod.

This leads me to the PC or Mac interface for the video's, I just FRIG'N love it. The GPS maps out everywhere you went and uses Googles maps to show you. This is without a doubt the best computer/car cam interface I've seen. They get a AAA+ on it, at least for now until I use it more.

The other PLUS I liked about this camera is the rear camera that records on the same card at the same time and in the computer interface program you can switch between each file seamlessly! Also you don't need a separate power cord for the rear camera. It comes with a 15 ft coaxial cable but I'll have mine mounted in my camper shell on the truck so I ordered a 50 ft one to run from the cab to the rear window of the shell.

So that's all for now, look at the reviews on Youtube there are couple of well presented ones that go into detail. If anyone is interested on other cameras and how the compared to this one, go to: http://dashboardcamerareviews.com/dash-cam-comparison-table/

You can buy most of them here on Amazon.

Feb. 15th Update:

The halo'd/star'd out lights in the video I found was the lens had a smudge on it. So if you don't keep them clean or touch it with your finger you'll get blur video or halo on the car and street lights.

Day time video is GREAT, I only wish it was 1080 at 60sec maybe they can do that in the next model. Nighttime is also good when you have lots of ambient light, like driving in a city, rural roads it's not as good but would do fine if you had an accident. I haven't been able to use the rear camera due to needing a longer coaxial cable, 50ft on order.

On one of the Youtube video reviews the guy also has a DR500 2CH he's using for a rear camera plus using the 650 and 500 rear cameras as side cameras for a 360 degree coverage.

So I'm going going to get another DR650 and do the same. I've already had the opportunity to use my Gopro cameras with the NCHP when I had a trucker try to run me off the road, got everything I needed to prove his intent. He was fired from his job, but without the video I would not have been able to prove anything.

So far I'm completely satisfied with the operation of the camera, except the firmware update. Still working on getting that resolved.

Feb. 18.

I just received my second DR650 for using as a rear view and side camera. Starting it up it immediately went into firmware update mode, unlike the first camera I purchased. With the new firmware it gives me more options then before. So I tried every way I could to get the first camera to update but it just refused to do so. So I'm returning it for a refund and purchasing another one, hopefully it will work correctly.

I've now installed two DR650 2ch on my truck (Tacoma) with camper shell. I have the main cameras for front and rear and the smaller (rear) cameras for L & R side views. Took all day to install both because I took my time and professionally installed it running rubber conduit to incase the electrical and the coaxial cable. Easy hookup with the Power magic pro's. product_title: Etekcity 3 Pack RoverBeats Bravo Professional Over Ear Stereo Headset with Microphone, Black/Green
review_body: Okay, here is my tale of woe: for my serious headphone use, I go with a higher quality (and higher priced) set. I want the set to fit comfortably right out of the box and I have very little patience for anything less than excellence.  Through the years, I've had to replace many $200 - $500 headsets mostly due to my own clumsiness. For example, I lost one set because the wire had gotten wrapped around my desk chair without my realizing it. I yanked the desk chair away from my desk to vacuum the rug underneath and bam, the headphones were rendered useless. Go me.  After I destroyed yet another high-end unit last week, I decided that I can't be trusted. I would rather have a lower-priced product, even if it means lower quality, because I can't justify spending over thousand dollars a year on headsets. Hence, this purchase.  The fit was a bit tight at first. I have a narrow head and these things hurt my ears. Fortunately, that only lasted a couple of days and they're pretty comfortable now.  The sound quality is just... okay. I can tell a huge difference between my previous higher-end sets vs. these, but let's be fair here: that's exactly what I expected considering the price difference. It took a few days but I am now used to the inferior sound quality and I consider it to be a small sacrifice for the savings.  The microphone seems to work well. I use it often and there hasn't been any issues; people seem to hear me just fine. I like that it can be moved out of my face when not in use -- that's a huge plus for me.  All in all, I am happy with this purchase but if your standards in headsets are high, you likely won't be.

product_title: Brainwavz M1 In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Very comfortable to wear, decent sound quality
review_body:
For the price, these are good-sounding in-ear headphones. They are extremely comfortable to wear also, and sometimes that is half the battle! These are very lightweight. Quality-wise, I think the wires have a bit too much "memory", and I can't get them to lay flat: They want to wave and bounce around.

Sound-wise, they are not bad for the money. They are not for serious listening, but just fine for multi-tasking and when you are out and about in public places. There is a bit of sibilance and the sound lacks the richness that I like. It has a very pronounced stereo quality, with definite change-overs from one side to the other. Another interesting observation (interesting to me at least...): I find I need to adjust the volume with almost every song I play.

For my ears, there was a definite breaking-in period, and the sound improved quite a bit over a relatively short period of time--not too many hours time.

**I received a free sample from Brainwavz.

product_title: Brainwavz S5 IEM Noise Isolating Earphones With Clearwavz Remote and Microphone for iPhone iPad iPod
review_body:
I did receive the S5s as a 'for review' unit from vendor. But I'm trying to stay objective and my enthusiasm is genuine given my general lack of enthusiasm for in-ear headphones.

The S5s sound 'awesome' and I am experiencing near-zero discomfort while wearing them. I've tried them on a range of sounds, from a Lorde to a Bach cello and then back to the rich sound of Amy Lee and Evanescence and... can I say again that I'm impressed?

So, to make it short, I'd rather use over the ear headphones but if, in ear were the only choice, I'd go with the S5s in a heartbeat if I could afford the price.

- 16 ohms rated impedance
- 18 HZ - 24 kHz frequency range and based on my listening experience I have no reason to doubt it. Not many headphones cover such a range.
- 110 dB sensitivity at 1 mW, again I believe it
- lots of ear tips provide to choose from
- 1.3m tape style cord
- 3.5 mm gold-plated plug
- 1/4\\" gold-plated adapter (sweet)
- beautiful black and red hard case with 2 interior pockets for ear tips and the 1/4\\" adapter

They come with a 12 months warranty so... I'm impressed, if I am allowed to make an understatement.

Being 'wired' headphones they will work with anything you can plug them in. They don't have noise-cancelling capabilities but, even with the standard ear tips, the noise isolation was good enough for me to easily ignore someone running a treadmill and playing some loud tracks only a few feet from me.

It's 5 stars for their true high end sound, the high end look and feel, the nice stylish and protective case and the overall quality of the set and package.

product_title: JAM HX-P930 Trance Plus Wireless Light Show Speaker
review_body: After the initial unboxing of the speaker, I was pleasantly surprised to read that the speaker comes fully charged.  I wish all companies would take up this practice of shipping their products fully charged.  The Bluetooth paring to my iPhone was relatively simple.  I like that the speaker talks to you to tell you that its powered on as well as paired.  The sound that comes from this little speaker was very impressive.  I don't like how the lights come on automatically with powering up.  It would be nice if it defaulted to no lights, but three touches of the dimmer button shuts them off, so it's not a big deal.  I like the size of the buttons on the speaker.  There's three buttons on the side.  One controls the dimming and the other two change the lights and the light patterns (mood inducing).  On the top of the speaker there are six buttons.  A power, two volume controls, a skip forward and back, and a pause/play button.  Next to the power button is a rubber flap that underneath houses the charging port, a aux in port and a spot to insert a key (included in packaging) to change language.  All in all I think the Jam speaker is a quality little speaker with great sound and an added bonus of built in mood lighting.

product_title: Nude Audio Nude Move L Bluetooth Portable Speaker
review_body:
I first ran across the NudeAudio Move L when staying at a botique hotel on Miami beach. It was a sheek looking room with this portable speaker that fit well into the room decore. I easily paired my smartphone, streamed Pandora, and was greated with loud, vibrant music that filled the room. I had to see how loud the little speaker would go but didn't keep it at max for too long for fear of being disturbing the room next door! The next week I purchased the Move L and couldn't be happier.

I'm an audiophile whole spent a pretty penny or two on speaker equipment. This portable speaker is not going to replace a decent stereo system but that's not what it's intended for. It's portable, it's plays at loud levels, and it won't burn your ears. And it does all this in a very afforable, small package. In my opinion, there is no other portable speaker that can match the size, performance, and price that NudeAudio has delivered. Easy to pair, long battery life, slick design, and it carries some low end to the music that other higher priced portable options can do.

product_title: 1byone OUS00-0181 Rectangle Digital TV Antenna, Anti-UV Coating, Waterproof and Lightweight, 60 Miles Omni
review_body:
This indoor/outdoor antenna from 1byone is a great way to cut loose from your monthly cable bill or to get over the air signals for rooms that aren't wired for cable. You can also use this antenna to get over the air TV signals in an RV, travel trailer or boat. Because it's an amplified antenna, you will also get better reception than with a passive, flat panel antenna.

This antenna picks up analog and digital TV signals as well as FM .

In the package is the flat panel antenna, mounting accessories, the power adapter, the power inserter and a waterproof connection cover for outdoor installation. You will need a coax cable (not included) of the necessary length to hook up to your television.

You can mount the antenna on a wall or on a pole (not included.)

I've found that outdoor mount gives me the best signal from the most number of channels, but mounting inside a window is also a good choice. Once mounted, try swiveling the antenna in different positions and then run your television's channel scan. (You'll need to run the channel scan every time you change the position of the antenna.) Once you discover what position provides the best reception, you're done!

I live in a large city so there are lots of TV signals around me and I am able to pick up loads of channels with this antenna. If you live in a more rural area, you may have the best results mounting the antenna elevated on a pole in order to pick up weak signals. Go to antennaweb dot org and plug in your zip code to see how many stations can be picked up in your area and what direction to orient your antenna to get the best signal strength.

I like the flexibility of being able to mount inside or out and the the fact that it's amplified makes it an excellent choice for the best signal possible.

review_headline: Not solving my issue and not returnable. But the product is good.
review_body:
This is a new item and not returnable. I learned a big lesson during replacing the lamp for my Samsung S7178W that I would like to share here. I bought a new Philips lamp from Amazon. After installed and watching for 7 days with beautiful picture then my TV started shutting down by itself with 3 LED lights flashing in front of the TV. The TV brightness was not adjustable for some reason while it was working. I thought it was the lamp was heating up and became defective so I returned it. When I got another lamp the problem was still the same that the TV will turn on for a few minutes and shut down itself with 3 LED lights flashing. If you have 2 lights flashing then it is other issue. I started to search the internet but could not find definitive solution. I then bought this ballast and it did not solve the problem either. The color wheel looks fine but when I use my finger to rotate it, it will only move about half turn. After I replace the color wheel the problem went away so it seems the old color wheel may not running properly with the rpm required especially after I replace the lamp possible due to the heat created with the new lamp.

During the investigation of the issue, I have learned that the DLP light engine is quite sophisticate system so no wonder there is so many possibility to cause this 3 LED flashing problem that seems no definitive one solution to fix all the problems that people reported on Internet. The ballast is used to turn on the lamp and keep it on. There is digital circuits on the ballast to control and feedback the status of the lamp to the DMD board. The DMD board is the major control unit for the light engine. It has sensors to monitor the color wheel and the DMD engine too. So any of these components, such as lamp, ballast, color wheel, DMD chip, and the DMD board itself, having issue will likely shut down the TV automatically to protect the circuits. This sophisticate feedback system is making the debugging very difficult without special investigation tool. All other components are easy to be replaced and with reasonable price in Amazon, except the DMD board which is likely TV model specific and hard to find.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_headline: It's excellent at finding the specific model number from it's vast ...
review_body:
This is my third unit. Once you have the App downloaded on your computer you plug in the USB cable, and the computer App asks you to list the components in your AV system. It's excellent at finding the specific model number from it's vast database. It will step you through the different activities asking you clear questions about who controls the volume, what input does your TV use, who selects the channels etc. In about 15 mins. your using the remote. Once your using the remote when things don't go right you push the help button and the remote asks a series of questions to get you back on track. If the same issue happens a few times repeatedly the remote will ask you if you want to try and fix the problem. The remote will walk you through a sequence of steps and ask you to verify if a unit is turned off or on or is it at the right input, etc.. I have found this little tune up to be very helpful at improving the remotes performance.
I have also done some crazy scenarios and invented some custom activities. For the tech savvy the programming App can be very powerful and allow for a lot of custom stuff like, setting delays, reprogramming buttons, learning strange remotes, etc. To name only a few.
I have used the Logitech for years and over time the buttons begin to stick to the point you have to replace the remote. I have used both the 700 which is rechargeable and the 650 which uses batteries. I actually like the battery units better. When the batteries go dead I do a quick swap and I am back. With the rechargeable unit when it goes dead it will be the next day before all the individual remote can go back in the drawer. The 650 is cheap enough to justify the battery consumption. It goes months on one set of batteries. I do compensate for the rechargeable unit by setting a recharge day once a month before it goes dead right in the middle of Sons of Anarchy.

product_title: Yamaha RX-V477 5.1-Channel Network AV Receiver with Airplay (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: but given my love for Yamaha audio products
review_body: I install Home Theater systems for a living, and my previous receiver didn't even have HDMI inputs. Not that I needed them, as the one item with HDMI (my gaming PC), was connected directly to my TV. The real reason why I did the upgrade was to be able to play my Amazon music and the music on my PC directly through the receiver. With my old receiver I would have to connect a 3.5mm stereo cable to the headphone jack on my tablet, and then plug the other end into the receiver. This tied me down to staying within a few feet of the receiver, and if I walked away, then there was the problem of my 15 month old fooling around with the tablet.  Along with this receiver I bought the Yamaha YBA-11 Bluetooth Wireless Audio Receiver. Obviously any Bluetooth stereo adapter would work, but given my love for Yamaha audio products, I decided to just go all Yamaha and I was not disappointed. The receiver comes with USB ports, so the YBA-11 which uses USB for power was able to plug directly into the receiver to get power. Also, because the YBA-11 properly decodes digital music transmission and transmits all the coding over the digital coax cable, the RX-V477 was able to automatically activate the relevant speakers and decode the specific enhancements on the digital Music such as Dolby II etc. With several HDMI inputs and one HDMI out which goes to the TV, I removed the 3.5mm stereo cable from my PC and sent both audio and video from my PC to the RX-V477 using just the HDMI cable. I also like the fact that I could connect my old school combination DVD/VHS player to the RX-V477 via Composite RGB connection plus digital coax audio, and the receiver would then send the video to the TV over the HDMI cable. The receiver is also future proof as it is capable of handling 4K video. Sound is crystal clear and a pleasure to listen to. We streamed a movie off Amazon and even the surround sound was clearer and more distinct, as opposed to the previous receiver. The only issue I had was that this receiver is taller than my previous receiver, and I had a problem fitting it onto the shelf of my entertainment unit. Fortunately I had some small rubber feet left over from an Ethernet switch that I had rack mounted just this week, and thanks to Yamaha's design team, the feet that came with the RX-V477 are removable. Totally happy with the purchase, so I guess that's why I've been playing \\"cuz I'm happy\\".    Update 12/09/2014 - Okay, did my first firmware update over the Internet and it went well. Note, if you want to turn your receiver on over the network using the app for Apple or Andorid, go to the network settings and make sure networking features are turned on even when the receiver is off.

product_title: Sangean RCR-5 Digital AM/FM Clock Radio
review_headline: Far superior functionality compared to Sangean K-200 (and any other clock radio I've ever owned)
review_body:
I own both this model and the Sangean K-200 (and this review is cross-posted). The K-200 has superior sound quality and a smaller footprint on a bedside table, but this model is better in nearly every other way that's important to me; it's so much better that the K-200 got demoted to our office/sewing room and I now use this one as my daily alarm clock and go-to radio. Here's my take on why the RCR-5 is much easier to use...
(1) Physical raised buttons for on & off and preset-changes. The RCR-5's buttons are easy to feel in the dark and work great. The K-200 has those flush under-the-skin membrane buttons and they do NOT work well; to the point that I have to press the on & off button several times to get it to work. So frustrating, especially when trying to turn off an alarm quickly -- I just gave up on snoozing it entirely.
(2) Amber backlit display. This is SO critical for a good night's sleep if this alarm clock is going in your bedroom. Blue light triggers the "awake time" chemicals in our brains and amber light triggers the "sleepytime" ones; I found the K-200's blue glow to be difficult to fall asleep next to. I have a much easier time falling asleep with the RCR-5's amber light by my bed instead.
(3) Weekday alarm. Both Sangean models offer this awesome feature (set an alarm to ring at the same time only on weekdays), but the RCR-5 is much easier to set. The K-200 makes you use the tuning dial to set the alarms (turn, then push to set), and it's hard to advance to the next thing without throwing your current setting off with an accidental twist of the dial as you push.
(4) Fade-in alarm. Love this feature, both for the easy wake-up for myself and because it makes it easier for me to snooze or turn off the alarm before waking my husband earlier than necessary. RCR-5 has it, K-200 does not.
(5) Volume set for alarms. One of the things you can set per alarm on the RCR-5 is the volume it will turn on to -- this is FABULOUS!! With the K-200, you have to physically turn the volume knob to the level you want the radio to turn on to in the morning; this is a pain if you also listen to the radio at a louder volume during the day. Or if you have a toddler...see below...
(6) Volume control is a wheel on the side of the RCR-5, not a big glowy dial on the front (as it is on the K-200). This is particularly important if you have a toddler in the house! With the K-200, my daughter would wander by and randomly crank the volume all the way up while the unit was off, just to play with the big fun dial...so the next time I turned it on, BLASTING SOUND! Ouch. I finally learned to turn down the volume before turning the K-200 on, but it was a hard-won lesson. The much more subtlety-placed wheel on the RCR-5 doesn't look like a shiny toy, so she hasn't messed with it yet. Hooray.
All in all, the RCR-5 has the best functions & features of any clock radio I've ever had. I wish it had the nicer sound of the K-200, but the RCR-5 just works better for me in every other way.

review_body: Overall solid piece of equipment for those of us who don't like cords. I bought this for the wireless, sport style and great reviews. I'm not a runner by any means but find myself in varying situations of physical movement - from a desk to a shop environment. The amount of up and down movement this set allows vs cords is second to none. Not getting caught on something anymore is a magical feeling. I had no interest in the big over the head studio phones for the reasoning of heavy physical movement and price. I can use this set for just over a week straight in 1-4 hour streaks without having to recharge it. It fits comfortably on my head and seals out most sounds pretty well (just ask everyone who's tried to get my attention). The only time it gets moderately uncomfortable is from having only one side hanging on my ear and the other on my neck. Sound quality is great and clear, only lacking in the true bass department. If you push these against your ears for a better seal you'll get the missing bass tones. Connecting these aren't a big hassle either. I use this primarily with my LG G3 & off and on with my laptop. Every now and then you have to go a screen or two into the control panel on the phone for it to transfer all sounds to the headset. The LED indicator light that blinks for any setting is based in one corner and doesn't do a great job of lighting the entire clear section up. Phone calls are about average from what I've been told by those on the other end of the call. The ear pieces are wide and will make you look like Princess Leia, but I wasn't exactly going for looks. It may also take you a few times to figure out where the user control buttons on the right ear piece fall. I've found myself trying to click volume up only to hit skip forward 4 times. I would definitely suggest these to a friend or colleague if they're looking for a headset that will stay on their head no matter how much they move around.

product_title: Etymotic Research MK5 Isolator Low Profile Noise-Isolating In-Ear Earphones
review_headline: A pleasant sounding earphone, worthy of the entry level price.
review_body: These are my first real in-ear headphones I've ever used, I've used many earbud style products, but never IEMs. I've always been hesitant to purchase a universal IEM because I fear they would be uncomfortable or provide an inadequate seal. Well, I'm happy to say that with these Etymotic MK5 I am able to get a good seal, resulting in a pleasant listening experience, sort of..  Personally, I am still on the fence regarding any future universal IEM, mainly for these reasons: -Initial discomfort during the break-in of the rubber materials -Loud microphonics, especially during lower listening levels -Discomfort after extended use (2+ hours), my ears tend to feel rather 'plugged up' after a longer session of listening to these, as if I need to let them breath -Sore ear for a little while after a long session  However, I have considered the future purchase of some custom IEMs, because listening to these MK5 has opened my eyes to the world of IEM, for example: -I really enjoy the isolation provided, lets me get lost in the music or my work more easily -I enjoy the discrete nature of the IEM, I can listen at higher volumes without any concern of someone else hearing my music -The overall experience of IEM is a very discrete, personal listening experience  The MK5 overall is a solid buy, I tend to use them for 1-2 hour periods throughout my workday. I enjoy the sound signature of them, but I can tell that a higher end model would sound better. There is definitely some room for improvement in the overall detail, but none the less it is a pleasant sounding earphone, worthy of the entry level price.  The size of the Ety MK5 is also worth mentioning; once installed they are extremely small and nearly disappear completely into your ear.

I am very pleased with this device- came in on time (Amazon Prime) and in fine packaging and was exactly as described.
Now- the product- this is such a handy little device! I found something I didn't see written in the description-

*** If you put your devices in a specific order, it can/will automatically change to an "active" signal source.

By this I mean, I put my entertainment computer (ASUS VivoPC) on port 1, Sony BDR on port 2, and my cable DVR on 3. The Sony stays off unless I want it on... the computer I use randomly throughout a given day, the DVR is almost always on (if we're awake). I keep the selected source as port 1- then, when I turn on/wake the PC, it automatically switches to the computer w/o my having to change the source signal. Within 2-3 seconds of the signal going away (sleep mode/turn off) of the computer, it moves to the next port (Sony BD is off), so it moves to the DVR (on) and away I go! Again, later, if I wish to turn back on my computer, I wake it, and poof- the signal source goes right back to port 1 without my intervention!

no power needed, just plug and go! BTW, Amazon also sells a little 3 pack of HDMI cables for <$6 so- no need for re-running wires through the wall to get to the mounted TV!

Update:
I've had this for 9 months, and initially, I loved it. However over the last few months I noticed that the USB port seemed to be "wiggly." Well today it broke completely off! If you read the reviews, you will see that the USB port, used for charging, is the Achilles heel of this product.

Original review:
I've had this thing for a week. It arrived the Saturday before it was scheduled (Monday), which was great for me, as I was leaving on Sunday for a 5 day cruise on a 41 foot sailboat.

I was initially concerned about the sound quality and battery life. During the cruise I learned that BOTH of these concerns were unwarranted, as the sound quality is GREAT, and the battery lasts over 6 hrs on a charge. We had to lower the volume while at anchor for fear of disturbing the boats anchored nearby. The quality of the sound is great, and amazing that it comes out of this little box! During our trip, at one point we had to beat our way through 6 foot swells in Buzzards Bay in 25-30kt winds. We did this while listening to Dick Dale via Pandora on my Android phone. The speaker's battery held out longer than my phone, so we switched to my crew's iPhone, and continued on our voyage. It was AWESOME!!!!

My ONLY critique of the speaker is that the control buttons (power/skip/etc) are black on a flat black button. They are hard for me to see with my 55 year old sailors eyes... I tried to fix this with a silver sharpie, but that is wearing off, and currently looks bad. I'll try to fix it again.

product_title: Dual Quad Bay Outdoor HDTV/DTV/UHF Bowtie Television Antenna
review_body: Appears well constructed, however, there is no packaging material inside the box, like shrink-wrap, peanuts, etc. The antenna just comes loose inside the box, so mine was minorly bent a few places upon receipt due to normal shipping & handling.  Was able to straighten it out, and don't believe it affects the performance, but the company could have packaged it better.  Easy to assemble, basically join the two pre-assembled  halves by clamping them together with the two main support bars, extend the bowties, and join the cables.  Mounted on my roof on pole extending above roofline - estimate the antenna's height approx. 28 feet above the ground. The antenna works okay.  Definitely needs a pre-amp antenna amplifier though.  Hardly received anything without one, but then I'm in a slight valley with trees so that probably accounts for much of my signal problems, and would likely be similar for most antennas.  I'm to the N of Metro Atlanta, GA.  Most of my stations are to the SE.  But a few are E, and a couple NW.  Wanted to compare this antenna's ability to aim at different angles, so first I tried pointing both sections to my main SE direction to establish a baseline, using a compass and direction headings from signal showing websites.  (There's one the FCC has, also Atlanta Digital TV for my area.)  Received 79 channels (with pre-amplifier), though roughly 10 or so would pixilate and go in and out.  When pointing one of the dual bay sections at a different angle to stations not at my main SE direction, was able to receive a few more channels that hadn't before.  But this also made a couple more of my channels to the SE to now sometimes pixilate that hadn't before when both sections were pointed the main direction.  Still, the majority of the main SE signals come in okay, though a couple I get at night, I don't receive at all during the day.  So overall, I'd say this is a decent antenna, for a decent price (approx. $50 - $60, depending on seller).  However, get a pre-amplifier! The antenna's ability to point in two directions is of some use, but you may lose some signal quality than when both sides pointed in the same direction.  But if in a bad signal area, you may need a much bigger antenna which will of course cost much more.

product_title: Klipsch RP-240S Reference Premiere Surround Speaker with Dual 4 inch Cerametallic Cone Woofers
review_headline: Don't sell your surround system short by skimping on the rear speakers!!!
review_body:
I've done a much more extensive review on the RP-280 floor speakers I bought as part of my Klipsch system purchase. However, it doesn't make sense for me to copy and paste it here because it was aimed more at the floor standing speakers. So I'll write a more condensed and "focused on these" one here.

Rear surround sound speakers are sometimes over looked, especially when buying a system where you purchase the speakers separately. "I don't care much about rear power, I'll just get cheaper ones for the back" or "They only provide a bit of sound from the rear, who cares" are sometimes things I've heard from friends or family. That is quite an incorrect way to thinking about it. It's almost like saying, I don't care if my back brakes work because my front ones work and are more important. If you're going to spend a fortune on front floor standing speakers and a subwoofer, why skimp on the "rear end" of the system? The speakers in the back do not have to produce the same amount of power or sound as the floor standing front ones do. But they need to be able to handle a lot of power if you're going to be blasting the system. Also, for audiophiles and movie buffs, you want a system that can really make you feel like you're there, 360 degrees around. These speakers will help you accomplish that and much more. Keep in mind, these are no small surround sound speakers. You're not buying a Bose system here with tiny cube speakers. These are heavy and meaty surround sound speakers for sure. They weigh a little over 13lbs a piece. I went with the 240's rather than the 250's due to the size of my room. It's a fairly small room and the 250's are meant for the largest rooms. Even the 240s are technically "too much" for a room the size I have them in, but I wanted Reference Premiere and these are the ones I liked most. Extremely easy to hang with a very sturdy bracket that is attached to the speaker. I bought some 27lb rated wall anchors and screws and used those. Twice the weight I needed, but why risk them falling off the wall.

They sound absolutely incredible. I have a nice Marantz receiver that is capable of creating some absolutely lifelike sound from my music and movies and these speakers come through in the clutch. When watching a movie, you feel like you're there. The subtle points in movies or music that you never heard before, you now know exist. When I play PS4, I'm hearing things in the game that I never heard before and they are coming from these rear surrounds. I'm very impressed with these and they are a powerhouse of a speaker. product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_headline: Big Sound In a Tiny Package!!
review_body:
Hard to believe the quality in this tiny box. I give it a five star based on price to quality. I read someone say the battery poops out quick - he apparently didn't give it an initial deep charge, needed by any new rechargeable device. I find it hard to believe how long it runs with such a tiny size.

There is a newer version with a bigger LCD screen. To me, that only means faster battery drain. The model I have is 4 gig with a micro SD slot. 4 gig is plenty for my purposes (working out, etc).

Lastly, the stock earbuds that come with it don't sound bad, but fall out of my ear. I also bought a good set of JBL earphones = and this thing kicks a**. So figure, for less than 80 bucks I got a system (player & phones) I can clip on my shirt that really does it. I am a professional studio musician and am very fussy about sound.

Remember, you always have to factor in a good set of phones - no MP3 player comes with killer "cans", and any music player is only as good as the output device (earphones or speakers).

review_headline: Simple and cost effective way to switch to banana plugs
review_body: These plugs are very high quality and easy to use. My previous receiver forced the copper wires into the terminals.  A pair of scissors to strip the wires, my maglite LED flash light, and these plugs and I was up and running in less than an hour. review_headline: Replay Audio SPKR1PK Portable Mini Wired Speaker - Pink - Good sound for its tiny size & price
review_body:
This is the smallest mini speaker that I recollect trying out; it is about 2 inches high, 1 3/4 inches in diameter, and weighs in at just about 1.6 ounces (per my postal scale). If you are looking for a tiny wired speaker that you can take anywhere with you, and are just trying to improve the sound from your phone speakers a bit, this this little thing is probably exactly what you might need.

Just a tad wider and shorter than a D-size battery, when seated on a good surface (like a table or counter) this speaker plays OK bass, with decent mid and treble. When held in-hand, the bass gets lost in everything else... but it still sounds a bit better than just listening to the phone's speakers. If you are looking for an ultra-portable speaker, then this surely is that.

Neither the Amazon listing or the retail documentation mention a warranty, so if an issue arises I would return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. We did receive this speaker gratis from the seller and our son put it to use to objectively find out how well it performed. My statements here reflect that testing.

If you are looking for a low-priced, very portable wired speaker of this style, size, and capability, for use similar to what I have described above, then we would recommend giving this Replay Audio Portable Mini Wired Speaker a try based on our experience with it. It is a basic, simple speaker that is designed to look cute and go anywhere you need it to. Has worked very well so far.

Recommended.

Go for it.

review_body:
i wasnt able to buy this through Amazon; its 2-3 months for delivery? Whoh. I'd prefer it from them but that seemed a bit too long. I did manage to find one though and bought it due to the great reviews I've read. It does sound great, holds its own even with music, and the subwoofer is really impressive give its size. I also have a pioneer SP-SB23W, another good bar, but this one edges it out a bit. Only problem was with the connections. I wanted to use this instead of a home theatre/surround sound setup which had too big a footprint. I've tired of all the speakers..the 10" subwoofer/ottoman in my living room, etc etc..but only had one HDMI out on my receiver. Only way to use it via the receiver (TV, blueray, cable box, modem into it, then out to the soundbar) was to cut RCA plugs and use the 2 leads as speaker wires. It worked, and I'm a happy camper. I wonder though why the soundbar- and the Pioneer had the same inputs- doesn't come with HDMI, RCA, AND speaker wire terminals. For situations like mine.
Its much more bluetooth friendly than the SB-23, the Yamaha is smoother going from lets say the receiver to a smartphone, or different devices. I found the Pioneer tends to hang up, just doesn't seem to work as well. And the remote pass through on the Yamaha works, i have the bar IFO the receiver and it all works well. Its not going to give you high end surround sound, no bar will, but given its comparatively small size it comes pretty darned close.

review_headline: Love Our Sonos System and Used it for our Wedding
review_body:
I really can't express how much our entire household loves the Sonos system. We have a 2-story corner unit town house that is about 1500 square feet. We have (2) Play-5 speakers set up in a stereo pair on either side of our television. We have a Play-3 in our bedroom which we use nightly to drown out the sounds of the city. Our Play-1 goes with us wherever we need it most. Generally, it is set up beside the couch to give us surround sound when watching movies. product_title: Sentey LS-4420 Warp Black/Red Headphones with Stereo High Definition, Over-Ear, Detachable Audio Cable 3.5mm, Foldable Headphone, Powerful Bass and Carrying Bag Included.
review_headline: Great look, great fit, but lacks bass and amazing quality sound that other reviews said it had.
review_body:
Let me just start off with saying that I hate reading reviews on products because I tend to read that a lot of people liked it, but then the occasional person says they hated it and all I can think is "What if I hate it as much as that person?" So I know why you're here. You're looking for good headphones that sound like Beats and look cool and feel comfortable, but without paying $300 for them. Well, I'm going to try my best to convince you that you should believe this review because I'm always afraid that the product won't be anything like the reviews say.

These headphones came in a very nice box and came with a little bag to put them in. They look nice and feel amazing. They cover my whole ears so there is no pressure on them and the top part is padded too so it doesn't hurt my head at all. They are very comfortable, but my ears are average size so if you have bigger ears, they might not cover the whole thing. They do adjust very nicely and are very flexible though and they look and feel nice. They are a little bulky so if you don't want that, then I wouldn't go with these. I like the bulky look so I'm a fan of it. They do stick out a little bit, but it doesn't look too weird to me. So now that I've hopefully convinced you that they look nice, now on to how they sound.

I'm just going to jump right in and say it as it is: the sound isn't the best. If you're looking for headphones with sound quality like Beats, I wouldn't recommend these. There is very little bass picked up through these and I honestly was looking for headphones with a good quality sound to them without paying an unnecessary amount of money, but I guess to get that quality sound, you need to be willing to pay more. These are good headphone, but I don't know if they were worth the $50 I spent, I'd say more like $25 or $30. Although they look and feel nice, the point of headphones is to sound nice which I am underwhelmed by with these. If you don't care about bass or anything like that, these are good to have, but if you're into stuff like punk rock music or just love to listen to the whole sound of it like I do, I wouldn't go with these. As a college student who has very little spending money, I am not willing to buy Beats and I can live with these. If I just turn the volume up enough, I can get a nice sound that satisfies me.

If you made it this far into my review, thank you. I didn't think you'd make it because I tend to like short and simple reviews. I hope that this helped you out in choosing the right pair of headphones for you. These are nice, but I wish I had an idea of the sound quality before buying them, but what are you gonna do, right? The comfort makes up for the lack of bass, but I hope when these stop working, I can get a pair of headphones with a nicer sound. Not that these sound terrible, they just sound like any other normal pair of headphones. If I could give this product 3 1/2 stars, I would because they don't deserve a full 4 but they're not a 3 either. I suggest Bose headphones if you want really good bass, I've heard music through those and they sound like Beats but they're cheaper and more comfortable. Okay, I think this review is done for real now. If you made it this far, I love you forever because I would've left after the second paragraph.

product_title: RCA Compact Outdoor Yagi HDTV Antenna with 70 Mile Range
review_headline: Cut the cable or satellite cord and enjoy free over air TV in High Quality HD
review_body:
I turned off my cable connection for TV and save close to $100 per month. I kept cable for my high speed online computer connection over 60MB.
I purchased the RCA ANT751 and after connecting it to my TV inside the house I picked up over a hundred free channels. I then mounted the antenna on the roof and pointed to Mt.Wilson about 8 miles from where I live. I was surprised to find over 130 channels however most were in a language I didn't understand. After using my TV hide/shown feature I was able to narrow it down to 32 channels of which almost half are in HD High Definition. I was able to pick up channels (Movies!, Get TV, Grit TV, Me TV, The Works TV and others) that we love that were not available even with cable. Before turning off your Cable or Satellite check this website (www.antennaweb.org ) to see how many channels are available at your exact location. I live very close to the towers however if you live in Burbank CA for example you can only receive a few over air channels, (ABC & FOX the only network channels available in Burbank CA) and none of the great ones I listed above that regularly show great classic films and TV shows. I save $1200 a year by switching to free over air TV and cutting the cable cord. Reception is better than cable even in rainstorms. I highly recommend this product.

product_title: Sennheiser IE80 Headphone
review_body: One word to describe these headphones are "Incredible". As a musician, I appreciate good music when I hear it. When I first popped these in, I was blown away by the bass these bad boys produced. I own a pair of Custom 1964 ears Qi IE monitors and these ie80 are on par with them. The sound stage on these are quite large but not as large as my custom 1964. The mids are not overwhelmed by the lows at the reference setting which I enjoy and will not change. The highs are tolerable and roll off nicely. These are not neutral at all but are a fun listen with slight emphasis at the bass region. These headphones  does require some burn in time to really appreciate the sound signature. Sennheiser pulled an extraordinary off with the ie80 and are my daily headphones when I am on the go. These headphones rival some high end over ears without hesitation. I hear no distortion with my Galaxy Note 4 driving these. The sound that comes out of these are high definition and tasty. You will need to try out the various ear tips to get the best seal. I went back to the stock tips that comes with the headphones as they gave me the best seal and bass reponse along with clarity after trying the others. The foam tips are a close second as they mold to your ears and probably the most comfortable for long wear. Despite having great bass response, I may not use it because it not very durable in the long run and they muffle the highs a bit. Comply foam tips are a bit overpriced IMO and will add up after buying several over the years. So I will just stick with the silicone tips and avoid that hassle. I do not plan to work out with these as I value them a lot and will take care of them. Lastly, you may not appreciate these headphones if you don't get the best seal and burn them in for some time. So try the supplied extra tips and see which one works best for you before making final judgment on these headphones. Thank you Sennheiser for another masterpiece. HD indeed!

product_title: Symphonized GLXY Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones with Mic and Nylon Cable
review_headline: Very nice and warm sounding earphones with good bass response
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:c622c2bcac662d9634e2243a8c218c5d]] This is a review of the Symphonized GLXY earphones. I was provided with a free sample for evaluation.

There are so many earphones in this price range it's challenging to know where to start. Fortunately for me, I wasn't looking for earphones... Symphonized came to me asking if I'd consider reviewing these GLXY earphones. I'd never heard of Symphonized before so agreed to receive a set for evaluation.

This set of earphones comes with 3 pair of silicone tips (S-M-L). That's common to most earphones these days. Although you may get a good enough fit with the provided tips, I always prefer to use Comply tips. Comply tips are foam and provide greater comfort and increase the amount of noise isolation from the outside world when listening to the earphones. But you may be happy enough with the stock ear tips.

The GLXY has a braided nylon cord. The total cord length is 4 feet 4 inches (3' from the plug to the Y and 16\\" from the Y to your ears.) These types of cords are less prone to tangles but due to the rough surface, do increase the amount of noise transmitted through the cord to your ears when they rub against your clothing. One thing you can do to reduce that noise, other than not moving, is to run the cable up and around the back of your ear before putting the earpieces in.

The earpieces are marked with a L and R. But an easier way to figure out which is which is to pay attention to which side of your body the in-line microphone is. There is an in-line microphone for use with your smartphone and the sound quality is very good. People tell me they can't tell if it's the in-line microphone or my iPhone microphone when I speak to them using these earphones. The in-line microphone is on the L side of the cord and that makes it easy to tell which earpiece goes in which ear.

The plug is gold-plated and that helps to ensure a good connection when you plug it in.

The wood earpiece is nice looking but more importantly is part of the reason that these sound so nice. Wood imparts a desirable sound characteristic that is different than using plastic or metal. Just look at how many high-end speakers have wood enclosures.

The sound is full and warm. Good bass response.

I like them and think they're a good earphone in this price range.ntly is part of the reason that these sound so nice. Wood imparts a desirable sound characteristic that is different than using plastic or metal. Just look at how many high-end speakers have wood enclosures. The sound is full and warm. review_headline: Was pretty happy with Sansa, DX-50 completes my joy.
review_body:
Can't call myself an audiophile, my hearing ends at 8 Kilohertz and
I often have a ring in my ear(s). I come from years of the use of the
Sansa Fuze, listening with Phillips she-9500 and Bose QC-1's, sometimes
using a Quinpu Q1 amp (which isn't compatible with the Phillips).
I was in band all through school. I also put in a lot of time listening to live
classical music in my younger years, mainly at the UAF concert hall in
College, Alaska.

I listen to mostly classical, emphasis on Bach.
The DX-50 is supposed to be a step up, and it seems to be, even
to me. Sound seems sweeter yet clearer. I've only had it about a week
and have only used it with the Bose headphones, just briefly trying the
Phillips in ear phones to check compatibility. My verdict is the DX-50
is a perfect match for my ears. I've been listening to FLAC's ripped
from CDs, mostly. Unit came with 6" coaxial, 2 Port usb charger, and I
think a standard RCA cable. No headphones. I did try listening to some
Low bitrate voice files (16bps) and got only a hi-pitched 8k? tone. I have
a higher bitrate version I'll load when I get a bigger card. Also, I have not
got the internal memory to work. It seemed unformatted, I tried formatting
to Fat32 using my desktop linux OS. Seemed to work but I couldn't access it
and it disappeared when I put a card in, seemingly favoring the card. I doubt
I will mess further with it, and it seems a small issue for the audience of this
player. Hi quality. You'll like the jacks. Sennheiser CX 300 II in ear buds are
on the way to upgrade the Phillips.

product_title: Hot %Original Superlux hd681evo Dynamic Semi-open Stereo Professional Audio Monitoring Headphones &Headset Double Detachable Audio Cable
review_headline: That awkward face when you press play.
review_body: You know that feeling when you press play and make that awkward face, like "what"?  A colleague bought one pair to detach from the rest while working. He's no audiophile, not even a big fan. Musically, he's "just a guy". Asked me for advice, since I own a range from Beyer DT990 to Sennheiser PX100. Browsed the reviews, told him do go get 'em. He thanked me later. But then I myself got curious. Took it away from him immediately, to test them in the comfort of my home. Instead of the weekend, as agreed, I brought him the phones back the very next day and got me mine.  Downsides: bulky, cheap-looking, not too comfortable (but that can be modded). And that's all, folks. Edit: 2 more slight downsides - pressure on the head and maybe too many lows. Maybe. More edited below.  Everything else is amazing for this price range.  Compared them to Grado SR80i, Audiotechnica M50s and Beyerdynamic DT990. They sound definitely better than Grado ($99) in all aspects, only Grado are smaller and handier, like grab-and-go phones. ATH has much more resolution, you can hear the seriousness (for 3.5 times the price) but are unbearably uncomfortable comparing to Superlux. And then, though there's more detail, there's also a serious peak in high lows, causing ATH to kind of mumble; this renders me tired quickly. To me, ATH is just for quick references, or field recording (being closed back). Back home, I need to be in top form to stand them. Supeluxes are modest in comparison, far less detail, but then... kind of... enough detail. Don't know how to say it. On the other hand, no fatigue. You can push them louder and louder, and no, no fatigue. No annoying serious peaks anywhere. Not that I can hear. Then, the Beyer 990. Not that is some serious sh1t, true professional studio monitoring headphones. How to describe - just everything is there, nothing too much, feather light, no pressure on the ears, maybe, just maybe lacking some portion of lows, but then... they're there. Youjust need to get used to them. Comparing them to Superluxes seems ridiculous. But wait. Put away the Beyer, put on the Superlux. And I don't hate them. I don't laugh. I don't feel pity. I don't. I keep listening. Guys, hey, it's forty one god damn dollar. Go get 'em now.  Ah, yes, you get velour (it's actually some soft cloth) pads, so you can change them if you want. I found the cloth ones more pleasing, both physically and sonically (maybe I'm imagining). Just to mention. That's kind of nice from Superlux. Go get 'em.  Edit: as for the pressure on the head - the plastic frame presses a bit to hard for me. I think this can be modded with a hot air gun or some other warm-up device. Also the overhead band have elastic straps somewhere inside, which are also strong. I'm thinking about replacing the entire band with a soft leather one, with adjustable length, without elastic parts (good experience with this approach in Beyer DT990). Also, when you lower the pressure on the ears the low end (that might be a bit too heavy on these phones) gets a bit lighter and more studio-like. I suggest you do whatever you can to loosen them and they will sound really insane for that price range.
