product_title: Sennheiser Momentum Headphone
review_headline: Great headphones for a middle of the road price
review_body:
First off, I am in no way shape or form an expert on headphones. The only other headphones I've ever had are the 20$ skullcandy ear buds, which are great to me. So knowing where I'm coming from, I was quite impressed with these headphones, it was a whole other world. The in unboxing was great. I got the brown ones and aesthetically these are stunning, simple headphones with clean lines. The cord with the controls on it had the coolest audio back that bends like an elbow joint, so handy and very sturdy.

They are very well made and the materials felt great. The leather headband fit great on the top of my head and didn't put too much pressure. The ear peices slide up and down to be adjusted. The comfort level of these is very high. I could forget I as even wearing them, they don't clamp too tight on the head at all. However, if you have larger ears these will probably not work for you. I have small to average ears and these fit me perfect but if my ears were any bigger it wouldn't seal correctly.

On sound isolation these did a great job , music could just barley be heard around 25% and it took the volume to be at 60- 70% to really start hearing words and the music's being listened to. It blocked out outside noise fairly well but still allowed you to be aware and hear your surroundings.

On sound, these had a beautiful sound. Now again I'm not an expert and have little to no knowledge on how headphones differ in the sound they offer. I can say that I thought these sounded crisp, very clear, and balanced to me. There was not much bass at all and highs, mids, or lows didn't drown out each other. There was no muddiness to the sounds like you get with some headphones that I've tried. These aren't bass head headphones at all, very balanced comfortable listening.

I did buy these along with the Vmoda LP2s, which are a little different, because I couldn't decide just based off of looking online. In the end I chose the Vmodas and returned these. It was a really hard choice and in many ways I felt that these were better headphones but chose the Vmodas because the soundscape they offered highlighted more of the lows and everything had a layer of richness and ambiance that these momentum didn't have. It was like comparing flat screen tv speakers (momentum) to a movie theater experience (Vmoda) where the lows are really rich and rumbling in the background and you feel it. The Vmodas are not exactly bass head headphones though, I didn't want hardcore bass thumping, the sound is still pretty balanced and does a good job across genres but just adds some extra lows. Again two different headphones with different goals, I just like the other one better for what I'm looking for. But Senneheiser is a great high quality company that offers high quality sound and would be the first place to look for audio needs. I would still recommend these headphones!

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 25 Headphones (wired, 3.5mm)
review_headline: Comfortable, compact and very good (but not exceptional) audio quality
review_body:
These headphones are great for the price. They lack the audio quality of my Polk Ultrafocus 8000's, but they're a bit less expensive, much lighter and smaller, and more comfortable. I tend to agree with reviewer comments that the noise cancellation is better on the Bose QC 25's, but it's a subtle difference. The difference in size isn't subtle though: the Polk UF 8000's are too heavy and large to travel with, but the Bose are not a problem. I've worn the Bose now on several California-to-Europe flights (~10 hours) comfortably, which I could not have done with the Polk's.

However the audio quality of the Polk's really is quite a lot better, particularly in the depth and clarity of the lows. The Bose seems comparatively thin in the lows and overemphasized in the mid range. The Polk's to me seem much more neutral across a very wide spectrum. Don't get me wrong, the Bose sound great if I listen to them by themselves, the differences become more apparent when I A/B them.

Have been delighted using the Bose on my flights and for long home use, but I still prefer the Polk's when I'm at home for shorter (eg < 1 hour) listening stints.

I've used both to make phone calls with an iPhone and through a computer with skype, and both seemed to work equally well. For that, the comfort of the Bose is a win since the audio quality doesn't matter.

product_title: Sony ICF-S10MK2 Pocket AM/FM Radio, Silver
review_headline: Good Functional Radio, Lacking in Quality
review_body:
This is a review of the Sony ICF-S10MK2 AM/FM radio sold by Amazon.

Pigs Do Fly !!! Amazon sent me 2 of these and the packing was over the top. You'd think Amazon was sending me rare china. Too bad they didn't take the same care with the $300 camera I ordered a couple of years ago.

I ordered these for my grab & go disaster kits. So far, I've used both for a total of 7 hours each. Sound is very decent at lower levels, breaks up at higher volumes. Made in China, fit & finish are ok, plastic body isn't as solid as it could be. Runs on 2 AA batteries, with no port for AC power. Red LED "Tune" light is on continually, so using it for its' intended use of fine tuning stations is impossible. 1 of the radios has an issue with the sound, as you turn the on/off wheel, the sound suddenly & loudly comes on. There's no smooth increase in sound. Not a big issue, just poor quality control.

Using the external sound jack, sound is decent using stereo ear buds (radio is mono, so only one side of the ear buds works).

Pros:
Good value
Decent construction for the price
Decent sound at lower levels
Lightweight
Good reception in metropolitan area (AM & FM)

Cons:
Inconsistent quality control between units
A little tippy when standing upright.
Antenna does not recess into body of radio, hangs at the side. Might catch on something and get damaged or detached.
May not survive rough handling, fall from table, etc.

product_title: Sony SRSX33 Powerful Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
This Sony speaker is small, but surprisingly loud for its size. It filled my living room with booming sound and didn't distort when everything was cranked up to max volume. Good EQ and really good bass. There is a "sound" button that turns on Sony's optimized surround sound, but I don't know that it makes a whole heap of difference. There is no information on this feature in the instructions- I had to Google it to even know what it was supposed to do.

The Bluetooth seems snappier than other Bluetooth stuff I have. The Sony seems to have less of a delay when I start my music or when I switch to a new song. The back of the speaker has an aux input so you can connect that way as well. Surprisingly, but I felt like I almost had better sound quality when I was connected via Bluetooth than hardwired in. There is also an option to connect via NFC (near field communication), but you needed to download an app for that on your phone and I didn't feel like it was necessary since the Bluetooth connection worked well for me. It paired easily with my LG phone.

The Sony can also be used as a speaker for phone calls. My phone rang and there was a different ringtone that came from the speaker in case the phone isn't nearby. It auto-paused my music and I used the phone button on the speaker to answer and end the call. There has got to be a mic in the speaker because I moved my phone away from the speaker but was still able to carry on a conversation. The audio from my caller came through nicely without any noticeable delay.

The included micro USB cable is really super short, but those cables are used for everything now, so most people who want a longer one probably already have one in their house. Battery life is rated at about 12 hours so it should easily last through a party on the patio!

product_title: Tecsun PL880 Portable Digital PLL Dual Conversion AM/FM, Longwave & Shortwave Radio with SSB (Single Side Band) Reception
review_body: This is an amazingly sensitive radio.  It's well built, has many, many features, and is pretty small considering everything it does.  It pulls in an amazing number of stations on all bands.  The sensitivity FAR exceeds any other radio in my house and my car.  It also has excellent sound quality (mono only) from the single speaker.  The rechargeable Li-Ion battery that comes with it will run it for many hours before it requires charging.  I really can't think of anything bad about this radio.  One thing you must understand is that if you are looking for shortwave (SW) stations you really need to be outside for best performance OR have an outside antenna.  By moving outside my radio received 10x as many stations, moving outside and using the external long wire antenna they provide doubled again the number of stations.  Also, you will get more SW stations at night.  I can't comment on the long wave reception as that is not used in the US.  OK, I've been using this for nearly six months now?  Anyway, I do have one suggestion for the manufacturers:  Please allow the external antenna to be used for MW reception.  Right now, even if you plug an external antenna into the external jack it still uses the internal loop antenna for MW.  I've built a nice loop antenna for MW DX, but I can't use it with this radio.  I can't think of a good reason the radio was designed to not utilize the external jack for ALL bands.  If you plug an antenna in that isn't the right kind for the what you're trying to receive that's on you.

product_title: MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphones with Memory Wire
review_headline: Passes my audio test, but some interesting design choices
review_body:
First off, this is a good sounding pair of headphones. I use the song "This Could Be Anywhere In The World" by Alexisonfire to test the quality of new speakers or headphones and this was able to reproduce the very low bass note that hits in the beginning of the song. I mostly listen to spoken word and I haven't had any trouble listening to all of my favorite podcasts. The price was also spot on for me; it seemed like the appropriate amount for a pair of headphones. The volume slider is also a nice touch to allow me to adjust volume even more subtly than I can on my phone. I haven't tried the microphone yet.

Now, the reason I took off a star - I'm not 100% thrilled with the design. I like the over the ear loop, the volume slider, and even the button (worked without any software to pause, play, and open voice commands on my Motorola Moto X 2014). The part I don't like is the material used to make the cable. It seems flimsy, weak. I haven't had any issues with it (no breaking), but it has retained the shape that it was in the package for a couple of days now, and it just feels cheap. I felt like I would rip it in half while taking the clip off of it. The part where the headphones split is awkward, too. Since it encourages the headphones to branch out, it's weird having the slider that would tighten the headphones sit right on top of it. I used a pair of scissors and (carefully!) cut that in half so the headphones are free.

So, they feel kinda cheap, but sound really nice, carrying case is a plus, and I'm glad it worked with no software on my phone.

product_title: Radius Atomic Bass 2 Ear Phones w/ Superb Bass Response
review_headline: Purchased for a specific purpose: Sleep
review_body: I have plenty of headphones for listening to music; I purchased these headphones for a specific purpose.  What drew me to them was their unique design that allows them to fit fully in the ear.    I recently had to spend several nights in the same hotel room with two other individuals who were heavy sleepers (read: snorers).  If you are a light sleeper like me, you know what kind of dread that can instill in you.  One night without sleep is bad enough, but three was something I just couldn't deal with.    I ordered the Radius headphones specifically for use while sleeping.  Owing to the fact that they fit completely into the ear (by reversing the sides), I was able to use utilize these headphones with a white-noise app on my Android phone.  Not only did I not hear any snoring, my sleep wasn't even disturbed by a helicopter that apparently spent several minutes flying only 50 yards outside my window one night!    I subtracted one star for an incident that happened while preparing the headphones.  As I was removing the rubber \\"ear canal\\" pieces that came pre-installed to use a different (provided) size, one of the headphones came apart.  I was a little disappointed in the construction quality (I don't consider $26 for headphones to be \\"throw-away\\").  I pushed them back together and had no further issues with them.    As for the \\"Superb Bass Response\\", I primarily used them with white noise (which has no bass).  However, I did play some music through them using my iPod nano just for the sake of this review.  While I didn't find it \\"superb\\", neither did it suck.  I would give their bass response a solid \\"good\\" for their size.  The music itself felt kind of shallow, like an FM station with a low-wattage signal.    In any case, they did do an overall \\"superb\\" job in allowing me to sleep in what would otherwise have been an impossible situation.

review_body: I wasn't sure how well these were going to sound since they costed me a little under $20. Once I received these from the mail, I connected these to my laptop since headphones sound better on my laptop than on my phone. After testing these out, I have to say that these have very good, balanced sound quality. Usually I would get Skullcandy earbuds since some of them sound really good compared to other headphones, and they wouldn't be very expensive. I saw these on Amazon as one of the highest rated earbuds, they also weren't very expensive so I wanted to try these. So far, I have no regrets.   My best experience with these earbuds was when I was watching Interstellar on one of the computers at my school, where these sound AMAZING! The bass was incredible, and the sound didn't lose any clarity. I was not expecting that sound difference to be honest. I recommend testing out these headphones on different devices so you can get a feel as to how good these can sound. review_headline: Value pack that is almot audiophile quality
review_body:
I received this set as a review sample and was surprised by the quality given the bargain price for this pack. The overall construction is a cut about similar cables in this price range.

One of the more interesting features is the strain reliefs, which are large and look more like a continuation of the connector housings (it's the orange part.) It is stepped and does function as a relief, but I have not had these long enough to determine how effective it is.

The cable is very flexible and the connectors are precision fits to female jacks. I mentioned that these are near audiophile quality. I fired up two tube amps in my studio, and placed the cable in close proximity to them while playing music through the cable to a pair of studio headphones. There was a little noise from the heavy RFI environment that I created, but it was sporadic and weak. It would have been much more pronounced and constant with lesser cables, so these do work fairly well in RFI dirty environments.

Overall, these are excellent for use in low RFI and EMI environments and are perfect for lower end applications like small speakers, headphones and the such.

review_headline: You Don't Know "JACK" Until You Read This! Helpful :) Xbox & Non
review_body:
The people who complain about this jack, don't know jack. Please see my uploaded photos for clarification.
When I see people whining and complaining about really good products, it really gets under my skin.
The reason why I felt compelled to start posting accurate and factual reviews about good items and good experiences.
For Xbox users, this adapter will most likely not work with your application. Please read further for advice.
For normal uses and common audio applications, this will work without any problems if you match your components properly.
Common things to look for and know when matching audio components like these are...
Tip, Ring and Barrel or Sleeve. Analog or Digital. Sticking with the basics for this application you can't go wrong.
See the tiny black strip on the metal shaft? That is important. Mono has 1 or 2 while Stereo has 2-3. Left, Right, Ground and Mic.
In most cases they are backwards compatible, but not always.
Xbox uses a mini-jack mono plug, but since it has 2 rings, it can be confused with a stereo jack. Also, it's a 2.5 mm (3/32") not a 3.5 mm (1/8").
One ring is used for listening and the other for voice. It is mono but with a microphone design. Left and Voice. Please research for more detail.
But overall, if you can see my photos, it's broken down visually to get a better understanding.
Connected to my laptop you can see the audio level is spiking and reading the audio clearly. Matched with a Cobra M29 BT EXT Microphone.
Overall from my experience alone, this jack works flawlessly and is an excellent deal for the price.
I did purchase the wrong jack but kept it, so you can see this same review for the other. Not much of a difference. 3.5 to 2.5 instead of 2.5 to 3.5.

review_headline: corded audio speaker that I loved (at the time)
review_body:
I don't usually write reviews, but with my latest experience, and the end result, I promised myself, if everything went well, I would; so here goes. Bought this speaker in October 2014. I had a cheap 5 watt, battery powered portable, corded audio speaker that I loved (at the time), but wanted a speaker with more oomph, bluetooth capabilities, usb battery option, and long battery life. Let me say first, I am one of those people that will research for months before buying, whether that product is for $10 or $1000. It's partly due to the way I was raised (thanks dad), but also the want and need for buying things that I will keep for a long period of time (my environmental friendly side). My research for portable speakers included both brick and mortar and online shops, written and video reviews, friends, outside users and professional reviews, etc. Pretty extensive for some, pretty normal for me. After a few months, I finally decided on the Sharkk. And I was not disappointed. Amazing sound, amazing battery life, good heft, felt strong in the hand, sank down strong into the bottle holder of my backpack, great bluetooth pairing and distance range; and the price was awesome compared to the competition.

Fast forward to July 2015. Speakers fell out my bag and fell more than five feat to the concrete below. Instant change in sound from deep lows to high and tinny. I knew they were done. Tried prying them open, but to no avail. Went online and emailed sharkk customer service on advice for opening them up. Their reply was swift. The speakers were not meant to be opened up (bummer), but if I sent them in, they might replace them. I have become accustomed to using portable speakers on a daily basis (if not hourly), so I went to post office, sent these in, and went back online to buy some replacements. Found some off brand speakers with good to excellent reviews touting more power, awesome sound, similar battery life, at a cheaper price point.

2 days later:got the new speakers in the mail and they f*<k!ng sucked compared to the sharkks and were just $20 cheaper. But they would have to do until I got the sharkk speakers back. A few days later and even more peeved at my replacements, got an email from sharkk saying that the speakers had reached their office and that they would send them out as soon as they could. I've been in this situation before and knew that the process could take up to a month so I gritted my teeth and tried to enjoy the replacement speakers as much as I could all the while thinking to myself: "Why didn't I just buy another pair of sharkk speakers?" I'm an idiot sometimes.

2 weeks later (which seemed like 2 years because of the replacement speakers sucking so bad), I received a refurbished pair of sharkk speakers and they ended up being an upgrade from may first pair! The new one's had illuminated buttons, what seemed like more power, better Bluetooth, and longer batter life. "WHY DIDN'T I BUY ANOTHER PAIR OF SHARKK SPEAKERS INSTEAD OF THE CRAP ONES I BOUGHT TO REPLACE THEM!!"

review_body:
I've gone through more than a few headphones in the past 3 months trying to find some that would give me the sound and comfort i was looking for to use while working. I tried california headphones, vmoda xs, sony mdr 1r and senheiser momentums. each had their pros and cons, but didn't have what i was looking for. I have to adjust them to get them to fit just right, but once i do i can keep them on for a long time. there's some warmth but not enough to make my ears sweat . they don't completely go around my ears, they rest on the outer edge of them, but it forms a good seal so there's no loss of sound.

I really like them, enough to be fine with whatever cons they may have. they do have the xl pads as a replacement, but at this point, i'm not sure i would need them. they sound great and look great, they have a really low profile, so they don't stick out from the side of your head like other headphones ( I felt sort of like frankensteins monster with the sennheiser momentums) they collapse very small and are very portable. all in all a headphone i think is worth giving a try.

product_title: BeoPlay H3 - Gold
review_body:
I really enjoy these headphones. The sound reproduction is excellent. I've owned countless headsets including Shure, UE, Sennheiser, Beats by Dre, Vmoda, and many others. These are among the best sounding single driver headphones I've heard. The sound is a good balance of high's mid's and low's. The bass is definitely there. I listen to a lot of hip hop and EDM and I was not disappointed at all. However, you MUST find the correct tip to ensure a perfect fit in your ear in order to hear these headphones accurately. As with most earbuds, the slightest dislodge will degrade the sound quality tremendously.

I would give these 5 stars, but I think they could be a tad cheaper considering the build quality. The buds themselves are machined aluminum, very sturdy and attractive, however, the cable is very thin and appears cheap for how much you've paid. Also, the built in control button is a little frail, and operating it is a little flimsy. All in all, I would highly recommend these headphones if you're in the market for a great sounding, medium/high priced earbuds.

review_headline: Solid little speaker.  4 and a half stars
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:9da6bcef881544606739450158c3bb2c]] This speaker comes with the instruction booklet (small print but has the necessary information), a combination micro USB to USB/male headphone audio (Aux) cable (about 2 feet in length) and a wrist strap.

The speaker appears to be a well-made rugged device that can handle being tossed around in a bag and carried around as it is small (less than 3 x 3 inches) and lightweight. The speaker has a rubber protective shell that appears to be able to handle being dropped without an issue. The speaker is also water resistance (not water proof) but is made to withstand most wet situations, even having a rubber flap for protecting the switches and micro plug. I wouldn't count on it working if dropped in a pool of water but it could handle being rained on or splashed onto.
Initial charging takes about 3 to 4 hours, which is a bit longer than some but does give about 6 to 10 hours of play time depending on the connection (Bluetooth versus Aux cable). Initially, I thought there was an issue with the micro plug of the speaker because when I connected it to my I-pod and began to play music it was cutting out badly. I determined after getting a replacement, that the combination cable was defective and not the micro plug of the speaker.

The speaker has a power switch that you can select either Bluetooth pairing (Or NFC) or an Aux (Headphone type) connection on the back. There are two small LED lights that indicate pairing and battery status. The top of the speaker has volume (next/back) buttons and a play/pause (answer) buttons as well but I found them to be in an awkward location on the rounded corner of the speaker that makes them hard to find to push. To me, the top of the speaker would have been a better easier to find location. Pairing was not a problem with my Galaxy S4 and paired within a few seconds of me powering on the device. The device's Bluetooth range was very good as I walked as far as I could on the same floor of my home and the speaker continued to play without any interruptions.

I also tested its speaker phone capability and the calls were clear and sounded good on both ends of the conversation. The mic is hidden somewhere near the play button. I couldn't find it as it was well hidden but it worked well nonetheless.

Overall this is a very solid portable speaker that is lightweight and easy to carry around for outdoor use that can handle being tossed around and getting splashed on. product_title: PRO-POWER - Portable speakers
review_headline: Excellent quality speakers for the price you pay!
review_body:
After owning and heavily using these little speakers for over 5 1/2 years, I can honestly say I can not be happier! My order history says I paid $0.00, but I think they were actually about $2 when I purchased them. I have used these speakers everywhere: in the shower, in the bedroom, in an office, in an industrial environment, outside, etc. The sound is good for the price of the unit. I frequently use these to listen to music and podcasts in the shower. Volume is plenty loud for rocking out and understanding spoken-word above the shower noise, and the sound quality has not seemed to degrade at all from the exposure to high humidity. When used in a noisy environment, they work well when pointed directly at you and within about 5 feet or so, but these speakers are not big or powerful enough to project far against other noise. They have decent bass sound for their size, and are not tinny. The distortion at high volume is also surprisingly low (almost non-existent).

I use these speakers for playing audio from my phone and tablets, and I find the attached audio cable to be much shorter than I'd like. It is permanently attached to the speakers, and just long enough to wrap one time around the battery compartment (the manner in which it is designed to be securely stored). Due to the convenient storage of the cable, and the availability of audio extension cables, I do not feel like this warrants any detraction from a 5-star rating. I use these pretty much exclusively with rechargeable AAA batteries, and get several hours of playing time before needing to recharge or swap out batteries. The LED power indicator on top is good for indicating when it's time to change the batteries. When the LED starts to dim during higher volume portions of the audio, it's time to change the batteries. I have used the included USB power adapter cable a few times, but it is also not very long, and there is no "onboard" storage option for it, so I find it easier to just swap out or recharge batteries when needed. Some other reviewers have commented that these speakers are flimsy and easily breakable, but I have not found that to be the case. They usually make their home folded up at the bottom of my quite full of gear backpack when not in use.

Pros:
- Good sound for their size
- Small storage footprint when folded up (good for packing)
- Folded storage configuration protects the speakers and audio cord

Cons:
- Short audio and power cords
- No storage for USB power cableto just swap out or recharge batteries when needed. product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_headline: I can't recommend this player highly enough.
review_body:
If you want an MP3 players that has a big multi-color screen that also plays videos, than this Audio player is obviously not for you, but you probably already have a phone that does that, so what's the point? But if all you want is a small, reliable, high quality audio player at an incredibly low price, you won't do better than this. This is my second Clip +, but I've also owned the a Clip and a Clip Zip and I find this one to be the perfect match for me. First it has micro SD memory expansion which the Clip lacks, and compared to the Zip, I find it has better battery life and better controls, and I don't think the bigger, full color display of the Zip really adds much value for me. In fact I find the mono screen on the Clip + easier to read.

The only downside of the Clip + is that it has a non removable clip on the back, and it is prone to breaking, and if it does break (Like it did on my Zip) there is no easy way to fix it, even with epoxy, and you will just have to do without, which is a pain. (Actually you can epoxy some other type of clip to the back, but it will likely not look very good, and probably end up making it much thicker). I wish they had kept the same clip design of the Clip, which was removable and much sturdier.

Another nice thing about this player is that the price is so low (especially refurbished), that you can get two, so that one is always charged and ready to go. Just swap the micro SD card or put the same content on both, and you will never be thwarted by a dead battery.

Anyway I can't recommend this player highly enough.

I know what you're thinking -- $1200 for an AUX 3.5mm to 3.5mm (mini to mini) cable??

You can ignore the marketing hype -- 99.99% Pure Silver, 72v DBS, PSC+, etc. It just simply works, and is FANTASTIC. I A/B'd (blindfolded, asked someone else to swap cables) this Audioquest Angel, a generic 3.5mm to 3.5mm cable ($10), and a mid-line Audioquest Victoria 3.5mm in my Lexus LS600H w/Mark Levinson Premium Audio. I could immediately hear the subtle nuances the Audioquest ANGEL brought out - deeper, fuller bass, excellent treble that wasn't sibilant or rolled off.

It's excellent for car stereo use via the AUX jack, or even for connection to speakers via iPhone/Andriod/iPad/Macbook, etc.

It's also worth noting that for a nominal fee, Audioquest can reterminate the terminations (e.g. 3.5mm to RCA or RCA to RCA, etc), should you need different terminations in the future.

Bravo, Audioquest, Bravo.

review_headline: Great Receiver with a couple of small flaws
review_body:
The Pioneer VSX-90 receiver is a great addition to my A/V setup replacing an aging Denon (that sounded good, but always had some nagging issues like having to have the TV on when listening to an audio source via the network). First off the sound is great delivering both pounding music and high energy TV/movies nicely to my Boston Acoustic speakers. With five HDMI inputs and two outputs (two zones), it handles my Cable, Blu Ray, and Apple TV with room to spare.

With the network connection, this receiver can play from so many sources, I probably won't ever be able test them all. I haven't tried the Spotify connection, but might. I don't really need all the over-the-network options (most won't as they will have their favorite) as I play almost all my digital content from my Mac, iPhone, or iPad using AirPlay, which works great once setup (see below for a few setup issues). My digital music sounds fantastic through this receiver into my living room.

Source switching is a little slower than I'd like, but not so much so that I really notice much. The auto-source detection works great switching between surround, digital, and stereo as the TV content changes (this was always an issue with my Denon and doing it manually was not much better). I still have some playing to do with these settings, so will report back if any issues come up.

Setup, oh setup. The physical setup of the receiver was a piece of cake with a nice layout on the back of all the inputs and outputs. The remote is also very easy to understand with plenty of source buttons (no need to choose only a few for custom buttons as other receivers make you do). Setting up the network access was ultimately easy, but fraught with early errors. You have to download an app for your phone or tablet to setup the wireless (I understand that you can do it from the front of the receiver, but that must be buried in user manual - another little issue there in a moment); the app was pretty straight forward, but very slow on the detection and crashed the first few times I tried to get it setup. In the end, when it didn't crash, the wireless setup flawlessly and I was able to access the receiver from my iPhone, iPad, iMac, and MacBook instantly over AirPlay. The setup issues cost it half a star in my book.

You can also download a controller app for the iPhone which can control the receiver and its settings and it can play your music right from the iPhone over AirPlay. When the setup app crashed the first two times, I tried to play music from the app via bluetooth and that worked well as well. Though the app seems to work well enough, its user interface has too much flash when I'd prefer a straight forward approach to getting to where I want to go in it.

This receiver also lost another half star on the manual. My previous receivers all had nice, thick books to reference for all functions and setup options. This receiver - with more options and features than any I've every worked with - did not come with a paper manual; instead it had a bfief quick setup booklet that mostly told you how to get the apps. review_headline: Very sturdy and seems well made with a nice finish
review_body: Very sturdy and seems well made with a nice finish.  I do think that the weight limits are probably a little bit exaggerated. The 47" TV I mounted on this weighs about 48-50 pounds according to the manual. But when this wall mount is fully extended, there is quite a bit of drop (guessing 1" at most) as it moves away from the wall. Probably more suitable for a somewhat lighter TV.  One needs to be very careful locating the mounting studs. Also the metal straps which mount on the rear of the TV are left/right so one needs to be sure of which is which if you want to be able to adjust the tilt more easily.  I like the double articulation for getting almost any viewing angle one might want.  Adjustment for final TV level required removal from the wall mount several times, and rotation adjustment of the mounting plate is easy to overdo. For this reason, before mounting your TV on the wall mount, if you presently have a factory stand on your TV I suggest leaving it on the TV (if physically possible without interfering with installation) until you have finished final leveling. With your factory stand still on the TV you can remove it from the wall mount and set it on a table or the floor in order to make leveling/rotational adjustments. After final adjustments I then removed the factory TV stand.  A little more sturdy for my mid weight TV would have gotten five stars.

product_title: Winegard FlatWave Amped Indoor Amplified HDTV Antenna (FL5500Y)
review_headline: Much better than an older amplified rabbit ear antenna
review_body:
I used this on a Dish Network DVR with add-in digital tuner. Using the same antenna, this tuner did not receive channels as well as a newer-model LED TV tuner. With the older antenna, the weakest channel would cut out every few minutes, making it difficult to watch shows. This antenna was easy to install and use, the 18.5 foot long cord made it easy to mount it on the window and run it across the room to the DVR. I found that the placement on the window was critical for optimal signal strength. Just a few inches higher or lower would make the difference between a 70 and an 89 according to the on-screen display. After using this for about an hour, I found I still got a signal cutout, but it was brief and only twice in an hour vs. about every 5-10 minutes with the older antenna.

The command strips to hold the antenna are too small in my opinion, the antenna fell down a few minutes after mounting it. I'd suggest getting a couple of extra strips to hold it or finding a means to take the load off where the cord attaches to the antenna. I ended up using additional command strips I had to hold it in place.

review_headline: Powerful bass. 4 and a half stars
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:8d16c222b41fc1ad7daadfa6e09d8020]] This speaker comes with the instructions, a micro USB cable (approximately 31 inches), and a male to male headphone audio (Aux) cable (approximately 32 inches).

This Frieq speaker is approximately 6.5 inches long by 2.5 inches in height and 1.5 inch wide. The speaker has a hard silicone shell with black metal speaker grill on the front and sides. The speaker is not heavy but has some weight to it in comparison to other small speakers. Charging time is between 3 and 4 hours and once fully charged this I get about 9 hours of play time. There is a red and blue led light on the top of the speaker that that flashes when turned on, indicating it is ready to pair. Pairing with my Android phone was quick and easy and the speaker beeps and says connected when paired. This can be paired via Bluetooth or NFC.

In addition to the LED light, the speaker has 6 buttons on the top (answer/hangup/siri, volume up/down, next/back and play/pause). The buttons are nicely spaced and a good size for easy use and operation. The back of the speaker has the power switch, AUX port and USB charging port.

Music through both the AUX cable and Bluetooth was loud, clear and sounded pretty good with enough bass to make the speaker bounce around a bit. Unfortunately there are no non-skid feet to keep it from doing so. Four rubber feet on the bottom would be a nice addition to keep the speaker from sliding around. The Bluetooth range of the speaker was ok but not as good as other speakers I have used, cutting out about 25 feet from the phone. Phone calls sounded ok on both ends of the conversation and would be sufficient as a hands free device if needed. Even though the instructions say it supports only Siri, I tried this function with my Android phone and the voice control works on it as well with no issues.

This speaker is a solid one with nice features, good sound and good bass that is powerful enough to make the speaker bounce around. The Bluetooth range could be a bit better and some non-skid feet would be a nice addition to keep this from moving when played at loud volumes.

product_title: JBL Clip Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: JBL Clip vs. JBL Micro (not JBL Micro II) comparison.
review_body:
The JBL Clip & JBL Micro are both nice and there are good reviews on Amazon so I'll focus on some key differences between the JBL Clip & JBL Micro for those who are trying to decide between them (like me).

Bottom line: I kept my JBL Micro and returned my JBL Clip because of the JBL Micro's superior audio fidelity and performance as a receiver-dongle for my home stereo.

I bought a new Bluetooth JBL Micro (not JBL Micro II) because it was on sale at a local store, and I was very impressed with the sound quality for such a small speaker. Then (after doing some research and thinking that the JBL Clip's speaker-phone capability might be worth the higher price) about 2 days later I bought a JBL Clip. As soon as I tried the JBL Clip, I could tell that the JBL Clip's audio-fidelity isnâ€™t as good as the JBL Micro. (I had used both over Bluetooth, but it's difficult to do a fair, side-by-side comparison when switching back and forth via Bluetooth, so I attached a wired headphone splitter cable to both the JBL Micro and the JBL Clip, I set them to the same volume, and I switched back and forth between them to compare the audio quality. The JBL Micro has better clarity, better treble range (cymbals are clearer), stronger base, and can play slightly louder than the JBL Clip. The JBL Micro's audio-fidelity advantage also applies when using it as a "Bluetooth receiver dongle" that you might attach to your home's stereo inputs (so that e.g. you can stream music by Bluetooth from your phone to your home stereo). I found the audio quality difference to be significant, but the average person may not care.

Unlike the JBL Micro, the JBL Clip has a microphone which works nicely as a Bluetooth speaker-phone. It also has the ability to skip-forward (by double-clicking).

The JBL Micro has a big advantage over the JBL Clip if you use it as a Bluetooth receiver dongle that you connect to your home stereo or if you want to connect (daisy chain) multiple JBL Clips or JBL Micros. Regardless of the volume-setting of the JBL Micro's speaker, the JBL Micro outputs (through its headphone jack, via wire) a very strong signal so that the connected downstream device (e.g. a home stereo, or 2nd JBL Micro/Clip) can nicely amplify the signal. However, the JBL Clip's wired-output-signal is relative to its speaker volume. That's bad if you want to use the JBL Clip as a Bluetooth receiver dongle for your home's hi-fi stereo system, because you need to turn up the JBL Clip's volume pretty high in order to output a decent wired-signal to your home's stereo. The result is that you have to listen to the JBL Clip's relatively-crappy sound blaring while you listen to your home-stereo's relatively-superior speakers. And you can't really listen to your home's stereo at low volume because the JBL Clip will be blaring in the background. (For this use-case, I want to be able to set the volume of the JBL Micro/Clip at zero so that I don't have to listen to its relatively crappy little speaker. I can do this with the JBL Micro but not with the JBL Clip.) Similarly, if you want to daisy-chain to a 2nd JBL Clip/Micro, the volume of the 2nd (downstream) device depends on the volume of the first one. That's energy-inefficient and a hassle. (The JBL Micro doesn't have that problem since it always outputs a strong signal through its headphone jack regardless of the speaker volume.)

If you plan to put this in your pocket and be able to control the volume through the cloth of your pocket, I found the JBL Micro's volume dial to be much easier to find and quickly adjust because you can feel the JBL Micro's volume dial above the bezel, whereas the JBL Clip's buttons are all flush-mounted (so no appreciable tactile feedback). I found that even if I put these devices in my ski jacket's pocket, zipped the pocket shut, and then tried to control the volume through the jacketâ€™s cloth, using ski gloves, I could muchmore easily, reliably, and quickly adjust the volume of the JBL Micro than the JBL Clip.

Because of the aforementioned issues (especially the first 2), I returned the JBL Clip to the store, and I kept the JBL Micro. (Also, I just didn't see a realistic case where I'd used the JBL Clip's microphone as a speaker phone, which is its primary advantage of the JBL Micro. Though I will slightly miss the JBL Clip's ability to skip-forward.)

Although it wasn't a deciding factor for me, and it may not be a real issue, I was disappointed that the JBL Clip's spring-loaded "clip" didn't have some kind of a reinforcing security hook (like that of a typical carabiner) such that when the latch swings closed, it would hook onto the upper-loop in order to help keep the upper-loop from breaking off. The JBL Clipâ€™s slightly flexible upper-loop seems pretty strong and probably strong enough for most uses-- unless maybe the device gets snagged on a tree limb when you're hiking or something. While the built-in clip is convenient, itâ€™s cheap and easy to attach a caribiner to the JBL Microâ€™s loop (which seems much sturdier), so the JBL Clipâ€™s â€œclipâ€ seemed like about as much of an advantage as a disadvantage.

product_title: Definitive Technology C/L/R 2300 120v Speaker (Single, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Incredibly lucky to find a like new pair of these in 2014...
review_body:
I know these are no longer in production and finding them has been a real hardship. But I actually scored two of these from one seller last month as used but you can not tell they are not brand new. I had one I purchased way back in 2006 that I have always felt was one of the best center channel speakers I have ever heard, including the newer series demo'd at Magnolia in Best Buy. It is still going strong, as are all my Def Techs from that original purchase. But now I have all three 2300's in the Left Center Right (LCR) positions in my media room, replacing the two Def Tech BP2006TL bi-polar towers I originally bought for my 7.1 system.

The difference adding two more 2300's has made in tonal continuity across the front sound stage is like night and day. The towers were excellent, don't get me wrong. Having subs in all the front speakers is great. But moving from bipolar to direct sound sources using the same model speakers makes for a seamless tonal experience as things move from side to side across the front.

A side bonus for me was that now I can move them in a little from where my towers had to be placed due to the projector screen. These 2300's on an 18" stand is perfect height for our seats.

I also found out by calling Def Tech that they still support these vintage speakers. So I hope to enjoy them for many, many years should any problems come up with the electronics. I would buy two to four more to replace my back surround speakers in a heartbeat for a totally seamless soundstage but I seriously doubt I'll find any more like this.

So if you have a Def Tech 2300 now and you see any used ones come up again in the future in Amazon, you might think long and hard about creating a matched system in the LCR positions of your system. These guys create an incredibly realistic sound for their size. I do not have any regrets... only grins.

review_headline: Fantastic product turns V-Moda earphones into amazing headset
review_body:
Let me start by saying these should work on most headphones with removeable 3.5mm jack. They work on Beats SoloHd among others wonderfully.

I honestly can't believe no other company has made this before. I know others like Beyerdynamics has made something similar but everything about this mic attachment is really well done.

The cable is high quality and wrapped in fabric, the mic is is also high quality with a very nice gooseneck that will keep the boom where you want it, there is a volume wheel and mute toggle switch that is easy to find lower on the cable, and even the plug is really well made and uses the V-Moda 45 degree angle to reduce stress on the plug. Using this with my M100 works as a top notch gaming headset on my PS4 and works even better with my Astro mixamp.

The only downside which isn't even enough to deduct a star for is that sometimes the mute toggle can be a little sticky and I think a nice springy button on the center would be ideal for a mute toggle. Overall though the switch works and im very glad the toggle and volume wheel are right there on the cable. If this mix will work for your higher quality or any headphones with removeable 3.5mm cable, this is just amazing.

product_title: Auray Deluxe Velour Earpads (Pair)
review_body:
Replaced the original ear pads on my Sony MDR 7506 today with the Auray Deluxe Velour Earpads.
When I opened the first package I had to go through the trial and error thing, but this is what I finally came up with, and after the first one the other three went on pretty smooth (I bought two sets). After opening the package I found that if I went round and round just pulling the leather away from the pad, but not turning it inside out, it made the leather part stand up, and was much easier to put on the head phones. I then started working them on the HP's by holding them firmly in place while pulling the leather over the edge of the HP's. I had to go around two or three times before they finally stretched and went completely over the edge. I didn't worry about the slot that holds the leather when done, just worked on getting them over the edge. Once I had them on, I lined the elongated pad with the elongated HP's until they looked right. I then took a retractable pencil that I have, put the point in the slot on the HP's and just went quickly around. The leather pretty much fell in the slot because of the pencil point guiding it. The pads fit real good. I haven't tried them for sound yet, but they did feel pretty good on my ears the short time I had them on. If they sound good, then I'll probably buy two more sets for my other HP's.

review_body:
First off, I want to state that I did not purchase these headphones from Amazon. However, as far as my experience is with these headphones I couldn't not write a review.
Now down to business. I purchased these headphones on a whim because, one, I'm partial to Skullcandy for their great return policy on their headphones and also their good build quality at (for the most part) a budget-conscious price point, and two, I found these at a Home Goods store on clearance for $50 and having known their retail value I couldn't pass up the deal.
I have to say these headphones far exceeded my already high expectations. Straight out of the packaging with zero burn-in time these sounded nothing less than amazing.

Sound: The vocals are super crisp, the highs are very colored with fantastic separation and the bass is very well-defined. Typically I listen to very bass-heavy music and prefer headphones that have very powerful bass response but with the quality of sound in these, they're a definite keeper. The overall sound in these I would describe as open, crisp and airy. I've tested many genres of music with these I normally wouldn't even give a second thought because I'm so blown away with the sound quality. I have nothing negative to say about these.

The build quality: surprisingly sturdy. I'm never hard on my headphones and make sure I take care of all the pairs I own so after about 4 months of almost everyday use these still look new. The outer cups are made of polycarbonate and do not scratch nearly as easily as I was expecting. The metal wire that holds these together is much more resilient than I was expecting as well. I thought for sure the metal would stretch out from continuous use but so far this has not been the case.

Looks: Very aesthetically pleasing (I have the black and chrome). A very unique design and awesome transparent earcups definitely make these stand out but also blend in. Not only are they amazingly functional butalso make for a nice fashion accessory.

Noise isolation: not as good as I had hoped. Really the only downfall of these headphones. They're not noise-canceling, they're passive noise isolating, meaning there is nothing but the outside of the headphones blocking outside noise. For me this is not an issue but I feel is something to address. Although they fall short for outside noise entering they do a great job at keeping music from escaping. Much better than most other designer headphones available.

Comfort: amazing. I've worn these for periods of 5 hours straight with no discomfort whatsoever. Very happy with that. Most other headphones I've had this can become an annoying issue but not the case with these.

Also something else to mention is the mic. The mic itself is good quality (sadly, better than the one built into my phone) and also not only has the play/pause/skip button most mics do but also volume control buttons that definitely add a nice touch.

Another thing to mention is the included soft storage bag and microfiber cleaning cloth that was a nice compliment in helping to protect my investment. The bag seems to be made well and also has a net pocket inside for the cleaning cloth or earbuds or whatever it is you want to use that for which I thought was pretty cool.

Overall, I'm very happy with these headphones. I recommend them to anyone and everyone that cares about really hearing their music and not just listening to it. I feel like these are even worth their retail value which for most headphones I've owned I cannot say the same. These headphones are well worth their price tag.

product_title: Pioneer Fully Enclosed Dynamic Headphone
review_headline: Works well for me, does not surround ear, but on top and not the most compact when folded.
review_body:
DOES NOT COVER YOUR ENTIRE EAR:
I opted for these headphones as I had a similar set years ago, that long since disappeared.
Discussing these with my boyfriend who is a bit more into music than I am, he felt the name was misleading: Pioneer SE-MJ532-K Fully Enclosed Dynamic Headphone
To him; \\"fully-enclosed\\" meant they should encircle your ears entirely. These do not. I have tiny ears and they sit on top of my ears, so most adults ears will not be encircled by these headphones. In fact when I recall my headphones of years past, they were considered a new idea of putting high end headphones on top of your ear. I found those fine and comfortable and these are also quite comfortable for me as well.

SOUND BLOCKING
Of course since they don't encircle your ear, they do not completely cut out ambient sound. To be honest I don't mind that. However I have another headset I take on airplanes that are also \\"on-ear\\" headphones and they have electronic sound deadening. These work fine for that. But, for casual listening, imperfect sound deadening is fine.

SOUND QUALITY:
Well, I'm not a very discerning customer here, so I'm quite satisfied. My boyfriend (a bit harder to please in this area) says he can tell the difference in sound quality between different music formats and compression. So my assumption is, that has to be good.

FOLDABILITY:
I was a bit confused when the blurb on this head set said \\"compact folding system\\". From what I can see the earpieces just rotate sideways and fold in as well. You still have the large head bow to contend with. Okay if putting a laptop case, not okay with an average purse size. My sound deadening ones also bend in the middle of the head bow and fold near the earpieces as well.

SUMMARY:
This will sound like a cop out, but depending on what you use these for, they will fit the bill or they won't. Some pros and cons

PROS
Nice sound quality
Comfortable
Some sound deadening due to nice ear fit

CONS
Not compact, but smaller than over-ear would be
Not over ear, but on top (if that is important to you)mpact, but smaller than over-ear would be Not over ear, but on top (if that is important to you)

product_title: PowerDriver® 1.2V 1200mAh Ni-MH Nimh Pre-charged Rechargeable Batteries AAA
review_body:
These PowerDrive AAA batteries are high capacity, rated 1200 mAh. This is the storage capacity of the battery. If you compare this battery with one with a 800 mAh rating, these batteries have about 30% more capacity. This means you will have a longer run time between recharges than with batteries with a lower rating.

Even though they are performing very well, I am giving them 4 stars rather than 5 only because I think we need to know more about how they hold up after numerous recharges over time.

Don't be put off by the 1.2V, all AA and AAA NiMH (Nickel Metal Hydride) batteries are 1.2 volts. Alkaline batteries are rated 1.5 volts because they start off at 1.5 volts but they gradually drop to 1.0 volts during use, averaging about 1.2 volts. However, NiMH batteries, like these, start off at 1.2 volts and stay at 1.2 volts for about 80% of their discharge cycle.

This means a NiMH battery is likely to deliver much closer to its rated capacity when it's powering high drain devices. In other words, a NiMH battery with a rated capacity of 1200mAh can take many more photos than an alkaline battery with a rated capacity of 1200 mAh

Because I was sent these batteries to test and review, I charged them just to be sure they would take a charge.

From all indications, these are excellent batteries being sold at the time of writing this review at a very reasonable price. I have no hesitation about recommending them.is review at a very reasonable price. I have no hesitation about recommending them.

product_title: Foxnovo F-4S 4-Slots LCD Battery Charger for Li-ion 26650, 22650, 18650, 18500, 18490, 17670, 17650, 17500, 16340, 14500, 10440 and Ni-MH /Ni-CD: A, AA, AAA, C, SC (Black)
review_headline: Supports C size and Li-Ion batteries
review_body:
The F-4S charger is just like its competitors:
- Charges up to 4 batteries independently, monitoring their charge level and capacity individually, with selectable charge current
- Capable of performing a refresh cycle (full discharge/charge)
- Comes with 100/240V power adapter and a car adapter
- Features a display showing the state of each battery

However, it adds some new cool features that are so far unique for a charger of this type:
- Supports C-size batteries [[ASIN:B0041TF5KQ like these]], a must for toys and power-hungry devices for which [[ASIN:B00JRF2GD8 spacers]] won't help
- Supports a wide variety of the new Li-Ion 3.7V cells (used mostly in flashlights for now, as far as I know)

Unlike other smart chargers, which offer a choice between four different charge currents, from as low as 200mA all the way up to 1.5A, the F-4S can only charge at 500mA (the default) or 1A. While it's nice to be able to choose the compromise between charge time and going easy on the battery, I only use 500mA on my other chargers, as more would be too rough on the battery and 200mA takes too long. The 1A setting can be useful for C batteries which have higher capacity and can take a higher charge current, so I don't see the limitation as constraining.

The end of a charge or discharge cycle triggers a very loud triple-beep. This may be an issue for some people, make sure you don't keep the charger near your bed! Unfortunately the signal can not be turned off (although if you're handy with a screwdriver it's easy enough to cut the beeper's wire).

Bottom line: a great charger, and its unique support for C-size and Li-Ion batteries make it the new king of smart chargers. Highly recommended.

product_title: Bose 901 Direct/Reflecting Speaker System
review_body: If you are shopping for the Bose 901 VI, the first thing to concider is if you can properly place these loudspeakers. The PDF manual is available at Bose.com. To sum it up, you need an available flat wall for the 16 rear speakers to reflect off of, while keeping them 8-18\\" away from that wall. They should also be positioned away from the corners so that the outer speakers do not point toward room corners. They should also be 2 feet away from furnishings that are sound absorbing, like a couch for example.    The above criteria alone will eliminate many rooms as a good choice for these speakers, unless they are hung from the ceiling to meet the criteria.    To add a bit further to what the manufacturer recommends, I would suggest being a bit further back from the speakers than they are placed apart. For example, if they are approximately 8 feet apart, I would sit about 12 feet away for the best experience. That is more or less close to my positioning and the results have been excellent.    The next thing to concider is that the Bose 901 VI -Must- be used with the original equalizer for proper function of these speakers. This is true of any series of the 901, dating all the way back to the originals produced in 1968.    To install the EQ , a \\"tape monitor\\" switch would normally be required in a stereo receiver so that all sound can be directed through the EQ, prior to amplification. Some stereo receivers and integrated amplifiers have \\"pre-out/main-in\\" RCA jacks that can be removed for installation of the EQ. However, these options are not readily available on most of today's recievers, which are primarily for surround sound applications.    The other option, which is likely the best option, is to use a separate amplifier and preamplifier, placing the EQ between the two. The rationale for separate components is higher quality amplification as well as higher power. It has been been pointed out many times that the 901 performs at its best by many users that high power amplification is important to the overall function of these speakers. I agree.    Unfortunately, even though Bose has stores throughout the country, many do not display or carry the 901's, and those that do fail to display and demonstrate them with criteria as suggested above. The only place for a good audition will likely be in your own home.    I would personally compare the sound of the 901's to the enjoyment of basking in sunlight. When the sun is shining, we enjoy the warmth and the beauty it brings to all the sights around us. However, if one can only enjoy the sun by trying to observe the details of it's surface, or by studying the sun itself, then the point is missed entirely. True, the Bose 901 VI may not get all the details, or all the details perfectly, but what it does offer is the warmth of its midrange, spaciousness and visceral impact. Very enjoyable.

product_title: Headphones, Sound Intone I66 Metal Earphones with Microphone, Bass Earbuds with Remote, Noise Isolating, Cute In Ear Headphones for Kids, Adults, Compatible for iPhone, Android, Ipad, MP3/4
review_headline: Amazing Sound, Especially for the Price
review_body:
I spend a good deal of time with headphones on or earbuds in my ears and I have formulated some very strong ideas of what makes a pair of headphones or earbuds worth consideration. I was anxious to try the Sound Intone i66 earbuds and they have far exceeded my expectations, especially considering the cost (as I write this, they are going for about $11, but price may change). For such low-cost earbuds these are among some of the best I have used.

Ok, right out of the package - I received a pink pair of earbuds. Bright, bubblegum pink! That does not bother me in the least as color is irrelevant but being pink these are just perfect for a teenage girl. These also come in brown so there is a choice if pink is not desired.

In the package are the earbuds and three sets of ear inserts so that getting the right fit is easy. The inserts are a little more stiff than some of the others I have used but they are not uncomfortable. The slight stiffness might be slightly less comfortable than more supple inserts but theyâ€™re much less likely to tear. To me that is a very worthwhile tradeoff. When inserted these buds create a very good seal and they do a fine job of sound isolation.

Like most headphones available today these have a talk feature that allows them to be used with a cell phone for two-way conversation. I admit that I have not tried these for conversation but will try these and come back to update this review when I have done so. I do like the fact that the microphone hangs about 6" from the ear piece which positions it almost perfectly by the mouth.

The most important aspect of any set of earphones or earbuds is the sound profile. For a very inexpensive set of earbuds, these get the sound awfully close to perfect. The highs are right on target and they are clear and crisp without being oversharp. The midrange is solid and full. The bass is strong - very slightly overdriven but not to the point of extreme. I compared these to headphones costing over $100 and these compete very well.

I am very hard-pressed to find much to fault with these earbuds. These fit well and they seem to be well-made, but their strength is their sound quality which is tough to beat in the under-$20 price range. And, if you really want a pair of pink earbuds, these will definitely fill the need. Regardless of the color, these are surprisingly good earbuds, better than most, but definitely one of the best values available.

product_title: Listening Headphones for Kids with Volume-Limiting Technology
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:d6083a9aa816d8784446e9f25594c477]] When I first got these Kidjamz headphones, I thought to myself that I wish I had these when I was a young kid. Loud headphones and stereos are probably why I say huh a lot to this day. The Kidjamz are Meelectronics entry into the kid's headphones market that has several different competing brands. I actually wasn't too familiar with Meelectronics prior to getting this headphones but I will say that they have really focused on making good kid oriented headphones.

Made BPA free, which is a concern these days especially since younger kids tend to put things in their mouths and chew on, is definitely a positive in my opinion. Volume limiting to 85 DB's, which to me as an adult use to listening to headphones over the years cranked to the max, seems a bit low but understandable considering the market it is aiming for. Even at that volume level though, the music is clear and crisp and allows for you as a parent to be able to be heard and protects your child's ears. Ear pads that are made to be hypoallergenic and even when I tried them on are soft and comfortable. One of the most impressive parts of these headphones I noticed that these have some of the most well protected cabling that I have seen in a while. Most adult headphones I have used has a tendency to get it wrong in terms of the headphone plug and cable but these kids phones have better wiring protection than most adult sets I have seen. The cabling is also made to so that they are difficult to tangle. These appear to be made to hold up to the wear and tear of a kid using them.

Although ME is careful not to say indestructible, I decided to put to the test just how durable they are. The head band is definitely flexible and holds up well without breaking and should hold up to most kid's bending and flexing. I will say though that they are some potential areas where they could break especially near the headphone area which is hard plastic and the plastic strap that allows for making bigger or smaller. Not a huge issue as this will be a weakness for most headphones of this type but hopefully that can be something in future iterations that can be addressed.

Customer service was very responsive in reply to my inquiries on the item and shipment. These headphones also come with a year warranty.

Overall, these are good kid's headphones that should hold up to most kids bangs and accidents. These are reasonably priced at 15 bucks. 5 Stars.

product_title: Audio Technica AT-HPH300 | Headphone Hanger (Japan Import)
review_body:
I purchased this headphone hanger for around $29 but I liked the ability of this hanger to adjust to many different thickness of tables and shelves.

It looks pretty nice and it will indeed fit a wide variety of tables or shelves. The hanger portion is nicely padded and doesn't seem like it will do long term damage to headbands on your nice set of headphones. Also, I really like the ability of this hanger to turn the hook inwards as to take up less space and conceal your headphones under the table/shelf. It just allows for a neater and cleaner look.

While it is of reasonable quality, there is more flex in the plastics than I would like. Due to this flaw, the clamp used to secure the hanger to the table/shelf has to squeeze tight causing flex which makes it look like it could break. Despite making contact with the table/shelf, you have to keep tightening it a lot so that it won't slip. Also, the weight of the headphones, in this case the V-Moda M100, causes the hook to slightly droop causing more flex in the plastics. I have been using this hanger for almost a year now with no problems so I am generally satisfied with the purchase.

For what I paid($29) I would have expected sturdier materials which would flex little to none. Although it doesn't cause too much concern it is still a concern and a valid one considering the amount of money someone might choose to hang from this hanger. I don't worry about it breaking with normal use so unless you're hanging something much heavier than the M100, I wouldn't worry about it. For the roughly $20 I see it listed at currently, I think it is a pretty good buy but if the price goes back up, it gets a little harder to recommend.

I will update the review should it not hold up to the test of time.

product_title: Sony MDR-ZX310/WQ ZX Series stereo headphones
review_headline: Not as 'cool' as Beats, but your wallet will thank you
review_body:
I looked long and hard comparing expensive headphones such as Beats and Bose, but decided for a cheaper, but for my purposes, comparable product with these Sony headphones. Both my bank account and I were thrilled with the decision in the end. I've had these headphones for 9 months now and, although I am sure I would have been satisfied with the flashier and "cool" Beats or Bose headphones, I am extremely satisfied with my Sony headphones. My main purpose in seeking out headphones to replace the standard earphones was the noise canceling component with a hint of better sound quality. I am by NO means a sound/music guru that dissects the specifics of headphones; I just want something that looks good, sounds good, and is of good quality. These headphones do just that for me. They are very light weight, the cushions fold in for easier transportation and storage, and the sound quality is FOR MY PURPOSES great! I have no complaints with these headphones and I am very happy that I did not spend the extra $100+ on Beats or Bose headphones.
Others may prefer other headphones on more detailed specs, and that's great. These headphones do the trick for me.

It also allowed for louder audio, which was a huge plus, as the rca seemed artificially limited to a too-low level.

The one issue I've had in many months of use is during power-on and power-off. When turning the TV and system on, I get a loud POP, and when turning off a not-as-loud pfft. This is normal operation, and not harmful in any way. It is, however, a noise that is unnecessary and could be enough to wake up a light sleeper if used in a bedroom.

review_body:
The stereo sounds fine--what you'd expect for the price. I bought this mostly for the Bluetooth support which is a bit wonky if you want to pair it to more than one device. I have it paired to both my phone and my laptop, and there is no easy way to switch from one Bluetooth source to another. For years, manufacturers have had you push "tuner" multiple times to cycle through FM and AM. Why can't Sony let you push Bluetooth to cycle through your Bluetooth sources? This would only be a minor inconvenience if the stereo didn't insist on automatically switching to my laptop source as soon as it is turned on. I'll be listening to a podcast from my phone, turn on my laptop, and suddenly the audio cuts out. Then I have to go through the cumbersome process of getting it paired with my phone again.

Sound is good and it looks great on the shelf. Just think twice before pairing it with more than one Bluetooth device.

product_title: SANUS Simplicity 37" - 80" Full Motion TV Wall Mount
review_headline: Easy Install / Great Product / Costco Sells This Cheaper
review_body:
For the novice this is by far the easiest wall mount to install. They actually provide really good instructions. Go to their website and you can watch a step by step video. It doesn't get any easier than this. The most critical part when installing any wall mount is measuring where the screw holes will go and finding the stud. TV's are heavy and expensive so you don't want to screw this up. Again for the novice use a stud finder ($20 bucks) to make sure you are putting the lag bolt directly into the stud. This will secure the wall mount and support the weight of the TV. The rest is easy. Make sure to use the proper length screw (provided by Sanus in the box) to mount the bracket on the back of the TV.

Sanus really sells a great product. I just bought this (5/20/15) at Costco on sale for $95.00. Check internet pricing before buying.

product_title: URC MRF100B PowerBlaster For Use with MasterControl RF Series Remotes
review_headline: For the sake of anyone looking for repair info. ...
review_body:
For the sake of anyone looking for repair info....
I had one stop working after 2 years. I tried swapping in all the included IR extenders to no avail.
The red LED would blink as though it was receiving from the remote, but it didn't appear to be generating an IR signal.
Finally ordered another remote/PowerBlaster bundle and confirmed it was the old PowerBlaster that was the issue.
Having the new one to use, I tore the old one apart and discovered that the built in IR LEDs were incredibly dim when viewed through a cell phone camera. They appeared to be daisy chained, so a problem with one would prevent them all from working.
No idea why they would be dim rather than just not working, but IR LEDs are cheap so I replaced them all (5mm 940nm) and lo and behold the old PowerBlaster works again.

product_title: JBL Charge Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Just a Button Away From Perfection
review_body:
Taking a look at the JBL charge, the box itself is slick. It comes with these hidden magnets that make the box appear to be seamless. When you open the box up the very first thing you notice is the lid of the box which has instructions on how to connect your devices to the Bluetooth speakers.

Besides the speaker, In the box you get a power charger, that does disconnect the USB cord that is nice, a microfiber cloth, and some warranty information.

Taking a look at the sound quality, the JBL performs admirably. The bass is deep and overall music sounds like it is coming from an actual speaker. But the most impressive thing was how loud the music got without diminishing the sound quality. I like to use Bluetooth speakers at parties and outside events where power is not accessible. So being loud while still preserving that crisp sound is important to me. I would say I have been amply impressed with the sound coming out of the JBL Charge.

Turning to look at the portability of the JBL Charge, I was impressed with the overall Design of the JBL charge but did find some issues with the connectivity. The design of the JBL just makes since, You get this cylindrical design that makes the Charge easy to slip into a backpack or a carâ€™s cup holder.

Another design feature I love, and the reason for the Speakers name, is that the JBL has a 6,000 MAH battery that allows for up to 12 hours of play time and since most people arenâ€™t throwing ragers that last for over 12 hours, you can connect a USB charging cord so that you can charge your phone if youâ€™re out and about.

My only real complaint with the JBL charge is how unintuitive it is to connect and turn off the device. There is just one button on the top that is responsible for turning on the device, connecting the device, and it can be confusing slash mystifying to get the device to try and do either one of those things because you basically just have to get used to how long you have to hold it down.

In conclusion, if you are in the market for a premium quality Bluetooth speaker I can safely recommend JBL Charge. It has some weird connectivity quarks but in the end you get used to them and are just left with an excellent all around Bluetooth speaker with some really nice functionality.u have to hold it down.

product_title: JVC Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black
review_headline: Watch out for that long cord!
review_body:
I love these headphones. They cancel noise well, have good sound quality from what I can tell, and they are decidedly un-flashy looking. I even bought a pair for my father's birthday.

But I'm still shocked at what happened to the cord on these headphones.

I was standing near the door in an L train, and as people were exiting the train, someone brushed up against me while walking by. As they did so, the cord to these headphones came along with them! It so swiftly and easily came simultaneously out of the base of the headphones and my iPhone that I hardly noticed.

I looked around myself, thinking it must have fallen on the floor after being yanked out, but it wasn't anywhere around me. I ended up leaving the train and following the bustling commuters to see if I could spot it hanging from someone's side bag, or if it had finally fallen on the stairs that descended from the platform. It wasn't anywhere to be found.

I found a replacement cord on JVC's site, but it was about $40! Roughly one third of the total price of the headphone package itself. I instead ordered a different replacement cord from Amazon, but the recess where the jack is on these headphones was too tight for the cord. Finally, I purchased the 3-foot cable from Hosa on Amazon (http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000068O37/ ), and it *barely* fits in the jack if you jam it in there.

Before this incident, I had already noticed that the cord on these headphones was a little too long for carrying an iPhone in your back pocket while wearing these headphones. I would try to roll it up a little bit and stuff the cord in my jacket pocket to keep it from catching on things (which it did anyway, a number of times). I had these headphones only a few months before the cord finally met its inevitable demise.

product_title: Eton American Red Cross, Multi-Powered, Smartphone Charger, Weather Alert Radio and Flashlight in One, FR1
review_body:
Eton American Red Cross FR1, Multi-Powered, Weather Alert Radio is another fine product by Eton. It's a great size for emergency bags, backpacks, and the dashboard compartment in a car...or boat (roughly 5 1/4" x 2 1/4"). I was able to receive a bunch of local radio stations without extending the antenna, the weather station was loud and present the second I turned the unit to "on", and the sound wasn't bad given the size of the speaker!
The buttons are easy to figure out and large enough to be seen by most anyone. The flashlight is bright with 3 LEDs, and the unit can be powered by USB or hand crank.
It is a simple radio with alternative power means to get one through a storm or camping or beach trip. Ideally, having a few around makes sense: car or boat, e-bags, garage or barn, kitchen drawer (where the batteries and flashlights are kept), or a hanging in a closet waiting for a disaster.
These make great gifts--especially for those who are the types to always have enough batteries, flashlights, bottles of water, first aid kits, and the like...organized folks. Also, a good idea for college students and those on their own for the first time. I buy them for all the coming-of-agers I know.
