review_headline: One of the best little speakers I've ever tried
review_body:
The problem with reviews these days is that there are so many folks like me getting complimentary review samples of items and then leaving meaningless five star reviews. I DID receive this speaker free of charge for the purpose of reviewing it and I AM giving it five stars but only because this speaker absolutely deserves a high rating. I receive many bluetooth speakers to review so my ears have become pretty darn good at sussing out which speakers are good and which aren't. Now of course speaker sound and music quality is largely a matter of opinion. Some folks like bassier speakers others prefer the midranges, etc. So I am hear to give my opinion and explain what goes into my thinking.

At the time of this writing this speaker is selling for about twenty five dollars. Frankly, I cannot get over the full rich tone that comes out of this thing. I tried classical, rock and a little jazz and this speaker hit it out of the park with every genre. I've tried larger speakers costing more that don't have the sound of this thing. At the time that this company sent me the speaker to review they also sent over the ear bluetooth headphones which are astoundingly good as well.

Don't get me wrong, this little bluetooth wonder is never going to replace your home stereo, but it doesn't want to. It comes with a karabiner so you know it would be happy attached to a backpack or other outdoorsy item. But I am sure it would be content to sit on your shelf waiting for you to send your music its way. I have mine in the kitchen. There is a punchy enough bass (which I love) and the mids and highs are well balance (actually lo mid and high are surprisingly well balanced for a speaker of this size and in this price range. I enjoyed listening to it for quite a while and couldn't find a weakness. There was almost no distortion at full tilt volume. I would go out on a limb and say that it can handle full volume and will only occasionally distort.

Beyond the sound of this thing is also the packaging. It is just really nicely packed in a thick hinged box. If you were purchasing this as a gift I have little doubt that the recipient would be pleased and impressed and think you'd probably spent more than you did.

BOTTOM LINE: I am really impressed by this company. This speaker is an outstanding value. If you are buying it for yourself I think you can't go wrong. review_headline: Energy savings at the flip of a switch, despite too-close outlets.
review_body:
To determine just how badly you need this in your life, try this experiment: Go through your house to find each of the devices that are plugged in but powered off and touch the power bricks which are inevitably on their power cord. Feel hot? That's energy being wasted while the device is not in use. Or put your ear up to the brick. Hear a buzzing or humming sound? That's also energy being wasted and wear being placed on the transformer. Have lots of these? Then you're wasting lots of energy. Solution: Get this Tripp Lite Eco Green Switched surge protector.

I currently have the following items on this switched surge protector:
TV, DVD player, Roku
Cell phone charger
All laptop power cables
Ink jet printer
Computer speakers
Computer headphone amplifier
Fluorescent desk lamp
USPS small package scale
That's a bunch of energy being saved, and a reduction of wear on my laptop power cables which constantly hum when plugged in to the wall.

Yes, the outlets are too close together for multiple "wall wart" transformer brick plugs. So, buy more of these surge protectors. It's a small price to pay to stop wasting non-renewable energy.

product_title: Brightech - BrightPlay Home
review_body:
Coming from an old Belkin Bluetooth Adapter from approximately 2008 I was sceptical as to how different this could be, however they are poles apart. The range on the Brightech is phenomenal - I live in a three storey house and even with all the doors closed and at the highest and furthest point away from the adapter I can still hear the music playing downstairs without any break in signal; and this was on my laptop, always the hardest device to connect if it was more than two feet from the Belkin. The second things about the Brightech is the sound quality - again it is light years better in terms of clarity than the old Belkin. Lastly, and this is the icing on the cake, is that ability to connect two devices at once - what I had always hoped for when having my weekly soundclash with my friend where we play the new music we have discovered and have always desired the ability to intersperse the tunes from each of our devices without having to keep disconnecting.

I know technology moves on and I have not tried any of Belkin's more recent products but if you are using an old one this is definitely worth the upgrade as that is what it is in every sense. The price is very reasonable too. I am in the UK and shipping took no more than five days from the USA.

Got this because my HDTV only has two HDMI ports, and they were both occupied, by our cable DVR and the HD DVD player. Then I got the Amazon Fire Stick and found NO place to plug it in. This HDMI switch solved both that problem, as well as the problem of the Amazon Fire Stick cable not being long enough to reach around behind our television set to the power strip since my power strip is on the opposite side of the TV from the HDMI ports. The switch gave us the extra HDMI port we needed, as well as adding on enough extra cable length that we can now run the cables behind the TV set. And switching back and forth is not a problem, it defaults to the Amazon Fire Stick when I switch over to HDMI1, but the DVD player comes right up when I want to use the connection for DVDs instead. This works exactly as advertised, I'm really pleased with it.

EDIT after having recently switched DVD players: Fiance gave me an LG Blu-Ray player a few weekends back, so I swapped out my Toshiba HD player for the LG Blu-Ray. And suddenly, the auto switching feature to swap between the Amazon Fire Stick and the DVD player is no longer working. So now if I want to swap between sources and go from the Blu-Ray player and the Amazon Fire Stick or vice versa, I have to stick my arm up to my elbow underneath our TV set, find the switchbox, and hit the button that switches between sources. Kind of a pain, but it IS still within fairly easy reach, so not a deal breaker given how few times we usually need to switch between one or the other. Just an unexpected change in performance, given how spot on it worked with the other player, to have it no longer auto switch because I swapped to a different player.

product_title: Sony Speaker Set
review_body:
These are outstanding speakers. I was prepared to spend over $3000 for new speakers. I'm really critical when it comes to sound. I've spent a lot of money over the years on high end equipment but I just purchased a new Sony 4k 65" TV and, even though it was expensive, I really thought I'd spend even more on new speakers.

After looking at and listening to a lot of different speakers I kept coming back to these Sony's. I liked the specs and the reviews were very good, I usually take a lot of reviews with a grain of salt. Even though I couldn't listen to these speakers anywhere locally, I thought, what the heck, I'll start with the fronts and see what they sound like. I said to myself, if they are decent I'll get the bookshelfs for the rears. If I didn't like them I'd send them back and start over.

I ordered 2 but for some reason they were shipped from different locations so the second was delayed by a couple of days due to the holidays. The first one came and I immediately could tell I was going to like what I was hearing. So I ordered the rears. Once again, I loved the sound from the rears. I was so impressed by the fronts and rears that I now ordered the sub woofer. I ended up replacing all my Mirage Speakers with these Sony's. I've never taken Sony seriously when it came to speakers, I always liked their video equipment but sound wasn't something they've been known for until now.

Sony has really stepped up their game with these. They are crisp, well balanced, bring out very fine details in just about everything I've thrown at them. I've been streaming lossless audio using Tidal HiFi audio in both FLAC though my AppleTV, and ALAC through my Sony reciever. I've enjoyed listening to Tidal on my headphones but I'm loving even more hearing it through these speakers.

In general, for the price, style, build quality, and sound you can not go wrong with buying these. If you buy these, make sure you spend time placing them andalso adjusting all your equipment to bring out the most you can. I'm very happy with these speakers. It makes watching my new TV even more enjoyable than I ever expected.

product_title: Zoom H5 Handy Portable Recorder & APH5 Accessories Kit w/ Windscreen, Remote, Power Cable Bundle
review_body:
When I first took the Zoom H5 out of the included hard shell case all I could say is "WOW" this thing feel fantastic in your hand. They gave it a slight curve to improve ergonomics compared to the standard square shape of most recorders.

The build quality is Amazing. This thing feels very solid. It's mostly made of plastic that is covered in a soft touch rubber type coating that is very nice. The microphone capsule is made out of metal as well as the guard bars over the gain adjustment dials.

The Zoom H5 is a recorder that has a very simple design and menu setup that I really like. It's easy to pick up and work with from the start without having to go into the manual to figure out how to do what you want. Zoom really took their time to design the recorder.

I love the manual dials to adjust the gain input. They are a huge improvement over other recorders where you have to click buttons. No only is the adjustment silent without "click" noises you can also adjust the levels much faster and you can visually see what you are currently set at. Along with that you also have separate dials for your different inputs.

Zoom also added a line output to go along with a headphone jack so you can monitor the audio and output it to your camera at the same time. Another great feature is the ability to input a line level in without a separate line signal adjustment.

This is the second recorder to use the new capsule system that allows you to expand the recorder. They have a shotgun mic, extra xlr inputs, and other capsules.

Basically this thing rocks! If you want to see more details with full menu/feature walk through along with audio quality tests/comparison check out my video review / comparisons on YouTube. Just search " Zoom H5 Max Yuryev " and it should come up!

product_title: Bose SoundTrue In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Bose Clear, Quality Sound In Comfortable and Stable In-Ear Headphones
review_body:
These Bose SoundTrue In-ear Headphones for Samsung Galaxy phones have impressed me with their comfort, awesome sound quality, and convenient in-line mic and controls. They are a bit pricy but, IMHO, I think you're getting good value for your dollars. I've not used other similar in-ear headphones in this price range but these compare to some great over ear ones I've had and they are infinitely better than any earbuds I've had.

When I first plugged them into my Galaxy 4, I was immediately impressed by the clarity and depth of sound as I listened to my favorite music. The clip is pretty standard and adjustable and the controls are conveniently located (for righties) on the line to your right ear. They worked well with my volume, track movement, and phone calls. My callers said they heard me well even as I was moving around while talking with them.

The earphones are amazingly comfortable and stayed in without any problems for me. The medium size were on when I unpacked it and they seem to work fine, although there are small and large ones included as well. I admit that I've not used them in noisy places yet so I can't say how they will fare in those situations.

I've only had these about two weeks so I am hopeful that my initial great impression is a lasting one. We'll see how well they stand the test of time, which will be the true statement about their price worthiness.

review_body: So I was at the Consumer electronics show in Vegas last week in the RBH Sound room at the Venetian hotel. They were demonstrating some amazing new tower and stone speakers.  But what really blew me away was the new EP-SB bluetooth headphones.  I already own a pair of the RBH EP2 headphones which are my favorite wired earphones of those I have tried (Sure, Sony, Klipsch, Bose etc.)  I also currently own a pair of Jaybird blue buds x in ear headphone for wireless use.  I considered them pretty good for bluetooth headphones, but when I listened to the RBH EP-SB 's I realized I was hearing something on a completely different level!  Wow!!  I left CES with a pair in my possession.  All I can say is these little bluetooth earbuds are game changers for wireless sound.  They use Comply foam tips like the EP2's, but I think I actually prefer the EP-SB's to my EP2's.  To my ear they seem to have a more balanced  midrange and clearer high frequencies and yet still have really good bass.  Finding them even comparable to the EP2's is pretty amazing given I am comparing a wireless to a wired earbud. If you are in the market for a Bluetooth in ear headphone, they are definitely worth checking out.

product_title: DUNU DN2000 Premium Hybrid 3 way IEMs in-ear earbuds earphones
review_headline: An earphone that delivers so much for its cost!
review_body:
Pros: Mids, lows, soundstage, looks, accessories and overall package
Cons: Piercing highs, overall weight, comfort

Packaging & Accessories: 10/10
Build Quality: 9/10
Design & Look: 9/10
Microphonics (higher ratings means lower cable noise): 9/10
Isolation: 9/10
Comfort: 8/10
Sound Quality: 9.5/10
Value: 10/10
My final Rating: 10/10

Review Date: June 2015
Review Price: Â£250

First of all I would like to thank DUNU for sending me the DN-2000 for review. After having reviewed the DUNU Titan 1 and being mind-blown by the value for money they offered I was very much interested to see how the DN-2000 compared. I saw them being compared tot he likes of the AKG K3003's and I was even more interested to see how they would compare with my personal favourite universal earphones, the Phonak Audeo PFE232.
The DN-2000 can be bought on AmazonUK for Â£250 and on AmazonUSA for $265. Yet again the UK/EU get horrible price conversions - the difference between UK and USA is near Â£100 - which is massively different.
As I live in the UK, these will be reviewed at Â£250.

The specifications of the earphones can be found on DUNU's website.

Packaging & Accessories

The packaging of the Titan 1 was reasonably impressive, especially for its price, but with a higher price tag, DUNU went all-out with the DN-2000. From the outer packaging, DUNU have really spent time on the presentation, where it looks like a very appealing offering to new buyers.
Within the package there's so much that DUNU have included that it's hard to think of things they've actually excluded. This is easily one of the best set of accessories I've ever had in an earphones' package - it sits up there with the old Monster Pro line (MTPG), the Vsonic GR07 MK2 and the PFE 232s.

Within the DN-2000s package there's the following:
Earphones
Over-the-Ear guides
Shirt clip
Aeroplane adapter
1/4" adapter
2x S, M, L canal adjusters
S, M, L dual flange tips
M foam tips
S, M, L harder-silicone tips (grey)
S, M, L softer-silicone tips (white)
S, M, L In-ear stabilisers
Hard metal case
Manuals

Overall the packaging and accessories are sensational - DUNU have really thought about everything here and it's nice to see the attention to detail.
The only thing I felt was missing was a soft carrying pouch, would have really been the icing on the case. Regardless, this is a near flawless inclusion by DUNU and I can't fault them.

Build Quality

The build quality of the earphones is very good - in fact it's almost perfect.
Starting off with the termination, it's terminated by a gold-plated right-angled 3.5mm jack.
Moving up the wire, the cable spits into two, for the left and right channel, where there's a small cable management piece.
The important thing to note here, is that there's no in-line mic, which is a shame and is something I would have liked to see at the given price range.

Speaking of which, the cable is not removable - this is also another feature I would have liked to see at the given price range. Granted a lot of earphones in its price category don't have a removable cable, but it would have still been nice to see. Thinking back though, the Sennheiser IE800 a set of near Â£600 earphones didn't have removable cable - but that's just Sennheiser for you!
Now the thing that slightly concerns me here, is that the strain relief by the housing of the earphones is quite small, and in-turn the earphones are actually quite heavy - this makes the handling of the earphones quite delicate. With heavy usage I wouldn't be surprised of the cable by the earphones to come loose.

Continuing on with the build quality, the earphones have an interesting design, where the in-ear stabilisers, which help with ear-strain, fit. Therefore, there's a small little metal piece that sticks out of the earphones, which is designed to accommodate these silicone stabilisers. Now the design seemed quite clever to me at first, until I removed them (as I like to wear them over-the-ear) and used them without any silicone stabilisers. This caused quite a lot of discomfort, where the metal part was rubbing in the outer-part of my ears.
In a nutshell, the earphones are built with the ear stabilisers in mind, but without them, you're left with an uncomfortable feeling.
I should also mention, that the earphones have a left and right indicator on where the stabilisers sit.

Finally to conclude the build quality section, I would like to mention the pretty cool inclusion of the canal adjusters - these are different sized spacers, where white is 1.2mm, blue is 1.5mm and red is 2mm thick. I find these extremely interesting, as they provide that little extra bit of adjustment needed for different sized canals. DUNU also have shown a frequency graph on the packaging that shows the sound differences the spacers make. I could hear a slight difference myself when testing, however I feel that's more to do with the correct and incorrect size for my ears, rather than these spacers actually changing the sound. Either way, I actually utilised one of the spacers and opted for the 1.2mm white spacer.

Overall, the build quality is near perfect - I feel a removable cable and the inclusion of a in-line mic would have made the perfect score for me.

Design, looks, comfort and isolation
Looks:
The looks of the earphones are absolutely beautiful - they somewhat remind me of the Monster Turbine Pro Gold, but less flashy and more professional looking. The design, especially with the DUNU symbol at the back of the earphones, make these look really nice and just to top it off, I love the finish of the earphones, which is an aluminium look.
The only complaint I can think of is that they cannot be bought in another colour apart from gold, which might not appeal to everyone.

Isolation:
The isolation of the earphones was very good - this mainly came from the earphones having a quite large housing, and therefore passively locking out quite a bit of sound. It therefore punched above its weight in terms of isolation.

Comfort:
As stated in the build quality section, the comfort can be hit and miss and personally, without using the stabilisers I didn't find these comfortable. Ignoring the stabilisers, the earphones are quite heavy and therefore can put a little bit of strain on your ears with longer periods of listening. With that said, they're greatly aided by their design, in that they can be worn over-the-ear and furthermore it's nice to see that DUNU have thought about the weight of the earphones by providing over-the-ear hooks/guides and stabilisers. I therefore can't fault them all that much, just be wary of running with these earphones on.

Sound Quality

The sound quality was something I was greatly looking forward to - after having a great impression with the Titan 1 and reading a little about the DN-2000s prior to receiving them I was excited.
I can now say that they didn't disappoint, in fact they, like the Titan 1's really impressed me for the value for money. However it should be said that the earphones are a little sibilant and also quite sensitive to certain sources - meaning pairing this and/or EQ'ing the earphones' highs is something I would advice for people buying these.
When I compared these to the Titan 1s it could be heard where the 2 BA drivers were working their magic - in the mids and highs. They sounded fantastic and really delivered excellent sound, making the Titan 1s sound very V-shaped, when in reality they're slightly recessed to my ears.
However, I saw these compared to the likes of the AKG K3003s, which are earphones I've only demo'ed for a short period of time and not owned nor reviewed. I therefore can't make a decisive comment on that, however it should be said that I did A/B the K3003 with my PFE232s and I saw how and where the K3003s were that little bit better (in the mids and highs) - with that said the K3003s are over Â£700 in the UK and over $1000 in the US, a mind-blowing price-tag to pay for universal earphones.

Now back to the DN-2000s it was interesting putting it against my Phonak Audeo PFE232s - I could hear the lush mids of the DN-2000s come out, however the highs, soundstage and the lows, notably the sub-bass on the PFE232s were noticeably better (this might not seem a parent in my ratings), however it was hard knocking down the DN-2000s in comparison to other earphones out there.
I shall break down the differences between the PFE232s and the DN-2000s below, in their respective sections.

Lows:
The lows of the DN-2000s can be best described as controlled, and cut-off in the sub-bass region. The mid-bass has just enough slam there for me to enjoy the DN-2000s on bass-heavy tracks, however the sub-bass, despite being there, just didn't extend all that much. I felt that in comparison to my PFE232s that the DN-2000s just had a cut-off, where they wouldn't provide that sub-sonic low-end rumble that all bassheads would crave. It therefore did stick out to me when doing my listening, where I felt the DN-2000s just lacked that little bit of finesse.
Regardless of the PFE232s, the DN-2000s were extremly capable, and when amped with the Digizoid ZO2, they produced excellent low-end tones, which were mainly mid-bass slams, but regardless could be bassy earphones if your heart would like them to be.

Mids/highs:
The mids, ah the mids, the beautiful DN-2000 mids, they were sensational - and easily were on-par if not identical to the mids of the Sennheiser IE800s. They had a great sound and a very lush sounding mid-range, which is excellent for all types of music. I can't really say much apart fro saying at the given price range, you won't find a single better earphones (at least that I've tried or reviewed) that can even come close to the mid-range of the DN-2000s - this is definitely their strongest point.
The highs, despite being impressive, were all too sibilant for my liking. They didn't have the smoothness and control over the other high-end flagships. Unfortunately, the sibilance and its sensitivity really dampened my experience with the DN-2000s - I'm not sure what the reasoning is, but my presumption would be the 2 BA (balanced armature) drivers overcompensating for the single DD (dynamic driver) within the housing.
A bit of EQ here, would and do the DN-2000s wonders, where the highs are slightly toned down. You can also try compesating the sibilance with a resistor adapter, something I used to tone down the Denon AH-C710s back in the day.

Soundstage:
Finally the soundstage - I would have liked to see a little improvements over the Titan 1, unfortunately this wasn't to be heard, the soundstage was relatively similar, where it was very impressive, but just lacked that little extra depth and width found in other earphones, like the PFE232s or Sennheiser IE8s.
Either way the DN-2000s did an amazing job - if they had to impressive here, it would be to have a slightly less congested sound and a little more width/depth to them.

Sound Quality Ratings
Lows: 9/10
Mids: 10/10
Highs: 9.5/10
Soundstage: 9/10

Conclusion & Closing Thoughts

Now there might be some critisms I have of the DN-2000s, but this is me comparing it with the PFE232s MSRP Â£400 and the Sennheiser IE800 MSRP Â£600, where the DN-2000s sit at Â£250, and even less in the US at around Â£170/$270!
It's therefore easy to complain at a higher price-tag, but when I put into perspective and look at what DUNU are offering with their DN-2000s, I can't think of a better earphone that comes close to them at their given price range and/or a higher price tag. What makes it even more appealing is that they're readily available and not discontinued like my PFE232s.
The DN-2000s in a nutshell do so much right and so very little wrong - even the things that are "wrong" can be somewhat forgiven and even tweaked - so if you're thinking of buying a set of earphones under Â£250 or even under Â£400, then the DN-2000 should definitely be on your buy list. In the US, there's no excuse not to buy these beauties, at Â£170 / $270, nothing comes remotely close.

Yet again, DUNU have impressed me and have produced another marvel - I'm really impressed and would definitely recommend these to everyone!

Hope you enjoyed my review!

product_title: Micca MB42 Bookshelf Speakers With 4-Inch Carbon Fiber Woofer and Silk Dome Tweeter
review_body:
This is a great little set of speakers for the price. These sound great, and do a great job of producing sounds across its frequency range. Sure, you can get some better sounding speakers for a little more, but these speakers' compact size were super handy on desk. They looks really nice with and without the covers, and the beautiful wood trim makes the speakers look "classy" :)

Treble:
The tweeter does an amazing job of reproducing the high frequencies, and gets the job done. It never gets "harsh" and sudden, it sounds kind of "warm" and all the high ranges flow very nicely.

Midrange:
Since these don't have dedicated midrange woofers (you're not going to get them at this price point), the midrange is ok. I would like it better if the midranges were a bit forward, but then again, these don't have dedicated midranges. That said, the midrange is quite nice sounding, and flows well.

Bass:
Bass on these speakers is quite good, even though the 4.5 inch woofers are a bit small. They do a good job of accurately producing the bass frequencies. These speakers are rear ported, meaning you should give them some space between a wall and the speakers to get the bass effect. Of course, if you want to get floor shaking bass, you're going to have to get a subwoofer; however, these can shake my desk at moderate volumes. These speakers can get pretty loud, if you have a good amp, so they can be used for parties, if you're amp is nearby.

Overall, these are great speakers at the price point. They look great, and sound great at all ranges. I especially recommend these if you are tight for space, as these will fit your need. I highly recommend these speakers.

So, If you are even hesitant at all about purchasing a pair of these wonderful music makers, don't be! All the 5 star reviews go to show that this is a wonderful product! review_body:
I received these headphones as a Christmas gift from my parents and instantly loved them. I am not an audiophile, but I listen to a lot of Audible books, Beats music, Youtube videos on my iPad and these headphones are amazing. It's a great experience to turn them on and shut the world out. It's my first pair of noise canceling headphones and all I can say is that I love it.

I also like that I can use regular (aaa) batteries to charge the headphones. My father has a previous model which uses a proprietory rechargeable battery and he says it takes a few hours to charge them.
My headphones feel light and comfortable and I can wear them for hours without even being conscious that I am wearing headphones. The microphone is build-in and therefore I can also use the headphones for FaceTime calls - the speaker quality seems to be very good, too.
Finally, I love the colors.

product_title: Grado Prestige Series SR225e Headphones
review_headline: Amazing sound and quality for a more than reasonable price
review_body:
This is my first pair of grado headphones and I could not be more happy. Lets get the good things out of the way first. The sound; it's incredible. As others have mentioned, the mid's and highs are crystal clear. The low's and bass aren't overwhelming, they are tame and accurate. (And this is a good thing). I have never heard such clarity on any other headphone. On top of that, the 225e's are comfortable even after several hours of straight use. Personally, I love the simplistic and classic design of them as well.

My only complaint with the headphones is how little they cancel outside noises. Hopefully, you are using these in a pretty quiet setting, otherwise sounds will definitely bleed in.

Overall these headphones are nothing short of amazing given the price. The minimal noise cancelation is the only thing holding me back from giving it a full five stars. Regardless, I couldn't be happier with my 225e's!

review_headline: free standing low profile versatile floor mount.
review_body:
Since mounting to studs in my wall was not an option I was looking for a floor standing mount that did not need more than 18 inches of clearance from the wall. This mount is the only mount I've been able to find that can fit in a tight spot.

Based on the reviews I was skeptical that it would be able to stay balanced and stand on its own. As it seems the reviews and questions/answers are split between whether or not the stand will stand on its own or requires an extra piece of furniture to be drilled into or slid under.
I can confirm this stand absolutely stands on its own without any need for additional heavy/large furniture. The TV I have up is a 42inch plasma TV that weighs about 92 pounds on its own. Adjusting the foot pads at the bottom of the mount stabilized the stand just fine to stand on its own.
Far additional support you can also use the adjustable pads to make it slightly lean back on the wall behind it if necessary.

The built in cable runs through the legs of the mount are great for hiding cables and keeping everything neat and tidy.

The only flaw I've found was the packaging and assembly. While they give you more pieces than you'll need so you can mount just about any TV mine was missing a few screws/washers and fasteners. It wasn't a problem though as I was able to find them on other pieces/adapters/etc... That I did not need for my TV.
Conclusion - this mount is a sturdy and reliable mount that can absolutely be a free standing mount. It can hold a lot of weight and be balanced to fit your needs. Cable runs keep everything looking neat.

review_headline: SHARKK BBBS are a great speakers and are at a great price.
review_body:
Here is my unboxing video for these speakers: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QpMN3e63wIc

There are times when the small â€œpocketâ€ bluetooth speakers are perfectly sufficient. There are other times when you need something more, something bigger. For those times, Sharkkâ€™s Bluetooth Boombox Buddy System (BBBS) has got you covered. As the name implies the BBBS is not a speaker but a â€œbuddy systemâ€ that includes two speakers that can be paired separately or, for the surround sound experience, together. Here is my review.

Whatâ€™s in the box?

The Sharkk BBBS comes in nice box, forgoing the hyper minimalism of most of todayâ€™s tech. Inside the box, you get two bluetooth speaker that have a surprise heft to them. Their weight was one of the most surprising elements, and was a good indicator of the quality that was to come. On top of that, the speakers come with two usb cables (usb to mini-USB), a dual usb charging plug, and two aux cables. The aux cables allow the speakers to be used with devices that are not bluetooth enabled. There are also two velvet-like bags that the speakers can be carried in, but their weight prevents them from being easily portable. They are portable if you are heading to the lake but not so much if you are running to campus. Of course, that is really not the point of these particular speakers. If you need ultra portability go with the smaller puck style.

Style

The BBBS have an incredibly nice build quality. I have already mentioned the nice weight of the speakers, but they also have a nice styling. Eschewing the the clown color styling of some of the available speakers (Jawbox, anyone?) and instead going with a matte black. The benefit of this coloring choice is that it allows the speakers to disappear into the background of a desk and not interfere visually with the screen. The buttons are in a nice simple layout on the top of each speaker, with the usual suspects of play/pause, ffw, rw, V+, and V-. On top of these, there is a mode button for switching between bluetooth and auxiliary functionality, and a â€œphoneâ€ button that answers the phone or activates Siri or S-Voice.

So How is it?

First, I wanted to get the full experience of the speakers, so I used multiple devices and multiple operating systems. I paired the speakers to a phone (OnePlus One) and tablet (Jide Remix) running Android Lollipop, as well as an iPad and iPhone on iOS 8.3. The only device that I was unable to get to pair was my Nexus Player running Android M, but as this is still in development itâ€™s not a point of critique. All of the other devices connected with no problem whatsoever, and the speakers easily paired with each other. To increase the diversity, I then used multiple apps, both music and video, for each of the devices.

Weâ€™ll begin with the music. For the Android devices I used Phonograph for music stored on the device and both Spotify and Google Music for streaming. On the iOS devices I used iTunes for both music on the devices and for streaming. The results were quite remarkable. The music for all of the devices was clean and crisp. One of the problems that I have found with Bluetooth Speakers is that they have a tendency to be tinny. I assume that this is a by-product of their portability, but, as I have mentioned multiple times, that will not be a problem here. Instead, the music was full and the speakers were even able to handle the bottom, bass line. It is possible that bass heavy music will not suffer a little bit from the size of the speakers, but for everything in my catalog they performed really nicely.

The movies brought more of the same and the speakers were able to mimic the experience of surround sound. Movies played from the devices all sounded great. I stuck with action films and as they tend to offer the greatest swing from quiet to loud. The speakers were great all way across the spectrum. This wasequally true when streaming films Amazon and Hulu. The only problem that I ran into was that sound was slightly out of sync when watching Netflix. My guess is that this is problem with the source and not the speakers. First, I did not have these problems with the other streaming services, and I used Amazon, Hulu and various channels on Kodi. I was only able to replicate the error on Netflix. On top of this, I had the same experience across all of the devices that I tested with it. This delay is rather slight and really unnoticeable with most of todayâ€™s modern films, where dialogue is at a minimum. So it is possible to ignore at least some of the time. Obviously, dialogue heavy films will make this harder to accomplish. You can solve the problem by using the aux cables provided by Sharkk, but this would require the speakers to be close to the source. Outside of this small problem, the speakers performed wonderfully. My favorite experience was the combination of the Sharkk BBBS with my Remix Tablet. Its nearly 12â€ screen combined with the speakers gave a nice approximation of a cinematic experience.

Final Verdict

All I really need to say is that the speakers are great. They were able to handle all of the music and films that I could throw at them, and they always sounded great. Combine the performance with their ease of use and relatively cheap price and the Sharrk Bluetooth Boombox Buddy System are a steal. While some may be more adventurous than I am when it comes to style, the matte black color allowed my to ignore the speakersâ€™ visual impact and focus solely on the quality of sound and the screen.

product_title: Flexion KS-901 Kinetic Series Wireless Bluetooth Headphones Noise Cancelling Headphones with Microphone/Running/Gym/Exercise/Sweat proof for iPhone 6, 6 Plus, 5 5C 5S 4 & Android
review_headline: Change of heart, great customer service from FlexionDirect
review_body: Bought some other brand of Bluetooth earbuds before (BK Connect or something like that) on Amazon for $30 based on reviews, but they sucked so I returned them.  I had a feeling the reviews were faked because they were an almost identical copy of reviews from a more expensive set, but I thought I would take the chance to save a few bucks.  That ended up costing me a few bucks in the end with the return shipping.  Lesson learned.  Next I bought these hoping that if I paid a little more, I would get better quality.  The quality is better than the other brand I tried, but I don't think these are worth the $50.  Music quality is good, but the microphone quality for phone calls leaves something to be desired.  People are always telling me they can't hear me, and if you're around other noises (kids, road noise, store), forget it.  Also, 31 days after delivery the volume button started to rattle as if the plastic piece is loosely floating.  Not a major deal, but just enough to be annoying when you're running to hear this little rattle in the background.  Other than that, they are light, do not fall out of my ears, and provide a very tight seal.  The seal is so tight in fact that they are like earplugs and I must take one out to hear what someone is trying to tell me, so for that I don't recommend for use in the car.  Now I'm past the 30-day Amazon return policy on these, so I have to try to go through Flexion support.  A hassle I was hoping to not have to deal with.  Time will tell how this situation resolves itself.  UPDATE: Bumping my review to 4 stars after I contacted FlexionDirect.  They responded immediately and sent another set of earbuds, no questions asked.  Can't ask for better customer service, I was pleasantly surprised.

product_title: Yamaha RX-V677 7.2-channel Wi-Fi Network AV Receiver with AirPlay
review_body:
When I set out to build my home theater I did quite a bit of shopping around for the receiver. I had almost pulled the trigger on an Onkyo, but I came across the Yamaha RX-V series. They seemed to be pretty good "bang for your buck" receivers, and it just so happened that Amazon was having a sale on the 677. For the feature set that it had, and the price they were selling it for, it was a no brainer. I hit the buy button and never looked back!

I previously had a "1000 watt" RCA Home theater in a box setup that was temporarily powering my new speakers, but it wasn't doing a great job of it. I also couldn't hook all of them up due to it being a 5.1 output but I ran speakers for 7.1. Once I got the Yamaha unit installed I was in for quite the treat. This thing blows my old RCA HTIB receiver out of the water! Outstanding sound, so many features, and it looks fantastic.

Initial setup is a breeze, with an intuitive on-screen menu that makes the process as painless as could be. You'll be up and running in no time flat. If you choose to use it, the YPAO auto setup is pretty neat. I went and tweaked the settings a bit more afterwards to get it to my liking. The auto adjustment is a great feature and is a good way to get your settings in the ballpark for further customization. Just make sure the room is nice and quiet while the YPAO program is running. It doesn't take long.

The companion app on my phone makes using everything on here a breeze. I use the app over my Harmony Ultimate for sheer ease of use and the feature set. I can tune in to internet radio of all sorts, to include scanner feeds (I'm a volunteer Firefighter/EMT so I enjoy listening to the radio traffic of big cities). I've never been big on the multitude of DSP settings, but they're there if you want them. The included remote doesn't seem too bad, but I don't use it. Honestly the app does everything I could possibly need it to, and in a more user friendly way.

Overall, I am impressed and very happy with the performance of this unit. With solid build quality, good looks, and great features, Yamaha has made a happy customer out of me.r />

product_title: Nyrius NSW500 All-in-one HD 1080p Video Selector Switch, 6-input, supports HDMI, VGA, Component, RCA-Composite and S-Video
review_headline: Works great for half of what I need...
review_body: Revised review as of 08.02.15, from 3 stars to 4 stars. ----------  I purchased this item back in May of 2014.  The primary function intended was to use the composite, component and s-video connections for my legacy video game systems.  For that function, the device works well enough.  I have successfully upscaled NES, SNES, GEN, TG16, N64, PS1, PS2, Xbox, and GCN games via Component, S-video and Component when available.  I even managed to upscale Master System 2 games by routing coaxial connections through a VCR and outputting the signal via composite.  The footage, I then use to export to video capture devices such as the Elgato Game Capture HD and the Hauppauge HD PVR.  Note that this will NOT magically make the picture appear in 1080 resolution with crisp lines of detail.  The video quality works about as well as one might expect when upscaling a 240i signal, using 15-30 year-old optical cables.  The Nyrius NSW500 allows for six connections to be plugged in simultaneously:  2 HDMI, 2 VGA and 2 of either component/s-video/composite.  The device has customizable contrast, brightness, saturation, hue and sharpness, as well as volume controls.  Another great, appreciated feature is the ability to manually select the aspect ratio option between 4:3 and 16:9, thus ensuring that you will not receive a distorted (stretched) video from your legacy consoles by default.  Output can also manually be set for 480p, 720p, 1080i or 1080p resolution.  The device seems to be well built and doesn't feel like a flimsy, no-brand knockoff from around the world that will fall apart after a week.  Sadly, while it works great for the intended means I need for these gaming systems, the Nyrius NSW500 is not without it's share of issues.  The video input is sometimes a little darker than otherwise the image would natively appear upon default (in which the controls are set at 50/100), but with a little tinkering, this can be adjusted.  The unit also appears to have a Digital Noise Reduction feature, with three different control settings.  Although, the provided instructions do not specify how to use this feature, and flipping between the three levels appear to emit no difference on my screen.  The included remote control, which requires direct line-of-sight aiming, is extremely tiny and is likely to be misplaced or lost of the user is not careful.  The two most striking issues I have experienced include the 1080i setting.  For whatever reason, both my HDTV (720p/1080i Samsung) and my computer (using both the Elgato Game Capture HD and Hauppauge HD PVR) will not register the 1080i signal for any game system.  The On-Screen Display indicates that the 1080i is being sent, but only a black image appears.  In addition, often an HDMI device I have hooked up to the Nyrius NSW500 will not hold an uninterrupted signal for more than 3 or 4 seconds.  The device keeps trying to refresh the signal constantly. This has happened with my cable connection (I suspected was likely due to nonsensical HDCP censorship), but my original model Xbox 360, my Retron 5, a cheap $20 upscaling DVD Player and my iMac outputting via Thunderbolt-to-HDMI.   This could be from the TV, a capture device, or the device simply does not work as it is intended for.  Unfortunately, I do not currently have anything set to output via VGA, so I am unable to address the status of the quality for these connections at this time.  In the end, I am happy that I have the Nyrius NSW500, but not amazed.  I was able to avoid buying multiple upscalers (separate S-Video+Composite and Component) in a time when this was the only affordable option on the market, I don't need to worry about defaulted 'stretched' images on my old systems, and the ability to adjust video output options directly are nice.  Having everything in one complete unit does not hurt, either.  And, while cable boxes and the PS3 are well known for their issues outputting HDCP crap, I don't hold anything against the Nyrius NSW500 for either of those two.  However, the HDMI signal and 1080i output issues make for an advertised feature I can't even use.   If you're planning to get something for multiple pre-HDMI devices, where you want everything all-in-one and don't mind spending the money, then this may be a decent investment.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling Closed-Back Headphones
review_headline: is very annoying and can make listening to any kind of music ...
review_body:
I had a problem right at the start with the earphones; only the right one worked, the left one dead; nothing I could do had any affect on it. I thought about looking through the reviews of other customers hoping to find someone else who had this same problem and how they fixed it, but there were just too many of them. Instead, I looked through the list of answered questions on the Amazon listing and found one that said make sure you get the cable connector securely into the earphone connector. I checked my connection and it seemed secure, but I pushed harder and it went in farther. I tried it out and the left earphone worked perfectly.

If you are having a problem of some kind that you can't solve, look through the answered questions list. You may find the solution there as I did.

My main problem is noise. I live in a small town that has a railroad track that runs right through the middle of it. The horn noise from trains, when they are approaching an intersection, is very annoying and can make listening to any kind of music or other programs very difficult. A second noise problem I have is that in the summer I always have a floor fan in the room about 15-16 feet from my main computer, so my music has been mainly in cooler weather. I like to listen to music while I'm using the computer, but the noise is such that I usually end up turning the music off. Buying these earphones was an attempt at solving my noise problems.

After I got the earphones working I put them to the test. With the noise cancelling off, the quality of the music was surprisingly good. The fan noise was lessened but still noticeable. After I flipped the noise-cancelling switch, the music quality sounded better, and the sound of the fan was barely audible. Voices on news and other programs were crisp and clear. I was amazed at the performance. I have a pretty good set of speakers on my computer but the earphone's sound quality was far superior.

The earphones have given me what I most wanted: noise suppression and good music quality. Are they worth the price? I think so. I doubt you can find better earphones for this price.

The one complaint I have is that I can't wear them more than thirty minutes or so. They aren't painful, just uncomfortable after a while. I can let my ears rest a few minutes and then go for another stint.

At the time of my purchase, others had given this product four-stars. I agree with that rating.

product_title: Sony SRSX33 Powerful Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Excellent Speaker -- Even better than the SRS-X3
review_body: This is the newer model of the SRS-X3 which I already thought sounded amazing, especially for a speaker in its price range. The differences between this and last years model is that its now 20% smaller. After comparing the two, the size difference makes it much easier to grip in one hand if you're carrying it around. In addition, the speaker now supports higher quality stream, so a big plus for those who wanted better streaming in the previous model.  Other than that, the speaker still sounds pretty similar to its predecessor, but does seem to push out a little bit more highs. Reviews on the SRS-X3 mentioned that the speaker did not charge while it was on due to the charge light turning off--that is incorrect for the X3 and X33. The manual states that the speaker does in fact charge while on, but the charging speed may be decreased (most likely depends on how much power is being drawn for the speaker volume). One final note, the SRS-X33 does not let you control the volume level independently, so you can't have separate volume levels on your streaming device and the speaker (they are synced to one volume control).  Overall, this an excellent bluetooth speaker for those who don't want to break the bank. I think this update puts the speaker on a much closer level to the Bose Soundlink Mini (both in terms of size and sound over the SRS-X3) and blows the UE Boom away if you're looking for a portable speaker that can actually push out impressive lows.

product_title: AmazonBasics Micro Ultra-Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Surprisingly Good Sound In A Lightweight Package
review_body:
I've purchased and enjoyed many AmazonBasic items so when I had a chance to look at this Bluetooth recevier / speaker, I jumped at it. The AmazonBasic brand means simple but also covering the needed features of any product. The Bluetooth Speaker is typical of the AmazonBasic brand which means superb value for money with functionality.

The Speaker is about the width of a hockey puck and maybe 1/3 more height. It's quite light weighting about 4 oz or 110 g. The body material is semi-gloss finished rugged plastic. I say rugged because I dropped it once without any issues afterward. The bottom has a non-slip ring to prevent walking and also to prevent undesirable resonance from the surface the speaker sits on.

Pairing is simple. You hold the on/off button down for 3 seconds until you get the LED flashing and then it'll either synch automatically or you can choose it from your broadcasting device. We tried it here with several iPhones and iPads experiencing no difficulties.

We compared the sound with two other Bluetooth speakers one which was comparibly price and one which sells for almost twice what the AmazonBasic does. The AmazonBasic sounded at least as good as the double priced one and much better than the comparably priced different branded one. Listening to sound sources as varied as opera ripped and transferred to an iPhone as well as several Internet 'casts both voice and music (Baroque and classic rock), we'd put the quality of the sound at the same level as a good quality clock radio. The sound quality did not vary whether the connection was with Bluetooth or 3.5mm phono plugs and cable (not supplied).

We hit two design flaws. First, the speaker will not initially synch when connected to external power. To use external power, first synch, then plug in. The result is a purple LED showing both red (power) and blue (synch). The second flaw is the on/off button which is located on the side making it all too easy to turn the speaker off when moving it. This is a bother.

I'm still going five stars because the sound quality, to me, along with the great price, outweighs this minor design flaws which are trivial annoyances at worst. This one is keeper.the speaker off when moving it. This is a bother.

There is only the one button which does not pause any app you happen to be listening to but seems to only function as an "answer call" button.

product_title: Cen-tech Automatic Battery Float Charger
review_headline: Bought Three And All Work Great
review_body:
I purchased three of these float chargers to maintain the deep-cycle batteries I use on my RV solar system and a spare truck battery, and so far they all work well. You need to make sure you use these on a fully charged (12V minimum) battery or it will not work to maintain the charge and could damage your battery or the charger. Check your battery level with a good, reliable multimeter beforehand and if it's not up to at least 12V then use a normal battery charger to get it to that level before using the float charger. A float charger only maintains your battery's existing full charge.

I read a review here stating this float charger doesn't work properly and won't produce the correct voltage but I have found, at least in my use, that isn't true. I've measured the output on all three units with a quality Fluke multimeter every day for the past two weeks and have seen no drop or fluctuation in the 13.2V output on the three that I have. My batteries have maintained a full charge and have performed as they should. As the included instructions clearly state, this float charger is for LEAD ACID fillable or maintenance-free (non-fillable) batteries only! It should NOT be used on gel lead-acid or AGM (Absorbed Glass Mat) batteries. Also, make sure you do NOT operate anything off the batteries while they are being maintained by the float charger. Even running a radio off the battery can drain it past the 12V minimum that must be maintained for the float charger to properly maintain the battery.

You should also use the charger on a surge protected outlet. Because of my natural paranoia with batteries and fires (I almost burned up in a vehicle fire once!) I have mine plugged into a surge-protected power strip connected to a heavy-duty timer at the outlet. I run it for 8 hours on then 16 hours off. I also made sure I have adequate ventilation (I keep them in the basement during the winter), the charger and batteries are off the floor, and during the first week I checked the batteries and chargers several times throughout the day to make sure everything was OK. Call me paranoid but I'd rather be safe than sorry!atteries and chargers several times throughout the day to make sure everything was OK. Call me paranoid but I'd rather be safe than sorry!

product_title: Grado SR80e Prestige Series Headphones
review_headline: Not perfect, but still the best out there in this price range.
review_body:
This is what music really sounds like. I don't know if the higher end Grado's are any better than the SR80's but I'd find it hard to believe. The SR80's are a significant improvement over the SR60's though...

I've had mine for almost five years now and I use them on an almost daily basis. I can wear them for extended periods with no discomfort (I did bend them outward just a bit because out of the box, they were too tight). I can't stand to go back to my old Sennheiser PX100's because they sound so flat (yes, I realize this isn't exactly a fair comparison). Before purchasing the SR80's I tried the AKG K240's on the advice of the salesman, and they sounded fine in the store, but when I was able to do an A-B comparison, the SR80's just blew the K240's out of the water. The only edge that the 240's had was that they were better at reducing external noise and didn't let so much sound out.

I use the SR80's for everything from talk radio to Beethoven to Joe Satriani to Kenny Burrell to Dream Theater to Lee Morgan to Otis Rush to Big Bill Broonzy to Rush to Mark Knopfler etc... No matter the genre, music just sounds better on the SR80's than any other headphones I've tried. I hate the kind of artificial bass attenuation that so many headphone makers seem to think is necessary. The SR80's are capable of producing clean and deep bass without a hint of boomyness and the mids and highs are clean without being tinny.

The bottom line is if you want a reasonably affordable pair of headphones and care about sound, get these!

The only weakness in the SR80's is that they are VERY open. In fact it seems to me that the sound emitted out the back is actually louder than that which is directed toward your ears! So if privacy or disturbing others around you is a concern, you might want to grab something else, but you'll almost certainly be giving up sound quality unless you spend quite a bit more money.

EDIT Mar 24 2014:

There is one more weakness that is common to Grados. The sheathing from the "Y" to the earpieces gets stiff with time (I had mine for several years before it got bad) and I never really did like the "Y" into both earpieces configuration anyway. After doing some thinking and looking around at parts, I decided to re-engineer the cord. I cut the cord just below the "Y" and installed a male mini stereo jack on the cord. Then I installed a female mini stereo jack the right earpiece, and ran an extension up through the head band into the left earpiece. Now I have a detachable single connector set up which allows me to keep the cord out of my lap while working. The whole process only took me about an hour to accomplish once I'd figured out what I was going to do and assembled the materials. I highly recommend it!

review_body:
Short review... for the price I cannot imagine a better set of bluetooth ear buds, so if you are like me and are not sold on the BT headphones give these a try, they are very impressive.

Long review.... these are great, but there are a couple things that could be better. The included ear bud tips are cheap and don't stay in place very well, I ordered some nicer foam ones and they fit much nicer. You have to make sure you get them sealed properly otherwise the sound quality will diminish, these can not be worn like the normal iPhone ear buds that are designed to have an air gap. Sound quality really exceeds what I expected and I am pretty particular about sound quality. Also like others have noted, the BT range is pretty weak. Anything over 5ft you start to get skips, so as long as you plan on having your phone on your person and not the other side of the room you should be good. The only other thing I would change is just to put a dedicated power switch so you could see at a glance if they are powered on or not, now you have to rely on a little blue LED to determine what state they are in.

All things considered well worth the < $30 price for admission... I have spent over $50 on many other wired ear buds and was not nearly as happy with the sound quality.

product_title: Yamaha NSIC800WH 140-Watts 2-Way RMS Speaker -- White
review_headline: Sounds fantastic.  FYI Speaker cone Diameter is 25% smaller than 8 inches.
review_body:
I purchased these 8" speakers and thought they looked small when I received them so I measured them at 6 inches. I emailed Yamaha and they told me the 8" was the "measurement of the cone is measured by the diameter not from the center out, this measurement also includes the suspension foam that attaches the cone to the basket" (direct quote). I sent them the attached picture and received this response: "Thank you for the replies and the pictures, we did manage to find some clarification on how the 8" cone measurement on this model comes to be...the cone is measured from the complete surface of the cone from the outer edge of the cone suspension, down "the valley" of the cone then back up to the other side outer edge of the cone suspension..." Thus they are taking the measurement from the edge of the blue cone, up to the center, and then back down to get their 8 inches. The actual diameter is only 6 inches. They sound OK when bench tested before installed, but don't have the bass I was expecting from a true 8 inch speaker.

****UPDATE**** System is now installed and finished. 5 pairs and a Yamaha NSIW960 for a center. Dialed in with a Yamaha 105 watt 8 ohm receiver to run the surround sound, tuned with YPAO, and a HTD 1240 amp bridged for 120 watts at 8 ohms to run 3 pairs around the house. All Oxygen free 100% copper wire, 12 AWG from receiver to wall plates and 14 AWG wall to speakers. Sound is stunning at less than 1/4 power. Better bass that the original bench test, and fine for all but the hardest rock without a subwoofer. VERY happy with the outcome and sound after being originally disappointed with the smaller than advertised size. Install was a breeze with the clips (hint: tighten them slightly in the open position to hold them in place before putting them in the ceiling, then loosen slightly and tighten to clamp them to the ceiling). They'll take banana clips but they have spring loaded direct wire connectors which were plenty tight. Magnetic covers have a death grip. I didn't box them. They're designed for use with blown in or rolled insulation and they were covered with each. For the price I can't recommend enough.s which were plenty tight. Magnetic covers have a death grip. I didn't box them. They're designed for use with blown in or rolled insulation and they were covered with each. For the price I can't recommend enough.

review_headline: Perfect for my fellow large-eared flappy friends.....
review_body:
As an avid gym nut I have large ears so it's hard to find earbuds that would stay in place. I have previously purchased and tried many earbuds (Apple's various versions over the years to cheapo earbuds) to no avail.

Fit & Durablity:
To remain intact within my ears only two brands have stood out: MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 & the Bose IE2's. I own both.

The MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 can wrap around the top of your earlobe. The disadvantage is that it's quite cumbersome to get on at times, especially when you are in a rush and have no time to fit it from a mirror. The earbuds hold in place after dropping my ipod or iphone many times. The connection however didn't say the ipod or iphone from being yanked (nor did I expect it to)

The Bose IE2's shines here. Designed to fit within the inner ear, it comes with three sizes to provide variability. The earbuds have stayed in placed no matter how many times the cords were yanked, and has even saved my iphone/ipod from potential drops!

Quality:
Bose IE2 shines. Wires are durable and sturdy, regardless of how many times they have been yanked. Easy to clean wax build up. the earbuds sit just outside the inner ear area.

The sound as expected is outstanding for the price. Sure they are not Shure's or Dennon's but for price and as an audiophile concerned about quality and price, it can't be beat. Plain and simple.

MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6, have decent sound. The earbuds tend to dig into the inner ear area, which can be potentially risky.

If you want to save on cost, get MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6. If you can afford the extra cost, definitely grab the Bose IE2 Audio Earbuds. You won't regret them!

I know what you're going to say; "Fix that with your EQ!" True, you could do that. But for me, with a phone, laptop, dekstop, and 2 work desktops (all of which I consume media through), not all of those support elaborate EQs, and frankly, I'm to lazy to "fix" the issue in my Source if the problem exists in my headphones. product_title: iBasso DX50 HD Studio Mastering Quality Music Player with WOLFSON WM8740 192kHz/24-bit DAC [Full USA One Year Warranty from Authorized iBasso Distributor]
review_headline: Very good FLAC and Hi-Res audio player
review_body:
I recently got some Sennheiser Momentum over ear headphones, which inspired me to upgrade from my iPod 5G and 320 kbps MP3s. After researching all the newer players that do FLAC and hi-res, and with the positive reviews plus the $200 price, the DX50 seemed a good choice. It only has 8 GB on board, so I also ordered a SanDisk Ultra 64GB UHS-I/Class 10 Micro SDXC Memory Card.

I received them both pretty quickly. I got the DX50 charged and running easily w/o the SD card. I checked and the software version was 1.60 which was the latest on the iBasso web site. I was able to load some FLAC rips just using normal drag and drop in Windows 10. It played them no problem and sounded incredible. I then added the SD Card. It's important to note that, in Windows, the DX50 and its SD Card will appear as separate drive letters. I was able to load to and play from the card no problem.

There are physical buttons for on/off/display, volume up/down, and back, forward, and pause. They all were easy to use. Other operations are done via the small touch screen, roughly 2" X 2". The screen responds fine, but some of the display elements can be a bit small, which could be awkward for those with large hands.

The display is pretty basic, don't expect an iOS experience. But that's fine, I wanted a player where the price went towards sonic performance, not necessarily UI. And it's easy enough to figure out and get around in anyway.

Sonically, it's really lovely. I compared it to the iPod 5G using ALAC vs FLAC of the same CD; the bass was tighter, and transients like percussion or pizzicato strings more defined w/ the DX50. I ripped to 44.1/16 FLAC using FairStars, then embedded cover art using MP3Tag. The DX50 had no problems with the files. The sound is smooth and clean, and I found I could comfortably listen at louder levels than before. The volume has 256 levels, which I find handy; I always hate when I can't quite get it where I want.

I downloaded the DX50 Manual PDF from ibasso.com, and it had some handy tips on things like firmware updates, playlists, and even the wallpaper.

I then signed up at HDTracks.com, and bought two albums: Rebecca Pidgeon "The Raven" (1994) at 176/24, and Adrian Boult "The Planets" (1979) at 96/24. They both played w/o a problem, and sounded great. The guitars on The Raven, particularly, were more "real" or "dimensional" and a touch less harsh than my FLAC version, and The Planets had a clarity and depth that reminded me of when I used to record live orchestras.

For $200, this thing is amazing, and a great entry into high end portables.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Home Control for Control of 8 Home Entertainment and Automation Devices
review_headline: Fine remote but lacks Vera support which is one of the most popular Zwave controllers around
review_body:
I own the previous model of this remote (without home control) as well as a fairly elaborate Vera (Mi Casa Verde) Zwave network to control lights, garage doors, and more. As a long time Harmony user, and a big fan of the previous model, I was really excited to unite my Harmony and Vera networks. Unfortunately, I can't because Harmony doesn't support Vera and has opted to go with Smart Things and other less established Z wave and propriety home automation systems (Phillips Hue). I'm hopeful that Harmony re-evaluates this decision, but since they are coming out with their own Zwave hub, I kind of doubt this product will ever get Vera support. So my options are keep these worlds separate or switch my Zwave over to Logitechs soon to be Hub or Smart Things. After spending hours getting my Vera where I want it, I don't look forward to redoing it to gain a couple hard buttons on my remote.

On to the remote itself. I prefer the Harmony remotes without a screen or rechargeable batteries. I own three of the previous models for the bedrooms and family room. The small remotes are easy to use, last over a year on the cheap coin battery and are rugged enough to be handled by toddlers and your kids without cringing. All of the "smarts" live in the Hub which sits hidden away behind the entertainment center. Using the iPad app, it's dead simple to program activities, upgrade the firmware, and more. Gone are the days of pulling out your laptop and plugging in a USB cable to program the remotes. Good riddance.

The layout of this new remote is less desirable to me since I was so used to this old one. The added buttons for home automation (which do me no good for now) have shifted the layout and caused the remote to grow in size. This has screwed up my muscle memory and the remote's larger size is less balanced to me.

Unless you have one of the supported home automation products that you're dying to use from your couch, I would recommend you skip this product and go with the previous generation. If you think you might buy something supported, then maybe it's worth it. However, any home automation kit these days will include a smart phone app, so the only gain here is support from within your activities or on the remote. I would like to be able to dim my lights with my remote, but I'm not willing to swap out my perfectly working Vera setup to get something that Logitech supports.

review_headline: ... work as a high end AV installer and I loved the high fidelity audio we provided for our customers
review_body:
I initially left a middle of the road review due to user error. I thought I couldn't control the EQ settings. It turns out I can, I just didn't know how to get to them in the menu. Using the user manual I figured out how to adjust the bass and treble for each of the modes: Movie or Music. Conclusion: I love the fidelity this bad boy brings.

Also, something to be cognizant of is the audio output from your TV. If you are like me you don't pay the ripoff cable or satellite TV companies. I use a lot of over the air (HD antenna), and then stream video using Roku. I have a Samsung 55\\" TV. Initially I had set the audio out to PCM (stereo), and that made this Soundscape sound indiscriminately loud on the loud parts, and too low on the quiet parts. It was frustrating watching movies.

Adjusting the audio out on the TV can mitigate this. For over the air TV, I can select Dolby Digital audio out (preferred format); however, since my Roku goes straight to my TV via HDMI, and the TV doesn't translate HDMI to Dolby Digital out, I don't have that choice when streaming content. My Samsung has a output format called DTS Neo 2.5, which is ok and I can set this option, but it really is a pain in the butt because I need to manually adjust the audio out thru the TV menu each time I switch sources (the TV can't figure out which audio out setting to choose when I switch from over the air to HDMI, i.e. when I choose Dolby digital out for over the air TV, then switch to Roku, the output resets to PCM, which isn't desirable setting for the Soundscape for movies). I can set the Samsung audio out settings to DTS Neo 2.5, and it would stick for over the air and HDMI, but I found that the lag in audio relative to video is too much and cannot be rectified on OTA TV.

It turns out that I will either need a video streaming device that separates digital video from audio, but I have another option. I have the ability to insert an A/V receiver in my cabinet. This will enable me to route the HDMI sources (DVD, Roku) thru the A/V receiver, then send digital audio out directly to the Soundscape. For over the air TV, I either bypass the receiver altogether (which is fine since the Soundscape is great by itself for audio), but I have aspirations to put rear speakers in my room to augment the audio for OTA. So, the only way to get the OTA audio to the other speakers is by getting an optical splitter and taking the audio out from the TV and splitting the signal: send one to the Soundscape, then send the other to the receiver. I'm not sure how bad the lag will be...this may not be feasible. Maybe the Soul Transform, SMS Active, or Monster Freedom could be an option if you are willing to pay for their celebrity endorsements.

review_body: Purchased these outside of Amazon, but here's my review ... Really good,tight sound and external noise isolation to boot (not perfect, but better than, say,  Bose).  I'm a little bit of a 'light-weight' as far as music is concerned, liking to hear nuance rather than base - so these phones are very good for  'base junkies'.  The sound is a little heavy, where it seems to be felt in the gut as opposed to, say, Bose, which is a little lighter more natural sound (not trying to be a Bose advocate, just a comparison.  On my iPod nano, IMHO, best performance when listening to podcasts are spoken word, but sound could be improved if I could choose spoken word with treble boost or base reduction (or both).  I still like the B&O EarSet 3 (not 3i because the control is too fragile) for sound quality and excellent balance between treble and base (you can actually hear the guitars in the ending of Sia's Breathe Me' - makes all the difference).  However, B&O cables are really flimsey so if durability is needed, they're not for everyone.  Bose is my next choice, but read reviews before considering purchase.  Finally, after using a lot of different earbuds, it seems to me that I eventually adjust to the sound of the one being predominantly used.  So, it seems only important to purchase a good quality set of earbuds and one will adjust to 'like it' in the end (... except for the Monster iSport blue).

product_title: Bluelounge Cablebox BoÃ®te de Rangement IgnifugÃ©
review_headline: Good idea, a bit expensive at $30.
review_body:
I bought it together with Belkin 12-Outlet Home/Office Surge Protector with 8 ft. Cord, Telephone and Coaxial Protection here: http://smile.amazon.com/dp/B000J2EN4S as this was in the Frequently Bought Together section.

The Belkin 12-Outlet Surge Protector barely fits into the box, but is shallow enough to accommodate wrapped up cables. I imagine you would have to buy right angle coaxial adapters to fit coax cable in there, but I'm not sure of the spacing (as I have my box closed at the moment). Phone wires should be fine in that confined space as most phone wires are flat-ish. Other than those two things I was able to fit a USB 2.0 hub as well as my control box for my Cintiq and put this all on a mobile Cintiq desk. Altogether I have my MacBook Pro charger with grounded cable, a desk mounted lamp power cable, USB hub (fairly big), a Cintiq control box that barely fits side to side, 3 brick adapters, and one extension cord that I snake out the side for extra outlets when needed (instead of opening the box to plug extraneous devices in). The only cables that are showing go in several different directions and have one detachment point (where USB, display, and power plug into the same area) so I have one mass of cables tied together with twist ties (included) and one power cable from the surge protector going out to mains power and that's pretty much it. Much cleaner than before and portable as well on the rollable desk. Eventually I plan on upgrading to a much smaller USB 3.0 hub to accommodate my USB 3.0 hard drive which I also have sitting on top of the box (both cables going into the box for a clean look). My only concern is that this is a bit on the expensive side (at most I'd pay $15-20), but I wanted to buy the best (according to Amazon reviews) first before looking at other brands with potentially less quality construction. Would I get one again? I'm glad I have this for my main devices, but I probably would get a smaller version for USB cable corralling. That or get a project box for that.

review_headline: This is a great set for someone new to rechargeable batteries
review_body:
This is a great set for someone new to rechargeable batteries. I long ago swore that I would never own another rechargeable battery! EVER! But I somehow stumbled across Panasonic Eneloops and was swayed by the constant praise and 5 star reviews they received. Let me say up front, these are nothing like the rechargeables of years ago! I am consistently amazed by how long these hold a charge. In my not so scientific findings, these actually have been lasting just as long as name brand non-rechargeable batteries! Whereas my old technology batteries would last maybe 1/3 the time.

The charger is also a great entry level smart charger. So many batteries are cursed to be sold with a terrible charger and thus give sub-par performance. Not this one! It will charge anywhere from 1 to 4 batteries in any configuration. Be it 1 AA and 3 AAA's or 2 AA's and 2 AAA's. You get the picture. It also gives a nice slow charge so the batteries get a deep charge and don't get hot, which shortens their life expectancy.

All in all, I highly recommend this set!

review_headline: Exactly what I was looking for in a projection clock
review_body: This was exactly what I was hoping it would be.  I purchased a LaCross projector alarm clock last year that I should have returned,  What I didn't like about that one, this one is the opposite.  For one thing, the face stays lit up and I can easily see the time on the clock when the room is too light to see the projected time on the wall.  Some complain that the face is too bright. Doesn't bother me at all, but the hint about applying car window tint seemed a good fix for those who are bothered by it. And there is the option of turning off the display, but that would require that the clock be close enough for you to wave your hand over to see the time.  Another complaint is the quality of the radio. This tiny device is way too small to have quality speakers.  If a quality radio is desired, I'd say look elsewhere and pay more.  I didn't want a radio or even an alarm, nor do I care about waving my hand over the clock to snooze, but those are features to check out in other reviews.  I just wanted a good projection clock, and THAT is what I got.  I've had an Emerson projection clock for about 10 years which is not made anymore and still works perfectly.  I wanted a second one for a different room.  That LaCross I mentioned buying a year ago was a joke.  It might as well have been a watch because you can't see the time on the clock unless you push a button which gives you a few seconds to see it.  Being as I keep it 6 feet away from my bed, it's only value was in the projected time. But the projection flipped between temperature and time, giving 6 seconds to temperature and about 2 to time, so we'd have to wait it out to see the time.  AND, a year later, so many of the LED lines have gone out that you can't read the projected numbers anymore.  I don't know yet if the  Magnasonic will last. That will be another review down the road.  But what I love about it is that the projection is big and easy to read and doesn't flip to temperature.  I project the time about 13 feet across the room, and the numbers are about a foot tall at this distance and can be focused perfectly.  Easy to see in the middle of the night through bleary eyes.  It was extremely easy to set up.  The only thing I had to look at the instructions for was to make sure daylight time was toggled on, and to learn which number time zone = Pacific time.  It is zone 6, Mountain time is zone 5, etc.  There was no wait for it to set itself to the correct time, and as I understand it, with daylight time toggled on,  it will automatically reset to standard time when daylight time is over. It has a small foot print and looks nice on my desk. The wires some people have mentioned are easily hidden where I keep it. I felt that $29 was a fair price, about $5 more than the LaCross and about half the cost of the Emerson.cross the room, and the numbers are about a foot tall at this distance and can be focused perfectly.
