product_title: Esky 1080P HD Ready Directional HDTV DTV Amplifier Outdoor Antenna, Built-in Amplifier, UHF/VHF TV
review_headline: Beast of an antenna, pulls and holds stations reliably.
review_body:
I purchased this antenna directly from HISGADGET. It arrived in perfect shape and was easy to assemble. It is light considering its size, which means that the metal is pretty soft. I don't see it making it through a hurricane, but for now, I'm enjoying it. I live over 30 miles from all of my local stations and it works perfectly well with the included amplifier. I'm even pulling in stations that are lower power of which I could not receive with my old TERK outdoor antenna.

This isn't a magical antenna. If you don't receive quality signal, an amplifier isn't going to help. Amplifiers are meant to help with quality signals when splitting and/or long runs. I run a modest 15db preamp running through a 11db/11db secondary splitter amp. One side is going to my HD HomeRun Dual Tuner and the other through a 3 way (-5.7db) splitter to 3 television sets. The preamp helps carry the signal on the initial run with the secondary amp keeping signals from dropping through the splitters I use.

Even though it's a monster compared to my old TERK and just looks pretty serious on the side of the house, I'm not getting pixelation as often as I was with the old antenna. Seems to pull and hold channels pretty reliably.

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_headline: Thousands of happy customers can't be wrong!
review_body:
And, clearly, those happy thousands are not wrong at all!

In this day and age of devices that try to do everything, there is still the need on occasion for dedicated devices that do just one thing and do it well. The SanDisk Sansa Clip is exactly that device!

I wanted an MP3 player that had expandable memory, would remember where I was when last I listened to something, that put out good audio quality and didn't cost a whole lot of money. I didn't need something with navigation, a built in coffee maker or any other range of crazy features, just a solid and dependable MP3 player that I could have in my car, or in the house, or out and about, hiking, camping, wherever.

This little work horse is FANTASTIC. It fills the bill completely for what I needed and has everything I was looking for, and I am absolutely pleased with its performance, especially at such a great price!

With the price of memory cards a lot lower these days, you can put huge memory in this thing, so don't let the 4 gigs throw you off. Just pop in a memory card, after loading up your music on your laptop or computer, and you have mega hours of listening pleasure.

Super easy controls give you access to your music how you want to play it, and the built in equalizer actually works great! Power lasts quite a while, and you can charge it on any USB port, so it charges in the car while you're listening, or charges off of any portable battery, or hooked up to your laptop or wherever you'd charge any other USB powered device.

I'm really glad I picked up this simple little unit! Sometimes simple is the best, and if you're looking for a super portable, highly affordable, dedicated MP3 music player, this, in my opinion, is easily the best on the market today.

I highly recommend!!!

review_headline: Nothing special about the sound quality
review_body: SOUND QUALITY: The main issue is that the sound is just ok.  There is hardly any bass.  It does not have "full bodied" sound like it says in the product description.  I believe this is on par with others I've seen at stores for around the same price, though.   It is loud enough for someone wanting a portable battery powered speaker for some background music or a louder speaker for sports broadcasts, talk radio or speaker phone, but I wouldn't really use it regularly for listening to music.  HARDWARE:  I have a few other Anker products, and the have a pretty good reputation for being quality pieces of hardware, and this speaker is no exception.  It looks and feels very solid.  It has volume controls and a play/pause button.  It has a physical on/off switch, a micro usb port for charging/power, and a 3.5mm jack for connecting non bluetooth devices.  It comes with a 3.5mm male to mail audio cable, and a micro usb cable.  You will need to supply your own usb AC adapter, which everyone should have one that came with their phone or tablet.  USABILITY: It couldn't have been easier to setup.  Just pair like you would any bluetooth device by going to your phone's bluetooth settings.  After that, it connects within seconds of turning the switch on.  BOTTOM LINE: Well built, easy to use, but I think you'll need to spend more for a better sounding speaker.

product_title: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone
review_body: I'm not a audio techie by any means & therefore don't know (or care about) the nuances espoused by audio-phile reviewers. All I wanted was a quality set of "over-the-ear" wireless headphones to use primarily when working out because ear buds do not fit in my ear comfortably or securely. So after a little research, I purchased Beats Studio2 wireless in Titanium. Here's my review on what was important criteria for me: The fit is very comfortable: does not shake loose while exercising but is also not so tight as to cause a headache.  The sound is very good to my UNtrained ear.  Easy to use controls. This "over-the-ear" style, which envelops the ear almost completely (vs "on-the-ear" which merely lays on top of the ear) provides a soothing noise-blocking environment. Yes, sweat does tend to accumulate round the ear during a good workout but, like other reviewers, immediately following my workout, I wipe the ear cups with a non-alcohol wipe & dry them off (when I get in my car) so the set is clean & ready for tomorrow.  My complaints?  I have two. First, these were very expensive -- well over $300. Had I waited a few more days before purchasing, I'd have secure this exact set for almost $100 less than what I paid. That's on me cause I was in too much of a hurry. Lesson learned!  My second complaint is that the case is a pain in the butt. It's very awkward to handle -- it's almost impossible to grip the thing because of the shape & rounded edges. Yes, there is a clip provided to attach to a cloth loop on one side of the case which does provide something to grab on to. All things considered, I'm very satisfied with my purchase.

review_headline: Easy streaming in cars, Poor microphone audio..
review_body: [[VIDEOID:7d03f721805c4e251a322895b65f39dd]] I received this product as a sample to review and here are my thoughts on why I gave it a 4-star score:      5-stars for streaming music from my Windows Nokia Phone via Bluetooth to my car's stereo system.    3 to 4-stars for using this device for phone calls through my car's speakers (Explained below).    First, I would like to mention that this description calls this wireless receiver HK008, but I received one that says HK009.      Connecting to this wireless receiver was really easy. My cell phone picked up the Bluetooth's signal in less than 10 seconds. I tapped the Bluetooth's name \\"HK009\\" on my cell phone and it saved into my phone's setting fast and paired very quickly. The battery's charge lasted much longer than expected for this compact receiver.      To stream music from my phone to my car's stereo, I simply plugged the 3.5mm audio jack of the device into my headphone port on my dashboard. I turned it on by holding the device's button (you will hear some beeps over your speakers to let you know it is powering on or off). Then I switched the stereo to AUX and made sure my phone recognized that the Bluetooth was on and paired to it automatically. I played the music on my phone. That's it!  This Bluetooth is perfect to have if your vehicle is not equipped with Bluetooth.      The overall streaming quality was as good as the quality I had on my phone's playlist. If I was streaming music \\"live\\" from YouTube, the connection was fine with no interruptions unless I had poor phone signal strength.      Now, here is why I knocked off a star for its rating. Using this device to receive or make phone calls, the output from the built-in microphone was not good enough for the other party I was talking to. They said I sounded distant and that they could barely hear me. I think if the receiver had a clip added to this device, I could clip it on something closer to me or my clothing. So, that the microphone could be closer. Hearing the phone calls over my speakers was awesome sounding, but not really good on the other end of the line.

review_body: From the start I must admit I am using the speaker with a wired connection, so I don't have the problems experienced by people using it wirelessly.  When I first hooked it up it sounded kind of thin and lifeless but then I remembered that many speakers benefit by a break-in period.  So I played it for a couple of days with a variety of demanding music. at a fairly loud volume.  That did the trick.  It opened up and sounds very good indeed.  I apply a bit of bass boost with the equalizer on Windows Media Player.  A small speaker such as this also improves with the appropriate placement--fairly close to a wall reinforces the bass and adds some spaciousness; open space thins it out and disperses the sound.  .I should add that I use the speaker with my tablet, on a built-in desk.  After the break-in period, with proper placement it is a fine speaker with spacious, clear, balanced sound.

review_body: Not much to say about wire but I purchased the 12AWG for use on my home theater setup redo. I have not hooked up the speakers but I can definitely say that the wire is of a really good quality and the 12 gauge seems a bit larger. I ran short of this wire during my install and because of the availability of my electrician, I had to run down to a local hardware and pick up 50 ft of additional wire to finish the install. I purchased 12AWG db-link wire which seems alot smaller that this C&E wire. I think this wire is really good and would definitely recommend.    -----------EDIT 25-11-2014-----------    I have hooked up the speakers. During my project I ran short of this wire and had to run down to a hardware to pick up about 50 ft 12 AWG in another wire to complete the project. The other wire is a db Link brand. I have my speakers hooked up and must say that I cannot discern any difference in sound. What is clear though is that the C&E wire is very thick, when compared to the other db Link wire. The insulation is much thicker too. The copper strands of the C&E wire are very solid and rigid, compared to that of the db Link wire which is much softer, finer and pliable.    As I said though, I used 12 AWG wire for my system which I know is way overkill, because based on my speaker distances, I could have gotten away with using 16 AWG. My reason for the 12 AWG was just to reduce impedance and have more conductor to transmit power. I maintain that this C&E wire is very good quality and will still recommend using it.

product_title: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones|Earbuds|Earphones with Microphone
review_headline: Excellent headphones with 1 or 2 minor issues
review_body:
I'm still having trouble understanding how Symphonized isn't going out of business selling headphones this good, for this cheap. By far the best pair of earbuds I've ever owned (out of 17 pairs), period. The sound is crisp, the base is resounding, and the noise canceling is excellent. These headphones have never been uncomfortable or lacking in ergonomic function either. When I run, they can sometimes begin to slip, but I wouldn't say this is a big issue. I've biked and done other activities with these, and they work excellently. If you're looking for headphones to do rigorous, high-impact workouts, these are certainly not the best product on the market. If you're an average Joe with an appreciation for high fidelity music, then look no further.
I originally bought a pair of these headphones, which were promptly stolen, and I absolutely had to have these over any others, so I bought a second pair. My new iPhone headphones sounded like someone putting a pillow over a speaker compared to these.
The only negative comment I can make is about the nylon cabling; since it has weaker insulating properties than other rubber or plastic coatings, some static from clothing or other sources do create slight clicking or activation of electric elements in the headphones, creating small noises. When walking or rubbing clothing slightly against the cord, it's mostly unnoticeable. However, if you're, for example, taking a blanket straight out of the dryer with these headphones in, the noise is pretty violent and you will feel a shock. Occurrences like this are pretty rare though, so I wouldn't say this issue has really depreciated my experience with these headphones.
One possible suggestion though; the ends of the cable that connect with any solid elements tend to fray slightly as time passes, so apply a very light coating of clear rubber cement glue or perhaps a cyanoacrylate-based glue (super glues) to the ends to avoid fraying over time. I did this before really using the headphones extensively on my second pair, and it definitely helped.
All in all, the NRG's are the best purchase I've made on Amazon thus far, and I've already convinced several of my friends to get pairs for themselves, and I would encourage anyone reading this to do the same!

product_title: Sennheiser Digital Wireless Headphones
review_body:
I have a set of two RS 170s, two RS 180s, and one base. I have owned them for two years and I use them every day. Although there are differences between the two models I am well pleased with both headset types; each actually have their own advantages and I use both equally. I will be investing in another base station and RS 180. A second base station can be used to listen to a different sound source, so different members of a household can tune into different sound sources at the same time.

These have been a remarkably good, lasting investment. Pair either with two Sanyo Eneloop AAA rechargeable batteries (eneloop XX 950mAh Typical / 900mAh Minimum, High Capacity, 4 Pack AAA Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries). If you use non-rechargeable batteries take care not to use the charging holster included with the base station. Also take care when taking the earphone pads on and off the headset to access the battery; the connector tabs won't survive carelessness.

Similarities between both models:
- Sound Quality: For most people both models will provide supremely good to near flawless sound quality. To experience better sound quality you would have to 1.) be an audiophile with perfect hearing and 2.) have a wired, studio headset. Range: Both headset models run concurrently off of the same base station. I have found in practice both have a range of ~50ft / 16m line of sight, and approximately 25'/8m through walls.
- Sound Source: Anything that can connect to RCA stereo jacks or a stereo headphone jack. This includes nearly all video gaming platforms, mobile phones, tablets, AV receivers, etc.
- Sound Level: Both headset types have volume controls on the headset; (both also have an on/off power button)
- Comfort and Fit: Both headphone models share the same headset frames, differing only in of the fabric covering the over-ear padding and two comfort pads where the arch of the headset frame contacts the crown of the head. The RS 180 has a faux-leather type covering helping to seal out ambient noise. The RS 170 has a high-quality, breathable fabric covering. I find both headsets equally comfortable, and I can either nearly all day long with little to no breaks. They are as comfortable as you could expect a headphone to be.
- Privacy: The RS 180 has the edge, but when used judiciously both headsets can be used without interrupting someone sleeping two to three feet from you

Differences
- The RS 170 has left / right balance controls, which may be useful to those with hearing impairments affecting hearing one ear more than the other
- The RS 170 allows more ambient noise. This is not always a bad thing; it is actually useful for someone trying to hear a phone or doorbell ringing in the background.
- The RS 180 allows less ambient noise, and in place of left/right balance controls, it has separate buttons on the headset for 1.) surround-sound boost and 2.) bass boost.

Speaking for myself, I'm blessed with extremely good hearing and have been labeled an audiophile by others. I use both headset types equally; when I can afford to be immersed in sound I use the RS 180, and when I need to hear more of what's going on around me, I use the RS 170.

Speaking for my boys, who love video gaming, they use the RS 180 when they're not collaborating, and the RS 170 when they need to collaborate. review_body:
I feel compelled to review these speakers. After reading through literally every review on this website: http://noaudiophile.com/Micca_MB42x_Bookshelf_Speakers/

I decided for the money that these were the best budget speakers you can currently purchase. These have far surpassed even those high expectations I had. Loud, clear, room filling sound from such a compact and affordable speaker. I'm using these with an iMac, coming from Logitech Z-2300, which over time I found increasingly lacking in the mid-range. No, these do not have that earth rattling bass like the 2300's. If you are looking for that punchy deep sound characteristic of subwoofers and larger diameter speakers, then you might be better off purchasing something a little larger, or getting a subwoofer in addition to these. But I really feel that is not needed unless you plan on throwing a party outside. Holy crap was I blown away by the loudness and quality these put out. They make the 2300's sound incredibly bass heavy and distorted, and I had no idea all the notes I was missing from my music after listening to the MB42X's. They have truly beautiful and balanced sound, I cannot give higher praise to these speakers.

The headphones are reasonably comfortable but start to feel a little uncomfortable after an hour or so - I wouldn't want to be wearing these all day but they're great for commute or taking a walk.

The biggest benefit for me is not having a cord while still having good sound quality - it's one of those things that you don't think about until it's gone, and I never ever want to go back to having a wire between my phone and my headphones again. product_title: Nyne Aqua twister
review_headline: The Leader Among Waterproof Speakers under 200$
review_body:
Excellent music playing device for the aquatic environment. Ive found it suitable to be used in the shower and not just out at play at places like the beach or pool. It sounds great and can be heard above the sprinkling water at not even full volume. The sound is crisp and clear. Great for a little jam in the shower you know.

It is also able to withstand drops. Ive dropped it thus far three times from a height of five feet and nothing appeared to be tossed out of place. It doesnt even appear chipped which is great. There is no rattling of parts either. The straps are easy to take off and on and are strong enough to support the speaker. I ended up having them around an over the shower head caddy which helps to keep it suspended in the shower and safe from falling over.

It says it cant be submersed more than a meter and some change though I cant imagine a situation where that seems possible. Even just lightly spraying it with water doesnt alter its performance, so I find it much better than other waterproof speakers Ive had. Many of them promised to be safe to water but none with the promise of being able to be submersed or even able to float.

Overall the NYNE speaker is a great bluetooth waterproof device. The picture may make it seem large but it isnt and is in my opinion portable. Definitely look into this device if you need a low cost speaker for the aquatic environment.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 25 Headphones (wired, 3.5mm)
review_headline: Excellent Noise Canceling Headset with Samsung Galaxy In-line Cable
review_body:
We have several Bose Systems/Devices (i.e. Wave SoundTouch Music System with multi-CD changer, SoundLink Mini Bluetooth speaker, and SoundLink around-ear Bluetooth headphones et al). In addition, several Apple/ Samsung devices (i.e. iPad, iPhone, Galaxy S6 Edge, iPod Touch et at). Having just replaced a land-line phone with a Samsung S6 Edge smartphone, I jumped at the opportunity to order the Bose QuietComfort 25 headphones with inline mic/remote for Samsung Galaxy. Currently using a Bose around the ear Wireless Headphones for audible books, taking iPhone calls, especially while watching professional sports (i. e. NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, Golf an IndyCar races). After setting up the QC 25 headset, following the pictorial manual, we tried using the inline mic and remote cable to take Galaxy S6 Edge calls while listening to the audible book "Exile" - worked as advertised. And, in fact just ordered the inline mic/remote cable to use with our Apple devices so we can control the volume, tracks, and voice stuff, plus switch between calls on our iPhone and iPad for $25.82 with free shipping from Amazon. Note - The Samsung Galaxy cable will work with any device for listening to audible books/music, its just the microphone and controls that are Samsung Galaxy specific. The Apple cable, I'm told will work with Samsung Galaxy devices for audible books/music, but the microphone and controls will only work with Apple devices. In addition, we plugged the cable into our Bose Wave System and Samsung HDTV with excellent results.
The noise canceling feature is outstanding, the headband fabric is far better than the Bose Wireless Headset stuff, plus the ear pieces seem to fit closer to my head, with R and L sides clearly indicated on the inside of the cups. Unlike the Bose Wireless Headset soft bag this case is small (see attached photo) and easily fits the folded headset, extra battery, inline cable and dual jack adapter. Bose indicates the triple AAA alkaline battery should last 35 hours and the indicator light will start flashing when 7 hours remain - nice feature. Overall, the QC 25 Noise Canceling headset is a quality product, a bit pricey, however, well worth the cost, especially if you fly/travel or are outside the 30 foot wireless range.. Excellent Customer Service at 800-367-4008. Highly recommended.

I'm currently running a Denon DL 304 moving coil cartridge on it and the sound is totally amazing. product_title: Sound Bar Red
review_body:
The TaoTronics Model TT-SK02 is a nice looking portable Bluetooth speaker. It comes in an attractive, easy to open box, includes a manual in several languages, a USB charger cable, an audio cable, but no charger. You have to use the USB charger included with your phone, tablet or use the on your computer. The replaceable battery is a good thing to have. There is no indicator on the speaker of how much battery life is left. But an interesting feature is that next to the bluetooth icon on my iPhone/iPad there is a battery charge level indicator for the speaker.

The housing is of a matt rubberized finish, which looks elegant. The status LED and all connectors are on the back and therefore not distracting. The speaker has an on/off switch but the manual is unclear on how fast the battery will drain if the speaker is left on in paired standby mode.

The front and top of the speaker look very clean and minimalistic. There are only three buttons on the top that have multiple functions. For instance the volume buttons also act as skip forward/backward buttons and the round multifunction button controls Bluetooth pairing, play/pause, audio source selection and phone answering. There is a loud double beep when the speaker top volume is reached. The speaker uses the older Bluetooth 3 technology. Volume changes on device and speaker are independent, which is not as convenient.

You can pair more than one Bluetooth device with the speakers. However, the manual does not list how many devices can be paired with speaker. Pairing is easy and fast.

To switch between the devices, press and hold the MFB until you hear a double tone. This disconnects all devices within range and then you can open the BT settings on your device and connect to the previously paired speaker or pair a new speaker

No NFC pairing with iPhone 6 is possible since the iPhone does not (yet) support this feature.

The sound quality for such a small speaker is quite good and a lot better than the built in speakers on my phone or iPad. The speakers are advertised as 2x3W, which is not the highest you can find on the market for this size speakers but the sound quality is amazingly good and loud enough to fill a room. This allows you to listen to music, watch videos or TV on your tablet and have great sound. In my experience the sound breaks up by exceeding 20 ft distance between the paired device and the speaker, which is less than the advertised 33ft.

The speaker has a microphone and can therefore be used, at least in theory, as a speaker phone. However, while the other party can be heard loud and clear through the speakers, the microphone did disappoint. The sound it picked up is very garbled and basically makes it useless for a conversation. I am not sure this is an issue with my particular unit but a few other reviewers reported the same problem.

In summary this is a very good sounding, portable speaker, the built quality looks great and if the microphone would work better and the Bluetooth would be upgraded to version 4.0 I would give it 5-stars.

review_headline: Impressive looking and even better sounding!!!
review_body:
The attractive real wood design of the Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones with Mic caught my eye right away. From the gorgeous wood earpieces to the brightly colored woven cord covered wires, these look very stylish. However, any audiophile knows when it comes to sound, stylish looks don't mean anything - the sound is what matters. With these lovely headphones - sound is not sacrificed for beauty in any way!

Much thought appears to have been given when these headphones were designed. The wood give a full rich sound and when it comes to deep base, I swear I can feel these move just a bit when those tones are hit. The cording gives extra protection and strength to the wires. Where the wires attach to the plugs, merge into one wire (or split into two) as well as at the jack, there is a rubber reinforcement at these stress points. The jack comes out of your device at a 45 degree angle which is different than any other set of phones that I have. They also come with extra pairs of silicone ear bud covers so that you can find the ones that fit your ears well. These make the headphones extremely comfortable as well as cancels out the noise for a peaceful listening experience. One thing I'll note though, it appears these are not soundless to others around you. According to family, they can hear a little bleed-through when I'm listening to them. Also included is a nice pull-string linen bag to store everything in.

I am very impressed with the Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones with Mic in all aspects, but the of course, the best part is that they sound great!

review_headline: Well Constructed and Solid Headphones, Might be a Little Pricey
review_body:
Considering that I bought these headphones 2 years ago, I think the Outdoor Tech OT1002 has held up pretty well. At the time I was looking for a decent, competitively priced, wireless in-ear headphones. All the big brands like Jabra seemed to be out of my price range, so I settled for the OT's.

I thought the audio quality was average. It's not the best and certainly not the worst. Effective range (paired with my smartphone) seemed to be about 4-5 feet before music broke up and got choppy; you need to keep your headphones and paired device close together.

As I originally bought these headphones to run with, I've been doing so maybe about 2-3x a week for about an 45minutes at a time; I have to charge about 1-2x every 2 weeks. Recharge times are relatively quick taking about 1-2 hours.

Outdoor Tech states that the headphones lasted about 5-6 hours, actual usage I got was about 3:30-4 hours of continuous usage (I got to test out that claim running several marathons. I'm a very slow runner.....)

Protip: Don't buy the white ones. After 2 years, these white headphones have turned yellowish from sweat and dead skin....

Revisiting this item, I see that the prices haven't really changed: I think it's still a bit pricey. You could probably find cheaper wireless headphones that are as good as the OT1002 Tags, if you do your research. Otherwise I think these headphones are constructed solidly and have lasted well over the past 2 years.

It's not a bad buy for a person who wants to use this while exercising without worrying up wires.

For the price, it's really tough to beat. It's more powerful than the Asgard 2, also from Schiit, which I don't understand because the Asgard is double the price. I would also hesitate to say the Asgard 2 sounds noticeably better, especially if you're listening to mp3's. The Asgard 2 does get slightly thinner in the mid highs to highs from about 700z for slightly better clarity, but the Magni's overall sound signature is more consistent and warm.

This thing is extremely powerful and seems to be able to drive any headphones on the planet, I've done Fostex TH600's, HiFi Man HE500's, and Mr. Speakers Alpha Dogs without a problem. Low impedance and IEM's are no problem because you can just switch it to the "low" setting.

Great sound, great power, well built.
Best value headphone amp I've seen so far.

The discs are somewhat of a hassle to deal with at first, and tend to pop off if you don't have them set correctly. I finally just went and bought some floor protectors that move easily on hard-surfaced floors so I could move the cabinet back and forth without a problem. product_title: 1byone 45~60 Miles Amplified Indoor HDTV Antenna for UHF/VHF/FM, Included Power Supply, 10 Feet High Performance Cable, Handsome Thin Flat Panel Design, Black Color Fits Your Home Decor
review_body:
I got this antenna to hook up to the spare TV in my master bedroom which is located on the 2nd floor of my townhome. It is supposed to allow me get rid of the secondary cable box I'm paying monthly rental fees for without using it much in the upstairs. All I mainly needed was local channels for the morning news, esp. since I have a PC for streaming hooked up.

Installed the antenna yesterday and it seems to be working pretty well.

I get all the local channels and a crystal clear picture. Did check the towers for distance and they are in a 35 mile range. There is a slight interference when I walk by, which I can probably rectify with repositioning. It found the channels and I really haven't played much with it after that.

It's surprisingly small and light-weight. My only complaint is that it has no power indicator, so if you had to trouble shoot it you wouldn't know if it had a power issue.

Otherwise, I would recommend this if you have towers within the range this antenna can pick up. You can google this info.

review_headline: but with a device like this it doesn't matter
review_body:
exactly what i needed. this device takes an analogue audio signal and transmits it over bluetooth. this means that you can send any kind of audio signal from any device that has a 3.5mm output or "headphone" jack. people may wish to purchase this device instead of a usb bluetooth adapter or anything with a digital interface because i game on my computer and some games do not send audio over the bluetooth connection, i can only get sound from my speakers. im not sure what causes this, but with a device like this it doesn't matter. if sound goes through your out jack, it WILL go through this. btw i use a Kinivo BTH220 headset with this no problem.

I would recommend this device over a usb bluetooth dongle any day because you won't run into any compatibility issues like i did with a usb adapter. the only reason the usb is more useful is because some bluetooth devices, such as my headset, have buttons on them that can interface with your source. for instance i can play/pause and skip songs in my media player just by pressing buttons on my headset. you cannot do this with this device because this, unlike a usb or built-in bluetooth adapter, does not send anything back to your source.

if you do not need any kind of device feedback to your source then this is the device for you.

review_body:
Love it! Great for several applications, computer speaker, bedroom alarm clock, FM radio and music player for shop or any room. In my den it's connected to the computer to be it's speaker for Pandora, YouTube, etc. Or unplug 3.5mm audio plug to switch to FM radio, plus huge blue digits show time, or radio station. Very easy to program and scroll through FM stations.

Noteworthy observations:

It's pretty big compared to standard bedroom alarm clock, more like size of loaf of bread, should you have very little space. The jumbo 1.75" tall yet mellow blue digits are great though, so pleasing compared to typical red.

You have to physically pull out the 3.5mm external input plug to switch from external/computer/device/etc input to listen to FM radio or MP3, which it automatically does when plug is removed. Why don't the FM radio and MP3 buttons simply override the external 3.5mm input? That would be better.

Audio is great for talk and classical music, but as a reggae fan the bass level won't nearly cut it. NO audio/headphone output, ONLY input.

Uses of the USB port beyond flash drives are unknown to me. It includes a USB to micro USB cable, not sure if it's to play music from a phone, charge it, both, or what? Haven't connected to phone or used any MP3 devices so far, I'll update if I ever do.

So as computer speaker, FM radio, and clock I love it! MP3's and smartphone connection aren't what I bought it for thus I can't say. Cheers!

- Default volume when turning it on is a bit loud, but tolerable.

product_title: Logitech Squeezebox Radio
review_headline: Wonderful alarm clock- shame is it no longer made!
review_body:
I bought this as I needed something that would play Pandora and also had many options for alarms. I have now been using a used Squeezebox I bought here (They are no longer made) and have loved it.

Pros-
- Programmable dimmable screen. Since I use this primarily as an alarm clock and I cannot sleep with any light, this is a HUGE must. One I did not even know I needed. Before I was always throwing something over the alarm clock to block that light. This product allows me to set it so that the screen turns off *completely* and when I do hit a button, it is automatically dimmed depending on light in the room. This means during the day it is bright enough to read and at night is is very dim, but still readable. No sudden shielding of eyes as you are blinded in the middle of the night just because you wanted to skip a song.
- Menu is programmable. Able to order the apps I use the most in order. This is nice in the middle of the night as I can reach over and know where the selection I want will be.
- Alarms are programmable by sound (you can select it to play Pandora, nature sounds, noises, ect), sound volume, time and day. You can set which days you want each one to sound, which is very handy- and each alarm can have a different sound.
- Unlimited amount of alarms! You can just keep adding more! (I have not tested this beyond 10 or so)
-Sound is good, even for my husband who is much more in tune with sound quality than I am.

Cons-
- No 'normal' alarm sounds. It is a small petty thing, but it bugs me. Plenty of options which are annoying enough to wake me up, but not the normal alarm sound.
- No snooze button. You have to turn the dial to select that once it pops up. Not a huge deal and understandable since it is not primarily an alarm clock.
- No longer made. This is a real shame since this product is wonderful.

This is possibly the best thing I've bought from Amazon, or anywhere else online, ever.

I haven't had any wear to the buttons, but I don't use some of them. I wipe it down whenever I clean the bathroom, and it still looks good.
This radio has been very useful during the ice storms and hurricanes we sometimes have here in NC, when the power is out.

This is like the tank of shower radios. I have been honestly amazed at the durability of this thing. I'm considering buying another, just in case mine does eventually wear out.

I recommend this radio strongly. It has been a workhorse in my daily life.

product_title: NAXA Electronics MP3/CD Bass Reflex Boombox and PA System with Bluetooth
review_headline: Kids love it, but a few issues
review_body:
This boombox was a hit with my son. He loves it, but there are a few small issues with it that you should be aware of.

First the pros - This stereo has good sound. The lights are a great feature, and my autistic son loves anything with lights and this was a great feature. The digital tuner is nice, and holds a signal. Reception on the radio is very good in fm mode. The cd player works well. The bluetooth works very well.

The cons - The stereo is VERY large. It has a carry strap, bit it is not really very portable. It is best suited to sit on a shelf or table. The volume always starts out at level 10, so you have to be ready to turn it down immediately when you turn it on. Seems like they could make it come on at the last volume level it was used at, but I guess not. Even the lowest volume level on this stereo is still pretty loud. You would not want this in your office because some office settings even level one volume would be too loud. Am reception is not so great, but the kids never use that band, so I am not counting it against it.

product_title: Portable Waterproof Bluetooth Speakers w/ FM Radio & LCD Display, IPX7 Water Resistant & Shockproof - Ultimate Wireless Handfree Rechargeable Shower Speakerphone
review_headline: Nice Sound From A Durable Speaker
review_body:
There was a time just a few years ago when I did not believe a speaker this small could deliver the sound quality and volume that this one can. Technology has come a long way. The fact that this speaker is waterproof will make it the must-have device when I visit my parents' house for a dip in the pool this summer.

The device is small and compact and to give you an idea of the size it is about the same girth as a soda can and about the height of a can and a half. The exterior is rugged and covered in a hard rubber substance everywhere but the speaker grille. The device is rated IPX7 which means it is pretty much completely water and dust proof. You can find out more by Googling "IP Code" and reading more about the rating system if you are curious.

The device floats, which is nice since it is a great speaker to have by the pool. While it may float with the speaker facing up, which is a genius move, the bass reflex port gets covered up so you'll lose a bit of bass if the speaker is actually floating in the pool.

The sound quality of this device is excellent. For a portable speaker the sound is some of the best that I've heard. It also gets quite loud. I happen to have a decibel meter so I turned the speaker up full blast and started the latest Kid Rock album on it and tested the sound force about a foot from the device and got a reading of 99.6db. To show how loud that really is the level at which sustained exposure may result in hearing loss is 90db to 95db so there is plenty of non-distorted volume here.

The Bluetooth connectivity works well and my phone has no problem connecting immediately to it every time the speaker is powered on. You can keep your iPhone safely out of harms way and still control the volume, skip tracks and even answer a phone call using the built in microphone.

The device charges via USB and there is a port on the back of the speaker that is covered by a rubber protector. There is also a headphone sized jack with the USB port if you want to plug a device directly into this speaker.

I tested this unit out with some Netflix videos on my old Macbook Pro laptop and was delighted to see there was no audio lag with this speaker. You can watch your content without the annoyance of the lip movements not matching the audio.

The unit has a built-in FM radio which is a nice little perk. I live far enough outside of Chicago that I can't really get much on the radio side when inside the house but outside the reception is quite a bit better.

There are two square plastic handles on each side which are a great addition as you can either attach the included lanyard to one to hang it or you can use just about anything that you can string through the holes to hang the speaker where you want it.

The included battery is rated at 2500mAh which is enough for 9 hours of playtime at the loudest volume level. While I did not test that specifically, I know I got over 12 hours listening to it at a lower volume level so it is very likely that number is correct.

Overall this is a speaker that is hard to beat for using outside and / or near water. It would make a great speaker for poolside or for hanging in the shower. The sound quality and volume are excellent as is the durability of the speaker itself no matter where you use it. Highly recommended.

nice cheap cable that does what it should, to an extent. the mic is mono, the headset is stereo. I use this to plug into my ps4, and I run a pair of open headphones that I am really liking, and I have a condenser mic and a mixer to plug into the mic port via an adapter. No I do have a weird issue with it. If I already have the microphone plugged into the mic port on the adapter, and then plug it into the ps4, then it will not read that there is a mic input. However, if I plug in the adapter first into the ps4 controller, without the microphone plugged in, then the ps4 will read that there is a headset, and then I plug the microphone in and then it works. So it works but only if you follow these steps:

1) plug adapter into the ps4 controller
2) plug in your headphones
3) plug in your microphone.

Really odd that I had to do that, but it works.

product_title: Sony NWZ-A15 Walkman Video MP3 Player (16GB) - Silver
review_headline: A device for the serious audiophile
review_body: Unlike others, I'm not going to compare this device sonically to any other because unless you've heard them, it's pointless. And as I've been in the audio industry, I'm not into gimmicks and pretties, I just want good sound.  So, to the device. As an MP3 player - clean, fully-expressed sound with lots of audio-altering processes which may or may not benefit your enjoyment of the music. The choice of setting comes down to the quality of your MP3 recording, the type of music you play and how you like to listen to it - no matter, there's a setting for you. But this device is, above all, a loss-less audio player so as an audiophile you shouldn't be listening with any modifications to the original sound, and as such, it's superb. Either way, you won't be disappointed.  Navigation is easy, except for the Shuffle/Repeat menu, which is not particularly clear. The online Help is annoyingly poor and could offer clearer explanations, better navigation and better English. One huge negative is the lack of a DELETE function for music. Why this is missing is beyond me. To delete a track/album you have to connect to your laptop/PC. Oddly, you can delete video and picture files directly from the device. Crazy! Whoever at Sony decided on that has never used a music player. If you're on the train and decide you don't want to hear this or that track any more, you should be able delete to it, there and then. Done.  The MicroSD card interacts seamlessly with the system storage (unlike other players I know) which adds a huge amount of file space. The Media Go software is like Marmite - you'll either like it or hate it. It's a good example of developers assuming they know what the user wants. I'd built a flat file playlist containing a large number of diverse songs. Medio Go fragmented all the tracks into individual folders based on Artist and Album and scattered them everywhere. Noooooo! Very clever if you've never compiled your own random artist playlist or you want your songs to be sorted and correctly designated. I assume a lot of people will love it for that and find it very useful - but it's not for me. If you know how to create playlists, you won't need it. If you just want to add an album, simply drag and drop from Windows Explorer. Easy.  Build quality is excellent but you'll need a protective cover to keep the face scratch-free. It connects to your PC through a special Sony player/USB lead, which is never a good thing, but that's a personal niggle (consider the pain when you lose it - you can't charge, delete, add...). At least the lead is a good length. The battery lasts more than long enough between charges (via the special lead). The FM radio was simple to set up and the stations were clean and sharp to listen to.  Videos play well, the images being sharp and clean, though don't expect a full range of controls. Photos are equally sharp with a minor yellow shift and slightly enhanced colour saturation. Picky picky, but nothing intolerable. At the end of the day, this is an audio player.  As for the styling, that's up to you. I'd have preferred it shorter and bulkier - but it is what it is.  Yes, the price is high, but then so is the quality of the product. Biggest tip? This is an audiophile product for audiophiles, so ensure you have an excellent set of cans/buds or you may be wasting your hard-earned cash.  10/10. Easily the most joyous device I've bought in a long time.  For more info, here's an online guide (how to use/technical) - http://helpguide.sony.net/dmp/nwza10/v1/h_ww/index.html

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_body:
Like several others, I've come to the 650 after needing to replace a Harmony 550. As with any product like this, you're bound to run into problems and they're certainly frustrating when you run into them, hence the one star reviews. I, fortunately, have not run into any issues. The new GUI for programming the remote the pretty nice, and superior to the old Harmony Remote software. As a bonus, you're able to import your settings from the older Harmony Remote software account which worked flawlessly.

One nice thing that this remote does - or something I simply never paid attention to with my 550 - is the ability to make new commands by programming button press sequences. On my Dish satellite receiver for example, you have to push the DVR button twice to get to the actual list of recorded programs. No problem: make a new command that simply does the two button presses back-to-back, and voila! OK - two button presses isn't the end of the world, but I have another one that takes 4 (and I always have to stop to think about which button to press next) and being able to string these together is a nice feature.

One final note about the Harmony remotes: They can be prone to failure. I've actually got several bad ones over the last few years. Even so, the convenience they offer is such a vast improvement over juggling multiple remotes that I can't fathom going back to any other way. I hope this one is as reliable as my other 550.

product_title: Tomameri Green Portable MP4 Player MP3 Player Video Player with Photo Viewer , E-Book Reader , Voice Recorder + 16 GB Micro SD Card
review_headline: Unbeatable Value, Accessories are practically worth it by themselves
review_body: (free sample supplied for review purposes)  Consider my rating 4 1/2 stars.  Because of the low price I did not expect much and was prepared for the worst, I still can't get over what you get for the price.  Let's start with the packaging and honestly this might be my biggest negative but really didn't effect my rating.  It comes in a two part clear plastic case wrapped in glued on cellophane.  Don't try to remove the cellophane, take a knife and slice along the sides where the two pieces of plastic come together, slice along the two long sides and the bottom short side, you will feel your knife slightly enter the slot along the sides.  By leaving the top side connected you will have a flip open case.  There is another version of this player that has 16GB built in for $5 less but no memory card slot.  For $5 dollars more I consider this player a much better value and a lot of that has to do with the included 16GB memory card, not to mention the included ear buds and charging/data transfer cable, these things are practically worth the price by themselves.  The player itself fits my needs perfectly, mostly for walking and listening to music and audio books.  I got nearly 4 hours of playing time using it for that and probably had more but decided to charge the player, I don't like to let the battery get to low.  The player does so much more than play audio files, there are even 4 games included but watching video and playing games might not be the best things to use the player for because of the small screen size but you can, pictures and video quality were very good.  You can also record what you are listening to on the radio to or use it as a voice recorder.  The radio worked great and the reception was surprisingly good.  My only real negative was the bass with the supplied ear buds was not very good even at the rock setting on the equalizer but I rarely get good bass out of ear buds, the bass was a lot better with an over the ear pair of headphones.  The player wasvery intuitive, I never did look at the instructions and only encountered a few minor bumps in the road that I eventually figured out.  The interface has a quaint old school pixelated look but really was a non issue for me.  For my needs it was perfect and is very highly recommended for those with similar needs to mine.

product_title: NuTech Software Solutions AD2USB Adapter for Ademco Vista
review_headline: Works perfectly with Vista20p and Veralite (after a serial port hack)
review_body:
Now that I have this working I'm very happy with it. I have mine attached to a USB hub attached to a Micasaverde Veralite and I can trigger scenes and alerts from any alarm sensor as well as control the alarm itself. Prior to this I used Total Connect on my phone, and because my alarm is on a cellular modem, it was always a 60 second, multiple click, PIN entry affair to enable or disable the alarm via phone - so painful I rarely bothered. With this, it is a single click 2 second operation (using the Android widgets in the AutHomationHD app). I also can do things like have the front door Z-Wave lock automatically disarm the system when the code is entered correctly - nice when returning home with your hands full. (the lock is smart enough to not disable the alarm if opened from inside the house with the lever)

It was easy to hook to the Vista - I mounted it in the alarm box and it is 4 wires to attach it in parallel with your existing hardwired panels, plus just activating alarm panel address 18. You need the installer code to do that but if you don't have it, you just power up your alarm and hold # * together to get into installer mode. Obviously the Vera needs to be within USB cable distance of the alarm panel; I ran a USB cable from the crawl space up to a shelf on the first floor where the Vera sits.

However, like many home automation integrations, it didn't work out of the box; it didn't show up as a serial port on the Veralite even after the AD2USB plugin was installed. This link will show you how to update drivers via command line SSH and Putty to get it to work: www.alarmdecoder.com/forums/viewtopic.php?f=3&t=122. My biggest struggle was getting to this article after a lot of head scratching..

product_title: Pyle 8-Channel Home Theater Amplifier Rack Mount Amp, Black, 8000 Watt (PT8000CH)
review_headline: Great value.  Can't beat the price vs. features.
review_body:
I purchased this amp to run 6-8 speakers in a coffee house I'm helping to set up. I connected it to some Pyle in-ceiling speakers and a Pyle bluetooth input. For the price and performance, you simply can't beat it.

Yes, it is bulky, and no, it's not the world's greatest amp. What it does have, though, are plenty of useful features for the price: three inputs per channel, bridging, per-channel selection of audio output (R, L, R+L), individual output levels per channel, and other good stuff.

The shop has ~14 foot ceilings and this amp does a nice job of filling the space with audio. Coupled with the Pyle speakers and the Pyle BT PWPBT67, I don't think there's any better value out there.

(BTW, the Pyle PWPBT67 gets a lot of "That's really cool!" comments when I show people what it does -- it's an in-wall BT receiver split into two halves. One side has the BT receiver, track controls, volume control and optional USB chargers; the other side (wired together using a basic Cat 5 cable) has the power input for the system and RCA-style audio out. It allows for a very clean and easy interface to start/stop music and control the volume without fiddling with your music device.)

I haven't had any issues with the buzzing that other folks mention.

In my opinion, you this amp is worth every penny.

product_title: BlackVue DR650S-2CH 16GB with Power Magic Pro, Car Black Box/Car DVR Recorder, Wi-Fi, Full HD, G Sensor, GPS, 16GB SD Card Included, Up To 128GB Support
review_headline: Best buy, if in the market for a Dash camera
review_body:
The BlackVue DR650GW-2CH 16GB was an outstanding choice in my opinion. Short Version: if you are looking for a quality dashcam for added security, this is the best choice. The price is a little steep, and there are definitely less expensive options out there. However, the product you receive for the price is unbeatable. Front and rear cameras, all the hardware you will need to mount the units and cables, simple instructions, and you plug it in and it goes!

How I came to pick the BlackVue:
I had been doing research on dashboard cameras for about 4 months prior to my purchase. The BlackVue had the best reviews overall, and the footage quality from the YouTube videos I watched from this particular brand's videos seemed very clear. I was lucky enough to have a friend who had the previous generation of BlackVue (the DR550) and he showed me his cameras, his set up, and the footage he had gotten off of it.

Some Features:
The DR650 has a 1080p front and 720p rear camera with about 130 degree views, so that was a plus for my car, I catch pretty much anything in front or rear of my car on camera. It is so simple to use, you plug it in and it does everything else for you. The wiring comes with tips on how to wire your car, which I have yet to do. The box came with everything you need to get started, microSD card, the cables, the hardware to mount the units and wires. The app you can download for free works pretty well, I like to use it to make sure I have set up the camera to view everything. The interface is pretty simple, no downloading involved. The application is stored on the microSD card, so you can pretty much review the footage anywhere. Another perk is the GPS, you can display your speed and location (or not) I opt not to display my speed, not because I'm doing anything wrong, but because I don't really feel it necessary. The data is stored on the card, so if you need it in the future, it's there. The location feature is pretty neat, you can see where you were driving when particular bits of footage need to be identified. The settings are also really easy to change (ie what you want an audio alert about, what time you want to display-like time zones, speed in KPH/MPH, which LEDs you want to light up). You can select the length of the clips, I opted for 1 minute clips, for ease with finding the clips I want, and discarding the ones I don't. It also has wifi, that you can turn on or off, which cannot be used to connect to the internet, but makes it easy to connect your phone/table to your BlackVue to the app. The voice recording is on by default, and with a quick swipe of your finger, you can disable this function.

My selection process:
With the company selected, I looked into their products. The X00 series are only the front cameras, and I wanted both front and rear, so the 500, 600, and 700 were out. Of the 550, 650, and 750, I narrowed it down to the 550 or 650, since the 750 has an integrated screen which made it too bulky for my taste. From the remaining two the 650 was the obvious choice. The prices I found on Amazon were comparable to some of the online vendors, and the fact that the 650 has the capability to upgrade to a 64GB microSD card was the deciding factor.

Some Tips I found useful:
1) If upgrading your memory, use a class 10 or better MicroSD card. You simply replace the microSD card that came with your blackvue, start it up, then hold the button (wifi-button) and it will reconfigure the card, no downloading involved.
2) Use the microSD card to usb adapter to access the card. Change your settings as soon as possible to fit your needs. I disabled GPS display (which disabled speed display on footage), changed the lights, to be less obvious, and disabled the audio notifications (my personal preference). But they are easy to play around with. Reviewing footage can be done from your computer or the app, and it's pretty easy.
3) I mounted the frontunit behind my rearview mirror, out of sight for the most part. It's where I kept my radar detector. Unfortunately this took the space of my radar detector, so now I need to find a new place for that. I tried mounting the radar detector under the blackvue, but it gets in the footage. My car is a smaller, semi sporty car, so if it fits for me, you shouldn't have a problem finding a place for it (unless you have a SUPERCAR, in which case it might be a little harder, but probably pretty easy-I don't personally know anybody with a Lambo or Ferrari, so I haven't had a chance to try).
4) If you have contact with a police officer, about an accident you were involved in or witnessed, I don't believe (don't hold me to this) you are under any obligation to let them know you have it (Washington State, USA). If you have a clear shot that is useable, I would submit it to the police department as soon as possible. Since we aren't required to have a dash cam, and it's fairly rare (around here at least) most officers won't even think to ask (from my experience). But I think it's useful to have, especially in a "he said she said" type situation, where you can clearly identify the person at fault. I personally have seen so many accidents as of late, that I thought I'd capture some interesting footage, hopefully NOT involving me.

Easily one of the most versatile speakers Iâ€™ve seen, this thing does it all. Bluetooth media/phone playback and mic (yeah, you can do a phone call on it) as you would expect. But also USB flash drives (thumb drives, etc. but it cannot power a portable hard drive - I tried) using a NORMAL full sized USB port. But wait - thereâ€™s more! It has a microSD card slot. Throw some music on a microSD card - plug it in and youâ€™re good to go.

If that wasnâ€™t enough, it does â€œaux inâ€ using a standard 3.5â€ headphone jack. So if you have a friend with a phone that doesnâ€™t have Bluetooth or an MP3 player or <insert whatever here> - you can literally plug the speaker in as if it were headphones.

Still listen to the FM radio? Yep, it has that too.

It is worth noting that it comes with a very proprietary cable that has an unusual configuration. If you lose this sucker, you might be out of luck doing â€œaux inâ€. Iâ€™ve never seen anything quite like it. On a positive note, ANY standard microUSB charging cable will charge the unit - so if you lose this little cable? All youâ€™re out is â€œaux inâ€ capability.

Itâ€™s plastic, of course - with a few hieroglyphic buttons on the top (more on that in a minute). The back has the battery case (yes! The battery is removable!) door, an honest to goodness ON/OFF switch, the microSD card slot, the microUSB slot and the standard USB slot. There is nothing on the sides, front or back. Itâ€™s a very clean design; possibly a bit boxy for some, but works for me.

Now that Iâ€™ve said the praise, it is time for the smack down.

First, take the manual out of the box and use it to line your cat box - thatâ€™s all it is good for. Youâ€™re lucky you have this review - save you a lot of trial and error decoding the Da Vinci code.

The buttons on top are not helpful nor self-explanatory. Here is what you got (from left to right - looking at the front).

Of everything, the Pause button is the only one that wonâ€™t bring on confusion. Well, it does double as a SCAN button in FM radio mode.

The MODE button could send you to early retirement. Each push of the button changes it to a different mode. But the modes are only of what is AVAILABLE at that moment. Some things like â€œBluetooth Modeâ€ and â€œRadio Modeâ€ and â€œAuxilary Modeâ€ are always available (even if nothing is plugged in to Auxiliary). review_headline: These headphones are worth every penny! Comfortable with great sound!
review_body:
I used to only use over ear headphones. Then I started seeing good reviews for in ear headphones. I needed something that would work well for doing chores and working out. I started with the Sol Republic Relays. Great sound but the opening for the sound didn't fit well in my ear canal so it didn't seal well regardless of the size of ear piece I used. Then I read a review of the Momentums in Wired magazine and decided to order them.

These little babies are amazing. The opening on them is smaller than the relays so they fit well in my ears and stay in place. The sound that comes out is impressive! The bass is like having a 12 inch sub woofer on your head and they create spacious sound. No idea how they do it with such small speakers but the frequency range rivals the home theater systems I have. I use a pair of Beats Pros at work and think the Momentums sound better.

The controls are easy to use and work well with the apps I have tried.

The only cons I can note are that they give up a little high end sound quality to get the bass. I am a bass head, listening to a lot of trance, so this worked for me. I also wish they had a clip to hold the cord in place. I just loop the cord around my neck and that has been working fine.

All in all, I can't say enough about these. I love them. I Will look to Sennheiser again in the future.

product_title: BeoPlay H6 - Special Edition Blue Stone
review_headline: Audiophile Headphones, comparison of the H6 and P7
review_body:
This is probably the best sounding headphone I have so far. All the lows are present (yes the very lows, but not loud). The mids are balanced. The highs are very vibrant. Overall, this is a very balanced flat sounding headphone with a higher emphasis on the highs (just enough to not perceive sharp). Overall, you can say this headphone sounds like er4-pt with better bass production.

I was actually deciding between Bowers & Wilkins P7 and BeoPlay H6. Both are very good headphones, but with a different sound signature. The H6 is acoustic-based (confirmed by Bang & Olufsen seller) meaning H6 produces the details of the instruments and drums very well. I do feel I hear more of the music with the H6. Does that mean P7 is inferior? NO. When listening P7, you would still hear every detail but with a more emphasis on the vocals (mid range). In other words, the highs are not as emphasized but you can still hear every little detail. The vocals are more noticeable. The bass are stronger too (however, H6 has a higher range of bass production). Compared to the P5, P7 is more natural (P5 is more dynamic). Initially, I chose the P7 over H6 because P7 has a more comfortable sound signature, but returned it later because of the strong clamping force of the ear-cups which is very uncomfortable (doesn't mean I do not like P7). The next day, after listening to the H6 headphone for 1 hr at a Bang and Olufsen store, I decide to buy it because the big upgrade of sound quality compare to the Bose QC15 is worth it. In addition, the wearing comfort of the H6 is much better than the P7.

Overall, I would definitely recommend the H6 because you would not be disappointed. If bass is a concern (as some of the reviewers here think this headphone do not produce enough bass volume), use a headphone amplifier or get the DJ version of this headphone.

Note: before buying, you should try both the P7 and H6. I love both of them.

product_title: Bose Wave SoundTouch Music System
review_body: Having had the Bose Wave Radio CD previously, I was looking to upgrade to adding internet radio for clarity not achievable with the FM tuner without an unwieldy external FM antenna6. The Wave SoundTouch fit the bill perfectly. Sound of radio and CD was pure Bose Wave which is excellent in a small room but does not substitute for a full stereo system.  Setup of the Wi-Fi based SoundTouch was straightforward when following the manual. One needs a PC and a working Wi-Fi router with the SoundTouch connecting to the PC or Laptop with an included USB cord. You need to know the router password. Next downloading the SoundTouch app onto an iPad or other tablet or smartphone is necessary to access the tens of thousands global, national or local internet radio stations which are free or paid for music services like Sirius XM or Pandora. The app works well and allows you to browse geographically and according to music or talk taste. One can save 6 stations on the app as presets and can save those same stations on the unit's remote control. Assuming a good working Wi-Fi system, the sound is absolutely pristine with no interference which may effect FM or AM reception. The sound is equivalent to a CD.  Setting alarms, sleep and snooze functions are routine. The sleep function, which automatically turns off the system can be custom programmed to shut off at 30 minutes, 60 minutes, etc. The alarms can be set to wake up with a buzzer, CD or AM or FM radio. The alarm will not allow wakeup with internet radio. This is the system's only weakness and buyers should be aware of this. You can access internet radio only through the remote control or, if it the last station played, by directly tapping the radio console.  Like other recent models, the console has no controls and requires the remote for most functions. What is very nice is that just tapping the top of the console allows one to turn on and off the system with the last station or track set. This touch sensitive feature allows youto turn off the unit in the dark when the alarm rings by just tapping the top of the case; no buttons to find and no need for the remote. This also resets the alarm for the next day.  It takes about an hour to set up, but no special technical expertise is required. Once set up to your tastes, this compact unit gives excellent clear sound with good bass due to "Wave" technology and serves as the world's most sophisticated and expensive alarm clock as well. It is expensive, but it delivers exactly what it promises.

review_headline: Works perfectly. Well worth the cost.
review_body:
My problem was that my new Sony TV sound often did not lip-sync with the picture when using my dated Yamaha analog receiver and speaker system. It was just a fraction of a second off, but very annoying; especially when watching singing shows! I was using the RCA audio connections from the TV to the old Yamaha amp. The Yamaha is still an excellent receiver so, I was reluctant to spend hundreds of dollars to purchase a new receiver just to get updated connections. The Fiio appeared to be a good solution to the problem so, I was excited to try it.
I received the Fiio converter in two days using Amazon Prime. Installation instructions were very clear and easy to follow. Everything you will need for the hook-up is in the package. It took less than 5 minutes to install. However, It did not work at first attempt. So, I re-read the instructions. The critical step that I had missed was to go into the Sony TV audio menu and change from: "Dolby audio- Yes" change to: "Dolby audio- No".
Now all program picture & sound sources are perfectly lip-synced.
I can not speak of the longevity of this gadget as I have only had it installed for a couple of days. It does appear to be sturdily constructed and of good quality. So far, I am 100% satisfied.

review_body: I bought this to extend music from our family room home theater system through four walls into our living room or out on the patio.  It's perfect.  The sound is great, there's way more volume than I would ever need and the bass response is quite impressive.  Because of my existing wiring and equipment setup, I had to locate the transmitter only five feet from my wireless router and I was worried about interference. I was happy to find out that there are no problems using a PC, tablet or laptop while using the speaker.  I'm very satisfied with my purchase.    UPDATE:  After using this for a couple of days, I realized there IS interference with my WiFi.  LOTS of interference.  For simple browsing on the internet using a laptop or tablet while I am playing music through the speaker, there is no problem.  But I have discovered that my download speeds are cut back to 5 or 10 percent of what they normally are. Downloading a large file or streaming audio or video is all but impossible, and doing so causes the sound from the speaker to break up badly.  I have also determined that the maximum range with this product is about 25 feet.  Hardly the 600 feet advertised.  Again, this is probably due to my WiFi and others in the neighborhood    With so many people relying on WiFi, I don't understand why they developed a product that would not work well in that environment.  I have dropped my rating from a 5 to a 3 for this reason.    UPDATE 2:  After placing the transmitter on the floor, therefore decreasing its signal relative to my wireless router, I have eliminated 95% of my interference.  I still get the speaker range and good quality that I need.  If I use any device with internet within 10 feet of the speaker, the audio breaks up.  But I can work around that.  4 STARS.

product_title: Soundsoul(TM) Noise-isolating Sport In-ear Headphones
review_headline: soundsoul U10's earphones deliver lots of treble...
review_body:
The Soundsoul U10 Sport Headphones produce sound with a heavy emphasis on the higher frequencies, with a minimal contribution on the bottom end. The ear buds are designed to be inserted into the aural canal a certain angle. The cord has \\"memory wire\\", which is a malleable sleeve, which can be shaped to fit over the top of the ear, or bent so that it fits below the ear. While the system works, it may not produce the most comfortable fit, or have a very stylish look.

The earphones come with silicone inserts of different sizes, so hopefully you will get a good fit. Even though I got a pretty good seal in my aural canal, there was still some bleed through of ambient sound. Some may consider these to be \\"noise isolating\\", but these earphones would not be my choice for use on a flight.

The light gray colored cabling is a little stiffer than I prefer, making the cord is a little difficult to wind up and store. The stiffness produces what I call the \\"stethoscope effect\\", which is the transmission of sound through the cord into the ears. I would have much preferred an L shaped fitting, because they tend to be more durable, but the gold plated audio jack is a straight pin type.

I was provided a sample of for evaluation, and think that the Soundsoul U10's are really great for those times when you just want to listen to a lot of treble. Whether its music or the spoken word, these earphones have a nice sharp edge, without being too grating. It's not something I want to hear all the time, but it does make for a nice change of pace, and I would probably buy a new pair of U10's in the future. Ten bucks is more than fair for this kind of sound quality, even if some of the design elements are not exactly ideal. Also included is a high quality carrying case.

review_headline: So I bought these having loved the previous V1's
review_body:
So I bought these because I had the original Hurricane headphones, which these are based off of. Those broke because of an accident with a backpack stuffed in the bottom of a trunk with a ton of wet clothes. So I bought these having loved the previous V1's. I would like to start by saying if I could give them a 4.5 I would but the 5 star review does serve more justice than the 4 star does.

So when I bought these they came in this awesome packaging and stuff, and I was immediately pleased with them. The very first thing to note that was better about them than the Hurricane headphones is that they fold, which helps out with carrying around a ton.
On to the sound quality, they sound great for the price. If you want something with spectacular sound go and buy some sony's for 100-150.
But for the Price these are fantastic. The bass is well balanced, (not boosted like the previous ones) The bass is clear and doesn't distort the highs and mids like the hurricanes. The highs are much clearer and crisp in these although they have a slightly telephone sound filter which is only noticeable when comparing to other headphones. The mids sound the best and makes everything smoothen out.
So the sound quality is about a 4.5 here.
They are very comfortable but fit oddly on your head at first unless the band is placed more forward. But the texture is very soft and comfortable. The hurricanes comfort was better mainly because their texture was softer and they fit your head less awkwardly.
After wearing them for about 3 hours they start to make your ears hurt, (like most headphones would.)
the battery life though. These things last forever. I wear them 4-5 hours a day and it took about 10-14 days to run out. But once the battery gets low the voice interface interrupts the audio and says "Battery low" literally every 30 seconds. So in order to avoid that I would charge them about once a week just to be safe. They also only take about 3-5 hours to fully charge which is fantastic.

I would recommend these highly for anyone who wants them for listening pleasure. As long as you can take care of them well. But for someone like a producer like myself, If you want to use them for producing, I wouldn't mainly because their main feature is bluetooth which will lag in the headphones. product_title: ViewHD HDMI Switch
review_headline: Nice Compact HDMI Splitter, But Auto Switch Does Not Work
review_body:
Great for helping to expand the number of HDMI ports on my TV and offers a number of great features compared to other HDMI splitters:

1. does not require a separate power cord

2. includes its own HDMI cord to connect to a single source on the output side

3. small and easy to hide (mounted mine to back of TV using 3M double back tape)

That being said, the only problem I am having with the unit I purchased is that it does not automatically switch between sources when one is powered up (product name states "Auto Switch"). The 2 devices that I have plugged in are my Fire TV and a DVD player.

Obviously if both devices are powered up I can see that there would be a conflict on which to select, but since the DVD player has a power button (Fire TV does not), the Auto Switch should cut back to the Fire TV when the DVD player's power is turned off which it does not.

So not sure if I received a defective unit, but I have to manually switch between sources using the button on the top.

Also as some others have mentioned, there is a few seconds of audio static when the TV is first turned on or sometimes when switching between sources.

Overall I like this device and find it very useful but was really hoping that it would switch between my input sources so I would not have to get up to do it manually.

review_body: Okay, I am leaving my original review below so in case if you happen to be interested in reading you know what kind of issues I faced.   I will say I changed my review from one star to almost 5 star, because as both sides of the headphone worked, it truly sounded amazing. I think it is worth the price and does provide solid experience. And for bonus it looks good too ;)    Now for the problem that faced here is the solution and a reason for calling it almost 5 stars and not full 5 stars. It is a design flaw in the way the cable has been designed or say the instruction manual are provided. The audio/microphone cable supplied with the headphone is a unidirectional cable, or for better clarity only partially works if connected in a certain direction. The cable pin (on the side of the microphone) needs to go in the headphone and otherwise in the audio player. If you do otherwise then you end up hearing sound in only one side, unless you press the volume control button in the middle. It's possible that many people at first may not notice this little thing and may end up getting the same issue as I got, like many online forums prove and some Amazon reviewers too. I suggest that Beats update their manual instructions about this requirement so they don't end up having their customers return their product due to this limitation. Else enjoy the music as it is supposed to be.     You off course don't need to read but my original and now not so relevant review is below --     The worst product I have ever purchased. First of all when you spend $200 you expect the product to work, with a solid quality. For my headphone, only one side worked and other side just did not. Then I realized that other side works only when I press the control button in the cable, but had to keep it pressed constantly. For once I really thought that may be it is named solo for a reason that only one side of headphone supposed to work ;) anyways, then I thought that it could be one off issue but I read reviews and forums and looks like it is a very common issue with these headphones. I can also say that sound quality was pathetic, no where close to what you would expect with such expensive product. Save money and spend it some place else. I am returning it back with a hope that I can find a better replacement.

product_title: Pyle Home  Mini Power Amplifier with LED Display
review_headline: you gotta cool this thing off first.
review_body:
Its great little unit but you must do a couple of tasks before you use it on a regular basis.
The unit as it comes from the factory builds up too much heat as the vents are inadequate.
Take the four little phillips screws(8 total) on each side end of the unit out and take the top cover off carefully.
Take(rip) the plastic mesh off the top vent cover to release some of the heat from this unit.
If you can while its off, take a drill and put some holes with a steel drill bit. I put 10--1/4 inch holes in the top.
Make sure to get all the filings off to prevent them later falling in the circuit board.
Screw the top back on carefully just line up the holes.
This will make the unit run a lot cooler and prevent it from failing later.
