product_title: Creative Sound Blaster Roar: Portable NFC Bluetooth Wireless Speaker with aptX/AAC
review_headline: Great if you keep in perspective
review_body: Everybody has ears and those ears hear different things different ways. I have personally owned the Bose Soundlink, Bowers Wilkins T7, Klipsch KMC1 and 3. Though all of them certainly have particular attributes none of them sell for the price or with the features of the ROAR. My KMC 3 is definitely the beast for the backyard however if want more vocal presence and upper sounds with a good presence of bass in a smallish portable speaker the ROAR strikes the best balance for portability, overall sound, features, build quality and if you factor in value to dollar, nothing comes close. I recently even purchased the ROAR 2 from overseas to daisy chain the two of them together and the new upwards configuration for those times I'm in the backyard and its on the table and I'm above the drivers. I travel a ton and the ROAR has also become my travel companion for watching movie in the hotel room versus using the poopy TV speakers. If you use this as your first foray into a Bluetooth speaker you will save a ton of money by not running through the gamut of speakers I have. It's a great product of you keep in perspective that it's the size of a big paperback book. Though the sound certainly belies its size.

product_title: RHA Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphone with Remote and Microphone - 3 Year Warranty
review_body: I bought these IEMs in early 2015. When I got them they were amazing sounding and didn't disappoint in the sound department. If you want to read about how great these sound, other reviewers have already written about that. My problem came about 6 months after I bought them. The rubber that makes up the cord near the end of the earphones that has the jack had a tear in it, exposing the wires underneath. I contacted their excellent customer service and they had me ship in the IEMs after sending them pictures of the tear. They sent me a brand new pair in its original packaging. I was very happy until the second pair started acting strange. Over a period of a month, I noticed that the bass starting wearing off, literally vanishing. Because this happened over a month, I didn't notice they were actually broken until the bass was non-existent. I contacted customer service again and they just sent me a new pair again without asking any more questions. Again I was happy with my third pair, until the left earbud cord just disconnected itself from where the two cords meet in the middle. Same routine: contact customer service, they send me a new pair. I'm currently on my fourth pair and have had no trouble so far.  I understand how the first problem could have been my own, but the other two problems both happened within a 3 month period. Maybe I just got bad luck, but for a earphone that has such a stake in their build quality, I for one haven't had such a great experience in that department. product_title: GE 25336 Receptacle, In Wall 1 Outlet 2 USB Ports 2.1 Amps
review_body:
In our busy household, USB chargers seem to be at a premium. Especially since the likes of Apple, Amazon, etc., seem to only think people need a USB cable these days and want you to spend another $20 on a simple plug. This "shortage" has led to my wife and kids poaching my charging station, moving chargers around, etc. Of course, that leads to the inevitable lost charger and the "I don't know where it went... wasn't me..." spiel.

Given the above situation, the GE In Wall Outlet with 2 USB ports was exactly what we needed! We have an outlet in our kitchen that is the popular plug-in spot, but this often resulted in someone unplugging someone else's device so they can use a different type of cable (lightning, mini-USB, 40-pin Apple, etc.), which then led to arguments. Such is life with kids. That location was perfect for this outlet, as we only plug in one thing there (besides chargers), which is a phone.

On the whole, assuming you have modern wiring (my house was built in 2006), the installation was quite simple. In my case it involved a bit of extra work, as the outlet I wanted to use was a GFI. After confirming I could move the GFI outlet to another location on the circuit (which happened to be the other side of the kitchen counter), it just required some basic outlet swapping and a few tools (a multi-purpose screwdriver and needle nose pliers for straightening out and trimming wires). In total, it was about a 20 minute job, and was not difficult at all. Having the two 2.1a charging ports is very handy, and looks much nicer than oddball USB chargers.

My only complaint is that the 'wall wart' of our cordless phone, which we plug in to that outlet, blocks the lower USB port when it is plugged in. So we have to unplug that if we want to use both USB ports, but since it doesn't keep the phone from working that hasn't been an issue.

Naturally the sound was muffled, but otherwise all was well. When I pulled it out of the water the sound remained muffled thanks to all the water in the speaker holes. I soaked up most of the water, but not all with a towel & the sound was once again normal. So keep in mind that if you want to enjoy good sound quality, try not to submerge the speakers while having fun.

The sound quality is good enough for what you get with four options for the sound: flat, rock, pop or jazz. The button controls are not as sensitive as I'd like. If this was not designed to be waterproof I would rate it less than five stars. As it is, it performs as I need it to & have no complaints. I'm more than happy knowing I have a small lightweight floating speaker that should be able to handle the rugged outdoor life around my family farm.

If you want better, louder sound, as well as a nicer looking speaker with International adapters for travel, you might want to check out the [[ASIN:B00I9ID070 NYNE TT]] I use it in the office & for when I have to travel for business. product_title: AKG Closed-Back Reference Class Headphones
review_headline: Better sounding, affordable replacements for Sony MDR V6
review_body: I wanted a new set of 'phones to replace an old Sony MDR v6 ('90s era, I think).  Did a lot of reading and was leaning towards Sennheiser open-backs (HD600/650 maybe) but I tend to listen to headphones while my wife watches TV so closed back seemed a better idea.  I liked the claims that the K550s had spaciousness like an open-back design.  Was concerned the K550s would be too bright and/or not fit (not be able to get a good seal).  They've only got about 10 hours on them so far BUT for me at least, both those concerns are unfounded.  Regarding fit - I was surprised how the gimbals that allow rotation of the cups into a flat position for storage ALSO contribute to a good seal.  In use, the gimbals allow the cups to be rotated through both vertical and horizontal planes as needed to match the contours of your face  Fit isn't reliant only on length of extension of the cups below the head band.  As others have commented, these headphones are VERY comfortable and for me it was easy to get a good seal.  Regarding tone - I'd say they are warmish with a bit of high end roll-off.  Highs are definitely not harsh or annoying.  The main reason I didn't give 5 stars relates to this.  High end could use a little more extension (sparkle) which might contribute to that last bit of resolution. Maybe the higher-priced K701s or 702s would bring this BUT it's really a minor quibble and for me doesn't detract from enjoying the music.  Given the trend towards \\"hot\\" in many remastered re-issues, this trait probably contributes to enjoyable listening.  Certain on-line reviews have commented about a wrongness in the treble (\\"tizziness\\") and a sporadic, annoying high frequency resonance (around 7000-9000 Hz?).  Can't say I've noticed this.  At most and only very occasionally - maybe twice in several hours of listening - a chord from the upper octaves of the piano was a bit harsh.  Really can't say whether that was an artifact of the K550s or the recording itself.  In general, these 'phonesare very easy to listen to for hours without fatigue.  Compared to the Sonys the sound is spacious and uncongested.  Words in vocals are more easily understood.  Bass is deep but won't rattle your brains.  These just aren't those kinds of 'phones (with artificially boosted bass).  There's plenty of good quality bass for rock...really enjoyed Band of Horses on these last night.  Also, Radar Men from the Moon (\\"The Wire\\") or Tony Levin on Black Light Syndrome's Duende have some deep bass that comes across very well.  They are easy to drive...plenty loud without amplification when plugged into a Macbook Air though my normal mode of listening is with an AudioQuest Dragonfly v1.2 plugged into the MBA.  For $203 with shipping, I think the K550s are something of a steal.  Definitely worth trying and if you don't like them, Amazon has a good return policy.  I'm sure mine aren't fully broken in yet so am looking forward to things sounding even better with more time on them.

review_body:
The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is that they aren't black as stated, they are shiny.

Installation is easy, they tell you what size drill bit to use (5/16ths) and then you use an allen wrench to screw the inserts in.
I used them for my 4-way JBLs with 12" side firing woofers, which weigh about 85 lbs. a piece, and didn't have near the difficulty other reviewers had prepared me for when placing the discs under the cones.

It would have been helpful if they'd included a cheap allen wrench, but I happen to have a full set myself.

I think that you can use these in two ways:
Using them with just the spikes will anchor them to a carpeted floor and allow you to level them if needed, and presumably give you good "ground rumbling" bass.

Then again, you can use the included discs with their little indented bowl-shaped divots which allow for the speakers to move very slightly from side to side and/or back to front, which effectively decouples the speakers from the floor a little bit, and seems to give a little bit tighter and more accurate bass, without shaking the floor and interfering with a turntable.
I find that I can now crank the volume up a lot more without having the bass rumble/feedback through the turntable.

I would highly recommend these for any speakers within reason (probably not too good for very massive speakers).

review_headline: Music In The Shower Just Got Better!
review_body:
Almost everyone in my home sings in the shower. Sometimes it's joyful and other times I wish there was music for them to follow along with. Unfortunately, I refuse to put my phone in the bathroom for them to listen to music, simply because I've made that mistake before and my phone ended up in the bathtub ruined! Luckily, Liztek has solved our problems with their waterproof Bluetooth speakers that are designed specifically for the bathroom! How cool is that?

The Speaker is very soft to the touch and the colors are bold and vibrant. I love the case that it comes in because it's made perfectly to fit the speaker and it holds the papers and charger so that you don't lose them. The attached suction cup offers a stable placement for the speaker. I love the stability of it and that it's strong enough to hold even when we constantly press the buttons. It's long lasting, making it where I don't have to charge it that often and I love that once connected, my phone automatically connects when both are on and in range. It's an added bonus for the mornings when I am rushing to get ready. I also love that there is a cover piece for the charger port. This is an added bonus to keep dust, water, and everything else out of your speaker.

I love that the speaker controls the volume. However, check your device as well. At first, I thought the speaker was way too low because I couldn't hear it over the shower. Then I realized that when connected the speaker automatically sets my phone volume at the half way mark (regardless of how loud it was before connection). This is a great feature for children who take baths, but when I am in the shower I have to remember to turn my phone's volume back up so that it plays loud enough in the shower. While it is an additional step for me, I love that I don't have to worry about the volume being too high for my kiddos.

I've used this product for about two weeks now and I absolutely love it. It's a great addition for anyone that sings in the shower or anyone that loves music. It also makes a great Christmas or housewarming gift.

product_title: FiiO X1 High Resolution Lossless Music Player
review_headline: Would Be 5 Stars If Not For One Major Flaw   ***UPDATE***
review_body: While the build quality and the interface is basically as I had expected from reading the other reviews, the main issue I have with this player is it's system of updating it's media library. I purchased this with a 128 GB SanDisk Ultra Class 10 microSD card. I am using approximately 97 of the 119 GB of storage on the card, and while all the songs show up in the file portion of the interface, in order to "categorize" the music in the media library to sort by artist, album, or even to get a playlist of every song  (to shuffle the entire device) an internal update must be done every time music is added or removed from the SD card. While I have around 15,000 songs on the device, every time I perform this media update, exactly 5,800 songs are recognized, usually the first 5,800 songs when arranged by artist, alphabetically. So only a third of my songs show up when I search via "artist" or "song" or "album." I made sure that I had the latest firmware, which I did and then I tried rearranging the songs alphabetically to test my theory of the "first" 5,800 getting categorized, and sure enough I was right. I contacted FiiO's customer service and explained the situation, to which they replied, "There are two situations about this problem: 1.Some songs x1 can't support because of their formats. I send you a form and you find whether relevant formats. 2.Some songs may be damaged. Pls check them." All of my files are supported files and as explained previously, the 5,800 songs that get categorized are the first 5,800 alphabetically, I can rearrange them and songs that weren't categorized the first time will be. Either there is a max limit for the media library or they need another firmware update. I am awaiting another response from FiiO, I will be sure to update this review if anything changes.  ***UPDATE***  10-1-15 Firmware 1.5 was released, removing the 5,800 song limit to the library. That really was my main complaint, and nowthat it is resolved it is the best portable high-quality-music player for the money, period.

product_title: AudioQuest - Evergreen (1.5m, Mini-to-RCA)
review_headline: An excellent cable for use in stationary home setups, not suitable for portable use.
review_body:
These are a fantastic cable if you are using them in a situation where 1) the cables won't be moved around too much and 2) your connected equipment doesn't have RCA jacks that are spread apart more than 1.5-2 inches. They are made out of solid core copper, which is more prone to breakage than stranded copper, and I am using them in an environment where I do not need to move it around much, so it fit my situation perfectly, but in a mobile environment or as a cable that is constantly disconnected and where the RCA jacks are disconnected and reconnected constantly, they will be prone to breaking.

That being said, this cable is highly transparent, and in terms of sound staging and detail retrieval, it is up there with the best of the stranded cables I have used in the past, which all cost at least twice to five times what this cable cost. I am using it to connect my FiiO X1 portable digital audio player to my Meier Audio Corda Arietta headphone amplifier, and in this setup it works fantastically. I only wish I could use it with my high end amplifier, as I would purchase another one to use with it, but alas, it has about a 4 inch spread between its RCA jacks, and the RCA's on the AudioQuest cables in this series will not spread apart enough to work with it.

product_title: Philips In-ear Headphones - Silver
review_headline: GREAT pair of headphones for the price!
review_body:
I found these to be a decent pair of headphones. I got a pair of the Skull Candy Ink'd 2 earbuds about 6 weeks ago. One of the buds in the skull candy is already at about half strength for some reason (very disappointed in that) but I was still able to compare and contract these Philips against the Ink'd 2 and found the Philips had the superior sound. I was surprised by that and very happy. I was also delighted that they stayed firmly in my ears during a 6 mile run this morning despite it being a sweaty & hot run. The one knock on these that I have is that there was a distinct whistling sound from them as I was running - not from the sound or the speakers, they just physically disturbed the surrounding air somehow as I was running thereby creating a mild whistling. I only noticed it between tracks though so it's not a big deal overall. Just strange.

One year later: these still work great! I run and workout with them daily still and the sounds quality is much better than any other cheap ear bud I have used. That whistling sound I mentioned earlier? Haven't noticed that in so long I forgot that it bothered me the first time or two I used these. I heartily endorse these and would happily buy them again.

product_title: SOL Republic Unisex Shadow Wireless In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Sound quality, build quality, and... did I mention sound quality? Solid upgrade over LG HBS7xx series
review_body:
Unlike some other reviewers, I would give the nod to these over the obvious comparison set--the LG HBS 7 series. I've had both the HBS730 and the HBS750, and also four other bluetooth headsets over the years, including the Soundpeats and another Chinese knockoff. These are my personal favorite of the bunch, though they aren't perfect..

SOUND QUALITY: There is one key factor in favor of these: sound quality. These are *noticeably* better in that department than either of the LG's or any of the others that I've tried. The bass is much more substantial but not boomy, making music listening a lot more enjoyable. Mids are not recessed and the highs are clear. I had high expectations based on various professional reviews on the web and am very happy to say that the expectations were met. Good job, Sol.

COMFORT: They don't rest around your neck as nicely as the LGs, but they're more compact and feel just as light, if not lighter. I wish the rubber neckband was slightly longer and come further down. If you have a thicker neck this could be an issue and I'd try to check them out before buying. I wear a 16.5 size dress shirt and they fit me well. I replaced the included tips with a set of Comply S-400 and they are extremely comfortable to wear all day. I carry around a small pouch to store them when I'm not listening and the Shadows bundle / bunch up easily and don't take up a lot of pocket space, which is another plus. And I don't worry about the wires. Speaking of which....

BUILD QUALITY: The wires on the LG Tones I've owned both gave out on me over time. They are very thin. The ones on these Shadows are flat and thicker and I believe will last far longer. Of course, you could buy the LG Infinim / HBS900 for this price with the retractable mechanism, but those are much larger / bulkier and the band is rigid. Doesn't make for easy portability.

SOME FINAL THOUGHTS:
- I wish these had full track controls. They could have been implemented rather easily with the volume controls but as it stands you only have play / pause, on / off, forward skip, and volume.
- I wish the battery lasted just a little longer, but it gets through the day for me listening to podcasts while taking the subway, going to the gym, etc.
- You can't run or anything like that with these on, but for elliptical machines, treadmills, stationary bikes, etc. they are fine. I use them all the time that way.plemented rather easily with the volume controls but as it stands you only have play / pause, on / off, forward skip, and volume.

product_title: AVR-X3100W 7.2 Channel Full 4K Ultra HD A/V Receiver with Bluetooth and WIFI Pro Audio Plug and Play Installation Package plus 2 x 6ft high speed HDMI cables (Bundle of 3 products)
review_body:
This receiver got to me fast! Awesome shipper, i wasn't expecting to receive for another couple of days.

As for the receiver, I've been a fan of Denon for a while now. With ultra 4k HDMI out, it was time to upgrade. Since I already had everything in place, installation was a cinch - of course I had a lot of dust to clean when I removed my old receiver.

The receiver comes with an Audessy mic for tuning. The tuning process measured sound from 8 different points, testing each speaker at each point. After the analysis of the data, it automatically tuned the eq & sound levels. Usually, I take out my reference tones and sound Meyer to do my own fine tuning. However, the sound was really great, so I didn't even bother with fine tuning!

It has plenty of HDMI inputs. I like that I'm able to reduce the number of cables going up to the wall mounted tv - no more need for optical cables! Www love our PS4, so it was nice that I could setup the system to automatically turn on the Tv and have out automatically select game. The kids were impressed with that. The GF was impressed with the internet music and the tuner along with the nice loud 100 watts/channel RMS into 7 Bose speakers!

I was honestly looking at the 4100 series with 9.2 surround & 125 watts. But there's not a lot of 9.2 media out there yet and I can get by with a loss of 20 watts per channel.

I didn't hook up the wireless. Since I ran network cabling throughout my apartment, I elected to make a new LAN cable and plug it into my network. The network functions are fine. Speed is decent. There was no lag our jitter in any of the internet music. Today, it prompted me for an update, so I let it do its thing. It took about 40 minutes. My son was disappointed because I interrupted his game (LoL). But after it completed, my son turned on the PS4 and lo & behold...everything turned right back on and back to the game without additional intervention.

Goodsound, wired/wireless networking, internet music, Pandora & Sirius, plenty of HDMI ports, powered USB, Bluetooth (which I haven't tried yet)...I think this is a good deal!

product_title: Dayton Audio DTA-120 Class T Digital Mini Amplifier 60 WPC (Black)
review_headline: Very pleased, solid value and better sound potential than garden variety powered PC speakers.
review_body:
Initial impression, so no idea over the long term.

This replaced a DTA-1 that I managed to blow up by accidentally flipping the DC polarity when I changed power supplies...

This has a lot more grunt and drives the cheap Dayton bookshelf speakers I have much better than the DTA-1 did. Much better dynamic range of course and generally a cleaner sound as a result. I have an old Polk RM3000 set that I may swap out since this should have enough grunt to drive it.

I use a Roland M-10MX mixer and feed my PC, numerous radios and scanners and a HomeSpot bluetooth dongle into the mixer and the output goes into the DTA-120. Makes for a very handy and flexible desktop audio solution for anyone with multiple sources.

I don't at all notice the hiss sitting less than 3 feet from the bookshelf speakers in a near-field monitor type configuration until the volume is nearly wide open on the amp and I would expect that from something in this price range. I'm wondering if other reviewers had either a defective unit, or a noisy source plugged in when they tested that?

The power supply is a 24VDC switching type brick (about the size of the old laptop supplies from the 90s), it's pretty large, but has a long cord reach so it easily sits on the floor under the desk.

This amp with a bluetooth audio receiver is a great combo for anyone looking to have a more powerful option to drive a decent pair of speakers from their phone or tablet. A solid value for the cash and the compact size is also very nice.

product_title: Emotiva XPA-2 Stereo Power Amplifier
review_headline: Good budget minded amplifier but certainly not an audiophile amplifier.
review_body: Update 2-6-2015: I had to update this to a 4 star as it sounds pretty good through my cheap Klipsch KF-28 speakers. Really brings out sounds I had not heard before. I guess they just needed the extra power. Also the buzz\hiss I complained about is so minor even with these 98db sensitivity speakers that it is almost not worth mentioning. That is not the case with the XPA-5 gen 2 I have which has considerably louder hiss and buzz with 94db sensitivity speakers. This amp for me is a for sure buy now and has really brought my 7.1 system to life when watching movies.     I would have given this 5 stars if this was not my second one replacing the first one that had an issue with the cooling fins or something making loud pings every 2 hours or so. It was like someone hitting the cooling fins with a tiny metal hammer. Clearly sounded like a expansion issue causing the metal to ping loudly. I sent it back and got a new one after posting a question here to see if that was happening to others which it was not.    Now for the review. This amplifier is a good budget amplifier. So if you are looking for an amp that will give your speakers the power to play more of their full range on a budget this is the amp. My NAD T748 just didn't have the power to push my front speakers properly. Using it as a pre-amp with this amp my speakers have now come to life. They will now play bass and their full range. I also have the Emotiva XPA-5 to power my surround speakers. That brought them to life as well.    Now for the bad. This amp is not perfectly quiet like my other power amps (NAD and B&K Components) though it is quieter than the XPA-5 even with more sensitive speakers on the XPA-2 than the XPA-5. If you run all Klipsch high sensitivity speakers like I do expect some buzz\hiss. I am not even running expensive Klipsch speakers either. They are R-15M Klipsch bookshelves for the surrounds a Klipsch RC-52 II reference series center and KF-28 floorstanding speakers for the fronts. Just a cheap7.1 surround system so I was not willing to pay anymore for the power amps and not willing to buy used.    Pros  - Feels and looks well built  - Brings my speakers to life compared to my underpowered AVR. In fact I would be willing to bet it will make all AVRs sound better as their power ratings are always overrated and only rated with 2 channels driven. They drop significantly when all channels are driven so don't believe ratings.    Cons  - Very large and heavy so you will most likely need a new cabinet to hold it  - Buzz\hiss on sensitive speakers  - Build quality is suspect as my first XPA-2 was making loud clicking noises coming from the heating fins. Hopefully the 5 year warranty means that I just got a bad one and this will last.    I would still recommend this amplifier if you are looking for a budget minded upgrade to your AVR powered system.

product_title: Brainwavz S0 In-Ear Earbuds Noise Isolating Earphones Clearwavz Remote & Microphone Stereo Headphone Headset For iPhone iPad, iPod & Android Devices
review_headline: The Good: Earbud-style headphones have always presented me with problems
review_body:
The Good:
Earbud-style headphones have always presented me with problems. While they are convenient in size and have a low profile, they also tend to get lost, tangled, or broken. Additionally, they can be uncomfortable to the ear, and sound quality is often sacrificed in order to create a product small enough to fit into the human ear.

Imagine my surprise when I stumbled across a pair of earbuds that addressed all of these issues.

The Brainwavz S0(pronounced â€˜S-zeroâ€™) In-Ear Monitors surpassed just about every expectation I had regarding earbuds. For starters, the box is packed with extra things that arenâ€™t necessarily required for earbuds, but might make your life a little easier. For instance, a zip-up hard case is included for storage of the S0s, which makes them harder to lose, and will protect them during travel. Also included is a shirt clip, which may seem gimmicky, but as someone who spends a lot of time working outdoors in various environments, I can tell you that nothing is more irritating than an earbud falling out of your ear while performing tasks. The shirt clip allows you to give yourself slack between the clip and the earbuds, meaning increased mobility. Not to be overlooked are the 9 different eartips included with the S0s. The human ear is very diverse, and earbuds certainly cannot be one-size-fits-all. Brainwavz knows this, and equips the buyer with a multitude of options so each buyer can find the perfect fit. One of the included eartips is known as the Comply Foam Tip, which is made out of memory foam and is sound insulating.

I was impressed right off the bat with how easy the S0s fit into my ear. Some earbuds take a little finesse to put in, but that does not seem to be an issue with the S0s. During the actual sound testing of the Brainwavz S0s, I decided to use a splitter so I could have two earbuds (S0s and generic iPod earbuds) plugged into the same device. This way I could preform a real-time comparison between the two earbuds.
Hearing the difference was easy within the first few seconds. As I listened to a song I had heard dozens of times, I was able to hear details through the S0s I had never heard before. The sound of someone taking a breath. The sound of a piano key as it is depressed. Melodic overtones that had previously just been noise. I couldnâ€™t believe the clarity and richness of what my ears were hearing, and the quality was evident through a wide range of genres. Good, solid bass is hard to accomplish in earbuds, but the S0s delivered a performance to match larger, over-the-ear headphones, and this is no small feat. The bass isnâ€™t just a low noise that your ear and brain interpret as bass, but instead is a dynamic sound that arrives to your brain as the artist intended.
While these arenâ€™t active noise-canceling headphones, they are noise-isolating. Essentially, they perform similar to foam earplug insertsâ€“they donâ€™t make you deaf to outside noise, but they dampen everything so that your listening experience is focused on what you are actually supposed to hear.

The Bad:
While it is hard to find anything â€œbadâ€ about this product, I can certainly identify an area that I would like to see improved, even if it is minor. Regarding the carrying case, I believe it would beneficial to have a loop or carabiner attachment. This way, they can be clipped to keys, backpacks, belts, etc.
The only other bad thing about these earbuds is that they are going to ruin your ability to use average earbuds. Your standards will be raised, and you just might find yourself throwing out your old pair.

The Verdict:
The name â€œBrainwavzâ€ is the perfect name for this brand, as the superb sound from the S0s seem to be happening inside your head rather than in your ears. With these earbuds, rather than listening, you are experiencing.

Would I recommend: Yes

product_title: GUSTARD DAC-X12 ES9018 XMOS 32Bit / 384KHz DSD DOP Decoder with USB
review_headline: The two units together (u12 and x12) have a wonderful smooth, dynamic
review_body: I bought the u12 and the x12 to see if technology and price to performance ratio had significantly advanced in five years. It had. My old DAC was highly rated and cost $1200 about 5 years ago. My old DAC is very clear and natural with a real sense of air, but not the last word on detail and dynamics. After about 4 or 5 days of continuous play for break in I listened carefully to the Gustards. The two units together (u12 and x12) have a wonderful smooth, dynamic, and detailed sound with a solidity that approaches analog. Instruments are distinct. Textures are vivid. The sound stage is realistically wide and deep when captured in the recording. Most of all the sound is dynamic and smooth. At times even too dynamic in that I find when listening to classical music I sometimes have to adjust the volume down because of the difference between the loud and soft passages. The options are overwhelming in terms deciding which is the best input and sample rate. I have tentatively decided that the most realistic is no up-sampling via the AES input. This will be a matter of personal taste. Up-sampling 44.1 PCM to DSD does sound smooth and pleasing, though, to my ears, not as clear, especially in the leading edge of the notes. There is no doubt that my CD rips played at their native sample rate now sound very close in quality to my SACD discs. Probably so close that I would have trouble justifying paying the extra money for the purchase of stereo SACDs. I would not say my old DAC was vanquished because it still seems superior in its natural conveyance of air, room ambiance, and balance. The Gustard X12 is the winner in detail and dynamics, though, as mentioned, in some music the dynamics could make the sound slightly too vivid for some tastes. Strangely, its dynamics are probably more realistic than many other DACs but we have become used to less than concert hall volume peaks when listening at home. The only complaint I have is that there is no manual. I had to figure out how towork the inputs and â€œshiftâ€ to the volume trim to adjust volume to best match to my preampâ€™s slope. Overall I am thrilled with the value and quality of the U12 and X12 together. (I have not listened to the X12 alone via its USB input.)

review_headline: Plays HI-RES audio and gapless playback.
review_body:
On this review I decided to concentrate on the not so obvious side of the NR636.
Been running some tests with it and here is what I found:
Buffering is awesome as it plays back 24/192 HI-RES audio files straight from USB sticks and straight from external WD 1TB USB Hard drives without any hiccups.

But this is what I really liked: if the playlist has gapless songs like Pink Floyd the Wall , or Pink Floyd DSOTM, it will play them back the way they were meant to be heard with no gaps in between. Also tested the amp's built-in WIFI playing back 24/192 tracks and did not pause or hesitate at all (than again the signal strength of my WIFI was in the upper nineties - not sure what will happen on crappier WIFI signal strength ). I made sure my DLNA server was not down-converting them to 24/92 or CD audio as that would have messed up the test.
This streaming was tested with Foobar2000 DLNA server running on Win XP.

I would suggest If you get hiccups and pauses in streaming HI-RES audio through WIFI because maybe your signal is bad or slow WIFI, put your songs on a USB hard drive instead.

I like this AMP a lot.

product_title: HyperPS - Bluetooth Mini Super Bass Speaker - Supporting Micro SD Card/USB Thumb Drive slots & Microphone for Phone call
review_body:
This is a good inexpensive Bluetooth speaker. The added LED light show might be really cool or it might be annoying. The controls are weird and take a lot of time to understand. And it uses an old miniUSB port to charge.

There are a lot of these small can style speakers around - maybe a dozen, all with different brand names, some have slightly different speaker grills. Essentially they are all the same sound and function (I've tested so many of them I lost count a long time ago). They all have the exact same annoying controls and the loud Asian female voice that tells you what the speaker is doing (oh some do mute that annoyance, HyperPS keeps the voice).

The sound is not bad for a $20 speaker. The product picture of the ground smashing bass is not anywhere near accurate. Yes there is some vibration out of this speaker - it does have some low end, but it won't break anything (you have to buy Beats to do that). Lyrics are intelligible. Music sounds reasonably good. This works in a small room for a couple of people, it is not a party box. As a travel speaker it works well.

The speaker design is the same on all the other cans - it has a just over 1 inch Mylar cone long throw speaker. The design is a sealed enclosure - that's a really good thing when paired with a fairly powerful amplifier. From the clear plastic ring / control round up is speaker enclosure. I've taken these apart and have seen the insides.

HyperPS added something that will make you smile or annoy you - two rings of LED lights. Just above the controls and surrounding the speaker grill are two clear acrylic rings. When the speaker is turned on there is a constantly changing colored light show. Now this would super cool if it responded to the music, or you could choose color modes. No, it just changes color constantly, no way to turn it off or change the light show.

Why are the controls so annoying? When you turn this on, the Asian lady yells "Brutooth mode" and then there is a chime. Once you pair this with your phone the speaker beeps. When you press the mode button to change inputs, she yells "Auto ---- something something" can't understand her - yes it is Aux input. The next press gets even more yelling, "Radiant mode" - which is FM radio (yes this has an FM radio built in that is virtually impossible to use). And then finally back to "Brutooth mode". If you have a MicroSD card inserted, I think she stops at that mode also.

The volume on the lady shouting is so loud and can't be changed.

Pairing is just like any other Bluetooth device - touch BT-Speaker on your phone Bluetooth settings and the two pair. When you power the speaker back on, if your phone is on and Bluetooth enabled, the two will pair.

The controls are what annoy me so much - there are four tiny buttons. Mode is already discussed. The - and + buttons advance the track with a short press, and change the volume with a long press and hold. The volume does change slowly, so you can make the adjustment. product_title: Samsung BP96-01472A Replacement Lamp w/Housing 6,000 Hour Life & 1 Year Warranty
review_headline: Works just about how I thought it would for the price.
review_body:
I installed this bulb on my TV in September and it has been working ever since. It doesn't come with any instructions but installation was easy since it's already in the housing. Just take the panel off the rear of the tv, unscrew and slide the old one out, put the new one in and tighten everything up again. MAKE SURE not to touch the bulb directly. The oils on your hands can make it burn out.

So here's the 4 star rating. When my old original bulb was going out, the set would randomly shut off two or three times before the bulb warmed up and it stayed on. One day it didn't turn on and I knew the gig was up. This bulb has done the random shut off a couple of times since I got it (although it only does it once and it's only happened a couple of times when the bulb was already warm). I'm not overly concerned about it though and if anything happens to it I'll post a follow up.

Overall for me this option works, is cheaper than the name brand alternative and much cheaper than a new TV. One other thing, if you're looking to get max life out of the bulb consider turning down the brightness in your setting menu.

product_title: Bluedio R+ Legend Deep Bass Bluetooth Wireless Headphones with Mic & Micro SD Card Slot(Titanium)
review_headline: Simply the best deal around. I've tried lots of hifi headphones. , these cans destroy the competition.
review_body:
Once again, I'm intensely happy with the all around price, sound quality, and build of this headset. I love the idea of a universal wireless music playing apparatus.

What's in the box: Well of course the headset itself. Both a well sized usb and auxiliary cable. Well detailed instruction booklet, and a silky smooth drawstring bag for your cans. Nice box as well with magnet clasp enclosure.

Build: Very solid design. Very similar to the early beats models. The ear pads are pleather, but are well designed, and keep lots of sound in. I like the strength of the sliders, very nice clicks. Not a huge fan of the branding, a little too much. The color for the titanium style is probably the best of the the three. (if your wondering, the r+ legend model and the r+ model are the same, only difference is the nice metallic color) oh and don't forget it's 32gb SD card compatable, and supports most lossless audio types as well as more common types.

Sound quality: If you like strong bass signature, clear mids and highs, and really want to hear every little nuance in your music, these should be your choice.(if your looking for good wired quality, these are not the choice without an amp.) I'm listening to Tycho on these headphones while writing this review. It's like I've never heard these songs before. If you're an audiophile, and can't afford Shure, this is the way to go. (metal/rock also sounds awesome)
So to wrap it all up, I'll just say these headphones have stolen my ears. Be using these for a long time.

product_title: Bose Bluetooth Headset Series 2
review_body: I've had the Series 2 for a little over a year. I work remotely and it was very important to me that my client be able to hear me clearly and I them. I tried a couple different headsets (wired and wireless) and this is easily the best. Even when I was driving in my car, the client did not hear any car or road noise...just my voice. Another headset caused problems when I didn't shave (they could hear my whiskers scratching the mic), but not the Bose. 3 different sized ear tips come with it. I found I could use the medium, but the largest felt more secure. The headset is very lite and small. I hold my phone in my hand, so folks walking by won't think I am talking to myself. The best part....after a year (and 9 days) I started having trouble with the headset not taking a charge. Even though I was 9 days out of warranty, Bose took it back and gave me a new one. I shipped it to them on a Tuesday ($10) and received the new one Thursday. All new packaging and warranty! I've bought things from Bose before this, and will buy more things from them in the future!

product_title: Sound Bar Red
review_body: Having used several other BT Speakers, this one stands out for build quality and sound. The TT-Sk02 came nicely packaged with the speaker, Micro USB cable for charging, AUX cord for a wired connection, 3.7 Li-ion 1500mAh removable battery, and of course the manual. The controls are very simple on top with an ON/OFF switch on the back. TaoTronics really thought ahead and put a couple pads on the bottom of the speaker to reduce vibration and provide better sound quality. Pairing the BT 3.0 was as simple as it gets. When using with a phone the the music or content playing will pause and enable you to answer the call with a push of the button located on top. You will need to be relatively close to the TT-SK02 for the built in Mic to pick up your voice so the other person can hear you clearly when on a call. Range on this little speaker was outstanding, I still had flawless connection from the phone and speaker being in separate medium size rooms. This is a very impressive Dual Cone Portable Wireless BT Speaker from TaoTronics!!!

product_title: Foxnovo F08 8-Slots Li-ion Ni-MH Ni-CD Universal Intelligent Battery Charger with LED Indicators, 5V USB Output & US-Plug Power Adapter (Black)
review_headline: Great size capacity and flexibility, but not the best choice for Li-ion
review_body:
Overall, this is a decent 8-bay charger that handles pretty much any type of battery you can throw at it. I've used it for AA and AAA Ni-MH batteries, and a variety of Li-ion sizes (18350, 18490, 18650 and 26650). However, the build quality of the sliders is just so-so, and it does not have an ideal charging profile for Li-ion cells.

The charger comes complete with a power adapter for a wall socket. I like that it uses an inline transformer rather than a \\"wall wart,\\" so it doesn't block adjacent outlets on a power strip.

The build quality of the charger frame is pretty good. It's plastic, but has a decent heft to it. The metal sliders (which are spring-loaded) are a bit fussy on about Â½ of the bays. This mainly affects putting in large batteries, such as 26650s, in that the slider sticks rather than move down smoothly.

On the plus side, the bays are sized so that you can put 26650s side by side without any problem. Each bay has a charge level indicator (a 3-segment LED) so you can keep tabs on charge rate.

It worked very well with Ni-MH batteries, charging them quickly. I used a multimeter to test the batteries after charging and they all came off at 1.5v, right where they should. Li-ions, however, were metering at 4.23 to 4.25 off the charger. That's a little high - my Pila and Xtar chargers shut off just shy of 4.2v (usually around 4.18). An occasional slight overcharge won't be a problem, but for long-term Li-ion battery health, a charger with a better charging profile would be a better choice. Four bay chargers can be had at this price point from Pila and Xtar.

While I can't give this a strong recommendation for Li-ion use, it is a good choice if you need a large capacity charger for NiMH cells. That's going to be my main use for this - I run through AA batteries quickly in photo gear, and having 8 bays is a lot more convenient than 2 or 4 bay chargers. I'd give it 5 stars as a NiMH charger, 3 stars as a Li-ion, so an overall rating of 4 stars.

product_title: iHome iDL100 Lightning Dock Triple Charging FM Clock Radio with USB Charge/Play
review_body:
I've had this alarm clock/dock for a few months now, and I am really happy with it. I got it primarily so I could charge both my iPhone and iPad at the same time, and it does that perfectly. Unfortunately, with the case I have on my iPad, I can't simply pop it on the second lightning connector in the back - there are two little rubber nubs on either side of the connector for the iPad to rest on when it's connected, and they're in the way when the case is on. So I either have to remove the case, or use a lightning cable and the USB port on the back of the clock in order to charge. It's a minor annoyance, but not that big of a deal for me. The case I have for my iPhone doesn't really come around the bottom, so it doesn't interfere at all.

I love that I can set the alarm via the iHome app on my iPhone or iPad - it's more intuitive than having to fiddle with a bunch of buttons on an alarm clock. Also, the iHome app allows you to ensure that the time on the clock is always accurate - it syncs up to the time on your phone when you dock it.

The sound quality is surprisingly good. Definitely better than I was expecting from an alarm clock - I actually use this as a true speaker dock when I'm doing work around the house, and it works nicely. Clear, loud sound, no distortion. It's not a super high-end speaker, obviously, but it definitely does the trick.

All in all, this was a great purchase. It does everything I need it to do, and it does it all as well or better than I expected! I'd definitely recommend this product!

product_title: Sennheiser Digital Wireless Headphones
review_body: My research for wireless headphones brought me to these cans.  I'm a moderate audiophile.  I use them late at night or whenever I want to watch TV and do not want to disturb others.  The sound is contained within the headphones, and I like the range - I can walk around the house and there's no sound degradation because of distance.  Although these are plug'n'play and were very easy to setup, maybe I need to adjust something - when there is no dialogue or the sound of silence, and then dialogue starts back up, at that instant, I can hear the background transmission hiss.  Maybe it's my fault, maybe it's just how the Kleer Technology works, but it's there, but it's not a deal-breaker for me.  The entirety of my ear fits within the circular padding, nothing pinches, no odd-placed pressure points on my ears or from the padding on top of my head - very comfortable to wear for hours.  Sure the buttons on the right can are indistinguishable from each other, but I never use them because I control TV volume with the TV remote instead.  I tried the bass boost and surround buttons once, and both effects stink, I don't use them ever.  But using a straight signal and no effects, these headphones produce clean low bass, crispy highs, and you can turn them up very high without distortion.  I have been using them for about three months with no problems, and don't anticipate any either.  Love these headphones.

product_title: Wharfedale - Diamond 220 (Black)
review_body: Very pleased with these speakers.  They are an excellent value proposition.  I bought them straight from music direct and I have them paired with a NAD D3020, which I also got at MD.  The two go very well together and the NAD has no trouble at all driving them in my medium/large room.  Since I'm not an audio reviewer it's difficult for me to articulate why I like these speakers so much, and I don't just want to regurgitate a bunch of stuff I've read in speaker reviews.  With that said, these speakers are pretty tonally neutral.  Highs are pleasant, not harsh at all.  The midrange is also very pleasing to my ears.  Low end is very satisfactory to me, but I'm sure others would want to pair this with a sub.  I've noticed that these speakers have no trouble resolving recordings with lots of bass  In fact, like all good speakers, these sound best with good records, but they are more than fair to lesser quality records.  One cool thing about the 220's is that they have a downward firing bass port and this means they can be placed pretty close to a wall, which helps bass response.  Vocal clarity is the one thing that really jumps out at me with these speakers.  The vocals are crisp and right in the middle of the soundstage.  TV dialogue also has the same vocal clarity.  Overall a great set of speakers.

review_headline: At last a small speaker that has exceptional sound
review_body:
I received this as a free review sample. I tend to rate high, but in the case of this speaker the sound quality earns it my highest rating. If you stumble across my other reviews of speakers I am usually clinical in my description and refrain from gushing.

Here is why I truly love this speaker. At the top of the list is sound quality. I expected the rich mid range and fuller highs because a lot of the newer speakers on the market exhibit those characteristics. What I did not expect is the fuller, more natural bass. Most modern speakers in this form factor either have somewhat anemic bass, or the design is biased towards the low end and it sounds artificial when playing music that is not bass centric. This speaker plays acoustic jazz with a very full and natural sound where the bass is where it should be in the mix. For more modern music where the bass is in your face, this speaker reproduces that as well.

It's tempting to compare this to a Bose, but since I only have an older Bose the comparison is probably not valid. I will say that this is one of the most balanced speakers I have ever tested in this small form factor. In fact, it sounds as good as some of my 10\\" powered speakers that have integrated bluetooth (but, of course, not as loud.)

Since there are ample product specs and some other reviews that cover the physical characteristics as well as compare this to a previous model I will not bore you with additional babble. Suffice to say that if sound quality is important this is a speaker that I highly recommend.

product_title: Polk Audio OWM5 Multi-Purpose Home Theater Speaker (Black)
review_body: These speakers state they are right-center-left speakers, to go with the OWM3s as the satellite speakers. I skipped the OWM3s and bought four OWM5s. Originally, they were everything but the center in my 5.1 set-up, but I have since relegated them to satellite speakers after my home theater upgrade to 7.1. They are fantastic! I have 12 AWG wires feeding them. The first night I hooked them up (in the 5.1 set-up), my wife and I watched a tropical television show. I heard the wind blowing under the dialogue! I had to rewind the program a couple of times just to verify that the sound was coming from the show and not real life. There's no reason why these couldn't stay right-center-left speakers for consumers on a budget, or if you want to go to eleven like me, send them to the surround positions to supplement something even bigger up front.

review_body:

The DJ mode allows multiple devices to be connected at once and share which one is using the speaker. Unlike normal blue tooth mode, up to 5 devices can connect at once. Only devices make you disconnect before someone else can connect.

Overall I really like this speaker. I like the sound and the controls. I do not like their choice to not use USB to charge it. That was a mistake.

Notes:
- Does not charge with USB. Needs external charger.
- The speaker controls your device. Volume up and down as well as pause.

product_title: X-Mini II XAM4-B Portable Capsule Speaker, Mono
review_headline: 6 Months in the Rain and Still Going Strong!
review_body:
Hello Everyone!

I'm from Hawaii; the North Shore, and about 6 months ago I was hiking in the jungle/tropical forest. I was carrying a backpack that was stuffed to the brim. The top two zippers were loose and about 20 minutes into the hike I noticed things falling out of my bag... I turned around and was able to find everything except for my Apple IPod Shuffle (and Ear Buds) and my X-Mini Speaker (Black with Red Top). Both were in the same little black bag (a soft cloth bag that comes for the X-Mini Speaker). I searched for maybe 1-2 hours, couldn't find them, and decided to head back home. Within about a week, I had already purchased another IPod and Speaker (same types and brands for each).

About 6 months later, a friend of mine was bushwhacking and came accross an IPod and Speaker in a little black bag (unaware that I had lost them). By chance he was talking to my Dad about it. He made the connection, and I promptly got my IPod and Speaker back (today in fact!).
(Side Note: What are the odds of all that coming together?!?!?)

The X-Mini Speaker STILL had battery and was working perfectly (in fact, my mom couldn't tell which speaker was which [between my old and new one]). The IPod battery was dead. I charged it, and both are now working perfectly. In fact I'm listening to music from the IPod and Speaker right now.

I'd like to point out a couple of things:

- Where I live, it rains A LOT!!! The little black bag wouldn't have stopped the rain AT ALL!!! The IPod and Speaker were completely drenched at least 50 times in that 6 month period.

- Things in Hawaii rust quickly because of the high humidity level; neither item has any hint of rust on it...

- Both the Speaker and IPod look completely new (I even wrote a little 'N' on one of the IPod's so that I could tell the IPod's apart).

- Both the Speaker and IPod work perfectly as they did the day that I lost them.

Besides all that:

Speaker - Absolutely amazing... Exactly what it appears and is advertised to be; a portable, powerful, durable speaker, good quality speaker.

IPod Shuffle - Undeniably Spectacular - Precisely what it looks like and is said to be; an easy-to-travel-with, strong, well-lasting, well-made IPod :)

I'm posting this same review in 3 places (for the IPod Shuffle, the X-Mini Speaker, and the newer X-Mini Speaker).

Incredible products. I will definitely be recommending these products and returning if they ever break (which I doubt will happen :)

Thanks for Reading!

review_headline: Perfect Solution for my Poorly Designed Monitor
review_body:
I don't know which annoyed me more, the fact that anyone would even make a monitor without a VESA mount or that I didn't notice my monitor of choice wasn't VESA compliant prior to purchase, resulting in the need for a VESA adaptor kit.

After researching similar type adapters that ranged from insanely over priced to reasonably priced but flimsy design, I ordered this adapter from EasyMount and crossed my fingers.

My HP 22bw monitor has a slightly curved back so I was concerned about fit since they recommend a flat surface. One of the reasons I ordered this adapter was because of the turned up feet at the end of the brackets, which I hoped would cradle my monitor a bit more securely due to that curve.

Installation was a breeze, even though I had to fiddle with the bracket positioning and angle of those feet just a bit in order to compensate for my hump backed monitor. Once the adapter was affixed, I was able to attach my monitor to its new home on my dual mount where it has articulated its way through a full range of motion without a slip, wobble or slightest inclination of insecurity.

In an ideal world monitors would all have VESA mounts but if I ever find myself in a similar mountless situation...I would gladly purchase this adaptor again.

Looking at W50 box, you are greeted with an outer sleeve featuring a high-res image of Westone new W-series 5-driver IEM on the front of the packaging. The look of the cover has the same layout as W40 but "W" logo is now in silver and there is a "Signature Series" label above the model number; exactly the same as in W60 packaging except featuring a silver plate instead of copper. On the back and the sides of the sleeve you have a detailed description of the design, accessories, and tech specs. You definitely get an in-depth picture of what awaits you inside. With an outer sleeve off, you are presented with a premium soft touch magnetic cover inner box which contains headphones and plethora of the accessories.

I have to admit, the amount and the quality of included custom accessories is very impressive for the first time Westone customer, but it could leave you a bit disappointed if you are upgrading to W50 from any of their lower model, even as basic as a single driver W10, since there is no premium accessory distinction. Seems that with accessories Westone made a conscious decision where every W-series customer can feel special, either if you spent $200 for their single driver or $1k for their 6-driver pair of headphones, with nearly an identical package including their 5 patented pairs of Star silicone eartips, 5 pairs of True-Fit foam eartips, 3 sets of interchangeable color faceplates, mini monitor-vault case, and 2 sets of Epic audio and MFI G2 smartphone cables with mmcx connectors.

I already mentioned in my previous reviews that I believe Westone has a definite advantage over other IEM manufacturers because they have been in audio business for over 55 years and have a full catalog of not only professional audio but also hearing protection products. As a result, donâ€™t expect to find a typical generic S/M/L eartips or a pair of Comply tips in a plastic bag. With a color coded marked stems, Star silicone tips are designed with multiple flex-zones and have 5 pairs in different length, shape, and size. The same with True-Fit foam tips, you get 5 pairs with color coded stems and shapes similar to Star tips. Their foam density has a medium recovery property - not too soft or too firm. You also get a cleaning tool with a small metal loop to clean inside of a narrow nozzle or eartip stems, and a pelican style small â€œvaultâ€ storage case. This case is OK to use with included thin flexible cable, but if you decide to go with a thicker aftermarket cable â€“ you will need to step up to a bigger case.

As part of their W-series â€œconsumerâ€ appeal, Westone also adds an option of customizable interchangeable faceplates. With W50, the same as W60, they made faceplate colors different from other lower models, giving Signature Series a more premium look with included red/silver/copper metallic finish plates. Plates are actually plastic but have a metal color finish which still keeps it lightweight and durable without adding extra weight to the shell. Also, with an included small screwdriver tool they are very easy to take off and secure back on, and you donâ€™t have to worry about losing a screw which stays with a faceplate. One important thing to note, Westone is updating their cover plate design to include a model number instead of just â€œWâ€. New cover plates will not be backward compatible with old plates and new W-series design doesnâ€™t work with old plates either. This is just a cosmetic change, nothing else is affected.

Included removable cables give you an option of either audio only Epic twisted cable or MFI G2 cable with in-line remote for smartphones. Epic cable is thin, lightweight, and flexible, with ultra low resistance tensile wire design reinforced with aramid fiber. For a stock cable it actually has a decent audio performance. G2 cable has a more robust rounded shielding, still soft and flexible, and comes with in-line remote/mic. Though multi-function button is OS independent and can be used for Play/Pause/Call, the volume up/down buttons are for iOS only operation. Westone offers a similar cable (Android version) with universal remote where volume buttons are removed to eliminate the confusion. In my opinion, the remote could be smaller and I would keep it universal with a single multi-function button covering both Android and iOS smartphones. Personally, Iâ€™m a big fan of aftermarket audio cables, such as pure silver or pure copper, but they do come at a premium price and heavier weight. Either way, removable cable option is a big plus and gives you flexibility of future upgrades.

One thing you do have to keep in mind, something a lot of people donâ€™t realize, is about the profile of Westone mmcx connectors. It is true that Westone uses common mmcx type, but these have slightly shorter length, not a standard size. As a result, you can use any mmcx based universal cable with Westone (new W-series or UM-series) IEMs, but you will not be able to use their Epic or G2 cable with other mmcx connector based IEMs, such as those from UE, JVC, Fidue, and others. For that reason, when you are looking into replacement custom cables, I would recommend to specify universal mmcx connector rather than Westone specific connector.

When it comes to a design, Westone bean-shaped shells are among the most comfortable universal fit IEMs I have tested. I think itâ€™s another example of how they have an advantage over competition while drawing from a pool of their knowledge and experience of designing ergonomic hearing protection products. These headphone shells have a very stick and lightweight rounded design, and the most important - they stay the same size regardless of driver config, with an exception of W10/W20 being slightly smaller. Westone model index is based on a number of drivers, where W10 or UM Pro 10 correspond to a single BA driver, while 20/30/40/50/60 represent upto 6 BA drivers per shell. It's quite possible they take advantage of combined BA driver modules to reduce number of components, and I can confirm there is no difference in size or shape going from 4-driver W40 to 5-driver W50 or 6-driver W60.

Unlike UM Pro series offered in clear and smoke translucent shells, W-series is non-transparent, made out of black lightweight durable plastic, and customizable with interchangeable faceplates that come handy when you mix the colors to distinguish L/R sides, perhaps using Red plate on a right side. Thatâ€™s how I have it on W40, but I stayed with a default silver color on W50 which still has a premium look and distinguishes itself from W60. Another point to make, something that already came up in questions after my W40 review, the shell joint around mmcx connector housing is not cracked! Some people freak out and go into panic mode thinking they applied too much force when disconnecting the cable, causing it to crack, while in reality itâ€™s just a joint gap intended by a design.

The shape and fitment of Westone IEMs is not symmetrical, so there is no confusion which piece goes into which ear, and for further guidance faceplates also have a large L/R letter for a better id. The wire fitment is always over the ear, itâ€™s very comfortable and produces no microphonics even when cable is rubbing against your cloth. There is no visible pinhole port to let the air in/out of the shell, while sound still remains relatively spacious. Nozzle is very narrow, build sturdy despite being thin, corresponds to T100 Comply size, and I never experienced a problem of leaving an eartip behind when earpieces removed from my ears, though I do have to admit I typically use the largest size tips.

Before I dive into sound analysis, I would like to mention a few things about eartips. I have come across a number of sound impressions and even brief reviews with people using eartips installed by default. There is a very good reason why Westone includes so many unique eartips bundled with their accessories. Go through different pairs (tip-rolling), study how it affects the sound, and spend more than a minute to figure out the comfort - experiment and you will not believe a sound difference!!! Especially with Westone IEMs and particularly W50, selection of the correct eartip size is VERY crucial in sound shaping. Ensuring a proper seal of your ear canal opening will guarantee the best sound balance, and at the same time â€“ the level of seal will control the amount of bass bloat.

With a proper eartip and cable selection out of the way, now here comes a sound analysis of W50.

It has a warm smooth lush sound, very similar to W60, but with a more noticeable low end emphasis and even thicker lower mids. I'm still on the fence if bass spills a bit into lower mids or were they [lower mids] tuned like this. This low end emphasis makes sound geared more toward V-shaped signature (maybe even borderline L-shaped). Soundstage has a good level of width and depth, but due to thicker sound the layering and separation is not at their best. This also affects imaging where sound can get a bit congested in more complex song passages. But all this put together is actually not a negative comment since the intention of these IEMs are NOT to be analytical detailed headphones but rather Audiophile Basshead in-ear monitors!

Low end has a great extension down to a textured layer of sub-bass, followed by a mid-bass boost with a smooth slower attack and a longer decay. Even with such enhanced bass, I wouldn't call it bloated, but rather warm and rounded.

Midrange has a thick warm lower mids that give a lot of body to a sound, and together with low end they do overpower spectrum balance a bit, taking away from some upper mids clarity. Upper mids have a lot of similarity with W60, but they feel a bit recessed due to V-shaped sound sig nature.

Treble is also very similar to W60, where itâ€™s smooth and clear, but has an early roll off. You will never experience sibilance or fatigue listening to W50, the warm lush sound stays throughout entire frequency range.

Itâ€™s really hard to describe W50 without constantly referencing W60; these two actually have a lot of similarities. In a summary:

W50 vs W60 - W60 adds a little more definition in upper mids which are also slightly brighter. With a little more brightness, sound perception is more expanded as well. In comparison, W60 upper mids are a little more forward. The biggest difference is in mid-bass boost where sub-bass is nearly the same, but W50 has a higher quantity of mid-bass boost which spills a little into lower mids (still flip-flopping on this one). As a result, a sound is more V-shaped (borderline L-shaped), with mids (and vocals/details) taking a step back in favor of a more predominant bass boost. W50 upper mids still have plenty of clarity, just a touch less details in comparison to W60.

Through experimentation I found 3dB cut around 125kHz to bring mid-bass under control. This was an interesting discovery since it brought W50 sound so much closer to W60. This way with EQ adjustment you can either have a more powerful bass or a more tamed balanced sound signature. But even in pop songs or slower tracks where there is not too much bass - mids were shining as much as they do in W60, except I found lower mids to be a bit thicker, adding a bit more warmth and body to a sound. But once you dive into a bass heavy or bass-drum pounding track â€“ hold on to your seat and enjoy the Basshead ride!

Conclusion.

I will try to be brief and to the point in my summary. It is very important to understand W50 sound signature and their bass-dominant tuning. Some people might have misconception they are dealing with 5-driver IEM that going to deliver crystal clear sound with analytical details.If thatâ€™s what you are after - W50 is NOT for you. W50 is Audiophile quality Basshead IEMs that require a proper setup in order to make them shine. If you want a smooth and more laid back balanced sound, go for W60. If you want faster and more aggressive sound with more mid-bass punch, go for UM Pro 50. But if you are craving a smooth sound with a more dominant mid-bass impact, warmer mids, and a fun signature - W50 is calling your name to start pounding on your eardrums!!!

product_title: Omaker M4 Portable Speakers
review_body:
I purchased the Omaker Bluetooth Speaker to improve the pathetically low volume that comes out of my ultra-thin laptop. To be clear, at a $35 price point, I was not expecting miracles from this thing, but I figured I'd give it a try. I am VERY happy that I did! I bought this primarily to use in the shower, because I like to listen to music or watch an episode of something when I am in the shower (clear shower curtain). This was impossible on my new laptop without something to boost the volume, and since this is waterproof... perfect fit. After trying it out, I like it enough that I now use it, instead of my Bluetooth headphones, all over my apartment.

PROS:
- Waterproofing: Flawless so far (been using it every day for the last 3 weeks). I was initially concerned, because the rubber panel that covers the power and audio jacks is not super tight, but it gets the job done. NOTE: This speaker is NOT meant to be submerged! I place it on a shelf, outside the direct flow of the shower - it ends up absolutely soaked, but I would never try actually putting it under water.

- Sound quality: Ridiculously good for the size and price. As other reviewers have mentioned, this thing DOES actually produce bass frequencies. They are not going to shake your eyeballs, but they do shake the crap out of the speaker case, which is fairly amusing. The highs are crisp enough, and the balance between bass and treble is such that the bass does not noticeably distort the upper frequencies, even at full volume. AS LONG AS you purchase this with reasonable expectations, you will be very satisfied with the sound quality (this is a SMALL speaker, not a 12 inch subwoofer or a Bose surround system).

- Battery Life: The battery life on this thing is crazy. READ THE DIRECTIONS when you get it, and follow the instructions for the first 2 charges, and it will easily meet the 12 hour promised life. I have actually only charged this twice since I gotit (after the initial charge), so averaging less than once a week, and I'm using it quite a lot around my apartment, generally. I haven't been keeping track, but I wouldn't be surprised if I have gotten at LEAST 16 hours out of each charge.

- Size: Obviously, the size of the speaker (case is maybe 3 1/2 inches wide/high) is going to limit things like volume and sound quality, but the size is also a benefit, because the speaker is very portable. Small enough to sit on the edge of my laptop and be carried around like it's on a plate, as I move from room to room. Also, none of the contact surfaces are hard plastic (all have a very slightly soft, non-slip texture to them), so it doesn't slide off easily.

NEUTRAL:
- Sound Volume: I usually have the sound volume on my laptop and the speaker maxed, but it IS loud enough to hear clearly over the noise of the shower, and I actually have a fair amount of hearing loss - for the average person, this speaker will still not be LOUD, but WILL be loud enough. I can leave it in one room and move to the next, and still hear TV dialog, for instance.

- Bluetooth range: Is about what you would expect. Clear line of sight it can hit 25 feet without problems. Going through walls and other electronic equipment degrades the signal, but that's to be expected.

CONS:
- As one other reviewer mentioned, the instructions explicitly state that you should not leave it plugged in for more than 12 hours. I don't know what will happen if you do - battery damage: possibly. Potentially bursting into flames? Er... *probably* not... right? Somebody would have written about that if it'd happened. But since I am aware of the possibility, I just plug it in and stick it in the bathroom sink overnight - that way I have to unplug it in the morning, and even if it melts down, it can't do any damage to anything. Just don't run water over it when it's plugged in... (duh :-)

product_title: Omaker M4 Portable Speakers
review_headline: Best speaker I have ever purchased.
review_body:
What can I say? This little thing exceeded all of my expectations.

It is exactly as it is pictured and if I had to roughly describe the size, it is very close to the size of a standard leather wallet (for men) and obviously a bit thicker, roughly twice as think as my wallet. The build is so durable. I feel very confident that I could drop this thing from ten feet and let it continue playing music. I have not tested the plash resistance but I never really find myself in situations where I am in water and need music (I shower for work at 6am so I am not exactly in a song mood at that point). The only issue from this is that the buttons are tough to use. They take some decent pressure and many functions require you to hold the button. If you have arthritis or a weaker grip (like children or the elderly) it could be a problem but I think for most people it will just be a slight misfortune.

The big draw in this is the sound. Holy hand grenade is the sound on this thing phenomenal. When at max volume this thing is louder than the old set of PC speakers I bought for $50 in 2007. Seriously, you could use this to play music for a room full of people. It has solidi bass despite that I don't see any option to alter it and there is about a half second delay from any device you have attached through Bluetooth (by the way, the Bluetooth works fantastically, fast and reliable connection). I haven't had any reason to test the connection distance of the device but my living room is at least 30 feet (I am guessing probably close to 40) and it has never faltered at that distance.

I highly recommend this speaker if you want something durable, or loud, or of good quality, or portable, or all of the above.

product_title: iGadgitz Al Series Bluetooth Speakers [The Cube]
review_headline: Very Small Speaker with Great Sound
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:3bdd17778455ef097fcffb1d018022b6]] There is a good variance in Bluetooth speakers, from physical design, extras in the box and sound quality. Not all speakers are worth your time and money. This little Cube speaker by iGadgitz is a very interesting speaker; it may be little but it has big sound and it works very well. I did find one potential issue when it comes to the range of operation that I will describe below.

This is one of the smallest speakers I have seen and used. In spite of its size, it is a solid and hefty little speaker, weighing more than you'd expect. In my mind this is a good sign: it means that there is more to this little speaker than a cheap little speaker and a sub-par receiver. To be honest I was a little skeptical that it would put out good sound when I first saw this speaker. It has pleasantly surprised me (more on that shortly).

This speaker pairs and connects very easily. When it is in discoverable mode it identifies itself as \\"Xquare 2\\". I had no issue with it pairing to my phone and once connected it remained connected without issue.

The range on this speaker is good and I have been able to carry it from the source to a distance between 20' - 30' before it began to stutter or cut out. I have seen speakers that have more range but the majority of them fall into this threshold. Now, that said I need to mention an issue that came up in testing that should be kept in mind. If the speaker is sitting such that the switch and controls are facing down (that is, the control side is on the flat surface where it is sitting) the range is cut very dramatically. With the speaker sitting that way the range dropped to about 6' before it started cutting out. It did not seem to matter if it was the speaker that was moving away from the source or the other way around.

I loaded up some music and played it through this speaker and was pleased with the outcome. The speaker has no problem with playing at higher volume, without distortion or \\"washing out\\". The profile is very good too - the bass is strong and slightly elevated but not overkill, the midrange is very good and the music has depth as a result, and the highs are bright and crisp. For such a small speaker, this one produces better-than-expected sound.
