product_title: Polk Audio AM6119-A Wireless Woodbourne Speaker - White
review_headline: I was severely disappointed by this speaker's performance (UPDATED)
review_body:
I am not, by predisposition, a negative person, and I hesitated before posting this review---my first "one star" Amazon review---but after giving the matter some additional thought---and particularly after interacting with Polk Audio tech support, I felt compelled to put my experience 'on the record.'
I purchased the Polk Audio AM6119-A Wireless Speaker a few days before Christmas. The product arrived promptly from Amazon and the packaging appeared sealed/pristine/undamaged. Unfortunately, after setting the speaker up, I was severely disappointed by the speaker's performance. In brief, except at extremely low volumes, the speaker's output was/is unacceptable: the speaker has significant distortion across all frequencies. The distortion was so severe I immediately contacted Polk Audio tech support, and briefly went through each of the technician's suggestions to reduce the distortion --- moving the speaker to different areas, playing music via the Bluetooth, USB and Auxiliary routes, using every possible equalizer setting (e.g. min/max bass, min/max treble, etc. etc.) ---- all to no avail. Making matters worse, two subsequent efforts to contact Polk tech support over the coming weeks went entirely unanswered, which I find unacceptable given this speaker's purchase price.
I enjoy listening to music and have pretty good stereo equipment, but I am by no means some elitist audiophile who seems to enjoy harshly critiquing equipment, recordings, etc. I have had a Bose Soundlink wireless speaker now for almost 18 months (I bought the Polk as an anticipated "upgrade") which still works fine (in all the same locations the Polk does not) and which I have now gone back to, because of my experience with the Polk. To be fair, I have scoured the internet and looked at many other reviews of this product; and while my experience seems to be unusual --- I have seen few criticisms of the speakers' distortion elsewhere --- my experience is what it is, and so I feel compelled to urge other potential buyers to exercise caution before buying this product.
*****Addendum 09/09/2015******
I have revised (upgraded) my review---I have significantly improved my rating, from one to four stars, based on my subsequent experience with this speaker.
After receiving some very helpful feedback from another owner (see "COMMENTS") I decided to give this speaker another try. In short, I played music on my iPad via Bluetooth almost constantly, but at varying volumes, over a period of about one week. To my shock/amazement, the (severe) distortion I noted after my first attempts to use the speaker began to subside. After approximately 30 - 40 hours of use, I had difficulty discerning any distortion, even at high volumes.

The bar that holds the headphones in place is padded and adjustable to ensure a comfortable fit for long periods of listening. The speakers swivel 180 degrees and tilt so that they cover the entire ear with soft pads that keep the speakers off of the ears while cancelling out background noise. The sound quality does not go down with phone calls either, the microphone is big and has excellent quality even when speaking softly. They come with a cord that can be used with any device if the Bluetooth battery is low or if the device does not have Bluetooth. This feature makes them ideal for people who have multiple older devices that would need a Bluetooth adapter. They come with Bluetooth 4.0 and have a thirty to forty foot range without sound loss or interruptions.

The three button design on both sides are evenly spaced and easy to use when they are in place with practice but it is always much easier to take them off and adjust them while looking at them.

Pairing is as simple as holding the power button on for three seconds to turn them on and then pressing and holding again to pair with your device. Once paired you can use the buttons on the device to navigate your music or go directly to your device whichever is easier.

product_title: 3 speed USB Turntable vinyl Record Player with Built-in Stereo Speakers and Dust Cover + convert your vinyl collection to digital with included software!!
review_headline: A Great Way to Get Good Recordings of Older Albums (or Just to Listen!)
review_body:
I'm so excited to have this turntable. I have a bunch of albums from my childhood that are not available anymore but I would love to share them with my children. My husband also has some rare albums that he would love to put on his iPod.

This was really easy to set up and start using. It has a built-in power cord and it comes with a removable USB cable. It will plug into any USB port on your computer. The turntable is adaptable to full size albums as well as 45s and it even comes with a 45 adapter to fit the middle peg. It's been a long time since I've seen them! The needle arm is secured for storage but when released, has a lifter that descends slowly for good placement.

The unit has a built-in amplifier for listening but the best feature is that you can record directly to your computer. It comes with software from Audacity to record and export your recordings. You need to download a .dll file (check carefully where you download it, you can search for the Audacity website and there is a link to a trusted (and free) site. When you export your file, you can label everything from artist, track, etc.

There is a volume control for playback on the turntable as well.

While this is not made of the highest quality materials (lots of plastic) it is not meant to be a high-end turntable replacement.

So if you are looking to do some reminiscing (as I have been) and transfer some old recordings in a moderately good quality, this is a great unit. I had to explain how it worked to my kids, who had never seen (or heard of) a turntable. Too funny.

Sample provided for review.

product_title: AUSDOM® M04 [Upgrade Version] Bluetooth Audio Streaming Stereo Headset Wireless / Wired Headphones with Microphone for Muti-Music and Hands-free Calling for iPhone/Android/PC Playback (Black)
review_headline: Attractive, comfortable, good sounding headphones for the money
review_body:
I've tested a lot of wired and wireless headphones recently. I have to say that the Ausdom Bluetooth Headphones are the best sub $50 phones I've tested so far. I tested both the M04 and the M06 models. Both are about the same, although the M06 sounds a tad bit better.

Both headphones have an attractive design and are solidly constructed. Adjusting the band for a comfortable fit was easy and smooth. The ear cups are comfortable, even during extended listening periods.

Set up was easy. Holding the power button for several seconds puts it in pairing mode, just the way you expect. The headphones connected to my Droid Turbo without any issues.

I like that both headphones have separate controls for volume, fast forward, and rewind. The controls are easy to find and easy to use while wearing the headphones.

Audio quality is really good. I tested the units with my favorite hip hop and R&B playlists. The bass levels were good. The sound remained solid even when I turned up the volume. I didn't experience any static or muddled audio. I thoroughly enjoyed listening to music with this unit.

Battery life has been great so far. I've used the headsets for a couple of days without recharging them.

Note that I didn't test making phone calls with the headphones.

While these headphones won't compete with headphones costing several hundred dollars, in the sub $50 range, the Ausdom headphones provide a compelling choice. Both units feature an attractive, comfortable design. Both units sound great and have a battery that lasts a long time. All in all I think these are really good Bluetooth headphones for the price. Definitely recommended. If they are at the same price, definitely opt for the M06 over the M04 as they sound a tad bit better. Both are excellent, however. Samples provided for review.

product_title: Casio Mens DBC310-1 Databank 300 Digital Watch (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: The Price Of "Old Faithful" Has Gone "Collectors Only"
review_body:
I have literally programmed my life around the Casio DBC310-1 Databank 300 Digital Watch and its lower watt predecessors for the past 30 years. I've used the Databank 300 model exclusively since the late 90's. I never forget passwords, telephone numbers, user ID's, membership numbers, PIN's, anniversaries, birthdays, haircuts, meetings or even Hallmark holidays, thanks to the EEPROM (programmable memory). I generally have about 15 to 20 of the memory "locations" available at any time and I program/re-program anytime I am waiting for something or someone. It's a great way to productively use downtime.

Quite to my personal amazement, I discovered Eddie Vedder of Pearl Jam wearing this watch or a smaller memory version on the Cameron Crowe directed "20" documentary of the first 20 years of Pearl Jam. Eddie is wearing the watch in both performance and non performance scenes in the film. I scratch my head and wonder what a singer/songwriter/guitarist creative person is doing with a "nerd special" watch, and curious to know how he used it during that period of time when he wore it - circa early to mid 90's.

Regrettably, with Casio's decision during the past 12-18 months to discontinue the product, availability has come at a premium. I "forced" my wife to buy my current watch as a Christmas present in 2009, finding it on Amazon for under $60 versus the current "collectors item" price at a 300% + markup. Given the keyboard/keys reputation for wearing out under regular thumbnail or other fingernail pressure/friction, I should have purchased a few more units to get me through to end of life. I'm on the second band for this watch, finding an exact fit virtual Casio OE band on Amazon a couple years ago.

I'm still equivocating about paying the $200 current seller's price, but then a good habit (programming to have all your important information on your wrist) is after all, "priceless".

product_title: Oroview Waterproof Stereo Bluetooth Shower Speaker and Speakerphone
review_headline: Very nice, moderately priced water-resistant bluetooth stereo speaker
review_body:
This is a very nice compact stereo speaker that has good water resistance and can easily be paired with a smart phone or other bluetooth device and used as an external speaker in the shower or outside, or really in just about any reasonable environment.

The water resistance is stated to be IPX6 here on the Amazon page, which is (in my opinion) very good. It can be deciphered as follows:

IPX6 Explanation:
-- IP - International Protection, standard for marking to classify the degree of protection against intrusion
-- X - first digit indicates degree of protection against solid particles, on a scale of 1 to 6 with 6 being the greatest degree of protection. This product has an 'X' which I assume means that they have not tested it for solid particle protection, which I think it probably ok since the water protection rating is good, but still I'm surprised they do not give a rating here.
-- 6 - second digit indicates liquid ingress protection, on a scale of 1 to 9. The 6 indicates protection against 'powerful water jets', requiring that water projected in powerful jets (12.5 mm nozzle) against the enclosure from any direction shall have no harmful effects, with a test duration of at least 3 minutes and specified water volume and pressure for the test.

Turning the speaker on or off is accomplished by holding down the power button and is confirmed by the speaker beeping.

I've used it in the shower and it has worked fine. The design of the case incorporates a hook which for my particular shower means I could hook it to the shower nozzle output which is fairly high on the shower wall and really higher than optimum for listening. It worked perfectly and was not affected by the moisture or water.

This speaker has a very good audio quality, with stereo since it has two speakers. Certainly it is considerably better than listening to something using the speakers build into most smart phones or tablets. The bluetooth profile used is not stated anywhere here on Amazon or in the information provided, and is probably a technical detail unnecessary for most users (see wiki article 'List of Bluetooth profiles' for explanation, if curious. For comparison, one other shower speaker I have is rated A2DP.)

It arrived at least partially charged but I plugged it into one of my USB chargers for long enough to make sure that it had a good full charge (a USB charging cord is included). It can be used while plugged in and charging (but should not be plugged into a charger when in a wet environment because it's necessary to open the rubber flap that otherwise seals the USB port from water intrusion). There is no indication provided as to when the battery is fully charged or what the remaining charge might be, which is a minor deficiency. I do like the fact that a rechargeable battery is part of the speaker and it will not require periodic battery replacement.

Instructions are included, clearly written.

When paired with my iPhone the volume of the speaker can be controlled both from the phone or using the controls on the speaker. The speaker also has controls to pause and start playback (if playing music files, for example), and for advancing to the next track or back to the previous track.

I will also point out that the volume ability of this speaker is very good. It has the ability to produce a louder sound than some other bluetooth speakers, probably a reflection of the larger size of the speakers and perhaps the amplifier, or possibly even the battery capability. Whatever the reason, it does play loud enough to hear reasonably well in the shower and with a fairly high level of water noise.

The speaker can also be used to answer phone calls when paired with a phone - an incoming call will automatically interrupt anything playing on the speaker, and the controls can be used to answer the call, or hang up when complete. The most recentphone number can also be redialed from the speaker, and voice dialing can be used with the speaker if the phone has that capability. I haven't fully exercised all of these capabilities and they would require a bit of familiarization, but everything I did attempt to do worked perfectly.

The only display provided is a small blue LED located on the front of the speaker. It blinks continuously while paired and in use.

According to the provided instructions, it can also be used as a power bank to charge other USB devices. That's a very clever feature although nothing is provided to indicate what the battery capacity is. I haven't tried using it to recharge a phone so I can't say how worthwhile this feature is.

Warranty statement is stated on the packaging as a one year limited warranty and a product support e-mail is provided on the package if the company needs to be contacted.

Long term durability and particularly resistance to water intrusion will only be known over time. If I find anything of note as I use this speaker, I will return and update this review.

The packaging for this speaker is very nice. It comes in a professionally designed and well done heavy box, and the quality of the packaging would make this particularly suitable for gift use.

My overall impression is very positive. I like the size and appearance of this speaker. It looks to be very well made and I like the styling. Functionally everything described above worked perfectly for me and there was no difficulty in pairing it with my iPhone or learning to use the features of the speaker. I think this is a good choice, would make a very nice gift, and it's reasonably priced for the size and features.

product_title: Denon DHT-S514 Home Theater Soundbar System with HDMI, Bluetooth Streaming and Wireless Subwoofer
review_headline: BEWARE: this is hazardous material and cannot be returned
review_body:
Every shopper should be aware of the return policy that applies this item.

We were disappointed to learn that we could not return this Denon. Amazon wrote to me: "Due to safety reasons, we cannot accept the return of any hazardous materials at any of our fulfillment centers; this includes but is not limited to items that are flammable, gas-powered or use propane or natural gas, have rechargeable batteries or contain powerful magnets". Apparently the magnets in these speakers are so powerful (!) that they are considered hazardous waste. Amazon went on say "...we advise you try to dispose of it locally".

It would be a joke if it was not true. These speakers can be received into and shipped from Amazon warehouses and handled by UPS or FedEx and customers without being harmful to anyone, but if you need to reverse the direction, then they are suddenly hazardous material that prove a great risk according to Amazon. Even if "powerful magnets" on the return policy caught your attention, you do not know the turning point from hazardously powerful to not hazardous, therefore you do not know whether or not this would apply to the product you are looking at. Amazon should be transparent on product pages of speaker systems to indicate whether or not the magnets are OK or deadly.

One more thing - please note also that their return policy states that nothing can be returned that has a rechargeable battery. So if you buy an expensive mobile phone and need to return it for any reason, they MIGHT tell you to dispose of it locally because it has a rechargeable battery AND a speaker.

Above was just so you know what you might step into. The reason this came about was because the product price dropped $200 the day I received mine. I asked Amazon to either accept a return or offer a credit. They provided the credit so all ended well though my loyalty is now questionably hazardous.

The speakers are plenty loudthough a bit below expectations on clarity. My wife and I are at the age where dialog is often lost in movies if there is a lot of noise at the same time in the chaos of a typical action movie. Clarity of speech is important; this Denon helps but it is not as clear as the old Bose set that it replaced. We are happy with it overall, Bluetooth streaming is great.

product_title: Sony ICF-C707 Clock Radio with AM/FM Dual Alarm and Large Easy to Read Backlit LCD Display
review_headline: Good for the way we use it
review_body:
We have had this unit for about a month now, and I like it a lot. Before going on I want to acknowledge that reading some of the reviews gave me a bit of pause, but this is one of those purchases where everyone uses it differently and will probably have a different view.

For example - the maligned display is 'bright', but for me it has one great feature that no other alarm clock has had - an 'off' position for the brightness. I am a very light sleeper and want a pitch-black room at night, and if I am a bit restless or something, I don't want to have a continuous reminder of the time I am losing staring me in the face! The medium setting is fine for non-night use, and when the display comes on bright in the morning it is just another reminder to me that that nature sound means I do have to get up.

The speakers are small and somewhat tinny sounding, but we never listen to the radio. I have always hated waking up to music almost as much as buzzer - it is a race to see which sound is more obnoxious to me, and I have my MP3 if I want to go to sleep by music.

The radio thing is not quite true - this is our second 'sounds' radio and we wanted one with two independent sounds alarms (which this has) so we could each wake to "natural" (but artificial) sounds. Unfortunately my wife is such a heavy sleeper that none of the nature sounds would wake her up reliably, so she uses a radio station up loud.

This thing has a lot of buttons, but they are generally well-grouped and placed. I saw one review that complained about the centrally-located reset button, but that is only for manual operation. When the alarm goes off, each individual alarm has a uniquely-sized on/off button (easily located in the dark) on the rear top corners of the radio. A quick double tap silences the alarm and resets it instantly for the next day, a single tap turns it off if it is a weekend or something and you don't want an alarm on the next day.

All in all we are quite pleased with this little but very capable clock/sound/radio/alarm.

product_title: Klipsch Reference On-Ear Premium Headphone
review_headline: Crystal clear sound with a full-room feel, but they hurt my ears after an hour
review_body:
I love over-the-ear headphones at work, they allow me to block out extraneous noises without making me deaf to things I need to hear like the phone or my boss dropping in to ask a quick question. My old set of headphones (V-MODA Crossfade) have wonderful sound, but begin feeling uncomfortably heavy after a short time. These Klipsch 'phones are about half the weight of the V-MODAs, so I was hoping they'd be comfortable longer.

First off, the sound is excellent, a little crisper and more defined than the V-MODAs, which are a little heavy on the bass and aren't as clear with spoken word. These Klipsch Reference headphones feel like a quality unit, are easily adjustable, and stay put even when I'm walking. The only downside? They naturally settle into a position that pushes on the outer cartilage of my ear in a way that's painful after a short time. I can re-position them to a more comfortable location, but they eventually slip back to that one painful spot.

I know everyone's ears are different, so it's quite possible that I just have weirdly shaped ears and that others won't have the same problem, but right now I'm only able to comfortably wearing these for an hour at a time and then I have to switch to my old and heavy V-MODA headphones.

It's frustrating because I really like the sound and the light weight of these so much better!

review_body: I live in the  Bay Area across the San Francisco Bay with about 30 miles distance from the City of San Francisco in the North West and 25 miles from the city of San Jose in the South.  These two cities are the major locations of the tv transmitters according to the data I got from Antennapoint.com.  There are a couple of transmitters from other cities about 50 miles away which I were also able to pull in nicely. As soon as I set up the antenna protruding about 3 feet above my roof, I used the auto tune function of the TV and I was able to pull in about 80 dtv stations. But since the Bay Area is highly diversed in terms of population, the stations I got in addition to the  English channels were Latino, Vietnamese, Korean, Chinese, Japanese and a couple of Hindi Stations. I'm planning to manually tune in available channels to lessen the time to channel surf. The channels I got were very clear although sometimes there were pixilation surge on some channels but does not last longer than a couple of seconds.  I even got some channels which I were not able to get with my leaf antenna which was attached to the glass of my window.  The nicest station I  got was Channel 1.1 which  streams viewing information like a tv guide.  It streams with the hour the current programs showing per channel and the  programs to follow. I was very happy that I got this antenna.  The only thing that I did not like about this product is that the contents of box was not given. So I have to wait and it turned out  no co-axial cable was included so I had to visit our local electronic shop for them.

So far so good. The battery was the same size and specifications as the original Verizon battery and it fit perfectly into the backup battery space in my Verizon box. The battery does have T1 terminals and not T2 terminals which is what the Verizon connector expects. But that was easily fixed by purchasing "F1 to F2 Terminal Adapters" at the same time I purchased the battery. The terminal adapters did add about 1/2" to the length of the wire attachment assembly but when I installed the battery the wires were able to flex enough that it was no problem connecting the battery to the Verizon equipment using the connector from my original Verizon battery. Be sure to save the wire connector (harness) from your original battery, you do not get another one when you purchase a replacement battery. Quick response, received the battery very quickly.

product_title: Tecsun PL880 Portable Digital PLL Dual Conversion AM/FM, Longwave & Shortwave Radio with SSB (Single Side Band) Reception, Color Silver
review_headline: ... bit about Kaito's latest addition to their line of fine, well built and well engineered line of small ...
review_body: I had read quite a bit about Kaito's latest addition to their line of fine, well built and well engineered line of small portable worldband radios. Being an amateur radio enthusiast and long-time shortwave listener myself, I am always looking for something new and exciting to add to my own collection of portable and tabletop receivers so, with that in mind as well as all of the positive feedback for this radio I went ahead and "took the plunge' and ordered one from Amazon. First off, I am an Amazon "Prime" subscriber so my little radio arrived within two days time; always a nice feature especially if you time it's arrival, as I did, to be right before a long, holiday weekend! The radio was sent through a company named "Electonnix".  Great packaging, o bumps or bruises to the box or to the radio which was, (of course!), contained inside of the package and which upon visual inspection was in excellent condition. The radio itself is truly a small portable rig in all of the best senses of that definition. Packaged with the radio were the following: 1. Ear buds 2. USB chord (for recharging the battery) 3. A small Lithium battery 4.A reel type wire exension antenna 5. User Manual The radio works great, folks!  Although the location I live in is not the best for any true long distance reception, this little radio, with the extra wire antenna extended, allowed me to listen to such far off shortwave broadcasters as Radio India, Radio Havanna, Radio Japan and many of the other more well known world band broadcasters as well! The radio does NOT come with a "wall wort",( i.e. an AC charger!)  It recharges the battery through the use of a small USB chord that can be plugged into any computer OR connected to the power plug of virtually any cellphone, Ipod or tablet charger! The controls on this radio are pretty straight forward!  Nice tunning knob as well as a fine tuning knob located directly beneath of it!  The tone of this radio is both rich and pleasant to the ear, unlike so many other of the other small portable radios out there in the marketplace! There are quite a few "hidden features" associated with this radio that I have read about on the various radio sites out there on the internet, (the synchronous detector, the muting feature, firmware version indicator, etc.)  To be honest, I haven't gotten around to searching out those features as of yet.  I plan on doing that very soon! In conclusion I can only say that, given the price for this little radio, and knowing something about the quality of Kaito built radios I have owned in the past, I do not hesitate to recommend this little gem to anyone out there looking for a well built, smaller portable world ban radio! Happy DXing!

product_title: AmazonBasics Ultra Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_headline: AmazonBasic Amplified 50 mile ultra thin antenna
review_body:
This is the best amplified digital antenna that I have owned. I have well over 30 channels even though I don't use all of the channels due to duplications or content, I have a range of 100 miles between broadcast points of channels available to choose from.

I have this antenna in a window facing south and the furthest channel received south (low population area) is about 40 miles. Surprisingly even with a southern facing, I am getting stations (high population area) 60 miles north. I live in a private home on a wooded lot in an area with rolling hills.

I decided to try a thin antenna that can mount to a window rather than continuing using an amplified large rabbit ear style antenna with a new HDTV purchased. Rabbit ear antenna was out of place with the new thin Smart HDTV. The first thin antenna I purchased was a MOHU Leaf amplified 60 mile range antenna. I mounted the MOHU in the window and got all but one channel group that my rabbit ear antenna got. Trying to get the missing channe groupl, while plugged into the TV with power on I tried to move the MOHU to a different location on the window and I got a shock (static?) and the MOHU stopped sending any signal to the TV. I returned the MOHU to WalMart and decided to try this Amazon amplified antenna. I am very satisfied with this product and after selecting a location in the window, the channels now received surpassed my expectations.

The only plus for the MOHU is that it had 4 velcro pads to attach to a wall or window. The Amazon Basic Amplified only has two 3M tapes and depending how you mount the antenna two may not be enough. I mounted this antenna with the cable at the top of the window to eliminate the cord being too visible.(running the cable around the window frame) With only two 3M tapes, the power connection (cable) did not hold flush to the window. I happened to have a few of the 3M tapes lying around so it was an easy fix for me. Eventually if there is a problem due to radiant heat from the southern exposure, I may change to four velcro pads. I think Amazon assumes that the antenna would only be mounted withe the cable at the bottom of the antenna and two 3M tapes may be enough.

I am very pleased with this product and would recommend to anyone wanting to get rid of the older rabbit ear style antennas or are just not satisfied with their current digital channel reception.adiant heat from the southern exposure, I may change to four velcro pads. product_title: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Black/Blue)
review_body:
Okay, let me do a head to head for a couple of the more moderately priced Bluetooth speakers - [[ASIN:B00OUEO4BI RND Ripple Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with two front speakers subwoofer and microphone (Gun Metal Grey)]] and [[ASIN:B00I9ICXFA NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green)]]. First off these are not the high end products like Bose, Sony or even Beats that can cost in excess of $200. These are more moderately priced items costing $30-$60. Your expectations should be appropriate for the price range.

Sound: first and foremost among what you probably want from a speaker. Both speakers offer good sound for the small size. The Ripple is a touch fuller on the bass, but both offer good sound across the volume range (better at higher volumes, a little tinny at lower volumes)

Portability: these are after all designed to accompany you mobile device. The NYNE is a bit bulkier, but is mountable on your bicycle (brackets and such included). Both units weigh in about the same when held, one in each hand, at less than a pound.

Charge: both are rechargeable, both come with a USB cable (you can use the plug adapter from you phone to connect the cable and charge), the Ripple is rated at 8-10 hours, I get about 6-8; the Cruiser does not seem to have an official rating on the Amazon product details and I have not run the battery enough to wear it down in the 4 hours of play time I've been using it.

Misc: the Cruiser is equipped with an internal microphone and can be used to answer calls, both are equipped with Aux input plugs so that you can play from non-Bluetooth sources, though that sort of defeats the purpose of buying a wireless speaker.

Pairing: both paired easily with my iPhone, nothing special here.

Overall, the Cruiser is nice as a casual bike mounted speaker for when you want to be 'mobile.' The Ripple is the less expensive of the two and a good solution for those times when you don't have your stereo with you and want to listen without a set of head phones. Neither measures up to our Bose, but then we expected that, these best use by giving them to the kids. P-)a set of head phones. The equalizer is preset, only music/movie, but I can't tell the difference between the two. I haven't synched a Bluetooth device to it yet.
So in short..if you want clear sound in a compact design for the price of a low end sound bar then this is for you.
Also I have a 48" LED sitting on it and I'm pretty sure it could handle a 55" easily.
If I had any negative it would have to be that there is no LED screen to show your volume settings but not a deal breaker at all.

product_title: Abco Tech Splash Proof Shower Speaker with 3 Firm Suction Cups - Black
review_body:
I have a 13 year old daughter who uses her phone to listen to music in the shower so when I was given the chance to test this Abco for quality, I was super excited. She usually puts her phone on the back of the toilet, as it's closest to the shower, and I am forever fearful that it will take a swim if she forgets to shut the lid.

It paired to her Bluetooth on her iPhone easily and she likes that it automatically reconnects. If her phone rings while she is in the shower, she is able to answer the phone call with the push of a button. The waterproof unit has three large section cups on the back which hold it to the wall securely. There is a digital display which tells the time, volume level and battery strength. The speaker has the ability to store up to 10 FM radio stations. By pressing a button, it will take you to your next preset station. We were only able to store 4 radio stations due to our bathroom being in the center of the house.

With the volume at max in the shower, you are able to hear the music but it is not extremely loud. It is loud, however when you listen to it outside of the shower. Overall, my daughter is very pleased with this and so am I as her phone can stay in her room next to the bathroom and I don't have to worry about damaging her phone.

product_title: SONOS Compact Wireless Speaker for Streaming Music
review_headline: Life changing - probably the best $200 you'll spend
review_body:
When I was traveling abroad in Europe, pretty much every "cool-guy" boutique had Sonos system. The model that particularly stood out was the 5. Because of the high price point, I was heistant to invest in one. I thought about buying a SONOS system for a couple of months, and I finally bit the bullet and bought the lowest end 1. The reason was that I just wanted something that I can listen to in my kitchen/living room while I'm random stuff around the house (I have Audioengine A5+ for my computers â€“ needed something casual).

I testdrove the 1, 3, and 5 all at my local bestbuy. I was totally indifferent about the sound quality and etc. I was completely wrong. The demo music was simply terrible. I was blown away when I played my HQ AACs and 320kbps mp3s. Despite the small size, it can totally fill a small apartment. One caveat I have is that the music is "engineered". I have monitoring headphones as well as speakers at home. Music doesn't really sound like the way it was intended. They rather sound somewhat artificial but made to sound pleasing (with exaggerated high's and low's - just like Beats but done in a tasteful way and without the bad connotation associated with Beats).

Setting up the system was very easy. If you can configure your home wifi, you'll be fine. The system is meant to be placed in a Mac OS X-based environment. The apps look and feel better on iOS and OS X.

The ability to stream music from the computer, iPhone, as well as Soundcloud (which is my go-to streaming source) keeps me entertained for hours.

Also, I'm probably one of the loneliest human beings. I have like no friends or family. It's cool to queue up songs as I approach my front door with the wifi turned on. I can listen to great music as soon as I walk into my house.

Anyway, $200 for the system is a bargain. I really wasn't expecting much but this thing is truly life-changing. Even if you are an audiophile, it is something to consider for versatility and most importantly, you are always in control of music wherever you are.

Don't waste your time reading this stupid review â€“ you need to buy ONE now.

Note: PLAY 1 is a newer than PLAY 3; it can play more audio formats and sound slightly better IMO despite the weaker bass compared to the 3

review_headline: I wasn't expecting audiophile performance and got what I expected
review_body: I have audiophile headphones for my audiophile system. What I wanted was okay headphones for use with the Philips bookshelf audio system in my home office. I like music in the early and late hours but don't want to disturb the household. These work fine for that purpose. Haven't tested the range; more than adequate for my 12 x 14 foot office. Work best with controls set flat on the system. + treble = tinny and harsh; + midrange = flat and lifeless; + bass = rampant distortion. Otherwise sound quality is good or better. The small buttons are a bit hard to find and operate, but I use the remote for my system to control volume anyway. The 'phones accept enough gain to hit the upper threshold of my comfort level with no distortion. They're comfortable and easy to adjust for fit. Battery run time, initial set-up, form factor, styling - no faults with any of those. If you're looking for a steal on high-end headphones, this isn't it. But if you're looking for a good value on mid-performance 'phones, these would be tough to beat.

review_headline: Great cable, cleans up a messy setup...
review_body:
Ahhh, finally. I dont know why its taken so long for people to realize that most people use HDMI cables now a days and no one (at least not out of choice) would want to use vga cables or your regular video in audio out cables. Anyways, point being, they should be made well and someone should put some thought in to it. Well, I am happy to say that someone definitely put some thought in to this cable. I have had many different HDMI cables in the past and even bought the Amazon Basics cable, which I thought was outstanding, except the fact that it was fine behind my tv, where there was more space, but not so much behind my monitor connected to my laptop.

It also would not lie flat since the thicker cables have a mind of their own and start coiling up on you or they just wont straighten out, which makes things look messy (I'm not a fan of messy). Anyways, this cable arrived yesterday, and as soon as I took it out of the packet I knew it was just what I needed, the cable lies flat on my desk, and does not coil up or anything. It is also very easy to move it about, meaning that I can put my laptop right in the corner of my desk without the cable being so hard that it wont go near the wall!!

The product also seems very well made and durable (only time will tell), and the results are amazing, the video is perfect and I feel like my audio improved a bit over my generic hdmi cable that came with my monitor. All in all, this has been a great purchase and after using a cable like this, I cant possibly see myself using anything else. Also, look at the price!!! Its crazy that you can get something this well made for under $ 5 bucks.

product_title: Xantech DL95M Universal Dinky Link IR Receiver, Manual Adjust
review_body:
I have a 60" plasma TV in the bedroom with my equipment rack in the closet which is on the opposite side of the wall that the plasma TV is mounted on. I use a Xantech extender kit (789-44 block, standard 291 receiver, and 4 emitters). For years I dealt with dodgy IR control. With the lights out in the closet where the equipment rack is, and the TV turned on, I could see the emitters glowing and flickering along with scene changes on the TV screen in the other room. It was the IR receiver in the bedroom picking up a signal from the plasma TV. This would "flood" the IR receivers in each of my equipment items that had an emitter attached. Some tolerated it better than others. The cable box was largely unaffected. The Bluray player had a hard time. Sometimes I would have to turn down the brightness on the TV so that I could control the Bluray player. Finally, I switched from cable to uverse and the uverse receiver box was completely unusable via infrared remote.

So, I bought the DL95M. It was much smaller then the standard 291 so I had to velcro it to the top of the TV. I turned on the TV and turned out the lights in the equipment closet. The emitters were no longer glowing or flickering. I went around to the bedroom and used the uverse IR remote to control the receiver box and each button-press worked flawlessly every time. The "plasma friendly" DL95M was the answer. I should have bought it long ago. (Well, I know why I didn't. They used to be very expensive. This one was half the cost of what they used to be).

Just FYI, I did *not* have to adjust the sensitivity (small screw on the back). It works fine right out of the box but I'm very glad to have that capability if I ever need it.

review_headline: As noted by previous reviews, the battery compartment cover ...
review_body: As noted by previous reviews, the battery compartment cover is HARD to open.  Solved by using a pair of Playtex rubber gloves which provide enough 'stickem' to rotate the cover off.  I hooked up the base station to the audio out RCA jacks on my TV.  My intention was to have the headset volume independent of the TV volume.  Initially, the volume was very low, even with the headset at maximum volume.  I could hear the hiss that previous reviews complained about and the headset volume directly coincided with the level of the the TV volume including mute.  Not what I wanted at all !  I then went into the TV settings menu, audio, audio output and found 2 settings: Fixed and Variable (which is the setting it was in).  I switched the setting to "Fixed" and the headset became loud and independent of the TV settings.  It works perfectly.  I gave the headset to my Mom and she's been watching TV with a big smile on her face because she can hear everything on the TV and I don't have to worry about the sheetrock in the living room coming loose.

review_body: As an Electronics Engineer, I was VERY SKEPTICAL when I read about this product. After charging the Batteries over-night, I installed the Unit in the Basement Rack with the IR Flasher Extension mounted on the front of the Cable Box.  Well, needless to say, THIS PRODUCT WORKS PERFECTLY & FLAWLESSLY!  I AM SO IMPRESSED & HAPPY TO FIND SUCH AN EASY SOLUTION for my Mom's problem.  In fact, it has been nearly 6 months already & they have not had to change either of the Batteries yet.  Trust me, if you can use either of these 2 Radio Frequencies (you have 2 choices when you purchase it), you will love this device.  It solved our problem because we have a Pioneer Plasma TV mounted on the wall in the Family Room that requires IR Commands be sent to it, directly from the Time Warner Remote because it then sends those Commands down to its Control Box in the Basement Rack.  So, my solution required both an IR and an RF Remote, to be used simultaneously.  THIS JUST WORKS GREAT!  I HIGHLY RECOMMEND IT.

product_title: Brainwavz M1 In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: A Great bang-for-buck earphone: Sweet, Laid back Vocals
review_body:
here a link to my video review for the M1:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wb5ju6AU5C4&feature=youtu.be
here is my full written review over on Head-fi: http://www.head-fi.org/products/mp4nation-brainwavz-m1/reviews/12455

The Brainwavz M1 has been widely toted as a popular option at under $50 for the last few years. Why is that the case? Well, because at the time of their debut, they were one the few balanced sounding earphones under $100 amongst a sea of bassy or V shaped sounding earphones.
How do the M1s fare years later, especially with heavy favorites from Vsonic, Havi, TTPOD? Very well in fact, for a â€œbudget earphoneâ€ they certainly have a very smooth and inviting sound that Iâ€™m very fond of.

hint- I nicknamed my M1s as â€œMini- RE 400s (referencing to the Hifman RE 400, an absolute standout earphone at $99)- See the â€œsound sectionâ€ for my comparison of the M1 with the $99 Giant, that is the RE- 400.

So letâ€™s dive right in shall we?
I would like to thank Brainwavz for sending a pair of the M1s out for review. I am in no way affiliated with Brainwavz, and every sentence down the last word, is my honest opinion. The pictures below are all mine, unless otherwise stated

Accessories: The Brainwavz M1 comes with:
6 pairs of single flanges (S,M,L)
1 pair of Biflange
1 S400 Comply Eartips
1 Shirt Clip
1 Hard shell Protective Carrying case
Overall: 8/10

Design
The M1s is a rather understated earphone, (that comes in 1 colour-black) with a very small footprint. It has a design that you would honestly not even notice on the streets. It has sort of a cone-like shape, with silver (metal band) to give the earphone a smooth finish, giving the aesthetics a nice lift.
Overall: 7/10

Build Quality
The earphones are lightweight with a mix of plastic and metal construction. The housing is made of plastic combined with a metal nozzle (allowing for greater durability). The y shape split is missing a cable cinch, this isnâ€™t a big deal for me but its something the note (you are covered with shirt clip though) . The upper part of the cable is a bit thin, but well made and braided underneath the â€œrubberizedâ€ sheath, similar to my Hifiman RE400 in appearance, but much more reinforced. The M1s terminate in a 45 degree angle jack, thatâ€™s very well relieved. * Something to note the cable carries a bit of memory*
However, my single biggest gripe with the build quality is the lack of strain relief when the cable exits the earpieces (there is none). This issue is magnified with the M1s, because of how small size, shape, smooth finish of the earpieces. They can be a bit hard to take out of the ear, and I often find myself pulling at the cable when taking off) ÃŸ obviously not a good thing for the long term durability of the cable.
Overall: 7/10

Comfort
Very comfortable in the ear, because of the small housing and the smooth housing (no edges that cause any irritation). These reasons make the M1s very easy to insert and stay into the ear, and I believe it will allow for a comfortable fit for everyone.
Overall: 9/10

Isolation
There is quite a large vent at the back of the earpieces, and in combination with the short nozzle this a result the isolations suffers somewhat. I would say the isolation is average at best.
Overall: 7/10

Cable noise is a mild when worn cable down, and is none existent when worn cable up.
Overall: 8.5/10

Sound
The sound of the M1s is the best aspect of this earphone by far. Its balanced, smooth, and slightly mid-centric. I would especially recommend this earphone especially for someone that wants to try a balanced sounding earphone for the first time but did not want to spend too much.

Bass: The M1s have a fairly linear bassline as in there is no particular emphasis anywhere. Some refer to thebass being a bit light, I can see that in a sense, but I wonâ€™t go that far. Bassheads will be disappointed with the quantity, but the bass here is well intergrated into the sound. The bass here has good control, and extends fairly well low, and retains medium speed and decay throughout. I felt the bass works more as a complementary piece to the midrange rather than steal the show, like on more bassier options.

Midrange:This is certainly the highlight for the M1s. So if you like basking in vocals, the M1s is one of the most affordable options that will get you great, smooth vocals, with good clarity throughout. The vocals here are slightly warm, but very natural sounding (with good note thickness (not thick, not thin) and its presentation is a bit laid back the midrange here is not pushing its detail â€œin your faceâ€ but conveys more of â€œsit back and enjoy the showâ€ feeling.

Treble: The treble is a bit laidback from what I call neutral (see my comparison below with the Hifiman Re400). The treble is â€œsmooth and politeâ€ with a roll off up top,taking away the â€œairnessâ€ and the height of the soundstage. However, it has have decent extension in the treble, with good clarity as well.
Soundstage: Surprisingly wider, than I thought considering how small the housing is, so slightly above avearage. Height and Depth is adequate and there is decent sense of space and separation as well.

Sound comparison with the Hifiman RE-400:
Pros for the RE400 ($99)
A drier, more up front, more transparent midrange.
A Smoother, more articulate treble, easier going sound
Tighter Bass, Punchier bass.
Greater level of separation and refinement overall.
Better vocals and instrument separation.

Pros of the Brainwavz M1 ($45)
Bass is more Linear
Fuller bodied vocals
Treble has a bit more crispness
Wider soundstage
Overall: 8/10

All in all, I think the Brainwavz M1 are a spectacular value at ~around $45-50, I think it has a similar price to performance ratio as the Hifiman RE-400, which is certainly very high praise in my book. I will wholeheartedly recommend the M1s to anyone looking for a smooth, balanced sound signature, love their vocals looking to unwind after a long day of work.
Overall: 54.5/60= 77.8%

product_title: Yamaha R-N301BL Network Stereo Receiver, Black
review_body:
The Yamaha R-N301 Network Receiver is a modern "connected" person's toy! While definitely not an audiophile's amplifier, it performs most of its functions well. Unfortunately, it falls down on a major function: It does not support the digital audio out format (usually Dolby 5.1) of most OTA (Over The Air) broadcasts on a modern TV.

I have used the Optical Digital Input, AirPlay, Internet Radio, and Line In functions, and all worked as expected except for the noted issue with OTA TV broadcasts. If the receiver is in Standby mode, it will power-on when a device connects and begins to play. There is no auto-power off function, but there is a sleep mode available via the IR Remote

I used the IOs controller app. There is an Android app with similar functionality. The App allowed for quick changing of internet radio stations and control of the volume when I was in another room. The App can also manage the power, and select other inputs.

For most of the advanced functions, you will need a network connection. Since this receiver does not directly support WiFi, a hard wired network connection is required. If not available, you will need a Wifi Network Bridge. Personally, I used a travel router configured in bridge mode powered using the 5V USB output on the rear of the receiver.

As of the writing of this review, there is no remote profile for this receiver in the Harmony database. Additionally, there are some issues with the "Network" modes since there are no discrete commands for these modes. Thus you may need to manually cycle through the "NET" modes to get the desired mode.

The FM & AM tuners are functional, but not exceptional, which is standard at this price point. Accessing the Treble, Bass & Balance controls from the remote is cumbersome, but possible. These cannot be changed via the IOs App.

PRO: Automatically turns on (if in net standby mode) when an AirPlay device connects and plays.

CON: The Optical input appears to only support PCM formats. Most TVs output a Dolby 5.1 encoded stream when viewing Over The Air (OTA) brodcasts, and this receiver will not play it. You will likely have to use the analog outputs to the one of the Line inputs. If you use a cable box, media player or bluray player, your TV may "down convert" these sources to PCM which the R-N301 will accept.

CON: There is no existing remote profile in the Harmony Remote database. No documented support for "discrete" commands such as "Power On," "Power Off," and "NET-Internet Radio."

CON: The headphone amplifier is very noisy.

The stereo doesn't like old school iPhones. I tried my old 3G in it, and of course I get the "PRODUCT NOT OPTIMIZED" message, but it still should have worked (because it does with my other radio I used to have with same error) but all I get is static. If you use an iPod newer than a 5th gen classic the screen will pulsate the iPod logo and pretty much look like a strobe light. So far though, my only cons. Not bad, Ridgid, not bad.

product_title: Cooligg 3-In 1-Out HDMI HD 1080P Auto Switch Splitter Cable
review_body:
This is a review of the performance of Cooligg Auto Switch Splitter in two difference uses one as a TV and one as computer. As a TV setup, I had a Dish Satellite, LG Blue Ray and Apple TV. Each will work with the HDMI input to the TV. But using the Cooligg 3 I quickly found out that the Apple TV did not have enough Signal strength to trigger the switch. By shortened the cabled length by 2/3 I was able to detect a useable signal. I then added the LG and both signals were present but did not switch based upon power.
Adding the Dish Receiver continued the process. Only by using the select â€œBUTTONâ€ could I get the until change inputs.
Now to the computer installation: two systems, Windows 7 and Windows 10, both with HDMI output, but the WIN7 Video card has an DVI to HDMI, while the WIN10 if straight HDMI. The WIN7 computer signal would not trigger the switch, while the WIN10 would work. Even the select button would not allow the signal to pass. I tried the Panlong HDMI Switch as a replacement and found it work perfectly. This switch is USB powered and does need and power from the device.
Bottom line: The Cooligg Switch requires a high signal strength with sufficient power to trigger operation of the switch. Cable length will make a difference. So if you have a deceive such as the APPLE TV you would want to go up to the Panlong switch ( Note: I used an old Cell phone charger to provide the power for the USB, the switch only comes with a cable â€“ no power source.) Both switches provide a service, but be aware of your input devices and their power when making a decision.

review_headline: Big on sound and quality, yet reasonably priced!
review_body:
These days the market seems to be flooded with bluetooth speakers. But don't let some of the marketing gimmicks fool you, not all of them are of the same quality or offer the same features. Below are a few thoughts and observations I have of a review sample I have recently received.

1. Big on sound, this speaker packs a respectable 20W of stereo sound.
2. It's battery is long lasting at 10hrs, which I have been able to replicate in real life use.
3. The finish is premium - the top is a luxurious gloss black piano finish. The front grill is made of metal, and not a soft material, so you don't have to worry about damage. 4. It still manages to stay reasonably small at about 8.25" wide x 2.75" high x 2.25" deep, which is fairly small considering all the reasons mentioned above.
5. Bluetooth 4.0 - It matters what bluetooth protocol your speaker is. 4.0 is the latest spec, and allows for quick reconnections as well as low energy consumption for both the speaker as well as the device (likely your phone or tablet) through which the media is being streamed.

It's recharged using a standard microusb cable (included). Also included (but not mentioned in the description) is a 3.5mm audio cable to connect to a non-bluetooth device (like an iPod shuffle etc), or if you just preferred to go wired for some reason. These are the only two ports you need, you can see them on the attached picture. Every time I turned the speaker on, a sound confirmed that it had been turned on and another that it instantly reconnected with my phone. The buttons have a nice, soft and waterproof finish.

I own a couple of other bluetooth speakers, but this one by Anker is my new "go-to" and it looks good enough for you to want to flaunt it.

Compare it to a popular alternative like the Beats Pill (http://www.amazon.com/Beats-Pill-Portable-Speaker-Black/dp/B00GJVF766), that costs a whole lot more ($199 as of this writing), packs a weaker output (4x3W = 12W) and lasts just 7hrs, and you can see that you are getting amazing value with the Anker product, not to mention an 18-month warranty.

I thought I would try in-ear phones one last time: you know the kind, the ones that seal off your ear canal, as opposed to the Apple kind that leave your ear room to breathe. (Does anyone else react this way?) The advantage of the Apple-like open-ear phones is that I donâ€™t have that feeling; plus the sound is pretty damâ€™ good even then.

So: I gave these a try. And surprise! I like them. They are extraordinarily comfortable. And they donâ€™t fit so tight that they make me feel (as I said) claustrophobic. I am quite impressed. There are three sets of inserts, so surely even Lyndon Johnsonâ€™s ears could find a fit (hmmm . . . I suppose thatâ€™s a dated joke).

The Bose sound is its usual magnificent self, with clean highs and profound bass. Thereâ€™s even a nifty little carrying case. Plus an itty-bitty clothes pin on the right cable to hold it to your shirt.

I am mostly an Apple user (iPhone, iPad), so I wanted to see how many of the features here, designed for Samsung, would work. Well, most of them do: at least the start/stop button; the volume button does not.

product_title: MEE audio M6 PRO Universal-Fit Noise-Isolating Musician's In-Ear Monitors with Detachable Cables (Smoke)
review_headline: A very well rounded IEM at a fantastic price
review_body:
This is my fifth pair of MEElectronics headphones and I'd been waiting a long time for some legitimate in ear monitors from MEE and these do not disappoint. I received these units over six months ago and have put them through extensive use both for on stage, and for regular air travel. I'd say that these have over 30,000 airline miles on them, including a round trip US to Israel, and US to UK (in addition to a ton of domestic trips). They've held up really, really well. In fact, I'd say they are still pretty much new. Let's take a closer look at them.

First off, let's look at the product itself:

-They come with a multitude of ear tips- silicone of all different sizes, and FINALLY some foam tips for extra isolation. I personally use the foam for everything because of the comfort and isolation. They also hold nice and solid. Don't come out or loosen with sweat or activity.
-The body of the IEMs are a great size, shape, and construction. Some of the IEMs out there tend to be a bit bulky and cause hotspots on the ears after long use, and these are not that way.
-They come with two different sets of memory wire cables. One is the standard cable with an on-line microphone, volume rocker, and button. It works well with phones both for phone calls, and for listening to and controlling music. The second cable is my favorite. It doesn't have the microphone or controls, but the build is much sturdier and a better overall feel. This cable is intended to be used for heavy IEM use (on-stage, and things like that). The connections on the cables seem solid and I've had no issues with them coming loose, disconnecting, fraying, or anything like that.
-They are comfortable to wear in almost any way- cable in front, cable in back, inside clothing, outside clothing. The slider on the cable holds tight so nothing comes loose with extensive sweat or activity.
-The case that comes with these is by far my favorite MEE case to date.It's the right size, relatively hard sized, and not too big.

Let's look at the audio quality:

This was one of my biggest worries with IEMs at this price point. In fact, when I first wanted to give MEE a try I was worried that the audio quality wouldn't be very good. THAT IS NOT THE CASE. These are great full range headphones that give you just the right mix of everything. I'm a bit of a basshead (I play bass, go figure.....), and these pleased me. There's enough bass coming through but not so much that it muddies up everything else. They take really well to EQ mixing so you can give yourself the exact sound that you want.

Overall thoughts:

I dare you to put these IEMs up against others that are 2-3 times the price. You'd be hard pressed to find a better set for anywhere near the price. I have to say, MEE does it again. Do yourself a favor and stop searching. Buy these guys.

review_headline: The speaker buy of the decade
review_body:
I've had a bunch of stuff in my life from EL57s, EL63s, DQ10s, Dayton Wright XG2s, Maggie 1Us through 1Ds, Magnepans, Sound Labs Pristines, A3s, A1s, Servo Statics, ML CLS 1s, and probably a ton more that I've forgotten about. Same applies to tube amps, although I did have quite a bit of solid state stuff 45 - 50 years ago from Crown DC300s to Phase 700b. Turntables, I stick with longer. Much prefer analog over digital. True digital has gotten much better, but analog has gotten better faster.

Ok, I've been around the block a few times in seven decades. I set my mind on getting a pair of Maggie 3.7i. Listened to them at a 'high end' dealer locally, and driven by 600w Classe' monoblocks. I was shocked that I didn't much care for them. They had to played rather loudly to get the involvement than you get at much lower levels with what I bought. Also, in the three or four pieces that they played for me .... pieces that I know very well, part of the soundstage was stuck on the surface of the speaker. It was like WTF! They were using a Classic 1 with a Dynavector 20x2, which is another combination I'm a little familiar with. Female vocals, in this case, Jennifer Warnes, mouth sound as if it was three feet wide. I'm sure I could have gotten them set up correctly at home after the number of Tympani and Magnepans I've had over the last 45 years. What I still did hear that I couldn't fix is still just a bit of that magneplaner sound .... a certain graininess from the mid bass up.

I had the money with me, they had them, I had my big car, I was all ready. Then I thought that maybe I had better come back and try again. Maybe it was me that day. I don't know other than I didn't much care for what I heard. I ended up at another the local dealer the following day who had the Martin Logan Electromotions. Had them set up properly too with them a 1/3 of the way into the room. And me sitting a 1/3 of the way from the back wall. I was just floored with what I heard. I knew of these little speakers, but never on earth thought I was actually going to buy them. But buy them I did and with the free sub as a throw in. Also received by FedEx that day, a cheap low powered integrated amp, the Hegel H100 at 120w /ch at 8 ohms and 220w /ch at 4. I've never had an integrated amp before, but only tube stereo amps or mono blocks, but that budget would be blown all to hell by $60,000 or $70,000 in preamp and amps.

Set everything up. Placed the speakers close to a 1/3 in from the side walls and a little more than a 1/3 out into the from the back wall. In this case 6'10\\". I listen near field so I'm about another 6' from the speakers.

I didn't much like what I heard at first as they were hot, lean and bright, but the imaging and sound staging were spectacular. I though, ok, the potential is here so let's burn them in for a 100 hours or so. Even by the next day they were sounding warmer and more natural. Now that I'm two weeks in and probably a couple hundred of hours of run time, they are just wonderfully natural and balanced with some of the most holographic imaging I've heard at any price. However, I can't stress enough that you cannot put these up against the back wall and expect anywhere near what these are capable of. They must be way out into the room. Start with the old audiophile 'Rule of Thirds' And you absolutely don't need this home theater bull crap of a center channel speaker. These will create your 'center channel' perfectly if setup correctly. A home theater literate friend of mine just left a little while ago after he came over to listen to these. He actually looked under a little two-person couch at the equipment end of my room thinking that I was screwing with him and hid the center channel. He did comment that it sounds much more natural this way, in that the 'center channel' voice had a body and dimensionality to the voice. I said ok, you're starting to 'get it'. He was very confused at first in that he heard nothing coming out of the speakers, that everything was 'out there' where it belonged. I said 'out there' is where it's supposed to be .... not on the surface of your speakers.

And another thing .... these speakers will absolutely tear apart a bad recording, but the good recordings soar. From a jazz trio (Three Blind Mice \\"midnight Sugar' to big band Harry James 'Still Harry After All These Years' on Sheffield to .... even techno (thinking Moby or Muse) .... these will play with incredible micro detail at 80db with Arvo Part or pound away at 105-110 db on Muse or Moby. I do use the sub occasionally to fill in the bottom half octave. And I found the best, most real vocal recording I've ever heard just a couple of days ago. Fairfield Four \\"Wreckin' the house'. True, gospel, but just an incredible recording with my favorite track being Noah. Take a look at the reviews right here on Amazon.

I started writing this review a week or so ago and have since added a second ML W700 sub. On power up for the first time, I didn't like it and was going to return it the next day. Then I though to myself that everything else requires a 100 or so break in hours so why would these be exempted. By the next day the bass started to congeal again and started to sound all right. product_title: New Wayzon Magic Rubik's Cube Portable LED RGB Light Deep Bass Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Speakers with Build in Microphone Hands-free Function TF Card Mode(White)
review_headline: Fun novelty speaker that performs well
review_body:
Resembling a Rubix cube, this is a cute and functional little speaker. It has a white plastic frame and the front has 9 square panels that light up when music plays; you can choose from 5 different light patterns or you can turn the lights off. The sides of the speaker are solid colors and do not light up. The black speaker grill sits on the top of the cube, and the control buttons are directly opposite on the cube (basically the bottom).

The speaker takes less than 2 hours to charge (it arrived completely dead and required charging before use), and the battery lasts approximately 5 hours (one time I got 5 hours and 43 minutes out of it!), which is much better than other speakers I have. I'm very happy with the charging vs music play time.

I'm certainly not an audiophile, but in my opinion the sound quality has quite a bit of bass; more than I'm used to with little speakers. Initially I thought the treble sound could be a bit better, but after listening to it for a while I'm now very accustomed to it. It does sound full and nice. (I've actually heard different things in my music that I hadn't noticed before.) And talk about volume! This thing can get LOUD, and surprisingly it doesn't even distort when turned up....however, I can't imagine ever cranking it all the way up indoors!

The bluetooth feature easily and quickly connected to my iphone 5, and also to my ipad mini (at separate times, of course). When the speaker connects via bluetooth to a source it makes a little sound to confirm the connection. As for the range, it preforms much better with my iphone 5 than it does with my ipad mini. (I've had skipping and jumping music with the ipad mini when it was literally sitting within 10 feet of the speaker. Not always, but it has happened.) The speaker works best if you can keep your device in a clear line of sight to the speaker; it gets a bit finicky if you get walls in the way or take your device into a different room. If you can keep a clear line of sight to the speaker you can easily get your device (my iphone 5 in this case, not the ipad mini) 30 or more feet away and still have a solid connection.

If bluetooth is not an option for your phone/tablet/other device, the cube also comes with a small audio cable so you can plug directly into it. Alternatively you can also insert a microSD card into the back of the speaker and it will play any music that is stored on the microSD card. This was a very surprising, yet nice, feature that I didn't expect to find.

I really like that this doesn't look like a traditional speaker, so it's not unattractive to have sitting out in the middle of a room. I sort of wish it had more light panels (only one side lights up), however then it wouldn't be as attractive when turned off, so I'm actually happy with it the way it is. I feel the current price of $20 is very fair when you consider the novelty of the speaker, combined with the decent sound quality and fairly long-life battery. It comes packaged in a nice looking box, so it would definitely look like a nice gift for a teen or any music lover. product_title: SANUS SYSTEMS VLF220-B1 37-Inchto65-Inch VisionMount Full-Motion Flat Panel Mount
review_headline: If you aren't willing to pay more to get a second arm and the ability to turn a larger TV 90*, this is a great full motion mount
review_body:
I had always planned on mounting our Panasonic TC-P50ST50 to the wall with a fully articulating mount. I knew the mount had to have a clean look to fit in with the rest of our new house. While searching for and ordering a mount before our house was completed, I had the idea that I would want one with double arms for smoother motion when adjusting the set. Unfortunately the Sanus version (the VXF220), a step up from this mount, was about $100 more and I could not justify paying more than the already pricy ($225) VLF220.

I also checked out other brands but no one else seemed to have the same combination of utility, style, price and practicality. The runner-up was a Peerless SA763PU. The Peerless even had the dual arm supports but the cable management system was not as integrated and the arms were not as inconspicuous as the one on the Sanus. Also, when reading reviews of the Peerless and looking over the manual, there seemed to be less adjustment allowed when mounting the support panel to the wall. Either the Sanus or the Peerless would have probably worked for my application but overall the Sanus edged out the win in my opinion.

As for cheap brands on Amazon and Monoprice, their price isn't incentive enough for me to trust hanging a $1,000 TV set on. Also, their features, build quality and style fall far short when compared to the likes of Sanus or Peerless.

Pros
Fully articulating arm
Clean, modern design
Well hidden space for cable management
The back plate is open so as not to get in the way of plugging cables into the back of the unit
Plastic covers on the wall mount plate hide lag bolts and other screws
Easy to install

Cons
Arm isn't long enough to turn the TV a full 90* (for a TV of this size you would need either the (Sanus LF or XF228)
Price
Provided lag bolts were longer than any of my drill bits (fortunately I had shorter lag bolts from previous TV mount installs)
The indicated drill bit diameter is too narrow to easily tighten the lag bolts (I used the next step up from the one recommended in the manual)
Center arm joint is difficult to adjust (even when completely loosened you will need two hands to change the arms positioning)
Even though the back plate for the TV is is open, I had to adjust where I mounted it to avoid covering up the power cord and outlet on the TV

FYI: The last three photos on Amazon for this product are not the VLF220. They look more like the VLF210.

review_body: I initially purchased 1 pair which upon arrival, after listening with the current configuration was installed to connect the Sony CD player to the preamplifier. The pre is an AR LS 26, amp is Krell 300cx speakers Martin Logan Request with Velodyne 18 DD subwoofer. The cable used are Kimber PBJ terminated with balanced Neutrik gold connectors. As soon as introduced The Serpent II XLR, I notice a difference compared to the Kimber PBJ. Although the sound was generally better, it is in the high frequencies the Serpent made a big difference. review_headline: Best set of cheap headphones I have EVER bought!
review_body:
For the price, you seriously CANNOT complain about anything!!! I bought these headphones for $10, and these are the best cheap headphones ever!!! I usually get skullcandy in-ear buds for everyday use, but in-ear buds fall out from time to time, or do not have the same effect of over-ear headphones, so I made a $10 budget for some over-ear headphones. Looked on every site, at every brand, and finally decided on some JVC Flats 'cause of the great reviews I saw everywhere. I was NOT disappointed, and these headphones went completely over my expectations!!!

They are lightweight, but surprisingly don't feel as cheap as I would have expected them to be. The cushions are light and do the job, and I don't even notice them after I put them on (meaning they are super comfortable). The cable is long and sturdy, considering all the yanking it goes through. Same for the plastic: sturdy, and does not crack or chip. The headband is adjustable and is not loose in any way or form. Absolutely perfect.

The sound is better than the skullcandy in-ear buds. I hear the base so clearly and smoothly. From time to time I will hear the treble slightly too much then wanted, but it is NOT an issue. The speakers are clear (not muffled) and wonderful :D.

I have had these for months now, and I will NEVER go back to any other headphones (unless they discontinue them, which I hope never ever happens)! I will keep my $150 Axent Wear headphones, or these bad boys with me from now on.

BUY THESE HEADPHONES. You will not regret it!!!

review_headline: I love these headphones! (Only one concern/Dislike): Here's a way to listen to music and talk on skype at the same time. UPDATE:
review_body: I ordered these on Sunday and got it here on Tuesday with two day shipping.  Look and Feel: I got the red one. I was going to get the gold one because that looked nicer but it was a tad bit more expensive than I had wanted to shell out. the look and feel of this one is amazing. The color is a deep red, burgundy color. It doesn't feel cheap. It feels well-made. For the price you pay, this is pretty nice. The headphones does not have a plastic feel where you can leave fingerprints etc. The outer cover (the colored part) is a satin, rubber material. It feels smooth. The inner cover (The black) is plastic. The cushion for your ears and the top of your head is made out of the faux leather material and feel comfortably.  Fit: The fit is perfect. It goes right over my ears. Then again, my ears are small so the cushion actually covers my entire ear and my ear is nestled inside.  Bluetooth Connection: Connecting it to bluetooth is easy. All you have to do is first fully charge the headphones and then press and hold the play button until it turns on. It will start pairing. Another way to start pairing is press and hold the volume up and volume down button. The headphones connected to my Windows 8.1 Pro HP Ultrabook easily.  Sound: WOW! For the price you pay, this headphone delivers an amazing range of sound. The highs and lows are really nice. The bass is also superb. I tested the headphones through what I usually listen to: Hardstyle, classical music, hip hop, R&B, rap, country etc. The headphone delivers clear, pure surround sound.  Microphone: Another reason why I chose these headphones is because I wanted a wireless headphone to talk on skype with too. It works very well with skype even when I was whispering. It does sound a bit raspy. But I can still hear myself so I am happy.  Conclusion: I am ecstatic that I bought these headphone. I think I might be buying this for my family too. I really enjoy using these headphone so far.  My only dislike would be when I am chargingthe headphone, the charger doesn't completely touch the headphone. Is this normal?  UPDATE: These act as an amazing stereo headphone and as a headset.   Stereo Headphone: You can listen to music but can't really use it to talk on the phone and listen to amazing music at the same time. The sound from a stereo headphone is amazing! The sound are clear.   Headset: This work as an amazing headset too if you were just using them to talk on the phone. The other side could hear you clearly. I use this mainly for skype. At first when I was talking on skype, I tried talking and listening at the music, but I found out that sound didn't go through. the only way I found that would let me listen to music, listen to the other person and use my mic all at the same time was basically:  When you are using skype or any type of app like that, you will have to set the Headset as a default playback in Control Panel--> Hardware and Sound--> Playback--> Right Click headset--> Set as default playback not default communication. Everything is now played through the headset.   When you are not using skype or talking, you can always set the stereo headphone as default again through the same way I mentioned above.  WARNING: When you set the headset as a default playback for music and hearing the other side at the same time, the sound is NOT AS GREAT. You will not get the full effect of the stereo headphones.   Anyway, definitely look forward to reviewing it after 1 month and 3 month.

product_title: TiVo Roamio Slide Pro DVR Remote
review_headline: Smaller and heavier than the standard TiVo remote, but no AV Receiver Power control.
review_body:
This remote is about 3/4 of the size of the standard TiVo remote (the one that comes with a Roamio or Roamio Plus/Pro). It is MUCH easier to use as it is smaller and most thumbs can reach all the buttons without having to slide your hand. It is definitely heavier, in a better way, than the basic TiVo remote. The buttons are responsive. I use the RF function for the TiVo and the IR function for the TV. The slide-out keyboard rocks and feels sturdy. It could easily be my favorite remote.

So, why did I only give this four stars? Just about everyone with a TiVo has a separate AV receiver. Although this remote can be configured to control the volume and mute on the receiver, it cannot turn the power on and off. That makes it unusable as a main remote for me. I have to continue to use my Logitech Harmony Smart Control remote (with the hardbutton RF remote) to power the system on and off. I would be happy to ditch the Harmony if the TiVo could just turn the receiver on and off. HDMI CEC works for the receiver volume from the TV, but does not work for receiver power.

If you have a TiVo Roamio, this remote is an excellent addition to your setup.
