product_title: SOL REPUBLIC 1211-02 Tracks On-Ear Interchangeable Headphones with 3-Button Mic and Music Control - White
review_headline: These headphones produce great sound coupled with background noise being filtered out to ...
review_body:
Pros: These headphones produce great sound coupled with background noise being filtered out to a large degree bc of sound isolation. I thought that wouldn't make a difference, but it does; listening to these headphones in a noisy subway station is a breeze. The bass is bumping but if you're into genres that aren't bass-heavy these won't completely kill the sound of those (though it is less pronounced). They fit well (you can adjust it) and the ear pads are mostly comfortable (I do have small ears though). The individual parts of the headphones are interchangeable--if that appeals to you for aesthetic or functional reasons. The mic is pretty good at picking up your voice, unlike some other headphones I've sampled. If you're weighing these against the Beats Solo HD (which I also own), I'd say in terms of price to sound ratio, these are the better deal.
Cons: --They don't "fold" like other over-ear headphones, which makes them a tad bulky for short distance travel. (For long distance, you could disassemble it for easier storage).
--The sound leaks heavily from these. If you put your volume 60% or higher, others around you can definitely hear it.
--The white headband gets dirty easily :/

review_headline: Good headphones, but not great. Surround sound effect is not obvious.
review_body: I honestly expected a better sound from these. But after having a pair of SONY MDR-V6 wired headphones I can't say it is the same. But I suppose I can't compare the two. I plugged mines into TV's 3.5 mm. The sound is good for vocals or simple music. However when many instruments introduced, I have to turn off surround sound, or sound is overwhelming, and it's hard to distinguish anything, even at lower volume. Watching the movie is the same thing. I saw Star Trek, and it's really not surround sound per se. The sound is only augmented to be louder and comes from 4 smaller but louder points instead of 2 centralized quieter points, but no surround sound effect one would get from the speakers. I am not expecting speaker surround sound, but some has to be present, since the headphones are advertised as such and that is why I bought them. To use volume controls I have to feel my way around the headphones, or take them off, but this is a minor inconvenience for me. All and all it is a decent purchase. I wanted quality wireless headphones and it certainly is, but only fulfilled 75 percent of my expectation.

The room is not acoustically treated and the sub has not been optimally placed within the room; it's just of to the right of the side channel speaker. That being said to my untrained ears this thing sounds great as is. Whether movies or music, this sub kicks with clear low end power. I've seen people write that this sub can be get distorted and "boomy" when listening to music but I've had yet to have any issues that are of any concern. If your looking for something reasonably priced to add a tremendous amount of clean low frequency presence it will be hard to find a better piece of equipment.

product_title: Nakamichi Wireless Bluetooth 4.0 Speaker BTSP80 - Matte Silver
review_headline: Little hefty speaker with Great sound
review_body:
I love buying bluetooth speakers, it's somehow become a hobby of mine. You can check out some of the others I've reviewed online.
The Nakamichi BTSP80 is a great speaker for the price. Well, I picked this one up for about $30 dollars when it first came out. I believe it's going for much more now here on Amazon. However, you can get for less at the worlds largest auction website (hint hint).

Now going back to the speaker, for the size of this thing the sound is amazing! This speaker will easily fill a larger room (enclosed) with no problem. It has great bass, neck and neck with the Bose Soundlink Mini and JBL Charge 2. However the mids and highs does become muffled at times. If you have an equalizer on your device then you can adjust them accordingly to your taste/music, problem solved.

It is also a hefty speaker, personally I like the weight. But still very portable. People have been reporting about 10 hr battery life, I've never gotten the chance to test it for I don't usually play them for hours on end, maybe 4 or 5 hours at the most. I've never ran into issues with it. Also when I'm done, I usually charge them right after.

The only drawback I need to point out.....it's the bluetooth range. If I carry my phone in my pocket, the farthest I can walk away from the speaker is about 12 - 15ft before it begins to start breaking up. If you don't have to carry your bluetooth device with you, then I say put on a playlist or station and leave it next to the speaker or use the aux port.

Overall I think this speaker is well worth it if you can find it under $40 bucks, look around online you'll find a deal.

product_title: Neewer 2X 6.6 inch/17cm Mini HDMI(Type C) Male to HDMI(Type A) Female Adapter Connector Cable
review_body:
Packaging and Contents:
The cable arrived on time and was well packaged.
It also came fitted with plastic plug protectors - a nice touch.

Usage Scenario:
My use for this item is to convert the full-sized "Type A" male plug of a standard HDMI cable (running to my HD TV) to the same length (but thinner) "Type C" male plug for inserting into the "Type C" female jack in the confined and recessed I/O jack area of my Nikon D810 DSLR camera. As such, the girth of the casing surrounding the male plug cannot be too thick - as it is with most low cost cables.

The girth of the casings at the ends of this cable were not too excessive for my case. However, the outer casing is still very square edged, meaning it might be a problem for jacks in extremely tight or recessed areas. However, I think this cable should serve well for all but the rarest of situations.

If your female jack is significantly confined or recessed, you may want to try a cable whose outer end casings are not shown to be square right to the flush mounting surface but tapered so as to allow the plug to fully penetrate the jack. If you can't find such an animal, I'd give this one a a spin as it works in the moderately tight confines of I/O well of a Nikon D800/D810 DSLR.

If the casings at the plug ends had been tapered, I'd give this cable 5 stars. I don't know why most of them have large squared off casing ends which make them harder to work with tightly spaced or jacks. Cost isn't the issue since its just a mold that actually uses a tiny less material.

review_body:
I am an unrepentant fan of Panasonic's low-end headphones. In fact, just a week or so before I received these, I purchased the two-pack of the RP-HJE120. And over the past four years or so, I've bought four other pairs of Panasonic ergo-fit earbuds of varying quality and price points. Because you can't have too many sets of earbuds.

For me, fit is the most important factor in choosing earbuds. If they don't fit into my ears correctly and/or comfortably, the sound suffers. Secondly, I don't want them falling out, which is why I shy away from the barrel-type buds. The Panasonic ergo-fit buds seat comfortably and firmly into my ears, and because of the shape, I don't have to look to see which bud goes in which ear. (Helpful when I'm not wearing my glasses.)

The sound quality is adequate, both when listening to music and when making calls. They are plenty loud and can be pushed to uncomfortable levels before they start to distort. The mic/remote is well-placed and handy for changing music. (Hold the button and you'll hear the iPod voice tell you what you're listening to, which is highly entertaining to my young son.) My only complaint is that the cables are rather thin and prone to tangling. That's to be expected at this price. All in all, they're a great value for the price.

product_title: APC Back-UPS 350VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BE350G)
review_headline: Best combination of price and replacement battery availability/cost
review_body: Haven't had a power outage yet to see how it performs.  I live in an area where this happens about every month or two though so I probably won't be waiting long.  About the unit, it has 3 outlets connected to the UPS and 3 non protected/"surge protected" outlets.  If you lose DC power the unit beeps loudly.  And cuts over to battery power giving you time to save your work and shut down the computer without damage to your hard drive.  I had been putting off buying this for too long, probably because it's not a fun thing to buy. But after so many problems with local DC power - blackouts, unexplained reboots, blue screen memory errors for no apparent reason along with flickering lights in the house, etc. I finally bought this.  This one has the highest reviews with the best price.  Replacement batteries are easy to find and relatively cheap.  I even priced ebay for used ones, and they have plenty of these, most of them just needing a new battery.  But the combined price of both is the same or just a little less, so there's probably not much reason not to buy new.  And there might not be another UPS priced so low.  Would prefer if it provided power directly from the battery to the computer, instead of just trickling some off the wall power on its way, but those kind cost more, of course.  So this was the best choice, for me.

product_title: Xmi Pte. Ltd XAM18-BL X-Mini KAI2 Bluetooth Portable Capsule Speaker
review_body:
What a great little speaker! It's thoughtfully designed--the weird mushroom shape is with the speaker open. It twists closed for ultimate portability, and the hard plastic shell protects the sound membrane. Closed, it's about the size and shape of a yo-yo, but lighter.

The Bluetooth function works well. The controls are easy to see. The quality of the sound is amazing for so small a speaker. It's not tinny at all, there's a bit of distortion, but it's not terrible, and the volume is adequate to fill a small room or patio, unless you like to rattle your fillings.

It uses a standard Android USB and the initial charge took a couple of hours. There are different colored lights to indicate which setting the speaker is on, which is nice for dim lighting and/or poor eyesight.

One really cool feature is the jack cable wound up inside the speaker so it won't get lost. It's very short, but that's a minor quibble. It's worth it to have the cable secured.

This is a handy device to throw in a purse or tote.

review_headline: Awesome headphones even for the price tag
review_body: I got these for Christmas this past year, and although they have a rather hefty price tag, they are very high quality. The construction is a mix of brushed metal and some plastic here and there. I'm not the type who is particularly cruel toward my headphones, but these cans should be able to withstand a few bumps or scratches within reason. Couple that with the nice carrying case provided, and it shouldn't be in issue for portability or protection. Sound quality wise, they are phenomenal. I'm no audiophile, but the highs (female vocals especially) sound superb on these headphones. I listen to a very random/mix of music, and they sound great regardless of the genre. Although the cost more, they are very much comparable to the Audio Technica ATH-M50's. They deliver a very flat sound, not oversaturated with bass. They aren't studio monitors, so there are a (minimal) amount of audio enhancements, but it isn't overkill by any stretch. If you've got the money to buy these, I would highly recommend them. Sony has always been one of my go-to brands for tech, and these really deliver.

product_title: RHA Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphone with Remote and Microphone - 3 Year Warranty
review_headline: Great sounding earphones; Mine were pre-tested.
review_body:
Bought these based upon the "Wall of Fame" award rating on InnerFidelity, a website devoted to headphones, earphones, personal listening, and the related audio gear. The site puts a good bit of emphasis on trying gear out before you buy.

Shipment arrived promptly but upon removing the product from the shipping envelope it was evident that the product packaging had been opened and the earphones removed, used, and then returned. Personal gear like this - it works best with a snug fitting into the ear canal - really should be inspected, disinfected, and resealed before sending it out again. (Or advertise it as an "open box" and offer a discount.) I've ordered dozens of things from Amazon and this is the first time something like this has happened. If it was something less personal, I probably wouldn't have mentioned it. I hate it when that happens.

My buddy had no reservations about trying the RHA 750 out. He tried a couple of different earpieces from the 8 or 9 pair that comes with the phones and found a good fit. Fit is important. A bad fit and the sound quality doesn't match the price tag. A snug and comfortable fit in the ear and these earphones (IEMs) produce spectacular sound, way beyond what Apple's earbuds or the cheap things given away with smartphones. They are worth every penny. Make sure you are comfortable with IEM's before you commit. Some people can't get used to them.

product_title: Nakamichi Bluetooth Over Ear Headphones BTHP02 Red
review_headline: Sometimes you get More than you paid for
review_body:
I was looking for a pair of inexpensive bluetooth headphones to use at home for watching tv and listening to the occasional music on my phone. I already have one pair I paid $40 for and I like them, but I'd like to have a second pair available for when the other is dead or charging. I couild either pay $32 for the black ones or $19 for the "red" ones (full disclosure: they're more of a reddish-orange....eek). I figured that since these were ghoing to be my in-house headphones I'd go with the uglier yet much cheaper version.

They turned out to be just as ugly and flimsy as I expected for under twenty bucks, but the positives were every bit that I hoped for as well. They paired easily to the two devices I've used them with so far, and they fit snugly and comfortably on my smaller-than-average head. The sound was actually good, although the mids and highs were sacrificed a little bit for the lows. They lasted about 8 hours (my others last about twelve), and took less than 90 minutes to charge. Because they are made with cheap plastic and are pretty flimsy, I don't see these as being very durable....I doubt they could live through being dropped on the street. But for home and office use these are a great option for the budget-minded person.

Pros:

Price
Comfortable fit
Good bass
Easy pairing
Reduces outside noise
Price

Cons:

Not durable
Not stylish
Volume control awkward
Battery life

I like these a lot, and if they stay under twenty bucks I'll probably get another pair.

review_headline: Replay Audio BTS1RD Portable Bluetooth Speaker - Very good sound for its size & price - Easy to sync & control - Recommended
review_body:
This very portable Replay Audio Bluetooth Speaker produces very good sound for its size and price range. It is just 5.75 4 inches long x 2.25 inches high and about 1.255 inches from front to back, and only weighs in at about 7.4 ounces (per my postal scale). Nice portable unit with good sound quality and volume when fully charged.

Upon arrival we plugged its USB power cord in to our Samsung phone's wall adapter, and the speaker fully charged in about an hour. After that, it rocked! Pairing with our phones was quick and trouble-free, and we tested it with our Samsung Galaxy S3 and HTC Droid DNA (with Beats Audio). Bluetooth range was very good, easy traversing 15 feet -- better than most other similar devices we have tested. Typically the phone paired with the speaker was within three to 8 feet of the speaker, with line of sight between the two devices.

Our son liked the controls on this speaker better than controls on other speakers he has tried out as the volume and track-change functions are quick push for volume, and long-hold for track change. This make so much sense as we play with the volume so much more often then track-change, that the quick push is easier to perform... quickly. That's a nice change.

When the speaker is seated on a good surface (like a table or counter), this speaker pushes out very good bass and nice mid-range, with good highs. When held in-hand or laying on a soft surface (like a comforter), the bass doesn't pop quite as nicely. The version we received is quite nice looking; black paneling surrounded by red trim, that feels like anodized aluminum. The four little rubber feet on the underside actually do a great job of keeping this speaker from sliding around, and we like its look, feel and performance very much.

Neither the Amazon listing or the retail documentation mention a warranty, so if an issue occurs I would return here to update the review and let you know what the issue was and how resolution was handled. We did receive this speaker gratis from the seller and our son put it to use to objectively find out how well it performed. My statements here reflect that testing.

If you are looking for a portable Bluetooth speaker of this style, size, capability and affordable price, for use similar to what I have described above, then we would recommend giving this Replay Audio BTS1RD Portable Bluetooth Speaker a try based on our experience with it. It seems well designed, looks quite nice and has worked very well so far.

review_body: I received these earphones as a gift to replace the old, high-end, Shure ones I lost several months ago. Perhaps I can't remember the Shure ones well, but these are really awesome.    Sound: They sound good out of the box and improve with a few days of burn-in. I really appreciate the expansive stage these drivers are able to create, you can clearly hear what is at the forefront and what is in the background. Music isn't muddled, there's a lot of depth, and the timbre is true to the instrument. For classical music, you can hear each section and pick out solos. Like everyone else has mentioned, the sound is very warm. I'm not sure it suites every type of music, sometimes music is meant to sound angry. The bass isn't as overwhelming as some may like for pop music, and the treble sounds tinny/thin initially. Both improved with burn-in and more sound-isolating tips.    The over-ear design was really intuitive and comfortable for me. Just dangle over my ear then fit the buds into the ear canal. Cord is a lengthier than most, but its convenient (I'm just over 5ft, cord dangles to my feet). There is some cord noise/microphonics that comes with running. One thing that my Shure's had was a connection midway down the cord, so you could unplug and move away from the computer without having to pause the music (else it would blast into environment), and easily move back. It as really convenient. With this cord, I feel tethered to whatever device I'm plugged into.    There are a lot of tips provided, but I didn't like them much. None fit great. Silicone medium fit one ear well, but not the other. They don't have great sound isolation. Foams fit the other ear better but were less comfortable, ears felt like a stuffed sausage. These foam tips are stiff, like dried out circus peanuts. I went with foams for sound isolation and ordered some other brands to see if they'd be better. RHA customer service is excellent. I lost some tips and they were kind enough to send a complimentary replacement pair without question.    UPDATE: With more burn in, I found the bass sometimes overwhelming and treble underwhelming (Caveat, I'm swayed to being a treblehead). The bass can really pop and cover up the already quiet mid-range frequencies. I recommend using an equalizer to achieve the sound you like. I toned down the bass, boost the mid and mid-high's. The drivers is very responsive, and it opens up the stage sound. The recording quality also becomes more evident now, and there's sometimes static with poor quality recordings. With regards to comfort, a lot of people say these buds are heavy, but I've worn it for several hours without discomfort. Foam tips definitely are the best of the lot for me. They are the most noise isolating (still not great 'cuz I don't turn volume up, but I can tune out the environment) and do the best job of capturing the music (especially the bass. Silicone ones seem to loose the bass and some of the midrange.

The USB part comes off, exposing a regular plug socket, so if you don't need that at the moment you can pop it off and have just a regular plug.

I'm not sure what the problem was, though, but while the USB ports did a fine job of charging my devices (an iPad 2 and an iPhone 5S) they did something funny to my devices. Didn't damage them, but when plugged in the touch screens behaved erratic when touched. It was like the juice coming from the charger was messing up the capacitance of the touch screen causing it to miss-read my finger taps. I literally had to unplug the device from the cable to use it, then plug it in and let it charge. That was a little annoying at times, especially before I figured out what was going on.

I'm not sure if it's a fault of the product, a symptom of the adapter and US equipment, or an incompatibility with Apple components (I don't remember signing a license agreement with Apple to allow me to travel with and use my ipad/iphone in this manner, so maybe that's the problem....)

product_title: AmazonBasics Ultra Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_body:
This antenna is excellent in Houston. I should note that the antenna is paper thin, but eyeball measurements put this at about 8 x 8 inches wide (bigger than I had expected it to be).

I found the most success with this when it is placed above the height of the TV, and somewhat away from the TV in distance.

I actually ended up placing this in the attic by using the existing DirecTV coax cables that were already running to the TVs in the living room and the bedroom (just got rid of satellite and I'm loving every penny). I plugged the antenna into the splitter that was installed by DirecTV, and then plugged the existing COAX cables into two separate TVs. This way I didn't have to run any new coax to the TVs. It is completely hidden up in the attic so it is not an eyesore for me in the least. It is just hanging from one of the rafters in the attic.

To reiterate, I am using a coax splitter to send signal to two tvs. I have not noticed any loss in signal quality. It recommends using the powered antenna if you plan to split, but I do not think this is necessary. Split signal works perfectly for me!

It gets excellent reception and fantastic picture quality. I have not had any issues with it so far.

To recap, this product works best when it is placed high in the air. You may need to spend some time figuring out the best way to aim it.
I suggest placing it in the attic if this is at all possible. For those in apartments, it may be a bit of an eyesore as it needs to be angled towards the towers and placed high up on the wall.

review_headline: Good price, Good construction and Good sound
review_body:
I bought it on sale. It was advertised for $40 with a MSRP of $140, what a deal. Guess I didn't notice the
street price was around $140. No big deal, for $40 I am still pleased.

I opened it today, Christmas Day, as a present to myself. The tag as wrapped by my wife said "To Dad From Dad".
It is of good construction and includes the necessary micro USB charging cable. The instructions were clear and
concise.

A few connections and switches on the side. One for the micro USB charging and an On-Off switch. Last would be an
AUX port if you don't have a bluetooth device. This entire area is covered by a rubber cover.

On the front panel which includes a grill secured by numerous machined screws. A red light helps to give you charge
status and a blue light for bluetooth pairing.

The body is covered in a rubberized material and has a good weight. On top are soft controls for bluetooth, volume and
skip/FF. The cover gives it substance to help it not slip from your hands. I've had it one day so I can't comment on battery life.

The sound is surprisingly good. It is loud while also being clear. A good amount of bass for such a small device makes it even better.
I haven't had other speakers, but to me it sounds good enough. I used to to play Christmas music while I cooked breakfast this morning
and wasn't worried about food spills.

For the price of $40 or even $60 I think it is a quite good deal and the rugged aspect gives you the ability to use it in many environments
beyond those of many other bluetooth speakers.

review_headline: HI 2050 VS ATH-W5000, not as unfair as it might sound
review_body: I bought these out of curiosity and at their price they are without question affordable, I have as my main driver ATH-W5000 which is a great pair of headphones but they start at $700 at the very least, I got mine for $850 and I decided to compare the takstar directly to them because why not. I mean what is the worst that can happen?  I will say the obvious, the ATH-W5000 won but, there was a few areas where the takstar handled surprised me or was better, sound stage on the W5000 is good for a closed back headphone, better then most or one of the best at that category. However the takstar was on a different level, sound stage was larger, hands down just larger. The highs on the takstar also were more present, however to me I personally find myself to be sensitive to high end treble. The takstar was just bordering on what I would deem as acceptable and too much, mind you I still need to burn mine in and I expect that to become more acceptable over time. What won to me is the actual pads they used on their headphone, the W5000 uses lamb skin from Spain, it feels nice on your skin and what not but there is one massive flaw with this. They didn't put enough foam in this and the foam they did use is soft. Because of this the driver actually touches my ears. Over time I got used to this feeling and it didn't bother me till I got the takstar, After using the pads on this which are a deeper and harder foam that doesn't let the inside of my ear touch the driver I really have to say that I prefer this cheap ear pad over the expensive lambskin ear pads the W5000 uses, no joke.  What got to me is this, the detail between the two is insane. The takstar is surprisingly close in detail to the W5000, a lot closer then I really thought they would be. Back in the 90's if you threw $50 on headphones what you got was something that sounded like someone was talking to you with their hand over their mouths. In the 2000's you got something even worse then that and it was just plasticy garbage that broke the moment you looked at it funny. Now in 2015 you are getting something that would have been $150-180 back in 2007. The build quality is something that shouldn't be possible at this price range. They are actually solid, the box it comes in is nice, it actually seated into a holder which is covered in cloth also. Mind you not amazing cloth but again, $30-50 headphones here. The due fact that you get a box the size of the traveling case my W5000 blows my mind. But what really gets to me is that this does not at all cut into the detail you get from them. The detail that they put out is simply better then any headphone I have heard at this price range. They are even better then the $150 headphones I have heard and actually compare to some of the $200 headphones, at sub $50 range.  Now I said all these nice things about it and crapped a bit on the W5000 yet still think the W5000 is a better headphone, the reasoning behind that is because the W5000 I can hear everything, bass, mids, and treble and to my ears everything is about on the same sound level and I have not heard these headphones distort once at what I consider normal volumes. Audio queues in games to me at least are more easy to point out on them and in music I feel like I am still getting everything. To me the takstars just don't sound like everything is coming through as clearly because they are more colored but they have a tightness which I didn't think was possible and I know for a fact that there will be someone out there that will like these headphones because they agree with their listening preference. To anyone who might like treble focus headphones and you are ok with the mids taking a bit of a back seat then these might be the headphones for you. For me, these are being used on my smartphone, they seem to pair really well and don't even need an amp. I'm still floored how well they handle at the sub $50 price range and I will be paying attention to takstar to see if they make sub $300 headphones now. Probably sound something like the sennheiser HD700 or something crazy like that.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Essential for those who are easily distracted while studying.
review_body:
These are great headphones. I will note one thing: The noise canceling by itself does not cancel out talking. But you know what? That's not what the technology was designed for! The noise canceling technology was designed for canceling out continuous noise, such as the noise that construction workers experience during their work. It cancels out background noise phenomenally. If you turn on a little bit of brown noise or music in the background, though, it does drown out talking pretty well, though. So don't discount the noise canceling. These work very well. In fact, when they're turned off completely the design of the headphones themselves still muffle sound really well. I bought these because they have the best noise canceling on the market, but they also have very nice sound for music. I consider that a nice perk since I did not buy them to listen to music.

Just a recommendation, but if you use these very often like I do, keep spare batteries in the small pocket inside the case. You'll know the battery is dying when it starts turning on and off continuously. (No, it's not broken!) I just wind up the cord in a coil and stick in the case instead of putting it in that pocket so I can use it for that purpose. See the photo for what I mean.

Enjoy the headphones! You'll love them.

review_headline: Great Antenna for the Money. Good Bye Cable TV Company.
review_body: Wow. What an antenna for the price! I purchased this antenna because Charter Cable decided to squeeze some additional bucks out of their loyal customers, by requiring all TVs in your home to have a cable box. Satellite systems are the only other alternative as UVerse is not available in my area yet. Having a TV in every room, I decided to try an HD Air Antenna as a possible alternative. I live out in the sticks 50 to 60 aerial miles from the city. Luckily I had wired the house with home runs of coaxial cable and was able to regroup my eight now unused TVs into one 8 way splitter/amplifier coming off this antenna. I installed the Antenna as high as I could indoors in my attic. I was really amazed that I am able to get 20+ clear HD Channels on every TV in my home. Rotating the antenna will bring in additional channels but will also loose some channels. If the wife could do without watching the Discovery Channels, I would do away with Charter Cable completely and save the $200 a month. review_headline: and holy crap they handle the lows really well
review_body:
To those who are complaining about a lack of low-end, I think you need to look into your audio source rather than blame these headphones.

I bought them specifically to use with an old bass guitar headphone amp, and holy crap they handle the lows really well. Even with a 5 string's low B (around 30Hz), it rattles my skull before it distorts. Literally cannot get the volume loud enough to distort them. I have zero complaints there.

They're only comfortable for ~20-30 minutes at a time. I wear glasses, though, and I have a strong preference for over-the-ear style rather than on-the-ear like these. I'm attributing my discomfort to these factors rather than poor padding/design.

Yeah, they feel kinda cheap. But they are cheap, so that's okay. I'm not expecting machined billet aluminum at this price point, nor should you. If you're looking for something that can handle some power and produce nice bass tones on the cheap, consider giving these a shot. Feed them a good signal and you won't be disappointed.

What I like: The platter stops spinning when you lift the needle arm. It also has a little lever to lock-down the needle arm when not in use. It comes with a little disk for 45's, too, that's in its own little slot near the platter. A great purchase for the price!

The footprint is much smaller than it looks in the photo. A 33 rpm record hangs over the sides. So, it doesn't take up much space. This has been a good purchase; I'm sure my friend will enjoy this and her many records which she hasn't been able to listen to for years!

CONS: Material is a cheap quality MDF board--laminate only covers the faces that are seen (the back and underneath the unit are exposed particle/MDF board). The instructions are not clear in certain points--the illustrations do not always accurately indicate which side of the board (the finished or unfinished side) is to be used. OTHER NOTES: WARNING: The lower shelving areas lack depth--areas for the AV equipment are shorter than the advertized width (15.5\\") of the unit! I could not fit my Yamaha AV receiver in this unit nor the matching blu-ray player until I used a jigsaw to cut out massive rectangular holes for the units to stick out of the back. Even then, the receiver barely squeezed beneath the top shelf. (On a positive note, the exposed rear made installation of plugs and wiring easier!) The shelf measurements are: ~21\\" wide (between the posts, and between the post and the support pillars at the end), 6.5\\" high (barely fits most AV receivers), and only 12\\" deep to the back wall. Fortunately, the full unit depth is 15.5\\", so any overhang you have with your receiver will still be below the top shelf.

On a related note, the shelves are also somewhat short, only 12\\" deep as well.

product_title: Sangean America Inc AM/FM-RDS/Bluetooth/USB Table-Top Digital Tuning Receiver
review_headline: Better Sound, Better Bargain Than Tivoli
review_body: Last summer my wife and I each bought a high-end tabletop radio: I, the Tivoli Model One Bluetooth; she, the Sangean WR-22. I loved the retro 50's look of the Tivoli and the outsized sound, but there were a couple of problems. One, the Tivoli does not pair very easily with the Bluetooth app on my I phone. It usually takes several tries, and you often have to "turn it off and turn it on again" to get it to connect. But I also thought the bass sounded "buzzy" as if I had blown the speaker, though I had not played it at an overly loud volume. The Tivoli people replaced the radio and new one sounds fine, though I'm still suspicious that the bass signal, especially if prominent in the mix, overdrives and distorts at even moderate volumes. Then I listened to my wife's Sangean. The bass is clear, clean and deep at moderate to loud volumes. Unlike the Tivoli, you can adjust both treble and bass. So, I got myself the Sangean WR-22 to have at home, and consigned the Tivoli to my office for background music. The Sangean has been remarkable: a huge sound with great clarity. The Bluetooth pairs immediately, every time. I got the model with the walnut veneer which looks very nice. Granted, the digital face is not as warm as the Tivoli but it is very functional and the remote works perfectly. I can easily choose 5 FM station presets. It hurts to say this, as I want to support an American-designed product in the Tivoli (although it is manufactured in China), but the Sangean (headquartered in Taiwan, made in China) beats the pants off the Tivoli in terms of quality of sound, functionality, programming options, and price ($50 to $90 less, depending on the Tivoli model).

product_title: EnjoyGadgets EGVGARCA Generic PC to TV/VGA to RCA Converter
review_headline: You wouldn't want to type a word document on it with 12 pt font but it provides a picture perfectly good enough for presentation
review_body:
Worked perfectly for me for the price. If you search around amazon, you will notice that there are a LOT of these exact unit with just different brand names printed on them. Seeing that, I decided to go for the cheapest one. The unit works well enough for my application. Does it provide as sharp a picture with any input resolution as my Kramer converter that costs about 20x as much? No, of course not but it was able to push a completely serviceable composite signal over about 75 feet of coax to my switcher and then back 75 feet to a 40" tv. You wouldn't want to type a word document on it with 12 pt font but it provides a picture perfectly good enough for presentations or standard def video.

It comes with all the cables but not a USB power supply. The idea is that you just plug the usb cable into your computer or laptop as needed but the settings will reset every time it is powered off so you will want to get a small cheap 120v to usb power plug for permanent installs.

There are 2 DIP switches on the side and the "manual" that comes with this does let you know that they are used in selecting between PAL (European TV standard) and NTSC (USA TV standard). What it does not tell you is which switch or which position for either setting. Mine came set to PAL from the factory and by just flipping the switches, switched to NTSC by moving the left switch down.

product_title: Outdoor Splashproof Bluetooth NFC Speaker,SOLEMEMO SE90 Rugged Shockproof Dustproof Portable Wireless Speaker,Rich Immersive Sound for Outdoor Sport and Shower & bath
review_headline: A small, durable speaker, but with quirky buttons for volume
review_body:
I've had good experience with a variety of SOLEMEMO products. This Bluetooth speaker is no exception.

It is well built, with a solid look and feel. Bluetooth pairing is easy (tested with iPhone 6), and sound quality is good for a speaker this size. For me, it is a good companion to take on the back deck and enjoy while I work on homework.

A couple things to note:
* At first, I thought the sound quality was bad...too much hiss. The problem was quickly resolved: turn up the volume on my iPhone to its maximum setting, and use the volume controls on the speaker to raise and lower the volume. If, on the other hand, I set the iPhone's volume to something in the medium range, then I immediately notice the hiss on the speaker. This is not a criticism of the speaker, though. I have experienced this same effect with other speakers as well.

* One minor complaint: the \\"+\\" button serves two purposes: skipping to the next song, and increasing the volume (similarly, the \\"-\\" button moves to the previous track and decreases the volume). The instruction manual says to \\"Press the 'Volume up' or 'Volume Down' button to increase or decrease the volume. It should say \\"press and hold\\" the button. Several times, I have made the mistake of restarting a song, when all I wanted to do was adjust the volume. I can never seem to get it quite right, but I'm getting better at it.

All in all, despite my issues with the volume buttons, I'm really happy with the quality of this speaker. A great choice for the price!

Reviewer's note: I received this speaker free from SOLEMEMO for the purpose of testing and reviewing.

Who knows if the bass boasts just the right balance between quantity and quality or even what the heck phrases like that even mean!?! Not me!!

It could be that despite their laid-back nature, detail and clarity are not at all compromised which is another statement that makes not one lick of sense to me. Attach a 33 Ohm impedance adapter (e.g. Cowon Sound Capsule), and the mids gain an even more balanced presentation which might or might not be a good thing. Who knows? Their treble very well might have a raw and edgy nature to it, but remains well within tolerance according to reviewers who think they know what their made up phrases mean. An airy and expansive soundstage is the Titan 1's true fortÃ© according to some but, again, no clue how that even is supposed to describe how they sound. Isolation is near non-existent unless you're an audiophile living in a dream world.

To reiterate: they sound good to me. They fit well in my ears. They remain comfy. All those flowery descriptions mean nothing. Got mine on Massdrop for considerably less.

product_title: Bluedio Turbine T2s Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Mic, 57mm Drivers/Rotary Folding
review_body: Great service by Amazon, as expected.  When I first turned on headset I was disappointed. Sounded muddy, tin can. I messed with preset EQ settings and still wasn't pleased.  I bought a pair of Nakamichi BTH06 at the same time that sounded twice as good out of the box for less money.  Decided I would keep the T2S for car / working out activity because they have a more secure fit.  Well after a couple of weeks of everyday use they are starting to sound better.  I have worn them for 8 hours staight and have had limited discomfort.  The battery life is stellar!  Went a week without charging.  It connects flawlessly to my Samsung S3 phone.  Phone calls sound great on my end, but recipients can tell I'm on a headset / speaker phone due to background noise, so on important calls I just hit the headset button on the phone and switch to phone mode.  Fortunately, it automatically reconnects when the call ends.  It would not connect to Windows 7 Ultimate on my Lenovo T500 bluetooth -  fault of Microsoft, Really?!  So I bought a cheap ORICO USB bluetooth dongle, installed and now it works great.  Nakamichis wouldn't connect either but now do.  I read somewhere in a review that these will sound even better once they are broken in.  So I turned them up full blast and left them for about two hours.  I don't know if that helped or just the constant use, but the sound has gotten much better from day one.  I just did another sound comparison versus the Naks.  The bass is finally hitting the lower frequency and highs are starting to sing.  I'm NOT an Audiophile, but own dozens of headsets and listen to all kinds of music from Dub step to classical.  I wasn't expecting perfect sound but compared to the Nakamichis, out of the box they sucked.  I bought mainly for the metal headband durability and battery life as these are gym / ball bound.  They are well made and have already taken some abuse.  Anyway, for $35 bucks - Four Stars for me!  If you are an impatient person who likes instantgratification - two stars.  I am just glad I didn't send them back and look forward to several years of use.   Update 07/13/2016 - I've been using the Bluedio T2s for almost everything. Gym, kayaking, basketball court, landscaping, job sites, etc. They have held up well.  The white is getting dirty.  Been caught out in the rain several times. But really, the sweat I have exposed these to is ridiculous.  Holding up well.  Getting a little loose on the head but they have been put through hell and still hold on better than the Nakamichis - which have had little use other than the office.  The Bluedio's still sound great.  Ordering another pair the instant they start to malfunction.

product_title: Grado SR60e Headphones
review_headline: Danm Brilliant Unique sound and US made! One word.........Winning!
review_body:
I wanted a high end set of headphones but I'm also on the Made in USA kick. From what I can find these are the only US made headphones; handmade in New York from a family business. Anyway, these headphones kick ASS! A lot of negative reviewers complain about the sound leakage but they must be listening from a train wreck. The sound is clear and plenty loud, yes you can hear outside sounds but it never distracts from the music. These might not have the thundering bass and may not have the deep theatre power of other spendy brands but Grado doesn't claim to. They're a bit treble focused but the low frequency sounds are deep and crystal clear not pounding. What sets them apart is the ability in any song to separate every instrument and vocals from the instruments. They especially shine on live recordings where most headphones and speakers fuzz and sound terrible Grados let you hear every thump of a drum stick, every pluck of a guitar string and even the lip smacks of the singer as if you were standing in front row of whatever concert. It's hard to explain but it's damn brilliant.
The build quality is great as well. They use a larger cable than most brands for durability and to get a better signal to the ears foremost. They have simple foam pads that are comfy and you can get replacements when they wear out. A nice tight steel head band keeps them firm to your head. Too tight for some but they stay put when you're somewhat active. Yes, they are very old school looking but I'm an 80's kid. I think it's kick ass to have a retro look and state of the art technology together. Compare them to Beats, or Bose, or Skull Candy you'll see they are every bit worth the $80 for SR60's or $100 for 80's with a unique sound experience. I love em.

This speaker replaces a tiny clamshell speaker with the Verizon logo on it. I use it about an hour a day to listen to my mp3 player as I get ready for work in the morning and when making dinner in the evening. 2. Nice weight and form factor. I don't think I'll travel with it a lot, but it's small enough to be tossed into a travel bag without too much worry. And it seems solidly built enough to stand up to the wear and tear of travel.
3. The amplification is a little noisy, much more so when using the wired jack. If you just turn the speak on, you will hear an audible hum. In a room without any other significant noise, you can hear it 5 feet away. The hum is not noticeable if playing music except between tracks, but can be distracting when listening to podcasts or other spoken word recordings because of the pauses between words and sentences. The hum reminds me of old tube amplifiers, something rarely heard with modern digital equipment.
4. The screen feels like epoxy coated metal, is quite sturdy (no flexing) and the diamond shaped indents are both stylish and make it easy to hold when carrying it around.

product_title: Monster Clarity HD High Definition In-Ear Headphones
review_body:
I received these pair of in-ear headphones to try out from Monster. Initially, based on some comments, I was skeptical about how well these would work for me, but I am impressed with the overall quality. As a baseline, I believe the Apple earbuds are pretty good overall. I am a fan of Sennheiser products as well in terms of headphones and overall I like a nice soundstage with neutral bass.

1. What's in the box?: You receive the headphones, plus a sound decibel warning booklet, and two different pairs of headphone earbuds besides the ones already attached.

2. Aesthetic?: These really look like a serious product for an audiophile. Though these are relatively inexpensive headphones, the look is impressive. The black version with silver buttons and the Monster logo is a nice touch actually.

3. Use?: I received these, plugged the headphones in to my Iphone and tried out the sound with several different types of rock music and hip-hop.
First impressions are of the earbuds, which fit my ears just fine and provided a good fit and solid seal. I was immediately removed from my external environment as well, meaning there was good sound isolation.

Music was really quite good. The sound was certainly more 'live' than the Apple earbuds I have used. Similarly, I have used the Logitech earbuds as well and these sounded better in almost every category. Bass is more present in some songs than I expected as well. Unlike most earbuds I have used, I did not have to turn up the sound all the way to get the music loud enough for my liking. In fact, turning up the volume to full tilt was way too much. This is a near first for me with any earbuds. Positive!

In terms of soundstaging, for this price point I would not expect the moon, and I didn't receive it. However, the soundstaging is quite adequate and is good enough.

Overall balance of music is quite favorable and I enjoyed just about everything I have thrown at these earbuds. They are clearly better than anything I have previously used.

Buttons and mic: First off, this has a microphone for use with a mobile phone. Given that I still use an old pair of Apple earbuds from time to time, the lack of an ability to answer the phone is annoying, so much so that a mic is an absolute must. The mic works fine and is easy enough to use. As well, this has a button from stop and starting music and with the Iphone getting to Siri. This works well enough and is a great, but again, necessary feature. However, I cannot figure out whether you can moderate volume on these buttons. The box provides no instructions at all (irritating) and I have tried every single motion I could think of. This is a bummer because music and phone calls are not always consistent in terms of volume. I will try to figure out definitively this is the case but this is truly a bummer for an otherwise excellent product. I will add the cabling is quite robust and is flat, which discourages tangling as well.

Overall?: I'll say it. Monster would not be my first conceived choice for headphones, but this product is changing my mind. Frankly, for this price point, the headphones are excellent. The overall sound isolation is very good and the features are good. The sound is quite good. Darn good for this price point actually and are among the best I have ever used, frankly. The only disappointment is the inability to moderate volume on the cabling (at least I have identified so far - this is disappointing. On the other hand, the cable is flat, and robust and should be durable as well.

This is a very good, near excellent product and I would give this heavy consideration for this price point. Those looking for bass-heavy (and I mean heavy) buds may be looking for more, but I think everyone else is going to be pretty happy with these.

Update: I have been using these earbuds more frequently. The sound is very good. I utilized a different pair of ear covers and this made a difference for me so I encourage a bit of experimentation. While I really think these are nice, I cannot understand the only quibble which is the lack of ability to control volume with the control set. It sure doesn't appear to exist. This is not a deal breaker, but it is irritating. Does anyone have a suggestion or is this really a design flaw?a bit of experimentation. review_headline: Connects Old Technology to Modern Devices
review_body:
Highs: Reliable, very easy to follow instructions

Recommend: Yes
Item Tested: Ziotek PS2 Keyboard to UDB Adapter for an IMB Model M keyboard.

After purchasing an IMB Model M keyboard, this adapter was perfect as modern computers do not have a PS2 connector. Instead, newer computers have USB connector-great for jump drives-bad for my IBM keyboard. Thus, this is where the Ziotek PS2 Keyboard To USB Adapter comes in. The adapter is small, yet works like a charm. Simply plug the adapter into the computer's USB connector and you are all set to go. The adapter will be ready for you to plug in a PS2 connector.

Think of the adapter as a bridge that connects a PS2 connector to an USB. I have noticed a slight lag when using the adapter. When I turn on my computer, it takes a few seconds for the computer to make the connection. I believe this is perfectly normal as the computer is powering on.

Why four stars? The adapter is easy to knock out of an USB connector.

I gave a thorough explanation that I did nothing wrong, I tried other chargers and cables but could not get to charge... Again, thought she would try to get away from warranty service...

Nope, she replied with the address and email to print off and send with the box...

After delivery, she was prompt in replies and after getting my box they sent my return own within a few more days...

I get the box back and it was a new box, worked perfectly!!!

I mentioned that my box did vibrate off the corner of the table twice because of how POWERFUL the box is!!!!

I sent a video demonstrating me playing a song that made the box "walk" andcautioned that they need better feet that are "sticky" because if your not paying attention your box will "walk" off the edge and you need to pay attention! product_title: Monster Mobile Clarity In-Ear Headphones with Apple Control Talk
review_body: I'm using these to replace some Jabra headphones that I actually really liked. Both sets are similar in that they are noise-isolating in ear phones that can be used with my iPhone or other device. They both also have a no tangle cord which is an important feature. Trying to untangle a headphone cord before use is always a pain.  These headphones actually sound a little better than the Jabra's and seem to have more bass. The tips that were on the phones seemed to fit me the best. I assume these are the mediums, but it says to try the different sizes for a tight fit for noise isolating.  These also have a few neat little gimmicks that come with them. The cord winding case is actually an iPhone stand, which is pretty cool. I use my phone when I'm sitting outside listening to podcasts and music, and having the stand makes changing songs and channels easy.  I also thought the magnetic ends so you can stick the earbuds together and wear them around your neck when not is use was kind of cool. There is also a clip so that one earbud can be in your ear, for phone conversations, and the other one can be connected to the shirt clip, so that it doesn't dangle and get in the way.  Many headphones/earbuds have the microphone on the right side, but the microphone side on these seems to go in the left ear. You will actually notice a sound difference if the earbuds are in the wrong ears, so if you are unhappy with the sound try switching ears.I thought these worked well and for the price seem like a good value.  The only drawback to these is they are slightly bulky. Once you have these in your ear the ends are big and stick out a bit. Not the end of the world, but the biggest con in my opinion.  My last pair of Sennheiser headphones cost around $300 and I wore them out in about a year taking them to work. I've noticed prices have come down considerably since then. These really sound pretty good, so I don't know if a Sennheiser comparison is fair unless you can find Sennheiser earbuds that are comparably priced.  Update 5/30/2015: I was using these headphones to listen to podcast during my hour wait at the DMV, when they called my number I put these in the side pocket of my cargo shorts and took care of business. The next day I was looking for my new favorite headphones and realized they were in the pocket in my shorts that had just gone through the washer. I hadn't put them in the dryer, but they did go through a full wash cycle. Miraculously, they still work fine. These ended up being more durable than I had imagined.

To start I pulled runs of quad shielded coax to each room and dropped the source end into my media closet.  Then I bought a $15 over-the-air  HD antenna (this one from RCA http://amzn.com/B001GGAIIQ)  and connected that as the "source in". review_headline: It feels very good in my hands
review_body: I have been looking for a bluetooth speaker for the last 4 or 5 months.  I was very close to buying the Bose SoundLink Mini and Grain Audio PWS, but I was unhappy with the muddy sounding low end, and I couldn't find a local store carrying the Grain Audio.  I stumbled across a review on YouTube from a guy named Oluv (ClavinetJunkie on YouTube).  Oluv has reviewed over a dozen bluetooth speakers over the last year, including the Envaya Mini.  He has a side by side sound comparison, he used high end audio equipment to record all of the different speakers, and I was very surprised when I heard the Denon.    So I ordered the Denon online, and it took a month and a half to get to me (I did not order it from Amazon).  I received it this week.  It is packaged very well;  inside the box was the speaker, a cloth carrying case, and a USB cable for charging.    First thing I noticed when I took it out of the box was the weight.  This thing is HEAVY for its size!  It feels very good in my hands;  The enclosure is all metal, with the end caps being rubber and the feet being rubber.  One end has 4 buttons;  Play/Pause, Volume up, Volume down, and power, while the other side has the power level indicator, Aux input, and USB port.    I turned it right on and it paired instantly with my computer and my smartphone.  To pair, I just had to hold down the Play/Pause button for a few seconds, this puts the device into discover mode.  I fired up some tunes via Spotify, and the first thing I noticed was the bass sounded fantastic.  I was very, very surprised how well this handles low end frequencies.  The low end starts to roll off at around 70 or 80 hz.  The frequency response for this is very flat and even.  The only frequencies I thought were a little off and could have been boosted a little more were the high end frequencies.  The high end sounds great, but I think it could have been boosted a little bit;  You can just adjust this via EQ if needed.    I also noticed the DSP kicking in and adding little bit of compression when your device is at 100% and the speaker is at 100%.  I run the speaker and smartphone at about 75%, and it sounds fantastic.  I have checked out dozens of speakers in the past few months, everything from Bose to Sony to Beats to B&O.  For the money, nothing compares to this speaker.  It outperforms speakers twice as expensive.  I was originally leaning towards the Bose or  Grain Audio PWS bluetooth speaker;  I am very happy I held off and discovered this little beast.  I say its comparable in sound to the $300 Bose SoundLink III with a slightly smaller soundstage and less stereo separation.      I highly highly recommend this device.    *UPDATE*  I have had the speaker for about a week now and have spent some considerable time listening to it.  I noticed the speaker isn't as loud via bluetooth as it is through using a 3.5 MM cable to the Aux port.  Also, if you angle the speaker back about 20 degrees I get a much deeper bass.  I downloaded an EQ for my iMac so I have some tonal flexibility (Boom 2), I plan on downloading one for my smartphone as well.  I have noticed the battery life isn't as advertised as either, which seems to be the industry standard anyway;  most companies release misleading battery life info.  They claim 10 hours, I have gotten between 7 and 8 hours while listening via Bluetooth at  50%-70% volume  (Mostly around 50%).  I know the speaker was only $150, but it would have been nice to have some more flexibility with the speaker.  Like a companion app for a smartphone with a visual EQ.

I purchased a swatch of the material large enough for anyone to build up to a 135' screen (I cut mine down to about 120'). After taking some measurements, I went to my local Home Depot, and bought the hardware I needed to build the frame and border. I then went to a local fabric store and bought about 3 yds of black felt for the border pieces (more than enough) and I built my screen. product_title: Sony ICF-S10MK2 Pocket AM/FM Radio, Silver
review_headline: What a Blast - Live Sports Won't Get Any Better
review_body:
In an age of ever evolving digital electronics, it's nice to know some things never change. I have iPods, iPads, Echos, computers, and smartphones, but you know what? I can't get a live baseball or basketball game on any of them.

There is no small amount of irony that the money obsessed big leagues who force you to buy expensive subscriptions to their digital feeds get absolutely nothing when you dial in on a little twelve dollar transistor radio.

I can't even begin to explain what incredible joy it gives me to tune in this little wonderful machine and listen to radio the way it was meant to be listened to. If you have never sat outside in the middle of the summer, sipping on your preferred beverage and listening to your favorite baseball team on a transistor radio then, my friends, you have been missing out on something special.

Just like you remember it, the stations feel like they are all jammed together on the dial and sometimes it is hard to tune into a specific one, but you know what? That's half the fun. Pull out the antenna and aim it as best you can for the best signal and you will be just fine.

What a blast. It's retro as retro can be and a great deal to supplement your digital life. Truly, I'm actually surprised they make anything this cool anymore.

product_title: The Anchor - THE ORIGINAL Under-Desk Headphone Stand Mount
review_body:
Never realized why I didn't get one of this amazing product to organize my headphones and keep them out of my sight while not in use. Well now that I have it, I can only say that I highly recommend it to anyone who uses headphones and want it to be tucked away in a place that does not become an eyesore. I took it, put it under my desk in a place that is completely invisible to me when I'm sitting on a chair close to it. Yet I can just reach under and grab my headphone easily.

So is it worth $15-20? That depends on how many head sets you have, how much organization you want on your desk, and whether you want a cheaper alternative or make one for yourself.
Thing is, while it maybe a bit pricey, it is really worth the money. I got it when it was on sale for $14 and I would say it's worth all the choices that are out there (unless you love DIY kit and projects).

One thing to note: Like others said, the adhesive is VERY strong. So be careful and decide beforehand where you want to place it. Once you put it there with a gentle push, it will stay stuck to that surface immediately.

If you think you want something worth getting to hold your headsets...this is one of those products. A must have for those who want beauty, elegance, and simplicity on their PC desks.

It will stick to you as a good product like it will stick to the surface you place it.

Would buy another piece when needed.

product_title: WHARFEDALE - ACHROMATIC WA-S1 BOOKSHELF SPEAKERS (PR)
review_body: I'm using these speakers as both mains and surrounds on an Onkyo TX-SV545 I picked up in a Goodwill for $15 (w/remote and user manual). Its dated but works flawlessly. The center channel is a Wharfedale WA-S2.with two JBL PSW1000 subs (dialed way back). The break-in period isn't over yet but I'm liking these speakers. The set-up is in an 11' x 12' room; small but its our "quiet room". Its got all the comforts of our living room but not meant for company. Used for both music and movies these speakers perform quite well at low and moderate volume. very detailed and warm. I have the mains hooked up to a speaker selector switch with 3 other pairs of speakers at the moment: Polk Audio RTi-A1s, Pioneer SP-BS41s and Panasonic SB-S270s. The latter intrigued me for their power handling capability (140 watts), age (20+ yrs.old) and price ($4). I find myself gravitating to the Wharfedales every time with a close second to the Panasonics. Sometimes I pair them up but most of the time is the Wharfedales only. Their small size produces a rich, detailed, natural sound at lower volumes which is what I wanted for that room. I'm very pleased so far.

My resolution for now is black electrical tape which works on black equipment just fine to prevent any stray signals from getting directly to the equipment. If the units were behind closed doors in a cabinet---- then it would be a non issue, but in any event, the soundbar would still be a problem as it is right under the TV and still would be exposed. No fault of this equipment, just the nature of the situation.

In the end, I will definitely use this unit again as it flat out works great and has up to three inputs without having to do anything hokey. Also the one IR receiver is on a 45' extension in the other room.... no lag, no issues, works great!

product_title: Sanus BF24B 24 Inch Speaker Stands (Pair)
review_headline: the quality is actually pretty decent. I've read some other folks that had ...
review_body:
These are on of the cheapest speakers stands that you can get. And for the price, the quality is actually pretty decent.

I've read some other folks that had problems with the wood cracking when they were putting this thing together. I did not have that issue myself. It might be that I just got a good batch, but I also think it's important to take a little care when screwing the stands together. Use a hand screw-driver, and when you have to tighten the 4 screws down for the top platform, don't just screw them down completely one by one. Screw them down until you feel a little resistance, then move to the next screw. Once they are all almost all the way in, tighten them up a little bit, one by one. This will ensure that the platform get's tightened equally on all 4 corners, rather then tightening one side down all the way. Doing the latter will make the opposite end come up a little, and then when you tighten that corned down the wood will crack.

According to the - very limited - instructions you should be able to put the wire cover in place, after you put the whole thing together. I couldn't figure out how to do that. I ended up having to take the top platform off to slide the cover in place.

Still 5 starts though, since they actually look quite nice for the price. Can't go wrong with these.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Home Control for Control of 8 Home Entertainment and Automation Devices
review_headline: Great, comfortable, universal remote that you can program via your smartphone
review_body:
We recently got one of these to replace our dying Harmony 880 remote as we had gotten a new cable DVR & the older remote wouldn't control it. We love this. Setup was pretty simple using my Moto X. That was one of the things I was looking for. We no longer have a PC at home & instead have 2 Chromebooks for my wife & I. The Harmony software will not run on Chrome, so setting it up via our smartphones is very handy. Setup didn't take long, just had to input model #'s. I love the fact that through the hub this will control things via IR, Bluetooth, or RF. This controls our Vizio TV, Sony home theater system, cable DVR, PS3 for blurays & DVD's (via Bluetooth), & Amazon Fire TV (via Bluetooth). We have the hub sitting in our entertainment center in between devices. From there it sends the commands via IR & Bluetooth to our devices. There are only 3 activity buttons, but all the buttons on the remote can be programmed to control 2 operations by a regular short press or a long press.

The remote is very slender & comfortable. It uses a small CR2032 (?) battery.

There are only a couple of things that we wish were different. We were used to our Harmony 880 being backlit. This remote is not & that would be nice, but the 880 also had a charging stand & I assume having backlighting would kill the small battery. The other issue we ran into was setting up macros. For example if you long press 1 on the remote we have it set up to change the channel on our cable DVR to channel 404, 2 is 409, etc. Due to the limited space on the smartphone programming screen, we could not set up as many macros as we would've liked, not because the remote was incapable of it, but because of the accessibility of the smart phone screen.

All in all, we love this remote & like that since it controls the hub via Bluetooth you do not have to have a line of sight connection with the remote & your devices.

product_title: B&O PLAY by Bang & Olufsen 1287632 Beolit 15
review_body:
The Beolit 15 is an amazing sounding, compact, Bluetooth speaker. Like many, for me Bang & Olufsen represents extremely high-end equipment. I recall going to the local audio stores and lusting for the B&O equipment. That said, this is my first piece of Bang & Olufsen equipment and it does not disappoint. I have listened to it for about 20 days and I love it.

The bass is deep and punchy but not muddled or overpowering, the mids are good (not perfectbut its a portable speaker), and the highs are clear but not shrill. We currently have it about 2 feet from a wall about midway down in a 45 x 20 room. This little gem fills this room with clear, unvarnished sound, even at max volume levels! I have been able to go anywhere in our home (3,000 sqft; 2 story) and have not lost the BT connection to my iPhone 6, this is quite impressive. The speakers front and back give a near 360 degree presence to the sound. It provides 70 watts of clean power from two Class D amplifiers so it gets loud, and stays clean and clear.

There is no volume control or EQ, which is standard fare for most BT speakers (Our Klipsch KMC-3 has volume and a remote). However, our devices have volume control and there are apps for EQ. However, I didn't find that the sound needed EQ whether listening to Beethoven, Led Zepplin, or Five Finger Death Punch...it just sounds great no matter what source you put to it.

We have gotten about 20 hours out on charge at low to medium volume levels. The cord is sufficiently long and stores nicely in the back of the unit.

Lastly, the unit is completely balanced when carried by the strap.

Yes, it looks a bit like a picnic basket, but this picnic basket rocks! If the Beolit 15 is in your price range and you want an amazing Bluetooth speaker I recommend it.

review_headline: Great for resting my Kindle in landscape mode while watching a movie on it.
review_body:
ZinGo offered me a free sample of this speaker in exchange for my honest review.

I have had the pleasure of owning and reviewing a couple Bluetooth speakers recently. I find that most of them are similar in terms of design, quality, and sound quality. The ZinGo speaker is certainly unique as compared to others that I have owned, which is a nice change.

This speaker is right around 12" long and fairly lightweight for its larger size. It is a pretty basic speaker in terms of its functions and really is designed to play music, and hold up your devices. My kids bought me a Kindle Fire for Christmas and I am just starting to use it more often, specifically for watching movies (Amazon Prime Movies). I'm getting older, so I sometimes have trouble hearing sound coming from my Kindle. That's where this speaker comes into play! I am able to place my Kindle in either landscape or portrait mode in the groove on the front of this speaker and rest my Kindle so that I can watch a movie while not worrying about holding it. The ZinGo speaker holds my Kindle at the perfect viewing angle. Whats more is that I get the added benefit of having an external Bluetooth speaker, which allows me to hear the movie I m watching with crystal clear sound that is loud enough for me to hear.

For my purpose of watching movies and streaming the occasional oldies music, I find that the sound quality is just fine with this speaker. I'm very happy that I received this speaker and it will get a lot of loving from me and my Kindle.

product_title: OM Audio INEARPEACE In-ear Headphone with Mic and Remote for Apple, Black
review_headline: Like sitting front row center at the concert
review_body: My wife originally purchased a white pair of the IEPs as a Christmas present for me.  Absolutely blew me away.  I don't have the terminology of some when it comes to reviewing equipment such as this, but I do have a pretty discerning ear.  I spent a GREAT deal of time about 15 years ago auditioning equipment before purchasing my Krell power amp, Enlightened Audio Designs preamp/processor, Aerial Accoustics 10T, center and surround speakers, and my Wadia 270 CD transport.  Pretty good stuff.  It gives me a tremendous wide, deep sound stage with lots of air around the instruments.  I could close my eyes and with just about pinpoint accuracy put the instruments and singers around the soundstage where they belong.  When I first heard my IEPs, THAT is what I felt, it wasn't like my other headphones.  I heard things, instruments, subtle things in the music, off to the side, or underneath, almost hiding behind other instruments.  Beautiful layering.  I heard instruments that were just not there with other earphones.  Also, the dynamic range is beautiful.  It reminded me of the first time I put an RG Dynamic Range Expander on my old stereo back in the mid-1970s, and the experience of a soft piano or accoustic guitar passage being played, then the singer's voice jumping out of the speakers.  The IEPs give that same, tingnling experience.  Then they broke.  Something with the cord.  I too had some trouble tracking someone down to help me.  That brilliant sound was gone.  BUT, I am happy to report that Dave at the company got back to me last week and sent me a new pair, in black (which I preferred anyway, the white ones had been on sale on Amazon back in December), which I just received two days ago.  I plugged them in, and the first song reminded me immediately just how much I had been missing using my other earphones, which, by the way, I had spent a good deal on.  The IEPs crush any I have ever owned.  That these are not flying off of the shelf at the prices here on Amazon,especially sub-$70, is insane.  If they had a differnt company name, one from a more visible company like Sony or JVC, these would be on most every high end reviewer's list of must have's.  I hope OM Audio gets there, because they clearly know how to make a quality product and price it more than fairly.  We consumers should be rewarding that effort. product_title: BRAVEN BRV-Pro Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker [15 Hours][Waterproof] Built-In 2200 mAh Power Bank Charger - Black / Red
review_body:
Bluetooth products are generally a hit-and-miss affair. There seems to be two important factors in whether Bluetooth will work well or not (i.e., maintaining pairing and not randomly dropping sound): first, it needs a recent version of Bluetooth (the Braven BRV-PRO has the latest); second, a good battery that is fully charged. So far, the BRV-PRO battery lasts longer than most such speakers I've tried, although I will purchase the optional $50 solar panel that mounts on top of the speaker. (Braven BRV-PRO accessories will probably be available on Amazon before long; otherwise you can to to the Braven website to purchase them.)

I got this speaker mainly for use on my motorcycle and bicycle and for other outdoor activities, mainly to use with my Amazon Fire phone and my GoPro Hero4. I also have an older convertible (without Bluetooth technology), so this will probably also serve as a hands-free communications option in my car, and the noise-canceling microphone is an important factor for use on a motorcycle or in a convertible. In my research I haven't found a Bluetooth speaker that is as versatile as the Braven BRV-PRO or that seems as durable (although, only time will confirm or discredit that impression). Another feature I welcome is that the BRV-PRO mounts on my GoPro accessories--I don't have to buy special mounting hardware. The light weight (less than 1.5 pounds) is also a plus when mounting any device on handlebars or dash mount. Finally, the IPX7 waterproof rating seals the deal. I don't do much in the way of water sports, and even when I do I like silence when I'm on (or in) the water. Nonetheless, it's nice to know this speaker will survive a dump in the lake or a sudden downpour. I appreciate the fact that a tie-down strap is included in the box. Even with the best mounts, I am always nervous when on my motorcycle that a pothole or road debris will dislodge the device and send it skidding and bouncing down the highway. Securing what I consider the "safety strap" through the little handles on each end of the speaker and around the handlebar gives me a little more peace of mind.

And I didn't forget about the sound. Of course, a speaker this small will not sound like your home stereo speakers or any decent sound system. Nonetheless, the Braven BRV-PRO sound is surprisingly robust. It is actually the best-sounding Bluetooth speaker I've tried (I have four other brands that I've accumulated over the years). Even the bass is pretty decent for such a small speaker--probably, I suspect, owing to the design of the surrounding space inside the speaker housing and advances in small speaker designs.

If you are looking for a versatile, great-sounding, and well-made Bluetooth speaker, I highly recommend that you consider this one.the "safety strap" through the little handles on each end of the speaker and around the handlebar gives me a little more peace of mind.

product_title: SPARC HD Radio SHD-TX2 Portable Radio with AM/FM & HD Radio Tuners, Built-in Speaker and Emergency Alerts
review_headline: Decent performing HD receiver for AM and FM.
review_body:
AM FM battery powered radio, runs on 3 AA cells. Receives regular old AM and FM analog, analog FM stereo, appears to also receive analog AM stereo. Also receives AM and FM HD (hybrid digital) radio. Reception is decent on both FM and AM. I own a first generation radio shack HD table radio, this radio outperforms it easily on receive sensitivity.
Non-dimmable display shows frequency, battery, signal strength, and any scrolling text from the station. All controls are push buttons, there are no knobs to turn. The telescoping rod antenna only swings side to side, not front to back. The radio is smaller than it appears in the photo here on amazon. It's case shape makes it prone to falling over, it does not want to stand upright, but can on a flat surface, but the case is rounded, standing upright is difficult. There are inputs for headphones and power supply (included).
Sound quality is decent for the size of the speaker. The AM receiver is not as good as an Amax standard AM radio but it does receive CQUAM AM stereo. The radio does not reject adjacent channel noise very well, the AM design is below average but they intended that you would be listening to digital AM radio (which seems to be partially abandonded by many stations).
This radio easily stores pre-sets on both AM and FM, then use the side to side buttons to step through them in order. Press power briefly to switch between AM and FM.
One thing you should know about HD Radio, it was intended to allow radio stations to place ads on the screen of your radio, in addition to one or two additional digital channels. There is also the capability for radio stations to change which stations you have memorized in your receiver. I do not know if this receiver supports those features, nor do I know if those are still being done in some US cities.
All in all, this is a decent performing radio, FM is way better than AM. I get most HD stations on FM without even pulling out the rod antenna.
Update: Been using this radio for a while now. I recently went camping in central-southern AZ. I was listening to AM, to 1070khz KNX from Los Angeles. I thought all AM stations running HD radio shut it off at night but my radio went into digital mode a few times listening to this distant station. The point here being, the tech works and the receiver on AM is well designed.while now. I recently went camping in central-southern AZ. I was listening to AM, to 1070khz KNX from Los Angeles.
