product_title: HMDX HX-P470 Titanium Portable Speaker
review_headline: Discreet, very portable, but has a big sound.
review_body:
Packs a punch for such a small speaker. It is only 6" long by 1" wide x 2 1/4" tall and weighs less than a pound. It has a nice matte finish with a hint of shine from the grill. I was skeptical at first. My other bluetooth speaker is much bigger and heavier and has great sound and range, but I wanted to be fair to the little guy. I gave it a full-charge which took about 5 hours the first time. It was a breeze to connect to my iPhone 5c. Just turned on the bluetooth on my phone, then pushed the button on the end of the speaker. It makes quite a loud noise (louder than the music) at start up and then again when it connects or disconnects so don't use it around a sleeping baby or light-sleeper husband. Once connected I was very impressed by the clarity of the sound. I had to share the amazing quality with my, now awake light-sleeper husband. He couldn't believe it either. It doesn't have the bass punch that my bigger one does, but a lot of the time, with the music I listen to, I don't want or need a lot of bass. The sound stays clear and clean even when turned up. Again, surprising for it's size. Of course it won't compete with a surround sound system, but I don't always need the full surround sound affect to be happy.

My biggest use for this speaker is to play songs that I have loaded on my iPhone so I can play along with them on my ukulele, anywhere. My ukulele will drown out my iPhone, but I can hear the music when I connect it to this speaker just fine.

It is easy to place out of sight if you want. It's so portable you can take it camping, or out to the deck and keep it by your lawn chair, grill. It's also good for the bedroom, kitchen or bath ( wouldn't get it wet though) It will sit on any shelf or bedside table or out of the way in the kitchen. The range is pretty good. We don't have a large house, but I was pleased that it stayed connected from one side to the other, even with a wall between. UPDATE: I would take off 1/2 star because it turns over pretty easily. The base could be a little wider or heavier. Other than that I still love it.
When my phone rings, the speaker picks up the call seamlessly (no loud noise this time) and then starts up the music once the call if over without ever touching the speaker. The battery life is very good when fully charged.
It has three soft touch buttons on top that control start, stop and volume or you can control it from your phone. It also has a headphone port on the side. One con, the charge chord is very short - just over 10 inches, and you'll need an adapter to use it in an electrical outlet. product_title: Definitive Technology CS-8060HD Powered Subwoofer (Center Channel)
review_headline: Clear gorgeous baritone dialog. Ear candy.
review_body:
I'm running this center with the BP-8060ST towers and Mythos Gem surrounds. I'm driving the setup with a Denon AVR-X4100W.

I absolutely love the power, focus and sound that comes out of this center. I was previously using a Polk CSi A4 center; the Definitive is a massive step up.

You will need a proper receiver to get the right sound out of the Definitive Speakers. I tried testing this center on a $400 Yamaha unit and got sub-par results (not bad but...not worth the price of admission). Anything in the $1000+ range should perform well and will show you what this speaker is capable of. If you run an Audyssey setup I got the best results by setting the sub volume to 12 o'clock on the back for the Audyssey setup, then dial it up to about 2 or 3 o'clock after running Audyssey if you are in a large room. Some tweaking is natural if you run Audyssey with a Bi-Polar setup (as is indicated by Definitive). Don't just go with what Audyssey gives you, experiment.

After tuning out my system I got just beautiful dialogue out of this center. The sub does exactly what you want it to which is add gravitas and full range to voices with a baritone signature. Sound effects and gunfire sound solid when they come through this speaker as well. There is plenty of punch and clarity. Voices like Bane's in The Dark Knight Rises really shine on this center channel. You get hit with the full impact of his voice.

This speaker fit perfectly into the center channel drawer of my BDI Avion cabinet and sounds great recessed in there as well. I had some concerns that placing this speaker in the cabinet would have a bad effect due to the 8" woofer being located on the top of the speaker. I have no complaints however and find it still sounds great. I'm sure not-recessing it would make the sound even better though if you are planning to use this with the Avion, i'd say don't let that hold you back.

If you're a fan of removing speaker grilles you may not like this center. The grill is more of a mesh that surrounds the speaker. Theoretically you could unwrap the mesh but there is no easy way to remove it and put it back on quickly. I could care less myself and find no point to removing the grille. The clarity on this speaker is top notch and that's even going through the 2nd cloth grille on my Avion setup.

Build quality is high and the speaker is really nice looking. The left and right end-caps come off the speaker easily allowing you to replace the mesh if you ever had to.

product_title: Bluedio Model R Revolution 8 Tracks Built in Mp3 Player Hi-Fi Rank Wireless & Bluetooth Headphones (Red)
review_headline: I am also able to wear the headphones throughout an entire day due to the comfortable design. The audio quality is superb and br
review_body:
I have had these headphones for 7 months after receiving them as a Christmas present and they have done wonders for my productivity at work. The noise cancellation aspect of the headphones really cuts down on the distractions from side conversations around me. Although it doesn't remove all external noises, it cuts down 85-90 percent of the noise. I am also able to wear the headphones throughout an entire day due to the comfortable design. The audio quality is superb and brings out nuisances in songs that are missed with lower quality headphones.

The only issue that I have had with the headphones, which many other reviews have pointed out, is that the plastic around the extension piece is too weak. The band has to be pushed out slightly to place on my head, which stretches the hard plastic and ultimately caused the plastic to break. The headphones band snapped after only 7 months of use, taking it too and from work. The reason this is still a four star review and not lower is because of the great response by the support team of Bluedio. They responded within an hour and ordered me a replacement pair within two hours, thanks to the 1 year warranty that comes with the purchase.

I would still recommend purchasing a pair of these headphones, but I would add the caveat that I would get a hard case for them and be careful about stressing the plastic.

review_headline: Impressive - Don't listen to the naysayers
review_body: I am compelled to write a review because of all the bad reviews out there on Bose about being poor sound quality and poor built quality.  I own the Soundlink Mini as well as several other Bose products.  The build quality is excellent and durable.  Do they use polymers or plastics for their headphones, yes.  That is on purpose to limit fatigue from weight.  Most reviews that trash Bose provide little evidence as to what they mean by poor sound quality.  They don't talk about the high or low registers, they just say a blanket statement like sound quality isn't the best or you can buy better for less.    Here is my review of the Soundlink Mini  * Easy to use    * Sound quality is impressive    * Low, mid and high registers are impressive. I have eclectic taste so I listen to a little bit of everything, gospel, classical, country, hip hop, etc    * Impressive bass    * Little detectable sound distortion when you turn up the volume.    * Price is Fair.  People state you can find something comparable cheaper but you aren't just simply paying for sound.  Personally I paid for their excellent customer service and a great product but I also paid for class and elegance.  I much rather have the Bose Soundlink sitting on my desktop that something like the Pill by Dre.  I am an adult not a teenager so when I spend my money I want it to also reflect who I am as a person.  Bose is the sports car not the Honda civic with the aluminum goofy spoiler bolted to the trunk. If I offended you by the honda comment, good.  That stuff is goofy and you should know better than putting a spoiler on a car with about 143hp.  https://lh5.googleusercontent.com/-0BzY4pf2csI/VIoC3eXsIQI/AAAAAAAACMA/FbcPuDU_qGY/w1000-h548-no/BoseSoundLinkMiniDresser.jpg    * Build quality is great in my opinion.  Anodized aluminum case. What more is there to say.  Did I throw it on the floor or drop it to see if it survives?  No, why would I do that.  If you want that I am sure someone on youtube has done it.    * Itbrings a nice charging base so you don't have to keep plugging in    **Cons**  For the price I think the could have thrown in a free carrying case.  Same thing with their wireless bluetooth headphones.  I paid $249 and it came in a little cloth bag.  Come on, you guys can definitely do a little better than that.    ** Customer service - I have had a product malfunction because I ran it over with my desk chair and customer service was beyond helpful.  They sent me out a new part right away with no charge.  Everyone's experience will differ but to me this means a lot.  The company truly stands behind their products.    ** Recommendation - Don't listen to people.  Go to one of the Bose showrooms and listen, feel and touch. You will be pleased.

review_body: Well I don't know about everyone but I do know that making a decision about what earbud to buy has been quite a challenge. I used to read up on every little aspect of an audio purchase and was comfortable and proud to be able to learn my way to the best purchase for me. Heck I used to know every car on the road by their shape. Now a days there's just to much information and to many choices and reviews and opinions etc. It can be a real challenge to cut thru the info. I do depend on Amazon's rating system, realize that many reviews can be bought or trumped up but also feel like I need to be part of the solution. "If you don't vote then shut the hell up" kinda philosophy. So for this review I will reveal that I originally bought the S5 at about twice the cost of the S1. And I love them, I listen mostly to books and what is now Classic Rock etc and they are great but I find I'm not organized enough to always have them handy and I wanted to buy something less expensive that I could keep in the truck for the times when I needed earbuds. I listen to books while I'm shopping, hiking, filling up with gas etc. Anytime I'm outside and not at home. The S1's are perfect for this kind of use. No their not as awesome as the S5's but they get the job done. Their not as flashy as any of the more popular brands but the price for me is doable and the sound, fit, cord length, tangle resistance etc meet the grade. If your older, ok with the cost and like a good set of buds without the anxiety, feel comfortable with this purchase. Oh, and I've got a 15 year old daughter that has borrowed these so much over her hip brands that I ended up seeding them to her and got another one for myself. That should tell you more about their quality than the longer reviews.

product_title: Sony SRSX5 Portable NFC Bluetooth Wireless Speaker System
review_headline: WOW. Packs a punch in the sound department.
review_body:
Wow. This little speaker packs a mighty sound. I'm very impressed with it. I wanted something that was bluetooth so I could listen to the music from my iphone 6 while at home, and to be able to keep the phone close to me at the same time. In other words, I didn't want to have to plug it in and then have to get it if the phone rang. Right now my phone and I are about 20 feet away from the speaker and it sounds great.
After I ordered this I went on to youtube and saw that someone posted a comparison between this unit and a Bose one. He played a jazz song to compare the sound of each unit. I was disappointed because the Sony sounded like it had too much treble, and the BOSE one sounded rich with much better sound. Please, please please, if you go to youtube and listen to that review, disregard it. It's so not accurate. This Sony SRSX5 sounds way better then the comparison on youtube.
First of all, it has a great balance of bass and treble. Neither one seems to be overbearing. It has an overall full sound. Also plays loud. I haven't even pushed the volume up all the way and it's plenty loud for my small one floor home. Earlier today, I just left the unit on, with the volume up a little high. A little while later, as I was sitting at my computer desk, I decided to listen to some music and just put my music on from my iphone. I didn't have to go across the room to turn the unit on because I had already left it on. I adjusted the volume from my iphone.
Some people say that if you unplug it you'll lose some volume, but I haven't tested that yet. I'm really not interested in using it without the plug. I just wanted a good sounding speaker to use at home that I could also pair with my phone via bluetooth.
It's also a very basic setup. I turned the bluetooth setting on my phone on, and in a few seconds it recognized the Sony SRSX5. Once it recognized it I was able to start playing music. Easy as that.
The AUX and USB is in the back next tothe power plug and easy enough to figure out how to use them if I ever need to.

If you want a small speaker system that has really good sound, then I highly recommend this.

review_headline: Music in the Morning-Works Pretty Well
review_body:
I don't have music in my bathroom, probably the only room in the house not wired for sound. So this seemed like a cute little product so that I could catch up on the morning news while starting my day.

=== The Good Stuff ===

* The unit is a reasonable size, maybe 4" across and about 3" deep. It sticks on my mirror with no problem, although it was somewhat more problematic on ceramic tile (sort of sticks) and the shower doors (not at all).

* The sound quality-what do you expect. It is sort of muddy through most of the midrange, and highs and lows just don't exist. But it is certainly OK for a few minutes a day, and fidelity isn't really all that important to me in the shower. It is loud enough to be heard over the running water without too much distortion. In short, if you want great sound in the shower, fork out some serious bucks for waterproof speakers. If you just want to hear a couple tunes, or some news while you get ready for work, you can't go wrong with this speaker.

* It lined to my iPhone6 with no problems, and syncs up in a couple seconds when I power it up.

* There is a phone capability, so this speaker can serve as a remote speaker/microphone for your bluetooth phone. It works, but I will never use it. I haven't reached the point where I need to have a phone conversation while taking a shower, and probably never will.

* It takes a couple hours to charge, and plays for roughly 6 or 8 hours at reasonable volumes on a full charge. (See note below). There is an indicator light to tell you when the charge is complete, but no way to estimate remaining battery life. The same indicator light indicates that the unit is ready to play/powered up.

=== The Not-So-Good Stuff ===

* The volume up/down buttons on my speaker didn't work. The iPhone did not respond to pressing these buttons. It did respond just fine to the skip track buttons and the pause function.

* The biggest problem is battery life. The unit powers itself down if not used for "a while", but this time seems to vary greatly. A few times it was on several hours after I stopped using it. As a result, I seldom get more than a couple mornings out of a single charge. I was hoping for a week.

* When you sync, or press some of the buttons, the speaker has a number of audio responses to tell you what is going on. Unfortunately these are at FULL VOLUME, the last thing in the world I want at 6AM...especially if someone else is trying to sleep. There seems to be no way to mute or quiet these sounds.

=== Summary ===

It works OK for what I want, but could definitely stand a few minor improvements. The auto-off should shut down the unit after a few minutes, and the control sounds need to be mutable. The sound quality isn't great, but perfectly acceptable for what this product is. As for being waterproof, it has held up for a couple weeks, but time will ultimately be the judge of that.

product_title: NZXT Digital Controller Cooling Fan with Grid AC-GRIDP-M1
review_body:
This little black box is very handy if you want to phase out your 5.25" bays but need a fan controller. Sure, you could control your fan speeds through bios, but not every board has that ability. Plus it's impossible to do if you're trying to change your speeds on the fly.
It's small, easily hidden behind many mobo trays, or near the top/bottom of the case.
It comes with velcro pads, and they're hard to pry apart, so I doubt they'll fail you. They're not the usual hook-loop type of velcro, but some weird hook-hook hard plastic hybrid.
It's also kind of small, so you barely notice it in your case.
The program that you run it with is pretty nice, but it is the weakest link for this product. While it let's you create a variable profile to ramp up/down your fans at certain temp readings, the polish leaves a little to be desired. Also, if you want a smooth transition from low RPM to high RPM, be prepared to be in the interface for a while. You have to plot each point to make it go up or down smoothly. That's the reason for 1 less star.
I still like it though. When I do my next build, I'll get this controller again, or the next one in line if this is not being made anymore.

product_title: SONOS P3 Color
review_body:
A pair of PLAY:3 speakers and a pair of the also excellent SANUS stands was my introduction to the world of SONOS audio, and I'm very impressed with both the quality and ease of the system. I had considerable anxiety on both counts prior to purchasing, but am a total convert now.

Ease: Unboxing the equipment literally took longer than setting it up. It really is as simple as downloading the app and following the brief directions. You'll need a WiFi network and the password to access it, and a free controller app (mine is on a Samsung Galaxy Note 3). That's it. As of September 2014 you don't need a bridge, just the speakers. I set up a left-right stereo pair in a room called "Portable" because I expect to move them around until I can afford to turn my house into a SONOS showroom. After setup the SONOS controller app found the music on my Android phone automatically and I was listening to music a few short minutes after unboxing the speakers.

Quality: The sound quality is surprisingly good. It's true that you don't get really deep bass, but it's an order of magnitude better than the Bose Soundlink II we also own. The ability to make a stereo pair also makes a huge difference in ambience compared to a single speaker.

The quality and ease of this system are well worth the cost. The flexibility of multiple rooms and multiple sound sources to me is icing on the cake, but also demonstrates the thoughtfulness of the designers. A very solid 5 star product if there ever was one.

product_title: uxcell 5 Pcs 4-Pole 3.5mm 1/8" Male to Spring Plastic Head Audio Adapter Connector
review_headline: Works well, but very difficult to solder
review_body:
They are a HUGE pain to solder, then close up without shorting out... The tolerances are very close. I trimmed every bit of extra solder and wire I could, and still they were nearly touching. Too small to tape all the bits, I resorted to filling it with rubbery glue, then letting it dry a little before squeezing it back together so the plastic cover could screw-on. You need to have just about exactly the right wire (thin, tough, solid, 4-conductor) for the job. You're not going squeeze 3 RCA cables, or a 3-prong cable+1-RCA cable through. Two strands of 2-conductor probably won't fit, either. I happened to find old USB cables (5-conductors) fit the bill quite nicely.

At some point, they shouldn't even sell solderable plugs like this, and only sell you the pigtail leads, with a few inches of wire already attached, ready for splicing into. I'd have bought the pigtail version instead, even for several dollars more, it would just save so much effort. Remember the old days, when you had 1/2" plugs with just TWO poles/contacts? These 1/4" plugs with 4-poles is simply a nightmare, only recommended for expert solderers.

Worked just fine for what I needed. Made some custom audio+video cables with multiple different plugs, adapters, splits, etc. Didn't really have any other options than these, or else buying several expensive 4-pole cables and destroying them.

I was not required to write a positive review and I do not rate products higher than they should have been. I am disclosing this in accordance with the Federal Trade Commission's requirements.

To test the receiver, I used another Bluetooth speaker that happened to have an audio input port so you could directly connect devices. Once I connected the Inateck Bluetooth receiver to the speaker, I paired my Nexus 7 tablet which was fairly simple. The audio quality was great.

The built-in battery allows for flexibility in where you use the device since you don't need to be near a power source. If the picture doesn't show up, the middle silver button is the size of a quarter so the device itself isn't much larger.

Versatile: Consider this device can act as a Bluetooth receiver (for music) and support phone calls, it gives options for how it is used. Some users may find this perfect for their car, where others may have a home stereo just waiting for an adapter like this.

Bottom line: If you are looking to add Bluetooth audio capability to an existing system (home, car, or whateveryou come up with) this is a great device worth considering.

review_headline: Unique look, quality build and a sound that exceeds expectations
review_body:
First things first, I received this product free for the purpose of review. It's my hope that the impressions and observations I share here will prove helpful to you in your decision making. If you have specific questions, feel free to post them to the comments section, and I'll do my best to answer them based on my own experience with the product.

What you're getting with this order is 1 pair of genuine wood, ear bud headphones from Symphonized. Also included are silicone earpieces in s,m,l for best user fit. They appear as pictured in the product description photos with the exception being that the grain of the wood is more visible than the pictures can portray.

Ok, when I review headphones,I want to make sure we're talking about proper expectations with regard to price. At their current price point, I am reviewing these in the upper range of the budget price category. Now, I tend to break the review down into 3 general categories: Looks, Build and Sound. I have thoroughly tested these in each of those categories with the following results:

Looks: This is probably the least important of the 3 categories, especially when it comes to ear buds, but if you're being completely honest, it's still important to most people. These are unique, the first pair of headphones featuring real wood housing that I've tested. I have to say that I really like the look. The wood is stained then has a silver accent between the housing and the white/blue silicone ear piece. These 3 colors look very nice together and combine to give these headphones an impressive style. Adding to the look is a braided nylon style for the cord which I've not seen a lot on headphones. Overall, these offer a different and individual feel that I like very much.

Build: With earbuds, there isn't a ton to talk about regarding the build but there are a few things at which I like to look. First the cord is firmly housed at the 3.5 mm gold plated jack end. I feel no wiggle or loose connection. The same is true where the cord meets the housing on each individual earbud. The housing has a quality build, with each bud reflecting perfect symmetry. The wood is sanded well and stained evenly. The silver collars on the housing are attached firmly and the silicone earpieces are well made and can be swapped easily. The braided nylon cord has no visible flaws. Overall, the build appears to be of high quality.

Sound: As usual, I tested the sound quality using audiocheck .net. I have to say that I'm always a bit surprised at the varying opinions on sound quality when reading reviews of the same product. This serves as a good reminder to everyone that sound quality ends up being a fairly subjective category because we hear differently than others. Here are a select few of the testing results:

frequency response: This tells you the bass and treble boundaries of the headphones. They advertise a 10Hz bass extension and a 23kHz treble extension. While this is fantastic, both exceed the range of human hearing, so I can't personally test them and it doesn't much matter. I was able to get 20 Hz and 20 kHz (and I have to recruit younger ears to hear the 20kHz), if you can hear a higher range, then you're in luck with these.

quality: Using a file that sweeps through a range of frequencies and is meant to physically shake the drivers, I tested the headphones for rattle and buzz. I found no problems whatsoever indicating a quality build.

driver matching: A quality stereo sound is centrally reproduced in these headphones indicating that drivers are matched.

wiring: There is a left and right channel (these aren't marked on the headphones) and polarity is preserved indicating proper wiring.

subjective listening: I listened to a variety of music from bass heavy hip hop, to treble ridden pop, and even the spoken voice only audio of a podcast. I was impressed with the bass in these and I do wonder if the wood housing is a help to recreating a rich bass in a small earbud. I obviously have no way of knowing, but I did like the response. While the bass is impressive, especially at this price point, these shine even more in the middle and upper ranges. Overall I'm very impressed with the sound quality, especially in the budget price range.

One other item of note: as of the posting of this review, these headphones are eligible for free shipping to members of Amazon Prime and that's always a bonus.

Were there any negatives? I've only been using these for a short time, but to this point I cannot point out any negatives. The build should allow for heavier duty than just about any earbud style headphones could be with the wood housing and the braided nylon cording. If I note any negatives in the coming weeks, I'll come back and edit my review.

Bottom line: From their unique appearance to their quality build these headphones impress and that's before you take into account that they're competing in the budget price range. Throw in a quality sound that, for me, exceeded expectations at this price point, and you've got a can't miss pair of headphones here. review_headline: Overall this is a very good AV receiver
review_body: Overall this is a very good AV receiver.  I have a pair of over 20 year old Polk speakers and this receiver had no problem driving them to very loud levels without distortion.  The sound quality was top notch.  The Airplay feature worked without a hitch with both an IPOD touch (4th generation) and an IPhone 5.  I have 3 minor issues with this receiver that keep me from giving it 5 stars.  The first is that the sound level from the headphone jack is very low.  You have to crank up the master volume level to almost the maximum to hear sound on your headphones at a decent level.  The second issue is that the tuner's ability to pick up AM stations is pretty poor even with the antenna connected.  I rarely listen to AM radio so not a big deal for me but if listening to AM radio is important,  I would not recommend this receiver.  Finally,  the zone 2 RCA out jacks will only work with analog sources and not digital.  As an example,  if you want to listen to one of the music channels on your cable system in zone 2,  you will not be able to hear if you only connect the HDMI cable from your cable box to the receiver.  You also need to connect the RCA audio out from the cable box to one of the RCA audio in the receiver to be able to get sound in zone 2.

product_title: PowerDriver 4 Bay Slot Smart Power Battery Charger Fast Battery Charger for 9V Lithium Rechargeable Battery with LED Indicator
review_headline: Simply put - an excellent little 9V charger
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:49338b8146f81dc53a9ad88fa075f04e]] Please note: I received a free sample for an evaluation and honest review.

I wasn't sure what to expect from a (currently) under $10 battery charger from a brand that I wasn't familiar with. Too good to be true? I'm happy to say - absolutely not. The hardware is well made, came packaged quite nicely, and works great. I can't yet speak to longevity, but it sure seems to be of good quality.

The video shows off the hardware (okay, there's not that much to show off :D) and gives my impressions of it, and below are the highlights.

Pros:
(*) Couldn't be easier to use. Plug it into the wall, plug in one to four lithium-ion 9V batteries, and the blue light on each battery slot will stay lit until it's charged
(*) Lightweight and nicely made
(*) Great form factor with a retractable wall plug. The charger sits flush against the wall when you have it plugged in, and it doesn't block the other outlet in a typical top/bottom arrangement
(*) Fairly quick charging times, with 400mA max for one installed battery, and 150mA max for each of four if you use all four. So, for a 600mAh battery, you can charge a single battery in about 1.5 hours or four batteries in about four hours
(*) Blue charging lights are easily visible but still subtle, unlike some chargers that have blindingly bright lights on them
(*) Charger was silent (from what I could tell), unlike several other chargers of mine that buzz especially once the batteries are charged and they no longer have a load

Those last two are big pluses in my book because I like electronics that aren't obtrusive.

I honestly can't think of a single con to this charger. Nothing feels cheap or poorly made, and it worked just great for me. A note, but not a con because the product page states this very clearly, is that it is designed to only charge 9V Lithium-ion batteries. I contacted the manufacturer to check if it is safe to charge other types of rechargeable 9V because the product description only specifically warns against trying to charge one-time-use batteries, and they said that this unit is not for NiMH or NiCd batteries. They make a [[ASIN:B00WZ8EDT4 2 Bay charger]] that will work with all three types of 9V batteries.

Overall, I'd recommend this if you have easy access to a wall outlet (and don't need an extension cord like some other chargers have). product_title: Pangea Audio - LS200 - Speaker Stand - Pair - 32 Inches
review_headline: These are really very good speaker stands
review_body:
On arrival you realize that these stands have to be assembled. I don't have any trouble with having to assemble them but I should have paid a little closer attention to the description where it said "Easy to assemble". Oh well.

These stands are heavier than they appear. If you have small children (I've had four) you don't want these. Actually I don't think you'd want ANY speaker stands because small children don't typically have presence of mind to not bounce off of everything in any given room. Not only will you have a damaged speaker, you may have damage to your flooring as well as a potentially damaged child. I suggest hanging surround speakers any time there are small children in residence. The stands top platform is a solid, thin sheet of metal. With such a thin sheet, given a bump hard enough to knock it over will give the stand enough force to cause all kinds of damage. Filling the front leg with lead shot will make the stand even heavier and I imagine that that would make it a little harder to knock over.

The stands are 32 inches tall making my surround speakers the absolute perfect height for my seated position. I am using Bostik Blu-Tack to "stick" my surround speakers to my stands. This has the added benefits of "adding" the mass of the stands to the surround speakers to help reduce smearing of the sound for louder, heavier or deeper sounds. It also gives the speakers a little added security so that light brushes or bumps don't knock the speakers off the stands. In addition the Blu-tack keeps the rough surface of the metal plate from scratching the speaker housing. The entire surface of the metal stands are a bit rough; not sand paper rough, mind you, but rough enough to scratch speakers like mine that are gloss piano black. I know that I'm not looking at the bottom of my speakers, but even still I don't want them scratched. I like taking care of my belongings and keep them as in good of condition as I can so that they stay good longer.

These are very sturdy stands and will give you very good service for a long time.that they stay good longer.

product_title: Polk Audio Camden Square Wireless Portable Speaker
review_body: At the Amazon price of <$100 I paid for this thing, it's a screaming bargain. This speaker is considerably larger/heavier  than many that sell here in excess of $100.  And it sounds it too.  While the sound quality doesn't reach the league of 'serious reproducers' (north of $300) , it's great at this price. If Amazon included the WEIGHT of various Bluetooth speakers in their listings it might help people calibrate their expectations about the quantity of sound and perhaps lower range capability they could expect.  The laws of physics really constrain what you can expect from a product of e.g. 50 cubic inches.  The diminutive size of many of these BT speakers doesn't really do them any favors.  My 'other' BT spkr is a Soundlink.  By comparison I'd say the Bose product is superior for portability and low-level listening.  But given the choice for a typical home scenario I prefer the Camden, it projects a much larger sonic presentation into the room.  My comments are those of a Classical/Jazz guy, so I am not qualifying my comments based on how much BASS the product can produce.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Home Control - 8 Devices (White)
review_headline: It's still a work in progress, but huge leap from the past Harmony remotes.
review_body: Frankly, I expected a lot more trouble with this remote based on many negative reviews. It is a product in progress and both the remote and App could be improved (the App especially feels likle it was built by amateurs). Nevertheless, for amount of functionality and breadth of supported devices this new Harmony can not be beat.    Here is my case. I owned a number of Harmony remotes in the past and am a big fan of the platform. All of my previous remotes were Infrared only, but I have PS3 and, recently, Amazon Fire TV Stick, both of which are Bluetooth based devices. So I was still collecting a number of different remotes on my couch that I had to switch based on what I was doing. The real reason though I decided to upgrade my remote was addition of the smart light switches to my home and SmartThings Hub that is controlling all smart lights, dimmers and AC outlets I installed over the past month. I wanted a remote that would not only control my TV and electronics, but also allow me to dim the lights when starting the movie.    I spent few hours reading and watching reviews of the new Harmony Home Control. Most of the negative reviews were split in two categories. The first revolved around the remote that did not work (either because it is faulty or device is not supported or user does not know how to troubleshoot it). When you see too many of these reviews, it gives you a pause about reliability of the product. Thankfully, this is not the case here as only fraction of the negative reviews were specifically describing faulty devices. The majority of bad reviews were centered around App and some very specific compatibility issues. So I reasoned that App will be improved over time and most of the specific complaints did not apply to me.    FIRST IMPRESSION:  First thing that surprised me when I opened the box was how slim the remote is. It is very stylish and feels great when holding. All the buttons are easily reached by one hand and are in the place I expect them tobe. It was almost as if I had used this remote for many years before and my hand had muscle memory of it still lingering.    I will also come to the negatives right away. First one (and this is BIG) is lack of back-lighting. Frankly, I don't understand the rationale for this. Yes, lighting keys would bring the cost a bit up and it would require a more beefy batteries installed, but this is such a common request from everyone that for Logitech to omit it in premium remote is a head scratcher. It's like buying a Mercedes only to find out that it omits cruse control. Ridiculous!  The second negative is the a lot of keys are grouped too close together. When you are trying to feel them in your hand, it is not obvious were one button ends and next one starts Logitech should have either created better spacing, put ridges around some most used buttons or use central pimple on buttons to quickly identify them.    INITIAL SETUP:  Setup was super easy. Gone are the days when I had to connect my Harmony to the PC over USB cable, carefully plan the activities, sync it, then go to TV room only to find out that something was not working just right and repeating the whole cycle again. This time I specificaly decided to do setup anew (as there is also an option to port it from your previous Harmony profile). So  sat on a couch in front of TV with remote and tablet (both Android and iPad tablets worked fine, though iPad interface was more refined). I prepared myself to struggling with setup and back and forth troubleshooting, but 30 minutes and 7 devices later I was done. The setup could not be easier. The time included firmware update on the Hub, installing Harmonmy app and creating new Harmony ID on the tablet, adding all the devices by vendor and model, connecting to my SmartThings Hub, pairing Harmony with PS3 and Fire TV, getting all the activities running, testing everything few times over and assigning custom buttons for few things I wanted to get covered. Great job, Logitech!SUPPORT FOR PS3/PS4:  PS3 is fully supported. You need to pair the Hub and the PS3 by following prompt on the tablet and using your PS3 controller to navigate to settings. This took a minute. After that I no longer need a PS3 remote. All buttons are migrated and assigned properly if you choose Watch PS3 activity. For few odd buttons (Subtitle, Angle, Pop-up menu) I quickly assigned custom buttons from the tablet. I like how easy it is and how Harmony App highlights all the buttons that are still unassigned on the App interface. The best feature though is the ability to test al of them right away. No extended synchronization required!  PS4 is not supported at the moment. This is mostly Sony's fault as they are yet to release a Bluetooth interface for PS4. Yes, you can use workaround to assign play/pause and some other basic buttons, but most of the functions would still not work (you can not wake up PS4 or put it to sleep, you can not get any of the Blu-Ray specific buttons to work). So if you have PS4, don't buy this remote for now and instead put pressure on Sony to release a PS4 media remote and allow Logitech to copy full Bluetooth interface profile.    AMAZON FIRE TV SUPPORT:  Easy. You need to pair Hub again with the Fire TV (I have  a stick, but the interface should be the same for the original Fire TV box). You also need  to make sure that you select activity 'Watch Fire TV' for all main buttons to be assigned properly to the remote. Not much else to say except that you can now ditch your original Fire TV remote (which is easy for me since the remote that came with the Fire TV Stick does not have voice search anyway) and enjoy.    SMARTTHINGS and various home automation networks support:  It was easy to pair Harmony Home Hub and SmartThings Hub. The tablet app moves you for a moment to Web page to login to SmartThings Hub Web interface and authorize Harmony Hub to be able to control connected devices (you can also chose at that time which devices you wantto be able to control if you want to leave some of them out). Then you start customizing the Home automation buttons on the remote by assigning them to specific light switches and dimmers. You can now control dimmers and switches both from remote as well as the App interface. I quickly assigned TV room dimmer to one of the buttons (short click is used to turn on the lights and long click to turn them off). Dimmer switch works OK, but lacks finesse. I was not able to gradually darken lights wit the remote as they went from bright to dim in big steps The App interface provides a slider with more granular control, but the UI, positioning of the slider and precision are all unrefined at the moment. Nevertheless, it does the job and I can now also integrate lights into my activities, so, for example, I can press Watch Fire TV activity button and it will not only turn on all the necessary electronic devices, but also, depending on the time of day (before or after the sunset), will turn on and dim the lights to the predefined level. COOL!  There is a big bug right now that gets a lot of SmartThings Hub owners in a frenzy. Apparently, one of the advertised features was the added ability to control electronic devices from SmartThings. Think about Wake Up Mode triggered by SmartThings that would turn on lights, TV, change channel to news and adjust volume to preset level. Or, connecting all the electronics to Away mode, so when you leave home, all electronics would automatically turn off. This is an intriguing features and they should be available except for the bug in Harmony Hub firmwware properly communicating to SmartThings, Not sure which vendor is at fault, but if you wanted to use SmartThings Hub to be able to control your electronics, you would have to wait until this is resolved.    ADDITIONAL THOUGHTS ABOUT REMOTE:  I like Logitech's decision to move all the sensors that control electronics to the Hub. First of all, Hub is powered, so it can use very strong IR andBluetooth emitter to cut through most of the problems in the past when you had either weak emitter or obscured path to the device sensor, preventing the proper sequencing from being executed. I placed my Hub on the shelf by the TV, facing opposite wall and no matter how hard I tried, I was not able to block signal unless I covered the sensor itself with my hand. It looks like emitter (we are talking about InfraRed as Bluetooth does not have this limitation), is strong and can bounce signal off the walls few times to be able to get to the sensor in most situations. Bravo Logitech!  If you are long time Harmony remote user, you would notice few things that were taken away from you. You can no longer fix improper sequence or out of sync devices from the remote. No HELP button or anything close. GONE! If you try to start activity and something goes wrong, you need to have smartphone or tablet with Harmony App close by to be able to fix it. Depending on how often this happens to your setup and how complex it is, this may be a deal breaker. My setup is pretty simple as most activities use only three or four devices and rather simple sequencing, plus I make sure to start activities only when there is no movement around the TV area that can block some of the IR signals.  Another function that is now solely relegated to the App is ability to control individual devices. In my case this was ability to switch sound profiles on my Yamaha Receiver and ability to set my LG TV in 3D mode. Thankfully, you can still reassign individual buttons for specific profiles to the functions that you would have to remember how to use. Otherwise, you can control any individual feature from the original device on the App interface. The UI can be significantly improved in this area. I would point LogiTech developers to excellent \\"Smart IR Remote - AnyMote\\" App to get ideas on how UI should be done.  Finally, I was not able to find a wat to create macro with new Harmony remotes. Specifically, putting my TV in 3D mode requires 4 button combination to get through and macro, assigned to single Harmony remote button would be appreciated.    ADDITIONAL THOUGHTS ABOUT APP:  App is a work in progress. Some things are done right (Like the whole Harmony Set Up section), some are OK (main display with activities and individual device support) and some screens feel plain simple under-cooked or amateurish. A lot of the complaints in reviews centered about sluggishness to start up the App, battery drain on your phone or tablet and lack of widgets for Android platform. I have not witnessed the first two so far but can attest that having widgets with ability to control activities and buttons directly from home screen would be appreciated. Besides that, comparing App on iPad, iPhone and Android Samsung tablet, I would rate interface for iPhone as 8 out of 10, iPad as 6 out of 10 and Android Tablet interface as 4 out of 10. All of them have huge room to improve and I hope this will be done as Logitech would spend more time refining  interface and adding more functionality.    Update 1. I was able to find Macro functionality. It is called 'sequence' (silly me) and can be assigned for any button in any activity. So I now have one button press to switch my TV in 3D mode.

product_title: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone
review_headline: Very Impressed! Wireless capability is Amazing!
review_body:
I am very happy with these headphones! I absolutely love the wireless feature. This is my first pair of wireless headphones and it would be hard to go back. I got a nice deal on these. I don't know why the Titanium ones were on sale, but they were only $229. And a bonus, I had a $70 gift card balance. I had been researching headphones for a few weeks wanting a new pair. I'd been keeping an eye of the Solo version, but this was too good of a deal to pass up. Titanium is probably the color I would have chosen anyway. They are a little less flashy. That's the one thing I actually don't like about Beats. Beats in general do feel flashy to me, but these are a fantastic looking pair of headphones.

I do feel Beats are overpriced and you are paying for the name. However, they aren't as bulky as other brands and I love a deep bass and I know other brands such as Bose have a flatter more even sound. My last pair was Bose. They sounded good, but so far these are better. The sound is crisp and I'm very impressed with it. I do have a set of the Urbeats earbuds that have good sound as well, so I knew the sound would be decent. Of course, these surpass the earbuds.

The fit is a little tight, but that also secures the sound and prevents leaking, which is something I hate. I've asked and been told, the sound doesn't leak badly. That is a big turnoff for me, when others in the room can hear what I'm listening to. If there is anything that annoys me, it's having to endure someone's headphone noise in a quiet room. I've been wearing them to bed at night and after a couple of hours, my ears do get a little sore. However, I've only had these a little under 2 weeks, so maybe I will get used to the fit and that will lessen. I've already noticed it's not as bad.

My only con is battery life. I haven't had it last 12 hours. Maybe 6-8 of playback. But I plug them in and they charge fast.

Overall, I'm very impressed! Would I pay $379 for them? Probably not, that's a lot of money and I'm not sure if they would be worth that. I guess it will depend on how well they hold up. If they last me 2+ years, then maybe I would drop that kind of money. Time will tell. But so far, so good! If you can get a deal on them, I'd go for it. product_title: Razer Leviathan Mini Portable Bluetooth Speaker with Microphone for Handsfree Speakerphone - 10 hour battery life and NFC Pairing
review_body: Pros  -Great bang for your buck  -Solid sound isolation  -Easy to set up  Cons  -No remote  -Not ideal for use in living room  -No custom EQ Settings    Picked this up because I was looking for something to upgrade my living room sound situation from the built in TV speakers to something with a bit more punch and clarity. The Razer Leviathan filled in both of those roles flawlessly. It comes with 3 methods of connection: 1 optical connection, 1 3.5mm audio jack, and Bluetooth 4.0. I have tested all three method and the sound quality is excellent with each. I use it primarily for watch movies through my PS3 which is directly connected through the optical input. Initially I was concerned about the inability to change the volume from a distance since I would have to adjust the volume on the TV constantly when the movie or show would move between action and dialogue but with the Leviathan I will set it at a single volume level and I will be set for the entire movie without needing to change the volume to hear the quieter parts or turn it down when it gets bombastic. There are only 3 EQ settings available: Game, Music, Movie. The game setting is very bass heavy while the music settings seems to be closer to flat. I leave it on the movie setting because it has a little more punch than the music but not overwhelming like game. The sub woofer has a lot of power and can get the floor vibrating without too much effort. All and all I am very pleased with my purchase and only a few minor design flaws keep it from being perfect. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a compact sound system for an apartment, dorm room, or desktop.

review_body: This is my 4th TV support sound/speaker base that I have owned. ZVOX (3), Pioneer (1) and now the Yamaha SRT-1000. product_title: Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
Wow, I can't get over how much I love this speaker. I initially had some reservations about buying this. I remember my thought process perfectly... "Bose? Good products, but aren't they overpriced? I'll probably be paying for the name brand and that's it. I can definitely find something comparable for $50 or $100 cheaper."

After a few days of debating and shopping around, I finally bit the bullet and ordered one. The first thing many people notice is its extremely excellent build. The whole unit is wrapped in anodized aluminum - matches current MacBooks perfectly - and has a good heft to it. Not too heavy, not too light, but just the right amount of weight to give off a premium vibe. The speaker has a large rubber base to support it, which I think is a great touch. Also included in the box are a simple charging cradle (another great touch, but I've always been a sucker for cradles, every since back when the old mid-2000s iPods and original iPhone still included them), cord, and some instruction. Setup was a snap (my phone found it and paired in less than 30 seconds), and I was finally ready to find out if this $200 speaker was worth the price tag.

Long story short... this is the best bluetooth speaker I've ever had the pleasure of listening to. I was literally taken back when I heard it for the first time. When I showed it off to my friends and family they shared similar sentiments; we just couldn't believe such a small device was outputting such large sound. The bass alone is unreal and sounds amazing, and for the most part the device plays nice, balanced sound that 95% of my music sounds great through (occasionally I found a song or too where the bass was a little too overwhelming, but a quick adjustment in equalizer settings fixes that).

However, there are two cons I have:

- Non-USB charging. Not that big of a deal, but it also means another cable to lug around while traveling. Also, this thing screams to be mobile; it's only a matter of time before this cord gets left behind at a friend's house or hotel. On the plus side though, the wall charger has a neat little folding mechanic to it, adding a teensy extra bit of portability.
- No bluetooth mic. Also not that big a deal, but there have been a handful of moments already where I'm cleaning or working, listening to music, and a call comes in. It would've been nice to take it through the SoundLink, but like I said it's really a non-issue. Also it doesn't help that the device looks like the microphone used in Charlie's Angels, kind of a lost opportunity if you ask me.

Overall, this is a marvelous speaker. The cons are hardly a dealbreaker and there is so much to love about the SoundLink. I'm not saying this is the best speaker ever, but it's by far the most excellent one I've ever heard, and in the end was well worth the $200. If you can spare the money, I'd highly recommend this.

product_title: Sony RM-EZ4 2-Device Universal Remote with Big Buttons
review_headline: Wonderful Remote that's a Pleasure to Use; Bought a 2nd Sony RM-EZ4 Remote - Still Love It! -  BUT. . .
review_body:
You do not need to be a senior citizen (I consider myself middle-age at 74) to appreciate the ease of use of a simplified easily read remote. Yes, sometimes I do need to use the original set top box remote, but 90+% of the time I only need to "Power" (ON/OFF), "Change Channels", "Adjust Volume", or "Mute". The SONY remote is a pleasure to use; the original remote keys are small (some really small) with poor contrast even with the light feature "ON" making it difficult to locate the right key (or, pressing only one key). Remote control designers would serve the end-user better by making them more 'user friendly': larger frequently used keys, and possibly even hiding the others (especially "Settings") with perhaps a sliding or flip-up cover.
******
2nd Unit:
Whew! I was in the process of returning this 2nd remote. The 1st remote 'setup' in a few minutes and worked perfectly. It replaced a complex 63 (that's (2Exp6)-1) button monstrosity that was difficult to use (My 'review' of the 1st Sony included, I thought, a comparison photo; not sure where such photos end up). And although my spouse was initially irritated by my ordering yet another remote (we have a bunch of remotes for all our devices) but after she used it just once commandeered it! So, I ordered a second one for myself. After spending more than an hour attempting to setup this remote without success I decided that it must be defective, and applied for a 'return'. However, before sealing the package, I decided to try one more time using a procedure I found online. Worked; now I have 2 great remotes. It looks complicated but took me less than 5 minutes.
Procedure:
1. Remove batteries > 2. Press each button twice, holding for a second > 3. Install the batteries > 4. Press and hold the "SET" and POWER buttons simultaneously for a few seconds > 5. Press and hold the "SET" button until the LED glows > 6. Quickly select one of the function buttons ("TV" or "CBL/SAT") > 7. Turn on only the device to be controlled (I chose TV as it is quickly obvious when it shuts down) > 8. Alternately press the [CH +] and the POWER buttons > 9. When the device (TV) turns off press the "ENTER" (ENT) button > 10. Test the TV power ON/OFF setting by pressing the POWER button; it should now function > 11. Repeat steps 5 to 11 for the other function button.

That I needed to find the solution online rather than in the Sony instruction sheet (or website) points out one of the major causes of product dissatisfaction: poorly written instructions. I worked in the product development and evaluation field, and found that too many instruction booklets are written by people deeply involved and familiar with the product, thus unable to write instructions for the average consumer.

review_body:
There's no doubt these can't possibly compete with the ATH-M50x (which I also own and unreservedly recommend), but for about $120 less, these will do just fine for casual (or disposable) listening. In my case, I ordered them for a trip overseas where, if I lost or broke them, I wouldn't cry. But dang, these are mighty, mighty fine for their price point.

Comfort: A -- no complaints. These don't have velvet earcups or cushioned headbars, but you won't miss them. You'll always vaguely know they're on your head, but you won't mind--at all.

Sound: Great for rock and pop. A fairly narrow soundstage (think just barely outside your ears, but no wider); however, a clear, punchy, well-balanced presence. Nothing supersonic, but pleasant and middle-of-the-road. Solidly central. For benchmarks, "Only You" by Yaz is perfectly balanced--vocals and percussion in the middle, synth dancing beautifully across the stage; "Bend and Break" by Keane is lusciously all over the place, as it should be--vocals just left of center, beats as well, with flourishes left to right and deep of center. Gorgeous, and perfectly balanced. Sting's "Jeremiah Blues" hits you perfectly from left to center to right, but without the sensuous depth and breadth of more expensive alternatives.

Classical music fails on these headphones. They just don't have the depth of expression. The instruments are almost all at center. Unpleasant and harsh.

Jazz does slightly better. But only slightly. You're still presented with the instruments at mostly center. No soundstage to speak of. "So What" by Miles Davis is an uninspired assault. No depth, no layers. Just intense sound--gorgeous sound, but dense and heavy and in your face, with barely marginal expressions.

Treble: Fine. Less than perfectly crisp, but not at all mushy.

Mids: Okay. I would have liked vocals with more authority, but reduced just a tad behind the instrumental layer.

Bass: Definitely lacking, but not unpleasant. There's no profound density here, but with the right equalization, you should find the sweet spot.

In a nutshell: Depth is mediocre; tonality is decent; sonic balance is excellent. As volume increases, quality diminishes, as is to be expected for middle-of-the-road cans.

product_title: BIC America F12 12-Inch 475-Watt Front Firing Powered Subwoofer
review_body:
If you are looking for a sub under 200, but want great performance look no further! This is an awesome sub! I have it running off a Pioneer receiver with Bose 151 Bookshelf's and Klipshe's Energy Take speakers. This sub is so powerful at 65% that I have to make sure the glassware in my cupboard isn't touching each other or they vibrate enough to crack!

I love how it has a frequency crossover knob so you can really fine tune it to perform precisely to proper bass frequencies while your other speakers will represent the frequencies you would like. You can also choose between having it fire more frontward if it's against a wall, or more in a 360 degree pattern if it's in the center of the room. The mesh grill cover is quite nice, but unfortunately a cat scratch magnet.

This sub fills my 1000 sq ft house with glorious bass tones and sounds just as good whether playing metal, classical, bluegrass, jazz, etc.

There is one minor fault with this sub. At times of intense and extended bass response, the subwoofer will at times cut out for 30 secs or so then turn back on. It only does this after longer periods of use and with music that has a bass heavy or wall of sound style. I'm not sure if this is an anti-blowout feature or if it's a lack of power issue from my receiver. It doesn't really bother me that much because it only does it once in awhile and only in extended sessions (especially with metal). Don't let this discourage you from getting this sub however because it never cuts out under normal use with say watching movies or TV or normal listening. I kind of play very bass heavy extreme music :D

This should definitely be a considered choice for a cheaper sub to tide one over until they perhaps want a higher end one.

product_title: PHILIPS In-Ear Headphones SHE9850
review_headline: Hey Philips, why did you discontinue these headphones?
review_body:
A little light on the base department at lower volumes, but the sound is fantastically crisp and clear. Vocal reproduction seems precise and rich to my ears. Some Hip Hop, Metal and Dance music come across weak at lower volumes(but you'll be cranking those genres anyway), Jazz and Classical make themselves truly felt. These can compete with some over the ear headphones, and are probably better than 90% of in ear models on the market.

The industrial design is amazing, the clear/dark metal shells make them look like a prop from a sci-fi movie. The only real bad part, Philips doesn't make them anymore, and you'll probably have to track down dead stock. That will probably net you a nice discount on the original too high price.

I have one serious complaint, sometimes the cable transmits more microphonic contacts than a headphone at this price point should in my opinion. It's not enough to distract you, but it's enough to not get 5 stars.

Set up

Simplicity

product_title: HIDEit Full Bracket Adjustable Device Mount
review_headline: Overpriced, but Solid Mount that Accommodates both Horizontal & Vertical Mounting Solutions
review_body:
Summary: Overpriced, but solid construction backed by excellent customer service and the only product I've found tailored to adjustable mounts to accommodate the xbox and playstation systems. I would buy this again in spite of the price tag.

********

Note that I don't use this mount as it was originally intended (vertical mount). Instead, I use it to horizontally mount my xbox 360 underneath my desk. See accompanying pictures.

Function: 5/5 stars. The mount is made of 6 adjustable pieces of steel to accommodate varying sizes. This particular model can expand to fit both the xbox 360 and xbox one. Playstation users need a different model. While this product is intended for vertical mount, it can also accommodate the horizontal mount as long as you provide adequate ventilation. In my quest for a minimalist desk, I found this to be the perfect product to mount my xbox horizontally underneath my desk (see pics). As far as function, there isn't much to say, it works as intended, looks professional, is sturdy.

Materials: 5/5 stars. Solid steel, coated to prevent rust. Will last a long time.

Price: 3/5 stars. Paying $60 for 6 pieces of metal, 4 screws, 4 drywall anchors and 4 thumb nuts is simply too overpriced. I understand this is a family owned business, everything is made/constructed in America, but I still can't justify the price tag on the simplicity of the materials. It's not even shipped in a box, the materials are just shrink-wrapped, supporting my argument that the price is simply too expensive.

Customer Service: 5/5 stars. The owner and creator of the product is very passionate about his business. I emailed this gentleman at 10pm EST and he responded to my email within a few minutes. He then continued to answer several emails regarding questions I had on the product for the next 20 minutes. Wasn't expecting a prompt response, but I was impressed with the customer service.

product_title: AmazonBasics Ultra Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna
review_headline: Works hugely better than rabbit ears, but some trouble in far-suburban Alabama
review_body:
My wife and I canceled our cable service some years ago, since then relying on our Roku and DVD player. Life was good and $100 cheaper a month, except for those times when we wanted to catch a live game or weather report. I grabbed a cheap pair of rabbit ears and a DTV decoder to hook up to our huge old Sony tube TV, and got a few channels, but always wobbly and never quite as many as I knew were out here to find.

Enter the AmazonBasics amplified antenna this summer: wow! So many more of our local channels, and all more stably than before (and no more "antenna yoga" to boost signal on cloudy days!).

I would have given four stars here, but sadly our location (on a large hill, far from antennas) is very susceptible to signal variance, meaning that if I scan for channels on two different days, I will get a subtly different list each time. Our major channels come in solid as a rock, but the minor ones can break up and even disappear on bad-weather days, or even days with lots of sunspot activity (I checked!).

I know no antenna can handle every situation perfectly, but it would be nice to have a bit better signal stability, or perhaps better ways to manage instability. Nevertheless, an excellent upgrade!

review_body:
This headphone is pretty awesome! I charged up the headphones fully before I used it. I didn't want to use it and have it die on me within like 30 mins. Okay, now that it was charged up fully, I connected it to my phone and started listening to my music.

PROS:
* It's wireless - I love that it's wireless. I can listen to my headphones and do things around the house without the hassle of getting cords in my way. Say for example if I'm cleaning. I can clean with ease. No more having to move the cord out the way. No more having to struggle with the cord always falling in my way or getting knotted up. It's just awesomeness not to have to worry about that anymore!

* It's foldable - Who knew headphones can fold? This makes it so much easier to pack away for storage. And it takes up less, unnecessary space.

* It's Bluetooth - Obviously, cause it's wireless! LOL. The Bluetooth connects very easily to all my devices. It was smooth sailing.

* While using this headphone to listen to music...the headphone puts out quite a sound! It has a nice little base to it. It's not overpowering. You can hear the music clearly.

CONS:
* Now on the other hand when you are using it to talk on your phone the sound is kind of low. It can be a bit hard to hear, even with the volume up at it's full capacity. So maybe this headphones isn't a good idea for using it to talk on the phone.

* The built in mic could use improvements. When talking with the mic, the sound, sounds muffled. It was kind of hard to hear. It sounds like you had the phone on speaker phone that was under a pillow or blanket. I wish it had put out a more clear sound to it.

* The top of the headphone where it rests on your head is a bit hard. It would have been nice if there was a bit more of a cushion on it.

Overall, I think these headphones are really nice to have. I like the easy use of them. The control buttons are easy to use and they are easy to store away.

product_title: V-MODA Crossfade LP Over-the-Ear Headphones
review_body:
I can honestly say these are by far the best headphones hands down for the price you pay compared to the other mainstream brands such as BEATS or Bose. I started by examining the outside package which already beats the packaged of the 2 mentioned brands by far the packaging is by far superior, but you can't judge a book by it's cover though. I went and broke the seal of the box and again I was amazed on how the packaged the inside of the carton, V-MODA took great care and detail to make sure that everything is very neat. The outer shell casing is an excellent design and is pretty hard and will withstand drops and maybe 10lbs or so of pressure wouldn't want to smash or step on the case with the headphones it but would do great just thrown in a bag on the go, however there is a carabiner clip that comes with this to attach to the outside of your bag for easy carrying and fast loading when you are done with them.

When wearing these you will know you are wearing headphones and not like the others that are made with mostly plastic and are really light. These headphones have a little heft to them, but when you put them on your ears they are the most comfortable headphones around. The ear cushions are very soft and can be worn for long periods of time. There is barely any sound that leaks from these headphones when the volume is all the way up. There is no distortion in the sound and everything sounds so crisp including the bass which you can feel around your ears. These are not your noise cancellation but noise isolation which prevents sound leakage and also cuts back on some of the outside noise that you get when you wear a lot of the on the ear headphones which is great because more of the sound stays in your ears and not out.

I have given this a try by playing many different types of music and by far this can handle anything you throw at it. These aren't your $250 + headphones but what you get is a great headphone set at a great price that I honestly believe sounds much better than the Beats Studio or the latest Bose headphones minus the Quiet Comforts which are actually noise cancelling and are pretty good but that is if you want to fork over 3 large bills which I did when I bought the QC 3's back in 2007. I wanted something that was more affordable and yet sound quality along with build quality is there, something that is much durable than a lightweight piece of plastic. I wouldn't waste much time looking at other headphones. Just look at the total number of reviews and star ratings for the V-MODA Crossfade LP's and see for yourself that this is a trusted brand Like the packaging says INSPIRED in ITALY and STYLED in HOLLYWOOD you can't go wrong.

product_title: Outlets-To-Go
review_body:
This review is for the basic unit. Some reviews mention surge protection and USB but the model I received has neither (unfortunately Amazon sometimes bulks reviews of different models which can skew results unless you read every single review).

Pros:
- 4 outlets so in places like hostels you're not hogging all the sockets.
- Outlet spacing wide enough to accommodate multiple transformer blocks (chargers).
- Packs very neatly and small for travel.
- Flat profile plug for fitting behind furniture.
- If you are doing international travel you need only carry one plug adapter instead of 4.

Cons:
- Slightly heavy. 6 oz. vs. 4.5 oz. for a standard US 6', 3 outlet, 2-pin extension cord. Maybe I am being picky but I have my 3 week hike New Zealand pack down to 15 lbs. because I have watched the ounces.
- Blue LED on plug. This could be annoying at night, though I guess you could put your suitcase in front of it. Most of my devices already have lights on them to tell you if the socket is live.
- Plug fits into wall sockets sidewise with cord coming out the side. The cord is only a foot long so the outlet end hangs awkwardly and unlikely to reach the ground. I can see though it would be difficult to change the orientation of the plug without making the cord only 6" long or inconveniently oriented socket, or to make the cord longer and still have the compact style.
- If you do international travel this strip will need a bulkier 3-pin plug adapter.

Summary:
Do you need 2 pin (cellphone, USB power sources, cameras), or do you need 3 pin (e.g., laptop chargers) sockets? If a standard 3 foot, 3 outlet extension cord will accommodate all your needs at one time (transformers can be a tight fit) it will be lighter, probably cheaper, and maybe a bit easier to maneuver with a longer cord to sockets which hotels tend to hide behind furniture. I received this strip in the same delivery as a camera battery charger I had ordered. My other charger blocks a double socket so I thought I would need the wider socket spacing this strip offers. However, I discovered with my new charger I can fit both camera battery chargers and a USB charger all into a standard 3 outlet extension cord (not pretty!) Since a 3 foot extension cord is about the same bulk but lighter and more flexible to stuff into a corner of a pack this strip will probably stay at home for my upcoming trip, but I can definitely see it being handy in some situations.

Many have reported no issue with this strip with 220-240V systems which was important to me for international travel. I am not sure the same would apply to using a lightweight standard US extension cord with higher voltage systems where cord insulation seems to be the issue.

review_headline: Great headphones with just a few small flaws
review_body:
These Yamaha EPH-M100BLs are great sounding earphones, but I expected a little more for the price point.

I have used everything from full size Beats by Dre and Sennheiser headphones to Apple, Beats urBeats, and cheap Sony headphones. These Yamaha earbuds fit my ears better than any of the others. They look bulky but are very comfortable and stay in my ears, even when walking or running. They came with a nice carrying case and five sets of ear tips... almost everyone should be able to find a size that fits their ears.

They sound excellent, but have less bass than my Beats (a good thing IMO). I really like how crisp the mids and highs are. I've been listening to music nonstop and love the clarity. I'm not an audiophile but they sound great to me. I think this is much closer to how music is SUPPOSED to sound (versus those headphones with tons and tons of bass).

My only complaints are with the build quality and materials. My beats are about the same price point and seem better made, with metal components. These are all plastic and feel a little flimsy. I also don't like that the jack is an "L." It just gives it something to snag on.

Overall I really like these a lot. I hope the plastic build quality holds up a long, long time because I really enjoy listening to music with the Yamaha EPH-M100BL earphones.

I've used them almost every day since I got them, whenever I'm out of the office (I have nice studio headphones at work and home) or when I'm at the gym or running, or traveling. UPDATE 7/17/16: STILL love these. Keep them in my laptop bag and they go everywhere with me. product_title: Carlâ€™s ProGray, 16:9, 71x126, Projector Screen Material, High Contrast Gray
review_headline: Great Value for the Money, OK screen
review_body:
I used this material as my primary projector screen for about 4 months, and was pretty happy with it, but ultimately upgraded to something much more expensive which greatly outperforms it. My projector is a Sony VPL-HW40es. It's a fairly high end, 1700 lumen LCOS home theater projector.

The gain on this screen is around 0.7 (which I established by comparison to multiple samples), and it's a dark gray surface.

Pros:
- Excellent value for the money. If you are looking at screens under five hundred dollars, this should be a front runner.
- Good color balance
- Improves the black level of lower end or older projectors
- Decent (but not spectacular) resolution and sharpness
- Very easy to install. Doesn't require stretching, just hang it on a wall. I used velcro on the back of it to hang it without making holes.

Cons:
- Crushes both the whites and the dark grays. The whites are a little bit dingy because this screen is a fairly dark gray, and the grays get crushed because of the inability to match the black level exactly with gamma.
- Shows artifacts in places where it's not perfectly flat
- Prone to damage during installation. Be careful while hanging.
- There are sharper screens available, albeit for a lot more money

The screen I replaced this with, after deciding I wasn't satisfied with the performance, is a DaLite HD Progressive 0.9. The DaLite is brighter, sharper, has more vivid color and better shadow detail. It was thirteen hundred dollars though.

So overall, if you're on a tight budget, want something to improve black levels of an old projector, or want a temporary screen while you save up for something better, this is a good choice. But the engineered screens in the over a thousand dollar range greatly outperform it, so be realistic in your expectations.

Cheers.
