product_title: Sony ZS-RS70BT Portable CD Player FM Radio Wireless Bluetooth Boombox Home Stereo Speakers with NFC
review_body:
I have tried this Sony ZS-RS70BT boombox with the mega bass and without it, and I like the sound better with it on (I think I got spoiled for having this nice feature). It makes the sound come out clearer, more defined. Well, I love this boombox very much. Now I can listen to radio stations that my other radios had trouble tuning in, because the signals were not so strong, apparently. These radio stations sound great in my new boombox!

My daughter has used the bluetooth feature, and has listened to her favorite songs recorded in her cell phone, this feature works fantastic! I have already my favorite radio stations recorded in the boombox memory. At first I thought the instructions were a bit confusing, but after really paying attention and doing what was instructed step by step, it was so easy! The feature of the light that follows the rythm of the music is amazing. I can turn it off if I wish, but I like it too much! I haven't tried usb memories yet, but I believe the bluetooth test had to be a far more difficult test for this boombox, and it passed it flawlessly! I havent tried the cd player either, and I think probably won't (not much, anyway), because the usb feature and the radio stations is what I was after. The bluetooth feature came along in the package deal, and I am glad it did!

I keep my boombox more in the kitchen because I spend there a lot of time, but when I am not using it, I disconnect it and put a cloth on top to cover it and avoid the usual dirt and grease that little by little tend to cover things stored around the kitchen. I noticed that when I keep the boombox connected, it "remembers" the radio stations I was listening to even if I turn off the boombox. When I disconnect the boombox, I have to select the feature "radio" again, and then choose my desired station that I recorded in the boombox's memory. All the stations I recorded in the memory remain there perfecty (are NOT erased), it is just that I have to look for them again if the boombox was unplugged. For me this is no problem at al, because due to seldom power failures in my country (Dom. Rep.), I prefer to disconnect it when not in use.

I tried to see how loud it could go without distorting the sound, and could not end the test because everyone close by in the house complained. As loud as I had the chance to make the boombox go, I can tell the sound kept neat. Later I tried putting the volume all the way to the top, as far as it would go, and had to lower it immediately! It went loud enough (without distorting the sound, too) to make me be able to have a disco party in a big family room, and having people with trouble communicating over the loud music. Just to give you an idea.

The design of this Sony boombox is very nice. It looks modern and neat.

Now that some time has passed, I can tell you about the CD, USB and BLUETOOTH features. They are just great! My daughter loves to play music from her cellphone with the bluetooth feature, and it has worked easily and fantastic since the first time she tried it. I play old cds that are original, and cds recorded by me. The ones I record have a lot more files and the old original ones, and take longer for the boombox to read (MY recorded cds take about 60 seconds to be read, t he old originals take about 6 - 8 secs). But I like better to play my songs from my USB memory, since it holds a huge amount of my favorite songs. It takes the boombox about 1 - 3 secs to read my USB memory, but keep in mind that this time will depend on how you organize your files, if it is with many forlders, subfolders... There are many functions that I could try, like making the boombox repeat all the playing, but my USB memory holds a lot, and I have not had the time to be around long enough to need the boombox to repeat it all, so I haven't tried that feature yet. There are many, many nice features that are explained in the operating instructions thatcame with my boombox.came with my boombox.

product_title: TDK LoR Bluetooth wireless speaker boom box A73
review_headline: Sound great, Lightweight but for the price electronics in this unit are a bit cheap
review_body: I like this product enough to have 2 of them. I bought them for use at the drive in movies in the summer time and they really do sound great for the weight and size. These little guys are easy to pack around anywhere. We take them whenever we travel and they work great for both camping and hotel stays. At the drive in you need loud and a lot of bass because your watching a movie and people around you are ignorant and inconsiderate right? So one of these is not always quite enough for that purpose, and the bass will fade quit a bit in many parts of movies. But of course its just a little box, you can only get so much bass out of a box this size. For the size and weight the bass is not bad at all. The first huge negative I will point out is the fact that TDK just leaves the raw speakers out in the wind to get kicked and pummled....piss poor design flaw in my opinion. I bought 6" covers and just glued them on to the front. It actually looks better I think? occasionally one of these units has a display problem. Sometimes the display just doesn't light up, but the unit still works fine with or without it. And the other seems to disconnect bluetooth randomly and has a crackly problem while using bluetooth and it doesn't matter the source, I have tried several Iphone and droid devices. I know what the cost is to come up with a sound system that sounds this good and also works on battery for this long without weighing a ton. (Its not that easy)  I have tried a few DIY's in my years and use to do car audio install. That is why 4 stars. A fully charged battery will last through 2 movies most of the time. These little guys sound great for what they are. anyone un boxing them would be pleasantly surprized. But they did scrimp a bit. It is relevant that the electronics in these units have a lot to be desired for reasons I previously mentioned. I Don't think for the price this unit should be anything but bulletproof. I will also mention I did have the previous version and itwas bulletproof and louder but the battery situation sucked and it was way to heavy. (That thing would eat thru 10 D size battery's in no time.) A happy medium would have been nice. The remote is cheezy and doesn't have great range (10 to 15 feet) but it works. I have had these A73's for about 18 Months now and I am overall happy just because they sound so good and they are so portable. But far from perfect.

product_title: OFC Express TV Stand 42 x 14 x 5.25, Black
review_body: We needed a platform for our 60" Panasonic plasma flat screen that would fit our entertainment center and allow us to place a sound bar beneath the flat screen without too much hassle (trying to avoid wall mounting either the sound bar or television). This product fit the bill - relatively inexpensive, good quality, not exceptional, but fair for the price, and designed for the size of our entertainment center and the weight of our flat screen. The stand comes fully assembled, but when I removed it from the box one side panel had broken off from the top. This did not seem to be the fault of the manufacturer, as the construction is sound and the packing seemed designed to protect the unit as much as possible. I suspect that the box was handled a bit roughly in transit and some impact on the end of the box was sufficient to break the side panel. I debated whether to return the unit, but after examining the damage I decided to use "L" braces to repair it myself, since the repairs could be made on the inside of the unit without effecting the appearance of the stand. I also realized that the unit has a center panel to help support the weight of the television - not immediately apparent in the pictures online, but evident on closer examination. Once again, not the fault of the manufacturer, simply my oversight while shopping. However, since the center support would restrict placing the sound bar underneath the stand as planned, and since I was already in "do-it-yourself" mode, I elected to cut off the front few inches of the center panel, leaving enough to permit weight-bearing. I also secured the center panel with an additional "L" brace. None of my fixes created a cosmetic problem, and we now have a shelf for our television that allows us to use our sound bar. My only recommendation to the manufacturer would be to ship the product unassembled. There are few enough pieces that could easily be attached by the consumer, and would help ensure theunit arriving unbroken.

product_title: AMP Note Portable Bluetooth 4.0 Speaker with Stylish Magnetic Smart Lid for instant on/off and pairing
review_headline: Simple to Use and Great Sound
review_body:
I'm comparing the Antec Note Portable Bluetooth Stereo Speaker to the portable speaker I have been using up until now. I've been using a Cubot Bluetooth portable speaker for my outdoor listening pleasure. It's been a good speaker, but it's range is spotty and the battery life, supposedly four hours, has not lasted that long for me. I am lucky to get three hours from it. If I go onto my front deck and try to put it on the deck rail and don't bring my cell phone outside to be within six feet of it, sound cuts out.

Range

I put the Antec to the test, as I am sick of having to have my cell phone close to the speaker. If I'm outside, I don't want to have to have my phone out, too, I just want to stream music. With the Antec, it boasts a 30 foot range. I found that's pretty accurate as I could get half way to the mailbox before it cut out.

Sound

I am impressed with the sound. It's crystal clear, no static or interruptions. Just clean sound with plenty of volume.

Instructions

First, I am impressed with the box it comes it. This isn't paper or cardboard, it comes in a clear, solid plastic container that's built to last. Inside are two cables (one auxiliary and one USB/mini-USB), the year's warranty information, and the instructions. The instructions are simple to follow. There's the volume and skip functions, the Bluetooth connectivity button, the power switch, and then a button to connect your phone to the speaker. I rarely use my cell phone for calls if I'm home, so I haven't tested that function, but everything else works perfectly.

Bluetooth Connection

Here's the biggest plus in my book. The Cubot often takes a few tries to get it to pair up with my device. The Antec paired up immediately, no fuss. I love that!

One Downfall

There's no real indication on when the battery is about to die. I'll be outside playing music and suddenly it just quits. It would be nice to have a power bar or something to show me that it needs recharging prior to it just dying.

product_title: Champion-DNT-PINK 3.5mm Jack Kokopa Retractable Doughnut Stereo Earbuds with One Touch Retraction
review_headline: and now the second is pretty much dead
review_body: I received this on June 24, and as of today August 12th, I can no longer use it. One bud had already died (wire cracked within the coating) from the stress of using it, and now the second is pretty much dead. I can get it to work if I hold it just right near the jack, but it's very touchy now. Initially, I loved these. The winding donut works great, and I don't need to fully pull out the cord before re-winding it. Plus, the winding donut stays down near my IPod, so it isn't a weight right in the middle of the cord like the other retractable buds I've used. However, my Ipod is the tiny 1 inch square Nano version that clips, and the donut is bigger than the Ipod and pulls at it, which is why I think the wire pulled apart. It looks intact from the outside, but it clearly isn't connecting right within the plastic coating. My other issue is that there is about 8 inches of cord that is wrapped around the outside of the donut on the Ipod side of it and is only held in place by tiny plastic tabs within the groove on the outside of the donut. I'm not sure why they designed it this way (so you can see an orange stripe on the outside??), but this means that the weight of the donut pulls the cord out from under the tabs, and I have to constantly re-wind it into the groove. I finally put tape around it to hold it in place, which only works for so long until the tape is shredded and looks terrible. Perhaps if my MP3 player were bigger, then I could better use the handy little wrap cord for putting the donut on your belt loop or whatever, then it would have lasted longer, but since my Ipod is so tiny, that is somewhat unfeasible. Either my Ipod or the donut was dangling, and it felt like a dead weight, so I'm sure it put too much stress on the tiny wires. Otherwise, these were great. Nice sound and the winder worked awesome. Maybe once I replace my Ipod to a bigger version that I can assure no dangling weight on the wire, then I might try these again.

product_title: Presonus Ceres 2-Way Powered Speakers
review_headline: Quick to set up, fun to use, and good sound quality
review_body:
These speakers are mainly designed to be used with bluetooth devices (phones, tablets, etc.) and computers (laptop, desktop). You connect the two speakers using the included ~7' bare wire connector, then plug the power cord into the left speaker and an outlet. With this set up, you can pair up bluetooth devices with the speakers to play audio. (The bluetooth device--tablet, phone, etc.--must be on and within range, of course.) I've never done this before, but I had no problems following their directions and easily paired up my Android tablet. You can also connect the speakers to a laptop or desktop computer using the included RCA Unbalanced to 1/8\\" cord.

There's also a 1/4\\" TRS socket to connect an external subwoofer into the back of the left speaker. There are knobs to boost or cut frequencies above 10kHz and one for below 100Hz. There are balanced 1/4\\" TRS line-level inputs, but the instructions don't say what they're used for (and I'm not techie enough to know). On the front of the speaker, there's a volume knob, the bluetooth button (to make the bluetooth pair with your device), the power switch, a 1/8\\" stereo connection to plug in headphones, and a 1/8\\" jack that allows you to plug in devices like an mp3 player.

I have these speakers connected into my desktop computer, but I also use them with my tablet as I tend to use both in the same room. The audio is much, much better than on the tablet speakers and much better than the cheap speakers I had on my computer. These speakers also give a more stereo and \\"fuller\\" feel than my previous speakers.

I get a very low hum that I notice when the speakers are on (not off or in standby power-saving mode) and no audio is playing. My old computer speakers had a much worse hum. I tried the one tip about this in the instructions, but it didn't help. I previously tried these speakers in another spot (and not connected to my desktop) and I don't recall hearing a hum, so maybe it has to do with my computer setup.

Also, one night I was listening to a video on my desktop at night and turned the computer volume down to about 6 to be as quiet as possible. The speakers went into standby mode after about 10 minutes even though they had been putting out audio. I found that if I keep the computer volume higher than 6 and turn the speaker volume down (the way you're suppose to), this standby problem didn't happen. So adjust your volume using the speaker volume. If you need tech help, you need to register at the website[...]The tech support was friendly, fairly quick to respond, and helpful. I doubt most people will need to contact them, though.

The standby feature is useful if you don't like to manually turn your speakers on or off. But the drawback is that when you want to listen to audio, the first few seconds of audio is lost as the speakers \\"wake up.\\" I turn the power off myself, so this isn't a huge plus for me.

Update June 2016: For some reason, the speakers stopped working (when connected to my computer directly. They still work via Bluetooth). It's probably a simple fix like some setting changed, but I've been sick and unable to quickly ferret the problem out. Just thought I should mention this problem.o, one night I was listening to a video on my desktop at night and turned the computer volume down to about 6 to be as quiet as possible. review_body: Obviously there is some risk in going with a budget audio brand like Pyle, but this amp is a great value for the money if you're looking for an entry level power amplifier and don't need much in the way of bells and whistles. The speakon outputs, variable speed cooling fans, and bridged output mode are all great features at this price. There isn't much to it aside from a power switch, two volume knobs for each channel, and a handful of lights indicating the status of the amp. However, I'm driving a pair of Yamaha Club speakers with this amp and it doesn't distort if you tap it out of power. There's decent headroom here and, though the speakers I'm using can handle way more power, the PTA1000 delivers what power it has pretty cleanly. If you get a decent one, and take care of it, it'll hold up for a while.

product_title: SHARKKÂ® Bluetooth 4.0 BoomBox Speaker, 18 Hour Playtime, 10 Watt Portable Speaker System, 4400 mAh Li-ion Battery, Ultra Bass Subwoofer Sound Effect / Built In Mic For Calls / NFC Function / For All iPhone / iPhone 6 / iPhone 6 Plus / All iPad / iPad Air 2 / All Phones / Samsung Galaxy Phones and Tablets / Laptops
review_headline: Quality sound and sound quality -- excellent speaker!
review_body: A couple of preliminaries thoughts. By its nature, any speaker review, bluetooth or otherwise, is  subjective. We all hear music differently, have varying sonic expectations, and listen to different genres of music. A true audiophile is likely to tell you that flatter sound is purer, would eschew adding an equalizer to an expensive setup, and would cringe at how most of us would crank up his or her high end stereo system that we would love to own (WITH an EQ). That said, the best way to purchase a speaker is to listen to it in a store and trust your ears, not the salesperson. You will often discover that more money or name brands donâ€™t deliver the sound you are seeking. However, more and more we purchase our speakers online, trusting posted reviews, or often brand names, to help us decide, not getting to listen until we open the box and turn it on.  Bluetooth speakers are even more unique because they depend on more variables, notably the music source. Are you listening to a flac file or an mp3? If the latter, whatâ€™s the bit rate? Is your delivery source a phone, tablet or computer and is the sound equalized? If youâ€™re listening to a music service, what quality are they delivering and how good is your connection? Etc., etc., etc. In addition, bluetooth speakers are unique because they have no bass or treble controls. Just a box delivering sound that was tuned by the manufacturer based on the listening preferences of a group of engineers (if that much thought even went into the speaker). You get the point.  Which brings me to the Sharkk Boombox, and for my listening needs, the company has met or exceeded every facet of what I hope for from a sixty dollar speaker. Sonically, the Boombox is lauded again and again for its bass (not base!) response, and indeed it delivers in spades. Itâ€™s logical that, with increased volume, the bass level would become even more pronounced, and it does, but it never muddies or distorts, nor does it overwhelm the mid-range and treble output. At lower volumes, the Boombox provides a good, audible low end that remains in keeping with the rest of sound being delivered. Itâ€™s obvious that a lot of attention went into the performance of this speaker, and itâ€™s sound remains very balanced and consistent across the spectrum at all listening levels. If I have any complaint, itâ€™s that trebles can be slightly overwhelming when both the speaker and my source (Galaxy Note 4 and iPad Air 2) are maxed and the Boombox is quite loud. Thankfully the bass, which is also showing what it can do at max volume, helps countermand this slight (and I emphasize slight) harshness. (FWIW, I used the stock music players with no EQ on both the Note and iPad, 320 Kbps MP3 files, and concentrated on the songs â€œFixurlifeupâ€ (Prince & 3REYEGIRL), â€œNowhere Manâ€ (2009 remaster), Mick Jaggerâ€™s â€œSweet Thingâ€, â€œBlack Chandelierâ€ (Biffy Clyro) â€œBelieveâ€ (Mumford&), and Toddâ€™s â€œTerra Firmaâ€.) There are hundreds of reviews here that attest to similar satisfaction with the sound, so I wonâ€™t belabor the point. (I did not get a chance to try the speakerphone.) Most of us want a speaker that gets loud enough so someone in the house (read: my wife) wants it turned down, and we want the full range of the sonic spectrum, especially at the bottom end, where so many bluetooth speakers fail. The Sharkk Boombox not only doesnâ€™t fail, it succeeds brilliantly.  What equally impressed me about the Boombox is that the attention to detail that went into the sound carries throughout the entire product. From the build of the speaker, to the materials used, and the attention to minor details that could have been left out or ignored completely, a lot of care has clearly gone into the Boombox. Even the packaging shows attention to detail. Consider a few â€œminorâ€ things. First, since its release, the Boombox has been constantly updated and upgraded by Sharkk, often in response to customer reviews. They are clearly acompany that listens (no pun) and theyâ€™re seeking to move from â€œbetterâ€ to â€œbestâ€. At the time of this writing (late May, 2015), the Boombox I received came with a 4400mAh battery (much more capacity than the competition in this price range), NFC that worked well with my Note 4, raised black buttons on the top with white inlays for the various functions, and an all black (not white letters on black) Sharkk logo on the speaker front. In a nice detail, the white button inlays light up when the light in the room darkens, making them easier to see and control. While this might use a minimal amount of battery, the 4400mAh can certainly handle the small added load. The speaker has a nice weight to it (1.8 pounds), and frankly I want to feel that weight. That speaks quality to me, and lets me know thereâ€™s a little more magnet on the speakers, and that the overall quality of the parts is solid. In no way does the weight impact portability. The Boombox is still a small speaker that is easily moved. The included wall charger with collapsible prongs, 3.5mm and USB cable (flat cable, which is a step up from the usual) and carrying case are again all details most other companies leave out.  The overall experience is not dissimilar to what Apple delivers -- a well packaged, premium product with careful attention to every detail and no corners cut before being released to the public. The most telling difference between the companies is price, with Sharkk achieving similar goals at a much fairer price to the end-user (uh-oh -- here come the fan boys).  Some brief comparisons to other speakers as heard by my ear: the Photive Cyren costs far less but is not worth even the sale price -- far too much treble, no balance and a harsh sound at volume and no bass to speak of; the Oontz Angle Plus was very disappointing as it offers a bit of bass but nowhere near what I was hoping for and has an overall unbalanced sound (leans too far to the mid-range); the Amazon Basics Portableis ten dollars less than the Boombox, is  kind of bland in design but uses nice materials, actually delivers some bass punch, but the balance noticeably lacks treble and it offers nowhere near as much sound and extras (charger, lit buttons, NFC, etc.) as the Sharkk does for ten dollars more; at this writing, the Lepow Modre is the same price as the Cyren, but offers a better balanced overall sound and isnâ€™t a bad speaker for the price of a Jackson but it canâ€™t touch the Boombox (nor would I expect it too based on size and weight). Finally, I found the Oontz XL in the ballpark with the Sharkk Boombox. It offers solid bass and good balance, and might be sonically preferable to some depending on personal preference, but the XL is a hundred dollars on sale, not sixty, it has a proprietary charger (not micro USB), no pouch, no NFC, and the buttons are flat black and difficult to see even in a well lit room. The XLâ€™s lack of attention to small details hurts the user experience and emphasizes Sharkkâ€™s attention to â€œthe little thingsâ€, making the Boombox look that much better and for less money.  All of the above delivers a message to the consumer -- Sharkk is a company that cares about what they market and is looking to deliver a premium product at a reasonable price. Not only does the Sharkk Boombox succeed, it exceeds expectations at this price point and rivals (or beats) speakers priced quite a bit higher. Five plus stars for helping bring the music home.  Oh, and I was NOT provided with a free speaker in return for my review.

product_title: Sennheiser Urbanite XL Over-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Comparing the Urbanites with the Audio Technica ATH M50x & the VModa Crossfade M100's!
review_body: I'll be comparing the Sennheiser Urbanite XL with the Vmoda Crossfade M100's & the Audio Technica ATH M50x.  I own all 3.    HEADPHONE BUILD:  1) Vmoda's get an easy #1 here. They're built like tanks. Made to take contortion, falls, & even can take being run over by a car (I read a story... honestly)  2) The Urbanites get 2nd. The band is rugged. The hinges are made of metal. Really well made!  3) The ATH M50x is made mostly of plastic. Not brittle, but compared to the Vmoda & Urbanite... not quite as sturdy    CABLE BUILD :  1) Vmoda's cable is amazing. It's made of kevlar. Ya know the stuff that takes bullets (haha!). Most cables take 10,000 bends & then they break. The Vmoda cable can take a million bends. Oh yeah... it's a detachable cable (Texas Longhorn Orange). And I love the 45 degree angle jack when you plug into the device.  2) The ATH M50x has a locking cable, but it's not 1/8in at the headphone. So, you can only use Audio Technica cables (but you have 3). The cable is thick & seems like it'd last a long time. The jack that goes into your device is a straight plug (my least favorite).  3) The Urbanites has a thick flat cable. It's the shortest of all the cables. But I love the 90 degree jack... especially for laptops. Make sure you have the cable fully locked in... or you'll only get sound from one side.    PHONE REMOTE:  1) Vmoda's cable is ingenious. The mic is closer to the mouth, while the control is further down where your hand can grasp hold of it. The controls are very easy to work with.  2) Urbanite's remote is the best designed in my opinion. The controls are well-made & easy to use.  3) The ATH M50x do not have any controls on their cables.    ACCESSORIES:  1) Vmoda's come with by far the nicest carrying case. It looks like Batman armor... haha! It also comes with an extra cable that doesn't have the remote, but allows for someone else to plug in and listen. 1/4 in adapter included  2) The ATH M50x comes with a shorter cable, a longer 3 meter cable, & a coiled cable. It comes with a pouch. 1/4 in adapter included  3) The Urbanite comes with a bag.    PORTABILITY:  1) Vmodas are more compact & fold in.  2) The Audio Technicas fold in the same way Vmodas do, but they're a bigger can.  3) The Urbanites fold horizontally, but they're poofy & wide.    COMFORT:  1) The Urbanites are soooooo comfortable! I was really surprised how cushy the ear pads were. They're made of some sort of velour. The headband which has very thin padding didn't bother me at all. Comfort is very important to me. I love love wearing these!  2) The ATH M50x is supposed to have much more comfortable ear pads then the original ATH M50's. But the cup size is still relatively small. The ear pads sit on the back of my ears. But since they're cushy, they don't bother me that much.  3) The Vmoda's clamp tighter than any of the above. The ear pads are small like the Audio Technica's... but with the clamping force... it's a lil more bothersome... I'm thinking of buying the XL pads.    THE SOUND:  1) The Audio Technica's have the best sound in my opinion. It's a very clear sound signature. It's a very mild \\"V\\". You hear the lows & highs slightly raised... but the mids are still present... and the lows don't bleed over the mids  2) The Vmodas have more lows... especially the mid-lows. So, it's more of a natural \\"V\\". But it still doesn't compromise the mids or the highs.  3) The Urbanites have the most lows. They're made for Urban music. With this can, the mids are more recessed & the highs are considerably more rolled off...    PASSIVE NOISE CANCELLING:  1) Vmodas tighter clamp makes for a better seal... you hear very little around you.  2) The Audio Technica's sit on your ear with a lighter clamp... you can hear more going on outside.  3) The Urbanites have velour pads. Velour lets more sound in.    COST:  1) The ATH M50x is $159  2) The Urbanite XL is around $200  3) The Vmoda's are around $300    The Urbanite XL is an uber comfortable can gearedfor urban music (hip hop & edm)... which makes for a fantastical fun set of headphones with the right type of music.  I really like the design, I absolutely love the feel, the build is great, & honestly I dig on this flat 90 degree tipped cable.    On Yelp I give 5 stars for the best. For right now, these are the Four Stars... cause I gave the 5 stars to the ATH M50x.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 25 Headphones (wired, 3.5mm)
review_headline: What else could you ask for?
review_body:
I'm not and audiophile. I just like to have a decent pair of headphone to listen to music and watching movies/videos on my devices.

Pros
- Comfortable. I can wear this for hours and won't feel any strain on/around my ears.
- Quiet. It dramatically reduces low frequency noises like airplane hums or background noises in coffeehouse.
- Detachable cable. If the cable fails for some reason, all you have to do is purchase just a new cable, not the entirely new pair of headphone.
- Crisp & clear sound. Usual for Bose, sound profile is leaning more towards mid and higher frequency while giving out a very nice/tight base.
- AAA batteries. No more proprietary battery like QC3.
- Looks nice. I prefer this look over the older QC15/QC3.
- Smaller case. Easier to carry around when traveling.

Cons....I can't think of anything.

Honestly, I can't find anything that I'm not happy with. Unless you like a bass heavy stuff, QC25 should give you everything you want. A crisp and clear sound with decent amount of bass. The noise canceling that block out background noises (not everything though).

Again, since I'm not an audiophile, I can't really critique the sound profile of QC25, but as an average consumer who cares about sound quality, this was a great buy.

PS. The box redesign is also amazing.

product_title: iLive iKB333S Under Cabinet Radio with Bluetooth Speakers (Silver)
review_headline: Great radio with two major issues. 3.5 stars
review_body:
Installation was a breeze and the sound is great for the price. A 12 year old would have no problems installing the radio to the cabinetry. Just tape the cutout to the bottom and drill 3 holes. Not audiophile quality, but the sound is crisp and clear. Wife loves being able to stream music from her iPhone to the radio.

Instead of drilling another hole to string the FM antenna (small black wire) in the kitchen cabinet, I wrapped it around the radio and had no issues with radio reception. YMMV though.

However, the unit has two major issues and is only deserving of 3.5 stars (amazon won't let me give it 3.5 so I'm giving it a 4.:

1) LCD display is HORRIBLE. Difficult to read the time with any ambient light. If you are not looking directly at the LCD head on, forget about it. Since bottom of our cabinet is not eye level, I have to stoop to see the clock. Bad choice and crappy LCD. Would much prefer the old digital clock.

2) don't know what BT version the radio uses, but make sure you turn the sound down if you switch from bluetooth to radio. All our music is 356kb+ (not lossless but still above average quality) and no matter how high the volume is from the phone/tablet, volume on the device has to be cranked up pretty high. When we switched to radio, I thought the speakers were going to blow due to the high volume. Now we lower the volume before switching sources.

One final minor complaint, the buttons on the radio are a pain in the ass. But not a deal breaker.

product_title: Coocheer Wireless Bluetooth Speaker - Portable Cell Phone Speakers with HD Sound and Bass, Compatible with iPhones, iPads, Androids, Samsung and all Phones, Tablets, Computers(Black)
review_body:
This is a small portable speaker that has pretty decent sound quality. It sets up and pairs easily to all of my devices. Upon getting this speaker it came with a micro usb charging cable, instructions manual, the speak system, and a small bag to transport all of it in.

The speaker is set up to provide bluetooth and has an aux. jack so you can attach it directly. My phone, my nephews phone, and my tablet all located this speaker and paired to it in a few seconds of doing the search and pressing connect. The speaker stops functioning if you plug it in to charge as a safety feature for the speaker, like every other bluetooth speaker on the market.

When it comes to charging this speaker it is super easy. I was able to charge this speaker from my wall socket USB charger, my PC tower, my laptop, my car charger, and from my back up power bank. Bascially anywhere you can plug into a USB slot this thing can be charged from it. While it is charging there is a red light around the volume control dial that is red. Once the charge is completed that light goes off. The first charge took about 2 hours. Since that first inital charge it only takes about 30 minutes now to get a full charge. With a full charge the speaker lasts for about 7 1/2 hours.

The speaker provides a decent quality sound. It is a small speaker in an enclosed plastic housing. On the back of the unit are all of the main controls to the unit. There is an on/off switch for the power of the unit. There is an aux. jack in the back that is a 3.5mm and can be attached directly to your player. The last so is the micro USB charging slot. On the top of the unit is a round volume control button. With the volume control button I was able to take the speaker near max before I was able to notice any distortion. I was to 90% max volume on my tablet when the distortion started. For me that is more then good enough since I typically listen to my tablet at about 40% most of the time. The speaker system is also a full range set up. It does not have driving bass but it does offer the full range. The base of the speaker has some small rubber feet. This makes it where it does not make vibrating noise as you are playing it. It also makes it where it does not slide around.

If you are looking for a good bluetooth speaker I suggest checking this one out. It sets up easy and pairs easy. I can listen to it thoughout my entire house with the sound that it puts out and lasts for a decent amount of time. review_headline: I must first state that initially I was unhappy with the underwater audio product because it seemed like one of the channels wou
review_body:
I have been using the underwater audio headphones for quite some time paired with my I-pod shuffle. I must first state that initially I was unhappy with the underwater audio product because it seemed like one of the channels would invariably "burn out" after a few weeks or few months. I finally called the company and they immediately identified the problem and recommended a simple fix. It seems that a small drop of water can get into the opening of the headphone and mute the sound. The fix consists of taking a Kleenex tissue and twisting it into a small point and "wicking" the water droplet out of the headphones. I tried that and "voila" - the phones were restored. While on the phone I noticed that Underwater audio has come out with a new slightly higher priced set of headphones. I gave them a try and am even happier with them. I now routinely take a few moments to dry out the headphones once a week and store them with a Kleenex in the port. Music has been fine since and I am back to swimming in bliss for ninety minutes of Clapton, BB King and Joe Bonamosso.
Cheers
j

product_title: Bose Acoustimass 10 Series IV Home Entertainment Speaker System (Black)
review_headline: Don't believe what others say, trust your ears, yours are like no others!
review_body:
First things first, unless you have perfect ears, and are an "audiophile", or eavesdrop for the NSA, then you don't need to read the thousands of negative, or for that matter, positive reviews. There are two critical things to consider.

First, the system will never sound better than what is passing through it. Junk in, means junk out. So you are much better served spending time finding the right receiver/processor that can handle the formats you will be using. If you have Blu-ray, then you MUST get a receiver that can handle the encoding, or you won't have great sound. Invest in one that not only handles the right encoding, but has passive pass-thru. Or you will be stuck swapping HDMI cables, when you just want to watch something without the sound system running. No passive pass-thru, you will suffer.

Second, listen to these speakers, what sounds great to you, will sound horrible to another. That is just a fact. My ears have been beaten to death by military service, anything from 9mm, 120mm , firing at close range. So if you listen to these, using a set-up that you can replicate at home, and they sound good, your done, make the purchase.

If you have perfect hearing, and deep wallets, then hire some professional to install some ridiculously over-priced, in wall, billion watt, satellite operated goofy system that needs NASA engineers to set it up, so you can brag. Then do so, and those of us without perfect ears, and deeper wallets, will giggle, since we achieve the same satisfaction at a fraction of the price. I checked my pants, and am very happy with what I have, so "one ups" bore me.

One final note. In movies, the dialog comes from the center channel, 90% of the time. This is the single most important speaker in your system. When you see the people on screen talking, it comes from the center channel, if it is coming from other channels, then something is not set properly. I read many complaints about the voices being too low to hear. Your receiver should have a way to increase the volume of just your center channel, fixing most of the problems you read about from other users. Again, get your formats right, and this shouldn't be an issue.voices being too low to hear. review_headline: Excellent initial impression -- time will tell if they hold up, but I already know these *sound* great.
review_body: I received these this morning, and they have not left my head.  I am very impressed with the clarity and detail of these on-ear headphones as compared to other on-ears I have owned and enjoyed for years (Philips Citiscape Downtown, Logitech UE4000, House of Marley Exodus, Sennheiser HD229). I will tell you that this is not the case, as my rock, EDM, and surprisingly *jazz* tracks are incredibly well timbered and well proportioned throughout the range.  Most of the headphones I listed previously have a some kind of glaring tonal failing in my hearing, or are somehow uncomfortable for more than one or two hours, but I have not found the like to be true in my admittedly short time with the AKGs (six hours so far . . . but I have not taken them off!)  They are very comfortable, light-but-not-too-light, and have an incredible range of adjustment coupled with a secure fit.  These are my first pair of AKG phones, but they will not be my last.  I should also mention -- I am not a huge fan of the styling, but the primary color bling is growing on me.

review_body:
I couldn't be happier with this sound bar. It was very simple to set up and sounds great. It sounds terrific, greatly improving the movie experience we were experiencing with the TV speakers.

They immediately paid to ship my unit back via UPS with the understanding that they would send a replacement as soon as they received ours. As it turned out the fault was mine. I stupidly managed to mix up the power supply cords between the sound bar and our cable box, connecting 12 volts to a sound bar that required 24. Klipsch immediately diagnosed the problem when they saw the power supply I had returned with the unit, and to my surprise still sent me a brand new replacement. I could not have asked for more. The generous, prompt service I received from Klipsch was frankly far better than I deserved. I can't wait to give them some more business.

product_title: C. Crane CCRadio-2E Enhanced Portable AM FM Weather and 2-Meter Ham Band (Black) CC2BE
review_headline: Great radio for times when Wi Fi is not available
review_body: In theory, if you have good bandwidth at home, you don't need this radio. Virtually every radio station is on the web, and the Kindle tablet makes a great Wi-Fi radio with TuneIn. So, what's this device good for? Its a great old-style radio receiver with excellent reception on AM. Listening in the Providence RI area, I've received radio stations from the Chicago area, based on some very brief time trying. New York stations are a cinch. The true value is as an emergency device, where its 200+ hours on D batteries comes in handy. Radio aficionados who go camping in areas without a mobile signal, or those who do not want to waste their data plan on streaming will also find it very handy. It has significantly better reception than those wind-up radio/flashlight combos.    My radio had a poorly fitting speaker cover (the mesh cover in the front with the product logo). To avoid the hassle of returning and getting a replacement,I was able to press it back into acceptable shape, but this is something that the manufacturer's QA should have caught. I'm deducting one star for this. The rest of the device appears well made.    In summary, if you like listening to radio, you will like this device. Check it out when you receive it to make sure that there are no build quality issues, and it will last a lifetime.

review_body: This is high-quality cable.  Just to see if replacing the old cable that came with the house with this new cable made any difference (one way or the other), I ran before and after tests using http://www.speedtest.net/ . product_title: Super Power SupplyÂ® AC / DC Adapter Charger Cord For PSA-120S Series Compatible With: BOSS Compact Pedals DB-66 DB-88 Metronomes DR-Series Drum Machines FC-Series Foot Controllers MC-202 SH-101 SP-202 TR-626 all TU-Series Tuners Replacement Wall Plug
review_body:
I'm going to talk the language of "BOSS" now. Many will not understand it and as such all you need to know is this power supply works well. Useful info to know is that the main bulky part of the unit is narrow so it does not obstruct neighbouring sockets on a power strip if that's what you need.
So, back to Boss. I had a good ol' PSM5 but I needed a noise filter so I ended up opting for the NS2 wich made the PSM5 now obsolete to me. It's a Japanese one and I think someone might still want it as it's a classic so I cannot break it up from the daisy chain, power supply and original box etc. Hence I needed a new power supply. After checking the price that Roland charge for the Boss PSA I got back up off the floor and tried to stop laughing and after a search on Amazon I discovered this. Adding a 1-Spot daisy chain to the order now took the PSM5 completely out and away we went with the new set up. Being narrow doesn't sound like too much unless you have a power strip like me and it usually meant that adjoining sockets were obstructed. Why this isn't adopted by more manufacturers I don't know. Seems like one of the first thoughts at the design stage to me now.

It powers the NS2, maybe the cable length could have been longer, but it's a small problem easily fixed by either location or use of the aforementioned power strip. However it does mean that now this is not perfect and so, reluctantly, I must remove 1 star. I only have 2 pedals being powered by the NS2, (DS1 and CS2), and there is certainly no issue with current draw. So, for those in the know, the plug IS configured correctly for Boss pedals and there are enough amps, (current, not Marshalls), to supply multiple pedals.

review_body: Previously had an Onkyo TX 600 bought 10 years ago, decided to upgrade the home theater setup to HDMI and the benefits of upgraded sound tech. Its obvious right away things have come a long way in 10 years.  Just the number of connection wires I was able to remove was a massive simplification  but the sound quality improvement blew me away. The clarity was was terriffic, no more listing to mumbling actors and not understanding them. Setup was all done on TV screen, in just a couple of minutes,and it was good to go. For the price you are not going to do better. Highly recommend!  By the way, I've read a number of reviews and questions and it seems there is a great deal of confusion among some of the purchasers regarding low volume levels and high heat in the component. These are the result of not reading the manual, this is a complex unit with simple adjustments. The receiver comes preset from the factory with speaker levels and internal volume set at the lowest level. This will have the unfortunate effect of having the owner turn the volume up for normal listening levels. It is first necessary to calibrate the speakers on the 0-10 scale (preset at 0) and likewise the Intelligent Volume setting. This will allow you play the tuner at much lower volume levels and the resulting lower temperatures. If you want to get your monies worth out the tuner, you better read the manual front to back. These aren't the tuners from the old days-lots of choices and settings. Good luck

product_title: 2x Pack - Sennheiser RS65 Battery - Replacement for Sennheiser BA151 Headset Battery (60mAh, 2.4V, NI-MH)
review_headline: Very misleading, Sennheiser has never made this Sennheiser RS65 battery, check their website.
review_body:
As far as I know, Amazon has only one product webpage that sells the genuine Sennheiser BA-151 battery. I now buy all my BA-151 batteries from this one Amazon webpage -

http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0009PL4CY?psc=1&redirect=true&ref_=od_aui_detailpages00

Most of the years buying the BA-151, I've noticed one significant Sennheiser-authorised design update to the BA-151. The new BA-151 external shell now comes in a matte finish, no longer the previous glossy finish.

In either case, genuine Sennheiser quality control in the BA-151, means that I have never had to struggle like I had to with those ill-fitting fake batteries. The genuine Sennheiser BA-151 always inserts easily, smoothly, and perfectly into the battery slot.

Over the years, after buying from those other websites selling their cheap, fake, counterfeit BA-151 batteries, I've noticed many problems :
(1) Odd-sized battery shells that are difficult to insert into battery slots,
(2) Fake labels peeling-off and jamming in the battery slots (genuine BA-151 never have labels),
(3) Fake lithium-labelled battery (BA-151 has never come out in a lithium format)
(4) Short total lifespan (due to the lower-quality internal button cells),
(5) Leaking battery fluids.

Sennheiser quality is not as cheap as the fakes, but it's worth paying a little more for the real McCoy.

product_title: Soundsoul(TM) Noise-isolating Sport In-ear Headphones
review_body:
Interesting, But Needs Improvement.the ear hooks and ear inserts.
The sound is very bright, and if your sound source has tone controls, you may want to cut the treble a bit, and crank up the bass as far as possible, as it is barely there at all. You can improve the bass some by reaching over your head with your left hand and arm, grabbing and pulling up the top of your ear, while at the same time using your right hand to push in the earphone and adjust the ear clip. Use a similar procedure to install the left earphone. Good luck. The only way to really get any heavy bass from these headphones, is to cram them into your ears to the point of a painful fit if you have small ear canals. Not a good solution. The frequency response is listed as 20Hz-20kHz, but that is definitely not a flat response curve. The sound gets 3 stars.
Adding things up, we get a total of 14 stars out of a possible 20 stars, or 70% (C-), and an Amazon rating of 3 stars.

The sound source that I used, is the same one that I always use for headphone testing: a SONY CMT-EP505 MICRO HI-FI COMPONENT SYSTEM. The music used is also the same: a CD called: Time Life Music, ULTIMATE LOVE SONGS COLLECTION: LEAN ON ME; 19691-2, A 70303. The audio test equipment that I used, is the only test equipment that really matters, and it is the test equipment that I was born with, -my two ears.

Please, do not blame the messenger. I always tell it like it is, the bad along with the good. These product reviews are only a hobby, and I do not have a vested interest in either selling or promoting the products.

I like the size and shape, it fits nicely in the hand, and while some of the buttons could use more definition to help find them easier overall it's a very nice remote, just not high quality. Iâ€™ll outline all of the (many) negative things I have run across with it. Iâ€™ll start with the online MyHarmony.

When this first arrived, I made my account from the app then tried to login online. I was told the password was invalid, even though I know without a doubt I was entering it exactly as I had created it (I use a password manager, so itâ€™s copy/paste). Turned out it had truncated the password due to it being too long (by 2 chars, FYI, maximum length is 30). Of course, when making the password, there was nothing stating a maximum length. I then ran into a similar problem on logitech.com, where itâ€™s 20 characters despite no mention of a maximum length (and oddly even then it says itâ€™s too long, so I had to reduce it to 16), though at least there it wonâ€™t accept it, whereas MyHarmony just took it, truncated it, and gave no warning. Trying to retrieve the password requires an email address and answer to a security question, though when registering via the app it never asked to set up a security question, so there was no way to do a reset. And to obtain support you have to login, which is obviously no help when trying to get help logging in. I created another account just to access support, only to find the only options are community and paid support. In other words, you pay $100+ for a remote control and Logitech will only help you if you give them more money, otherwise your only support comes from others you bought this overpriced junk, which is bad enough when youâ€™re having issues with the product but useless when youâ€™re having issues with your account. This is appalling to say the least, and I canâ€™t support a company that treats its customers like this. More on this later.

Moving on to the software (computer and app), I was reminded of how much I hate Logitechâ€™s programming team. The software is EXTREMELY slow/laggy. Every step takes forever, it would error every single time I would do a certain action (Settings > Edit devices and activities >>> Connecting to MyHarmony >>> "This is unfortunate. Please restart your app to proceed."), and the menus are unintuitive. Thereâ€™s no way to copy button mapping from one activity to another or even access previously made sequences (which takes a very long time to build), so if you want to use the same one in more than one activity you have to create it all over again. At one point it lost all the programming for an activity including a long sequence I spent several minutes putting together. Setting this thing up was an extremely frustrating experience. The software also doesnâ€™t keep you logged in very long at all, which makes no sense, because itâ€™s not like this is a sensitive program or something youâ€™re going to be using on a public computer.

When â€œfixingâ€ an activity, when it asks if it's working, if it's not, it will check that everything is set up properly, and if it is and things still don't work, it just keeps going around in circles with no way out except saying it's working when it's not or having to killing the app. When configuring an activity, it tells you all devices involved in the activity must be on and does its typical spinning circle for several seconds while it turns everything on, even though there's a good chance you already have everything on, so it just wastes your time and frustrates you. It also takes a long time to complete the actions for an activity even when there's only a few of them.

Itâ€™s also not terribly smart. It doesnâ€™t track when devices areon or off. If they turn off on their own (sometimes happens from me falling asleep and the PS3 and TV will turn off after a few hours), they donâ€™t turn back on properly, and you have to manually turn them on to get things working right again.

One of the main reasons I bought this was to control my Hue lights. I was very disappointed to find there is no direct Hue control, and I was only able to set it up to control them indirectly with a very sloppy, roundabout method. It also took a while of being frustrated before realizing changes made in Hue programming are only saved once you back out of the app and that remote mapping changes aren't implemented until they're saved. One of my biggest complaints about this remote is that sometime around June or July Logitech released an update that took away what little Hue control it had. There were several complaints in the forums, including from myself, and all they did for months was say they were working on it. It took a good ~5 months for them to fix it. In the meantime, they could (and should) have released a way to roll back to the previous version, but instead they just simply ignored the problem and took their time fixing it. Because of this, in the time Iâ€™ve owned this, more of that time has been spent with it acting as an expensive, glorified universal remote than being able to do one of the main things I bought it for. In my opinion, I should be offered a partial refund due to this. Of course, this wonâ€™t happen. I will never buy another Logitech device again because of this experience.

What made me finally stop being lazy and write this review is that the remote has been failing lately. For the past couple weeks certain buttons, the ones I use the most, donâ€™t work unless I press them very hard or multiple times. This has made this already irritating remote extremely frustrating to use. But just now, it has completely stopped talking to the PS3, making it totally useless to me.

For all the headache, all the time, all the months of being unable to use it for one of its primary intended purposes, and now the fact itâ€™s already, after less than 8 months, failing, this remote was very overpriced and a massive waste of money. If not for the firmware fiasco, I would give it 2 stars, as it is nice when itâ€™s set up and working properly. But the total lack of support and the way that situation was handled forces me to downrate it even further.

product_title: Yamaha RX-A830 7.2-Channel Network AVENTAGE Home Theater Receiver
review_headline: If you use HDMI Control / ARC read this.
review_body:
If you use HDMI Control for Audio (control your receiver sound / power with one single remote) or (your tv turns off and on when you turn off the receiver / receiver turns off and on when you turn tv off) then read this review. Knowing what I know now I would not of bought this receiver / returned it as soon as I found out. So that's what the bulk of my review is about.

When you have HDMI Control turned on then every single time you turn on your receiver it switches to your TV input (by default AV4). It doesn't matter if you turn ARC on or off. There is zero way to set a default. Google "Yamaha AV4" and you can see the thousands of people all with the same frustration. For whatever reason Yamaha doesn't have an option to turn this off. I've opened a ticket / support case with Yamaha over 2 weeks ago and they have ignored it. Zero response. The problem is every time you turn on your TV you have to wait 10 seconds, then hit the HDMI (or whatever) input button on your Yamaha remote. That's the only reason I have to keep my extra Yamaha remote. Once it's on then I can control everything with my 1 TV remote, but every single time the receiver comes on I have to grab my extra Yamaha remote and then press HDMI 1. I can't seem to teach my family to do this or have them understand why you have to. Why you can't default to HDMI 1 or turn off the auto switching I don't understand. My 6 year old Onkyo receiver I switched from had HDMI control and it never had this issue. This can be solved if you buy an expensive Harmony remote then program it to hit the HDMI button for you automatically, but I don't think I should have to spend a couple hundred dollars for a workaround for a serious design flaw.

As far as a receiver goes I love all the other features. I primarily bought this to get ARC and AirPlay. I also bought it for Zone 2 Audio. All of which work really well alongside everything else you expect from a receiver. Airplay crashes every so often but it's not terrible. I love being able to stream music while the receiver is turned off. I can't speak for most of the features as I just use mine for Airplay, ARC, and primarily a HTPC.

The mic auto setup is somewhat of a joke, where other brands (like my 6 year old Onkyo) uses Audessey EQ to actually equalize the sound it appears all Yamaha's does is set the sound levels and pick from "Large" or "Small" settings on the speakers. With that in mind though the sound is better than my old receiver through the exact same speakers so I can't complain.

The only other reason I gave this 2 stars is because nowhere it was made clear the recent price drop was due to a new model on amazon. It would of been nice if somewhere it stated this has been replaced by a more recent model / discontinued. By the time I realized it, which was too late, the only thing I saw worth purchasing the new model for is 60hz 4K support. I would of purchased the new model, it would of been nice to know I wasn't getting an awesome Black Friday sale like I was led to believe, I was actually getting an outdated model of receiver that was replaced / discontinued.

review_headline: A little on the smaller side, but sound quality is very nice.
review_body:
I'm often curious if I can figure out how to work a product without looking at the instructions. Since these rechareable sport wireless headphones came in a language I don't know how to read, that is exactly what I had to do. The first thing I did was plug in these headphones using the audio jack/usb cable that this set comes with for a few hours. It has an LED light on the controls side of the ear cuff that is red while charging, and blue when fully charged.

To turn on these headphones, I pushed the power button that looks like a circle with a line in the center, and when on the LED light is blue. I pushed the capital letter M, that is across from the power button on the ear cuff to bring up the LED menu on the other ear cuff, then pressed the FF/rewind buttons to toggle through the menu selection, which is music, FM radio, to settings. Once on the settings menu, I hit the letter "M" to bring up another menu to be able to change the contrast and backlight of the LED screen. I then hit the letter "M" to go back to the main menu and after pushing the FF button, and while on the FM radio menu I pushed "M" again to turn on the radio function. After playing with the controls buttons I figured out I can change the station for the FM radio by pushing the center play/pause button. To turn the FM radio off I pushed the letter "M" button again. Hitting the FF button after that brings me back to the music button, which I could not figure out how to get working once on the menu.

I did plug the audio cable into my iphone 6 headphone jack, which once in the LED screen read "line in". I was able to listen to pandora radio but couldn't skip, rewind, or use the play button features with it. I also used the music app the iphone 6 came with, and received the same results. After fooling around with the FM radio searching for a station, I was able to pick up a few inside my house with this headset, and one or two others outside in the yard. The sound quality is very nice, but these headphones aren't adjustable, and are rather on the small side to fit my head. I included a picture of my 10 year old son wearing them below to show how they fit him. Overall, I have rated these headphones a 3 because, although they aren't adjustable, are on the smaller side, and the instructions weren't written in a language I can understand. They weren't that hard to figure out on my own how to work them and once set the sound quality is pretty good.

review_headline: Drawbacks can take away from the convenient size and sound
review_body:
So after writing my first review of this product I received an email from the Anker support team. They apologized for the poor range of their product and offered to send me a replacement which I accepted. The new speaker arrived within a week and I began to test the range again.

I am happy to say that the new speaker range was much greater than the first. Direct line of sight, indoor, with no obstruction range stretched to an impressive 40 feet with no break up. However it was quite easy to block the signal at this range by merely waving my hand between the speaker and phone. At 20 feet I was no longer able to obstruct the speaker even standing directly in front of it and trying to block it with my body. Quite respectable since I could do this easily with the first at less than 5 feet.

The issues with the unit beeping at low power, and when auto shutoff kicks in 5 minutes after bluetooth disconnect still keeps me from using it in the bedroom while falling asleep. I even wrote an app that mutes the phone and shuts off bluetooth which I had hoped would stop the warning beeps but sadly they remain. Hopefully, when they release their next version they will add a button to disable notification sounds.

Another negative is that while the unit does disconnect the bluetooth after 5 minutes of no signal if does still seem to draw power which runs down the battery. I noticed this when trying to reconnect to the unit one day after disconnecting the bluetooth but leaving the unit on the previous day.

All and I would really like to give this 4 stars due to the excellent service of the Anker company but I just can't because this is a product review, not a company review. But I did give the new speaker an extra star. Anker gets 5 stars in my book.

product_title: Etymotic Research ER-4PT MicroPro Noise-Isolating In-Ear Earphones (Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Comparison of 3 IEM's after heavy testing: Shure SE215, Shure SE425, Etymotic Research ER-4PT
review_body:
In short, these sound amazing but I can't recommend them for purely physical reasons: microphonics, difficulty getting them in my ears, and the heavy weight of the plastic thing connecting the wire to each ear.

I'm not really an audiophile, but I did a lot of research on IEMs (earbuds that sit deep in the ear), and I thoroughly tested a few of my finalists. So, in this review I'm going to compare the Shure SE215's ($99), Shure SE425's ($299), and Etymotic Research ER-4PT's ($299). My main selection criteria were comfort, sound quality, and ability to block out outside noise (note that for this reason I first tried the Bose QuietComfort 20i's, but the active noise canceling pressure made my ears hurt).

SHORT SUMMARY: I easily recommend the SE215's in terms of price-performance; but, if you have more to spend then get the SE425's. The ER-4PT's are very crisp, but they have some significant physical downsides.

LONGER REVIEW:

First of all, I hear that it's important to choose headphones based on the kind of music that you listen to. So, for my tests, I used ten songs representing my favorite genres of EDM (house/trance), synthpop, and pop rock. Songs included Instant Crush (Daft Punk), Good Morning Kaia (BT), Crush (Dave Matthews Band), and A Sky Full of Stars (Coldplay).

Overall, the SE215's are excellent, especially for the price. When switching back and forth between them and the 425's, I could notice a clear difference, but not necessarily a $200 difference. If $200 isn't a huge deal to you, definitely get the 425's; but, I think you'd have to be a very discerning listener to really appreciate the increase in quality.

So what's better about them? Everything is clearer. After listening to the 425's, the 215's feel almost like a light blanket was thrown over the speaker -- everything is just a little muddier and the individual instruments are less clear. There's less separation between the layers. But again, this wasn't a dramatic difference, so you'd still be very safe with the 215's (and I understand that $300 is an insane amount of money for most people to spend on earbuds).

What about the ER-4PT's? They were even clearer, but almost clinically so. It felt a bit like I was in a perfectly empty room listening to every little nuance of the sound, but that sound was less warm than that of the Shures. To be honest, though, this difference was minimal -- in most cases, there wasn't a hugely noticeable difference between the ER-4PT's and the SE425's. I most preferred the Etymotics in songs involving crisp cymbals and complex background noises; but again, it wasn't a huge difference, and overall I slightly preferred the warmer bass of the Shures.

More importantly, I found two dealbreakers that meant I couldn't keep the Etymotics: (1) That crisp clarity of sound sadly translated to the wire as well; every time I moved my head I could powerfully feel/hear the wire moving, to the point that it was quite distracting. I believe that this is called microphonics. (2) The plastic piece connecting the wire going to each ear was surprisingly heavy, to the point that its weight very quickly became annoying compared to the other earbuds.

The other nice thing about the Shures is how easily they slip into your ears. Fair warning that it took me a while to figure out how to get them in right -- I was about to return them because it was so confusing at first, but I watched a youtube video and realized you have to actually significantly bend the rubbery part. Once you get the hang of it, it's extremely fast and easy to fit them in compared to the Etymotics that I really had to work in every time while holding my ear open with my other hand.

So, like I said, I recommend either one of the Shures depending on how much money you can spare on headphones. One other tip, by the way: Be very careful about trying all the different types of tips thatare included. I noticed a dramatic difference when I finally found the right set that made a truly tight seal in my ear canal -- the bass became significantly stronger and the overall sound became tighter and cleaner.

Overall, I definitely recommend IEMs over regular earbuds (unless you're riding a bike or something that demands attention), but keep in mind that none of these will fully block out nearby voices on their own -- I needed to play white noise or music to achieve the true isolation I was looking for.are included. product_title: Denon AVR-S900W 7.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
review_body:
I am very disappointed in this receiver, the Bluetooth just flat out refuses to connect to any blue tooth device in the house (our tablet or one of our three smart phones). If I factory reset it the Bluetooth will connect initially but then a couple of days later it will stop connecting. I've been to a forums based around this receiver and one suggestion was to turn off the WiFi in the receiver. That seem to work for a couple of weeks but then it goes back to not working anymore. So if I turn on the WiFi after that, it won't even connect to my home Wifi. I've done a factory reset and gone through this entire process three times and i'm not doing it anymore because we always end up with the same results. I shouldn't have to turn off one function to get another one to kind of work.

This receiver also has a issue with video being choppy at times. If the receiver, tv, and cable box are all turned off and I turn on the cable and tv before the receiver sometimes we get no video or some times the video is so choppy I have to turn everything off, let the receiver set for a minutes then turn the receiver back on wait for it to fully boot up and give that "click" ready sound before I can turn anything else on.

Also, the Spotify function isn't worth the hassle.

So I would avoid this receiver, I would return it to Amazon but it does function 75% of the time, it just creates a lot more hassle than necessary. Because I can't use my surround sound for streaming music via the Bluetooth or the WiFi, the receiver can't receive updated because of the WiFi and I do a lot of rebooting to get the video to look right. You can get a receiver that has the same functions that ALWAYS works for a much better price. I always heard good things about Denon although I never purchased anything from them and I will never by another Denon product.

review_body: I bought this to switch between my Charter HD cable box & my DVD player.  Pros: 1. No extra power cable needed  2. Solves the problem of having only one HDMI input on the TV  Cons: 1. Because the 4 ports are placed on 4 different sides, it makes it very cumbersome to position it on my TV stand. It would be far better to have all the ports on one side (the back) so that the cables are not going in every direction.  2. Although it does automatically switch to my DVD player upon inserting a DVD, it does NOT automatically switch back to my cable box upon turning off the DVD player. I even tried to turn off the cable box, and then back on, to see if it would detect the signal. No luck. I have to walk over to the unit and manually press the switch button to switch from DVD back to cable box.  I would have given it 4 stars if it were truly automatic for all devices. I kind of wish I paid a bit more to get one with a remote instead. But for the $10 I paid for this, I can't complain. It's still better than unplugging & plugging in the cables to the back of the TV every time I want to switch between cable and DVD player.  4-6-2016 update: This splitter can no longer be relied upon. While watching movies through the DVD player, it will often blackout in the middle of the movie. It will come back on, but then it will blackout again every few minutes. Wasn't sure what the problem was. Thought maybe my DVD player was failing. But when we bypass this splitter, and plug the HDMI cable directly into the tv, everything works fine again. Downgrading rating to 2 stars. Probably should be one star, but it did work for about a year, and it was cheap. I do not recommend this product.

product_title: Beats By Dre Powerbeats 2 Wireless In-Ear Headphone
review_body: Update: Well, I thought the cutting out problem mentioned in my previous review below had been resolved, but I've continued having the same problem, so I'm downgrading to one star. This type of performance is unacceptable, especially considering how much these cost. If the bluetooth loses signal from my pocket to my head, there's a real problem with this technology.  Original Review:  I was ready to give this only one star the first time I used it. It kept constantly cutting out. I packed it up and was ready to take it back when I decided to call customer support. They had me do a reset, and that fixed the problem. The sound on these earbuds is great. I've read reviews about how these focus on the bass with just so-so mid-range and treble, but I did not find that to be the case. The midranges were smooth, and the treble crisp. These are great for people who have a problem keeping earbuds in. They are very secure. They have an interesting fit--it almost feels like they are loose but still secure--they don't feel jammed up into the ear like a lot of earbuds. It's almost like they hover just outside the ear canal. But it doesn't affect sound quality. I can press then against my ear, and the sound doesn't really change. These let in a lot of ambient noise. The sidewalk I walk on is adjancent to a street, so I can hear all the traffic. If you are into sound isolation, these might not be for you. These are a bit safer when running or walking in a public setting, I would compare the sound to listening to music in a car. While there are wind and road noises, your mind eventually blocks those out and all you hear is the music. These also take a little time to get on. The first few time I kept having to fumble with them. They do get easier the more you use them. They are very comfortable once on. I could hardly feel the arm that goes around the ear. They feel very secure without feeling like they're pressing up against the ear. They are more comfortable when you don't try totake up the slack. I haven't had these long, so I can't speak to longevity. However, I will only be charging these through the computer terminal. Some of the charging issues may have to do with people charging through wall chargers. These are probably too strong for the battery.

review_body:
I used it primarily to receive "external service" and news from foreign sources. This seems to be the replacement technology to shortwave radio, except that very few smaller nations have English-speaking external services anymore. When it worked, it worked nicely.

Pros: It does what it says, and also has a number of domestic feeds listed through the Receiva interface. Bunch of other functionality that I don't particularly need but you might like. Sound was very good.

Cons: It won't do my Sirius-XM subscription. The push-the-knob-and-turn-it-to-configure-and-change-settings interface is clunky. You get used to it, but it feels like dialing in a really long combination into a safe or entering your name into an 80s video game. I'd rather set up a PC and program it that way, but that is not an option for this product. The display is adequate, but menus can take you somewhere you don't want to be, or to lists of several hundred stations that you have to scroll through. There is no battery backup. My power supply on the main circuit board "went." There is no service manual available from anywhere, and no reference to replacement parts, so the thing sits in a bin waiting for me to troubleshoot the point of failure and shop for possible replacement parts.

review_body:
This is NOT a splitter. It is a switch.
The product description states it's a "Switcher and Splitter". A true splitter splits the signal from one source to two (or more) receivers (monitors) at the SAME TIME. This box only switches the signal from one receiver to the other, so only one device can receive the signal.

I wanted to be able to split the input to two different monitors, so that both monitors could receive cable at the same time.

This device can not do that, and it's worthless as a splitter.

I do not recommend purchasing this, unless you need an expensive paper weight.

product_title: CPR Call Blocker Shield - 1500 Number Capacity - 2000 Nuisance and Scam Numbers Pre-Loaded - Block Telemarketer Calls, Political Calls, Election Calls - Block Robocalls Now
review_headline: This could be good if my problems are solved.
review_body: I initially blocked 112 area codes, then had to go in and block all but the 3 or 4 from which we receive legitimate calls.  When I blocked the rest of the area codes the thing started blocking my son's cell.  I couldn't see anything unusual  about his number and it was letting other cell calls thru.     I called their customer service number and talked to a very nice guy who seemed not to have any suggestions on what   I could do to solve the problem.  He did suggest replacing the unit if the problem persisted.  He also emailed me a couple   of websites to check but they weren't any help either.     So, today I set the unit back to its factory settings then had my son call to be sure it would now go thru.  I then blocked all area codes   except the 3 or 4 we use and had him try it again.  The call went thru this time so we'll have to see what happens from here.   It may be fixed or it may not.     One thing I should have tried first and didn't do would have been to unplug the unit completely and keep it off power for a few   minutes to see if it would reset and solve the problem.  I'll try that next if the problem comes back.  If that doesn't work I'll go   for a new unit.     When you block a number, or area code, you first get a dial tone, then enter **7# and get a beep, enter the number or area code, followed   by a # and by a second beep.  If the number has already been entered you will hear 2 beeps.  The manual doesn't mention this the double beep.    It appears you have to turn the phone off, then back on and do each number separately.     BUT, I found that after I hear the second single beep I can enter the next number and the #.  You can enter 5 or 6 numbers (each followed by #)   at a time.  Then turn the phone off and start again.  The manual also doesn't mention this working but I'm sure it did because I always   got the single beep after the #, and two beeps if I re-entered a number.     It would be really nice if they had an option to block ALL area codes at once. Then it would be a simple matter of going in and unblocking   the few you want to allow.     This doesn't cause a problem, but incoming calls now show up twice on the phone.  Once from the blocker and once from the caller ID.   Blocked calls apparently do not show up on the caller ID.  Actually, I'd like to see them go ahead and list them.  That way you can   see if the blocker is doing it's job and also if it has blocked someone it should't have.     If it doesn't persist in blocking \\"good\\" numbers and continues to block everything in the area codes I've entered, I'd give it the   full 5 stars.  Time will tell.
