product_title: *NEW* With the ingeniously inventive LG AN-MR500 Magic Remote Control you'll be able to use your voice, gestures and point and scroll methods to operate your 2014 LG TV. Take full control of your 2014 LG Smart device with the LG ANMR500 Magic Remote.(English Keypad).
review_headline: Almost There - AN-MR600 Version is Better
review_body:
Aesthetics: 5 out of 5 stars - Looks great, and feels great in the hand. It is very smooth, sleek, organic-looking, and ergonomic.
Material: 4/5 stars - High-quality plastic. Most of the remote is made of shiny/glossy plastic, while the button panel/area is a matte plastic.
Craftsmanship: 5/5 - Built well, no creaks with the creases and button areas while handling/pressing the buttons. The buttons have a nice firm "click" and tactile response.
Size/Weight: 5/5 - It is right at 6 inches long, and weighs 4.25 ounces with the 2 AA batteries installed.
Functionality: 3 out of 5 stars - While the remote itself is high-quality, beautiful, lightweight, and easy to function, the functionality is lacking. First, it takes a while to get use to the "air mouse/Wii controller" functionality and to wave it around and properly place it over the areas where you want to click. Second, when you perform a button press, the controller naturally is lowered because of your button-pressing movement, so you have to be very still and precise when you press the button. Finally, there is no dedicated "OK/Enter" button - rather, you press down on the scroll wheel like on some mouses. But because you have to click down on a scroll wheel, it is very easy to slip off the scroll wheel and miss the press, or have the pointer move out of place and miss the area where you are supposed to click on.
The other negative is - although there are few buttons on the controller so you don't get caught in "button-hunting" - there are not many dedicated buttons to function what you want. So to bring up the settings menu, you have to click on the "home" button, then move the point or directional button to the settings on-screen button, then lick the scroll wheel. There is also no button to quickly change the video/visual modes, so if you're watching a news program, and switch over to a movie, you can't switch from standard to cinema mode easily, and have to go through that whole procedure to get into the settings menu again. There is also no dedicated Netflix button, no channel number buttons, and so on and so on.

So in the end, although this is a good remote control, there is still a lot of room for improvement. I recommend the 2015 edition - model number AN-MR600 - but on the LG website it lists that it can work only with certain 2015 TVs, and are not backward-compatible. Let's hope LG comes up with a firmware update so you can use the 600 version with older TVs.d have to go through that whole procedure to get into the settings menu again. review_headline: Technically strong headphone with some serious design flaws
review_body: [4 Edits over time]  I have these plugged into a Creative Soundblaster Z which, in my opinion, has done an excellent job of powering these headphones. I also considered the more expensive Asus Essence line, but I'm glad I decided this would be sufficient - it was.  Others have gone into the sound quality, and I'll happily defer to their judgement except to say that I whole-heartedly agree with the praise this model gets for the presentation of its lows without being overwhelming. The only thing I'll add is that sound-staging is above average and well-suited for gaming.  Then the problems.  The SoundMagic HP150 seems to be the result of a team of people who understand acoustics and how to design a fantastic headphone, technically, but lack any common sense.  1. The cord is extremely short. I'm not sure where SoundMagic imagines people put their computer, but I'm assuming the cases at SoundMagic are placed either in front of the monitor or worn as helmets. My computer is located 6 inches from my leg below my desk and I have no range of motion. Every moment I am at my computer I have to be conscious of the cord and how short it is. It's not fun.  Now, normally this wouldn't be a big deal, right? I could just swap the cord with something longer. Well that brings us to:  2. The cord has a proprietary locking mechanism. Apparently someone at SoundMagic was asked what their feelings were about consumers being able to install longer cords or attach microphones and their response was to devote the entire company to figuring out how to ensure consumers would never be able to do either.  3. And my final edit. Like many of the other negative reviews, the plastic around one of the headphones cracked. After reading how terrible the SoundMagic customer service is for warranty replacements, I think I'm just going to trash these and go with something else.pretty nice. The big issue, however, is that you can't use a mic adapter like the V-Moda BoomPro Mic. You'll either need to use a desktop model or a mod mic which attaches to the outer cup.

product_title: Sony Walkman NWZA17SLV 64 GB Hi-Res Digital Music Player (Silver)
review_headline: love the sound but don't like operation and build quality of the player
review_body: I am writing this review because after reading the few reviews available it sounded like this would be a great Media Player. But after receiving the player (a Christmas gift from my wife) I have to wonder if most of the people who reviewed the unit have actually used or even seen one in person. So I reread the reviews and noticed a trend that they don't actually say anything about using the player (all except one).  So here is a real user review.  The good. (I use it for music playback only)  The sound on the player is superb. I rip my cd's using the FLAC format and I have listed to playback using Wired (Grado's) and Bluetooth headphones. I have also listened to it on my home stereo using wired and a Bluetooth connection. There is a slight difference in the tonal quality but in a noisy environment my ears can't tell the difference. Sony digital processor does seem to color the music a little but it is on the warm side so it not objectionable.  I must say I love the sound of this player.  The media program (Media Go) that comes with it is very good for ripping music in any format that the player supports. Setting up playlist to send to the player is a breeze. The program does not have the options of JRiver Media Center but it is simpler to use.  The Bad  It is cheaply built - If feels like a toy. I do not believe it will stand up to daily use. Not a quality product that I have come to expect from Sony. For the price of this unit I expect it to at least have the build quality of my FiiO player or my cassette Walkman (which still works)  Bluetooth- It's a joke. My main reason of wanting this player was Bluetooth connectivity. If you disconnect it from the headphones, stereo -car and home, It take at least three tries for it to reconnect the next time you want to use it and you have to navigate to the Bluetooth screen to do it.  This creates a problem on its own. If you were listening to your playlist and stop at a particular track you now loose that place unless you navigate back to the home screen (more on that later) and bookmark your spot before you try and reconnect to your Bluetooth playback source. This is a major pain.  Screen Navigation. The player has 4 main buttons. The toggle button which surrounds the play and pause button is use for navigation.  The navigation is more cumbersome -not user friendly- than it needs to be. Try and navigate while you are working out or somewhere not so well lit and it is frustrating at best. At this price it should have a touch screen. My 29 dollar SanDisk player is easier to use that this setup.  The next problem.  You really can't power down the player. Once you power down the player if you accidently touch any button on the player it powers back up. I keep the player in a soft case clipped to my belt. I have bumped the player while in the case and have ended up with a dead battery the next time I wanted to use it.  There are other problems but they are minor and I can live with those.  If Sony wants to play in this market (no pun intended) these major flaws need to be fixed.  Tried to post a review on Sony's web site and they would not let it post. So I don't trust any reviews on their web site at this point. This is why I am posting it here to at least let potential buyers be aware of what it is really like to use this player.

product_title: COWON X9 Touch Screen Video MP3 Player (White)
review_body:
I've owned several cowons & been extremely pleased with them over a decade.
The first X9 shipped dead/bricked.
The second was operational until the screen cracked & became useless after a few days of receipt.
The screen cracked during a normal calibration setting, wherein you're supposed to press dots in the corners of the screen.
The dots were unresponsive to tapping/pressing unless I really got a finger in the deep corner. I even had to power-reset to escape once as there seems to be no way to back out. On the third dot, after the X9 struggled to even acknowledge any user inputs the X9 finally accepted the press yet cracked. I'm not sure if the glass wasn't seated properly. But something wasn't designed right.

During normal operation, the X9 screen is difficult to use, especially singlehandedly. Either the pressure is too light and unrecognized, or too light and you end up tap-selecting instead of scroll-dragging, or you really have to press & drag with high focus.
I was prepared for an unresponsive screen, from reading reviews ... but reality is its a bit of a pain at best, defective at worst.

The external speaker is a bit on the quiet side. I think the J3 was louder.

Although the picture on J3 & S9 is smaller, they had better quality than X9... and nothing near as good as say a samsung note2.

X9 is harder to modify sound settings on the fly, as one has to back out to the settings screen... more steps than other cowon players.

The pause & FF/RR are too close together to easily manipulate without looking, when gel case is on.

And actually its sorta large & very very heavy, making it cumbersome to operate & bring along.

product_title: NZXT Digital Controller Cooling Fan with Grid AC-GRIDP-M1
review_body:
I just finished putting together a new system based around a core of NZXT products (case, cooler, fan control, etc) because the components had impressive features, the reviews were good and, coming from the same company, I expected the pieces to work well together. To my surprise and disappointment, every single product that I used from NZXT had moderate to significant flaws in design or execution. Either the product wasn't well thought out - features that looked good on paper didn't work as you'd expect - or the product was poorly made - software worked badly, pieces were flimsy or components were of low quality. While on paper their products may hit all the check marks when it comes to features, I can't say I could recommend any of the pieces that I had experience with and I have my doubts about NZXT's portrayal as a top-tier company focused on innovation and quality.

This may have been the biggest disappointment - this could have been a really impressive product but instead is a dud. What you should know before you buy this product:

- This does not individually control fan speed. You set one speed and all six fans rotate at that speed. If you have some fans that rotate faster or are louder and want to set them to a slower speed your only option is to use an in-line resistor (which sort of negates the whole reason for having a programmable controller like this)
- This is not compatible with four-pin PWM fans. Even though PWM fans can be voltage controlled and could be used with this product, the connectors are three-pin only. If you want to hook up a four-pin fan to this controller you'll need a three-pin to four-pin adapter. They include two in the packaging but they could have just made the product with four-pin connectors, no?

The other major problem is the CAM software. It's just not ready for Prime Time. It crashes every few hours and while I *hope* that it keeps the fans running after it crashes, do I really want to rely on that happening? Just like the other NZXT products, documentation is reduced to the point of usefulness. If I hadn't read in a review that it was possible I wouldn't have known that you can name each fan input to describe the fan ("front case fan" "VRM fan" etc...) but how can you rename the inputs? Nowhere in the documentation does it tell you, nowhere on the website does it say, you're just left to randomly click around until you stumble across the solution. Even then, double clicking on a fan name to type in a description worked sometimes and other times the change was lost when CAM was restarted - go figure.

Sadly, the Grid+ is too large to easily fit in the NZXT H630 case - it's just a bit too thick. They do recommend a placement that's physically possible but it blocks the SSD mounting sleds so that's not as helpful as you'd think. You would have thought that a company that designs both computer cases and computer case accessories would have put more thought into making the two more compatible.

Once I discovered the (multiple, significant) flaws with the Grid+ I uninstalled it and found another way to control the system fans. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone else and can't really imagine a scenario where it would be a practical solution.

product_title: Philips FLEX Wireless Portable Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
This speaker I gave only 3 stars for the following reasons: the tinny sound quality, the lack of information, and the gimmickiness. I thought the bright blue and green speaker with a shoelace made this a very cute and portable speaker. I liked the fact that it could fold down to what was about the size of a compact powder cosmetic and can be thrown into a handbag or backpack with ease. However, this is as far as it goes. Philips has no right to charge what it does for this item due to the lack of features it has. First, the pop up speaker part that is supposed to give it more oomph and better sound quality is a gimmick. I did not hear any difference with it popped out. It was still the same tinny sound like you get with those speakers that you can get at the dollar store. They may not be Bluetooth but at least those speakers are not the price that Philips charges. The lack of feedback that you get from this speaker is a joke too. I put it on the charger but I am not sure if it was fully charged or how long it would take to charge. I left it on the charger overnight assuming that it was fully charged. I had to use my own plug to charge it. There is no indicator when it is getting low so I just had to put it on the charger if I used it more than a few hours. I did not test if it held a charge for 12 hours.

Now, I will admit that this speaker is good in one respect. It is very easy to use if you are technologically challenged and you want something very simple to work. This is also a good little speaker for children because there is very little for them to play with and they can't ruin it by pushing the on/off button or pairing button.

The directions were useless to me and I just figured it out on my own since I have other Bluetooth items I had to pair with my tablet and cell phone. The technique is basically the same. I am disappointed that there is no volume control button on this item. Why not? The whole point was that I could have the speaker near me and keep my cell phone or tablet in a safe place so if I am cleaning or cooking, I do not want to have to worry about my cell phone or tablet getting damaged. I consider this a huge drawback to this speaker.

There are other Bluetooth compatible speakers that are portable with better sound quality. Many of them that I have found are less expensive too. I think Philips needs to rethink their design with this speaker. They sacrificed quality for cuteness which, is useless to me when I want to hear music.

review_body: UPDATE:  Now, I cannot even play content downloaded to my iPad.  This used to work, at least 2 times.  Even though I painstakingly downloaded the content (not streaming) to my device, and I can see it in the "offline" list, it refuses to play it.  Or the "Watch" button is simply greyed out.  You can't push it.  Again, what I'm attempting is not OOH streaming.  It has nothing to do with the port forwarding or any of that.  I download content to my iPad.  I go on the road expecting to play that downloaded content.  Then.... nothing.  This is all the DirecTV app and my have NOTHING to do with this piece of hardware.  But you can't use the hardware without the app.  Pass on this item.  ORIGINAL REVIEW: I don't know how to distinguish this hardware from the DirecTV apps that manage it.  Much of my issues with this hardware, may be bad programming by those writing the DirecTV (iPad) and GenieGO (iPhone) apps.  For all intents and purposes, you can't separate the hardware from the apps.  So this negative review may NOT be this hardware's fault.  I give this item 2 stars, instead of 1, because the install went relatively smoothly.  I got the solid blue light almost immediately.  But then, trying to use this via the GenieGO and DirecTV apps was a nightmare.  It would constantly complain about some of my DVRs not having the right access permissions, even though it downloaded content from them just hours earlier.  Content would seemingly download and just not be there.  The "out-of-home" access would constantly complain about not being active, even though I specifically set up port-forwarding correctly.  (This I know how to do.)  Then, the next day, OOH was fine, according to the tests.  Then, later on, it was not fine.  Content that had already downloaded would still show in the apps as "preparing."  You have to download content multiple times, it would appear, before you can view it on your device.  Yada dada dada....  I could keep rambling onabout the problems but you get the picture.  The only good things that can be said is that you can eventually get content to your devices and, at least for me, the playback (audio and video) is stellar.  There were no hitches or glitches.  I was happy about that.  I almost gave this thing 3 stars.  But, I couldn't.  I'm unhappy with it.  I'm not "okay" with it.  So, if you're looking to eventually get content on your smart device or laptop for later playback and you don't mind going through hassles and hoops to view that content, buy this box.  If you're the type that insists on things working as advertised, take a pass on this one.  Perhaps GenieGO 3 (with updated less buggy apps) will get you what you want.

product_title: aoeyoo AY33 AV S-Video RCA Composite Video to PC Laptop VGA TV Converter adapter box New
review_body:
WORST. PACKAGING. EVAR.

I just cancelled my return on this item. I thought they had shipped me the wrong item because:
1) The converter box itself is shipped inside an opaque sleeve
2) The instructions, packed inside the clear baggie that everything comes in, said "VGA To Video".

So I initiated a return.

Then I was looking to see what other sellers had a reliable composite-to-VGA adapter, and found several other instances of "wrong conversion direction" and "wrong instructions". So I figured, what the hell, I may as well open it up. And I did, and the item inside was indeed the thing that was advertised. *AND* it turns out that the instructions are for both composite-to-VGA and VGA-to-composite boxes, and which way they're folded determines which one shows. Maybe everyone who buys one of these in its country of origin knows better than to trust what the manual cover says it is.

So if you buy one and the manual says you have the wrong one, unpack it anyway. You may be pleasantly surprised.

As for how it works: the colors are all wrong (they cycle--the color clock isn't synced to the picture), but also the resolution shows up as "not detected" so perhaps if I try it with a really-multisync monitor, instead of something that's trying hard but not really getting it right, then it might work. It does definitely give me all the Luma information nice and sharp--it's only Chroma that's screwed up. At any rate it clearly IS taking a composite video signal and mostly displaying it on an SVGA monitor, so it at least minimally works.

product_title: Philips GoGear Raga MP3 Player
review_body:
I had an older version of the GoGear Raga, but lost it. I bought this to replace it. I was very happy with the original, which is why I bought this one. I'm disappointed with this product.

Pros:
- Small
- Easy to set up
- Enough space for my needs
- Plays my music
- Screen is better quality than my last device (higher resolution, better colors, clearer text)

Cons
- SLOW start-up - Every time you power the device up, it must update itself. It takes nearly a minute to do that.
- SLOW song selection - When trying to select a specific song, the device only displays three songs on screen. When you move down the list, the whole screen refreshes SLOWLY. I have a lot of patience with slow hardware. This bothers me. It might drive you insane.
- SLOW interface - The interface is unresponsive at times
- Glitches - This player froze on me more times in less than a month of use than my original unit did in its 3 YEARS of operation.
- Volume - This seems to be an EU device. The volume is limited to "20." Every time you turn the player back on, you have to
1) raise the volume to 20,
2) press the volume up button again,
3) wait a couple seconds for the message damaging your hearing,
4) hold the volume up button, wait for the beep,
5) have it return you to your song,
6) then press up on the volume again to get to max volume
You have to do this EVERY TIME you turn the player back on.

Final Verdict
I just wanted a simple, no frills mp3 player. This has the potential to be a great device, but the user interface lets it down horribly. I'm tempted to try a firmware update.

If I had known these issues going in, I would have taken the risk on the Sanza Clips, or I would have done better research on the GoGear Ragas.

review_headline: Great headphones... for about a month
review_body:
I'm something of a connoisseur of folding headphones-- I do a lot of traveling, and I hate in-ear headphones, so I'm always on the lookout for portable, durable, reasonably priced headphones with decent sound. I had high hopes for this pair-- they looked pretty sturdy, they had good reviews, and they didn't cost an arm and a leg.

When they arrived at the end of April (right on time, packaged nicely), I was pretty impressed. They're a little bigger than I was expecting, they don't have any kind of carrying case or bag, and the black plastic material of the band shows every possible smudge and fingerprint, but they fold up nicely and the sound quality is pretty great-- as other reviews have mentioned they're a little thin on the mids and highs, but the bass is fantastic, and they create a decent seal over the ear to give some passive noise canceling.

As the title implies, I was perfectly happy with these headphones... until I wasn't. After just over a month of gentle use (I mostly used them while stationary with my laptop, and I took them along in my carry-on for a weekend trip, folded up and with the cord loosely coiled) the sound in one ear went quiet, staticky, and distant, occasionally blaring back in when I jiggled the cord. I'll admit I didn't handle them with kid gloves, but I was reasonably careful about not tangling or tugging too hard on the cord and not subjecting them to unnecessary pressure or roughness.

For that first month, these were absolutely 5-star headphones. If they had a detachable cord that could be replaced, they would probably still be 5-star headphones. Unfortunately for me, they stopped working right just a couple days out from the Amazon return deadline, so I'll have to hang on to them and continue the search for headphones that work for me.

review_headline: These headphones cannot be charged any longer!
review_body:
This product was delivered on Monday, September 29, 2014. The product was packed well and the accompanying user guide was clear and comprehensive.

I use the product three times a week when I run on the treadmill in my gym. On each occasion I use it at least for 30 minutes and for no more than 90 minutes. The quality of sound is excellent as is the fit of the headphones in my ears.

The problem is that headphones have stopped working and cannot be charged. I have used the product for at most 35 times (on 35 days) when it stopped working. It simply does not get charged.

I used to charge the headphones fully once every 4 or 5 days. It worked very well for the first 6 weeks or so. Around the first week of December it started taking 8 or 9 hours to get charged. I made sure that the laptop was on and did not enter sleep mode (I did the same with my iMac). A couple of weeks ago it took 13 hours to charge.

It stopped working altogether the last two weeks. I cannot charge it at all from my MacBook Pro, nor from my iMac or from my Mac at work. There is nothing wrong with any of these Macs as I can charge other products (including my iPhone and an older set of headphones) on these Macs. The headphones are useless now.

I searched the internet and as well as the reviews and found several buyers that had expressed similar problems with this product.

I am appalled that expensive headphones such as these were so poorly made and broke down after very light use.

I'm a happy owner of the Bose V35 and was looking to replace it with the 520, as I desperately need the 4th HDMI input. I'm happy with the sound of the V35. Well, this is not the system for me and it is going back today. The 2 main reasons are:
1 - The sound quality compared to the V35 is just not in the same league. I hated it and this is the main reason Iâ€™m returning it.
2 - The system menu or volume doesnâ€™t come on your TV to show you what you are doing. You need to look at the 520 minimalistic display to see what is going on. Major disappointment! I love the volume bar on my V35 that comes up on the TV.

Now, i understand why this system is so much cheaper than the Lifestyle systems... the control unit is the problem. I connected the 520's speakers to my V35 (same speaker connections on the back of the speaker) and the sound was really good. I might just look and buy the speakers separately. I really like the sound from these new speakers, more detail, better voices, and better clarity with all the sounds.
Hope this helps. If you are looking to replace your lifestyle system and same some $$$, i don't think this system is for you :)

After playing around with these, it became clear that the red and black plastic inserts are simply too wide and prevent the screw-in base from screwing in as far as they need to. You can remove the plastic inserts and the screw-in base is able to screw in much farther and eliminate the gap that was there when the plastic inserts were in place. I wound up using these without the plastic inserts in place. I simply put the plastic inserts on the wire itself as shown in the last photo. product_title: JFJ Easy Pro Video Game, CD, DVD, Blu-Ray Repair Machine 110V
review_body:
I'm in my 30s and very capable of handling technology, and this machine is the worst. I was extremely careful with the instructions and attempted to repair 8 discs, but they were all made worse with my attempts to repair them. Most of the discs had some light-medium scratches and skipped in a few sections before attempting to repair them, and after using the machine they were worse or became unplayable. I started with some shorter cycles with the fine sandpaper without improvement, and then gradually got up to trying longer cycles with the course paper to try to buff out any visible scratches - this had a 100% fail rate and made most of the discs completely unplayable. Not only did I waste $120 on the machine, but I ruined several DVDs (mostly Disney DVDs that still sell for $15-20 each). My kids could at least enjoy most of them before, but now they're useless and a lot of them aren't for sale currently.

The company was not responsive to my concerns. I got this as an Christmas gift and it took a few weeks to get around to using it since I wanted to test a lot of discs and do them in a batch so it was too late to return it once I figured out that it didn't work. I contacted the company twice through their website and never heard back even though I let them know I was planning on reviewing the product and wanted to give them a chance to respond first.

Most of the reviews for this machine are decent so maybe I just had a bad experience, but I think I followed all the steps as carefully as possible and feel like this was a huge disappointment that has left me worse off. The lack of a response for my concerns from the company is equally frustrating. This may work for some people, but the machine is not inexpensive and I would consider it a gamble.

product_title: Aether Cone
review_headline: Has great potential...but not there yet
review_body:
**UPDATE** The company has gone out of business. The cone will only function as a Bluetooth/AirPlay speaker and will work with a Spotify Premium account

The Cone's coolness factor is way off the chart. Sleek and unique design, music at your finger tips (literally), and wireless (when fully charged). However the delivery of the entire experience is highly flawed. First off is set up. The instructions make it seem easy enough, but I had do repeat them three times until everything was set properly. Yes, it is quite cool to turn on the cone, press the center button and use a voice command to select your music. However, there is a long pause of silence before the music starts causing you to question whether you need to repeat the the process again. Repeating the process only makes it more difficult to get the music you want to play.

To change the music but keep within the same genre, you turn the dial around the speaker slightly. Once you do this, there is nothing indicating that something is going to happen. The music eventually changes, but with a long pause. The same goes for the big turn of the dial. Music selection is not great. Only one service is available at this time, Rdio. You can sign up for a free account, but to really get a greater song selection or select specific songs, you have to buy a subscription. You'll need to download the Cone app to identify songs, but even the app is buggy; Slow to load and identify songs and long pauses when trying to control the volume or change the song.

Which brings me to the one feature that is the Cone's saving grace, AirPlay. If you have an Apple device with AirPlay, you can listen to your iTunes library and any other service that also supports Airplay, like that hugely popular free streaming music service free from the long pauses that come from Rdio. If Aether can lock down relationships with some of the major music providers (and work out the bugs), then the Cone will be well worth the investment.be well worth the investment.

review_headline: Good for what it is, but what it is isn't good.
review_body:
This is the third or fourth mini-amp I've tried, it's the best of the bunch. Overly detailed in the high end, most real instrumental music practically unrecognizable, big band and orchestral music sounds almost comical...but apparently that is what people are satisfied with these days, convenience and portability being paramount. My brothers-in-laws (who don't really "listen" to music), are so proud of their wireless systems. Most everyone is uninterested in the effort it takes to reproduce real music with the "older" technology at their disposal. I would feel sorry for their loss, but they probably feel sorry for me for being so burdened by my "superior" tastes.
Music/Sound is the movement of air requiring detailed and substantial physical force. These anemic systems don't do it.

My wife called what came out of this thing "a reference to real music." Then I hard wired the tablet I was streaming from to my old Eton plug-in A/C radio with its single three inch speaker. "Wow," she said, "put that other thing away."

The reality is that this little speaker DOESNâ€™T sound better than the old KLH floor speakers. However, it does LOOK better, and it has no background fuz noise (this was a problem with the old setup).

The problem is that the unit does not handle virtual surround well at all. It also doesn't down-mix to stereo well. And to make it worse the uni-volume and clear voice settings are terrible. Customer Service at Powerbridge was very helpful, BOTH times. Each time, they sent a new lower box (inlet) to me via FedEx. product_title: AwoX StriimLIGHT LED Light Bulb with Integrated Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Clear your schedule. You may need some time to figure this out.
review_body:
Ok, let me start off by saying I consider myself to be fairly advanced when it comes to anything computer or phone related. With that being said, I feel way more dumb after trying to get this thing to work. It took me 3 hours to finally get this going. It looks like this was made by a french company, and they used google translate on the installation disk. First of all, the apps they want you to download don't exist. either they are misspelled, or they changed the name of the apps after they made the directions.
After some google searching and some youtube digging, I got the right apps for the android and computer. Notice I said apps, because you need 2 of them. After downloading them, they don't look like the screenshots that are included in the directions. At that point, I knew I was on my own. I'm a guy, so I don't need directions anyway, or so I thought.
For the next 2 hours, the speaker light kept telling me FAILED FAILED FAILED. I was 1 FAIL away before that vein in my head finally exploded and for no reason... BAM!! Success. Hot damn! I had finally hooked up to my Wi-Fi. I thought I was on the right track.
So now I need to learn how to use the apps. Remember not 1, but 2. These are probably 2 of the most unfriendly user apps I've ever seen. Anyway, when I finally figured out how to add my music library, I was able to play music through my light. Not just some music, all of it. The app doesn't separate albums or anything, so all your music is clumped together.
The sound is very good I must say. And it's louder than I expected which is also nice. The light is bright enough as well. You can control the brightness with a few dozen clicks on the un-friendly app.
Now I will say that I bought a used one. I definitely wanted the wifi version in case I wanted more and wanted to play the same music throughout the house. But I didn't want to pay $80. My used was $40, which is the only reason I'm keeping it. And I hate to admit it,but if I can pick up a couple more for $40, I probably will. But I wouldn't pay much more than that. Not unless it comes with a bottle of Advil.
The light is also fairly large, and a little heavy. So if whatever you're screwing this into is delicate, rethink your choice.
All and all, it does what it says. It's a light that plays music, and plays it well with good sound, and loud enough to please you.
It's not a bad product, but hopefully my French friends who created this will combine 2 apps into 1, and make it so humans can understand how to work it. Oh, and a sleep timer would be good too.
I'm dreading buying more and trying to sync all of them together.
I would be happy to give tips and tricks on how to get this all set up for you, but quite frankly, I don't know how I ever stumbled on the right way myself.

review_headline: It Works But Not UL Approved
review_body:
The plug works, but it is not designed for the US market. The top plug accepts standard US style fat plugs, but the side plugs do not (unless you use an adapter). It did not come with instructions on how to program it. Here is how I programmed the one I have.
1. Plug the HDE Infrared Plug into an outlet.
2. Press the small black button once to turn it on. A red light will turn on and stay solid.
3. Press and hold the black button again until the red light goes off and then comes back on and stays solid. Then stop pressing and the red light will start to blink.
4. While the red light is blinking, press and release the button on your infrared remote that you want to use to turn the device on and off. In a few seconds, the red light will stop blinking and turn off.
5.Press the black button again and the red light will turn on. The HDE plug is now programmed for your remote.
6. Test it be pressing the button on your remote and see if it turns the red light off.

product_title: Crosley CR8005D-BK Cruiser Deluxe Portable 3-Speed Turntable with Bluetooth, Black
review_headline: Uuuuuuggggghhhh, I should have thought this purchase through!
review_body: I did not purchase the Crosley Cruiser from Amazon but the review here may help others.  This player, like a few other Crosley models, are sitting right next to vinyl displays at various retail outlets.  So, if you're like me and have a teen who's discovering vinyls like they are something new, you'll be tempted to grab this player when you buy her/his first few albums.  Please fight the temptation as these units are complete rubbish.  If the album is not completely flat, or if it is not in pristine condition, or if the sun and moon aren't in perfect harmony, the album will not play well or at all.  The players are toys and either never work well or work with only a handful or perfect albums.  Your teen will be bummed and you'll think, \\"Maybe it's the stylus so I'll buy a new one for $14.99 and swap it out.\\"  Good luck with that.  First, it's a thought of desperation that a brand new player might require a new stylus.  Second, you'll likely never get the old stylus off without breaking the arm in the process.    The ONLY thing a Crosley player has is built-in speakers, which sound tiny with zero bass.  Don't let this fact, or the cool retro packaging trick you into buying it.    You'll be so much happier purchasing an Audio-Technica AT-LP60.  This player is well-built, has an AUTOMATIC start/stop arm, and sounds great.  All you'll need is a separate pair of powered speakers, such as a pair of powered computer speakers.  Some reviewers have purchased Bose computer speakers, Dayton powered speakers, or in my case, I simply plugged the AT-LP60 into my Bose Soundlink Mini's aux input.  Now my teen can toggle between listening to vinlys or streaming Bluetooth from her cellphone.    Good luck with whatever you decide but my experience with Crosley was dismal.

product_title: Altec Lansing LifeJacket Next Generation Ultra Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Great speaker, with many hidden (not emphasized) capabilities!
review_body: This thing really surprised me, with a few extra features that I didn't expect or think of. First off, the sound really is great. I will follow that statement up by saying that I am not a huge audiophile, and I don't have any incredibly expensive sound systems. However, I do listen to music fairly loud, and this thing more than gets the job done.  Another cool/somewhat disturbing aspect I never considered is the ability to use Siri (or the android analog) through the speaker. This never occurred to me until I literally took a call in the shower the other day. Since then, I've been using it to select songs in the shower, as well as any other random Siri questions I have like making calls and reading/sending texts [not all in the shower :)].  The one major dissuading factor for me was the price point, but I was able to pick it up on during Black Friday week for a significant discount. After having it for a few months, I don't think the regular price is even that inflated for the value you get.  EDIT: As  a few others have pointed out, the charging point must have some flaws in construction as mine came dislodged. I was able to get an RMA through Altec, but their CS has been a disgrace. Difficult to get ahold of, and I've had no update on the status of the warranty. I was fairly vague when I described the issue, but they "guranteed" me a new one would be shipped out.

product_title: IOGEAR 3-Port HD Audio/Video Switch with Remote GHDSW3,
review_headline: Does not work with my Apple Macbook Pro
review_body:
I looked at various HDMI switches before picking the IOGear GHDSW3 switch. To be honest I picked it because I know the brand name IOGear better than the many others I saw and figured that IOGear would support their product. I am disappointed to report that they don't.

I have two computers I want to share the same monitor. One is my Windows 7 desktop and the other my 2012 Apple Macbook Pro. The Windows side works perfectly well through the switch; however, the Macbook has all sorts of noise (white specs flashing all over the screen) which can go from annoying to preventing me from using the Macbook with the monitor. The Macbook works perfectly well when directly hooked up to the monitor using the same cable as I use with the switch. Furthermore, I have another 5-port Sabrent HDMI switch which works with the Apple. (I intend to use the 5-port on my home entertainment system) The Sabrent system has a power supply.

I contacted IOGear's support through their web-chat and after explaining the problem the rep said it was either defective or required a power supply. The rep then declared the unit defective, in my opinion hastily, when he learned I had bought it through Amazon within the last 30 days. However, I suspect the problem is that the Apple side does not supply enough power through its HDMI connection. A power supply would solve that issue; however, the unit was sold without a supply.

Since I really don't believe the unit is defective I am reluctant (honesty is a curse) to return it to Amazon vendor. So I am left with a quasi functional switch for which the only recourse is for me to buy a power supply or eat the purchase.

product_title: La Crosse Technology BC1000 Alpha Power Battery Charger
review_headline: Charger is over priced and lacks a much needed feature. Included Batteries are Garbage
review_body: I have charged my own batteries. Discharged and Charged Batteries. Done the refreshing mode testing out each feature the charger has with 30 plus of my own rechargeable double AA and triple AAA batteries. The one thing I really don't like about the charger is it lacks the function to tell you the time remaining until the battery is charged  so you are constantly wondering when are the batteries going to be charged. Hours? Days? Who Knows.Yes I know you can crank up the charging amps and get those batteries hot for a super fast charge or just pop the batteries in and let the charger go to the 200 milliamp charge rate and just leave it. But I was looking for a smarter charger and actually add some life to my batteries. My cheap rayovac battery charger at least tells you the time left until the batteries are fully charged. For the price range of the charger it should have this function. Yes it has many functions to tell you the rate in milli amps that the charger is putting into each battery and all sorts of good things. But in my opinion  it is an over price re-branded cheap Chinese Battery Charger. Yes I know all of our electronics come from China and I have bought hundreds of items directly from China and the price is about 1/2. I have owned dozens of battery chargers over the years and this one for the money really doesn't show me that there is that much benefit to it based upon it's cost versus other lower priced chargers. Also the cheap La Crosse tech NIMH Batteries are junk. The 2600 mah double AA batteries will only charge to 2150 mah and less and 2 of the batteries show signs of leakage from the tops of the batteries. Batteries are total garbage. The triple AAA 1000 mah batteries will only charge to 800 mah max. Another Fail. I guess the La Crosse technology name must really suppose to put some magic into this charger. Not... If I had it to do over I would not buy this charger.

product_title: Sony  Digital Media MP3 Player
review_headline: OK if you have big ears, but low bang for buck
review_body:
I had two players now, which gives some points of comparison.

I used this player and the "Diver (TM) Waterproof MP3 Player with LCD Display".

The Sony Walkman has the advantage of being in one piece, which means you don't have to plug anything to it when swimming. It is also light and compact. This has drawbacks too, though: first, it always gets entangled in everything that come in contact with it (my goggles, my swimming bag,...). Second, if you have small ears, the Sony will not fit well, and you spend about 1/4th of your time readjusting it. After 30 minutes, it starts aching, because the pressure on your ears becomes too strong. I also find it difficult to operate, since it has no LCD display.

The "Diver (TM)..." is more classic: you have a player, to which you connect your waterproof earphones. These have buds of different sizes, and there is one size that fits my (small) ears :). It fits my head much better, does not hurt, and is easier to operate. The main two issues I have with this one are (1) the first player I had did not work well, and I had to return it. Apparently, they fixed the problem: the company had great service: they returned the new model immediately, kept inquiring about whether the new one worked better, and offered to replace it again because of one quibble I had. The one I have now works great. (2) The player does not play mp4 files; only mp3 and wma (who's still using these???).

In both, the sound is OK, but not outstanding.

All in all, although it looks a bit old fashioned, I thus prefer by far the "Diver (TM)".

review_headline: Fantastic Looks and Functions, But Sound and Radio Reception are Only Okay
review_body:
When I opened the box and unwrapped this radio the looks alone promised fantastic sound and great radio reception. This is a seriously good-looking box. Mine is the glossy piano black. It's classy and high-tech looking with controls laid out well. I use it in my business office and, frankly, it's a bit of a showpiece. Everyone notices it and asks me what it is.

Yet, the sound is only okay and the radio reception is no better than any other radio I've every had...except my car radio that picks up signals flawlessly.

The bluetooth connection connects and works well with my iPhone 6 and the controls on the front of the unit allow some control of the playlist--at least in the sense that I can skip to the next song, etc. However, the sound coming from the bluetooth is a bit thin and no amount of adjusting the tone will change it significantly.

The radio comes with a thin-wire external FM antenna so I've tried it in many positions but I can take the "fuzz" out of the signal of the most powerful radio signal in my metropolitan area. I ordered another T-type external antenna and it did nothing to improve it. Thinking that perhaps I received a lemon, I returned my unit to Amazon and had them send me another one. The next unit was exactly the same with no improvement.

In the end, I've kept the radio--partly because I love the way it looks and the sound is okay. I also like the way it displays the date and time. I really only use it for occasionally listening to talk radio anyway, so I figure it's adequate for what I need.

Those who aren't picky about sound might find that it sounds great to them. And radio signals are simply finicky things. It may just be that my office building just isn't very radio signal friendly.

review_body: I have a 5.1 Onkyo home theater system and wanted to upgrade the receiver component to this Pioneer VSX-1123 for its 4K upscaling. My Onkyo 5.1 system is still working great and is 3D but not 4K so I am still wondering if a 4K upscaler would give me a more enjoyable viewing experience but I couldn't determine that with this Pioneer VSX-1123 even after spending so much time trying to get it to work.

review_headline: READ THIS IF THE AUTO-SLEEP IS A PROBLEM
review_body:
I returned the first one because the auto-sleep function didn't work right. Its shut itself off every 30 minutes if you didn't change the volume etc. even when there was input signal going to the bar and the bar was in use. Its not supposed to do that. Returned the first one, got the second one, same thing. I was really irritated. By total luck, I found a page online that mentioned a function to disable the auto sleep altogether. That was not mentioned AT ALL in the documentation I received with the sound bar. TO DISABLE AUTO-SLEEP: With the bar turned off, hold down the Mute button on the remote for 5 seconds, the unit will turn on and auto-sleep will be disabled. The BD/DVD will not be lit when it turns on - this is the indicator for auto-sleep disabled.

After disabling the auto-sleep, the bar works great. I paired it with a sony subwoofer. Music and movies are both really good.

review_headline: Noise cancelling works well, but headphones have serious design flaws
review_body:
These headphones worked really well for a few weeks, and I thought they were an amazing value. Unfortunately, there are two massive flaws with this product:
1. The On/Off switch is really flimsy, and stops working after a few weeks of moderate use. It must be some weird analog electrical switch inside that wears out. Once that happens, the right speaker (opposite side of the switch) stops working entirely.
2. The noise cancelling amplifier picks up any sort of RF interference and turns it into a loud clicking noise. So basically, you can't use these with noise cancelling turned on plugged into your phone unless it is on airplane mode.

I like the AT brand, and these seem like a good value, but trust me: avoid this product. Many other reviews echo my same complaints.

product_title: Phobya 3-Way PWM Splitter Cable (Power 3 PWM Fans from a Single Connection!)
review_headline: Great shortcut, but you're taking a risk having 3 fans feed off of one splitter cable
review_body: Initially, I thought this was a great idea. My motherboard only had 3 system fan sockets (excluding the CPU fan socket) and my case had an option for up to 6 fans. Since I was running a gaming rig setup, I wanted to use as many PWM fans as possible to keep the whole unit cool. Hence, this 3-way splitter. I connected 3 SP120 High Performance fans into this splitter and into my motherboard. After hours of diagnosis, I found out that this shorted my motherboard. I believe this splitter cable would be fine with 3 low powered fans, but high performance fans all feeding into 1 cable and into 1 fan socket on a motherboard is risking it. Otherwise, I'd find another way of linking multiple fans onto one mobo.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
Bought this speaker at another store, but this is a better place to leave feedback as it reaches more people. I've used this speaker about once or twice a month since I bought it 15 months ago. This speaker has never been abused - never dropped, played at 100% power for extended periods (except for a few seconds when curious people wanted to see how loud it could play), splashed with water, kept in cold, damp or extreme heat, etc...

Last time I used it, everything was fine. Out of the blue, it sounds like a speaker is blown or part of the electronics have fried - there is very bad distortion even at the lowest volume from the left side. This is the only reason for a 1 star - a speaker should give more than ~65 hours of use before packing it in.

My internet searching has led me to believe that this is an isolated incident, as I cannot find this probleme duplicated elsewhere. If anyone has had a similar, please let us know. A speaker like this should last a minimum of 10 - 15 years (as a plus, the battery can be user-replaced).

I intend to buy another Soundlink Mini in hopes that this will not happen again, since the sound is the best I've heard from a Bluetooth speaker that small and portable (plus I already have the pricey travel bag, plus the pricey protective cover). I still recommend the Mini even though I gave it a one star for letting me down so soon.

Edit 09 Apr. 2015 : I ended up buying a Denon Envaya Mini DSB100. It compares favorably with the Soundlink Mini - a little smaller around, but a little longer; doesn't have as much bass, but also doesn't sound as muffled, with a tighter bass and crisper highs; it can be charged via USB, so it might take a little longer to charge but you don't need to haul around a special charger. What it has that the Bose doesn't - it can be used as a speaker phone, can connect using NFC and is splash-proof (nothing major really). Lastly, the Denon is $50 cheaper but doesn't seem to have a user-replaceable battery (I Hate having to throw things out because I can replace a simple battery. There ought to be laws to force manufacturers to allow consumers to do such a simple thing!). Either way, you can't go wrong with the Bose or Denon. Personally, I find that the Bose looks better with it's metal case, and will also impress more with it's heavy bass for it's size. After extended listening to both (my father has a Bose for me to compare), I prefer the Denon but the difference is not earth shattering. Check out online reviews and YouTube to compare both.

review_headline: No bluetooth volume control from phone while making calls

I wanted more robust sound from those speaking on the other end of the phone.  The device pairs with my phone with no problem and the sound quality is good as expected.  However, there is one major flaw - there is no way to adjust the volume on the speaker from my phone (Samsung Note 4) and the volume is much lower than it should be because the phone's volume cannot be adjusted.  The volume bar with the bluetooth symbol on my phone will slide up and down while on a call but does not change the volume on the speaker.  So there is no way to control the phone's volume with the phone itself..  And this issue creates another problem -  the default bluetooth volume on my phone is not set at the highest level and cannot be changed... therefore the volume on the speaker does not get loud enough for me.  The bluetooth feature for making phone calls is clearly broken.  I sent an email to Sony for a fix... otherwise it's going back.

product_title: Ematic Accessory Kit for Tablets and iPad with Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: It's best attribute, is that it looks like the photo.
review_body:
I do not generally buy into the notion that you get what you pay for, however, this speaker certainly does it part to convince me. I purchased this to use as a basic alternative to my laptop speakers, which don't really provide much in the way of volume. On the few occasions that this speaker actually did function, the volume was fine, and exactly what I needed. The first issue was that it did not charge at all. Not necessarily a big deal, since it sat very near to an available outlet. The real trouble came in trying to actually get it connected for use. While using bluetooth, I never placed this any more than 2 feet from my laptop. Even at this close range, the connection was useless. It connected, and then immediately disconnected, and continued to do this until I had to just turn off the bluetooth entirely. To add insult to injury, each time it connects and disconnects, it lets me know by producing the world's most annoying sound. After many attempts and failures, I resigned myself to just connecting it directly with the auxiliary cable included with it. To my surprise, this connection gave me more trouble than the wireless one. In addition to the constant connect/disconnect problem (and the accompanying annoying connection sounds) the speaker also produced constant static, even at very low volume.
For less than $20, I certainly did not expect any kind of amazing audio experience, but I did expect something that functioned, even in part, as advertised. The only positive thing I can say about this item, is that it looks like the photo.

At first glance this mount has a level on it, tilt, pull down bottom install clips, end stops, VESA 400x400 and is all one piece. However, I didn't catch that this mount was only 16" long, it looks a lot bigger on their picture. Mount is solid enough for up to 40" TV's but you better know exactly where you want it on your wall. I installed two of my own 40" TV's right next to each other on drywall with metal studs. For drywall all you need for these is toggle bolts (they hold about 100 lb's each bolt and you don't have to find the stud). I put about five toggle bolts in each and am not worried about the 40's falling down. I'm a special case, I install TV's for a living, I would recommend you go with a peerless instead. Peerless mounts go for $30 on amazon sometimes (worth the wait). Remember, you get what you pay for. Good luck with your install.

product_title: Sennheiser Digital Wireless Headphones
review_headline: Reduced my rating to 1 star. Unit died in three months of intermittent usage.
review_body:
PLEASE SEE EDIT at the bottom of the review BEFORE you buy.

I purchased the RS 170 for my wife, for use with her PC. We have a mostly wireless office, due to the fact that we have cats and cats seem to love anything resembling a cord.

I did a lot of looking and reading reviews. I looked at all of the Bluetooth offerings and the other wireless offerings, like this one. I really thought I would go with Bluetooth, but what I found was a big discrepancy from very high end, (Expensive) sets, to very low end and low quality, sets. I know the Sennheiser name and their quality first hand and eventually I came back to this set.
My biggest concern was interference.

As I say, we have wireless everywhere in the office. Two wireless mice, wireless keyboards and a wireless router. None of them have ever had an issue with each other, but I was concerned about some of the comments of people having issues with wireless audio.

There are no issues. None at all. The base unit is sitting on the desk right next to the wireless mouse and keyboard. It is within 6 feet of the wireless router also and the headphones are crystal clear. Let me state that again. Crystal clear. Absolutely no background noise at all.

I had to use a splitter, from one jack, to two, so I could keep the regular speakers and still have the headset. I plugged it in and turned on the base first, then the headset. The sound is really very good, but I want to mention something here that seems to be left out of many reviews. That is the source of the sound. I think some people have high expectations and they are disturbed when they don't hear the kind of sound they are hoping for. Well, consider the source. What kind of audio output do you have to begin with? The sound is only going to be as good as what you put out from your device, to the headset. In my wife's case, the PC has onboard sound, with absolutely no adjustments, other than volume. No equalizer, nothing. So my expectations were not high, but this set of headphones exceeded anything I expected. They are clear as a bell and the sound is much better than the desktop speakers. We did turn on the extra bass, for deeper bass sounds and it did a good job of enhancing without killing the bass. We did not like the surround sound at all and turned it back off.

My other concern was range. Our office is in the back of the house and I knew my wife would want to be able to wander around while listening. Well, the range is better than I expected also. She left the office, went through the kitchen and out to the garage and closed the garage door. She still heard crystal clear sound, with no interruption, even while she was in the garage. This means the signal had to go through the brick wall of the garage. That is amazing to me. She also walked all around the ranch style home and found no place where she had any problem at all. Even in the front bedroom inside the closet.

The headset itself is light weight and the full sized cups allow for over the ear use. The cups are very soft and the pressure is light, so they do not hurt the head. I would not want to run with them, but I would want to sit and listen for a couple of hours, no problem. The volume controls have the on/off button centered between them and I think that is a mistake, but it's so minor compared to the positives, that it is nothing of consequence.

We love the headphones and are very glad we chose a good name with good quality.

All I can say is that the RS 170 was worth every penny for us.

review_headline: Everything except the clarity of sound is great (Sound is thumpy, dark, veiled, and colored).
review_body:
Wow, I really had high expectations for this product. Especially given the price. It is competent but the audio quality is sub-optimal in ways I did not anticipate.

First: The Noise Canceling.
The headphones do a good job of blocking a lot of background noise irrespective of the noise cancellation feature. With the headphones turned off, they still block a lot of outside sound. However, turn on the noise canceling function and it is noticeably quieter. It is however not as quiet as I expected, and some noise bands (lower frequencies) are attenuated more than higher frequencies.

Second: General Audio Quality.
Here is where I was most disappointed. Don't get me wrong, these are fairly good sounding headphones but certainly not in the league of what half that price will buy you for non noise canceling bluetooth headsets. Bass is overemphased - more thumpy and dark than a good balanced headphone. Some people may prefer that sound but it is not natural and flat. High frequencies seem veiled like you have a thin blanket over your head and the headphones on the outside. High hats, snares, fret slides and breathy sounds are muted and the top end is wilted. There is also a noticeable color and a hollowness in some of the vocal range. This is present whether blue tooth connected or hard wired. Of course hard wired sounds better than bluetooth if connected to a high quality source but the same audio compromise still manifests. I'm 45 years old and my ears can still very clearly hear the finished highs. I brought an AKG K551 headset a few weeks before for $200 and expected the Senneheisers to sound better. In actuality the AKG K551's really (unexpectedly) had a substantially clearer and truer soundstage, flatness, clarity and natural sound than the Sennheiser Momentum Wireless. However I did have to make sure the fit was good on the AKG's. Until I figured that out I thought the AKG's were lacking bass. However fitted correctly all is now very good. I have decided I cannot accept the downgrade in quality for the Sennhiesers so I will be returning them - the noise canceling feature is not that great and not worth the $300 extra than the AKG's.

Third: Build Quality
I cannot fault the Sennhiesers here. Immaculately presented. Nice carry bag. Good accessories. Great build quality. Good size. Very comfortable. If only they could give me a nice clean,Nnatural, Uncolored, flat EQ response, less thumpy bass, and good crisp high frequencies then this would be a match in heaven. Not good for classical, folk, or vocals and in my opinion the 'pop' EQ really gets in the way of my listening pleasure. However I'm a purist and can tell great clarity when I hear it. review_headline: Looks Great, Works Well, Smells Horrible
review_body:

The zipper is sturdy, works smoothly and is attached to the case quite well. You can shake this case like a maraca, but once the CD's are inside their sleeves and the case zipped close nothing will slide loose. There's some room at the back/bottom of the case to fit CD literature (there's no pocket, these will simply lay loose).

The Bad:
Lightly pressed/glued rather than stitched sleeves. The sleeves are not made for heavy-duty use; so if you're a DJ, or serious music lover who'll be sliding CD's in and out multiple times a day I would suggest a Slappa hard body case instead - you get what you pay for.

The Ugly:
Case arrived smelling like it had marinated in a cigarette factory prior to shipment. I'm not sure if the smell is from the materials that the case is made of or if the case was somehow exposed to something adverse. Sadly the smell is so strong that it's nauseating, but it isn't worth the hassle of returning. My hope is that this is an anomaly and that most buyers won't experience the same issue.
- If it weren't for the cigarette smell I would have rated this with 4 stars.

Overall:
A functional and good-looking (dare I say sleek) storage option for the average user - that is priced reasonably.

product_title: HDTV Antenna - High Performance & Multi-directional - Use Indoor or Outdoor - Compact and Easy to Install - Diamond Image TV
review_headline: Decent Antenna, but the description is misleading.
review_body: I am about 30-35 miles from my broadcast towers and live in a hilly area with lots of trees. When the item arrived I was surprised at how small it was. Hooked it up, did a scan and received nothing. No signal on any channels. Even my homemade tinfoil fractal antenna gave me low to moderate signals indoors. I moved it outside and wedged it between my gutter and siding in a horizontal position and was receiving most of my towers at low to moderate signal strength, but the signal was constantly dropping out. The weather was clear but windy. I was disappointed in the performance, especially after reading all the stellar reviews here. This morning, with no wind, every tower but one was receiving a moderate to strong signal with no dropouts. Leading me to believe that if I mount it higher so that it misses most of the tree line I will have very steady performance. I will note two issues. 1. This antenna, would not pull in our local NBC affiliate which like most NBC affiliates still broadcasts on the VHF spectrum, leading me to believe that this is a UHF only antenna and should be noted as such in the product description. 2. While this is a decent moderate distance antenna, the claims of it being good up to 120 miles are greatly exaggerated. Even at 30-35 miles, I am most likely going to have to add a pre-amp to get solid performance from all of the major UHF stations.

product_title: RAYOVAC PS73-4BT6 Rayovac 7 Hour Power Pack
review_headline: Primitive voltage regulator / Poor utilization of disposable batteries
review_body:
I purchased the [[ASIN:B00PSON0AU Rayovac 7-Hour Power Pack]] (PS73) from my local HarDware store, because the price was too good to pass up (it was cheaper than buying 8 alkaline batteries alone). I figured that it could come in handy in case my neighborhood suffers yet another extended power outage. After testing the PS73 power pack, however, I was disappointed.

I expect the PS73 to contain a power converter to regulate the 5V output at USB port, whether the input battery voltage is 6V (when using a fresh set of 4 alkaline cells) or 4.8V (when using 4 NiMH cells). As it turns out, the PS73 has a simple linear regulator inside, so it is only able to step-down the battery voltage, but not boost up.

When using a set of fresh alkaline cells, the combined voltage is 6V (1.5V * 4), so the USB output port can be regulated at 5V (the extra 1V is wasted internally). As the alkaline batteries become partially used up and the combined voltage drops to 4.8V (1.2V *4), the USB output voltage drops to just 4.5 - 4.6V (the regulator itself drops additional 0.2-0.3V). This is the same situation when using a set NiMH cells (1.2V * 4). An output of 4.5V is borderline too low for most USB-power devices.

How much energy can the PS73 extract from a set of 4 alkaline AA cells?
A typical AA alkaline cell can only deliver 500mA for around 2 hours, before its terminal voltage drops below 1.2V. So the total energy that can be delivered by this charger is 5V * 0.5A * 2 hr = 5Wh. This is a relatively small amount of energy given the size and weight of this package. Just as an example, to fully recharge the 2100mAh lithium-ion battery in my Samsung Galaxy S3 cell phone requires 3.7V * 2.1Ah = 7.8Wh of energy, not counting conversion losses. So the PS73 is only able to recharge my S3 by about 60%, after exhausting one set of alkaline cells.

The 3-LED battery status indicator comes on whenever an USB plug is inserted (there is a mechanical switch inside the USB port to turn on the voltage regulator). It consumes 20mA and is excessively bright. This is just a waste of power - unless you like to use it as a nightlight. The number of LEDs seems to correspond to the output voltage as shown below:
- 3 green LEDs = Over 4.7V
- 2 green LEDs = 4.6 to 4.7V
- 1 green LED = 4.4 to 4.6V
- 1 Red LED = Under 4.4V

Conclusion:
All things considered, the PS73 is still useful as a last-resort charger. Suppose there is an extended power outage and I have exhausted all my rechargeable power bank units, I can put alkaline batteries in this product, just to get some power for my essential USB devices. I consider it an 'Okay' value at the low price I paid. But I cannot recommend it at the present Amazon price (~20 USD). For about the same price, you can easily get a power bank unit such as the [[ASIN:B00GRQ8AQM KMAX-812 4400mAh Rechargeable Backup Battery Pack]]. It can deliver 3x the energy (15Wh), at half the size and weight of this PS73.

If you need a well-designed power converter that takes alkaline or NiMH cells as power source, consider the [[ASIN:B004B9ZK4M Duracell Mobile Charger CEF23AU]]. It can step down as well as boost up battery voltage, to maintain a regulated 5V output. The converter will continue to function even when battery voltage has dropped to 3.6V, so it is able to squeeze at least 50% more power from a set of alkaline cells. Its only problem is that the output is rated 500mA max.

On the positive side, the PS73 is a lot better than the [[ASIN:B00HCBDV10 PortaPow Battery Charger and Power Bank]] . The PortaPow unit does not even have a voltage regulator, only a diode in series with four batteries. Now THAT is a real piece of trash. See my review on it for details:

product_title: JVC- Marshmallow Earbuds
review_body:
I bought my first Marshmallows in 2007 or around there. That pair lasted me so many years. They retailed $15-20 at the time, but I got them on sale for $8 back when Circuit City existed. These...are not Marshmallows. A cheap imitation with the same name. I don't know why JVC scraped a few dollars off the price to remove all the quality with it. The wire feels cheap in comparison, the plug feels cheap. And the sound, they sound like tin cans. The highs have this pinging sound to them and the mids are nearly non-existent. The bass is OK, still sounds decent. But that's all that's left.

I've never been so saddened to see the quality of a product fall like this. They still sell HA-FX33/34/35s (ignore the FX30s) in many places, and they are usually only a few dollars more. You will not regret going with them instead. No wonder they used a lower number (FX32) instead of a higher one, because it was a huge downgrade in quality.

I see a lot of positive reviews here, and if you are upgrading from your stock iPhone/Droid earbuds, then yeah, sure, they sound better. But if you get the older Marshmallows or just Google "best earbuds under $20", you will see the difference.

product_title: Studebaker SB6051 Wooden Turntable with AM/FM Radio
review_headline: New Records Skipâ€¦Not Worth the Money
review_body:
Bought this as a birthday gift for a loved one. Looks great. Speakers are cheapish but okay if you don't want it to be too loud. We hooked it up to a small amp we already owned, so sound wasn't a concern.
It plays old records fine, but after buying new records, I noticed that the records were skipping on the "outside" tracks (outer part of the album = first couple of songs) even though the records were factory sealed and brand new. At first we thought this was the fault of the records, and returned a few multiple times for replacements. Unfortunately, the problem persisted, so we started google searching the record player and have discovered that other people have had this problem as well. Apparently there is something wrong with the needle that prevents it from playing the new records properly. We bought several different albums new and have had the same problem, although the older albums play fine.

I am very disappointed in this record player, because I chose it because of the high ratings and reasonable price, but it won't play new albums made in the past few years without skipping, which is a major problem. If looking for a good, solid record player, I would buy a different one that isn't so finicky. Who cares if it looks great if it doesn't play all of your albums correctly?

review_headline: Don't throw away the instruction manual

For example, to set the time zone you have to pick a number from 0 to 7. Which zone belongs to each number? There's no way to know except for digging out the manual. Then there's the button with the seemingly contradicting labels 'alarm reset' and 'off'.

Want to turn the radio on and off? That's two different buttons that don't look like they have anything to do with each other. One says 'off' but the other just says 'radio' - that's the one that turns it on.

The bottom line is a clock radio should not need an instruction manual. The engineers dropped the ball on this one.

The PS3 is an alkaline charger with NiMh as an added bonus. product_title: Sony STRDH550 5.2 Channel 4K AV Receiver
review_body: OK let me start by saying that I typically purchase lower end audiophile equipment (not the stuff rock stars buy but the stuff serious listeners buy) so my expectations of audio gear are high.  OK, My mom was looking for something basic that would not be very confusing just to listen to Pandora, DVD, Netflix and anything else her smart DVD player could show or play.  I had some older Boston Acoustic book shelf speakers I have her and thought that this stereo looked simple enough so I purchased it along with a 5 CD carrosel changer (I didn't know those were not really made anymore :) ).  Anyway everything setup pretty easily but I noticed that the weight on this was pretty light suggesting a less than robust power supply.  Again I get it this isn't a flagship receiver but still I thought it might be beefier.  Next I was disappointed to see that simply tuning the FM radio required that the HDMI be hooked up to a TV since you can only cycle through programmed presets via the remote or front pannel (as far as I could figure out).  The remote and controls are basic which is what I wanted but I had to get an HDMI cable and hook up to the TV to essentially use the FM radio.  One the presets were programmed I could change between programed presets.  The sound quality is a bit flat - even for an inexpensive unit.  I know the speakers can do better but the sounds is a heck of a lot better than what the TV can do which is what I was looking for.  A minor thing but I felt that the FM antenna loop was a bit small - fo something so inexpensive it would have been nice if it was a few feet longer to get it up higher.  Again not a big deal.  I was impressed that an inexpensive unit like this includes a mic to auto callibrate the surround speakers.  I did not use this as I have not installed rear speakers yet but I will try it later on.  Overall not overly impressed with this unit but not entirely disappointed either.  I would imagine any entry level unit is similar in this class however if you enjoy your movies and music I would advise that you pay about 30-40% more and hunt down a higher end unit that was refreshed recently (so last years low-midrange model) over this entry piece.

review_headline: Use of the included stakes (which were nicely heavier duty than I would have expected) or some ...
review_body:
I bought this for the convenience of having a screen to use outdoors and when travelling. As a user of lighting reflectors, I was not dissuaded by the spring steel frame and this feature did not cause any problems for me when putting it away after use. Use of the included stakes (which were nicely heavier duty than I would have expected) or some other weight is a must to keep the screen from tipping over as it is front-heavy and without something holding it down the breeze from someone walking by is enough to tip it.

But the thing that does bothers me most and ultimately is causing me to return it is the amount of wrinkling on the screen. I was hopeful that the synthetic fabric used for the screen would be magically wrinkle free but that is not the case. Even after leaving it open in a warm environment for three days the screen had many wrinkles that were very visible while watching a movie. I tried stretching the fabric by pulling on the flexible frame and I even set it in the full sun for a day. The only thing I didn't try was ironing it or steaming it. The former would have been difficult to attempt and I lack the tools to perform the latter.

I think I shall try one of their more conventional pull-up screens.

product_title: Comply  Isolation PLUS Earphone Tips
review_headline: Stay away if you have Jaybird Bluebuds X.  Not worth your time.
review_body:
I was quite disappointed by these earphone tips. Here's why:

Extremely poor fit on my Jaybird Bluebuds X. I watched the video multiple times to see exactly how to get the tips onto the earbuds, and not only does it take an uncomfortably large amount of pressure to force these onto my expensive headphones, they never sat straight on the posts. It doesn't make sense to advertise that these are compatible with these specific headphones and then force me to modify them to work.

The build quality leaves a lot to be desired. As I mentioned before, they take a large amount of pressure to seat onto the posts of my headphones. Well, luckily I tried putting the wrong size on first as the foam ripped off of the plastic interior portion. For such a niche product that is supposed to elevate my listening experience, and charging ~$4 a piece for these, I was very let down.

They don't stay put during any kind of workout that causes you to sweat. After all of the above drama, I get continually frustrated during my workouts to have to re-insert my earbuds multiple times. I'm not doing any exercises that are putting any strain on the cord of my earbuds, but almost instantly after beginning a rep, the sound quality diminishes to a very low level. With normal tips you would just have to cram them back in, but with these you still have to compress them and then wait for them to re-expand once in your ears. Not how I want to be spending my time in the gym.

tl;dr - Frustrating to add to earbuds, disappointing quality, and even more frustrating in actual use. Stay away if you are buying these for Jaybird Bluebuds X.
