product_title: Bose SoundTrue Headphones On-Ear Style
review_headline: Audio is muddy compared to similar headphones, lacks detail.
review_body:
I'm not an audiophile and only just recently purchased my first pair of mid-range headphones (Sennheiser Momentum On-Ear), and it was a minor revelation that music could sound so good. I ordered this pair on Prime Day, thinking I'd get something even better than the Sennheiser's, due partly to the higher original price, but also the Bose name. Sad to say, I'm a little disappointed. The Bose look nice, they are lightweight, fold into a very portable size, and come with a nice case, but the sound quality is nowhere near what I was expecting. Compared to the Momentums, everything is very muddy, and the highs are difficult to pick out; it's almost like listening underwater. I've swapped between the two several times, with different music, and the result is the same, the Sennheisers are crisp, and the music sounds very detailed (for lack of a better word), and the lows are silky and very warm (they could be deeper, but they're still very comforting). The Bose, on the other hand, just sound muffled. Debating sending them back, the only thing keeping me from doing so is the price and size - I may be able to use them for travelling, as they'll pack easily, and I won't be worried if I lose them.

EDIT: Sound quality is significantly better with an iPod than with my MacBook or Nexus 5, still prefer the Sennheisers.

review_headline: and it's recessed a good 1/2". The ellipse (the oval looking part before ...
review_body:
This review is for the swiss adapter. It's junk. Avoid.

The actual shape of a Swiss receptacle is a polygon, and it's recessed a good 1/2". The ellipse (the oval looking part before the metal plug bits) is supposed to be able to fit into the polygonal plug. It doesn't. Too big. You might force it in with a hammer, but then there's no getting it back out. I purchased the 4-pack and all of them are this way. Compare these to, for instance, the Apple european adapter which is of the correct shape and size (though it only has 2 prongs vs the Swiss 3). Fits perfectly.

So... the adapter advertised as working in Switzerland? It may well be the bee's knees elsewhere, but in Switzerland it's crap.

product_title: RCA ANT702Z Digital Amplified Indoor/Outdoor Antenna
review_body:
I bought this to get better reception since I am 26 miles from the closest tv tower. The antenna by itself got worse reception than my Winegard antenna that I was going to replace. I got three crisp clear channels with the Winegard and three spotty channels with the RCA antenna by itself. The kicker was the power amplifier. It boosted the signal to three crisp clear channels on the RCA antenna but when I attached the Winegard to the power amplifier, thats when I got all the local channels which where 13 total channels.
I gave three stars because it is a good antenna with the power amplifier for a range under 30 miles and not the 40 miles it states. The three channels I got were 26 linear miles from me but the other channels I got after the power amp on the Winegard are 38 and 42 miles from me.
Summary: if you live in the stix, this isn't the antenna for you! Get a yagi style. Longer range but its directional.

product_title: Denon AVR-X4000 7.2-Channel 4K Ultra HD Networking Home Theater AV Receiver with AirPlay (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body:
Apparently it's a hit or miss proposition getting a reliable, problem-free AVR-X4000. As with many others, in many other forums, ours kept powering off, then powering immediately back on, eventually even freezing to the point of having to unplug the power, from the very beginning.

We gave this unit the benefit of the doubt, despite the numerous complaints about similar issues (unexpected shut-downs) from other users on different forums, but will be returning this for another brand (Onkyo TX-NR1030 -- since "board"-related issues have been resolved for 2012-2013 models, or Yamaha RX-A3030, 3040). The obvious "Troubleshooting 101" steps were taken, including ensuring speaker wires were not grounding against the chassis or other speaker posts/wires, even connected new Klipsch RF-62 IIs and RF-82 IIs, etc., etc, etc.

Originally, our thoughts were to upgrade to the Denon AVR-X5200W, however, Denon is evidently going through senior management changes (high churn) and financial turmoil (Bain Capital unable to restructure debt, for "struggling audio equipment retailer [sic] D&M Holdings Inc.â€ which includes Denon), which has also affected our decision to shift our focus toward other manufacturers.

On the other hand, contrary to what some have said about Denon Support, we've found their collaborative style tech support to be very helpful. This is one of the main reasons we had wanted to stay with Denon, but after reading all the same complaints about the same issue, plus the aforementioned management and financial concerns (historically implies organizational instability), we're simply gun shy. Personally, I detest, absolutely detest, having to return or exchange products. My schedule is far too busy for those types of needless, time-consuming transactions. While there's no guarantee that we won't have issues with another manufacturer, we'd rather roll the dice with another brand after our problems with Denon (again, other than support).er than support).

review_headline: The only negative review I've ever written for a product I was given for free
review_body:
Edit: mine started charging again (not sure why it ever stopped), and so, because of the excellent radio and good sound quality, I'm bumping this to 3 stars.

I wanted to like this. I too owned the iPod nano this is so clearly meant to replicate. I was offered a free sample for evaluation, and I was excited to get it. I've spent many weeks trying to decide if I should evaluate it, but I've been pushed to do so by Charles Spanky's brave 1-star review as well as my brother's much higher four-star rating. Plus... I'm just tired of the need to review it hanging over my head.

So... why two stars instead of the one that Charles gave?

Because this item does have some nice aspects to it. You get a 16GB micro SD card, a mini USB cable (useful for 15 year old devices you find in drawers, perhaps), earbuds (low quality, but serviceable), and a fun little puzzle ("how to I get this darned thing to work?"). You also get a surprisingly decent audio recorder and an FM radio that actually sounds fantastic with better headphones plugged in. Music sounds really good as well. I mean, truly, genuinely good. I wasn't expecting that.

So, why two stars instead of the four my brother gave?

Because I fear that rating it higher would kill the little that remains of my soul. This just isn't, in my opinion, a four star device, even at $25. Maybe it's worth half that... maybe it's a four-star $12.50 device, because then you could part it out upon its death and recoup your expenses. Maybe.

But... look, I love tech. I love love love love tech. I have more phones than fingers. I get giddy around anything mechanical or that consumes (or generates) power. I'm excited by this sort of stuff usually, even the low-end things. But I just cannot stand this one. The button-circle-control thingy is *horribly* inaccurate/laggy/inconsistent. The movie player only plays movie formats that no one living has except maybe on a PC from 1994 somewhere in their basement. Ebooks? Um, no. Even if you could manage to get one on-screen, the control pad would make reading it unbearable. Music plays great... but the 1999 folder scheme has been out of date since the first iPod and is - again - near useless when using the control pad to navigate it.

Worst of all: the thing died on me. I let it run out of charge, and now it cannot be used when not plugged in. It simply will not hold a charge for even a second's worth of playing - it's like there is no battery at all. I've tried charging at 500mA, at 1A, and at 2A. Nothing. So, as little as this was worth as a $25 device, it's worth less as a $25-plus-external-battery device.

If it played movies in formats known to modern humans, I'd rate it higher. If the directory structure made finding music easier, I'd rate it higher. If the control pad worked well, or if it used micro USB, or if it didn't die after going uncharged for a few days, or if it came with a 64GB micro SD card, I'd rate it higher. As it is, I just can't.

You want something better? New prepaid cellphones are often near this price and will perform so much better. Not long ago, the nice-for-the-price now-discontinued [[ASIN:B00E45043A Nokia 520]] was $20. The fantastic [[ASIN:B00HPP3QD6 Moto G]] has been as low as $25. I own both of these, and they ABSOLUTELY BLOW THIS OUT OF THE WATER and can do everything this can (except the Moto G doesn't use a micro SD card).

Look around at prepaid cellphones. They are cheap, and many will do everything this does and more. Buy one of them instead...

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_headline: This product has both good and bad features
review_body: This product has both good and bad features. First the good: it is not just an MP3 player - it will play many different digital formats including MP3, WAVE, AIFF, and several others, intermixed. The lossless formats allow the reproduction of sound waveforms with absolutely no waveform distortion or tone coloring, so the audio quality is as good as a CD player. It is intended for use with earbuds, but can also supply audio to a Hi-Fi system. It is tiny and very light, and will run for several hours on its internal battery. One bad characteristic is its GUI - there are many modes, options, and settings, so the menu tree is complex and not very user-friendly. Another problem is its battery charging circuit: if the battery is run down, you cannot run the player from the charger while the battery is charging. This is not a problem if you only listen to the audio when you are out jogging. Another problem is the USB connector, which is used both to charge the battery and load the audio tracks. This connector is tiny, but very sturdy, with a metal shell, but is not well supported inside the player. Unfortunately, my player was totally destroyed after I had used it for just a few months when the charger cord was accidentally jerked and the USB socket broke away from the motherboard inside.

review_headline: Just a reminder on speaker wire parameters -
review_body:
The concept is good, has been used many times under limited conditions for decades, and the results can be adequate, but there is a ...BIG... catch in all this -

Speakers (the physical end point of your audio system) require power and are rated in wattage they are designed to use. Most people just concentrate on the RMS ratings, peak rating, and dB efficiency and don't really give speaker wire much thought. Speakers will normally have a minimum wattage which must be applied to get the speaker to move/actuate (for most this will just be a few watts); but at minimum watts the speaker will only deliver very low levels of volume. Due to the 'gauge' of this flat cable, it is comparable to very thin speaker wire (16 AWG), so be forwarned that you will never be able to adequately power 100 watt speakers and above; for that you will need 12 AWG or larger speaker wire depending on how long your speaker wires actually are.

Five things to remember when purchasing speaker wire (for anything larger than small 'book shelf' speakers [60 watts RMS and under] a few feet away from your stereo) -

1) Pure copper (not copper clad aluminum [CCA]): hopefully oxygen-free copper [OFC] so the copper wire will never suffer from oxidation and be ruined over time for conductivity (think "Statue of Liberty" green).
2) Gauge: is dependent on the power desired and length of your speaker cable run for each channel. Speaker cable used is just as important as the speaker, speaker staging, and the A/V receiver to obtain the end result of what you have spent money to hear. Fatter speaker wire is ALWAYS better, as long as it will still fit into the connectors your system has.
3) Length: the longer ANY given gauge of wire is, the more resistance will be encountered and the less power capability will be delivered to the end point.
4) Connections: if you had the beefiest speaker cable on Earth and somewhere along the path (beginning, end, or inbetween) you introduced a tiny (small AWG) section, then you have degraded the entire flow properties of the cable, and the resulting power capability delived to the speaker.
5) Staging: you must have a long enough speaker wire run to allow you to properly stage your speakers for the room they will be in. Think science, not convenience. This means that unless you have very expensive equipment to conduct staging analysis, you will initially need more cable length then you thought due to your need to conduct experimentation on speaker location. For that room, there WILL be waste the first time, and if done properly... the last time you will ever buy and install speaker wire for that room). If everything else is in order, but your speakers are in lousy locations for where you will sit ('sweet spot' or 'King's Chair') to listen to the audio, you have just degraded all your work and money spent.

review_body:
I bought this thing because it's pretty much the most affordable turntable I could find, and its really cute honestly, and with built in speakers, I could just throw the whole thing up on a shelf and call it a day. When it came in the mail I was excited, and the thing does look really cool in person. Playing records on it, the sound was really poor compared to what i'd heard on my friend's turntables. I expected that, but after playing one record on it, the second was already starting to sound wonky and distorted. The same night i got it, it had already fallen apart. The part of the player that holds the needle was hanging off by its wires.
I went into a little sound system shop today and talked to the owner and he explained to me that Crosley is basically the worst brand to look for when it comes to turntables, and these little portables are really designed to fall apart in a matter of weeks!
Anyway I'm not angry or anything, but I thought it might be worthwhile to get this info out there because $70 is a lot of money to waste. I ended up buying a whole sound system (used speakers/amp new turntable) for about $300. Which is a lot more than $70 i know, but LPs are expensive and if you're gonna collect them, you might as well have sturdy equipment to play them on. It sounds much better than the Crosley did.

product_title: Outlets-To-Go
review_headline: Wasteful Blue LED Makes Restful Sleep Impossible!
review_body:
If you have traveled in Europe (or a lot of other continents) you know that many hotel rooms, and especially the older ones, have only one electrical outlet. So if you have computers, cell phones, tablets, camera batteries, and other devices to charge, you absolutely need something like this to travel with. Just add an adapter, and all of your devices have an outlet to charge from.

So what's not to like about this one? For some reason, Monster decided that you need to have the a bright blue LED suitable for a Christmas tree in an arctic climate to illuminate the outlet. Imagine trying to sleep in a European hotel room with such a thing running, especially if that outlet is located right next to your bed. Blue LED light, like green LED light, is even worse than amber or red if you are trying to sleep.

One of my tricks in traveling is to carry Frog Tape to cover all the unwanted LED lights in a hotel room and get some sleep. This one is so bright that several layers of Frog Tape don't cover it up. Why waste all the electric power? Why should a power outlet strip have an LED that you can't turn off, when all the things you are likely to plug into it also have LEDs you can't turn off? What a waste of resources!

product_title: MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphones with Memory Wire
review_body:
I have a pair of bluetooth MEElectronics on-the-ear headphones and love them. I was optimistic about these.

The "around the ear" wire thing results in a HORRIBLE listening experience. I struggled for hours to come up with a "process" that would allow me to put the headphones on so they lined up with my ear canal. And as soon as I took the headphones off, the process started all over again. If i took the "sport" thing seriously and attempted to work out or run with these, I would end up fidgeting with them for the entire workout. As soon as i moved my head or tugged on the wires, sound became muffled or "unbalanced" since one ear sounded OK while the other didn't. I tried ALL of the provided ear "adapters", even the cool Christmas tree ones (similar to earplugs). The built-in wires do not look like the picture and easily flatten out, so don't expect them hold on to the ear. Again, it took WAY too long to get the optimal position for these to sound OK, and even then, the sound was just "OK"... nothing good, and definitely not worth the money IMHO.

If you enjoy being frustrated and like spending your time trying to "fix" stuff, only to be disappointed, then buy these. Otherwise, I recommend going with the cheap and easy Panasonic RPHJE120K or perhaps a set of wood "Symphonized XTC" headphones, also cheap and easy. I bought both of these with this same order and am happy I did, both sounded better than the MEElectronics and were easy to stick in my ear.

review_headline: Avoid This Particular Apple Product: "It Stinks."
review_body:
Having owned the following:

1st Generation iPod Nano ( I loved it and dropped it in the snow.)
4th Generation iPod Nano (I loved it and still have it, but it's only 8GB.)
6th Generation iPod Classic (I liked it, but it was heavy.)
7th Generation iPod Classic (I loved it, but sold it to buy this version from Apple.)
iPhone 3G (Pretty neat, I sold it so I could get the 4.)
iPhone 4 (Best version I've used. I sold it so I could get the 5.)
iPhone 5 (Meh. I sold it so I could get the Samsung Note 4 - which I like better than the iPhone 5, but it's no iPhone 4. That was a good phone.)
and
iPad Mini 3 (I've given it to my significant other, because I have the Note 4.)

I can honestly say that this is the absolute worst Apple product I've ever owned. I could not and cannot get my audiobooks onto the device through iTunes. Then, after having it sit for 4 weeks after getting it back from service, I have another issue with it in addition to the original issue. I'm now sending it in for service a second time. If it were a cheaper (cost) product, I'd have smashed it to pieces in frustration.

If you're looking for a music player, look for the iPod classic or Nano - they're 5/5 stars from me. If you're looking for a device to play games, surf the net and play music over a wi-fi connection, but without a cellular connection/contract, then go for an iPad Mini or other smaller tablet device - particularly one that has a Micro SD card slot, so you can load and back up files. I can't recommend this until they either change the buttons for easy tactile feel or add button lighting that automatically turns on when the alarm goes off.

review_headline: Bass-Heavy Sound at a Budget Price
review_body:
These headphones have too much bass -- so much that it can drown out vocals -- for me to enjoy listening through them, although music listeners in search of huge bass will likely be happy. Still, I find it disconcerting for vocals sound as though they are in the distance. Even though this is only a problem with heavy-bass music, it results in somewhat muddy vocals even in music without less emphasis on the bass. These perform according to their budget price point.

Of course, bass lovers may appreciate these -- a lot. They look great, are comfortable, and have an adjustable headpiece that, at the very least, fits smaller heads. You can use the mike and controls on the cable to answer calls. The folding design is nice. And the fabric-covered wire does not tangle easily. They may be good headphones for a preteen or teen or anyone who doesn't want to spend a lot on over-the-ear headphones. Note: I received a sample for review.

-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann

product_title: Logitech Harmony Touch Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen
review_headline: Cool toy, good potential, suffers from flaws
review_body:
I received this remote as a gift. It is a cool remote with a lot of potential, but suffers from some weaknesses.

The Good:
- Will control all your devices
- Can pretty easily learn any function from any existing remote
- You can map the buttons however you want
- Favorite channels is a handy tool
- Supports firmware upgrades - looking forward to the future
- Once you have it configured to optimal settings, you won't miss your old remotes at all

The Bad:
- It's awkward to connect the USB cord to the remote due to the way the port guard works and how deep the port is set into the remote
- When you need to use the number pad on the touch screen, it's kind of annoying
- Some of the gesture commands are difficult to differentiate
- The remote lacks two of the most commonly used buttons on my DirecTV remote -- skip forward and skip back. Fortunately, I could reconfigure the remote to utilize these functions, but first I had to make the Harmony learn the functions from the DirecTV remote before they worked (lots of steps involved!)

The Downright Terrible:
- The MyHarmony software is pretty bad. Every other time I use it, it hangs when trying to sync the remote. I have to exit the program, disconnect and reconnect the remote, and start over. Sometimes this works, sometimes it doesn't.
- MyHarmony sometimes hangs for long periods when not syncing as well, with no apparent reason, and no way to cancel out of whatever screen it was on when it hung.
- The remote appears to remember the last state of your devices, which can be really frustrating. I've noticed that if my TV turns off on its own from inactivity, then the next time I try to use the Harmony remote, it won't work and I'll have to use Fix It Myself to turn the TV on or get to the right input, which takes 4 actions on the touchpad. I'm not sure why the remote does this as I don't think it's mandatory from a functionality standpoint (I could be wrong). Either way, it's really annoying.

I'm hoping that after a couple weeks of use I now have the remote configured the way I want it and I won't have to use the mediocre MyHarmony software anymore. That only leaves the very annoying quirk of the remote remembering the last device state, which can be worked around by being diligent to press "Off" whenever you're done using the TV.

product_title: Stereo Wi-Fi Music System
review_headline: Before Sending Back - Modify Network Settings
review_body:
I've done a few reviews on products from Amazon in the past few years and I've been pretty consistent...4 stars for most products. Why 4 stars? I believe if a product meets your expectations, a 4 star rating is warranted and if you are pleasantly surprised by a product then up goes the rating to 5. If the product is below expectations, but still functions as stated, then down to 3 stars it goes. Unfortunately, the GDI-IRC7500 doesn't quite provide the quality in hardware that I would expect for an internet radio in this price range.

The sound I would have to classify, as O.K., not great, but O.K. I'm comparing this to Boston Acoustics Solo Clock radio purchased 2 years ago for ~ $100. With one speaker, the Solo's single speaker provides a noticeably richer and crisper sound than the 7500's dual speakers and subwoofer. This is based on the same aux source. Considering that the 7500 is over twice the size and double the cost, I would at least expect equal, or superior, audio performance.

The second issue is connectivity. I was experiencing the problems with connectivity seen in other reviews where buffering and periodic loss of internet connection occurred often. The radio would only hold a connection if the unit was in the same room as the router, but considering this was not where I intended to place it, this was not a solution. After 2 days of experimentation, saw the connectivity improve noticeably by turning off the wireless network security...again not much of a solution, but a step in the right direction. Finally, dropped my connection speed from 300 to 145 MBits/s on the router and the connectivity problems vanished.

My impressions? The wireless hardware in the radio is at least 5 years behind present day technology. Considering that the users are moving to the 5.0 GHZ range, are running dual band routers at a combined 600 MBits/s, and the standard is moving to AC, the GDI-IRC7500 feels a bit obsolete right out of the box.

Finally, the interface feels a bit sluggish especially when scrolling through long lists of stations. Again, it just feels like the hardware is a bit underpowered for its purpose.

Overall verdict? Just a "Meh". It's working, It will provide much enjoyment in the future, but considering I need to slow down my network to make it work and it's $200 price tag, I'm underwhelmed.els a bit sluggish especially when scrolling through long lists of stations. review_headline: Bass, Bass, Bass, and not good bass.

I can't understand how anyone can say the sound output on this radio is anywhere near acceptable. I needed a simple radio for the bathroom to listen to news in the morning. AM radio is the easiest answer. News, traffic, weather, and the sports while I shave then out the door.

But all I can say is Bass, Bass Bass. And not good bass. Muddled, cloudy, indistinct and warbly bass that distorts all spoken words making it impossible to understand. I had to turn up the volume just to be able to figure out what was being reported on the news.

So, if you have any desire to listen to any talk radio, and understand it, this is not the radio for you.

The speaker is directed down, which is NOT the direction for treble sound. That's ok for bass, but any high frequency is not transmitted in any meaningfully clear manner.

I returned it for
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0012YFY54/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o06_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Sangean PR-D7 AM/FM Digital Rechargeable Portable Radio - White

And yes, I returned it.

product_title: Anker Classic Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker, Powerful Sound with Enhanced Bass, 20 Hour Battery Life, and Built-in Mic, works with iPhone, iPad,Nexus, Laptops and More
review_body: I am disappointed in this speaker.  I purchased the smaller version of this speaker about a month ago and love it.  This speaker does have better sound quality and more bass.  However, the speaker is about 3 times the size of the ultra portable version and is not nearly as loud.  It is probably about 3/4 as loud as the smaller speaker.  I bought this speaker because it was larger than the other one and assumed that it would be much louder.  I was mistaken.  If you need to fill up a room with music, get the ultra portable version from Anker.  If it is just for your personal enjoyment and you will have the speaker next to you, this is a nice speaker and has decent sound quality.  I may be a harsh critic, but most people would assume that when you purchase a larger speaker, you will get more volume to go with it.  That is not the case with this speaker.  If you need volume, look elsewhere.  Update: After considerable use and testing of the speaker: it is louder than first thought.  It may be slightly louder than the other Anker speaker mentioned above.  Here is the catch:  The volume button on the speaker does not actually control the bluetooth volume of the device it is connected to.  IT is independent of the device bluetooth volume.  Thus, you can max out the device volume, but still have low volume out due to the speaker's volume being set to low.  Unlike many other speakers that control the device volume, this one does not.  I would recommend maxing out the speaker volume and controlling volume through your device.  This is not very good good work from Anker.  I will raise my review from 2 to 3 stars.  However, I am still disappointed in the overall operation of the speaker.  This field is full of bluetooth speakers and Anker is not quite there to be considered a quality contender.  I still recommend looking elsewhere for a quality, budget-friendly speaker.

review_headline: Another mediocre product with stellar customer service
review_body:
First the review.
Plus. Attractive, comfy in ear, great friendly customer service
Minus. Mediocre sound, scratchy sound as textured cable rubs on your clothing. Defective plug kept stopping music, even calling Siri!! After complaint, the earbuds were replaced. We'll see how long they last.
But please, read on. This product is emblematic of a relatively new, alarming business model.
How to climb to the top of Amazon rankings? Sell a cheaply made good looking Chinese product at low prices and pay off your customers for flattering reviews. No, not bribing. Send them a follow up email inviting to post only + review and get replacement product if unhappy.
This has the following consequences.
(1) it skews the ratings towards favorable
(2) it saves the company on quality control costs: it's the customer who is performing final control, by scrapping the junk they should never have sold in the 1st place.
If they really wanted to improve the quality of their products, they'd ask for the return of the defective ones, in order to analyze them. But no - they are content to just ship another, no questions asked.
As of today there are 1800+ reviews of this product with 18% rated 3 stars and below - this suggests thousands of dissatisfied customers, assuming that most do not bother to review. So why do people continue to buy products like this? Because theyâ€™re relatively inexpensive and because thousands of people buy them. product_title: ArrelaÂ® External 5V 2A AC/DC Power Supply, 1.35mm x 3.5mm
review_headline: Two units failed to work with compatible, known good devices
review_body: The first and replacement shipments of this AC adapter I received failed to work with either of two known good devices. They both delivered about 5.17v with no load, but failed to work with either my Foscam FI8918w webcam or my OOMA Telo unit.  Both of the devices are rated at 5.0 v 2 a, and continue to work successfully with other power supplies with the same rating, and tip size, in fact I am able to run the webcam successfully with other power supplies rated as low as 1.2a, with no problem, for days on end. I've had that webcam and OOMA unit for several years, and have never had any problems with either of them.  I went ahead and measured voltage output from the AC adapter with no load, and then when connected to my FI8918 webcam, using the Arrela supply, and a couple of others, for comparison.  Arrela 5.0v 2 a output rating: Unloaded = 5.17v, Connected = 4.9v, fails to initialize webcam  Foscam Model SAW-0502000, 5v 2a output rating: Unloaded = 5.24v, Connected = 5.13v, webcam operates normally  Compaq Model SA0105-A, 5v 1.4a output rating: Unloaded = 5.14 v, Connected = 5.07v, webcam operates normally.  I have since received other 5v 2a AC adapters, from Amazon, but a different manufacturer, which have each worked properly with both devices.  While I was unable to get either of them to work with the adapter from Arrela, I was very pleased with the Amazon replacement/return process and execution, and I appreciate the attentive and prompt responses from the Arrela rep, Andy. He always responded to me very quickly and helpfully, even in the middle of the night, in once case, and he arranged, via Amazon, for a complete reimbursement of my cost for the unit after the second one proved defective.  I don't know what the problem with the units was. I doubt that I was the victim of a statistical aberration, receiving two defective units out of a collection of serviceable ones. Perhaps there was a small cluster of defectives in inventory for whatever reason. I do know that the devices I attempted to use it on were and are functional and compatible with the specs of the Arrela unit.  One other minor point. The cable provided with this adapter is quite short. I measured about 35", which is notably less than others, and makes it problematic for use in some of my applications. I suggested to Arrela that they should include a comment on the Amazon listing for the device.

review_headline: Written up in reviews as the best bang for < $100
review_body: Written up in reviews as the best bang for < $100.00 and given the stats for lower, highs and mid range by one viewer I was sold. I had a pair of Sennheiser adidas over a year ago (stolen) and loved them. First the way the connected to your ear, unique, effective and comfortable. The sound was well defined through all ranges and had great volume. Months later I ordered another pair, absolute disappointment. The highs, treble dominated resulting in a tinney, cheap sound. Sennheiser either changed speakers in their Adidas or I got a bad pair. Feel like an idiot for recommending these to friends and for buying the CX 300 II buds. The ratings on these put them above the rest in class (<100.00) so either most people are used to poor quality sound or my ears have finally failed. I realize that any speakers are very subjective but having had the Klipsh Forte's and Forte II's, which were a sound I loved, I know that these were popular with thousands, of happy customers and friends who had heard. So I am not unique in my audio speaker tastes but very disappointed in Sennheiser as I thought that I found a company I would use for all ear bud purchases. As you undoubtedly know (you are searching for a new pair) it is not easy to find a pair that has quality sound. I am amazed that they can create, or used to, such good sounds for the size but it appears that things have changed and I am done buying and trying ear us which you can not try first. Of course you can return but how long till you find another pair that you will hopefully like.

review_body:
I've been trying to find a good pair of Bluetooth headphones for the longest time and have tried out a few different pairs on Amazon, but all have sounded like crap (crap = worse than the apple ear pod's sound quality, for reference). However, that control bit is the big flaw with these headphones. It's so heavy! It would be okay if it wasn't so close to the right ear bud, but it's practically three inches away, and it will HANG off of the ear bud. It won't rest on your body, you can't support it by clipping it to your shirt, so it will hang off of your ear. And did I mention it's heavy? It feels like a giant hoop earring, without the clip holding it to your ear for support. It kept falling out of my ear with the slightest head movement. So that was the deal breaker for me. I couldn't go running with these due to them falling out all the time.

In the end, I'll be returning them. Only because of how awkward the control bit is. Everything else about the headphones is great. If the control bit was farther away from the ear bud or if it was lighter, it would be perfect.

product_title: JVC HA-MR77X Xtreme Xplosives Headphones
review_headline: Who are the people writing these reviews.
review_body:
An Honest Review.

I had my father purchase these headphones after I suggested them from my research. I had convinced him to buy a pair of over the ear headphones after I recieved and loved my Samson850 studio monitors headphones.

TL:DR: Don't but these.

These headphones have bass. Not good bass however. The mids sound like ass coming from a studio monitor headphone,and the highs are unimpressive. I would honestly suggest returning these and saving up for a better headphone. There are many out there for the same price and cheaper.

Box/Accessories: Shipped in a nice sturdy box. No Accessories aside from the headphones themselves, an small guide, and a small piece of paper detailing the warranty policies. (1 star from box/accessories)

Build Quality: The reason this product got more than one star is mainly due to its build quality. The whole product is quite sturdy, and somewhat flexible. My initial impression was that these could be dropped a couple of times with no noticeable damage to the headphone. The headband is flexible and the ear cups feel to be firmly attached to the headband, despite the rotating cup feature. However, the product is somewhat heavy. If you plan on wearing these for an extending amount of time, you will feel the band irritate the top of your head. Which leads me to this products comfort. (1 star from build quality)

Comfort: I only wore them for about 5-10 minutes, but I could tell that these headphone and not suited for long listening sessions. The headband will irritate the top of your head even after short listening sessions. The ear cups are not very comfortable either. While they do swivel up and down for DJ use, they do not conform to the shape around the ears or the angle of the head very well. I felt higher pressure on different points around my ears -especially the space between the front of my ears and eyes. The padding on the ear cups is also uncomfortable. Now I knowI could be biased coming from a cloth padded headphone (Samson850), but I genuinely think the parts of the skin in contact with the material for long periods would start to become irritated. Lastly, and as mentioned before, these are slightly heavy.

Sound: I won't spend a lot of time here. I'm no sound engineer or audiophile, but I can give you an impression from my Samson850's which are branded as a neutral headphone. First off, let me be blunt. No offence to JVC, or the others who purchased this headphone, but if your coming from anything aside from a pair of Ipod ear buds, prepare to be disappointed. These. Sound. Like. Ass. I don't know what sort of audio equipment these other buyers are coming from, but that was my honest impression coming from a $50 ( yes, 50 USD) Samson850's.

Highs: Disgusting.

Mids: What mids?

Bass: Over marketed.

Okay, you may be thinking - "wow, this guys seems like a total snob, he probably sits in a studio all day listening to $1000 headphones on $1000 DAC/Amps". No, this is not true in fact. I have two headphones. A pair of ear buds that came with my android phone, and my Samson 850s. No amps, no dac's. I am your run of the mill Joe who enjoys music just like you.

Just to give a comparison. Like I've mentioned a thousand times before, I own a Samson 850 studio monitor headphone. These are considered neutral. The highs, mids, and lows and are supposed to be as balanced as possible. The only thing, and I mean ONLY thing these JVC's have that my Samsons850's do not, is deeper base extension ( and twice the price!) Like who would have guessed right? I can't give this headphone a plus for that however, simply because it can't even do it well. Sometimes I find my self yearning for bass when I listen to hip/hop, metal. heavy rock on my samsons, but I wouldn't switch to the JVC's even if you paid me...that's not entirely true...but you get the point.

Other gripes-
Short cord.
Non-detachable cord.
I had researched these as closed headphones, however, these leak sound quite a bit. I would not use these for travel or office listening.

In conclusion - Please save your money. JVC is one of my favorite brands, and maybe I was expecting to much, but these simply do not deliver...what so ever. Leave a comment with any question.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Lousy Bluetooth Connection/Retention. Bose's Bubble has Burst for this former fan.
review_body: I am not a big spender but I've always secretly enjoyed the Bose deep base sound. I also really like technology, electronic devices and the convenience factor of WiFi and Bluetooth. My latest fad seems to be Wireless Bluetooth Speakers. Even though BT speakers are light and portable I find I need one in each section of my home so I don't have to go to far to get one going to provide better sound than my iDevices alone provide. Thus I have purchased five BT speakers in the last year. This is probably a lot for an old lady in her seventies. But I do like tech! Recently I found myself in a Bose store with my son shopping for a Blutooth speaker for his daughter. He left with a $300 unit, the newest portable Bose Bluetooth device. I left with this $200 Bose Mini. It does have its pros but it's cons are simply unacceptable. For instance: The sound is pretty good. Not the full Bose quality, of course, but pretty decent for a small device. It is adorable with the pretty teal cover I bought for it. The cons are its operating light positions and it terrible Bluetooth connection quality.  The control lights are on top where they can't be seen from a distance unless one is standing and standing close. Bluetooth connection and retention are horrible. It is not the worst Bluetooth Connection I've experienced, that goes to a Etekcity Bluetooth Speaker. The Bose easily earns a close second for Worst, Most Troublesome Bluetooth Connection EVER! The Etekcity is a cheap device. The Bose is a very expensive brand that should work blissfully easy but doesn't!  I've owned it a week and can't wait to return it to the closest Bose Store. What was Bose thinking? Do they believe that folks don't care how easy it is to connect or that people enjoy running between devices flipping switches back and forth, doing resets, reboots and touching the Bluetooth signal send button again and again? And the Bluetooth drops!  OMGosh. Drives me nuts. Each drop turns off the Bluetooth Bose receiver meaningI have to stop what I'm doing and go turn it on again at the device, hoping it stays on long enough for my device to find it ten short feet away. The little light is atop the device so  you can't see what's going on from across the room. You have to get up and go see. This happens frequently within minutes of getting the Bose to connect for the first time in any given session. Is Bose so into their sound technology that they can simply ignore strides made in related technologies - like Bluetooth?  I've got a cheap Anker Bluetooth Speaker I bought weeks ago to replace my wonderful (initially) G-grip brick that just died in me. The Anker from Amazon has good sound, decent volume and is bargain priced. This Anker cutie connects, fast and easy -EVERY SINGLE TIME AND WITH EVERY SINGLE DEVICE!! It wins my Best Bluetooth Connection device award. It's easy and pretty darn wonderful! The Bose is going back and I'm gonna look for another sound brand to lust after when my next ship comes in. Bose no longer impresses me.

product_title: Denon AHGC20 Globe Cruiser Over-Ear Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones
review_headline: A Great Piece Of Technology Hindered By Poor Sonic Performance
review_body:
Denon is an old line Japanese company, founded in 1910, that was well known to audiophiles in the 1960's through the 1980's for their mid-to-high end audio equipment. The Denon brand name came after a merger with DENki ONkyo in 1939 and they specialized in developing digital technology and professional/consumer recording equipment. After merging with Marantz in 2002 they became D&M Holdings. They obviously have great musical cred.

I was really eager to receive and test these headphones, wondering if the combination of bluetooth technology with the highly respected Denon name would result in a versatile product able to leverage today's technology to a higher level. What I found was that the technology is good, but the sound quality disappoints. Before we get into an important discussion concerning what \\"sounds good\\" to anyone, a few caveats are in order. Back in the late 1960's I always bought the highest end audio equipment that I could afford. Music was a passion that ranked up there with girls and cars, and I ended up selling high end equipment the last two years I attended college. My hearing was acute and I prided myself on being an audiophile. Today I have less than one-half my original hearing to work with. Music is produced differently now (to our disadvantage) and my hearing is pretty limited.

Those things being said, what each of us hears, whether from the daily noise we encounter or the music we love and appreciate, will sound different to each and every one of us. I listened to several old favorites using both these Denon AHGC20's and the most recent Koss Pro4S's. Please keep in mind that how each musical piece was recorded GREATLY affected the sound quality, whether the noise cancellation system was engaged had a large impact, and even the type of connecting cord used changed the sound noticeably. So the statements I'm going to make on a comparison basis are by necessity quite general.

The Koss Pro4S's are light and airy, weigh less, have a brighter/clearer sound, but are more brittle on the highs. The musical tone is quite flat with minimal bass and the effective sound stage is narrow instead of evenly disbursed. The Denon's are quite a different animal. They are weightier, more comfortable, seal against the ears better, and seem almost over designed from an industrial perspective. They are built more like the early professional models of the Koss Pro4AA's, a highly respected studio model used four decades ago. The noise cancellation function is not as good as today's standard (Bose), but you won't be lacking much if that is what you use them for. When listening to music there is a huge difference depending on whether the noise cancellation is \\"on\\" or \\"off\\". In MOST cases, musical sound was vastly superior with the noise cancellation \\"off\\", but not always. That caused me more than a little consternation until I reasoned that the type of recording was most likely responsible for favoring one over the other. I also observed differences by switching the connector cords. Connectors have always been a problem for some audio companies, both the connectors themselves and the quality/construction of the actual cords. More than one audio company has submarined themselves by using inferior materials in their cords/connectors.

Overall though, I would have to give the Denon AHGC20's a low mark for sound quality. They do have a better overall tonal quality than the Koss Pro4S's and their sound stage is more balanced, but the bass is overwhelming, resulting in a mushy/boomy sound. This probably has to do with the compression of the recording reducing the dynamic range, resulting in too much sound being compressed into available bandwidth. Perhaps a sound engineer out there could school me better on this premise. So if you are looking for all the features offered by the Denon headphones, you will probably appreciate the advanced technology. But if your main goal is to listen to your favorite music with some of the same products that the professionals use, this isn't your set of phones. If you are given the opportunity, because of the fore-mentioned proclivity for all of us to hear and process musical sound differently, try to visit a local store so that you can comparison shop one model against the other. What sounds terrible to me might hit your sweet spot. Good luck!al is to listen to your favorite music with some of the same products that the professionals use, this isn't your set of phones. product_title: StarTech.com HDMI Over Dual CAT5 / CAT6 Extender with Infrared IR 100ft /30m HDMI Over Ethernet Cable Extender Power Free 1080p
review_headline: It works well, IF your HDMI port supplies enough voltage to the unit
review_body:
Ok, here is the deal with this device. It's a passive device, meaning it does not have a power supply that plugs into it, it uses PoE or power over ethernet, in this case, power over HDMI. This was the feature that was so attractive to me for this device because I do not have utility power at the receiver point in my blu-ray to projector setup. So the transmitter unit relies completely on the power it gets from the HDMI port of your device. IF your device (blu-ray, computer, game system) does not provide sufficient current to the transmitter unit from the HDMI port, it can not stay connected whether you run 28m or 3m of cable. This was the case for me. I would plug the device in and it would flash the display for a moment and then go away. The lights on the StarTech would just blink. I must have re-crimped my CAT 6 connectors 4 or 5 times before I just got frustrated.

I had set up an return authorization with AV House to return the device but decided to give it one last try, so I went over to RadioShack and bought a $20 powered HDMI in line amplifier, key word being powered. This little bugger has a 5VDC/1A power supply that ramps up the power of the HDMI signal and when I plugged that in front of my StarTech transmitter, the signal locked in and I had a very solid transmission that has streamed without lag, skip, or fail to this point.

My advice, would be to buy a powered unit to avoid the hours of frustration I had to deal with, but if you can't supply utitlity power to the receiver end of your extender then this device is a better option. Just be prepared to potentially drop another few bucks on a powered amplifier if your device can't support it.

product_title: Koss The Plug The Plug In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Better than any stock earbuds, but not by much.
review_body:
I had pretty high hopes for these after great success with the Koss SPARKPLUG. I was horrified to see that they had been discontinued. I managed to break the cable inside by the 3.5 mm adapter, so I just wanted a replacement. I figured these would be just as good.

Unfortunately, these earbuds do not have the same high quality as the SPARKPLUG or PATHFINDR, but they were a big step down. The sound quality is a step up from stock earbuds, but that may be due to their superior noise isolation. The foam design works like an earplug and does a great job of blocking outside noise, but the drivers can't deliver the sound to back it up. The bass is too high (not in a good way for you EDM or classic rock people out there), which leaves everything in the midrange pretty muddy. I didn't expect miracles from these, but the PATHFINDR sounds WAY better and I would strongly recommend them over these for the small price jump. product_title: HomeSpot NFC-Enabled Bluetooth Audio Receiver for Sound System
review_headline: Poorly designed audio receiver and highly impractical for daily use
review_body:
DO NOT BUY!

These bluetooth audio receivers are very frustrating to use. I purchased this product based on the seemingly overwhelming amount of positive reviews and so I had no idea about how truly impractical and annoying this audio receiver is to try and use. First red flag I should have noticed is the manufacturer's claim that there MUST be a clear line of sight from audio source to receiver. Anyone with basic common sense can come to the conclusion that this is something that can be quite problematic if there are people walking around or if there are objects in the way. When they say there must be a clear line of sight, they really mean it. If even a thin piece of clothing or fabric disrupts the line of sight for a millisecond, the receiver "freaks" out and starts skipping parts of the song. Sometimes, it even does this odd thing of playing the music at a much higher rate of speed to catch up. It's ridiculous. I tried setting it up in different conditions to try and see if I could improve the consistency and reliability of the sound but even when my iphone was literally inches or a couple feet away, there would still be occasional speed-ups in the song or skips. It's very annoying to use and a very poorly designed product.

product_title: EBL AA AAA Battery / Battery Charger
review_headline: Does not work and play well with others
review_body: I use these batteries 3 at a time in a device that requires frequent recharging.  I just purchased a few, so I did not have enough to always use  these 2800 rated batteries exclusively.  What I found is these batteries do not mix well with other batteries.  Using them alone is probably OK,  but I have had trouble with devices malfunctioning when used at the same time with batteries of a lower rating, such as EBL 2600 and Amazon rechargeable batteries.  Initially I was so puzzled by many malfunctions I nearly threw the devices away.  Fortunately, I noticed that there was a mix of batteries including one or two of the 2800 rating EBLs in the malfunctioning devices.  Mixing other batteries such as Amazon and even Enloop do just fine, but these 2800s do not mix.  They are also very slightly larger in diameter than other AA batteries so in some cases where there were tight tolerances in the battery compartment, I could not use them.  So in spite of the higher power ratings and good reviews, these batteries did not serve my purpose well.  June 17, 2015 Update.  The manufacturer contacted me and offered that I could return the batteries.  A nice gesture.  The bottom line is that the batteries probably work OK and live up to the good reviews when  used together, but have caused malfunctions (at least with my equipment) when mixed with other brands and ratings.

product_title: Samsung WMN1000B Ultra Slim Wall Mount
review_headline: Does NOT Hold Up Long Term!
review_body:
Because it was recommended for my TV, used this to mount a Samsung UN55B8500 which cost around $3700 in early 2010. Today with no warning the TV dropped to the floor. What failed is the part (cable) that mounts to the back of the TV, not the parts that mount to the wall. I installed those to never come off the wall, and they have not. No, one of the cable ends that bolt to the TV came apart. They're supposed to be rated for 110 lbs. My TV weighs 60 lbs., only a little more than 50% of the load rating. The TV is now just 60 lbs. of junk. The cable itself is steel, but the terminations are just plastic, it turns out -- there's no embedded steel reinforcing them -- so it's impossible to see how they can carry their rated load.

product_title: Apple iPod nano 16GB (7th Generation)
review_headline: Apple missed the mark - lacks key functionality
review_body:
I would give this POS 0 stars if possible. I can't believe Apple, one of the largest companies in the world, would push this product to market. The company is so out of touch with its customers and has completely lost its way.

Pros:
1. This generation has a built-in GPS and no longer requires Nike+ shoes (discontinued) and sensors. Obviously this frees up runners up to use whichever brand of shoe they find most comfortable. The GPS is also far more accurate than the old sensors.
2. They've added Bluetooth, enabling users to connect wireless headphones and speakers.

Cons:
1. This nano is longer than the previous generation so it can no longer be worn around the wrist. I can only assume this was done intentionally to encourage sales of the upcoming iWatch.
2. They've removed the built-in clip which was a very convenient and popular feature of the previous generation.
3. The iPod has an FM radio tuner however it does not have an antenna. Your headphones function as the antenna. That's all well and good except that one of the key selling points of the newest gen iPod Nano is the Bluetooth functionality. The iPod cannot connect to the radio unless you use wired headphones. And you can't plug in headphones or anything just to function as an atenna and continue to play over Bluetooth because if anything is plugged into the headphone jack, the iPod defaults to that device for audio output. The output cannot be changed. This is exceptionally annoying if your gym broadcasts the sound of its TVs over FM and you wanted to use wireless headphones.

If you don't care about the size, convenience, or FM functionality when using wireless devices, then this is still a quality mp3 player and the fitness app is nice to have, although it still only works for walking and running.

In my opinion, the target market for this product is people who want to use it while they exercise. I prefer an iPod to a phone because phonesare too big and heavy when I'm running and because I don't want to receive calls while I'm working out. Apple moved away from catering to people using this product for working out with this iteration. I find it somewhat hard to believe that their were many people complaining about the size of the screen on the previous generation for viewing pictures and videos so the larger screen does nothing but make the nano too big to wear on the wrist.

Anyway, I bought the iPod to use with wireless headphones and for the gps running app function. I'm not sure what the alternative or solution is to the problems I have since encountered.

product_title: Thump Blu Xtreme Waterproof Bluetooth Headset (Black)
review_body:
I purchased a Thump Xtreme at a Rock n Roll marathon expo. I previously used the LG LBS-730 but found that the ear plugs on the LG block out all external sound which isn't good when running on the street. I thus bought the Thump Xtreme as it provided a looser fit. I had never heard of Thump so bought them on the basis of trying them at the expo. I've found that when running they tend to "cut out" at times even though my iPhone is only two feet away (the iPhone is in a flipbelt).

I notified the manufacturer (previously qakgear.com) and they said..."We are very sorry you are experiencing this." and "We have included Todd in this email for advice in regards to your clipping issue that is occurring from two feet away from the headphones."

After a month I hadn't heard anything further so I sent:

It's been a month and I haven't received any further emails. The Thump Extreme still suffers from "clipping". I've found that it is usable if the iPhone is on my back (I use a flip belt to do so). Anyways, I believe I either have a defective unit or this is a systemic design flaw.

to which I received this response:

"The Thump Xtreme is a bluetooth headphone.
Bluetooth is a wave between items.
If there is not a clear line of sight between the headset and pairing item clipping can occur.
Clipping will occur more often when you are in the open.
The bluetooth wave needs to bounce off objects to then pair with your headset.
The design flaw is with bluetooth.
It probably works better when it is on your back or arm wrap."

So far I'm living with the "clipping" as I can position the iPhone on my back and not move my head too far forward which seems to break the signal.

Also, the blue/red light is very dim and hard to see in lighted areas. You can hold the on/off button for five seconds and the unit will turn on/off even if you can't see the light change.

The sound quality is good while allowing external sound to be heard (e.g. cars).

review_headline: Turning Orei converter off may make it appear to die.
review_body: I have owned this product for about a week and it seems to be doing what it is supposed to do.  The sound fidelity seems full-bodied with good lows in the bass frequencies.  I have the transformer for this unit plugged into a power strip and when I turned my power strip off the sound did not come back on.  It seemed absolutely dead.  After experimenting, here's what I did to make the sound come back on ;  1) I turned EVERYTHING off. TV, DVD player, and the power strip with the Orei converter. 2) Then I turned on the TV,  turned the amplifier ON and started PLAYING a movie on the DVD even though I couldn't hear any sound. 3) AFTER everything else was on and the Movie was PLAYING, then I turned on the power strip that had the Orei Converter. (Note; the movie must be playing, not just the main menu) 4) There was a "pop" and then my audio was back on. So I guess this unit has to stay on all the time.   I almost gave up on this unit because nothing else I did made the audio come back so I'm passing this info on to everyone.

product_title: APC RBC35 Replacement Battery Cartridge 35
review_headline: Does not hold an adequate charge
review_body:
This battery arrived quickly via ground shipping, and overall appeared to be a genuine APC product (e.g. APC cardboard box, APC labels on the battery, only minor labeling differences between this and the original UPS battery). I plugged it into my APC BR700G and allowed it to charge unloaded for 24 hours; the following evening the display indicated zero minutes of estimated runtime on a 110 watt load. I assumed the UPS firmware needed some calibration period to adjust to the new battery and didn't pay too much attention. After two weeks of use and charging (without power interruptions), the device still indicates zero minutes of runtime and has approximately 15 seconds of runtime after the power is disconnected (under a 110 watt load, the UPS manual claims an approximate 25 minute runtime at this wattage.) After three weeks the device won't allow the computer to fully boot up, as loading the UPS causes it immediately to flip to battery mode (when the mains power is still up and running without issue), and will quickly power off afterward. In short, my computer isn't usable with the UPS connected regardless of what the mains power is doing. So I've unhooked my UPS and will try to find another solution with either a new replacement battery, or an entirely new UPS (since this replacement batteries seem inadequate.)

Pros:
- Genuine APC equipment, in all packaging and appearance
- Recent manufacturing date on the packaging (< 1 year old)

Cons:
- Doesn't hold enough of a charge to boot my computer after 3 weeks of use

In summary: Would not buy again. Additional regret: Having to take the time to send this junk to the local lead acid battery disposal.

product_title: OM/ONE - World's first Levitating Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Beautiful idea, but it fails in practice
review_body:
I ordered the pre-release of the Om/One speaker a couple of months ago. The thing just looked great! Feb. 28, it arrived.

There is no manual included, but there is a card inside the points to a Youtube site and the box has a note that says you can visit the om-audio web site to download a copy of the manual.

Setup is easy. Hold your finger over the top of the speaker and it will power on and attempt to pair a smart phone, PC or other Bluetooth device. Getting the hang of positioning the speaker over the magnetic base took some time, but if you follow the instructions in the downloaded manual, you can do it with just a little patience. Sound quality of good for a mono speaker, not great, but good. The speaker will pair with another Om/One for true stereo. Unlike others who complain about how hard it is to get it to levitate or the sound quality, those are not my issues.

I ran into my first problem when I tried connecting the speaker to the charging base. The speaker will announce when it's low on power (20%), then alert you in 5% increments until it hits zero. The charging cord has flashing LED lights integrated into it that indicate the charging level. The faster the lights move, the lower the charge left in the battery. My problem was that the LEDs would flash for a couple of seconds, then go out without ever starting to charge the battery. I finally figured out that the contacts on the charging base were too close to the surface and did not make contact with the charging points on the speaker. Once I gently raised those, the charging process took off.

I let the battery charge for about three hours, then I ran into my second problem. The flashing LEDs in the charging cord had slowed, then stopped, indicating a full charge. I put my finger over the mic hole on the top of the speaker to power it on and nothing happened. I put the speaker back on the charging base and tried again. The speaker powered on andsynced with my laptop, but as soon as I lifted it off the charging base, it disconnected and shut down. I tried forgetting and re-pairing it with the laptop, but nothing worked. Yes it levitates and that looks really cool, but nothing else happened.

I sent an email to om-audio/sparkart support for help. They contacted me two days later and said the orb is defective and they would ship a replacement. I've had the replacement orb for about a week. It worked the first day. I synced it with my laptop and my smart phone and all seemed well. I used it as a hands free speaker for Skype calls and really enjoyed the usefulness and uniqueness of the product.

I was away for a few days and when I came back yesterday, I put it on the charge base because it wouldn't power up. The charge LEDs flashed as one would expect while the unit charged, but I've not been able to power it up. I wanted to make sure it was fully charged, so it's been on the charge base today for about six hours today. The LEDs on the charge cord have been flashing the whole time. The top of the orb is warm, but it's totally dead.

I sent another email to support describing the problem. It could be the charge base or another issue with the speaker orb, but I asked for a refund if they can't resolve the problem.

This is a great looking product and the concept is cool, but it looks like there are significant kinks with Quality.

product_title: Beyerdynamic iDX 160 iE In-Ear Headphone
review_headline: seems good. I know there have been some issues in ...
review_body: I'm giving these three stars. I was going to be more harsh, but these do have some redeeming qualities. Build quality, so far, seems good. I know there have been some issues in the past, but the manufacturer seems to be standing behind the product there. The design is good, I have no problem unlike others with the cord setup. I like it. That said, I'm not sure about the audio quality here. Bass is clean and the treble is nice, but the mids are pretty muted and overall vocals on many songs seem very recessed. In order to hear lyrics clearly, you have to crank these up and run the risk of hearing damage. After an hour or two of listening, I was perplexed as to why these high end earbuds seemed, at least to me, to have such poor midtone performance, so I popped in some of my old Apple earbuds. In comparison the Apple earbuds have more pronounced vocal performance but they did help me appreciate the more broad quality of the Beyers. The Apple buds lack clarity overall compared to these despite being able to hear vocals better. All this said, I believe that my old Klipsh earbuds sounded better overall. I'm disappointed with the volume and midtone performance on these Beyers.

review_headline: Sound quality is OK; they do stay on your ear
review_body: These really are not \\"in-ear\\" headphones.  They are \\"on-ear\\" headphones because they do not insert into your ear canal and seal in the sound.  They rest in the 'bowl' of your ear and the silicone fin holds them from falling out.  I tried all three sizes they include and the large size worked best for me.  But still, the sound quality/spectrum compared to my current favorite headphones [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Noise Isolating Headphones]] sounded like the music was played into a tin can; the bass was weak and the highs were muted.  Now, if I hold them close to my ear canal so that they cover it, then the bass came alive and the highs were better.  But when you let go, they fall back to the bowl of your ear and the bass and treble goes away again.  These may hold in your ear better than other on-ear headphones because of the silicone fin, but I still think that the in-ear phones I use have much better sound quality, are more isolating, and with the right tips, stay in your ear canal just fine.

product_title: Blue - Waterproof Portable Wireless Bluetooth 3.0 Mini Speaker,Shower,Pool,Car,Handsfree Mic for Apple iphone 4/4S,iPhone5/5S,ipad,ipod,Samsung galaxy
review_body:
Cool concept with one major drawback: the volume of the speakers depends on the volume of your phone. For instance, I have an iPhone and have always complained about the weak volume (even at the highest level) of its speakers. From other reviews, I took a chance on this, what a let down. Yes, the pairing is ridiculously easy but that's about it. The suction cup doesn't stay up no matter what you do, the flap covering the charging port easily pops up if/when the speaker is dropped...too many problems to name. I will still keep it though until I find a better option. The hands free feature is surprisingly good, I was able to understand my 9 yr old son just fine with the water running (kids are pretty hard to understand on a phone regardless). I can live with the suction cup but I can't live with the low volume. This would be an amazing little speaker if it had its own volume control (the volume buttons control your phones volume control only). Save your money and look elsewhere.

UPDATE: the sound is way louder on my son's phone (Nexus 5) than on my iPhone but the level was bearable on my phone once I closed the shower doors. I ordered a different, more expensive waterproof speaker for my iPhone and sadly the same problem. Oh and I forgot to mention, the flap covering the connection has now popped off in the few days I've owned it. I raised my review to three stars only because it sounds better using an android phone. If you have an iPhone, you're screwed cuz their speaker volume sucks!!

UPDATED May 21st - What a piece of junk!! After the initial charge and only 20 - 30 min of playtime max, this speaker will not hold a charge. It died on my son while he was showering so I charged it for approx 6 hrs. He attracts dirt like no other so he took another shower that night...and the speaker died once again within 10-15 min. The last straw for me was when I charged it a full 24hrs and it died within mins! This speaker is supposed to notify you somehow, (be it the red light goes off or another light comes on) yet my son's never did, it was always red when plugged in. Save yourself the grief of returning it and spend a few bucks more on a better quality speaker.ght goes off or another light comes on) yet my son's never did, it was always red when plugged in. product_title: SMSL SA-36A Pro 20WPC TPA3118D2 Digital Amplifier AMP + 24V Power Supply Black
review_body: I bought mine on aliexpress.com. The amp sounded very nice, did not get hot, I was very satisfied with it - for a month. It died today. Never played it loud, never abused it (no short circuit, used the vendor-supplied power supply etc.). Update #1: as it turned out, it's the power supply (adapter) that failed. You may find the amplifier online without a power supply, so you may want to buy it that way and buy a reliable adapter separately. I must mention that the mains power of the vendor-supplied adapter was quite loose, and slid out of the power brick, then gave me an electric shock, as the IEC320 C7 "figure 8 / shotgun" plug does not properly extend to cover the electric connector, the metal can be touched by accident! (I normally unplug all wires, but I did not realise the cable became loose.) Update #2: It's not the power supply - I switched to a laptop power supply rated at 90W, with a 19.5V DC output. The amp ran fine for 2 weeks, but started the same behaviour: the music abruptly cuts off after a few minutes, then returns on its own a minute or so later, then cuts off, comes back... it comes back immediately if you turn the power off (you can hear the music until the internal power supply capacitors are depleted). I'm now playing it with a 6V / 2A 'wall wart' style PSU, and it did not shut down yesterday, and I hear no distortion or clipping. Via the HifiVision forum, SMSL has suggested that I buy a 12V PSU, it should work and perform better than the 6V wall wart, but prevent overheating. They also said Amazon.com seller 'Gemini Doctor' was their authorised dealer. FYI, my speakers are relatively lower impedance, 6 Ohm nominal, 4 Ohm minimal (Q Acoustics 2020i). I'll try with a 12V PSU and update.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_headline: There were two annoying issues with the 650
review_body:
Bought this to upgrade from the Harmony 650. There were two annoying issues with the 650. First, the dogs kept getting in the way of the 650 and the TV so when hitting the "watch TV" button, one device would frequently get out of sync. (DVR, TV, and Bose Speakers) Of course, that meant manually turning on whatever device didn't get the signal. Second, there was always a extra long period after hitting "watch tv" before you could control anything, most especially, the volume. So, for instance, after watching the Walking Dead the night before (and failing to turn down the volume before turning off the system), you would be welcomed to high volume Matt Lauer the next morning, and being locked in for at least 15 seconds. I really don't like to talk about that day....

The Smart Control has solved the two above problems. This is hardly a perfect remote though. The set-up can be frustrating and it is far from intuitive. I thought, mistakenly so, that I could import my 650 settings over and things would be beautiful. Not. They did import over, but there were all sorts of tweaks that needed to be made. Also, I think this remote (and all universal remotes) should have an "input" button. Most people have a TV with multiple inputs and it is nice to be able to change for things like hooking up a laptop or any HDMI device to one of the HDMI inputs. I ended up programming the "E" button as "input." Also, I had issues with using the remote to control my Smart TV (Netflix, Hulu, etc.) - the up and down and side to side buttons kept defaulting to my DVR in "Watch TV" mode. Of course, you want that default when you are watching cable and going through the screens, but not when you are using your Smart TV functions. The solution there was to create a new activity, and they do have a Smart TV activity you can use. So, I will chalk that up to my mistake. Oh - and the fact that you can use your Smartphone as aremote is really not practical. The control screens are terrible. It should only be used in emergencies (like when you can't find the actual remote). Anyway, after 2 hours of tweaks and cursing, I finally got this running correctly. The hub does work fantastic though. My dog interference problems are history.

product_title: New SweetPea3 (v.2.0) 4 GB MP3 Player for Kids (Blue)
review_headline: Disappointed but can make do with 1 playlist
review_body:
Pros: Construction. Simple volume button. Volume limitation is nice. USB interface was OK for transferring to this device.

Cons: This product's functionality is very limited for a pre-k child. Going to a different playlist is not possible for my 3 1/2 y.o. Battery only lasts me a couple hours. Screen menus are not very intuitive. I doubt if even at 4 my kid would be able to use this beyond simply playing one playlist.

In sum, If you want to program this SP3-200 to play what you want in a single playlist that you create, it's OK. If this is your expectation, you will most likely like this device and rate it higher than I did. I guess I was expecting too much and was hoping my kid could go through different playlists to find what he wants. Unless especially gifted or older, a kid won't be able to choose the playlist they want to hear unless you change it for them. I was hoping to avoid a more expensive tablet device, but they are getting cheaper and may be the alternative of choice.

I regret not returning it before the window closed.

product_title: Mpow Cheetah Sport Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Stereo Headset Headphones Earphone Earbuds with AptX,Mic for Running
review_body:
I bought these to replace a set of bluetooth headphones that suddenly stopped charging after a year and a half of use. They weren't sweatproof, and I did use them for working out and running. I'm not sure if that's what killed them or not, but I decided this time around to get something that was sweat proof and ended up buying these.

Sound: I'm disappointed with the sound, the low end really sucks compared to the Alpatronix bluetooth headphones I last had. Overall the sound is just a bit muddy. Hopefully after using them for a while and getting a burn in will help improve the sound a bit, but I am doubtful.

Fit: The fit is good and they are lightweight. They come with extra ear pieces, a small and large set. The medium ones that were on the headset fit me fine.

Connectivity: Paired up easily to my LG Nexus 5. I can go to the bathroom which is next to my room and leave my phone in my room and I'm still connected.

The mediocre sound is really a bummer, I was really looking forward to these headphones. I am going to keep them considering they didn't cost much for a bluetooth headset and I hate using wired headphones when working out and running. But if I had a choice to buy again, I would rather buy another pair of Alpatronix headphones and risk them dying again because they sound so much better.

product_title: Polk Audio Omni SB1 Wireless Sound Bar System
review_headline: Multi-room audio only works from a phone/tablet
review_body:
I bought this device hoping to use it along with two (and probably eventually more) Omni S2 satellite speakers to play music all around my house and for the audio for TV & videos. My music collection is on a Windows PC. So I hoped to connect the TV to the soundbar via the optical connection and the Windows PC via the 3.5mm cable. Internet radio was a tertiary, but useful application. There are several flaws that prevented this from working and I had to return it.

First the sound quality is pretty good, though I'd have to say it didn't knock my socks off, and I think you could find better sound in other hardware at a better price.

2) The multi-room wifi feature ONLY works when you stream audio from an Android or Apple phone or tablet. If you play audio via either the optical or wired connections, it ONLY goes to the soundbar and not to the satellite speakers. So this means that my hope of playing music from my music collection to the Omni S2 speakers was impossible. So much for "whole house", multi-room sound!

3) There is no Windows app to stream music from a PC. The closest thing to that would be setting up a DLNA music server on the PC and playing tunes from it on the Polk phone app. And it HAS to be a DLNA server, not a shared network drive or Amazon music library.

4) So the only way to stream music to all the speakers is from a phone/tablet. And the app is really weak and clumsy. You can read what others have to say about it -- no Spotify, crude controls, crashes, it only does the simplest tasks. And a little side note, if I'm streaming some music from my phone and then go to the grocery store (with my phone), the music stops. A little annoying to my wife. I don't think Sonos does this -- I think it continues playing.
