product_title: Paradigm Shift SoundScape Soundbar(Black)
review_headline: ... months to buy this soundbar after I read the great reviews, especially the superlative review in Wirecutter magazine
review_body:
I had saved for months to buy this soundbar after I read the great reviews, especially the superlative review in Wirecutter magazine. I was so excited when it arrived from Amazon. After unpacking it and reading the directions, I went to plug in my digital optical cable into the Soundscape's port, and the port broke. To this day, I do not know if it arrived broken or broke upon connection, but either way it shouldn't have happened. After all, I have connected optical digital cables dozens of times and never had a problem. I called Paradigm customer support and reached their voicemail and left a message. No one ever called me back. I then left an e-mail with their customer support and again received no response. After a few more days, I called again and reached an unfriendly rep who nastily told me the port is not covered by the warranty. Let's see, I just received this thing, spent $1500 for the privilege, and I was SOL. I then fired off an extremely vitriolic e-mail again. This time I did get a response, an e-mail from a rep named Pietro Ferrari who promised to call me. He did and told me they are investigating this issue. I informed him I had returned the product to Amazon, who by the way was fantastic in quickly refunding my credit card. So apparently this occurrence is more widespread than just me, since I had returned mine to Amazon. He told me they, like Amazon, are out of stock and to order it again from Paradigm when it is in stock again in February. No apology, no offering a discount due to my ordeal, nothing. No, I give up; no way will I order another. I'll stick to my old Klipsch.

Update on 2/21/15: I bought the Yamaha YSP-2500 Sound Projector from Crutchfield and I love it. It has 3 HDMI ports and an optical cable port, sounds fantastic, has Bluetooth, several audio options, and is $500 less than the Paradigm. I am extremely pleased. Thank you, Paradigm.

product_title: Audio-Technica LP60 Turntable
review_headline: Other than being non-functional, what's not to like?
review_body:
Arrived not functional.

Also, I noticed there was no clip around which the tone arm could be secured on the tone arm cradle. This means, during movement, the tone arm flops around back and forth, up and down, exposing the needle and cartridge to damage. Also, it's a good idea to secure the tone arm on the cradle when not in use to prevent an accidental bump by the wrist or something from dislodging the tone arm from the cradle onto the record or the bare turntable, neither of which would be a happy experience. It is, however, a comforting "plus" to have the clear cover, which prevents the build up of dust on the turntable when either playing a disc or when idle. Some turntables do not have a cover, which I regard as a disadvantage.

To be sure I had made the correct assessment, I did move the pre-amp/line switch back and forth several times during our attempts to get the item to function, and tried every line input on the amplifier in both switch positions of the turntable. Then, I substituted another turntable on the amplifier and the substitute turntable worked fine. It was on that basis that I concluded that the item was defective upon arrival. I returned the item because it didn't produce an audio signal.

I gave it two stars because I felt that the quality control of the manufacturer and/or the packaging by the manufacturer could have prevented this failure, regardless of the poor packaging by Amazon. I wasn't too happy with Amazon's packaging, because they didn't put enough bubble wrap stuff around the inside of the outside shipping box so the inside product box wouldn't rattle around inside the outside shipping box.

These ear cushions are ok, at best. They're definitely not as soft, nor as comfortable, nor do they block as much noise. I didn't notice until I just took them off to replace them with official Bose replacements, but these are also considerably smaller. I've attached quick pictures to show the difference.

They might be fine for casual use, but I wear my QC15's ~8+ hours a day (and have for almost 2 years until I needed to replace the ear cushions). These replacementsâ€¦Â they just really aren't that good. I tried them for a week before going to the local Bose store and getting official replacements. I don't really see the point in having QC15s if they feel (and block noise) like a far inferior set of headphones. No reason to spend $300 on headphones only to put super cheap replacements on the main part of the headphones that actually touch your head for hours and hours a day.

Unfortunately, now that the QC25 is out, Bose isn't selling the QC15 replacements anymore. They can't be ordered from their website, and the guy at the store said he couldn't even order more from his system. I'm hoping I can get official replacements in another 2 years.

EDIT: The QC25 replacements work just fine for the QC15, so that's good.

review_headline: one weak link leads to very poor results. Ansmann quality control has slipped badly
review_body:
Ansmann batteries used to be the gold standard. Recent purchase of around 8 4-packs of AA batteries have been extremely disappointing. Note that these have been sets with matte finish, which according to reports may be different/poorer than sets with bright silver finish.

Batteries are used in sets of 4 in an underwater flash (Ikelite DS-51). I used to get 200 flashes from a set of these batteries. The recent sets have managed only 40 flashes or less. The reason is that in each and every set purchased within the last year there have been one or two batteries that are duds. Have had experience with some not charging right out of the package, and others with far below rated capacity. Tested by running a discharge/recharge cycle with LaCrosse charger to measure capacity. If you are relying upon 4 in a flash unit, one weak link leads to very poor results. Ansmann quality control has slipped badly.

review_body: Be VERY careful about buying any Onkyo product. If the products works, you're golden. But if it ever has problems, you are screwed, even if the problem is a defect in manufacturing. I own two Onkyo's and one experienced an HDMI board failure. Just Google "Onkyo HDMI problems" and you will see what I mean. review_body: I ordered the following items: Channel Master CM-4221HD HDTV UHF Antenna, Channel Master CM-7777 Titan 2 Antenna Preamplifier, Channel Master 1805 Super Mast, & a Channel Master CM 9521A Complete Antenna Rotator System. Nothing with thier set-up.  I  purchased this setup to get channels that were further away.  When I hooked up their equipment I got nothing.  Plus I wasted all this money and time on their equipment, and because of the time frame between when I set it up and when I actually moved into my newly constructed house, too much time has passed and I can't return the stuff.  If I were you I would save my money and by a system that actually works.

product_title: EBL 9V 600mAh Li-ion Rechargeable Batteries or 9V Charger or Battery with Charger
review_headline: Seemed like a good idea to try
review_body:
The electronic lock on my Canon residential safe goes through 9v Duracell Alkalines about once every 10 months or so.....so I thought maybe next time I would try one of the new 9v lithium ion batteries. While searching on Amazon...I came across these lithium ion batteries that are RECHARGEABLE. Seemed like a good idea to try. I bought 4 of the rechargeable 9v batteries and the 8 station 9v charger that EBL also markets that is specifically for 9v lithium ion battery.
The BAD NEWS ... A new Duracell will generally read about 9.5 to 9.8 on a digital volt meter. A few minutes after charging in the EBL charger, all of the EBL 9v rechargeable lithium batteries read 8.35 to 8.37 volts. My 10 month old Durecell 9v in my safe reads 9.03 volts. It was still working to open the electronic lock on my Canon Safe....but one could easily tell the old Duracell 9v alkaline was getting weak and needed replacement.
One by one, I tried all four of the EBL rechargeable batteries and NONE OF THEM would operate the electronic lock on my Canon Safe reliably. I did get one open in about 7 tries with one of the batteries.
My guess is that this particular electronic lock is looking for slightly more voltage that the 8.35 volts that the freshly charged EBLs were able to put out.
Rather than go through the hassle of a return ... I will keep the batteries and charger for other less demanding gadgets I have around the house. Maybe the seller might see this review and let me know if/when the company has a 9v battery that really does put out 9 volts. In the mean time...I guess I will try the non-rechargeable 9v lithiums made by a major brand on my safe.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Smart Control with Smartphone
review_body:
I haven't written many reviews but this is the 'strangest' I've attempted thus far, regardless. I want to give this piece of technology five stars. The reason I'm giving it two is because one star indicates that I 'hate' the device and I still don't hate it. When I got it set up, I LOVED it. (I set up via a laptop, not phone.)

It worked flawlessly since March. The past couple of weeks I noticed that the LED had turned red and was staying that color and that the Harmony smart remote would no longer control my ROKU.

Support for this device is 'virtually' non-existent. You get a nice message from William Wong but you don't actually get to talk to a 'real person'. At least, I didn't after being on hold for at least ten minutes. I logged onto the forum for Harmony and found that many people were experiencing this same issue. It went page after page without a 'useful' response from anyone at Harmony.

Someone suggested resetting my Wi-Fi parameters. That ain't happening. Everything else in my house that runs through my WiFi is working flawlessly.

The suspicion, at least from what I could gather from reading (I'm not techie by a long shot) is that Harmony released a firmware update that scrambled the brains' of the hubs out in the world. One reader suggested resetting and re-synching the hub. If you hold the reset button down on the hub while plugging the power back in the LED will blink red rapidly. This is supposed to give you a reset to original default parameters.

You then plug the hub into your laptop (it comes with a USB/Mini connector cable) to reload your devices. All this went well, the hub returned to green, but this lasted for only a day. However, it will eventually find 'green' again and stay that way for a period of time. I've read here that Harmony was having server issues. I encountered that yesterday when I attempted to reset and reload my hub.

It may not be the hubs at issue with regard to the LED status, or it may be a combination of a bad firmware update and faulty servers.

Anyway, take this review for what you will when considering the purchase. If you happen to get one that works, it is a wonderful piece of technology. (I had range issues with my standard remotes that made them operate sporadically, which is infuriating when controlling pause, volume, etc., during a movie.) The Harmony eliminated all that.

I don't like companies that don't offer accessible human support or support to those who sign on to their forums willing to try and fix problems that they shouldn't have to deal with as a result of poor technical upgrades by a company that once had a great product on their hands. A hundred dollars isn't a great deal of money but I'd love to have it back to purchase other things than a paper weight.

Unfortunately the receiver crapped out after a day, with major feedback through all my speakers (Definitive surround). So, I tried changing HDMI cables and upgraded to HDMI 2 - no luck. review_headline: you can do better. The color they sent me is not as ...
review_body:
All in all for the price, you can do better. The color they sent me is not as blue as the picture, it is more of a pinkish purple instead of blue around the edges. The sound on it is so quiet for just me in my little studio apartment. If you are looking for 1 speaker that will suit your needs for a portable speaker, look elsewhere. It would take 2 of these to be decently effective without some tweaking, I used an app to boost the bass and volume a little bit which does help make it useable. But the color, along with the fact that i have to tweak it, and also I noticed when i have an equalizer you can play with setting with this speaker, if you raise the bass the treble fades away, and vice versa. The only way to get the good loudness you need from this speaker is to leave the equalizer on flat, all 0s. And crank it up pretty loud with bass boost enabled.

With all those tweaks you can get quite alot of sound out of it, i have cranked it up to max with all the boosts and still not gotten any real distortion. I have gotten ALOT of vibrations from the resonator, but only on extreme volumes with extreme tracks too. It is very picky about what music it likes to play well too. A virus named Tom soundtrack plays clear, with good bass, and loud. But when i play creed on it, it makes me want to return it. Its just not as capable as i would have hoped. The more layers a track has, the worse the speaker sounds.

review_body:
I already own the LG HBS-730 model and have always used them heavily. When I saw the HBS-900 model I, of course, was attracted to the flat top design to go under my riding jacket and also the Harman Kardon name as far as the sound.

I got the package today. The package was half opened but I didn't really care as long as the unit wasn't damaged. I picked them up and was thrown off by the rigid design LG had went with. The 730's were very flexible as I had previously enjoyed. Bypassing that con, I turned them on and noticed the louder volume response than the 730's. I was okay with that. I paired my phone and turned on my music just I had done previously that day with the 730's. The sound was muffled and very bass heavy (did I buy Beats by Dre?). You could certainly tell the difference when any song with a horn or string instrument piece had a solo. I was reading the instructions to see if there was a extended bass button that had been selected that I had not seen on the headset. To my dismay, there was none.

I was really looking forward to this new model and for the price, seemed like a suitable upgrade. The sound quality is night and day with my older 730 model winning that battle with crisper, "cleaner" sound. Sending them back.

I bought the wife the HBS-800 model at the same time. We'll see how she likes those before I try to "upgrade" again.

review_headline: Just over a year and 3 charges one dead already
review_body: I purchased these on December 18, 2013 and already one is dead. They were used in my Swiffer and rarely need a recharge. In fact they die from self discharge over time more so than actual usage drain. These Amazon batteries in fact do not even hold charge as long as the second generation of Eneloop contrary to the claim. Now just over a year and a month one is dead. I have dozens of Eneloop that get charged with my Lacrosse charger. Never had one go bad and I that's why I buy mostly Eneloop when on sale. These Amazon batteries were on a special offer for 10.99 which was hard to resist. Still not a bad deal if the rest actually hold up a few more years. However from this point on I will be sticking with nothing but brand name. They cost more but they hold charge longer, can handle more charges and have never let me down. Not to mention 70% shelf life over 5 years beats the pants off everything else out there. The newest generation of Enloops will probably still be working long after I'm dead.

product_title: Panasonic RP-BTGS10-A Premium Bluetooth Wireless Water-Resistant Open-Ear Headphones
review_headline: great for music, not for voice
review_body:
Pretty unique approach to headphones.

The bluetooth wireless is great, though not revolutionary. There are plenty of other wireless headphones out there.

What was unique to me was that this set is not supposed to go over your ears or in your eardrums. It goes against your cheekbones and transmits the audio to you by vibrating your cheekbones.

I've always hated people that had headphones and couldn't hear you talking to them (either at work or even my wife). Being able to use headphones and also know when there's an ambulance, or someone talking to you is quite important to me, and that's why I was excited with this new approach.

While these headphones solve that problem, I still find them to fall short. The sounds are a bit muffled. I was expecting sounds more "clear", something like "ambient" sounds. I was able to listen to music, but when playing games on my computer, I wasn't able to understand any chat.

Overall, I think they're ok. While I would use them to listen to music in the gym or walking, I wouldn't necessarily use them if I expected "clear" audio.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Home Control for Control of 8 Home Entertainment and Automation Devices
review_headline: Didn't work as intended. Very disappointing!
review_body:
Unfortunately I could never get it to work properly with all of my devices. I would connect all of my devices to the hub and then sync up one of my TVs in the living room with the surround sound to one button on the remote and the other TV in the living room with the soundbar to another button on the remote. When everything was connected and set up, all of the stored syncs would seem to flip flop and randomly turn on/off whichever device it seemed to feel like or make contact with (at least that's certainly what it felt like). The app on my phone, albeit hard to navigate, could actually turn all of my devices on and off individually. After spending several hours trying to get it right, using both the computer and my cell phone, I finally gave up on it and returned the product. The best experience in all of this was how easy it was for me to return via Amazon.

I really wanted this remote to work as it has a lot of positive reviews and any way to minimize the now 7 remotes I have would've been great. This looked like the best remote option that didn't have a touchscreen. I wanted real physical buttons with no screens. I will probably try Logitech again because the hardware seemed to be built quite solid and they are a big name, but for the time being the software on this device let me down big time.

product_title: Photive CYREN Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built in Speakerphone 8 hour Rechargeable Battery
review_headline: Not as good as it used to be. Shop around.
review_body:
The sound is pretty good once it is connected and playing. However, try and buy an older version if think you really want one.

I bought one a few years ago, and liked it enough that later I decided to get another one for another room in my house. However, they behave differently. The first one would make a simple "pong" sound when turned on and when then connect and work. If you used the direct audio cable it would not bother trying to pair. Makes sense.

The new one has an annoying voice that likes to tell you what it is doing. Loudly. It will announce that it is connecting, and then, as music is playing, interrupt the music to announce it has connected.

If you use the direct audio cable it still tries to connect over Bluetooth, and while music is playing it tells you (loudly) it is trying to connect, and then tells you (loudly) that it can't.

Quite possibly the stupidest design ever. What's frustrating is that it is otherwise a decent speaker.once you get past the brain-dead "helper" software. But you have to deal with that crap every. single. time. you use it.

These speakers, for their price, are fairly impressive, but they are too far from an accurate reproduction that I just couldn't continue listening to them on a daily basis.     The goods:    The sound is very punchy for the size. There is a good amount of bass and mid there to keep people happy. Even the highs are plentiful in my opinion. You'll like them if this is the upper limit of speaker quality you've dealt with.    The appearance (especially without the grill) is very impressive. They look great on a desk and are the perfect size for that duty.    The build quality is as-expected at worse. Everything is tight and you *really* have to look at them to see any imperfections.    The bads:    While the sound is present across the board there are some issues that I couldn't deal with. The lows are there, but a bit muddy for my taste. The mids are also there, but a bit over-emphasized and almost have too much punch. The highs are missing probably half of what's really there, if you don't believe me test them alongside some $150 bookshelf speakers with a few live recordings. Are they  better than most PC speaker setups? Absolutely, but compared to low-mid range bookshelf speakers they just can't compete.    The construction was good, but generally unfinished in comparison to something from JBL or Sony. Admittedly you pay a bit more for competitors bookshelf speakers, but you also get more so the value is about the same.     The placement was just too finicky in my opinion. They sounded awful on-axis, and really smoothed out off-axis so there was no way to make them toe-in to reduce the soundstage. Also, they had to be 6-8\\" from the wall to clean the bass up but keep it present. This was too limiting on a desktop setup that is against the wall as they end up taking up more room than I thought was realistic. If they front-ported these speakers you could back them right up to the wall, though you would lose a bit of bass I don't think that would be a bad move to even things out a bit.    I was going to run a test on frequency response and post it, but decided instead to go with 'why bother?' The sound is what it is, and nobody buying $60 speakers cares about FR. The issues with the sound are so pronounced that there is no need to get scientific.    In all honesty I could have lived with them, but the issues with balance were just too irritating to listen to for 8 hours a day while working. It would have left me wanting to upgrade quickly to balance out the sound. I'm now running these: [[ASIN:B00167340E JBL ES20 High-Performance 3-Way Bookshelf Speakers (Black, Pair)]] in my office and the difference is huge. I'm *very* familiar with these ES20's and while they are about double the Micca price, they are worth that much and more in my opinion.    Overall:    I would suggest these for a few purposes: primarily a way to get a good desktop setup for under $100 including a Lepai LP-2020A+ amp and some amazonbasics speaker wire.     If you're the type of person that thinks your Logitech 2.1 setup is good, you will be floored by these, but I'd caution you that this is merely a stepping stone into better audio.    If you like to upgrade things, don't expect these to last long once you hear some $100-150 bookshelf speakers. They fall flat on their face by comparison.    If you normally listen to better speakers but want something for casual listening every so often I'd probably look elsewhere.wn to about -2db. This takes the emphasis off the mids and levels out the speakers a bit. This is giving me what I feel is the best fill you can get from these speakers after a few hours of trying out different settings. Keep in mind, these settings are in my environment and a very specific positioning, and I'm tuning things to work well with modern recordings. Your results *will* vary.    Why not send these back and get the MB42X with the crossover? I wanted to keep the budget under the price of the Bose Companion II setup while trying to beat it out. With 100ft of wire and the Lepai amplifier, I've done it by $10. The fill and balance on these is leaps and bounds better than the Bose speakers. I have no doubt the crossover version would be better, but I don't think the average user needs to spend the extra to have an acceptable setup. I would rather save that little bit for the next upgrade than spend it on marginal improvements in sound on a cheap system.    All-in-all I'm happy with them for an office setup on the desk for listening while working, but it took a large amount of tuning and tweaking to make them acceptable for my taste. I'm a bit finicky when it comes to balance, and these are inherently out of balance due to their constraints, but with some effort I've found them to be great value for the money. Had I not tuned them so much I probably would have just shipped them back, but I was sure there was something more to get out of these and I'm glad I've gotten that.    These speakers hit a sweet-spot for me. They allow you to complete a setup for under $100 that works very well and is better than anything under $200 that I've heard from pre-built systems. I wouldn't go looking any further unless you want to spend at least $400, at which point you get into some fun and expandable options.

product_title: Philips HTB3525B Bluetooth / NFC, 80W Integrated Sub Surround Base with Blu-ray
review_headline: Good, but could be much better.
review_body:
This device does quite a bit, but I can't say that it does them all equally well. I mainly bought it for music and figured it would be a good way to get rid of a couple other devices since it's an all-in-one. After more than a month of use, here's my extremely long review:

The Surround Base has decent sound. It's loud and bass fans won't have any issues there. There are adjustable and customizable audio settings for the usual bass, mid, and treble, and you can select the type of sound you want: balanced, powerful, clear, warm, personal, etc. My TV has pretty good sound, but there's a clear difference. The Philips is powerful and has more depth. My issue is that when listening to streaming music, no matter which setting or how I adjusted it, the vocals were overpowered by the music. This was not an issue with CDs.

Speaking of CDs, I tried a bunch and the player wasn't able to provide the name of the song, artist, or album for any of them. And these weren't burned or mix CDs or obscure artists. This is puzzling because all that information shows when I play music from a usb drive, and all those songs were copied from CDs. Perhaps someone can let me know if they had a different experience.

Also with disks, you can set the player to play disks automatically when the device is turned on, but it won't play disks automatically when you insert them. You have to go back to the Home screen and select Play disc. In fact, if your TV is off and you insert a CD, you then have to hit Disk Menu to play it. I think makes more sense to automatically play the disk when you insert it, as with most other players. A disk playing every time I turned on the device got really annoying so I disabled that feature.

I compared the blu-ray quality with my Sony BDP-s5100. Visually, I didn't notice a difference, but the enhanced sound was obvious. There was a hint of virtual surround sound. I don't know how it compares to other sound bars and bases, butdon't expect anything near surround sound. The Sony is also a smart blu-ray payer with a lot more apps, but I don't feel like I'm giving up much by switching to the Philips, but only because I have a streaming player with Amazon Prime and all the other apps I use. This Philips comes with Netflix, Pandora, YouTube, Facebook, Twitter, Picasa, Vudu, and Accuweather.

As for the apps, the interface for Pandora looks nicer than most I've seen, but the type is small. I wish, and I wish this of all streaming players, that I was able to select more than one station, not just one or all with Shuffle or Quick Mix. If I have 60 stations, sometimes I'd like to listen to 10 of them, as I do on my computer. I'm guessing it's a Pandora limitation since I haven't seen this feature anywhere else. But I digress, back to the Philips.

I've mainly used Netflix and YouTube and man, they are sloooooow, and this is even with the shortcut buttons on the remote. I compared them with Apple TV, Roku 2 XS, and Amazon Fire TV, and the Philips came last in launch speed and navigation. Also with YouTube, perhaps because it loads slowly, some videos appear low res as first, compared to the other devices. They all load at 720p, but YouTube videos on the other devices are sharp from the start. One cool thing is that if you use Google Chrome as your web browser and you've loaded the Google cast extension, you're able to cast videos to your TV through the Surround Base. The quality is better, and obviously, searching YouTube is a lot quicker when you're able to use a device with a keyboard. You can do this with other players, so I'm glad the Surround Base wasn't lacking there.

As others have mentioned, the lack of Amazon Instant Video is a big negative. The other big drawback for me is lack of a phone app as a remote control. I can't imagine any new device released within the last couple years not having an app. I also wish I could eliminate the unused sources from the display screen on the Surround Base. I use optical and radio, so I wish I didn't need to also scroll through the inputs I don't use like coaxial, auxiliary, ARC, and audio. I know that's how it is on TVs when you need to switch manually, but I would think that this would be more advanced. Switching automatically would be even nicer.

The Surround Base is attractive, so it doesn't look odd or out of place beneath the TV. One of the reasons I got this was that it takes away the need for bookcase or floor speakers and gives a cleaner look.

The bottom line is that if you mainly use the few apps provided with this device and you like booming sound, the Philips Surround Base is all you need. It's great to have the audio options, and even the FM radio is a plus for me. I didn't need to replace my blu-ray player, but for the options the Surround Base provides, and for the fair price I paid, I find it a solid buy. I'm hoping that there's a phone app in the near future.

product_title: Homedics SS-5010 Soundspa Premier Am/Fm Clock Radio
review_body:
I really wish I could give this 4 stars. It's got all I want, but unfortunately it's missing enough beats/thoughts that I just can't.

First I really like this clock, it has AM/FM, Temperature readings, Sound loop, Alarm, even Projection.
I have to say, I would still buy this clock without the projection and the temperature readings.
The sound on the device is good. I recently moved and my room is so quiet that I wake up in the middle of the night on every little noise. I was happy to get this device and found that the sound on it quite nice.
Even though, this item has all I want, unfortunately half of the features doesn't work as intended or as should be.

First, the radio. It doesn't get half the channels that I could on my other AM/FM radio. That's a major thing. The other thing is that the digital display and the frequency the device is getting is not accurate. Example, for FM the display will say 88.9 but the channel is actually 96.5, same issue with AM. If anyone has knowledge of this, please enlighten me. My parents love listening to a few AM stations in my city and I was going to buy an extra one of this item for them if it had worked properly.

Secondly, it's the temperature. I am not sure if it's faulty but I noticed that I get different reads when I put the outdoor reader next to the clock itself. Granted, it's only a two degree difference. I also noticed that at night the clock is reading my room at 81F when it's more like 77F/78F. Very odd.

The manual says my backlight has "High/Low/Off". Yet, the device itself only has High/Low, why? It doesn't quite make sense. There's a projection clock already. I don't need them both on at the same time. Even if it doesn't have a projection time, it would have been wise to allow the user the option to turn off the backlight completely. I mean, when we press the "Snooze/Nap" button it can trigger a 5second backlight.
This backlight issue is my biggest peeve about the item, even at the low level, it's still VERY bright. In the morning it's fine but at night that thing is like a lighthouse. I have to put a shirt over this clock every night in order to fall asleep.
--- Speaking of sleep. Let's face it, homedics, the reason why we buy this item is because we have trouble sleeping, for whatever reason (sound, light, movement.. etc). Maybe not giving us the option to turn backlight off was a bad idea.

Lastly, the projection issue. When I shine it on the ceiling or to a far off wall, I can see a ring around the time. Other than that, I love it. It's a nice little feature to have. It rotates almost 360 Degrees and can tilt 90degrees. There is also a focus ring to give it clarity. I was impressed.
--- I think the ring issue can be fixed by sharpie-ing the plastic ring around the edges so light doesn't shine through as easily. I haven't tried this yet. I will if I decide to keep the device.

Honestly, the backlight is what's giving me a hard time deciding whether I want to keep this item or not. At the time of writing this review, I have owned this item and is using it for about four days now. I think in the end, the deciding factor will be.. Whether or not I want to keep putting a shirt over the item every night, for the rest of the time that I have this clock?

I would have gladly given this item 4stars if the radio worked and backlight could be turned off. I would have decided already to keep this clock if the backlight could be turned off.

A little question for everyone. Is there a similar item anyone can recommend? Something similar with good AM/FM radio, clock, an alarm, and nature sounds.

**UPDATE**
I had to return the item. The light was just too bothersome. I did not want to keep hanging a shirt over it every night just to sleep nor did I want to buy a dark film to cover the screen.
The radio frequency keeps jumping even though thedial isn't touched and the station is playing fine.
Some reviewers said it was hard to press the buttons without the device moving on the desk/counter. Yes, I find this quite annoying. I can't press the buttons with just one hand.
I hope they have an upgraded version later with the fixes.g on the desk/counter. Yes, I find this quite annoying. I can't press the buttons with just one hand. I hope they have an upgraded version later with the fixes.

product_title: Jam Transit Wireless Headphones
review_headline: Amazing headphones at a great price, but with a HUGE drawback.
review_body:
**Update after around 7 months of use on the new set, I decided to change my rating to 2-stars. The new pair started developing a crack in the headband again and also the left speaker emits this high-pitch static noise both when turned on and off. Totally unusable now. These headphones are just not reliable enough for the price. It's a shame because they are lightweight, sound good and have decent battery life. But the headband design and apparently electronic components cripple it. I am going to contact CS again about the issue.

**Update after over a year of use: Headphones continued to perform well, but the headband cracked making it unusable. The headband is a two-piece hard/soft plastic and the hard part is very thin. You must be VERY gentle in pulling apart the earcups when putting on the headphones or a crack will develop and collapse the headband. I was about to buy another, but figured I'd give the company a call to discuss the issue. I was not expecting anything since the headphones were out of warranty, but to my surprise the courteous CS rep said they will just send a new pair! The rep said this is a common problem and actually wanted to know details of how it happened so they can correct it. Needless to say I'm thoroughly impressed with the JAM company. I changed my rating to full 5 stars for excellent customer service, and really just a delicate product that performs superbly if treated right.

Writing this review after using the headphones for a day. Used them at the gym, around the house and outside. Used them on an iPhone 4S for music, Pandora, Youtube and to make a call.

PROs:
- Works flawlessly with the iPhone and have very good range.
- Sound: Bass is simply amazing for headphones such as these but treble is lacking. And you can crank the volume up all the way without distortion even on basshead music. Simply amazing. Overall sound is a bit muddy, but still able to jam real well with them. Stereo performance is excellent with nice spatial separation. An EQ will liven the sound up a bit. iPhone treble boost works best I've found. Sound quality coming from a audiophile is 6/10, but 10/10 for headphones in this class and price.
- Comfortable enough to wear for over an hour without ear fatigue. Haven't tried longer than that but should be good. Headband wont fatigue your head either. Nice positive stops for the headband adjustment. Earcups have plenty of swivel. I've used the headphones while jogging, doing yardwork, woodworking and just general stuff. These are perfect for all of the above (except some gym exercises) and have great isolation from outside noise.
- Nice and light weight with a nice rubberized finish. Simple design with buttons on one side and logo on the opposite. Stainless headband under the plastic looks good and makes me think the headphones won't break from stress.
- Buttons work well with call answer, volume, track skip/search, play/pause, power and pair. Only thing lacking is the ability to use Siri to dial out. A separate call button would fix this, but I understand these headphones main functions are to listen to music and answer a call if it comes in.
- Call quality and speakerphone are top notch. Other party can hear me just fine and I them. Music is paused when call is answered and resumed when complete.
- Battery life seems super long. Been using for over 8 hrs and still going. Simple mini USB style charging port for computer or wall adapter.
- Nice subtle flashing light while connected and not a super bright annoying LED like some of the other made in China gadgets.

CONs:
- Biggest for me is that the earcups swivel forward and backward a bit. When using the flat bench at the gym, the headphones would about fall off when the headband moved backwards. I'm a bald guy so this might be a non issue for those with a full head of hair. A real shame cause I really like these headphones, but just can't usethem on the bench.
- Buttons feel kind of cheap, but I don't expect them to break. They don't look cheap, just feel it.
- The pressure from a good seal of seating the earcups on your ears cause the drivers to crackle. I don't know if this will present an issue down the line, but it's not a good feeling.
- Sound is a bit muddy, but no so much that I'd consider it a CON. Thus my sound review went in the PRO section.
- If you accidentally crush these with some light force, I'd venture to say they're done for. I think they'd survive a drop though.
- Battery is non-replaceable so it'll suck when it just won't hold a charge anymore.

This JAM company got it right with these simple Bluetooth headphones. Just about everything is perfect on them with only a few slightly major cons. I would recommend these, especially over some headphones for double or triple the price.

review_headline: The Jekyll and Hyde of Alarm Clocks
review_body:
Hubris. It will get you every time. I read the reviews here for this diabolical clock, but I thought that surely those who claimed they were unable to program the clock were simply stupid. Iâ€™m not stupid; Iâ€™m really smart. So I ordered the clock in spite of all the negative reviews, blithely assuming that with my Much Larger and Superior Brain I would program the little sucker in a snap. Like I said, hubris. Sheer, dangerous hubris.

It unpacked well, I will say that, and I liked the look of the thing at that point, before I had seen its dark side, I liked the look of it a lot. It has a non-digital display! I have lots of cool old vintage stuff, and the clock fit in pretty well. I plugged it in and found that, yes, you can adjust the light of the display up or down to suit your mood and the ambient lighting of the room (although the light is a very cold white no matter what you do, so its potential as romantic mood lighting is limited to say the least.)

With a smug, self-congratulatory smile I glanced at the instructions so roundly lambasted here as being unintelligible. Unintelligible for the dim-witted, I thought, but surely not so for me, genius that I am.

Meanwhile, while I sat in stunned disbelief trying to make any sense at all out of the instructions, the cute little clockâ€”in full, cheerful Dr. Jekyll modeâ€”spun its charming hands in a whirlâ€”having sought, all on its own, and foundâ€”a radio station broadcasting the correct time. How cool! How nice!

I returned to the instructions, They had clearly been originally written in Mandarin, then translatedâ€”poorlyâ€”into Swahili, then re-translated into Cantonese, then into one of the minor regional dialects of Polish, then into English. That much was obvious. The â€œwhyâ€ of it remains murky, but not as murky as the odd little drawings that accompanied the instructions, containing tiny, blurry illustrations of buttons and labeling that exists nowhere on the actual clock. I picked it up and turned it over and around to be sure. When I put it back down it began playing a radio station that evidently only rotates through music by Megadeath, Meatloaf and Madonna. More on this unholy station later, suffice it to say for now that, being utterly unable to understand the instructions, it took four songs until I managed to turn off the alarm. Or so I thought. Because, as you will see, I had only succeeded in putting it on â€˜snooze.â€

Iâ€™ve seen electronics possessed by the Devil before, as have most of us, Iâ€™m sure. In my personal experience these paranormal events are short-lived, and the wisest course is to pause and walk away. Do something else for a while. Leave the offending item in an unoccupied room. Alone, left to ponder its fate, most sane devises will shrug off the influence of the Evil One and return to a happy state of willing compliance.

Downstairs, I began working on my newest book, tentatively entitled â€œReally Hard Quantum Physics Stuff Explained by a Really Smart Person for Dummies.â€ Itâ€™s just a little project I use to exercise my super-human brain. Suddenly, coming from my bedroom, Meatloaf blared plaintively: â€œTwo out of three ainâ€™t bad.â€

I took the stairs two at a time. The bedroom walls seemed to shimmer from the volume of sound coming out of the little monster. As other reviewers have noted, the sound quality is annoyingly tinny, but it will fill a room.

I fumbled with the clock. The volume control functioned as hoped (although the instructions mislabel the control as â€œMaster Force Object Controlled Buttonâ€) and I got Meatloaf down to an obnoxious drone. Turning it completely off proved more humbling, but I am nothing if not persistent. Persistence, after all, is almost, but not quite, as valuable as highly superior intelligence. After a mere 2.864 hours I had completely mastered the clock. Or so I thoughtâ€¦â€¦..

Another reviewer noted the deeply disturbing experience of having the clock alarm go off randomly, always, however, in the middle of the night. It is interesting to note that fully 96.423% of diabolical hauntings are reported at more-or-less 2:00 AM, local time. So it wasnâ€™t as complete a surprise to me as it might have been to you when I was awakened at 2:12 AM by Madonna. It was â€œlike a Virgin,â€ and it was, very, very loud. This although I had (or so I thought) pre-set 6 of my favorite radio stations, none of them this hideous compilation of schlock as a playlist! I struggled with the fiendish contraption. Megadeath was halfway through â€œHead Crusherâ€ before I succeeded in silencing it.

No one makes sterling decisions at 2:26, which it by that point it was, no one. Not even the super brilliant. I went back to sleep.

It was Meatloaf at 3:47â€”â€œBat Out of Hell.â€ Madonna at 5:07â€”â€œVogue.â€

Setup was as easy as it was my with Onkyo which both have the same Audyssey program built in. In contrast, however, it had me test 7 or so different locations as opposed to 3-4 with my last one.  The menus offer quite a few options that worked well for me. I haven't yet figured out how to turn on audio return. I thought I had it set up right, but today when I tried to play Netflix from the TV no sound came out.  Playing online music from online radio stations and Pandora worked great. I haven't even hooked up the FM antenna and I'm not sure I will very soon because the audio quality is often poor from an antenna. Logging into Pandora was easy, but I don't pay for premium and I know they'll limit how many hours of music I can stream. It's likely that I won't hit the limit on this receiver like I do when listening from my computer just because of how little I'll be playing from the receiver. We'll see.  I was extremely disappointed today to learn that Spotify doesn't work as well as Pandora. My biggest complaint is that it seems like false advertising with a prominent Spotify sticker on the front of the unit advertising support. #1 it only works if you have a premium account. #2 you start it from your cell phone, and then tell Spotify to play to the receiver.  I also tried Bluetooth streaming from a cell phone local music player. That worked fine EXCEPT that the track information was wrong. Instead of showing the album I was playing, it showed an audiobook I have been listening to. That is odd because the audiobook app wasn't running, nor was it playing. For the record, I have a Samsung Galaxy Note 4 running Android.  If I can get audio return to work, I'll upgrade my rating to 4 stars. My experience with Bluetooth and Spotify would cap it below 5 stars though.  Edit: Four months in, the front LED display went out. Denon support was unhelpful and my only option is to pay to ship it to a facility 2 states over. Uh, no thanks.

product_title: Master & Dynamic MH40 Over Ear Headphone - Black
review_headline: All my big-headed brethren, purchase at your own risk...
review_body:
Let me start off by saying that the reason behind the two star rating for a headphone that's been getting mostly favorable reviews online has nothing to do with build quality or the sound. You do get premium materials and you do get a stellar sound.

Of course, I couldn't really analyze the sound profile of these MH40's as they were HIGHLY UNCOMFORTABLE!

First thing you should know...if you feel that you have a huge head, you might want to find another set of headphones. I had to set the rods at the largest setting in order to get them to fit. I'm sure the last thing you wish to do is spend $400 on a set of headphones only to find out they don't even fit.

Secondly is comfort, or lack thereof in my experience. Initially, they had a rather tight clamp going on. If the earpads themselves wouldn't have been so comfortable, I would've given up before I played the first song through them.

A couple of hours later, I started to notice that the tightness was subsiding.....giving way to a fit that wasn't quite as snug or securely mounted to my noggin. Not only that but I started to feel what was firstly just some slight pressure where the middle of the headband was making contact with my head. That "pressure" turned into pain. Granted it wasn't a sharp, intense pain, but at this price range, any level of discomfort is unacceptable.

For those with prominent craniums, tread carefully.

Otherwise, I would recommend these to whoever wanted to go all-out with their portable audio set-up. Sure, they're fairly heavy, but they're built like a brick outhouse, they sound great, with a neutral sound and an ability to put the low end frequencies out there as necessary, and if you have a small enough head for them, they'll be one of the most comfortable headphones you've ever worn.

product_title: SONY sealed inner ear receiver XBA-C10IP / B Black (Japan Import)
review_headline: Little Bass, Uncomfortable. Great Clarity and Separation.
review_body:
A little background on what I listen to. I listen to a pretty wide diversity of music, from Metal and Hard Rock (Slipknot, Van Halen and Foo Fighters), to Pop Rock (Del Amitri, Sting and Matt Nathanson) to Alternative (Talk Talk, et al.), and Blues (Keb' Mo', Buddy Guy, B.B. King, Stevie Ray) to Instrumental (Branford Marsalis, Joe Beck, Bill Frissell, Snarky Puppy) and vocal jazz (Gregory Porter, Melody Gardot, Jane Monheit, Catherine Russel, etc.) and even some orchestral work.

I needed to replace my Klipsch earbuds, and thought I'd try something else. Reviews here and elsewhere on the web were good for these Sony's so I thought I'd give them a try. While the separation and clarity is very good, I had two issues with them.

The first is the lack of bass. I am used to the Klipsch earbuds where they have killer bass. Sure, the Klipsch's lose a little in separation and clarity in comparison to these Sony's. But when I want to rock, or hear that bass sound as a backdrop in jazz, I want it full and resonant. Not the thumping like a nightclub where you only hear the bass, but a full sound of it. These didn't have that. Even when I bumped up the bass on my PowerAmp App, they couldn't give me that. So the clarity and separation are wonderful, and if that is all that matters to you, then go for these. But I like the full gamut of tone.

The second is they were uncomfortable when worn for a long time. I take the train into Chicago everyday in an commute that's over an hour. By the end they were hurting my ears, not because of volume (I don't listen to them loudly), but because of the physical shape. I don't work out with them, so I can't comment on how they work when running or working out. I did return them because of the lack of bass and the comfort issue.

With that put aside, they would be good even as on ear earphones if they weren't designed to hug your head like most over the ear earphones are. If I'm going to spend $170 on headphones, I have to be able to tolerate wearing them longer than a half hour. So, I promptly returned these to Amazon and bought some Audio Technica's ATH-M50x. I've experienced the same intractable problem that others have complained about. Of all things...the Denon loses the the ability to "send" an HDMI signal to the TV. Mind you, I received this on December 11th and used it for less than 4 hours! It didn't last a day. C'mon Denon!
If that wasn't enough I found it doesn't play nice with my Slingbox. It won't relay the signal to the TV if the Slingbox is hooked up between the Denon and cable box. I haven't had this problem with any other brand of receiver I've tried.
I thought both problems might be corrected through some sort of firmware update but how do you update a receiver that's not network capable? I will contact Denon and update this post within the next few days. But for now...I'd give it negative stars for wasting my time.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home [Discontinued by Manufacturer]
review_headline: Works well as universal remote but some disappointments given its cost
review_body: I mostly like the Harmony Ultimate but there are a number of issues that disappoint and detract from its appeal. First, it doesn't seem to be able to turn on my TiVo when I use the "Watch TiVo" activity that I set up. It turns on my TV and my receiver and sets them to the proper inputs but powering on the TiVo itself requires a separate step for no reason that I can understand; the Harmony explicitly states that this is what one must do. Powering off that activity also requires several steps. At this price, they should have found a way to do it all in one step. I also experience a problem getting my receiver to set itself to Dolby Digital for broadcasts, TiVo recordings and movies as well as getting the remote to adjust volume in some of the activities. Using the "Help" options fixes these issues but they don't stay fixed for the next time. Again, at this price, these issues shouldn't occur. Also, the Web site, iPhone and iPad apps don't interact with the Harmony as smoothly as they should. For example, setting up favorite TV stations took several attempts. And when I tried to change the order of my activities on the remote to reflect the frequency with which I used each, setting the most frequent at the top of the list, then the second most frequent, etc., it never got transferred to the remote. These issues aside, the unit appears to be well-made and has allowed me to use just the one remote for my viewing and listening activities instead of 5. That is a big plus. I imagine that with some investigative work on their Web site, I may be able to solve some of my issues but one of the Harmony's big selling points is its ease of set-up and use. It is not as easy as they claim and should be easier at this price point.

review_headline: and I heard a $300 Sony sound bar that sounded almost as good, if not as good
review_body:
We purchased this sound bar from another retailer. We used it for about 3 weeks. One day I was in a different retailer then where I bought the sound bar, and I heard a $300 Sony sound bar that sounded almost as good, if not as good, and had a lot more features (bluetooth, more in depth EQ control, NFC pairing).

The sound left a lot to be desired. I am somewhat of an audiophile; I am not an expert but years of playing different instruments and recording my own music, I have acquired an ear for what a good speaker should sound like. For the price of this sound bar you are getting average sound quality. Mids are great, highs are a little low and not as wide as I expected. The sub has crossover and phase controls, but I could never get it dialed in right; I could never get that smooth bass with just the right amount of punch. I also had the same crackling problems everyone else had with their devices. Whenever my house phone rang, I would get the crackle sound.

Granted, this sound bar is a little bit older so it is lacking some technology. But even for a $600 sound bar from 3 or 4 years ago, it should still have bluetooth 2.1 at the very least. No remote is also a killer for a sound bar of this price.

We ended up taking this back, but we didnt get the Sony sound bar yet. I am holding off and shopping around some more.

review_headline: Poor Customer Support for Defective Product
review_body:
Item arrived tightly folded in a zippered canvas pouch, yet instructions state item should not be stored in it. Pouch is just for protection before and during shipping. Too bad, because it's a nice sturdy pouch.

Problem is, my unit apparently spent a lot of time in this folded state as it sat on their shelves waiting to be shipped. As a result, the screen had deep creases everywhere it was folded (about every 18" vertically and horizontally), as well as several spots that were heavily wrinkled in many directions, similar to what it would look like if it were made of tin foil and someone grabbed a handful of it and then let go.

The instructions say that the creases will go away on their own if you just leave the screen hanging for a few days. Not so! I stretched the screen with bungee cords on the top, bottom and on both sides for over 2 WEEKS and the creases never went away. Then I tried their suggestion for gently warming the back side of the screen with a hair dryer. I even gently rubbed the back of the crease as I was doing so. No luck. The creases are just as sharp as ever.

I then contacted Elite Screens via their online customer support form to ask if they had any other suggestions for removing these very prominent and distracting creases. They had none, so they initiated a warranty claim. At first I thought this was very proactive customer support, but then all attempts thereafter to contact them have been met with utter silence. They won't return any communications, even when an e-mail is sent directly to the person who e-mailed me initially.

This has the potential to be a good product, but ONLY if you get one that hasn't been permanently and irreversibly creased. If that's the case, you are out of luck because Elite Screens won't do anything about it.

review_headline: at best, marginally functional and without a doubt
review_body:
My wife and I own two televisions. One is in our den and the other is in our master bedroom. Both are Samsung 1080p LCD sets. Both sets are hooked to Marantz NR-1403 AV receivers. In the den, we have a Cisco 8742HDC dvr provided by Oceanic cable. The bedroom only had a Cisco cable box that allowed us to play back recordings that were stored on the den dvr hard disk. Time Warner calls this service â€œwhole house dvrâ€. We found this service to be, at best, marginally functional and without a doubt, way overpriced.
I decided to come up with a plan to get rid of the overpriced service, save some money, and actually get more functionality. My plan was simple, or so I thought. My plan was to buy a HDMI splitter to split the cable box's output, sending one output to the den receiver and one output to the bedroom receiver. Add a IR repeater so we could control the den dvr from the bedroom and we now have full dvr functionality in both rooms.
I saw the J-Tech Digital splitter on Amazon. It had good reviews so I purchased it. That is when the nightmares began. First, Amazon shipped the order via Parcel Pool, the gold standard in slow, horrible shippers. The order was so late getting to me, Amazon offered a refund and told me to keep the products if they did finally arrive. The order did arrive days later.
I hooked everything up and was exited to start enjoying the new setup. Unfortunately, it was not meant to be. The picture on the tv would continuously flash on and off. I tried everything to get it to work but had no luck. I called J-Tech for help. They had me try some things but finally decided that the unit was defective. Only problem, since Amazon had already given me a refund, J-Tech did not want to honor the warranty. Apparently, when Amazon gave me my refund, they took the money away from J-Tech.
J-Tech did decide to do the right thing and was nice enough to send me a replacement splitter free of charge. Kudos to them for trying to make the customer happy!
Well, I received the replacement today but unfortunately it does the same thing.
I ended up buying a HDMI Matrix Selector from Radio Shack. It allows me to do the same thing the splitter was supposed to do. It works great! We are now enjoying the use of one dvr in two different rooms. I don't know what the problem is with J-Techs splitter. All I know is it does not work for me.
I would be careful if you decide to purchase this product. It appears it has some kind of compatibility issues. I have two of them now that I'll sell cheap!happy!

product_title: Sanyo NEW 1500 eneloop AA Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries
review_headline: Not so fast on the 'holds a charge' claim
review_body: I got curious about these batteries and how well they held a charge while waiting to be used, so I bought a battery load tester. It's a nice one, even has a little battery in it to put a load on the batteries being tested. The Enelopes, both AA and AAA, drop one bar after charging. They do so rather quickly, and then don't budge for a couple weeks. Then, about a couple weeks later they drop another bar. I've got a AA and AAA sitting to see just how far they drop. I've also got a AA and AAA that went through a complete discharge/recharge cycle on my battery charger. They're a few days behind the other two I'm testing, and read 1 volt higher. I'll report back in a couple weeks. I gave them three stars, and I will reduce further if they continue to discharge. I started getting curious because I'd charge up a pile of batteries, then a couple months later have a week where I'm constantly using my head band flashlight. I noticed the light not starting out as bright with fresh batteries that had been sitting, but on fresh batteries straight out of the charger the light would have that bright powerful 'new battery' oomph to it. I've got alkaline batteries that have been on the shelf for over a year and they test pegged at 1.5 volts. So..... after sitting these might be good for remotes, thermostats, etc, etc.....but, unless you're going to top them off they might not be so good for exactly what rechargeable batteries are good for--- items that blast through the batteries and require juice to get the best results from the item they're used in. There is always the option to top them off if you're not constantly using them. I guess that's fine, but then Panasonic shouldn't make the claims they're making.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home [Discontinued by Manufacturer]
review_headline: PC Setup is Glitchy and Took Forever
review_body:
This is my very first high-end universal remote. Out of the box, it's beautiful. Glossy, sleek and modern. It controls all of your devices via the included \\"harmony hub.\\"

After charging the remote, I set out to download and install the Harmony app, via my iPad 2. I didn't look closely enough at the instructions, because you cannot use an iPad 2, or iPhone 4 (which I also have) to connect the hub to a Wi-Fi network. Setup must be done in those cases through a pc.

This is when the nightmare began. The site gave very little guidance on what to do--I basically had to guess and try things. I could not configure any of my devices through the pc connection. I had to reset the remote and hub three times (15 minutes each), even though I hadn't set anything up yet. It couldn't find my Wi-Fi. I just kept going around in an endless loop of nonsense. Called the customer service number and they were closed for the day. (While this was going on, I received four emails from Logitech, congratulating me on owning such a fine product...)

After about two hours spent on the above, it finally worked, for no discernible reason. I was then able to set up devices through my iPad. Stereo, Wii, and blu-ray player connected easily. Had more trouble with the combined cable/DVR player (would only recognize the DVR player and there was basically no cable functions).

I'm intrigued by the ability to control other devices, such as light switches, shades, thermostats and the like. However, the list of supported devices is very small, and one is not likely to already have these specific models installed. For instance, the Harmony only works with Lutron Serena window shades, and Honeywell Wi-Fi and Nest Learning thermostats.

Overall, I like it, but it shouldn't take an entire afternoon to get it set up.

review_body:
First of all, the hoopla for this speaker completely got me, people rave and rave about how amazing it is, I thought, "wow this has to be some one of a kind artisanal speaker!". It was all very deceiving.

I love Bose, I always have. Bose tends to have a great overall sound, clean, crisp, loud, deep base, the soundlink has all these great qualities.. until you raise the volume to its max level. I upgraded to the SoundLink from a JBL Flip (which I totally loved). I felt I was due for an "upgrade" and did a tiny bit of research (mistake) and felt this one would do it for me. Truth be told, I was super disappointed within 10 minutes of turning it on with full charge. I LOVE bass, love it; the JBL gives a much crisper overall sound without ever distorting, so I assumed the SL would blow the Flip out of the water and it just plain didn't! Song after song it distorted pretty heavily at high volume, mudding the sound completely. While I think this speaker is great to have in a small room, because it does sound great at a mid volume level, I still prefer my JBL... it just didn't live up to its portable "outdoor" friendly sound and not at all to these crazy reviews. For $200 it should deliver a much better sound than a speaker for half its price. I am considering returning it and searching for another Bluetooth speaker instead. IF I decide to keep this one I will most likely just use it around the house and will definitely keep using my Flip for louder/on the go purposes instead.

I suggest you test the sound out in person!

review_headline: I'm warning you: Don't waste your time or money!

Well, there is 6 hours of my life I won't be getting back! Hopefully, I'll get my money back from Amazon.

product_title: Amplified HD Digital Outdoor HDTV Antenna 150 Miles Long Range with Motorized 360 Degree Rotation, UHF/VHF/FM Radio with Infrared Remote Control
review_headline: No such thing as a free lunch, or an ity bity high gain antenna.
review_body:
I will go ahead and list the specifics for this install first, so you can see if the review might be relevant to you.

Distance to channel source: 44Mi NW and 51Mi NE
Elevation change to source: <20 ft for either
Height of antenna: 35ft, unimpeded line of sight
Number of available channels: ~60
Number of received channels: Zero, Ziltch, Zip, Nada, None.

I live in a two story house 40 miles from one large city, and 50 miles from another. The antenna was installed on the roof and there was a good connection from the amplifier to the antenna (good enough to power the motor anyways). There is almost no elevation change from my home to either city, and according to TV Fool there is are no line of sight obstacles.

Given what I saw in the reviews here, this antenna should have received every channel from both cities. After hours of manually adjusting in 2 degree increments, scanning the full range with 2 different tv's, and swapping out every cable with new low loss 75ohm RG-6 I never got a single channel to come in.

I know it's possible, as many of my neighbors houses still have some of the old antennas from before they ran cable to our area (10 years ago or so) and most look to be about two to three times as large as this one. But that was the point, this antenna is supposed to do as well as the big ones.

So, either I got a bunk antenna (not entirely unlikely given the quality of the components), or the other reviews from people who had success at these distances are receiving channels that are transmitted with much much higher wattage than the cities near me.,

product_title: AmazonBasics High Capacity Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteries, 500 cycles -Packaging May Vary
review_headline: Dang, I really did get what I paid for--batteries that don't perform as well as the brand name. Boo!
review_body:
I bought these AAs, which are marked marked as "min. 2400mAh," in October 2014, along with the Opus BT-C2000-charger-set AC 100-240V Battery Charger Tester Analyzer** based on the great reviews, and overall they've performed admirably. Of course, these were my first high-capacity batteries, and it was quite refreshing to go up to three weeks between battery changes in my Harmony remote and seemingly indefinite periods in my mouse and bluetooth keyboard.

However, unless my Opus BT-C2000 is lying to me, the batteries, are already losing capacity, even though none of them have gone through more than half a dozen cycles. I started them off with a few refresh cycles, after which they read between 2500 and 2700mAh. None have had more than half a dozen cycles, I set the current at no more than 500, and I only charge when they're completely run down. However, over the past month or so I've noticed their capacity, even after a refresh cycle, has fallen to between 2100 and 2300mAh. I've tried running sequential refresh cycles, and then tried discharge and charge cycles in case the refresh cycles weren't discharging them fully enough, and can't get them back to 2400mAh. In contrast, my year-old Eneloop AAs still test well above their 1900mAh rating. Unless there's some reason that the Amazon Basics batteries will stop losing capacity, I'd expect these batteries to degrade below my 1900mAh Eneloops within a few dozen more cycles. And that's pretty shocking, given how highly these have been rated by some very knowledgeable reviewers (who I still have a lot of respect for, by the way!).

Of course, I'd welcome any comments that would give me reason to hope for a better result, I have to say I'm disappointed. ** I love the Opus BT-C2000 charger--it does what it says it'll do, and gives me a ton of control along with easily digestible information about battery performance. review_body: The PCAU48BT seems like a very functional design with front line input, USB, SD, and BT inputs, rear stereo line inputs and stereo speaker outputs, panel input controls, front headphone output, gain control, two tone controls, and remote control.  I purchased it for a bedroom audio system, in particular to connect to a TV for amplified audio, and to connect to a smartphone by BT to play internet podcasts and radio stations, and music files on SD cards.    Seconds after I plugged it in with speakers attached and a line input from a radio it made a loud POP and gave off an acrid smell, probably a capacitor.  The amplifier functioned for a short while, and I had time to connect to it on my phone by BT, but not long after it started oscillating with a loud \\"wub, wub, wub, wub, wub, wub\\" sound, the VU light bars were going crazy, and no controls worked.  I was disappointed because I have another model Pyle (without BT) connected to a computer that has been faultless for years.    The PCAU48BT model was out of stock on Amazon and at the manufacturer at the time so I returned the fried unit for a gift credit, thanks Amazon.  Recently I ordered the Grace GDI-BTAR513 as replacement, which has BT and remote control except no SD or USB.  Had the Pyle instead failed outside of the Amazon return period, I would have had to spend $20 to have it repaired at the Pyle factory, shame on you Pyle.    I may wait several months for the PCAU48BT to be back in stock. Maybe the manufacturer will discover the problem with the design or issue a new BT model.  Or I may buy the PCAU46A and a separate BT receiver to connect to the aux input.  I will buy the Square Trade insurance if it is available.

USB ports were conceived and designed for just this application.  If you are a geek, you could disassemble this and build up an epoxy shoulder to reinforce the the pitifully fragile two little solder points on the circuit board being asked to secure this connector. That must be connected HUNDREDS of times just during the warranty period. This would cost a few cents during manufacture, and save the company,(and Jaimee) so much time and untold costs. The great reviews are for the operation of new,WORKING units. It IS a great value. Most of these will end up in the trash the first year. Such a waste of resources and money. This is so fixable. product_title: Bluetooth Speaker, DKnight Magicbox Ultra-Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker Powerful Sound with build in Microphone, Works for Cellphone
review_headline: A $15 Dollar Speaker at a $30 Dollar Price Point
review_body:
This speaker would be worth it if the price were halved. Why?

1. The sound quality is around that of low-tier capsule speakers
2. The buttons only work sometimes
3. There is a persistent hiss that scales with volume so you always hear it
4. It feels like holding a toy instead of a piece of audio equipment (an admittedly nitpicky flaw)

I showed these to my friends a while back and they were convinced I just got "a bad one" but after listening to one I found at a store, I know that it is in fact, every Magicbox that sounds this bad.

The only reason someone should buy this over a better $30 speaker is that it resembles the old Jambox. But anyone who cares enough to know what a Jambox is will immediately know it's not one (and a lot worse than one) when you start playing music.

Instead of this, I would recommend buying a Phillips Soundshooter or an Oontz Curve which are some of the best portable Bluetooth speakers at this price range. Although if you care about sound quality I would highly recommend looking for portable speakers at a higher price range.

product_title: HD Frequency Cable Cutter Aerowave, Indoor Outdoor HD Digital TV Antenna (CC-17A)
review_headline: Brings in some stations, but needs a base to fit on a windowsill
review_body:
I bought this almost six months ago to replace a $15 Radio Shack antenna. It got the same channels (it might have got one more, but so many OTA channels are foreign-language or shopping channels that I don't remember). However, it was more solid on one network channel that's in a bad direction for me, so I was happy with it.

I live in an apartment building. The only place I can put it that gets a signal is right in my window. As others have noted, the hook that comes with it does not work to hold it up in a window. In my apartment building, it also doesn't work to lean it against the window, because the vibrations from people walking by (or walking on the floor above me) make it bang against the window, causing too much noise.

This company needs to make a stand for this. As you can see from the image, it has a metal "leg" that would attach to a pole if you used it outside. I haven't found anything that will make it stand up straight on a windowsill (the best I could manage was standing it in a tall mug and wrapping washcloths around it to try to make it stand straight).

It's back to the $15 Radio Shack antenna for me, since that at least is flat and will sit on a windowsill without falling over all the time.

review_headline: Great Sound But an Unacceptable App
review_body: I did a considerable amount of research before I purchased two Polk Omni S2 speakers.  I was aware that the Polk iPad/iPhone app was missing some features, such as Spotify integration.  I purchased them when they were on sale for $50 off per speaker.  For the size of the speakers they sounded great!!  However, these are Wi-Fi speakers and the functionality of the speakers is TOTALLY dependent upon the app.  First there is NO app for the Mac.  You have to use a media server such as Plex.  The iPad/iPhone app is poorly designed, lacks functionality, is unreliable and the interface is amateurish at best.  It does not integrate with the TuneIn radio app.  The included radio functionality is not the least bit user-friendly and would constantly drop the connection.  I could only get the Polk app on my iPhone/iPad to recognize the Plex media server on my Mac once even though other Plex clients could find it immediately from the same location in the house.  After a month frustration I returned the speakers.  I exchanged the Polk Omni S2 speakers for the Sonos Play:1 speakers.  The Play:1s sound great and more importantly the app the light-years ahead of the Polk app.  The Sonos app is easy to use, has rock-solid reliability and there is an app for the Mac that acts as an audio media server.  Sonos fully understands that Wi-Fi speakers are all about the app. Polk does not.

product_title: Bose SoundTrue In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: I'm going to tell you a secret...
review_body: I was so excited to get and try these headphones. I've owned many different earbuds over my lifetime, and after my most recent broke, I decided to splurge and get something "better" since headphones are something I use almost everyday. I usually stay in the $10-$25 range as you get the best value for those before stepping up to the ones in the $100 and up range. My current pair was extremely uncomfortable so I was dying to change and this pair really stood out to me due to it's reputation and reviews. The anticipation was killing me as I opened the box, and it took a minute to figure out how to even put these in my ear. The fit was not very secure and they dislodge easily, but they were comfortable nonetheless. The problem was the sound. The first thought I had was, "Have I gone deaf?" The quality was OK, nothing special, but I noticed quickly that I couldn't hear anything. I changed the eartips thinking I could get more isolation, but the improvement was marginal. Even when I dialed up the volume to the dangerous side, I still had a hard time hearing. I couldn't hear the words being sung or the words being said in commercial breaks. I was completely and utterly shocked when I realized that, no, this was not a defective pair. I went into the gym and the volume/isolation became exaggerated. Never before had I heard the environment around me so loud and clear. I could barely hear the music but instead heard the sounds of the background noise at the gym. I tried turning up the volume but that didn't really help. The words were faint and the base was not crisp. I was quite miserable for the next hour during my workout.  I did some research and bought the stayhear plus tips that they use for the quietcomfort earbuds. I noticed immediately that while there was more noise isolation, the sound quality plummeted to the point where these sounded like cheap headphones. I even compared them to another pair of earbuds that I had that are priced at $30. The $30 pair actually sounded BETTER. So, while the sound quality of the Bose actually is quite superior, it is not the actual product itself, but a result of the product design. Something about noise isolation and using earbuds decreases sound quality.   So while these headphones have such good ratings, it is merely a mirage. I just saw a review saying exactly what I'm describing about low volume (even that person used them at the gym) and I cannot agree with it more. You basically can't use these unless you're in a quiet room, and they are not good when any movement is required. The cord is also pretty short. I would never have expected $100 Bose headphones to be this flawed. I've started to learn that brand name audio accessories almost never live up to their price and that products 5x cheaper are often BETTER. I am just shocked. I really want to keep them, but I think it will be a horrible decision that I will leave me miserable whenever I use them. I don't think I have any choice but to return them.
