product_title: Phorus Speaker with Play-Fi Multi-Room Wireless Audio Streaming
review_headline: Wireless is poorly implemented, serious incompatible with Cisco Wireless (corporate APs)
review_body:
I've been putting off reviewing this since Christmas when I bought it direct from Phorus.

Soundwise, the speaker is good. I find sound quality to be very subjective. I don't think the bass is a deep and vibrant as on others. However, it is all the other technology that I was most interested in and this is where I see the product simply failing.

For setup, You can only perform setup wirelessly on the 2.4Ghz band with a Windows, Android or iOS device. I had turned off 2.4Ghz on my Windows PC because I was only interested in using the better performing 5Ghz band at my house. This was a stumbling block.

Pretty much every time I attached to the speaker with iTunes I got a dropout within the first song of a few seconds. It was like a guaranteed hiccup. The speaker constantly associated on the 2.4ghz band which always has greater levels of interference. Only when I shut down my 2.4Ghz radio, would it finally move to 5Ghz--where every other device in the house already was. I was able to get it to play from iTunes, but iTunes would loose the ability to control the volume. Only a reboot of the Phorus would get it back. This became a common theme. Reboots solve all issues temporarily.

This week I brought it to work as a device for testing. I associated it to a MAC filtered WLAN with no other security. Associating with the Cisco APs (3502, 1142) takes too long (15-35 seconds) and if it re-authenticates the Phorus disappears for 15-30 seconds or forever. Sometimes the wireless light goes solid, but it isn't associated to the Wireless network it is supposed to be. Pull the power plug and restart. Without a doubt , working with Cisco APs, which is typical in corporations, this box works inconsistently. Corporate authentications schemes vary, and they often require you to periodically re-join to ensure you are still allowed on. Phorus can't handles such a world. A few hours of troubleshooting and the Phorus clearly has problems that all the other test devices don't.

This is very disappointing. Dual-band wireless, and specifically 5Ghz, is where all speed & performance development is focusing on in the world of wireless. 2.4ghz was crowded years ago and only getting worse. Everything interferes with 2.4ghz (your bluetooth devices, your microwave oven, your DECT/DSS cordless phones that SAY they don't interfere, motion detectors, fan motors). Yet this device relies and prefers 2.4 over 5ghz. I'm sitting here with an AP and the Phorus within 5 feet of eachother. A few minutes ago it gave up on 5Ghz and just switched to 2.4Ghz for no reason. Now it is continually blinking. It appears this wireless is DEEPLY incompatible with Cisco APs. Wireless is a bit too mature for such catastrophic failures in compatibility.

I don't have any android or iOS devices at home, so I don't have a lot of experience there. I recall the marketing talkign about how when Pandora is playing to the Phorus, the other sounds from your phone won't route through the Phorus (like the phone ringing, etc). On the Windows DTS Play-Fi application, there is no such finesse. It routes all of windows sounds to the speakers, every ding, bing, and buzz.

When Airplaying from iTunes it isolates iTunes, which is good.

As new firmware comes out I'll add more to the review. I bought this just as the PS-5 was announced. As far as I'm concerned I don't think there is a reasonable dual-band wireless speaker in the market yet. I like the Play-Fi idea, but the wireless implementation or chipset is not very good. Maybe they only test with Linksys, Dlink and Netgear home routers.

product_title: Status Audio HD One Headphones - Noise isolating. Matte finish. Foldable. 2 cables. Mic.
review_headline: Not for people with large heads.  3.5 Stars.
review_body:
The HD One headphones have a lot going for them. I was ready to sing praise before I even received them. Aside from the headphones, the box comes with two auxiliary cables (one long, another short), and a carrying pouch. One huge plus is that the cables are detachable, so you needn't worry about replacing the entire headset or trying to figure out one of those DIY fixes when the cable goes bad. More companies should take after this.

The design on these is quite nice. Similar in looks to the Beats Solo, the HD One folds up to the size of an average fist with a small knuckleduster. That combined with the matte material and aforementioned pouch makes these conveniently portable.

As for sound, these little guys provide some solid results, despite being on-ear headphones for a reasonable $50. There's a punchy, bass-driven sound, but they don't drown the highs out like Beats. The mids are realized quite nicely too, so if you're like me and you enjoy music with a meaty sound, these will suffice on a budget.

So why 3 stars? Well, for someone like me with an above average head size, these headphones are puny. Each side only extends four clicks, which makes them look and feel diminutive. They barely cover my head and ears, which is amplified by the inherent tightness of most on-ear headphones. As a result, my ears feel cramped after a few minutes of use, which makes listening difficult to enjoy.

Status Audio have potential, I only hope they offer more products that can accommodate people like myself who need audio products that are more comfortable and flexible. If they make a feasible alternative to the Sony XB-500s, for instance, I want to be the first person notified. For the moment, however, the HD One is all they have, and while I want to like these, they're simply too much of a strain on my ears to give a full recommendation. If it weren't for that, I'd have given these 4 stars. What tipped it down to a 3, however, was the included cord (the small one anyway). Within a day of casual use it already began breaking up the audio when I simply nudged my phone to the side. product_title: Monstercube Music Bomb Bluetooth Speakers
review_body:
12/2014 - 4* Rating
Very surprised on the quality and sound. I used to own a Philips grenade looking Bluetooth speaker about a year ago and this thing blows it out of the water! Big time! It even has some weight to it which makes you confirm it's better quality.
The reason I give it 4/5 stars is because I don't believe it's waterproof at all...neither packaging, instructions or speaker itself mention anything about it being waterproof. Also the section where the carabiner goes is the same silicone that surrounds the speaker and when you turn on the speaker a voice prompts you searching for Bluetooth and for some reason I don't know how it happened but the language on the device was changed and went from English to Chinese... I don't know how I fixed it but I was able to place it back into English mode. There are no instructions to how to switch languages either.
If you're a person like me that doesn't care about brands name products as long is it works the way they should...then buy this...you won't be disappointed. All in all, it's a great buy.

---UPDATE 3/11/2015- 2* Rating---
What I originally posted about the sound is still good, rumbles sometimes but that's just do to high volumes just like any other speaker at it's peak. BUT...the Bluetooth...WOW...SO BAD!!! I'm 5 feet away from this and it's cutting out...I can be sitting right next to it and...YUP, STILL CUTS OUT!!! SUPER ANNOYING AND EMBARRASING!

review_headline: 5 star review downgraded to 1 star after 2 years
review_body:
UPDATE April 2017:
2 years in light use and the FM receiver has crapped out - strong local signal comes in and out on the station I leave it tuned to.

Sorry A/V enthusiasts, this review won't be much use to you.
I bought this Yamaha RX-V379 strictly for listening to the music on my Samsung Galaxie 4 via bluetooth in the living room. I wanted good sound but a simple interface without too much gobbledy gook to mess with. I have some decent bluetooth speakers but wanted stereo separation and this unit (in my limited research) represents the lowest cost, quality option to get me there.
I'm running with a pair of late 80's Polk Audio bookshelf speakers, and 2002 or so rear surrounds and subwoofer by Cambridge Audio. Sounds great to our ears and my Wife and I are very pleased.
This receiver is exactly what I wanted. I like the simple remote and the quickly accessible setup levels for speaker setup etc. The SCENE functions look very handy as well and I will delve into those tomorrow.

product_title: ITIS Replacement Inline Remote and Microphone Audio Cable Cord For Bose QuietComfort 15 QC15 Headphone With IT IS Logo Headphone Cable Cord Clip
review_headline: Works Perfectly (with a trivial issue) BUT Annoying Emails from Vendor
review_body:
After spending $300 for Bose Quiet Comfort 15 headphones some years back I found out my model has been discontinued. Discontinued as well was the headphone/iPhone accessory by Bose leaving no legitimate option for millions of 15 owners???. So, this item looked like a good replacement and I could always return it.

I received the package promptly by US Mail, and it looked and felt exactly as my original headphone cord in every way (and was even labeled Bose). The first thing I noticed was the silver retaining clip was pushed into its opening and did not spring out to hold the cord tightly to the headphones like it is supposed to (minus one star) but yet the fit was perfect and no way will the assembly ever fall out since it plugs into the headphones firmly and it's a tight fit. Rather than dealing with sending it back for a hidden non-functional trivial issue I decided to keep it.

In all my testing the first day, everything works perfectly (e.g. the microphone, audio, volume, phone calls, etc.) And you would never know this is a knockoff because it is EXACTLY like the original, so close I thought this might be a discontinued leftover vs. a knock-off. I'm crossing my fingers on trouble-free continued use.

But, "It Is" has been barraging me with emails, FIVE the day before yesterday, THREE last night, asking me to write a good review (for a 50% promo discount on the second batch of emails). Of course it's all in broken English with grammar and typos? everywhere. For these annoying emails (one reminder to review would have been fine) I subtract a star (and if I get any more today, this will go down to one star).

review_headline: Beware!.....The Quality of the Headphone Jack & Wire Have Declined!
review_body: I have purchased 5-6 sets of this particular product, over a period covering a number of years, and here's my experience with them.... I listen to audiobooks off and on throughout the day, everyday. In the past, with reasonable care I could expect them to work effectively for 6-8 months, then without fail, one side or the other would stop working. As soon as I receive a new set, I immediately wrap the area where the wire joins the headphone jack with several layers of Gorilla brand duct tape, so I guess the old adage about duct tape being good for about everything is true! This area seems to be the major point of failure for ALL headphones. It's simple physics, if you walk around with them on, like I do, for hours at a time, the swinging action caused by the motion of walking creates stress on the wire as it moves with your body, and the wire eventually breaks in half...Always...Every time...In reality, I expect this to eventually happen, and in fact, I have resigned myself to accept it as a cost of using this product to the extent in which I do. In, the past, this particular set of headphone lasted longer, and the sound quality was far superior to all others, which I have tried in the past at their price point. Unfortunately, this no longer seems to be the case. The last two sets only lasted me a couple of weeks, then they too went mono on me. Out of curiosity, I dissected the last pair that failed so early with an Exacto Knife, and much to my dismay, I discovered that the quality of the wire, and that of the jack itself has wquite obviously taken a nosedive! So, where I once championed this product as being the best headphone value for about $20 no longer holds true, which is a shame. So my search begins again. I'm looking into sports models, which have recently come down in price. I just hope the quality hasn't on them as well......P.S. I gave them an extra star, because the sound quality is still outstanding........

review_headline: Cheap bluetooth gadget for the car that works but there may be better out there

The interface is a bit clumsy also, there are no raised buttons but you have to swipe the screen at the top and then it lights up - typically this will inadvertently play or pause.

- Mostly good audio
- Battery life appears to be pretty good

Cons:
- Cannot charge the device and listen at the same time - there is a lot of interference when plugged in

product_title: Grace Digital 100-Watt Digital Integrated Stereo Amplifier
review_body:
Had this for about a day and a half, the night between days was used to "burn-in" the amp by simply playing low volume streaming audio all night.

Pros:

Very nice form factor.
Well built.
Binding posts are tiny but sturdy.
Sound is acceptable but not great.
AptX quality was nearly as good as line in with just a bit more noise.
Pretty lights.

Cons:

Sound quality lacks clarity, just doesn't sound "open."
Bass/Treble buttons were reversed on the unit but fine on the remote.
Turned off a few times by itself, even when under no load.
Power supply is terrible, noticeable buzzing, just very very low quality.
Remote is merely adequate. Maybe not a Con at this price as it DID work.

Details:

The sound quality is compared to both my Onkyo TX-NR1009 and old but great Pioneer VSX-505S with JBL Studio Series S312BE and S38, and Pioneer SP-FS51-LR and SP-BS41-LR, as well as my Pioneer Elite X-Z9 as a general reference.

Sensitivities are almost the same between speakers but the JBL's are a more mellow speaker, JBL's being 8ohm and the Pioneer's being 6ohm. The JBL's sounded good, but not great. Both receivers were noticeably more full sounding. Switching to the Pioneer speakers, this amp sounded like a muffled version of the JBL's, not the airy crystal clear audio I've come to expect from them from either receiver. The X-Z9 was not easily discernible as being better than the SP speakers on either receiver, however the tower speakers had a more rounded sound due to the lower extension inherent to them. The XZ-9 simply trounced the Grace Digital when side by side with either pair of SP's. I wasn't easily able to do side by side testing with the JBL speakers due to size and placement.

To put this mess into perspective, I have two 5.1 surround systems with Monoprice 8" 2-way kevlar in-ceiling speakers (4104, 4929) and Onkyo TX-SR606's,and they both sound noticeably clearer. Not exactly a high end setup, but you'd be surprised! ;)

This amp does have enough power to get any single pair going at a pretty good volume, so no issues there.

The treble buttons controlling bass and bass controlling volume speaks, well, VOLUME's to the lack of quality control on this product in my opinion. These are obviously cheaply made, even if it's with pretty decent bits. I didn't expect perfection at this price point, but the basic functions working as intended would have been nice. At least the remote controlled everything correctly.

The power supply was just a disaster. It buzz's a great deal, loud enough to hear with no audio output and it located on the floor a good 10 feet or so away from my listening position. It's light, very definitely the cheapest thing they could come up with. I would not trust it to provide reliable power, let alone for a long period of time.

I didn't get this for the BT function, but I did try it out. AptX worked great, this is the first BT device I've had that supports it and the sound is so far superior to the normal BT audio profile, it's ridiculous. That said, the line-in still made a noticable improvement, I think mostly because the noise floor was lower.

There was no buzz via BT or line-in like some others have had, but there is indeed a faint hiss with no source connected, or playing, or with the volume turned all the way down. This isn't really a negative as it wasn't even remotely noticeable when actually playing music. Maybe classical at very low volume would be a problem, but I didn't get that into it since the normal stuff I listen to just wasn't that great. Electronica, POP, Country, Rock, Metal, tried a bunch of stuff on it.

The reason I sent it back, the power supply and the fact that it randomly turned itself off. That's just not acceptable for any product. I don't believe it was a defective unit in that regard either. It never got even warm to the touch.

I used my Moto X (Gen1) and SGIII as well as my Fiio E17 as line inputs. I also used the Graces line-out to chain to the VSX-505S for direct comparison between the Pioneer speakers, as well as the stand-alone tests. The attached picture was my first use, just making sure it worked, before I started moving things around.

product_title: ViewHD Video Converter
review_headline: A necessary idea, but a bad product
review_body:
The product did NOT meet my expectations. I wanted it not only to display whatever is on the portable's screen, but to capture it with a video capture card. But the picture is too blurry, because, I believe, whereas the device does convert the screen signal to video (PAL or NTSC), it only captures one of the fields (upper or lower) at a time. That is, instead of 576 lines of vertical resolution it should have in PAL, I believe it has 288. Instead of 480 in NTSC, it has 240. If you capture a video with Final Cut Pro (or iMovie?) and look at the two consecutive fields of a frame, you'll see that the upper and lower fields are the same. The device just repeats the field, so interlacing the two consecutive fields, instead of combining two images, amounts at deinterlacing the frame by duplicating each horizontal line, which results in blurriness. I don't know about vertical resolution.

So, this gizmo has limited utility. For the price, it could do much better. It's a pity, because devices like these, even in the upcoming (?) age of 4k, are still needed.

product_title: Generic Digital Indoor Outdoor Wireless Weather Station with 3 Sensors
review_headline: Buy an Ambient WS-10 System Instead
review_body:
Sadly, I cannot find anything good to say about this product, and I have many years of experience with similar products from Accurite and others.

I ordered this because I had 6 points around my very large home that I wanted to monitor and my older systems were beginning to fail, one from Radio Shack with 3 remotes and one from Accurite with 3 remotes. I ordered this one to get three of the 6 I needed and the Ambient WS-10 system with three remotes. The Ambient WS-10 is a far superior product. Everything worked fine right out of the box. This "Generic" system is another story. I should have paid attention to the "Generic" in the product name/title/description. It did not register at the time as meaning exactly that. I took it as a brand name.

When it arrived in an Amazon box, I opened the box and the box inside containing the product was truly "generic"; Plain white, no name, no product/item number, nada. Inside I found one small sheet of instructions, again with no one claiming ownership; no manufacturer's name, no product number.

So I installed batteries in the remotes and the display unit and set the remote numbers to 1, 2, and 3 with the switch in the battery compartment and pushed a button beside the unit switch to switch the display to degrees F.

The remotes linked up with the display OK, in a short time. But after I cycled through reading them remotely using the "channel" button on the unit, several times, the change channel displayed stopped functioning. I had to remove and reinsert the batteries in the display unit to get the change channel function woking again, and shortly it failed again. In the process, I discovered that when one removes the batteries of the display unit, even for just a few seconds, it loses all of it settings, which are a pain to set up all over again, like the day, date, time, and any of the many other settings you might be using such as various alarms, etc.

Then I discovered that even if I didn't have these problems, the system is basically worthless to most of us here in the U.S. who think in degrees F, not degrees C. Because while you have the option to select whether the temperature reading displayed on the face of each remote is in degrees C or F, oddly enough, THERE IS NO SUCH OPTION FOR THE MAIN DISPLAY UNIT. Either you learn to think in degrees C, or you are up the creek trying to navigate with a unit of measure that your brain is not calibrated for. I'm not against degrees C or the metric system, and I think the sooner the U.S. makes both official here, to get in sync with the rest of the world, but until that happens, I need this system to give me a degrees F option, thank you very much!

Another feature problem is that this is advertised as a Weather Station. Sorry, but it's really just a remote thermometer and hygrometer system. But with that billing, 70% of the face of the main station display is devoted to extraneous data like the date, time, day of the week, pictures of clouds, etc. This leaves so little room for the portion of the screen actually displaying temperature and humidity readings, that they are hard to see from any distance. And they are not very bright, so one must go to the unit, and press the "Light" button.

Meanwhile, the Ambient WS-10 display unit is 100% devoted to temperature and humidity readings. It shows 4 sets of readings, nice and easy to read in passing without needing to turn on a screen light; one row is the "indoor" readings, at the unit itself, then a row for each of three remotes. And, if you add more remotes to your WS-10 system (it can handle up to 8, as opposed the the "Generic" having 3 maximum), you can set it up to automatically scroll continuously through all the remotes.

Finally, the Ambient WS-10 system came with at least an adequate multi-page instruction booklet.

I'mreturning this "Generic" system, and ordering (for only a little more money) a second WS-10 system. The total of 6 sensors I will then have will cover my 6 sensor requirements, and I will be able to have a display in 2 different parts of my home showing me the readings from all 6 sensors, on each display unit.returning this "Generic" system, and ordering (for only a little more money) a second WS-10 system. The total of 6 sensors I will then have will cover my 6 sensor requirements, and I will be able to have a display in 2 different parts of my home showing me the readings from all 6 sensors, on each display unit.

product_title: TOTMCÂ® 1HZ-500KHz DDS Function Signal Generator Module Sine+Triangle+Square Wave
review_headline: Reasonable value for the money, but don't expect perfection -- there are some "bugs" and limitations.
review_body:
Overall, this unit offers reasonable value for the money, but donâ€™t expect perfection â€“ there are some â€œbugsâ€ and limitations.

Nice package. Nice size. Light weight. Well-made internally.

Comes with a USB cable for supplying power to the unit. No ac adapter is supplied. (I use a 5 vdc â€œwall-wartâ€ with a USB output connector.)
The unit has 50 ohm output impedance, but will only produce about 2.75 volts peak-to-peak into a 50 ohm load prior to clipping. Will produce greater than 20 volts peak-to-peak into a high impedance.

Amplitude and dc offset adjustments work smoothly. The output voltage clips when the dc plus ac excursions become excessive. Amplitude is adjustable, beginning at a low of about 10 mv p-p. There is no amplitude scale, which could have been included around the amplitude knob. (I drew in by hand a scale around the amplitude knob on the side of the unit.)

Awkward frequency adjustment scheme: You have to stop (disable) the output to make any frequency or mode change. Each time the unit is stopped, the cursor position reverts to the most significant digit of frequency. To change frequency, it is necessary to tab over to the desired digit by repeatedly pressing the cursor button, then increasing or decreasing the highlighted digit by repeatedly pressing the + or â€“ buttons, then doing this again for any other digit or digits to be changed.

Crystal-controlled direct digital synthesizer (DDS) produces good frequency stability and readout accuracy. Looks like there are about 127 amplitude steps in the waveform, or a few less. This would indicate about a 7-bit digital-to-analog conversion is being used. Fortunately, the amplitude adjustment does not reduce the number of steps â€“ the internal gain is merely changed. When producing low frequencies, these steps can be seen on an oscilloscope. These can also be heard by playing what should be a sub-audible frequency such as a 10 Hz sine wave into headphones.

Aside from the steps, the sine wave looks nice (if the amplitude is set so it is not clipping) at all frequencies. Though the unit is advertised to go to 500 kHz, it will continue to produce sine waves (at reduced amplitude) all the way up to 999,999 Hz, which is the highest setting possible.

The filter button activates a low-pass filter that has 3 dB attenuation at about 400 kHz on my unit. I canâ€™t see that this filter has much utility.

The other waveforms are another matter â€“ these will run at higher frequencies, but are best kept in the audible range (less than about 20 kHz) in order to look â€œprettyâ€. There are obviously some programming errors in these. The square wave has some pulse width jitter, and at higher frequencies becomes grossly un-square, having about 20% pulse width distortion or more at 500 kHz. Some of the pulses are wide, some are narrow. The triangle wave has 8 minor glitches (where a step that should be present is missing) in the downhill slope, noticeable at low frequencies. These glitches are not present in the uphill slope. These glitches are not present in the sawtooth or reverse sawtooth. The triangle, sawtooth, and reverse sawtooth all show some jitter and perhaps a bit of superimposed low frequency distortion, along with some rounding, as the frequency increases, becoming noticeable above about 20 kHz. These may be related to the same or similar timing error that is present in the square wave. Some additional output distortion may appear when driving low or reactive output impedances.

product_title: EnjoyGadgets HDMI to Composite CVBS / S-Video Converter Adapter
review_headline: I used a set of composite cables that I already had and both picture and sound were fine. Obviously not HD quality
review_body:
I purchased this converter in September 2014 to connect an Amazon Fire TV box to an older TV. When I first hooked it up using the composite cables that came with the unit, the picture was really grainy. I never could get the S-video to work. The picture would constantly flicker. I used a set of composite cables that I already had and both picture and sound were fine. Obviously not HD quality, but adequate. As others have stated, the electrical cord is very short and comes out easily.

After about 6 weeks of use, I started getting a pop-up that said "license error" then a blank screen when I tried to watch any shows from Amazon. I contacted Amazon customer support who told me that my Fire box wasn't working. They sent a replacement, but I got the same "license error" message when I hooked up the new Fire box. I contacted customer support again and was told the new box must also be bad. That seemed suspicious to me so I did some research online and found other people were having the same "license error" problem. It seems that Amazon made a software change and HDMI converters have to be HDCP compliant to use with Fire box and Amazon Instant Video now. This converter is not HDCP compliant.

I purchased a different converter that was more expensive than this one but is HDCP compliant. I've only had the new one for 3 days, but it was allowing me to watch videos using the Fire box without getting the "license error" message. Apparently the problem was the converter box not the Fire TV box. The EnjoyGadgets converter was a waste of money since I cannot use it with the Fire TV box anymore, which is why I bought it. It may work fine with blu-ray players or other HDMI devices, just not Fire TV boxes.

* Great stereo sound.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 20 Headphones
review_body:
I bought these earphones a little over a year ago and they are fantastic. The noise cancellation works great especially if you're on a plane or in a busy street. It just works and fits my ears perfectly when running, working out or running errands. The battery pack lasts well over 8 hours even after a year's use. I use my headphones once or twice a week. The only thing that kind of irritated me was that I paid over $300 dollars a year ago for these hoping that it would last me for a few years considering how great I take care of my electronic equipment but the Aware button, the button that turns the noise cancellation On/Off by the microphone stopped working. Basically, I can click the Aware button but the noise cancellation always remains on. I cannot turn off the noise cancellation other than turning it off from the battery pack which turns off the whole unit.

The product is in mint condition but it was very disappointing to see it break. It's minor but I want my electronic equipment to work 100% considering the price I paid. I spoke to a Bose rep and he was extremely helpful and said Bose will be able to replace the earphones for $50 considering it's out of warranty. I respectfully declined since I don't believe I should have to pay any more than I did but that really disappointed me in the quality of the product. I expect that for the money paid, the product should have lasted at least 2 to 3 years.

Just wanted to put this out there for everyone that if you buy this, don't be surprised if a button fails on you after a year. If you are willing to accept this then it's a great product and it works as it's intended. If you're going to be surprised and have high expectations for the money you're paying for a premium product, I would skip this product.

product_title: Sony MDR-J10 Headphones
review_body:
I'm just want to say that I bought a pair of these when I was 14 years old...TEN years ago, and they only just broke on me today. So that should say something. For their intended purpose these headphones are fantastic, and I was confused to see a rating of only 3 and 1/2 stars when I came trying to see if anyone still sold them. I wear these biking and at work while doing lots of physical activity, and they never fall out. You have to snag them on something to get them to come off. They are comfortable and can be worn for hours without hurting (or perhaps my ears have grown to their shape over the years.) I've gotten them sweaty and disgusting and they never failed on me, until today when I snagged them just one too many times and something happened to one of the speakers. I've caught them on things HUNDREDS of times before though and they were ok, so these things last. The sound quality isn't going to blow any minds, but you don't buy earbuds for that. They sound good enough. The design does let in ambient noise however, which is a good and bad thing depending on where you want to wear them. If you want to drown out the world, you might want some closed headphones. If you are biking or working, this is great for hearing cars and when people are trying to get your attention. I'm buying a second pair right now, so I'll be good till 2025 hopefully.

EDIT: Well it's been only a year before this pair broke, and unlike the last unbreakable set, I don't even know what did then in. They worked one moment and not the next. Based on other people's reviews, I suspect that there has been a drop in build quality over 11 years, despite the price more than doubling! No thanks, Sony - you could've had a customer for life but instead you went ahead and ruined a good thing. I'll try and find a new brand, one that's not 40$ and lasts longer like the original build.

I was so impressed with the sound profile of the X10 that I ordered the X10i.

After a month of use, the headphone started falling apart. Stripping of the wire around the ear buds and audio jack. The volume rocker falling apart and not working. I tried emailing Klipsch for sending them back but they blew me off. So instead I went and bought the X11i hoping that I just got lemons.

To my shock after a month of use of, the same problems are showing up again and again I emailed Klipsch expressing my dismay and they said in a round about way that this is my fault.

I tell you, I am very careful with these, always putting them in a cloth pouch before putting them in my pocket. Never wearing metal that would cause the kind stripping of rubber you would see with normal wiring.

A warning to everyone, if you want something that will last a while, go find something else. Klipsch customer support is awful. They just want to deny responsibility for anything.

product_title: Philips ActionFit Sports In-Ear Headphones
review_body:
Mixed feelings on these headphones.

Pros:
- I sweat. A lot. I am a very sweaty person in general. Not many headphones stay in my ears when I run at all. These manage to stay in even if I'm doing 10 miles during a hot summer day. Among headphones that are in-ear and do not wrap around my ears, these are the only ones I have tried that do this.

Cons:
- The 3.5mm jack is at a 90 degree angle from the cord. However, the part perpendicular to the metal jack sticks out rather far (relative to headphones with a similar jack design). This results in it getting unplugged from my phone very easily when I put my phone into my pocket or pull it out. Very annoying.
- These things are cheap. I continue to buy them for the pro listed above, but they inevitably break. They break much faster than I'd like. I have probably bought this or a very similar Philips headphone model 6 times now. To be fair, I'm a bit of a workout junkie who uses these much more than most.

Neutral:
- Sound quality. They are decent. You get what you pay for. The sound quality isn't stellar nor poor.

Conclusion: Buy if you are a casual, sweaty gym-goer/jogger/etc. I will probably buy a better, more expensive pair of headphones from another company if/when these break.

product_title: Sony MDREX15 Fashion Color EX Series Earbuds
review_headline: Play stations better on other products
review_body:
I recently purchased these ear buds for $15 from Best Buy. After owning various kinds of said devices (including one pair which had the audio fidelity of the Samsung S4 mono speaker on "Low" volume) , I can safely say that these are not particularly good audio pieces. It should honestly come as surprise to no one that they are sub par. After thinking about it, the fact the prices of the products next to it in store were somewhere in the neighborhood of $7, I feel like the increased expense is the result of being "Sony" branded, and nothing else. These are actually marketed as
"High Quality" on the box, if you can believe that. I can't. They look, sound, and feel like "premium" $8 ear buds.

So, are they really as bad as I make them out to be? Let's find out. For starters, the body is absolute miniscule; that is plainly apparent. What's not apparent is what happens as a result. Because the body is almost as small as the earpiece, these things tend to slip out of my ears quite easily. I find myself frequently trying to wedge them back in, with little success.

How do they sound? Meh. They're okay, a fair balance of instrument, voice, and bass (though I tend to prefer bass-heavy devices, but for the most part I can recognize good sound quality when I hear it). The volume, even on medium, is kind of low and only when you get to dangerously loud levels does it start to sound good. I tried using my iPhone 6's channel calibrator to equalize the volume, but that wasn't successful; maybe mine is defective, because it sounds like the connection between the receivers is unbalanced and the right driver seems to get more signal than the left.

Like many other ear buds, the cable is rather poorly designed and feels really cheap, the kind of "cheap" feeling you get from using airplane headphones. If you like playing Cat's Craddle, you'll have field day with these things.

I like to think I'm a person who values the quality of the product over the brand it wields, and this definitely feels like a case of form over function. If you like Sony ear buds and can deal with okay audio quality, plus the annoyance of having to jam them back into your ears frequently, have at it. As for me, I'll have to live with them for a bit, because I still have to get my money's worth. All-in-all, they're not the "worst thing ever", so there's a marketing slogan.

review_headline: Great technology, but not for me.
review_body:
First of all, I'm really surprised about this "noise-cancelling" technology since this was my first headphones with that feature. This is definitely the advanced technology that we might not expect 15-20 years ago...

BUT, even with that amaze, I was not so convinced to use them. After maybe 2 seconds of the amazement, I quickly noticed the sound wave they are making (from now on I'll call it white noise cause the sound really is white noise to my ears) was not pleasant at all. After a few 30-to-60-minute sessions, I found out that the white noise put pressure on my eardrums.

And when there was a car noise on the street (motorcycle / pickup trucks), the white noise's frequency caused tremor on my left eardrum. This may not happen to you because I have very vulnerable left eardrum even though I was never diagnosed with anything. (When I hear certain sound, usually a high pitch sound, I hear buzzing in my left ear.)

I also found that the battery is really bulky to carry around if you carry your cellphone in your pocket. As some other posts say, the cable that connects the battery with your music device is only about 2" so it was really awkward/hard to place the battery, even on the desk.

Since my purchase was for noise-cancelling feature I won't talk about the sound quality - I actually didn't pay much attention because I knew I'm returning this only after 10 minutes of using it.

I'm pretty sure many people will like it because of its technology and different personal preferences, but personally it was not a pleasing experience for me.

I'm giving it 3 stars for its amazing technology and its comfort (it actually is really comfortable and you won't notice it much).

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR838 7.2-Ch Network A/V Receiver w/ HDMI 2.0
review_body:
I would love to give this a 5 star review because it seems like it could be a great product
I wouldn't know because the 2 brand new ones I bought didn't work.

The short version
I bought one and there was a short in the microphone jack preventing me from passing the initial setup screen. So I bought a new one and shipped the first one back. When the second one came in, it worked great and I was so happy. Then after a few minutes of actually using it, it just shut down. and wouldn't run anymore. But I had a great experience with customer service.

The rest of it.

I never like hearing that others had a fine time with customer service if I didn't. But when I called Onkyo, I was quickly connected to someone who could help. Probably a 5 minute wait. The guy I was transferred to actually hooked an 838 up and he walked me through doing a factory reset, then we went through the screens together through the initial steps of the new startup. Finally we could pinpoint what was wrong. His receiver was getting to a screen that mine was not and eventually he realized that the issue was the receiver.
This first receiver had a short in the microphone jack. this made it impossible to bypass the AccuEX initial setup - because it was detecting the setup microphone as plugged in when it wasn't.
I didn't want to wait for the return process to get a replacement so I just flat out bought a new one and just shipped that one back.
The second one arrived and I hooked everything up like I did with the first one. plugged in the power and was thrilled when it prompted me to plug in the microphone. so far so good.
Everything was working fine. I finished the AccuEQ, was prompted to remove the mic. then it tested the Connections (Cable/Sat, Playstation, and Phono) all of which were fine. It had detected my setup accurately (7.1 with Front Height)
Then while playing a record about halfway into the song the Receiver shut down. I tried turning it on again and it came on then powered down again. It smelled like it was cooking so I let it cool down for an hour. when I went to start it up again it sparked and shut down.
So I thought.. alright then, I guess this receiver is just not for me.
Now I'm apprehensive about even buying another Onkyo receiver. which sucks because I know this is supposed to be an amazing receiver. it has everything most people need, and the company I bought it from said that it gives you more power and connection than a Denon at the same price point.
Some of the functions I bought it for were: Phono, THX, 7.2, bi-amp
I don't know if this review is useful but that's what happened.

product_title: Sony MDR10RBT Bluetooth Wireless Headphones
review_body: [EDIT: Happy New Year!!!]    I can only suppose that those who give them 4 or 5 stars have never had a good pair of headphones in their life.    I may sound merciless, but I just tested 5 headphones for a few weeks [EDIT: in the while I have tested MANY more. I can give you a list if you write me a comment. And, no, my opinion about these Sony did not change, but I can tell you something: I would surely prefer them over the Beats Studio Wireless]:    Sennheiser MM400_X  Jabra Revo Wireless  Bose Soundlink On Ear  Philips Fidelio M1BT  and these Sony.    About the Sony:  They look cheap. The \\"silver\\" plastic is very bad taste. They are also too big to go around, unless you are one of those guys who like to show themselves with headphones bigger than their head.  They are Around the Ear, which makes them probably the most comfortable of the five on long term, and also gives them a good Soundstage.  I prefer the Soundstage of the Fidelio, which is less in quantity but more in quality, because for some reason the sound of these Sony tends to come from behind. This is for me very disturbing. The sound should come mostly from the front and the sides, or from everywhere like if you are in the middle. But these Sony make the sound come a bit more from behind.  Also, they do not fit tightly enough, and according to how you move your head they leak sound and you lose basses. You can see the difference if you press them a bit against your head.  The overall sound is dark and dull. Too many basses, much quantity, low quality. But also if you decrease the basses and increase the highs (with an EQ) the sound remains dull.  In very few occasions I was pleased with them. But generally I was disgusted very quickly and I just put them away everytime.  They are APTX, but Sony ships them with the APTX disabled as default. To enable it you must press a combination of buttons till the led blinks three times. In my tests the led blinked always two times, and I could only confirm the APTXvia notifications on my Phone.  The best thing on these headphones is the carrying bag. Robust, a bit rigid, very practical and easy to put in a backpack crowded by many things. You can than slip the headphones in and out of their bag easily while the bag is there compressed in the backpack.  Another good thing on the Sony are the buttons. Two buttons for the volume, one lever for pause/next track/previous track. IMO the best solution together with the five buttons of the Sennheiser.    In comparison, the Bose are much more fresh and balanced and true to the sound. And much much more portable.  The Philips have a much better quality of basses, and a better Soundstage and detail. And are a bit smaller (but with a worse bag).     Quickly:    Overall Sound:  1) Fidelio and Bose (somehow the Bose perform a bit better on my Phone and the Fidelio on my PC, but they are overall comparable, with the Fidelio a bit more spaced, and the Bose a bit more present)  2) Revo  3) Sennheiser  4) Sony    Basses:  1) Fidelio  2) Bose and Revo  3) Sony (nÂ°1 for quantity, nÂ°5 for quality)  4) Sennheiser    Detail and Room:  1) Fidelio  2) Bose and Sennheiser  3) Sony (would be at the first place for Room if the sound would not come from behind)  4) Revo    Portability:  1) Sennheiser  2) Bose  3) sony (because of the better bag even if bigger dimensions)  4) Fidelio and Revo (Fidelio because thinner with the speakers turned 90Â°, Revo because foldable)    Look:  1) Bose (even if plastic, the form is elegant and the dimensions discrete)  2) Fidelio  3) Revo  4) Sony  5) no. Sorry. Sennheiser just NO. The designer should be ashamed...    Battery:  1) Sennheiser (because you can have an extra one)  The others have all a good similar battery.    Price:  This may vary according to where you live. In EU:  1) Sennheiser (IF you buy them from their Outlet)  2) Sony  3) Revo  4) Fidelio M1BT  5) Bose and new Fidelio M2BT.    Comfort:  1) Sony (because Around the Ear), Bose and Sennheiser  2) Revo  3) Fidelio (but do not get fooled, they ARE comfortable enough for many hours)    Bluetooth Range:  1) Bose (just a tiny bit more)  2) Fidelio, Revo and Sony  3) Sennheiser    Functions:  1) Bose (clear winner for the double connectivity)  Then the others are more or less the same, each with little pros and cons.    Conclusions?    If you look for these headphones you clearly do not need something very portable.  In this case the Fidelio can be better for you than the Bose. They do not cost much more than the Sony. Apart for the new model.  If you plan to use them only at home, or if you like to have huge headphones while going around, and if money is not a problem for you, I would suggest you to stick with the Around the Ear and look for something better, bigger, more expensive. I did not try them but Thewirecutter says the AKG K845 are good. Eventually you could try the Sony MDR-1RBT MK2 (the ones with APTX). Some people say they are very good.  But believe me, these MDR10RBT are only worth if you just want big plastic headphones which make bum bum.    A short note about voting a review up or down: if you have a different opinion you do not need to vote mine down, you just can express yours in your review.  It is important to have different reviews from different people with different tastes and opinions.  Votes are for if a review is useful. And a review is useful when the reviewer explain in detail what he thinks of the product and why. No matter if you agree with his opinion or not.  I have spent LOT of time in comparing BT headphones and writing reviews, and although I had fun while doing it, I didn't do it for fun, I did it to help people, including you.  I would also be happy to give you more suggestions if you write me in the comments. In that case please specify which music do you listen most, and what do you want from a Headphone.    Hope this helped!

review_body:
"High Quality" - NO WAY !

"Reasonably Priced" - NOT unless the product is "High Quality" - or even works WELL - unfortunately this one DID NOT work well!

Straight out of the box - looked OK. But upon looking closer - then actually trying to USE this product, it was found to be VERY POOR quality to the point of being non-operational - thus USELESS!

The neat little cup caster thingy they sent for free as a "Bonus" is FAR more appealing - and used 100% more than the retched converter!

I have purchased several Chinese manufactured products which are of sound quality and which worked very well - at a very reasonable price. I use those products frequently and have no issue with their performance.

This product however "looked" pretty solid - but performed - NOT AT ALL.

The issue I have with this product is with the canister (12V power outlet) in which one would normally insert their 12V "plug".

Specifically -the part of the outlet/canister that "should" make firm contact with your 12V plug's "tip" - was SO poorly made that contact (firm or otherwise) could NOT happen. That piece was nothing but a small metal tab - connected to a loose and dangling wire going back to the adapter itself. That critical piece was not connected nor secured to ANYTHING - hence it COULD NOT be positioned in any way in order to make the required contact with the tip of the 12V plug!

Even while holding that piece by hand/fingers to the tip of my 12V plug, I still was not able to force enough contact sufficient to gain the 12V power this product was supposed to "Supply". Putting a multi-meter on the product showed no juice even making it from the adapter to the canister and/or tip contact. So - sadly - even if the tip contact had been rightfully secured to the base of the canister - I doubt the product would have worked due to other poor quality connection issues in other parts of the product.

The product I received must not have even been tested for anything - certainly NOT for "Quality", workmanship or operational ability.

The product I received simply COULD NOT have ever worked - yet they shipped it to me - "as was".

Given the extensive time and expensive (more than I paid for it) cost to return the item, I didn't.

Rather, I disassembled it - salvaged what little I could (wires) for other 12V projects I tinker with - and TOSSED the rest in the TRASH.

EXTREMELY disappointed. I would NOT recommend this product to anyone. HUGE waste of time and money!

Instead, I got THIS unit (below) - and I absolutely LOVE it. It performs VERY WELL and I would purchase it again. I recommend this product (below) to anyone needing a quality reliable durable AC to 12V converter. It is very high quality and a very reasonable price.

The standard battery for the mower is 36V, and has a simple port to charge with the recommended battery charger, and the main drawback is that it is north of $100, and will set you back another $20 for shipping. Lasts 3 to 5 years with reasonable care. This Mighty Max battery is 12V. It may be possible that 3 of them connected in series would work, but then once you used extra wiring required, you would have to use extra precautions against the vibrations and bumps experienced when mowing a lawn. And then there's the rub about how to connect it to a proper charger.
The standard battery, made by Duracell, is fully enclosed, waterproofed, and made for the Neuton exclusively. Even has a cover for the port for the charging of the battery. Mighty Max is advertised as a replacement for the Neuton. It is NOT, and won't work.

product_title: Veho VSS-009-360BT M4 Black | Bluetooth Speakers | Wireless Speakers | Portable Rechargeable Travel Speaker | Built in MP3 player
review_headline: Great Sound & Features In A Frail Package
review_body:
First off, I love music. I'm also a gear nerd... And an impulsive spender. I've accumulated quite a few Bluetooth speakers over the past few years. There are 10+ in my house, of all shapes and sizes - from the Bose SoundDock, to a portable speaker with a solar panel on top (Rukus Solar).

This little Veho 360 speaker gets the most use of all of them, by far.

For such a small and portable speaker, It has very impressive sound. It's not uncommon for people to come up to me and ask if "all of that sound is coming out of that little speakerâ€. Itâ€™s actually louder than the Rukus Solar speaker, which is about 5x the size of the Veho.

I use it in the shower, at the beach, while traveling, and even on my bike - I put it in a cup which sits in my bikes bottle holder, and it project sound out much louder than I need it to. It's a little lacking in the low-end, but you're not looking for that from a speaker of this size anyway.

The microSD slot is a killer feature. I keep a card filled with my favorite music. When I don't have my phone handy, or I just want to listen to something random, I'll play right from the memory card. Great option to have.

It has great battery life, too.

My only issue with the speaker â€“ and it's not a small one â€“ is the construction. This thing is just not durable at all. I'm actually on my second one, as you'll see in the pictures.

And I'm very gentle with my electronics, and the extent of the abuse that the speaker has been subjected to is being placed in a book bag with some water bottles and clothing.

I had my first Veho for about 6 months before the auxiliary port warped. No more line in! Shortly after that, the top (which houses the controls) came off. So I ordered another one, assuming that the damages to my first one were a fluke and this one would last longer.

Within a week, the auxiliary port on this one was warped too. Not a huge deal, as I rarely use line in. Still, this shouldn't have happened.

Rukus, I love your product, but please make it more durable! There aren't many speaker options in this size range with microSD... Make the 360bt a bit more rugged and it will be perfect. Until then, Iâ€™ll have to explore other speaker options in this size range when this one inevitably starts falling apart., as I rarely use line in. Still, this shouldn't have happened.

product_title: SummitLinkÂ® Logitech Z-2300 Computer Speaker Replacement Control Pod Wired Remote
review_headline: So, it has come to this has it.
review_body:
If you're reading this then you purchased the magnificent z-2300, and then something catastrophic happened to the remote.

I know what you're thinking. This looks nothing like the original. Here are some insights.

Three stars. Middle ground. The 'meh' of Amazon. This is actually a courtesy rating.

I had read shining and not so shining reviews for this piece of technology. "Better than the original" some claimed, and "Cheaply made" others claimed. That is a rather confusing dichotomy. The truth is, this does work well, or it did (past tense) for me for about a month. The audio once again became vibrant and full for my z-2300. I was reminded why I got the sound system in the first place. The bass, the audio, crystal clear and sharp. Thank you, Summit Link.

However, the 'cheap construction' jab isn't just gossip, folks, but it isn't all around either. I had noticed the diverse number of types of failings people had experienced. For me it wasn't my power button, that worked wonderfully. It wasn't the nobs, those have a great weight to them. It was the insertion point for the audio jack. You see, SummitLink rightly made it possible to remove the 9.5 mm headphone jack from the back. This is awesome, as that was the original failing portion of the original control box for me. After about a month of use, however (switching sound outputs from tv to computer and so forth) the insertion point on the back of the box was visibly moving, and the sound cutting out on one or both speakers with the slightest touch. It wasn't ready for that much use at all.

So, three stars? I have no way of knowing if this is an isolated incident, if I had just a lemon of a product. But, I would also--sadly--like to point out, that you don't have much of a choice here.

My z-2300 is sitting by the TV, dead as a door nail, until I get another replacement box, and these guys offer the only one. So, props to them. Here's to hoping it this was just one bad example of a good product.hoping it this was just one bad example of a good product.

product_title: Libratone Zipp Portable WiFi Speaker
review_headline: Impressive sound but expensive with very limited wireless performance
review_body:
Great audio quality. Terrible wireless connectivity and range. If you're connecting wirelessly directly from your device, not using a central wi-fi router connection which is a nice feature, you'd better stay in line of sight with the speaker, and not more than 20ft away or you'll get highly annoying audio drop-outs. Not what you want to tend to while listening or have playing during a party. And unfortunately, connecting using your typically much more reliable home wireless is not much better. Was getting "signal too weak" errors on the mobile app and disconnected audio signal when just one room away from a new wireless N router. The same room as a PS4 and Apple TV (which is 6" square in size, btw) that have no wi-fi connection problems at all streaming HD video and are tucked back into a media shelf. So just keep your wireless expectations low and you'll be impressed with the room-filling sound it offers for such a small size.

Pro tip: Definitely utilize the free Libratone app to dial in the right output settings and tonal options that fit the room, placement, and music style. It's simple to use (a small finite number of intuitive options) and I got much better sound quality after doing this than when I just plugged my iPhone into the speaker for the first time and used whatever defaults it was set to. Plus you need this app to even access the speaker wirelessly and to add your home wi-fi connection.

Bottom line: if you're not a gadget and network tinkerer this may not be the speaker for you. You can always just plug in with a USB cable for more reliability but then why pay a premium for a bunch of wireless features you're not using. There are tons of quality options for non-wireless speakers. In hindsight I wonder if the Sonos brand is much better for wireless range and ease of use, with it's larger market share and assumed larger budget for more frequent updates and quality control. It also has options for expanding speakers into a whole house or theater sound system, which now seem appealing, even if also pricey.

product_title: Bose QuietComfort 25 Headphones (wired, 3.5mm)
review_headline: Doesn't Fully Cancel Out Office Jibber Jabber
review_body:
I sit in the most dismal location at work. *START RANT* At all four corners of my cubicle farm pen, there is always someone talking. Right behind me, I have an IT guy making constant phone calls to our call center site, telling some poor joe to get the cheapest Dell promos and trying to finalize some sort of contract. To my right, a big shot manager negotiates left to right with folks who can't seem to get their act together on the other side of the world. To my left, a hippy dippy recruiter asks typical interview questions over the phone to dozens and dozens of hopeless candidates each week. Of course, they don't respond well to the STAR interview questions, so after she hangs up, she vents her frustration by yelling \\"AGHH!\\". Now, to the front of me, I have a pair of co-workers who talk like valley girls. Like, y'know Omg! Their conversations are as shallow as a kiddy pool. *END RANT*

One faithful morning, I visited my local Target to buy a pair of these headphones, recommended to me by half a dozen of my co-workers. I used my Target gift cards to pay down the cost of tax and with my purchase, I went straight to work.

What I have found so far is that it does a good job of canceling out male voices since they are deep in tone. Sounds that I never noticed before such as the whir of the AC are also drowned out. Noise cancellation is at its best when music is playing. However, even with music I can still hear, but not as loud, exactly what my female co-workers are saying. Their high pitch voices are impossible to drown out completely. I could continue to up the volume, but there's only so much my ears can withstand without hurting. Also, if I do up the volume, people can hear what I'm listening to. Not cool.

My overall verdict is that these headphones will almost do the trick for now, but I'm still going to be in the lookout for a better solution.

product_title: Logitech Li-ion Battery for Harmony Remote ONE 880 890 720
review_headline: New Battery -- Swollen Again. Faster this time.
review_body:
I purchased this battery from Amazon for a Logitech Harmony 900 on 6/16/2013 to replace one that had swollen after approximately three years. The new one lasted a year and a half before swelling up again. Customer feedback in the Logitech forums seem to suggest that the culprit is not the battery, but the charger not cycling off when the battery reaches full charge. Several customers reported that when they contacted Logitech about the swollen battery, Logitech's response was to replace their charging cradle AND ship them a new battery. Someone else recommended *not* storing the remote in the charging cradle until the battery was low. I ordered a replacement battery on 1/26/2015 and I will follow that advice.

Also, this battery is (advertised) rated at 950mAh but Logitech units using the same battery reportedly now ship with 930mAh. Speculation on the forums was that this was possibly a response by Logitech concerning the swelling issue, but I could not source that directly to any statement by Logitech. It was reported, however, that the lower rated battery seemed to work just fine in the remotes.

For those of you who find you cannot remove your batteries due to the swelling (and your unit is out of warranty), an internet search for "Harmony 900 Disassembly Video" will result in detailed instructions.

product_title: Lepai LP-S60 4 x 25W Desktop Amplifier with Remote/USB/MP3/SD/FM
review_headline: not great, but okay and has a few problems
review_body:
This cheaply made modified Chinese car stereo is decent for the price, not great, but okay and has a few problems. I own two of the $20 lepai lp-2020a+, they are better sounding amps and both work great, but have no remote, no tuner, no line-out, and only run two speakers. I moved a TV to my fireplace mantel and no longer had room for a full-sized amplifier. I replaced the slightly better sounding lepai lp-2020a+ with this Lepai LP-S60 because I wanted a remote control for the volume - the FM tuner is a nice extra - I have not used the SD card or USB reader. Mine is driving two Dayton Audio bookshelf speakers and sounds decent. It came with one sheet of English instructions. The remote is very cheaply made, flexes and works from about 6'. I plan to find a standard universal learning remote to to replace the factory remote with before it fails.

DEFECT: My unit arrived with a defective power adapter. The power adapter cord would short and the unit power down with any movement of the connector. There was also a loud feedback hum over the speakers coming from the power unit. The included power adapter is 12V 5amp, and the unit will accept 12V < or = 5 AMP. My AC adapter from the old Lepai LP-S60 is 12V 2Amp it fits the new LP-S60 and drives my Dayton speakers with more then adequate sound.

The closest similar small amplifier with a remote I could find was about $90, at $30 I think this unit was worth the price, but it is cheaply made and I think unlikely to be a long lasting solution.

product_title: Bose SoundLink Mini Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Subpar bad bluetooth range, not loud outside
review_body:
The soundlink mini is pretty loud but could be a bit louder when you're outside. The speaker has good bass for such a small speaker. It's pretty heavy but feeIs like it can take a beating. The bluetooth is really horrible on this product. It's a pain to connect 30 percent of the time. Then once it's connected sometimes you can be 4 feet away and it will cut in and out. This product by far has the worst bluetooth range I have ever seen. Ill put it in my backpack and it will break up with my pack on and the phone in my hand.

The battery life is okay nothing to special you'll get about 5 hours out of it. It takes a long time to charge and they should have used a standard 12 volt plug.

I used the unit for about 4 months and then I had an issue with the battery not wanting to charge. So I sent it in to bose which takes a long time like a whole month. They took my unit apart and cleaned it and think they gave me a new cord. I went to use it and the speaker would shut off after ten minutes of use. I sent the speaker back to bose to be repaired a second time. Now the speaker turns off after an hour and after that it just keeps shutting off every 5 minutes. Now I have to send my unit back a third this time but I should receive a new unit. When I do it will be a backup speaker, because I'm going to have to get something else that will be bit loud, lighter, and with better blue tooth range.

It's an okay speaker if it would work. It has decent sound and battery life, but horrible bluetooth. The bluetooth is really insulting for such a high priced item. The sound output has nice bass at low volumes. When you turn it up it loses some of it's punch and bass bais. Outside the speaker will leave you wanting just a little more volume at times.

review_headline: These wipes are terrible. They leave behind a bunch of lint. Rubbing alcohol and microfiber towel is better option.
review_body: These wipes are terrible. They leave behind a bunch of lint, which is most unhelpful when you're trying to clean up your phone before applying a screen/back protector. I would only recommend using them if you have some real grime build up to remove from your computer/phone/tv screen, something that calls for a little dampness to get off. You'll definitely want to follow up with a microfiber cleaning cloth after using these, to remove all that darn lint the wipes left behind on your device. I think they do dry alright, didn't have much streaking left on the back of my Edge+ phone, but the lint is a real headache and deal killer for me. Also, the dispenser is poorly designed. It's way too big of an opening, and you have to manually tear off a wipe (then push the other dozen that came up with that wipe back down into the canister). I purchased my can of these at Meijer for $4.99, surprisingly a bit cheaper than the Amazon price. For 5 bucks, 70 wipes seems like a good deal, but these in the end, are not worth the purchase. I recommend using a high alcohol, such as 91%, rubbing alcohol with microfiber towels for cleaning electronic devices. Cheaper, cleaner, and far more effective than these wipes.

product_title: Tomameri Pink Portable MP4 Player MP3 Player Video Player with Photo Viewer , E-Book Reader , Voice Recorder + 16 GB Micro SD Card
review_body:
This is the classic bare-bones imported MP3 player. That means low quality construction, a screen that seem to have come from a different era, and a user interface that is puzzling at best. To the first point, the image I've included shows the middle button, which fell off as I was taking it out of the package. Thankfully, everything else is in working order.

Navigating the menus requires some trial and error, and I don't think you will have much success with customizing playlists or quickly searching for songs as you might with a phone. However, for the basic functionality, it works fine. Like other devices in this category, it won't play the common AAC format, so make sure to convert if you can.

Speaking of converting, the video format is a strange one. I tried to play the normal video files I download with no luck. There is a sample video in amv format, so I guess you will need to download software to put your videos in that format with the correct resolution and bitrate. I remember doing this back in the day with a hacked Nintendo DS, so it is funny to see it in 2015. With that said, it would be a large nuisance to convert all of your videos to that format, even if you know how.

On the bright side, as I said, it has worked fine for what it is so far. I also like that the micro SD card is removable. That makes it easy to pop it into a card reader to transfer files, or use for other things. It is a generic unnamed brand, but works.

Overall, I find it difficult to recommend this over an old Android phone that you might find in this price range. If you go in knowing what it is, though, you might be happy with it, and the older iPod style design makes it easy to hold.

Thank you to the company for a review unit.

review_body:
These earbuds are comfortable, provide a great sound and are affordable. However there is a one MAJOR flaw with them, these earbuds do not work on iPhone 6 and iPhone 6 plus. When you plug them in for some reason Siri (iPhones voice control system) turns on. You can turn it off only if you go to iPhone settings and disable Siri after that you can use the headphones. It is too much hassle to turn Siri on and off every few hours. Also the microphone button on the earbuds does not function for turning the music on and off (it does work as a microphone).
I went to Apple store and their tech people said that they have heard of these complains before, you can do online search and there are people with earbuds from other companies that have the same exact issue. Certain earbuds with microphone are not compatible with the newest iOS system.
I have tested these on Android phones and everything works fine, it is a great product especially given the price.
I have used Jlabs other units and they work fine on iPhone 6, it is for some reason that these Diego units that has issues. I contacted Jlabs about this, they said they are aware that some people experience the activation of Siri with earbuds that also have a microphone but they can not do anything about it. Their customer support said they do not have a solution for this issue and basically they would not do anything about it. If you have an iPhone stay away from these as they are useless and will not work unless you are willing to disable Siri completely. If you have another phone I would look into buying these. So this calls into question every Jlab product in a way, if you have an iPhone you need to make sure that they work on your device first and once you confirm that you can make a purchase.
As I have tested these on another phone the sound is good so I give it 4 starts, but since Jlab does not stand behind itâ€™s product and said outright they can not and will not do anything I have to deduct 1 star.

review_headline: Not perfect, but excellent. Almost 5  stars. (Edit: 1 Star now)
review_body: Edit:(Changing from a 4 Star to a 1 Star)  These headphones "sound" incredible.  But the pause/play clicker stopped working in less than a month. The durability in these headphones is unforgivable for a $100 retail price for a product. I tweeted to @KlipschAudio asking for help and they ignored 15 plus tweets over the course of 6 months. This is the 2nd Klipsch product that has failed on me in less than 6 months of owning. Klipsch has great sound, but terrible durability. I bought a $400 speaker from them, failed under 6 months, they want me to pay like $30+ to ship this heavy thing back to them. How about you send me a return label?!? They don't really care about the customer service portion or the durability unfortunately. I was so blown away by the sound that I have been raving about Klipsch products since December 2014 to hundreds of people in my business sphere of influence. Will be warning them away from Klipsch now. Very unfortunate because the sound is so pleasing to the ears.  TLDR: Mic controls stopped working in less than a month. Unforgivable for a $100 product (really any product, even a $30 pair of headphones). Stay away even if you're under warranty, and it's their quality problem, they want you to pay return shipping for them to fix or replace.     The sound in these are great. As I write this review, I'm using them while sitting at a computer at work. The completely isolate the sound around me. I can't hear anything but the music I'm listening to. No strokes of the keys or the loud co-worker next to me who is always shouting into the phone like she's trying to make us or the person on the phone deaf. Just me and my music. I love it. I'm reserving myself from giving these 5 Stars because of all the eartip pieces that it comes with, the most comfortable tip is still slightly too big, and the small, too small. So they are slightly uncomfortable. So far I've been able to wear them without any problem for hours at a time. When I take them out though, my ears feel slightly stretched out from the inside. It's just a slight discomfort though. No irritating. Another reason I'm not giving it 5 Stars is because of something similar to what a bunch of other reviews said. The remote for play and volume controls is huge. It's bigger than it looks in the picture and is heavy. It's the very first thing my wife mentioned when I told her to listen to these awesome headphones. She was blown away by the sound and asked if she could have them. DENIED haha. Anyways, they are a great pair of headphones, and the influence of the weight of the remote can be reduced by using a clip.  I've been using these for 4 days. I will update this review if I have any problems, praises, or nuances that arise in the future!  Bottom line.  Ease of use  5/5 Sound  4.5/5 Convenience  4/5 Comfort  3/5 Noise Isolation  5/5 Value (opinion)  5/5 @ $50 price range. I got them for less than $50, but I would pay $50 for these easily.

review_body:

I didn't experience pressure on top of my head from the pads as others complained about. It is an over-the-ear headphone, so naturally you will feel warmer wearing it, but it still felt comfortable. Good bass that doesn't sound muddy. Good mid-range. Earpieces swivel around for 1 ear listening.
Cons: Poor treble. The sound is not crisp even after I turned up the higher frequencies up all the way on my phone equalizer. There is no spatial separation of the sound so it all sounds like it is coming from one place. i.e., very narrow soundstage. My noise cancelling headphone is much better in both of these areas.

I just need an inexpensive replacement to occasionally monitor live sound from my mixer, so it suffices. But I would not recommend them for personal listening.

product_title: Eton Field AM/FM with RDS and Shortwave Radio, Black (NGWFB)
review_body: Eton's Traveler III is a nice portable (almost pocket) radio that offers many features (AM, FM, SW, RDS) but is hampered by poor ergonomics and some over-sensitivity.  The Traveler is compact and, despite its light weight, seems well-constructed. Its display is very readable and the backlight can be adjusted. One glaring omission is a direct entry keypad, an oversight that becomes annoying due to the Traveler's small and quirky buttons. This may not impact AM and FM users but it makes roaming the shortwave bands a painful exercise. The tiny buttons used to select bands require a very firm and deliberate push and getting the radio into scan mode is difficult. One can adjust the tuning speed of the tuning knob but the knob is too small to make manual tuning over the shortwave bands practical. The radio lacks any provision for an external antenna and that's probably a good thing for most users; the radio exhibits a surprising amount of over-sensitivity to AM/MW interference on the shortwave bands. Bleed-over from strong local AM stations is present (although faint) at times using the built-in whip but becomes overwhelming if a modest longwire (15') is attached to the antenna. On the plus side the RDS works well and the radio has good sound for its size.

product_title: Unique 200 Hours Back-up Battery Life Time (Standby), Reecom R-1630 SAME Weather Alert Radio (Light Grey), Display Event Message and Effective Time At a Glance, EOM Detection, 25 Event Memories
review_body:
All of the positive reviews appear to be straight out of the box rather than with months or years of experience...

I am an engineer as well as licensed amateur and commercial radio operator. Out of the four 2-5 year old RE-1630C radios I own three of them have failed in the exact same manor. After a year or so of use, they stop responding to weekly tests and more importantly actual alerts of severe weather or emergency situations. If the radio is left unplugged and without batteries for several months the problem sometimes corrects itself but returns within a few weeks of putting the radio back in service. All the settings remain correct as programmed and the ongoing weather information can be heard by pressing the radio button. There is no announced capability to reset the radio to factory "as shipped" status like many other SAME radios provide. Reecom has sanded away any identifying marks on the internal microcontroller chip (a big red flag) to discourage anyone from trying to effect their own repairs; repair charges plus shipping equal the purchase price.

Reecom doesn't answer their telephone, apparently preferring to pick and chose which voice mail messages they respond to. When someone finally called me back, she blamed the problems on the National Weather Service not issuing a successful weekly test, FOR WEEKS IN A ROW! When the radios work, NWS tests are spot on 52 weeks a year. My contact at the NWS informs me that a weekly test hasn't failed for several years.

I used to highly recommend these radios as did the NWS on its web site but an emergency radio you can't depend upon CAN ENDANGER YOU AND THOSE AROUND YOU. I won't recommend a specific alternative as I've switched to building my own; continue researching SAME radios until you find one with a better track record than Reecom products.
