product_title: Sony HTCT260H Sound Bar with Wireless Subwoofer
review_body: I never write reviews, but I felt it was my personal duty as a consumer to write one for this product.  I received the Sony HT-CT260H as a gift. Immediately after hooking it up the subwoofer didn't work for about 10 minutes. I figured it was just an initial pairing issue. No big deal.  In the week I had it, however, it would constantly cut in and out --the subwoofer, not the soundbar itself. It became very annoying. I tried all the troubleshooting steps multiples time. I moved the subwoofer, I turned off other electronics. My WiFi router is located on the other side of the house.  I went to the Sony forums where it was apparent that other people were having the same issue. as I read through the thread I was impressed; Sony had a moderator communicating with people, trying to get to the bottom of the issue. However, then all of a sudden, the moderator disappeared and Sony marked the thread as \\"solved.\\" Needless to say, people were angry. This was worrying.  I decided to call Sony. The tech support guy had no idea what he was talking about. He told me even I f I had a WiFi router in the same room it wouldn't make a difference. He said it's not connected to the WiFi router. I explained that it says in the manual that the wireless subwoofer uses the same 2.4GHz frequency. He said it wouldn't matter. He told me I would have to send the soundbar/subwoofer to them at my expense to have it repaired. The repair was covered under warranty, but shipping a 10+ pound product isn't cheap.  Now, I should mention that the soundbar --when it's working-- is very good. I had the receipt so I convinced myself it was just a rare defect and I went to the store to exchange it for another one...  Right after I setup the new soundbar, the same exact problem occurred. I returned it for a different soundbar entirely and I'm very happy now. I won't mentioned the brand or model of my new soundbar so it doesn't seem like this is some PR tactic.  So, yeah, I just wanted to write my experience with this soundbar. It's clear there's a defect. A lot of people are experiencing it (based on Sony forums). I'm just glad the defect presented itself right from the jump, so I wasn't stuck with a lemon. Just make sure you keep your receipt and don't throw away the box if you decide to go for it.

review_body: This radio, features, performance, and size wise, has a lot of potential, but, as already stated, its usability experience is not the best. I'll not mention the manual tuning idiosyncrasies, as that has already been mentioned, what I would like to alert potential buyers to, is the faulty memory preset implementation. I've owned this radio for three weeks now.  Contrary to the Grundig G3 (previous implementation of this radio), the Eton Satellit does not store the tuning mode, i.e. USB/LSB or SYNCH modes (as well as bandwidth), therefore you will have to check, and possibly choose, the correct tuning mode and bandwidth after each retrieval of a memory preset. When you copy and paste a memory page the assigned name doesn't get copied. Also, every time you change the bandwidth, or tuning mode, the radio comes out of memory page mode, therefore changing the function of the memory buttons, so frustrating.  These design faults, yield an unpleasant user experience, please note that all of these memory functions were properly implemented in the G3, and this is therefore unexpected. Itâ€™s like you are purchasing a radio not designed for real users, or at an early beta version of the firmware! The owner's manual makes an even bigger mess of all of these memory functions, as it gives the wrong instructions, again contrasting to the G3 owner's manual, which explained it correctly.  Lastly, I should mention that the quality control by Tecsun (the Chinese maker of these units) is apparently still bad. The first radio I received, was overall in good condition, but had a defective display. The second radio, out of the box, had a folding stand that would not clip back on, a very wobbly tuning knob (missing the holding screws inside!), the speaker metal grill was not properly attached and had a damaged corner, and also the display screen had a defective border, overall very bad to the eyes.  At this price range, the consumer should not have to go through the hassle of ordering multiple units in order to find a good one!  As an owner of other previous wonderful Grundig made Satellit radios, I'll reiterate that calling this radio a Satellit is pure marketing and an abuse to the rights to that name, even the packing materials are totally unacceptable and likely to allow damage to the radio during delivery.

product_title: Bluetooth Speaker, Portable Wireless Stereo Speaker and Speakerphone with 2 X 3w Surround Sound Speaker Ultra Bass Subwoofer Speaker, NFC Function Mic for Tablet Laptops Computers Mp3 Player (Silver)
review_body:
The speakerphone feature of the Taco is far inferior to the speakerphone on my iPhone 5c, to the point that the Taco is not practically useable as a speakerphone. I tried calling 2 different people to test the Taco. Both could can barely hear me at 3ft/1m away from the Taco. At 9ft/3m away, all each could hear was a bit of noise. In contrast, when I switched to the iPhone's speakerphone on the same call, the other persons could hear me loud and clear as I walked around the room at more than 9ft/3m away. I tried the Taco at different volumes and with different positions, in case it's microphone was covered, but no improvement. I tested the Taco in a quiet home environment.

In an attempt to get around this problem I tried using the Taco with a wired connection in headphone mode. This allows the Taco to play the incoming voice over its speakers while using the microphone on the iPhone to pick up my voice. In terms of microphone volume, this works, but there is a very loud echo because the iPhone's microphone also picks up my voice coming through the Taco. As a result of this very loud echo, that headphone mode is unusable as a speakerphone.

Perhaps I got a bad one, or perhaps the design uses a low quality microphone without any noise and echo cancellation technology.

Since I bought this unit primarily to use as a speakerphone, I will be returning it.

As for music sound quality, it's pretty good and loud enough to fill a bedroom with sound. It does distort at the highest volume and is a bit boomy for my taste. If I wanted it only as I Bluetooth speaker, I would have kept it. Since I haven't tried other comparable Bluetooth speakers, I don't have an opinion about relative sound quality.

I also don't like the location of the charging port, which is on the bottom of the unit. When plugged into USB power, the unit does not sit flat but flops over on its side. If you plan to keep this unit plugged in, it willnot sit upright but will look funny and may roll around. While the unit can certainly operate on USB power, its physical design is intended to be run off of battery power and charged between uses, rather than to be plugged in on an ongoing basis, unless you don't mind it laying on its side.

So, two stars off for having an unusable speakerphone and one for poor power port position.

review_body:

(2) SOUND. There is substantial noise leakage, even when listening at a moderate volume. I don't think people around me want to be listening to my music.
(3) WIRELESS PAIRING. The pairing is atrocious. I've owned several pairs of bluetooth headphones in the past and these are without exception the worst. If you disconnect from your phone/ipad etc you need to power off your headphones and then re-power on to pair. On top of that, there's no pairing memory beyond one device. (4) BATTERY LIFE. The power design is fairly poor. These should power off automatically if there's no music for an extended period of time. They have a wireless or with-chord option with these, but what the heck is the use if you need a full charge to listen with the chord as well? I bought these because the with/without chord didn't make you a slave to a full-charge, but thats absolutely not the case. If the battery is low, you can't use these, with or without a chord.
(5) COMFORT. These are okay if you're wearing them for an hour or two, but anything beyond that (late night working/studying or on a long flight) gets really uncomfortable because the ear pieces don't properly cup your ears so your ears get pretty hot and sweaty and sticky after a short while... maybe 90 minutes in.

CONCLUSION: I'm usually reluctant to buy high-end mainstream consumer headphones (like Beats) instead opting for the audiophile alternative since of the $400 paid for Beats, $100 goes to their advertising budget, $100 is the cost and $200 is the profit. For a $400 pair of headphones with a 50% profit margin, I'd rather have headphones that cost $200 to manufacture with higher-quality components/design/construction... even if that means that my favorite athletes aren't photographed with the same headphones as me on TMZ.com. I caved this time because I needed a decent pair of wireless headphones in a jam and I ended up with an overpriced sub-par product. If I paid $100 for these I'd be fully satisfied. But for $300-400, severely disappointed.

product_title: iHome Portable Speaker for MP3 Players
review_headline: Good Audio Sound Quality, Fair Volume, Annoying Buzz
review_body:
I had originally bought a speaker, mainly to use in my workroom where there are limited available outlets that are not in use; therefore, I needed a wireless device. I loved the convenience of the speaker so much that I bought another for a different area of my home and since they are relatively inexpensive I then purchased a third one. I now have a variety of 3 different speakers to compare.

The iHome IM60GT 3.5mm Aux Portable Speaker is my least favorite of them all. Although the sound quality is good, not great, the volume is not very loud and even worse is this speaker has a tendency to buzz. The only thing that it is plugged into this speaker is my Samsung Galaxy Note 3. While the music is playing, I do not hear the buzz, but every time it switches to another song, there is a rather loud and distracting audible buzz. It ruins the flow of one song blending into another.

My favorite of all the speakers that I now own is the iHome iM59WC Rechargeable Color Changing Mini Speaker. It is identical, comes with the exact same accessories, is the same size, phenomenal sound quality, and the speaker has a louder volume, WITHOUT any maddening buzz. No Bluetooth necessary, just charge and plug into your music device. Like the iHome IM60GT it is able to be compressed, easily fitting into a regular size pocket and it is the same price.

The only visible difference is that IM59WC only comes in white, and the option of the color-changing chamber that can easily be switched off. The audio difference is that the volume output is louder and there is NO ANNOYING BUZZ.

To summarize my review, Yes, get the iHome portable speaker, just a different model at about the same price, for under $20.00. There is a huge difference. Although, the IM59WC has the same features, and the same convenience, it has a louder and a better quality sound without the irritating and distracting buzz that I received from the iHome IM60GT.

product_title: iHome  NFC Bluetooth Stereo System with Speakerphone
review_headline: Good mid range BT Speaker, one Glaring Flaw
review_body:
Works just fine as a mid range Bluetooth speaker system, and even provides the ability to make speakerphone calls. However, be aware that you can basically never turn it off. It has a power button, but also has a "feature" that turns it on automatically when you receive a call. Or at least that's how the manual describes it. In reality it not only turns itself on when you get a call, but any other time your phone emits an audible tone. Text messages, button clicks, you name it. The iHome engineers apparently figured that when people turn off their device, they must not have really meant to do that. Why even have a power off button if the device won't stay off. Because obviously the only thing anyone wants to do is make speakerphone calls all day long.

I emailed iHome and asked how you can disable this auto on feature, and their response was as follows:

"The only way to control this is by turning off the Bluetooth on the iPhone.

Thanks,

iHome Support"

So there you have it. If you are OK with your phone constantly streaming every little tone through the speakers whenever in range, because it doesn't believe in powering off, then this is the speaker system for you. Or if you are OK with constantly turning your Bluetooth on or off on your phone, just to stop the device from fixing your power off mistake, then again you have found the speaker system for you. Or just do a bit more research and find another system that lets you have full control of it and doesn't try to make it's own decisions about when to turn on.

product_title: Bowers & Wilkins In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: We need transparency for these earphones
review_body:
What a completely dishonest approach this manufacturer has with respect to how they merchandise these earphones. They may sound great -- I don't know -- but these are not wireless. There is a wire that connects to the source, but not a single photo or video provided by the marketing team of Bowers & Wilkins shows you anything more than a wire or wires coming from the earphones and just cut off, not to show where these wires go.

I am all for great earphones, and I have terrific earphones called the Jaybird Bluebuds X which are fully Bluetooth wireless. I would have had an interest in seeing if the Bowers & Wilkins earphones had an advantage over the Jaybirds, but they are wired and that's not my interest for these. I already have wired earphones, probably the best out there since they have advanced noise cancelling circuitry. They are the Bose QC 20. If I want wired, that's my go-to earphones. If I want wireless, the Jaybird Bluebuds X are my go-to earphones.

I'm always in the market for a better mousetrap, so when I saw a review of the Top-Rated Headphones for Runners I naturally took an interest in the Bower & Wilkins earphones which, at first glance, appeared to be wireless since I didn't see a wire going to the source. Then, in a subtle mention within the body of the review, it was revealed that these are wired.

In my opinion, honesty is the best policy. It should be very obvious from product photos that this is a wired set of earphones. I could just see the conference room where advertising decisions were being made and someone on the marketing staff saying "Why don't we obscure the fact that these are wired so we can at least get people to try them out." Honesty, please.

1. Noise cancellation. It is not particularly effective compared to Bose or full ear plug type noise isolation headphones. It will block out the sound of an airplane or a dishwasher, but it does a terrible job with anything higher pitched than a low rumbling. Still, it's better than nothing in a noisy environment. But what about a quiet environment? That hiss!!! The hiss is around the same loudness as the lowest volume setting on an iPad. That is very noticeable when listening during work or at home. I understand this is a necessary part of active notice cancellation, but it could easily have been avoided by making active noise cancellation defeatible. Instead, if I'm listening at work under low volume, I get to hear this delightful white noise accompanying my music. And it is definitely noticeable.

Sound quality. Bass sounds compressed. I don't know how to describe it other than that. It's like all the sounds are there, but they are indistinguishable from each other. Every bass drum hit sounds like it gets flattened out or something. The highs sound brittle, like when you overdrive a speaker system, except these headphones sound that way at any volume. Pretty unacceptable IMO. For those wondering what my comparison points are, I've had in ear Etymotics ($130, great sound but a bit flimsy), the classic Sony MDRV6 ($110) and a pair of Event 8 inch studio monitors with a Rythmik 10 inch sealed sub ($1,500 total). The Beats fall massively behind all of these in audio quality, but rank number 2 in cost. I just can't justify spending $300 to hear brittle highs and unintelligible bass painted on a canvass of white noise. Good thing I didn't buy these, but instead received them as a gift. For free, I'll take them! I honestly wouldn't pay $50 for these. I've had $20 Sony headphones that sounded better.

Believe the critics! These are terribly overpriced and all of their money has been put into branding, celebrity endorsement, and a faux feeling of high quality. Do. Not. Buy.

product_title: Air 2 Floating Wireless Bluetooth Speaker
review_body:
Got this device today 6/24/15. I was impressed by how large and hefty it is which suggests its made out of high quality materials. The floating feature really appeals to the nerd in me and is what I like best about the device, and the fact that it slowly rotates as its floating looking just like a flying saucer. Setup was simple although getting the device to float the first time took some time. They give you a holder that you put the speaker in, then place it over the base until you get it positioned just right then you remove the holder and the speaker floats. At first it wasn't working I'm not sure if the magnets shift during shipping or some other issue but the speaker kept slamming down onto the base at an odd angle. It took me about five minutes on the initial setup to get it to float and I was concerned that this would be the case every time, but after that it seemed to find its home and stay in place quite well. I could adjust the controls and float the speaker without using the supplied holder, just as they do in the video.

Now, down to the reason I could only give it 3 stars (actually I would like to give it 3 1/2 but that's not an option). The reason anyone buys a speaker of any sort is for sound quality. All the other features are just fluff. If you are expecting sound quality that rivals Bose, JBL, Harmon Kardon, etc etc, then you should pass this buy. For the price this costs, trust me, you can get a nice Bluetooth speaker that gives you the rich quality you're looking for. A few weeks ago I helped a friend buy and setup a little Bluetooth speaker inside his old pickup truck. He didn't want to spend a lot of money so we went to best buy and picked him up a small $19.99 speaker. I swear the quality on that speaker is the same as this one with the only difference being that this one will play at a higher volume (but not much higher). Lets just say that at max volume on my iphone and on this speaker, I still don't have to worry about disturbing my neighbors through the thin wall of my apartment building. The sound fills the room but it wont fill a room enough during a dinner party.bout disturbing my neighbors through the thin wall of my apartment building. The sound fills the room but it wont fill a room enough during a dinner party.

It took multiple attempts for the software to even recognize that the remote was connected. Once it was recognized, the interface is painful to use. The setup is a little time consuming under normal circumstances because you have to gather the model numbers of all the devices (TV, receiver, cable box, etc.) and then enter them in manually. Then you create activities using your devices such as watch TV or play Xbox, which requires you to assign the appropriate input settings for your TV and receiver, if you have one.

On the older harmony software, this was relatively simple but a little time consuming. On the new software, it is painful and unintuitive. I don't even know where to begin so I won't try but probably the most annoying aspect was that the software sometimes didn't respond and I wasn't sure if what I was clicking was actually clickable. The second most annoying thing was probably trying to get the remote to be recognized by the software.

product_title: KabelDirekt 1 x RCA Male to 1 x RCA Male Subwoofer / Digital Audio/ Video Cable - Pro Series
review_headline: KabelDirect cables disappoint. Can not recommend. Not as nice as the pictures
review_body:
Based on the positive reviews here I ordered a set of stereo and a single one to use powering my external 3 channel amp for fronts and center. Rears don't need that much attention.
After research, it proved more cost effective to add a good quality amplifier to a recent receiver than buying a powerful new receiver and still be limited to a maximum of 140-150 wpc.

I was using a set of 3 cables borrowed from my other stereo. (Monster Cable). These are no longer available. I looked in Amazon for something reasonable in a short a 3ft length to use. Both units are in a cabinet next to each other and there is a lot of wiring there, so right length helps. Therefore, I could plug my old 6ft cables back into the stereo equipment.

Shipping was fast and properly packed. That is where the fun stopped. The color coding is quite subtle and difficult to see from a distance. When looking at the back of a receiver, it would help a better way to visually see each channel by color. And the deal breaker was that they do not hold well to the RCA connectors in the back of the receiver. They would EASILY get disconnected and render the installation incomplete. If I pull the receiver forward, to check thing, it would loose grip and disconnect.
I ended up using a much better set of cables bought locally that have a significant difference in the hold.
For the great reviews I wonder that anybody else got any problems with this. I am using a Marantz receiver and an Anthem amplifier. Neither are cheap unit and both end would come loose if not careful.
Because they are inexpensive and not defective , I chose to keep them as shipping them back probably was 50% of the cost.
In summary, quite disappointed with these. I cannot recommend them. I wish Amazon had more choices in different price ranges to these RCA cables.

product_title: FiiO X5 High Resolution Lossless Music Player
review_headline: Brilliant Sound, Abysmal User Interface, Glitches Galore, Lack of phone customer support
review_body: UPDATE: ADDITIONAL PROBLEMS.  1. the player is displaying random freezes for no apparent reason. I have no idea why.   2. The player randomly disconnects the usb signal leading to a "drives disconnected unsafely" message.   I am not really sure how to solve these problems. I do not unplug the usb cable without ejecting the flash drives first. The freezes don't seem to have any precursor either.   I'm not sure what the cause of these problems are aside from poor design. This is the latest firmware, and a new version of this player is being released, so the player should work properly at this point.   2 PROBLEMS SOLVED!  1) how to update firmware. What will NOT work:  1. copying the zip file to your sd card does not work 2. copying the unzipped FOLDER to your sd card will not work  What DOES work: 1. copy the firmware file INSIDE the unzipped firmware folder directly onto your sd card.  2) How to use the USB DAC function on a MAC  1. set the usb setting to DAC, not storage 2. plug the usb cord into your computer 3. open the midi audio program. 4. WAIT several seconds until the X5 shows up in the midi audio list. 5. select x5 on the midi. 6. open sound in system preferences 7. select x5 in sound in system preferences 8. check to see if the x5 player shows the dac interface on the screen.  NOW, you are ready to use the x5 as a dac.  It took me hours of troubleshooting with the seller and manufacturer AND extensive trial and error on my part to get this nailed. Hopefully it saves some of you a bit of time. Best of luck.  The sound quality is absolutely top notch. There is absolutely no way a run of the mill "smart"phone can touch the Fiio's sound quality. Load just one lossless music file on this DAP, press play and you will be grinning from ear to ear. You will want to load your entire music library onto the player and listen in one night, one sitting.  Alas, no one and nothing is perfect. And here, the flaws show themselves with glaring brightness. ThisDAP is literally a tank of a player. It is far larger and heavier than any latest iteration smartphone. It is gargantuan compared to a sony DAP or a sansa clip. Despite the superior sound quality and even though this player is ostensibly designed to be a portable player, I can't imagine anyone looking forward to lugging this small brick (no pun intended or wanted) around.  The scroll wheel is just smh clunky. The clicks of the wheel do not correspond in any way to movement from one screen icon to the next. You move the wheel, the icons flash one to the next, in no particular order. Terribad.  Third, the installed firmware only allows a max of 5800 files. There's a firmware update you say? Good luck trying to install it. I have followed instructions to the 't' and it is impossible.  Same problems trying to install a driver for the DAC function.  As a minor nit to pick, yes, you will be picking quite a bit. A lot of dust that is, from the included silicone case. I think it's fantastic that fiio was thoughtful enough to include screen protectors and a silicone case. Having said that, I've never owned a silicone case which attracted as much lint as this case.  Drop this DAP into your pocket (yeah, right, as if you'd actually ever use this as a portable player), and it re-emerges as a furry, mammalian version of it's former self.  If you are looking for top notch sound quality at a reasonable price, look no further. This player absolutely rocks for sound quality.  If you actually want to USE IT, the UI, firmware quirks, installation problems and circa 2005 scrollwheel will frustrate you to no end.  The X5 is the hottest chick in town, but try to take her out dancing, and 9/10 times, she falls on her rear.  A remarkably frustrating user experience. Fiio is to be commended for it's sound quality, and condemned for it's abysmal user interface, and bottom of the barrel firmware updates.  edit: I'm in contact with fiio customer service. I will let you know if they have a fixfor me re: the firmware updates.  Unfortunately, I've discovered another bug: some of the tags are not identified properly by the player. For instance, if you check each sd card file, the song may show up, but it may not show in the list of albums or artists.  The bug list is very long, and it can test your patience if you consider a user friendly interface a priority.  Fiio is apparently trying to market this player as a very low cost player for the sound quality. However, they are taking massive shortcuts with the user interface.  Although you may not pay upfront in initial costs, you will pay down the road in dealing with bugs, customer service, and perhaps a series of frustrations with firmware. Caveat emptor.  edit 2: I am lowering my review rating to a single star. This is the single most non user friendly piece of electronics equipment I've ever used. Basically, fiio exploits their customers as beta testers: their products don't actually work properly: you. as a customer, are granted the rare privilege of sending fiio endless reams of feedback on how their products DO NOT work and fiio eventually sorts out the problems slowly through firmware updates, which in and of themselves are just as problematic as the glitches they are supposed to fix. Fiio is a joke.

review_body:
[[VIDEOID:84bb0714c8cb71a3269c22aa2c6eab2d]] [[VIDEOID:845811c48b90123c2e09962801c2f346]] I do not recommend this product. I wish I could've give it at least two stars, but it failed to serve its main purpose--that is, to play cassettes. The affordable price doesn't justify the unacceptable quality.

Had it worked, these things would've swayed me to recommend it:

- The headphones port is useful, and it works well, especially for a cassette player.
- The speaker is good and loud, especially for a device of this size and price. Noise level is decent or acceptable.
- The item comes with an AC cable (hidden in the battery pouch). I've bought electronics that didn't include a power cable.
- The automatic battery saver prevents the device from using battery power if the cable is plugged in.

There were just too many things that went wrong:

- The cassette player only worked the first couple of days for a combined 60 minutes of playtime.
- Now the play tempo is slow and erratic. Very rarely will it return to normal, and then quickly bounce back to the cumbersome pattern. This isn't suitable for playing music or speech. I've tried over 10 different tapes.
- Rewinding or forwarding a tape takes about just as long as playing it. (There's no automatic end-of-tape stop, but I wouldn't count that against an inexpensive cassette player.)
- The item is a cosmetic catastrophe. The imitative metallic finish gives it the appearance of an inexpensive toy, covered with scratches, cuffs, and blemishes that aren't signs of use, but signs of bad manufacturing. (The design is beautiful, but poorly implemented.)
- The radio receiver disappointed me, too. I get nothing in short wave, a poor signal if any in AM, and a few (but not by favorite) FM stations. My radio clock, which has no extensible antenna, receives a lot more stations in the same room.
- Again, the radio tuner adds to the misfortune. The display is too narrow and the turn is too fast to allow you to tune into a given frequency.

* * *

The device broke before I was able to try the microphone. The bottom line is: *Don't buy this product.*

product_title: Polk Audio UltraFit 2000 Headphones - Black
review_headline: Fragile cord failed on FOUR pairs
review_body: I bought my first pair of these in 2013.  Having tried many headphones in this style (several Sony models, Philips, Sennheiser) I found the Polk to have the best sound for me...good bass...clear treble...overall fairly flat response.  They really sound great.  The problem is that the cord on these became intermitant after a short time so that the left channel would drop out.  I contacted Polk, returned the headphones, and they sent me a second paid that lasted a good year or so before failing.  Frustrated I used some other brands for a while.  This year (2015)  I bought a new pair hoping they had addressed the cord issue, and right out the box the cord was bad.  Same problem as the first pair I bought in 2013, only now their tech support has gotten worse and they no longer reply to service requests in a timely manner.  The cord has a 90 degree plug and a very fragile flat cable that seems prone to breaking internally near the jack.  This seems like a manufacturing defect since both pairs I have bought have had the same issue.  I am very disappointed that they have not addressed it in recent years since the headphones themselves seem to be really well constructed and superior to most other brands.  They are also not inexpensive so they should have a good cord.    UPDATE: Polk finally replaced this set of headphones after several weeks.  The new pair worked for perhaps two months before developing the exact same failure in the cord.  This time the break is closer to the middle of the cord.  Mind you, I baby these headphones since this has happened before.  This now make FOUR pairs that have had the exact same defect (two pairs purchased, two pairs replaced by Polk), and I have downgraded my rating as a result.  It sounds like others have had the same issue, so shame on Polk for continuing to sell a product with a design flaw.  I sure won't be buying another pair.

product_title: Accell D080B-010K Travel Surge Protector with 612 Joules Dual USB Charging, 3 Outlets and Folding Plug
review_headline: A Practical Alternative to a Travel Surge Protector
review_body: This Travel Surge Protector will do the job for a number of people.  It appears to be well made, the A/C prongs fold into it in the rear, it weighs 1/2 lb., and comes in black or white.  However I returned it.  I find that a large number hotels do not have accessible duplex outlets where you can plug this in.  They are frequently behind headboards or other furniture.  Usually you will find a duplex in the bathroom which should accommodate this Surge Protector.  Some hotels have a desk with A/C outlets incorporated into a desk lamp.  Plugging this unit in may present a problem due to its bulk.  It is rather clunky, does not pack so easy (check the dimensions), and tends to be an eyesore.  At some airport terminals I have found so many charge devices plugged into the limited number of wall A/C duplexes that this unit would never fit.  If it works for you, great.  For under twenty bucks at Staples on-line I purchased an APC Surge Protector (Model P3U3) that includes 3 a/c outlets, 3 USB ports, a small form charging stand, 1080 Joules, Led Lights confirming a solid ground connection and whether or not the unit is working, and a 6' grounded plug and cable.  For me it packs flatter, yes it weighs one lb. but it protects all 3 a/c outlets and 3 USB ports.  Actually, the cable and grounded plug weigh more than the APC unit.  But it should plug into just about any grounded duplex receptacle or line tap that fellow airline travelers might have plugged into an existing Air Terminal Duplex.  I find the APC more practical and it certainly looks better, black or white.  What do I plug into it?  A Netbook (A/C), iPad Mini and iPhone (USB or A/C) and usually a couple of devices of my wife's.  For me the APC works much better.  It also can serve as a great desk or nightstand charging station of multiple devices.

product_title: Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style
review_headline: Loved them when I put them on, Returned them after I pressed play.
review_body:
Depending on what your looking to get from these headphones they can leave you satisfied or disappointed. For me I found these headphones to be a swing and a miss. I must say that I did not use these headphones for more than a few hours but I don't think using them any longer would have changed my opinions. I have previously used Bose headphones and I loved the AE2's but these don't provide that signature sound and I found that there are better alternatives on the market.

Personally I was looking for two things, great sound and comfort. I decided I loved these headphones as soon as I put them on, they were extremely lightweight and extremely comfortable. I have no doubt in my mind that these headphones would be comfortable to wear for a few hours at a time. The problem with these headphones I would not have expected from Bose; the sound was hollow and lifeless and not as clear as I expected. I'm no audio professional or audiophile but sound quality is one of the most important factors when spending even this much for a pair of headphones and I was extremely disappointed. There might as well have been a low pass filter inline with the cable because the mids and lows felt very under powered. Now I'm not the kind of person who likes base heavy music, but there just wasn't enough of a presence to supply what I felt like was a flat / even sound response. Another thing I immediately did not like about these was the clarity. These headphones do produce crisp sound but you can get such a cleaner and more distinguishable sound from other headphones on the market.

After only a half hour I decided to return these in favor of Audio Technica ath-m50x's becuase for me sound quality was the primary goal for these pair of headphones. If you are reading this article and you are looking to buy a pair of headphones with sound quality in mind I'd highly recommend checking out the m50's or m50x's you can get much better sound quality for around the sameprice, or even the Sony MDR 7506 or V6 which cost much less.

Unless Comfort is the the single most important factor you are looking for, I would not recommend these headphones. If you are taking the time to read reviews already, look at the head-fi forums for more experienced opinions. You will learn everything you need to know to make the right purchase. I doubt it will be these.

GOOD: If you are already part of Apple's consumer universe, I'd say go for it. Mechanically, my Waterproof iPod works fine.

BAD: If you are NOT experienced with Apple's closed consumer model, I would suggest other swim mp3 players are easier and cheaper.

On other MP3 players, you add songs (in my case podcasts) by dragging them from your computer to the device. 10 seconds. Easy peasy. Apple's iPod loads files only through a program called iTunes, and as far as I can tell you can't just copy files from your computer to the player, you have to buy the music, or find the podcast, at Apple's online iStore. Then you don't just copy the file, you "synch" your computer with your player. And iTunes is set to synch not the files you want to move, but every MP3 file on your computer. There is no doubt a good reason for this, and it no doubt all makes sense to people who have it figured it out. I don't WANT to figure it out. I just want to drag 4 fricking files from one device to another.

Also, you can't sign in to iTunes --i.e. can't put any mp3 files on your iPod-- without creating an Apple Account, and giving Apple your email (they check), date of birth, and CREDIT CARD info. Why do I need to give them that personal info, just to put files on MY mp3 player? Creepy.

Again, all this WORKS. But why bother? For 1/3 the price you can get a Diver Waterproof MP3 Player here at Amazon, and quickly drag your files where you want them.

product_title: JBL Synchros 400BT Bluetooth Wireless On-Ear Stereo Headphones
review_headline: Better than the other JBL BT Headphones, but way too overpriced.
review_body: [EDIT: Happy New Year!!!]    I've compared many BT Headphones for weeks (if you want a list, write me a comment), most of them side by side.  I am not going to speak of my personal tastes, which are not important in a review. I will only talk of objective sound quality.  Something that after comparing so many headphones, you can judge a bit better.    I actually have tested all JBL BT Headphones.  These S400 are the only ones with sound quality.  The E40 and E50 have decent sound quality but mediocre detail and (specially for the E40) lack of bass.  The J56 is like the E50 but with more bass, unfortunately dull and of low quality detail.  In comparison, these S400 are more exciting, with good dynamic, strong bass of good (but not excellent) quality, good highs and decent mids. And with overall a good sound quality with decent detail.  The Soundstage is just mediocre.    The comfort is, complicated. They are not uncomfortable. The pads are soft. But all JBL BT Headphones have something strange in common, and these too: their speaker do not move (or not enough) to adapt to the form of head and ears, and so the bottom of the speakers do not touch the ears, which feels strange, and leaks sound.  To be honest, in the S400 this problem is minimal, compared to the other JBL Headphones. But is still present.    Another problem is that their touch controls are a bit oversensitive.  I did not have so many problems as many other reviewers had (and as a friend of mine also had). But, it also happened to me that with only putting my hand close to the headphones or move/adjust it a bit to my head, the controls changed track or paused the music.  Other people had even the problem that the headphones made a call...  When I was reading the other reviews I thought \\"nah, impossible. I want to try by myself\\".  Unfortunately they are right. It IS true. The controls are too sensitive.    And then the price.  Part of the review is also the price. One must consider all, sound, functions, design, comfort, and price.  In few words, there are much better BT Headphones for less money.  So, although these S400 ARE good, they are NOT so good to be sold at $270. EVER.  You can buy them if you really need or want a JBL Headphone.  But they are not much better than the Supertooth Freedom, which also have touch control (which are not oversensitive) and are much cheaper.  They also are not much better than the Jabra Revo Wireless, which have better Touch controls and cost the HALF.  They are not better AT ALL than the Samsung Level over, which lack a bit bass but this can be improved with some EQ. The Samsung cost the same and offer much better sound quality and more functions, including a very good active noise cancelling. And MUCH better touch controls, and MUCH better comfort.    For all these reasons, I would give the S400 3.5 stars, but I cannot, so I give them 3 stars, because they do not deserve 4 stars.    A short note about voting a review up or down: if you have a different opinion you do not need to vote mine down, you just can express yours in your review.  It is important to have different reviews from different people with different tastes and opinions.  Votes are for if a review is useful. And a review is useful when the reviewer explain in detail what he thinks of the product and why. No matter if you agree with his opinion or not.  I have spent LOT of time in comparing headphones and writing reviews, and although I had fun while doing it, I didn't do it for fun, I did it to help people, including you.  I would also be happy to give you more suggestions if you write me in the comments. In that case please specify which music do you listen most, and what do you want from a Headphone.    I hope this was helpful!

product_title: CyberPower PFC Compatible Pure Sine Wave Tower UPS
review_headline: Be careful: may not be pure sine wave output.
review_body:
Be warned: although this is advertized as a "pure sine wave" output UPS, the unit I received was NOT pure sine wave though it was the correct model number. I'm not sure if they are all like this or maybe I just received an "old stock" product, but the box and instruction manual I received clearly stated it uses "adaptive sine wave" technology which is NOT pure sine wave.

I called CyberPower and they said it was just marketing terms, but then I read the original CyberPower press release which clearly stated that adaptive sine wave technology was a cheaper alternative to pure sine wave, and it uses a triangular wave instead of a true pure sine wave.

Now, for most people the adaptive sine wave technology this product uses is fine. It WILL work with active PFC power supplies. That said, if you really need pure since wave output then this is NOT the unit for you.

Also, my unit does not advertize "line interactive" AVR, just AVR, so again I don't know if this is just the way they printed the instruction manual or if I got an older unit with older features because line interactive AVR is able to stabilize voltage without using the battery which is a great feature.

I gave it three stars because it was not Amazon's fault (CyberPower themselves are falsely advertizing the product, not Amazon) and Amazon was very helpful with their customer service (since this is not a returnable item, we had to work something out).

Again, I might have received an older unit and maybe the new ones DO use "pure sine wave" output, however the unit I received uses "adaptive sine wave" output which is similar to, but not the same as the advertized "pure" sine wave output. If you really do need pure sine wave backup power, I suggest testing whatever unit you receive with an oscilloscope before hooking up your equipment. This unit is fine for active PFC power supplies because they don't really need pure sine wave output, adaptive triangular output is good enough, but some equipment DOES need true pure sine wave output.

Let me say again, this is not Amazon's fault and Amazon was very friendly and took care of my problem quickly.

review_headline: Worst speaker ever -- company offers free product in exchange for reviews ...
review_body:
This is the worst portable speaker I have ever had and no, my unit isn't faulty -- it's just a dreadful product. The company sends out letters stating they will send you a free product if you write a review (I'm receiving at least three email nags per week), hence the masses of reviews on Amazon. I had a coupon and only paid $10 for it. It wasn't worth $5.
The battery is terrible and I use the audio cable, not the blue tooth. It's dead in a couple of hours and the increase in volume is negligible. Stick your phone in a coffee can and you'll get better amplification. There are so many good options out there in the $20-$25 range. I have a round portable speaker smaller than this one from a company called Home. It's not blue tooth, granted, but it's really loud and two years after I bought it the sound still isn't distorted. It charges to full in about 90 minutes and the charge lasts over 12 hours.
No doubt this speaker has more functions, but I didn't buy it for the radio or because you can play music directly off a smart card. The only thing good I have to say about The Adfilic is that even in black it's adorable and the build quality and design of the case give it an expensive look.
So Adfilic -- you wanted a review. No need to bother with the free product. Just take me off your spam list.

It sounded a bit thin and lacking in detail in the mid to low range in pop and rock songs. But after a while, I realized this was partly due to the type of music I was listening to. Once I switched over to higher/lighter vocal types (on lighter instrumental tracks) and classical music, the headphones performed. They handle higher ranges better and quite clearly. They can "lift" crisper vocals. Despite the muddier mid range, these are definitely worth the $15 and perform better than most headphones and earbuds I get in this price range.

I guess if you're into rap or RnB, these headphones aren't going to impress you. They don't fail but there are plenty of better choices for those music styles. I also didn't appreciate the lack of definition and boxy sense of space it expressed in electronic music. Overall it's weak in very busy and loud music styles.

product_title: eXtreme Bluetooth Shower Speaker, 5W Portable Waterproof Speaker Also Ideal for Outdoors
review_headline: Update: OMG, this thing should not be sold as waterproof!
review_body:
Update 9 May 2015 - Speaker died due to water intrusion
Well, it's dead already. One day the Volume Up/Track Advance button stuck "on" at which point it was impossible to turn off the speaker. It just kept beeping over and over. At that point my choices were disassembly or to bury it in a pit and wait for the battery to run down. I chose disassembly and was shocked at what I found. This speaker is at best splash resistant, and not very good even for that. The claim of "waterproof" is unrealistic at best. Around the side of the speaker is a wide band of rubber, below which are the controls. This band is held in place by friction and tension only. No glue, no O-rings, just tension.

This would not be an issue except that below the band, the speaker enclosure has four large holes. In fact, the speaker enclosure cutaways are shaped to allow the enclosure itself to flex to activate the buttons inside. So any water that gets under that band will be inside the speaker. There are no O-rings, no tongue and groove fittings on the case elements, just gaping holes. Which is why when I opened it up I was able to shake out a tablespoon or so of water.

This speaker is unfit for purpose. If you need something waterproof, or even just water or splash resistant, look elsewhere.

Original review...
This is a good little speaker. For purposes of comparison, I also use a Monster Clarity and until recently a Boom Urchin. This speaker has plenty of volume in the mid and top end but very little bass. What sound it does put out is clear, even at higher volumes but I could never give it 5 stars without more low end. It has a few other issues for which I kicked an additional star.

When turning the unit on or off, a voice announces "POWER ON" or "POWER OFF" and the all caps here is intended to indicate the volume at which these announcements are made. There is at least one other function that generates an announcement, that of setting the device to pairing mode.

A design issue for me is the positioning of the controls. The speaker is about 3 inches in diameter and the controls are large buttons along the outer rim. At the top is a plastic loop for hanging the speaker. To the right and left of that at approximately 10 and 2 o'clock are two buttons that do double-duty for volume up/down and track forward/back. At 180 degrees opposite of these at 4 and 8 are the buttons for power and start/stop/phone. There are three hand-hold areas at 3, 6, and 9 o'clock.

The problem this causes is that it is almost impossible to handle the device without hitting the buttons. If you consistently remember to grab at 3 and 9, it's possible. The result is that I am constantly advancing or replaying tracks, turning the speaker of or on unexpectedly, and so forth. But in the event that I want to intentionally adjust it, the buttons are poorly placed for that as well. For example, the 10 o'clock button goes back a track if pressed quickly. To adjust the volume requires holding it down. But the force to hold it down requires two fingers and the second one ends up on the power button. In fact, all of the buttons have a counterpart at exactly 180 degrees that you *will* hit when attempting any "hold down" function. This is how I discovered pairing mode whilst attempting to adjust the volume.

Finally, there is a slight issue with the suction cup on the back of the speaker. Every other suction-cup equipped device I have was designed with a small tab at the edge to lift the suction cup off. This speaker's suction cup lacks a tab and since the suction cup is a tad smaller in diameter than the speaker, it is necessary to wedge one's fingers between the speaker and the window/wall/whatever in order to break the suction and dismount the speaker. Since I have large hands and have to force the speaker out a bit to do this, I expect the suction cup to break off at the center mount point any day now.

My suggestions for Mooitech:
* Make the buttons a tad smaller and relocate them so they are not at 180 degrees from each other.
* Add a tab to the suction cup.
* Allow disabling or volume adjustment of the announcements.
* Do what you can to improve the bass. I realize it's a small speaker but at low volumes it would be possible to adjust the frequency response curve to get more bass.

Overall, I'm happy with the speaker for the price and believe Mooitech can improve the design in a future version. review_headline: Be aware of the 2000 file limit !
review_body: The previous reviews are accurate, it sounds pretty good, it refreshes quicker after adding or removing data, its easy to navigate, and its light and compact with better battery life. That being said, if has a major flaw that all should be aware of, it is not advertised or written into the specs, but it will not display any more than 2000 files in its menu system, you can load more than 2000 files into its 8GB of memory and see them with a computer, but the menu system will not see or display all of them so you will not be able to select or play the extras over the 2000.  After two weeks of fighting with this issue, and many phone calls to SanDisk (in not so helpful, and ignorant of the products capabilities and limits, India) someone in India either tested it, or was told by an informed manager to call me back and tell me that it will not hold anymore than 2000 files on its internal memory, they went on to say that if I used an external SD Card that it too would only hold 2000 files visible, so if you intend to buy this and add a 32GB card to load up several thousand WMA's or MP3's you will be horribly disappointed. I hit the 2000 limit at 4.9GB leaving the remaining 3.1 GB unusable for music, my only option at this point is to add a 4GB card for another 2000 files of storage. I even went into all of the folders and removed the hidden files and cover art to lower the file count. There is no workaround yet.  Again, the unit works fine, and is a very good value at under $40, and I will definitely use it, but if I knew of the file limit before I purchased it I might have just made due with my older 4GB SanDisk M260 unit I have used for many years. If they issue a firmware update that fixes this limitation I would be happy to award it with 5 stars for it's quality, value, and performance.

product_title: SOL REPUBLIC  Wireless Bluetooth Speaker
review_headline: Updated review:  Originally a 5 Star Review.
review_body:
I'm quite surprised how well this little speaker lives up to expectations. The whole package is well designed and smartly executed. It looks like a nice expensive electronic gift from the wrapper all the way down to the unit.

The sound quality is good - for a small speaker. You can't expect big hardware sound out of a small box like this. But it is good sound and is loud enough for a small setting. You can get it pretty loud before you sacrifice sound quality too much. The real bonuses of this speaker is it's Bluetooth connectivity and its easy mobility. The wireless range is pretty good with line of sight increasing it significantly.

Sol Republic wants you to go out in the world and explore with this speaker there to play your personal soundtrack. It has a 1/4 inch threaded hole in the back where you can mount it to the frame of your bike, or on the camera mount of your choice. I have no doubt that this self contained little unit is water, dust and shock resistant, just as claimed. All the button are pressure buttons that are mounted under a membrane that covers the entire unit. This skin-like membrane is flexible and thick enough to keep out a significant bit of moisture. I wouldn't want to submerge it.

Excellent gift idea.

review_headline: we ask if the unit we would get would be just like photos and if ours would have all Nichicon KZ ...
review_body:
I don't know where to start...

Pros: Solid exterior construction and buttons. Sounds decent (not outstanding). The price is right.

Cons: Tried communicating with seller before sale. No responses and we needed the unit. After placing the order and sending another email, we ask if the unit we would get would be just like photos and if ours would have all Nichicon KZ audio capacitors. A guy replied saying yes but they would be the middle grade KG series.

Received the unit directly from China in about 2~3 weeks. Immediately noticed they sent the optical out only, not with the RCA outs as ordered and shown. Also could not confirm the DAC version chip. The outside says Breeze Audio as does the "menu". There is no menu just a start screen that says Breeze Audio. They also sent us a 220v version which we did not order.

Contacted the seller via Amazon messaging and email, and went thru a 2 week battle of their not understanding half what was being written or said, as they seem to only use Google translate or another translator. Their emails in broken translated from Chinese to English was really bad. Horrible.

Finally got them to realize we wanted the better DAC chip, 110v, the best Nichion KZ caps, and the RCA outs. One email stated it was no problem (they would not admit fault) and if we were good at DIY they would just send us a new board to internally solder and wire in. Waited another 2 weeks.

Received the "new board" and took the cover off. The unit they first sent had two boards in it; the main board was completely empty. Let us state that again. IT HAD NO COMPONENTS ON IT AT ALL (no capacitors, resistors, transistors, DAC chip). Completely empty blank main board. We emailed they for a explanation and they would not answer why. Nor why ours says Breeze Audio all over it.

New board did not contain the best Nichicon KZ or KG series audio capacitors. It was a mixedbatch of different brands. Their explanation was "whatever was in the warehouse". At this point this was about the 5th deception and lie.

Continuing to work with a Noobsound rep named "Vivian" vial email. It was a simple process to disassemble the whole unit and put in the new board and change the voltage to 110v.

Using the unit with 24/96 hi def flac music files works ok via a USB thumb drive. Unit hangs and locks up at times merely trying to read the different music files and folders at times, and no matter what you try it always says it is recognizing the SD card reader not the USB input. Will ONLY work if USB thumb drive is formatted in FAT32. There is no menu, options, or operating/users manual. All you can do is increase/decrease the output volume and move between folders and tracks.

Unit gets really hot; there in no ventilation at all. Heavy aluminum or metal case.

They sent us two remotes; one a old version and one a smaller new version. All they can do is change volume and change between folders and tracks as stated.

The photos posted by seller are completely deceiving. You do not know what youre going to get.

product_title: Crosley CR8005D-BK Cruiser Deluxe Portable 3-Speed Turntable with Bluetooth, Black
review_body:
Okay. So my record player that I've had for about a year had recently started playing vinyls slower. I instantly started to browse the web for a new and affordable record player. I found this and was interested in its low price. I did some digging through reviews and decided I had better find a different player.

While my parents were out today, they found this at the store for the same price as online. I asked them to buy it. I was so excited for them to bring it home so I could finally play some of the vinyls I got as gifts. I thought that it couldn't be as bad as people said. I was waaay wrong.

So I open this thing up, plug it in, and hook it up to some speakers. I put a record on and started to play it. The first time I use the thing, its already playing slower than my old one. So I figure I'll let it spin without a record on it for a little and see if that fixes the problem. It did end up fixing the problem for a little while, but there are still so many more problems.

This record player has a major design flaw. The lid does not go back enough. My records ended up rubbing on the bottom of the lid. This is awful. How are you going to put out a product that could ruin what its made to play? Crosley really needs to do some work.

This record player also skips a lot. Yes, it can be fixed with tape and a coin, but that's beside the point. I want a quality product, not something that I need to modify at all.

Finally, this is what made me box it up. Everything else I could deal with, but this drove me crazy in less than 5 minutes, The record player does not maintain proper speed. It weaves in and out of going to slow and going to fast. Its ridiculous. One moment it sounds fine and the next it sounds to fast or too slow.

If you want a quality record player, don't buy this. This is garbage and a complete waste of money. If you have any suggestions for a decent, affordable record player, please let me know.

review_headline: Energy Use Monitor lacks features that would make it a winner in my eyes.
review_body:
I am totally unimpressed with the Belkin Energy Use Monitor. It is cute, but lacks some of the features that would make it truly useful.

First, the design is poor in that it doesn't sit flat in a readable position unless it rests on a back piece where the cable comes out. It doesn't rest on the cable if it's a hard surface, but it's close enough to that and I see no advantage to the otherwise odd shape of the device.

Second, it seems to provide an immediate measurement that updates a little more often than once per second on the wattage. It does compute what the cost and CO2 impact is on an annual basis from those momentary measurements, but you can't get any sort of cumulative kilowatt number or a graph of usage over time. The dollars measurement is useful if you update the cost of energy to match what you're paying, but the CO2 emissions number seems just to be an attempt to interest the rabidly green in this device. Let's not delve into politics here, but if you know the kilowatt hour usage of a device, those other numbers can be computed for those who want them.

Third, if you unplug the Belkin from the wall, all the cumulative numbers reset. They don't reset if you unplug a device and then plug something else in. Make sure you fully unplug everything if you decide to measure a different electrical device. If you unplug a device or turn it off, the Belkin display reverts to saying that you're using less than half a watt and you can no longer access either of the cumulative measurements until you plug something back in and power it on.

On the up side, the screen is on an approximately five foot cord so you don't have to stick your face down to the outlet to read it like on our other device. That device did, however, have a memory that allowed you to read data after the fact.

In today's age, I expect this device to at least store data over time on an internal memory card that can be downloaded via USB. A premium model might be Bluetooth capable and have apps to collect that data wirelessly. This device doesn't do enough for the cost to earn my recommendation.m model might be Bluetooth capable and have apps to collect that data wirelessly. review_headline: Good protector, somewhat bulky and needs a lot of space behind furniture
review_body:
This review is for 2.1A (10-watt) protector.
While it is advertised as a travel protector/USB charger, I guess many people use it at home.
Here is my impression of this product:
Pros:
- It is a solid construction
- Has 2.1A USB charger which allows fast charging for iPad, large smart phones etc.
- Has swivel power plug to allow turing it 90 degrees.
Cons:
- When you plug it into a wall socket, the other end is somewhat loose as it has 1/4" gap to the wall, so it would be nice if the other end has small raised area that would actually touch the wall. With that design, the protector would not bend when you try to plug something into it.
- If you keep this protector behind a furniture, it would be nice that 110V plugs are actually on top (or side) so that they use minimal space behind the furniture. As it is designed now, you need space about 4 inches or so for the protector itself and the actual plug/cable from the electric device (for example, a lamp on the bedside drawer).
It is interesting that some other cheaper protectors like http://smile.amazon.com/dp/B00EYCEZLA TRIPP LITE actually provide two 110V plugs - one on each side. I think the Belkin has a higher quality device and it would be good if they make some design changes for this product, or make a new compact space saving protector.

This is why I it should have twice the Strength of the 2V. But instead got less channels.

Not sure why people dont like the review? Please tell me what I need to add for you. Basicallly this is TWO 2V's put together, so why does it only work 1/2 as well?

review_headline: P7's not all they are cracked up to be - at least for me
review_body: I am a minority here, but I can only report what I hear. Many of the very positive reivews refer to the fact that the P7's are NOT flat - boosted bass, boosted treble. But they still love 'em. For me its a deal breaker. They ARE seductive. VERY smooth compared to my Grado SR80's for example.  and on some music that works. But they are WRONG and I hear it in a not pleasant way too often. Piano gets tipped up to the clinkier part of the sound but leaves a hole or a bit of emptiness a long way down till you reach its lower bass notes. The bass boost sometimes covers it sometimes doesn't.  The Grado's on the other hand, while less refined, are more honest - accurate octave to octave and piano sounds like ....piano with the right weight in the right places. The bass and treble boost on the P7's work better on my 128k mp3 files than my 44k or hi-rez ones. Adds some sparkle and life where it might be missing. But that's a net negative on higher quality recordings that don't need to "put anything back in" - its already there. The hi boost also tends move voices and instruments "into each other," you loose the space between instruments and voices as if one starts right where the other leaves ends. With the grado's there is more space between each performer or instrument. Not that the P7 isn't clean and clear, they are, but they are not "right", and that for me just is fatiguing.  I wanted an upgrade from my 20 yr old Grado's - these won't be them. And I've gained a new found respect for just how good these slightly over $100 Grado's are.  Most listening was done off a SONY HAP Ze1S, a totally excellent digital media play back machine and with a tubed head amp. I also used the P7's on my Marantz 5.1 digital surround amp listening to cable classical.  Similar results. So the stars reflect that this is a sophisticated tool but that at their price, they should have been more accurate. (in my opinion)

review_headline: Worked for about 2-3 days at shutting off the "energy saving ports." Then stopped working.
review_body:
This worked for about 2 days, then stopped working to shut off all of the "energy saver ports."

I have my HTPC connected in the master port, and all of my external hard drives plugged into the "energy saver ports." My plan was when I would shut down the PC, the external hard drives would shut off as well so I wouldnt have to switch off 5 of them each time my computer shuts off.

This failed to work as planned after 3 days. When I shut down the computer, the "energy saver ports stopped working." I even tried rotating the adjustment dial all into every position, but this did not fix it either.

I then tried plugging in one of my external hard drives into the master port (this drive shuts off automatically once the PC is shut down) and this still did not shut off the "energy saving ports" even with the dial tried in multiple locations. I tried this method thinking that an individual hard drive would pull less "standby current" as a PC would, and could possibly trigger the device to shut off the other ports.. This did not work either.

Now I have an over-priced power strip. This makes me hesitant to try to purchase something like this online again since returning stuff purchased online is usually a lose-lose situation.

product_title: Fixed Frame Projection Screen
review_headline: Be prepared for a less than stellar product, especially if it is missing parts since the phone support wont be able to assist.
review_body:
I purchased this product because it was supposed to be high quality, pre-built and all I had to do was assemble.
I ran into several problems right off the bat.
I called the tech support # on the outside of the box as it said should I run into issues.
The gentleman who answered was courteous but of no help.
When I told him things were missing & other items did not align he said that it happens sometimes and there was nothing he could do on the phone. I would have to go online to their page to fill out a warranty claim. I was not happy & indicated I expected better for a $350 item bought brand new & indicated I felt I should not have to jump through the extra hoops to get this working. He down played it by saying "its not an extra hoop to jump through. It is simple & you will be done in 5 minutes or less".
Needless to say, now that I am on their page it is not 5 minutes or less. It was the model, serial, proof of purchase & that's just as far as I got before coming over here to post my experience.
Here is a list of what I have issue with.
#1 The person answering the user call support line should not down play the required online experience to get parts shipped out to fix the issue.
#2 Why did the label say to call for support if the person on the phone cannot actually support me; why not just say for parts go to xxx to fill out a claim?
#3 The 4 corner brackets holes did not align with the pre-drilled holes in the frame.
#4 The single vertical back brace & its 2 accompanying plastic ends (one of the last pieces to do during assembly) are missing.
#5 There are 4 missing clips to pull the screen cloth taught to the frame assembly. There are marks on the frame all around it that indicate where clips are supposed to go. Mine is 4 clips short.

I could have built my own screen for less $ while making sure I had all the required parts.
All in all I would not recommend this product & will not makefurther purchases based on the tech support (lack there of) I experienced.
I understand from time to time parts go missing but to tell me to call for support then have that person tell me they cant assist me & I am making a big deal of the process of getting the missing parts is not a smart process.

product_title: StarTech.com 2m 4 Position TRRS Headset Extension Cable
review_headline: OK For the Price, Cable Has ZERO Shielding (literally)
review_body:
I bought this as part of a project to add AUX input to the ISO connector in the back of a stock car radio. The first order of business was to chop off the female end and strip a couple of inches off of the outer jacket to get access to the 4 conductors. The cable went straight into the trash after this because there is NO shielding around the signal cables. None, whatsoever.

I still give this 3 stars because the price is super low and the cable should be fine if it is used indoors and away from any EMI sources. However, anyone that is looking to use this in an automotive environment should look elsewhere, because this product is NOT suitable for use in a car. An unshielded cable is almost guaranteed to pick up ignition noise when used in a car, particularly if it is run inside the dash or under the carpet, adjacent to factory wiring harnesses.

product_title: #1 Best Bluetooth Shower Speaker, 100% Waterproof & Dustproof â€” Portable & Wireless â€” A Top Model for Indoors or Outdoors, Beach or Pool â€” Compatible with Mobile, Tablet, PC + more â€” One Year Warranty
review_body:
I recently tried a Mooietech shower speaker and discovered it wasn't sealed at all. This one by comparison is tight as a drum. I haven't disassembled it but all the exposed seams are joined by four screws. In other good news, the speaker stands off far enough to make lifting the suction cup off the glass easy. The rear-firing speaker keeps the worst of the shower spray from waterlogging the sound.

And that's about where the good points end for me. The charging cable has USB on one end and 1/8 audio jack on the other end. Although this may make it easier to waterproof the charging port, which appears to be the most vulnerable point on this device for water intrusion, it also means that if you lose or wear out the cable you are out of luck. I absolutely hate non-standard charging cables. Anyone who insists on using non-standard cables should provide a spare with the initial purchase.

Also, the volume up/down functions share buttons with the track back/forward functions. This is normal for the other speakers I've tried, except that on this device the volume up/down are reversed. On every other device I've tried, volume down is paired with track back and volume up is paired with track advance. On this one track back is on the left but is paired with volume *up* instead of down. Track advance is paired with volume *down*. This drove me nuts.

All of these issues would be mere annoyances if it wasn't for the deal breaker - this speaker is all treble and no bass. I don't mean "all treble" comparable to all the other palm speakers I've tried. After all, it is a little palm speaker and you can't expect studio quality sound here. When I say "all treble" I mean that I fully expect dogs half a mile away to be covering their ears and saying "make it stop!" I mean "all treble" in the sense that if I turned it up all the way, I'd expect all the glass in the bathroom to shatter. My Galaxy S5 is waterproof and if it put out more volume I'd use it in the shower instead of this speaker.

In terms of sound and performance, my favorite wet speaker was the Urchin Boom which unfortunately died after a year due to water intrusion. It was big and heavy but it sounded great. On disassembly I saw that it was sealed with sticky goop which I suppose dried up after a while. The Mooietech speaker was OK until it also died of water intrusion, but after only a month. On disassembly, I saw that it was sealed only with a wide band of rubber that covered holes leading to the innards of the device, and not even glued on. The Joshal speaker appears to be sealed the best of the bunch and may last years. But it has the worst sound of anything I've tried so however long it actually lasts will *seem* like forever.

Time to go test something else.roof and if it put out more volume I'd use it in the shower instead of this speaker.

review_headline: 500 file Audible limit.  No Updates from Sandisk.  Apparently an abandoned product.  Dont invest in this, Sandisk isnt.
review_body: Use clip+ mainly for audible extensively.  Have 200-300 audio books in 605 parts or files. Looked at all available info on jam to see if it may be ok to use as a replacement for my aging clip+'s.  All I found was '2000 file limit for songs and books' so I took a chance.  Plugged in my micro sd and it was able to read it, but info said only 500 books instead of the 605 on it.  Apparently a 500 book limit that Sandisk fails to mention.  -edited-after using Jam the improvement on the time it takes to refresh, less than a minute vs 30 to 45 minutes for the clip+ should allow me to live within the 500 file limit and not make me feel like I need my whole library.  I can split it up with smaller cards now.  Also I had problems activating with Audible, as many are.  I was lucky and found a way to activate mine, but Sandisk says this issue is resolved now.  The improvement in battery life vs the clip+ is real.  I do not use mine for mp3 so I can't verify the 18 hours that is specified,  But I have measured both the clip+ and now the Jam and the Jam lasted 3 hours longer than any of the clip+'s I have owned playing Audible files.  To me to be able to purchase a NEW replacement for my clip+ players and get good battery life and quick refresh is well worth it.  I have seen minor glitches with the Jam that I expect Sandisk to correct over time with firmware updates, as they did with the clip+.  Therefore I am bumping my review up to 4 stars, as it is usable for me, and I am happy with the Jam.  I will buy more.  Update-7/31 Listened to one book, swapped to a bigger device that supports bluetooth and gigs of storage for books.  will never use the jam or buy more unless an upgrade expands the device to 2015 levels instead of 2008 levels, but by then I will have spare bigger devices so this will end up in the junk pile.  goodby sandisk.  Update-1/26/16 Pulled out of junk pile.  Checked to download new firmware release.  No new firmware release since product was released last spring, though numerous opportunities to improve the product exist.  Apparently Sandisk doesnt see this as something they want to invest in, and you shouldnt either.  Changed to one star and putting back in junk pile.

product_title: BNC Male Compression Coax Connectors RG59 Pack of 20 Pcs by Cablesdirect
review_body:
Not very rugged. If you jostle the connector once its connected with a cable the BNC end may become separated from the body of the connector. This happened on 2 cables out of 8 when I connected them. I could put them back together but I'm not impressed. The center pin doesn't crimp and is held in place by friction. It's OK but a more robust connector is suggested if you want to move the cables around very much. Since I'm installing the cameras for keeps and the BNC ends will never move, I'm thinking I'll be OK. If not, I'll replace with another type. If you're a pro, and you want to make your customer happy, spend a few extra bucks on a crimped center pin BNC connector and a good crimping tool.
You could possibly solder the center pin to the center of the coax if you're an expert. Foam core cables make this hard to do (they kind of evaporate when heated). If you're going to this much trouble, I'd suggest looking for a better connector. You paid for new coax and a DC feed line, drop another 3 bucks a connector on a pro product.

product_title: Kanto OASIS Tempered Glass Shelves
review_body:
I will briefly review the stand overall, but my main goal is to share additional measurement info because it's home theater, and a couple inches can really matter for your components...

The stand:
- Build Quality: Acceptable, but not impressive. It will look nice in the room, but under scrutiny you can tell it's not high-quality furniture. The wooden end pieces are hollow, and I can see small gaps in their black treatment that show through. Do not overtighten anything! The anchors you are threading into are just little inserts in the porous, weak, hollow wood - they can be easily stripped from the wood and ruined. Snug is fine, strength will come from the completed structure. (3/5)

- Assembly: No damaged or missing parts on arrival. Parts are well labeled, but instructions are not foolproof. The orientation of the end pieces and the shelves matter, and the diagrams change perspective from step to step. At the beginning of each step, be sure to correctly identify both the TOP/BOTTOM and FRONT/BACK orientation before starting. I consider myself at least average at assembling this type of thing, and I got it wrong the first time. (4/5)

- Value: This is pretty much the only TV stand with a mount that I could find that was rated for a 70" TV. If you're putting up something that is 60" or smaller, you probably have other options for less money. If you're thinking 65" or 70" but don't want it on the wall... this is one of your only options, and it's a decent one. (4/5)

Detailed Measurements:
The glass shelves are the useable space for components, speakers, etc. Consider the wooden end pieces decorative.

- Bottom and Middle shelf interior dimensions: 42" W x 7" H x 16.5" D (if you move the middle shelf up or down from center, you get one shelf at 5.75" H and the other at 8.25" H)

- Top surface glass: 42" W x 17.5" D. Beware that the TV mount pillar comes up the back of the unit, and at the top of that pillar the mounting bracket hangs forward several inches toward the viewing position. The part of the bracket that touches the back of your TV is 5.5" closer to the viewer than the back edge of the TV stand is. In other words, mount your TV high enough to clear any speaker you put on the top surface glass, or plan on 17.5" D - 5.5" bracket - TV depth = remaining space for speaker.

- Highest mount option: this stand can put the upper two mount holes on the back of your TV up to 52.5" above the ground. This highest setting puts the highest mounting holes on the bracket 33" from the top surface glass.

Hope those details help, they are the measurements I wanted to know before purchasing, but couldn't find online!

review_body:
BEWARE: These headphones are very "colored." Some people like (adjust?) to this presentation of sound, but personally I found it LACKING CLARITY, muddy, and uninspiring.

If you like to listen to "flat-ish" / "analytical" headphones, these are not the headphones for you. Better choices are Harman Kardon CL, Sennheiser HD 280 Pro, AKG K550.
