product_title: Sennheiser Adidas Sports In-Ear Neckband Headphones - Black
review_headline: A disappointment but they're still better than most things
review_body:
I was terribly disappointed when I originally tried these headphones. I used to wear the PMX 680, but once that model was discontinued I decided not to spend an arm and a leg holding onto the past. Eventually I knew I would be unable to find new pairs of the 680 and now that my husband has resorted to buying a pair of the 685i, I'm guessing that time has come.

Here are the issues I had with the 685i. The controller is obnoxious. I got over it and I wear it during my workouts but I terribly miss the 680 option to remove that useless piece of junk. The cord is now unalterably long. In the previous version, you could use an attachment to adjust the length of the cord, but this cord is just ridiculouslessly long for sports use (unless your sport is bobsledding and the guy behind you is holding the iPod). When I first ran with these headphones, I tried securing the long cord to my armband and I tried wrapping the cord around my fanny pack strap to keep the cord from hanging wildly, but then the tension in the cord caused the control to smack me the in the face rhythmically as I ran.
Now I find myself either holding placing my iPod on my treadmill or holding the iPod (fun!) and the swinging controller no longer smacks me in the face. I usually forget about my issues with the device unless it's a particular night where our home treadmill zaps the headphones intermittently as that long ass cord swings back and forth across the treadmill display. At least it keeps my mind from wandering!

There are some positive things about the headphones. They are incredibly light, so much that I hardly feel them against my head (lighter than the 680) and the earbuds are smaller (probably more compatible with generic earbud covers). I like the color and once in a blue moon I feel like using the controller. The major wtf I can't quite figure out is why they seemed to take the reflective markers off the back of this model. It is a sports headphone, no? I thought that was a cool if not obviously necessary feature of the PMX 680.

Anyway, I have used this for so long I may have headphone Stockholm Syndrome, but I generally like and accept these. They are still better than all the bulky, dangly, ill-fitting headphones I tried before Sennheiser. I just wish the designers would go back to the drawing board and Frankenstein up a hybrid that takes the like 3 nice features from this model and the remaining awesome features from the PMX 680 and give me back my dream headphones worthy of the $60 price tag. product_title: SenteyÂ® In-Ear Headphone Amplitude Series
review_body:
After going through about one pair per year of Skullcandy Ink'd earbuds for the past five or so years I decided to change things up. The price of Skullcandy Ink'd's keep increasing and the quality seems to be decreasing. I stumbled across these "Sentey" Earbuds and I saw the amount of good reviews and thought I'd give them a try. I'm currently listening to music through these earbuds and after 30 minutes of listening I'm just as disappointed as when I opened the Amazon package.

First, I opened Amazon's padded envelope and found the Sentey box smashed on one end with none of the other items in the envelope damaged (Strike 1). After I opened the damaged box I immediately saw that the earbud cable was not wrapped neatly but rather smashed into the opening where the cable belonged (Strike 2). I decided to try out the earbuds anyhow. I switched out the stock rubber tips for the larger set that came in a small, opened ziploc-style bag. I plugged them into my phone's earbud port (I noticed that the earbud plug seemed to fit a bit too tightly) and gave them a listen. This is where they failed to impress yet again (STRIKE 3).

When it comes to sound quality I consider myself to be an audiophile in training. I'm currently a college student and can't afford to be buying and using top-end audio components all of the time but I do happen to have a USB DAC and a pair of Sony MDR V6's for my everyday listening pleasure. I even tested the earbuds with the DAC to make sure that it wasn't just my phone's headphone port that wasn't cooperating. These earbuds seem to be designed as in-ear subwoofers rather than in-ear speakers. The amount of bass that these earbuds put out is overwhelming in a completely negative way (and this is coming from a guy who absolutely loves bass-heavy music). The sound produced by these earbuds is completely muddy and muffled. I understand that these are only $15 earbuds but I am completely disappointed.

I will be copying this review and sending it to the seller promptly. Please heed my warning and DO NOT buy these earbuds. I've heard that Panasonic RPHJE120K earbuds are fairly worthy of a $15 price-tag but sell for about $6. I intend to try them out with my refund money.

review_headline: Does What the Manufacturer Claims but Is Now OBSOLETE Against Telemarketers
review_body: Although I've found this device to do everything the manufacturer claims, it has become obsolete. The telemarketers have evolved to outwit this device by spoofing caller ID information, using a different number for each call. I can add numbers to the blacklist until I'm blue in the face, and the telemarketers just keep calling relentlessly from numbers they seem to choose at random.    I wish this device had a feature that asked callers to press a button to ring the phone to help weed out the robocallers. However, I'm sure the robocallers would soon defeat that by setting their automated systems up to transmit the appropriate DTMF tone.    Another shortcoming this device suffers from is a difficult-to-manage blacklist. There's no way to view the numbers currently on the list. It would be great if you could log in to the device from a computer and manage the list via a web interface.    This device should work for you if you have specific numbers you need to block, but don't expect it to work against aggressive telemarketers that employ caller ID spoofing. Unfortunately, the only escape from telemarketers I know of is to get rid of your phone.

product_title: Denon AH-C400 Music Maniac Black In-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Sturdy looking phones with a somewhat unique sound to them.
review_body:
Bought this back in September 2014 for my iPhone, the packaging is very appealing, extra's are welcome (large choice of ear tips, carrying case). At first I was impressed, the sound is flat but very clear, just like other reviews said it would be (might sound strange at first, but after a while you'll get use to it), the cord is tick and sturdy, everything seems to be of top quality.

I've had some problems with it (no product is perfect), it might have been back luck but, since I ain't a US resident, and paid quite some import tax to receive this, it wasn't affordable to send it back for replacement and/or repair, so I had to take it upon myself to fix it.

After a few weeks, the remote started acting strange (buttons didn't work, moving the cord would make it skip all songs, like it middle button where being pressed repeatedly), one day I decided to open it up and have a look (there are no screws or glue, so you can easily open it up and close it again), i found out that the wires that went into the remote were making contact (short circuit) with the ones that went through to the earphone, so i reorganized the wires inside the remote and close it again, problem solved.

After 6 months, the right ear-plug started failing, so there I went, taking it all apart to find the problem, the wire leading to the earphone was short circuiting somewhere near the "Y" where the they split, so I found a way to open it up (it's some rubber covering a plastic case, which holds together a small pcb where everything is soldered into, 6 wires come from the mini-jack plug, which are soldered on one corner of the pcb, and the wires leading to the earphones are soldered on the other corner of the pcb, no wonder that "Y" is so large). So i cut a small part of the problematic wire and soldered it back to the pcb, covered it with a thin layer of tape, bent a paperclip to strengthen the wire (in case i accidentally pull it) and covered that withanother nice layer of tape (it looks neater than that gigantic "Y" now). While searching for the problem, i opened up the earplug to see if something was wrong in there, the "black spheres" are nothing but a glued cap covering small screws that keep together a "housing" for the small (closed up) earphone, so the manufacturer's preview stating that these "black spheres" are acoustic chambers for better sound is just plain wrong.

After these 2 fixes, the phones are performing great. I have to say it was pretty hard to repair them, and at this price range, I expected them to be more durable (it might have been bad luck tough).

In short, these are nice enough earphones, but the price range should make you think twice.

(2) If you use the bluetooth than the screen is permanently fixated on showing it's connected via bluetooth and therefore, the clock feature is voided. (3) The sound when you turn bluetooth on is rather loud for a quiet office space. I was disappointed that even with the actual volume turned down fairly low, the chime for the bluetooth was still the same (high) volume.

I haven't tried playing music from an SD card or USB or any other method aside from bluetooth. The range I used it up to was about 5ft away and it worked perfectly.

Would I purchase one again? Maybe - if I just needed it for the speaker feature (and not also as a clock)
Would I recommend this product? Maybe - but only after mentioning my "gripes" noted above. If you're cool with those than this is a great little speaker.

product_title: Panasonic RP-HJE350 SLIMZ In-Ear Earbud Headphones
review_body:
I originally bought these in 2011 and lost them in August of 2015. I've always been a fan of Panasonic stuff, and the overall quality of these is very good. This set has never come apart or broken in the 4+ years I had them. Not a single problem. When I went to order replacement set, I decided to try a couple other sets that were lower in price and do a comparison. The other 2 sets were the Panny RP-TCM125 and RP-HJE120.

I'll get the HJE120 out of the way first...easy decision as #3 out of the 3. These are apparently the bestselling earbuds here. I'm guessing it's because of the price, because the sound quality is mediocre at best. OK for voice or videos, but missing both bass and high end for any sort of music listening. They block out sound about the same as the other 2 sets, which I would rate as OK.

After listening to the 3 sets back-to-back on several different tracks, I've come to the conclusion that these HJE350's definitely lack bass, especially as compared to the TCM125's. Also, these are just a wee bit too bright, I think. Would describe it as "fatiguing" after listening for a longer period of time. I guess I did not notice the lack of bass in the prior 4 years of ownership. The HJE350s do have the best construction of the 3 I tested and the cable is bit thicker, so tangles less. Plus these have the little clip thing and you can put it behind your head so they are more secure and you don't get as much cable noise physically transmitted to the earbuds.

Of these 3, I think I prefer the sound of the TCM125s. Absolutely have stronger bass, and maybe better midrange (vocals), too. These are just missing a bit at the high end...but only a bit. These have a microphone, which doesn't really matter to me, just mentioning it. These buds are shaped the same as the HJE350s, which is a good thing as they fit me well. Unfortunately, the cable on these is cheap and tangles easily. I'm going to use these and keep theHJE350s as a backup pair.

product_title: JBL High Performance In Ear Headphones with JBL Drivers and Microphone
review_headline: Poor sound compared to other earbuds, keeps falling out when working out.
review_body: I purchased these specifically for two purposes: for working out, and talking on the phone in the car (no Bluetooth). They're definitely sturdier than the apple earbuds, the wires are flat instead of round, and the rubber coating is thick. They've lasted longer than most apple earbuds I've had over the years.  But the sound quality is horrendous compared to other brands in the same price range. There is no depth at all, the sound is muddled and just slightly muffled, and the mid-range overpowers any treble in the music. No matter how much I mess with the equalizer it will never sound the way I want it to.   When using the mic to talk, unless I'm standing or sitting still, everyone I talk to on the phone says the sound goes in and out if I'm moving. Even just pacing back and forth causes problems. As soon as I take the headphones off they other person can hear me just fine. It makes them completely worthless for use in moving vehicles.  The buds themselves are also too small and they fall out when working out. They come with replacement buds, but it looks like those are even smaller than the ones already on it. If the quality of the headphones were better it would be easy to replace them with a larger size. I do not recommend these at all, even for the price they're pretty terrible. Spend the few extra bucks and get a brand that actually understands how audio engineering works.

product_title: Yurbuds (CE) Female Inspire Pro Earphones
review_headline: They Started Out Good, Downhill From There
review_body:
I went into store to replace my apple earbuds, which I had given to my son to replace his lost ones. These cost twice as much, but I went ahead and purchased them anyway because they appeared to be high quality, plus, they would be easy to identify amongst all of the white apple earbuds that everyone else in my family is using.

The sound quality is good. For the price I expected a vast improvement over my previous set, can't say that I noticed a major difference.

The 1st problem that I encountered is that the removable earpieces kept falling off, to the point that I finally lost one. The set includes 2 pair, (2 sizes) so I switched to the smaller size. That was fine until I lost one of those. It's ridiculous how easily they fall off (without notice) so now I have one in each size.

I opted to wear the bids without the earpiece, which was working fine for me. But, new problem cropped up.. When I use them to talk on the phone, the other party can't hear me very well, even though I can hear them.

Recently, I'm starting to have problems with static sound when I use for telephone or music. I've owned these for about 6 months, going back to Apple, half the price, none of the problems.

review_body:
Pros:
I think they look nice. The sound quality is good, with nice bass response, and they fit comfortably in my ears.

Cons:
Although the braided cord seems sturdy, it produces a lot of distracting cord noise on my shirt while typing at my desk. I don't notice it as much on my train commute.
There is a cord control for pause/play and a microphone, but no volume control, which I think is an important feature. I must take my phone out of my pocket to boost the volume when a train passes by on my commute.

Quality and Customer Service Note:
The pair I originally received was defective. Upon plugging the headphones into my iPhone 6, it would cause my podcasts to stop and start playing randomly, and repeatedly activate Siri. Symphonized was very helpful and prompt in sending a replacement, which have been fully functional for the past month of daily usage.

Summary:
These headphones are just average. I find myself missing my old cheap Sony earbuds which didn't look especially sexy but were small and light and had a volume control.

product_title: SanDisk  Clip Jam MP3 Player
review_headline: An improvement in some ways and a step back in others
review_body:
I'm a longtime Clip fan ever since the 1st model came out 5 or 6 years ago having owned every version and model. This latest model fixes my biggest gripe of the Clip+ model (the last great model): short battery life. I have yet to recharge it since I began using this little guy and this improvement in battery life alone is enough to warrant an upgrade to this model.
However, for some reason unknown to me, SanDisk decided to augment the size of this model which makes it bulkier to clip or hide in your pocket. Although it is still small, it's not longer one of the smallest players in the market. Bad design decision by SanDisk.

But the thing that really makes me remove 2 stars from the rating is the software used to power it. As I stated above, the Clip+ was by far the best Clip iteration with a perfect redesign while maintaining the small footprint and simple, fast and functional software. Sadly, SanDisk decided to carry over the colored screen and redesigned software from the horrendous Clip Zip. It's slow, buggy and clunky. After the catastrophic release of the Zip model, you'd think SanDisk learned their lesson: that nobody cares for a colored screen in a pocket player made for exercising, especially a low-res one. Not only that, but it now takes forever to fast-forward and rewind (in increments of 30 seconds) which is maddening for somebody like me who only listens to 1-2 hour long podasts and radioshows.

Bottom line: this Sport model is a massive improvement over the terrible Zip before it but it's still not better than the Clip+. While I greatly appreciate the improved battery life, I'm still disappointed by the clunky larger redesign, useless low-res colored screen and slow OS. It's still the best gym companion out there, but it could've been better.

Now if only SanDisk could put this new battery inside my trusty Clip+..

product_title: Aether Cone
review_headline: NO Android app til 2015 - limited to a single source and single speaker, requires constant re-sync. Not ready for prime time.
review_body:
I had high expectations from this product but must admit, I'm totally underwhelmed. Out of the box it's a nice looking unit with solid feel and weight. It powered right up and has audio instructions to walk the user through set-up. That was the last time I looked at this unit with anything other than contempt.

So, why the three stars/neutral rating? I've opted to wait until the rest of the features roll out. It seems like more and more products are pre-releasing half finished products.....while I don't personally like paying for the privilege of beta testing half finished products, this is the reality. Cone promises to add more app's and enhance functionality plus play nice with Android in the near future. If it takes care of some of these issues like the ability to add more speakers, apps etc, this will GREATLY enhance the product.

First things first...it would not sync with the wifi. I tried time and time again using a desktop, laptop, two different tablets.Turning off the firewalls/protections, attempting to add the device via wifi settings on the laptop, desktop and even direct via the router controls...nothing. Started all over and again, nothing. Went to the website troubleshooting section which seems to be the most redundant bit of non=help available. Tried their \\"support\\" link...it basically states the exact same thing. Went to Facebook...it's only a sales pitch. After over 2 hours of doing exactly the same thing over and over, it was finally recognized. Okay terrific...nooooo, not so fast.

Next, it immediately stalls and shuts down. Reboot everything and start over...once again, Cone not connected. Meanwhile, the start.aether.com site won't load which of course, adds to the irritation. Try again, start to go through set-up again and for the upteenth time, get tossed off the site. Go through over and over and once again, finally recognized only to get tossed off. By now I'm more than a tad miffed. As a side note, I'm running a Centria dual band router and rarely have issues but just in case, turn off everything else...same problem. You would think they would build in a work around or manual input...apparently not. The itsy bitsy instruction insert provides zero help for trouble shooting. The website was barely better. After doing a Google search, I ran across information about the buggy app, sync issues and a few other notable items including the lack of support for Android users which is NOT something they seem to actually mention on the site or other information...if you read long enough you will run across this tidbit...'{an android version of the app will be available in early 2015). So dear readers, if you are running Android, absolutely wait because this isn't ready for prime time whatsoever.

Also own Denon Heos products which we adore! In fact, the more we use them, the happier we are with the product. Thought the Cone would go great out in the garage and/or porch thanks to the ability to recharge etc but aside from the set-up issues and the less than impressive app, this is tied directly to Rdio with minimal sue without paid subscription.

About Rdio - this cone makes it sound like you get free Rdio access...but in fact, you get the same free access as anyone else using the freebie version. Yes, you can skip' 6 songs in an hour but for truly advertisement free listening, you must pay the subscription rate of $10 per month. Now, that wouldn't be a big deal but unless you are a Rdio user already, it's just adding one more app for what feels like an inferior service compared to other options. In fact, this really feels like a Rdio device that tries to get the user to sink even more money into the service after paying a pretty nice premium for a speaker...or oversized paperweight given the number of times needed to sync, then resync and resync again. Lest you think I'm exaggerating, be sure to take a look at the FAQ's of the company website which clearly liststhis as a commonly encountered problem...and if anything, they are being modest.

Users Held Hostage

In addition to holding the user hostage to the paid Rdio version for ad free listening, I was surprised to find there is all but zero other ability to add other app's....No Amazon Cloud, No Pandora, No nothing. This is VERY limited...again, you get the freebie/ad version of Rdio or an option to add a monthly subscription for yet one more service...and one that very few people are using at that. Blah!

Even worse, if you want to use your playlists of other standard features, you MUST upgrade to the paid subscription. To truly get this to play the entire album via voice command, you need the full paid subscription...otherwise, it just plays something similar. Ditto for songs. In short, if you don't intend to use the Rdio paid version, this device is only half functional. And remember...you ONLY get a choice of Rdio...no other major subscriptions or choices!

Privacy
So, another thing I initially thought was a benefit turned out to be a very real negative. I've been waiting to buy an Amazon Echo device which is \\"always listening\\" but able to talk/respond. We have a visually impaired family member who would really benefit from this feature but like many others, I was a bit concerned over privacy issues. This Cone has a press button to allow the user to speak a requested song/other...initially I thought this was a much preferred way to use audio without the constant listening. I was wrong. Reading through the online information, it seems this device is also 'always listening' but without the ability to respond to anything more than a command or song.

I understand addition app's are supposed to be forthcoming and if these plus other updates help improve the item, I'll try again. This feels like a beta release/rush of the product which is only half done. It's filled with glitches, does not easily recognize the item, requires constant attention to sync and re-sync and sync again...only to then be limited to a single rdio feature filled with advertisements.

Single Speaker
Another disappointment was the inability to use more than a single speaker at a time. Frankly, for this price, I expected to be able to add additional speakers to other rooms like the Denon HEOS which allows us to sync the music from room to room or play independently...it's a feature we absolutely adore in this household! Instead, this runs a single speaker at a time and only a single speaker. BIG disappointment!

Bottom line - Check out Denon Heos for roughly the same price....more options, multiple speakers and rarely requires a reset. This is simply NOT ready for prime time!.and if anything, they are being modest. Users Held Hostage In addition to holding the user hostage to the paid Rdio version for ad free listening, I was surprised to find there is all but zero other ability to add other app's....No Amazon Cloud, No Pandora, No nothing. This is VERY limited...again, you get the freebie/ad version of Rdio or an option to add a monthly subscription for yet one more service...and one that very few people are using at that. Blah! Even worse, if you want to use your playlists of other standard features, you MUST upgrade to the paid subscription. To truly get this to play the entire album via voice command, you need the full paid subscription...otherwise, it just plays something similar. Ditto for songs. In short, if you don't intend to use the Rdio paid version, this device is only half functional. And remember...you ONLY get a choice of Rdio...no other major subscriptions or choices! Privacy So, another thing I initially thought was a benefit turned out to be a very real negative. I've been waiting to buy an Amazon Echo device which is \\"always listening\\" but able to talk/respond. We have a visually impaired family member who would really benefit from this feature but like many others, I was a bit concerned over privacy issues. This Cone has a press button to allow the user to speak a requested song/other...initially I thought this was a much preferred way to use audio without the constant listening. I was wrong. Reading through the online information, it seems this device is also 'always listening' but without the ability to respond to anything more than a command or song. I understand addition app's are supposed to be forthcoming and if these plus other updates help improve the item, I'll try again. This feels like a beta release/rush of the product which is only half done. It's filled with glitches, does not easily recognize the item, requires constant attention to sync and re-sync and sync again...only to then be limited to a single rdio feature filled with advertisements. Single Speaker Another disappointment was the inability to use more than a single speaker at a time. Frankly, for this price, I expected to be able to add additional speakers to other rooms like the Denon HEOS which allows us to sync the music from room to room or play independently...it's a feature we absolutely adore in this household! Instead, this runs a single speaker at a time and only a single speaker. BIG disappointment! Bottom line - Check out Denon Heos for roughly the same price....more options, multiple speakers and rarely requires a reset. This is simply NOT ready for prime time!

review_headline: and comfortable. Need to run them for a few hours ...
review_body: Edited 12/15  I am changing my rating to 1 star.  One of the ear covers came off and was lost.  I called sennheiser to get a replacement and they told me I have to buy a 20 pack for $25 dollars.  They would also have to get them from Germany.  The product does not come with any spares, so if you lose them you are screwed.  I lost one in just under a year, why do I need to buy 20 for such a steep price?  Maybe a 4 pack for $5?  That would be more palatable.  Maybe include 2 extras with the product?  That would have been the right thing to do.  Sennheiser has always been a top choice for me and a product I always recommend.  It will be hard for me to purchase or recommend them any more if this is not addressed.  I paid over $70 for these when they first came out and now I have to pay an additional $25 for ear covers that cost about 3 cents each.  Absolutely unacceptable.   Received them today, sound is very clean, they seem to stay in the ear very securely, and comfortable.  Need to run them for a few hours and see how the sound is after they burn in.  So far they are very pleasing.  Been looking for sports earbuds for several months now that aren't noise isolating.  Will update my review once they burn in and I have spent more time with them.  Update: After having used them for a few weeks I am changing my rating to 5 stars. The reason I purchased sport earphones was for skiing.  I can say that they stay in your ears the way you would expect, perfectly.  I will admit that initially I wasn't positioning them correctly due to poor instructions, but once I figured out how to position them properly, I am now impressed.  Secure, great sound comfortable, and I can still hear enough around me(depending on volume level of course).  A little hint for positioning them properly, the "hook" goes up toward the rear of your ear.  The body of the earphone should be diagonal, not straight up and down.  The portion that sits in your ear rotates to align the opening to your ear canal.  Once you get the hang of it, it is a simple process.  Until you get them to fit properly, they won't sound very good.  They actually sound great after they are in your ears correctly and you burn them in for a few hours.  Inline remote works correctly for me on HTC M8 running Lolipop.

product_title: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones with Microphone (Gray)
review_body:
I bought these because I lost (ok, as it turned out washed and dried) my Klipsch earbuds, which I was fairly pleased with. Based on the reviews, they sounded like an exceptional value. My opinion is that they are decent for the price, but don't really compete with my more expensive pair in terms of sound quality.

I will say that the bass is impressive, but like I read from some other reviewers, somewhat overpowers the mids, at least for rock. Probably this could be corrected with a decent equalizer which I have not taken the time to explore, but by default I would agree with the balance being a little off. Mids and highs are ok, but not great.

The other thing that I was concerned about with these after reading the reviews was the noise interference caused by the nylon cords. This is indeed an issue, as when those cords rub on clothing or bump against your body while walking around being active, it does transmit the sound up and into the earphones, and overpowers the sound. These are not the earphones for you if you're planning to have them in while putting around doing chores, etc. I'll also say thanks for pointing this out reviewers...I had never noticed this before but now I also notice it on my other earphones that have a very light rubber cord, although it is much less noticeable.

Regarding fit, I do sometimes have problems with one ear, and have gone through quite a few pair, some which fit and some which don't. These fall into the hard to fit category for me. I've tried all different sizes of fittings with these, and none of them stayed in very well for me. Probably due to the somewhat heavier, larger wood piece that produces the nice bass.

Bottom line, they are ok for the price. Would I pay $15 for them again? Probably.

review_headline: Another cheap clone imported from China.
review_body:
This power supply is very poor quality and does not match the photos. When buying these types of supplies I look for some sort of conformity or certification mark as well as some sort of brand name to get some assurance that the supply is not an unsafe imported clone power supply. The picture in the description showed a CE marking and a brand name/logo, but the supply that arrives contains no CE markings and no brand name, instead simply saying "MADE IN CHINA" across the bottom.

The power supply arcs sufficiently upon plugging in that sparks actually fly out of the receptacle when it is first plugged in, and the enclosure arrived with a crack in it. This is not surprising considering that the plastic is so thin that I can deform the enclosure by squeezing it between my thumb and index finger.

If I had intended to order a cheap power supply, I wouldn't be complaining, but this one was advertised on the product page as having attributes that the delivered product did not have. I'll return it and once again attempt to find a power supply on Amazon that isn't cheap knockoff junk.

review_body: Sony, what happened to you?  I purchased this as a Christmas gift last December for my daughter.  She tells me a couple of months ago that it has never held a charge and its use is limited because she must always plug it in.  No problem says I, I have the warranty in my hand and it says 'one year'.  I called Sony to get a replacement.  Well, Sony says that it only has a 90 day warranty.  Who the heck has a 90 day warranty?  Even the off brands go a full year.  But not Sony.  I spoke with customer service, sent them a photo of the one year warranty that came with my device and they are still telling me that despite the physical evidence of their warranty they can do nothing about it.  I escalate and get customer service to promise to fulfill their warranty.  They send me a link to get ball rolling with notes to their fulfillment center honor my warranty.  Fulfillment sends an email back that says they won't do it because there is only a 90 day warranty.  This is ridiculous.  So, to Sony, to whom I have been a loyal customer for over 30 years, I say this - my next camera is Canon.  My next TV is a Samsung.  My next tablet is an iPad.  My next phone is and iPhone.  All over a $50 speaker which you shipped in non-working condition.  My Sony computer just died and they don't support it any more either.  We are witnessing the end of a once great company.  Sony used to mean quality.  It now means nothing.

product_title: MA Audio MA5817 800 Watt Home 5.1 Powered Sub & Multi Speaker System
review_body:
I really was not expecting much from this HT system because of how cheap it was but after I set it up I was very disappointed. The satellite speakers lack clarity and do not reproduce mids and highs well but the biggest problem by far is the subwoofer. Its a 6 inch subwoofer and therefore cannot hit anything below 45 hz well and MA Audio did not put any sound dampening material in the box so leaving it sounding strained and boomy even at low listening levels. Also, the claim that it is a 300 Watt subwoofer is just 100 percent false. After 3 weeks of frustration with the sound quality of this system i decided just to take it apart to see if there was anything i could do to make it sound better, and thats when i found that they were using a subwoofer rated at 35 watts at 8 ohms. Then out of curiosity I tested the plate amplifier and it struggled to push 42 watts rms into an 8 ohm load (not anywhere close to there ludicrous claim of 300).
Overall this system is grossly overrated and really had no strengths, i recommend you save your money and buy a decent 75$ subwoofer and 2 pairs of 50$ bookshelf speakers. That will create a 4.1 system that will blow this one out of the water.

product_title: BlueAnt Pump - Wireless HD Sportbuds - Black
review_body:
So I've been up and down the bluetooth path for some time to find the perfect or near perfect headphones and these aren't much of a contender. If you don't want to read the whole review scroll to the bottom breakdown.

Was really hoping for the best but these are on par with my sennheiser cx 300 II Precision Enhanced Bass headphones when they actually seat right. That's one of the many problems I've experienced with these.

Finding the "right" fit was near impossible because when I would move my head they would lose the secure fit I thought I had(no matter what size ear tips I used). Also no matter what positions/tips I tried I would experience pain both inside and out of my ear after only 15 to 20 minutes.

This product also boasts 100 feet for signal range but issues began when the device was about 30 feet or less away, with constant disruption.

The only really good that I found was the microphone quality was excellent. First time I ever experienced perfect sound from the person on the other line and vice versa. They said it was so clear they had no idea it was a headset.

The buttons for volume and other features was OK and in a reasonable place, but the response and ease of acting out commands takes some hard presses as well.

Breakdown

pros:

Good sound if you can get a good fit

microphone great for calls outgoing and incoming sounds

buttons for control are easy to feel for

cons

Too uncomfortable to use for much of any extended time

Hard to get a secure fit

signal cuts out much closer than boasted(20 to 30 ft instead of quoted 100ft)

maybe you'll have a better experience but I wouldn't bet on it. My opinion would be to look elsewhere. I recommend bluedio r+ legends over the ear if you're alright with a little more bulk.

hope this helps someone

review_headline: Terrible Sound Quality. No Vibration. Rosewill RHTS-8206 far better.
review_body:
I just received my ROCCAT KAVE KTD 5.1 Digital Surround Sound Headset. First off, it sounds terrible compared to my original headset, Rosewill RHTS-8206, which was only $49. I do not think the product itself is really this bad though. I may have received a faulty headset. It sounds the same as an older headset I had, the Creative Fatal1ty, which was only $25.

Here are my issues:
- The sound quality is lower than anything I have ever used. It is set to 16-bit, 48000 Hz (DVD quality), which is the highest option available.
- There is barely any bass. I did use the ROCCAT control panel and tried the Dynamic Bass, but it just muffled everything.
- I was told that there is a vibrator unit in the headset, but it appears to be disabled. I feel no vibration when there is any bass.
- The Movie button does nothing (I can tell no difference)

Here is what I have done and checked so far:
- I have installed the latest Drivers from the website (I am not an idiot)
- I set the headset to 5.1 surround (again, I am not an idiot)

Other notes: I tried a custom equalizer setting that sounded amazing on my previous headset, Rosewill RHTS-8206. It made everything sound worse. Everytime any bass played, the volume dropped with every beat, like the headset could not produce sound and bass at the same time.

My hypothesis:
- I installed the wrong drivers somehow
- The new drivers that I used are garbage
- I received a faulty or broken headset

So far, this $169.99 High-End Gaming Headset sounds worse than $25 Headphones. Something is not right here. The ROCCAT Syva earbuds for $29 have more bass, AND THEY ARE EARBUDS!!! This is probably the poorest excuse for a high-end gaming headset. The Rosewill RHTS-8206 is far superior, probably the best I have ever used. If you want the Rosewill RHTS-8206, get them here: http://www.amazon.com/Rosewill-RHTS-8206-5-1-Channel-Vibration-Headset/dp/B007ZS9T1Q. They are only $49. I highly recommend them.

product_title: RCA RP8078 5-Disc CD changer (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_body: Bought this CD changer second-hand as an alternative to only playing CDs in my car or on my Discman. It works well enough (so far) on CDs that are factory-clean and are kept in absolute mint condition. However, the error detection is extremely poor on this unit. CDs with some light wear that play just fine in the car or on my Discman will skip horribly, sometimes several times per track, on this player. You have to fast forward through them, as the player will not be able to work through them. I bought a used CD on eBay with a couple of faint marks--and I mean the kind you have to hold up to a light to really see properly--and you would think I was trying to play a disc that was kicked around a gravel parking lot and encrusted with filth in the process. As this was an early CD pressing from the mid-80s, I would suggest not playing really old CDs on it. Also, as another reviewer noted, there is a pause between tracks, similar to when a CDR is burned incorrectly, except it happens on every disc you play. Just try listening to something like Judas Priest's "The Hellion" segueing into "Electric Eye" or Black Sabbath's "Don't Start (Too Late)" into "Symptom of the Universe" where the tracks are supposed to fade into each other, and you will be instantly annoyed. One positive thing I will say, is that a couple CDs I own where other players will fail to read the first second of Track 1, play fine. So there's that. I can't speak for mp3 discs, as I don't have any anymore, but other reviewers have a litany of complaints about that particular feature. Overall, I strongly recommend buying a different CD player.

product_title: Pyle-Pro PHA40 4-Channel Stereo Headphone Amplifier
review_body:
This is going to be a live review typed while I listen through The Pyle-Pro PHA40-A. If you dont want to read it all, just skip down to the CONCLUSION

My setup to get the fairest most balance review that I can is to take my laptop through a Roland Duo-Capture (USB) and then run a patch cable from the Duo-Capture to the Headphone Amplifier. All volumes on the laptop is maxed and the Duo-Capture are set at 75%. The Pyle is set at neutral (with knobs at the 12 oclock position)

My Test Playlist is: Safri duo - The Bongo Song, E-Type - Campione, The Irish Symphonia - Feet of Flames, Haiku D'Etat - Non Compos Mentis, Sponge - Plowed, and Queen - We Are the Champions.
The Heaphones I am using in this test are: Grado SR125, A&H Xone XD-53, AKG K701, and Beyerdynamic DT770's.

The first song starts off and I am wearing my Grado's. The Bongo Song is pretty much all drums. but there isn't enough power driving my Grado's to make it pop. The XD-53s work well with this song even though they tend to require more power. I am not noticing a particular loss of sound quality but the volume is softer with the open pack cans than with the close back cans. The 701's are miserable to listen to on this one. Very little definition from the song and the huge soundstage of the cans make it sound even smaller, the DT770's require the most power to drive but are still at a good volume.

Campione, a techno song is again soft in the Grado's and the 701's, the Xones are getting some distortion without volume change but the DT770's are awesome on this song. They are right at home.

So far no clicking or any jack issues as reported by other reviewers. Also so far Im noticing that closed back headphones are definitely at an advantage. I am not playing with the volume knobs at all.

Feet of Flames, heavy on the strings is okay with the Grado's. Soft, but thats expected. Not muddy, but not brilliant either. On the Xones, the sound is a tad darker than the Grado's but without the driving baseline all I get is a higher volume than the Grados. The 701's... Oh wow! The definition and clarity is amazing. Yes its softer than the Xones, but each note is carried, each instruments voice and tones are captured perfectly. By far this is the 701's favorite song through the Pyle. The huge soundstage is loving it and really sounds great. The Beyerdynamics are loud. Louder than the XD-53s they are flat sounding and I get my first blip in the sound. Im not sure if thats the small laptop clipping or having problems keeping up with the dataflow from this high bitrate song. The volume is appreciated through the DT770's but it doesnt have the clarity that the 701's did.

Non Compos Mentis is hip-hop. As expected the DT770s and the 53's are louder than the Grado's and 701s. Its just subpar on all the cans.

Plowed is a standard rock song. Its not well known but is decent. The vocals are coming through no issue with the Grado's. Im hearing all the instruments and the song is shining but I wish the volume was better like the Xone's, which are louder but dont carry the clarity. The 701's arent any better, in fact they are softer than the Grados. Much better clarity than the 53s. The DT770s again strike the best balance between volume and listenability, but even then there isnt enough juice to power more than the mids on this song.

Queen starts off wonderfully in the Grado's. There is a great punchiness to this song despite being softer. This is the best song so far for the Grado's on this setup. The Xone's are good with this song too. The thematicness of the song comes through well. Its also softer than other songs but better than the Grados but not by much in the loudness section. The 701s enjoy the song but the Grado's still are better. There just isnt enough umph from the Pyle to make the headphones really sing. The DT 770's are the loudest on this song but dont treat it nearly so well as everything just runs together and creates a kind of muddiness. There is a buzzing sound too with the upper registers of Freddie Mercury's voice that wasnt present in the Grado's like the amp really cant push as much.

Now for more of a test. Im using the Grado's for this in the #1 jack. As I adjust the volume knob, the levels change smoothely with no clipping. I get distortion at the top end as the headphone drivers can't keep up. Queen sounds great! Playing with the volume knob I get the Bongo Song to come alive, but as I move the levels around I lose clarity with volume change. The Pyle really likes the higher volumes over the lower volumes and as I move into another song I have to find the sweet spot for that song for the best listening to the song to strike the right balance between loudness/volume, clarity, depth, brightness, etc. Its definitely better than neutral but I loose so much as I lower the volume that there are definitely more changes than just volume as I turn it. Im not exactly pleased with that. I get all the songs to really come through but now for the next test.

I bet you were all wondering why I included the Duo-Capture huh?
Well, I unplug the Pyle from the Duo-Capture and plug the Grado's into the Roland. First off, the volume is much better than anything I was getting out of the Pyle (granted 1 headphone instead of 4 but still...) and I get much better clarity. The songs pop. Feet of Flames is inspiring, Non Compos Mentis is not perfect but is much better than the sad mediocrity is sounded like on the Pyle. The Bongo Song is roughly about the same but with more bass hz input and sounds more well rounded. Campione sounds more like the game-score it is than something roughly thrown together While Plowed comes through with such great guitar that there is no comparison to how it sounded on the Pyle. Queen comes in again softer than the other songs, but that probably more due to the recording. As I adjust the volume on the Roland, all that changes is the volume. And Max volume is still loads louder than max volume on the Pyle.

CONCLUSION
The Pyle PRO PHA40-4 is most definitely NOT a headphone AMPLIFIER but is does make for a decent powered headphone SPLITTER. I would expect an amplifier to better drive large driver headphones and provide more volume than the originating signal on its own does. I expect a headphone amplifier to provide the same audio quality and (for lack of a better term) "features". I want to hear the same song the same way no matter where I position the volume rheostat and the Pyle just doesnt provide that. Granted not alot of people will know, but this is something that I would put in the guest bedroom or take to work and not worry about.

REDEEMING QUALITIES: Price - Its CHEAP compared to others. It does not require batteries. Its small. And people who haven't really compared it to much else wont notice what its lacking.

MY ADVICE: Get something else for yourself. Spend more money and get something that sounds better. FIIO's E9 (or E1 for that matter) or an ART, or Creek or Topping or something that isnt THIS. And Yes, I gave it TWO stars mainly because its price and having a powered headphone splitter could occasionally come in useful.

review_headline: Inexpensive, cool looking...useless as a clock!
review_body: It stopped working properly about 10 days after I put in the water.  I'd purchased another water-powered clock from a store probably over a year ago.  I loved it because it was perfect for a bathroom that steams up a lot--no damage to batteries and I could still see the digital numbers through the steam.  I purchased this one because the older clock's digital numbers had begun to wink out and it was impossible to determine what time it was showing.  I'd tried cleaning it with apple cider vinegar as recommended, but it still didn't work consistently.  This soda can version was a very poor substitute.  First, it is VERY small.  Best for use on a desk where you can are going to close to it to read the numbers.  But, in a room, even a small room, it was not visible.  I had to get up close to see the numbers inside the disc, partly because the numbers are very small, and partly because the numbers are set into the disc area, obscuring the view.  Next, the digital numbers winked out within 10 days.  It recommends you fill up every 2 weeks, to keep the read-out showing strong, but this happened in less time.  And, when I refilled, the numbers never returned to their original fullness.  A missing bar here or there with a digital number means...you can't read it.  So, I would not recommend this, even if you are using on a desk.  I've purchased much better.

review_body:
When I received them, I was really happy with how they look, and the way they work using this KLEER wireless technology. The sound was so clear, unlike most of the bluetooth enabled headphones.

The Sound of the music was so clear, and rich. The bass was Okay! . On the other hand, the mids, and highs were very VERY good.

My biggest issue with these headphones was that they are NOT comfortable headphones at all, by anymeans.

First, the padding is very good and well built. To be honest, they looked premium.

Unfortunately, after wearing them for a long time (not even long enough, around 1.5 hours) my ears started to hurt and I had to keep on moving them around. (To me this is so annoying, as I want to be able to forget about the headphones while working)

Second, It's doesn't have a 50' range, sometimes it even disconnects while it's in my pocket.. and I need to reconnect it, and this happened a lot.
Sometimes the headphones just stopped responding, and I had to wait for around 5 mins till they work again. (This also happened a lot (Every time I turned them on, this had to happen at least once.)

From the sound point of view they sound absolutely great and if you are listening to high quality music, you will feel like you are in a studio.
While raising the volume to maybe 90% or the max produces a huge distortion (I mean both the headphone's volume and the device's volume, which is pretty insane. I don't think anyone needs music to be this LOUD.)

I had to return them, since for me, comfort while using the headphones is the most important aspect.

review_headline: Almost a Slam Dunk!  But just too Harsh, with Mid-range forced into a treble-range.
review_body: These IEM's have been described by most to be bright...that is the understatement of the century. These go beyond bright. The so-called mid's are un-naturally forced into what is actually the treble range while the highest treble notes stab your ears like daggers.  Vocals on these often suffer from sibilance as well.  I have seen that some complain of a lack of Bass which is just not true.  The sound signature of these is clearly a smiley curve with a severe narrow drop somewhere in the lower mid-range that picks back up so sharply as to completely obscure the fact that many notes that should be heard at a lower mid frequency are actually being represented in the lower treble range.  As stated by MEElectronics they are improved slighty by Burning them in a bit. I did about 20 hours.  But nothing fixes the sound signature to make it natural.  Its as if there is only tight low bass and sharp treble.  You could never call these muddy.  But they are lacking the smooth frequency blending of many more expensive alternatives and that is the rub.  They aren't bad for the money and they do respond to forced EQ adjustments. So you can tune the treble down but how many people really have access to a small portable player that can do that well?  Sure you can do that with winamp on your pc but if you want to use these with your ipod prepare to bleed out your ears.  What really drives me crazy about these headphones is how close they come to a slam-dunk.  Great features!  remove-able cable, extra cable included, tons of ear tip options and a great case all for roughly $50  Ultimately though that sound signature and over-bright treble just hurts too much.  There's no point in hearing all that detail if it isn't pleasant to listen to

product_title: Music-Link Stereo Hearing Aid Compatible Headset (Single Ear)
review_headline: WARNING: If you've ever ordered Sea Monkeys from the back of a comic book, you're ab...
review_body:
First: I never write reviews. Just don't take the time because as a consumer I don't feel the need to give feedback on everything I use in my daily life.

However, this time I gave in because I sincerely couldn't believe how poor the quality of this device was for the price being charged.

Want to visualize the quality level? Think about the cheapest headphones you could find, something equivalent to what you might find at the dollar store -or maybe at walgreens on the rack right next to the cashier. You might pick this cheap item up as a complete impulse purchase for your 5 year old (because (s)he was just begging you the day before for a set of headphones to replace the set that came with their fisher price kids mp3 player you bought for Christmas).

For the price, I was expecting something of medical quality. At least an equivalent quality as the hearing aid ear piece or maybe even just to the level of the headphones that come packaged with an iPhone.

The unit I received did not work. I spent an hour plugging it into device after device, and yes, I do know what size mm jack it is supposed to be compatible with. Tried it with my iPhone, iTouch, iMac... then on PC headphone jack, you get the idea... no sound.

I get that things can be defective from time to time, but this time it was an insult to injury scenario. Pay $49.99 for something that should cost no more that $1 or maybe $2, feel duped (like the time you ordered Sea Monkeys from the back of a comic book) for paying that high of a price for complete junk, but go ahead and try to use said junk because, well, you were duped, no luck getting device to even meet your expectations remotely, feel even more duped (like when you realized your hard earned lawn money got spent on Sea Monkeys that turned out to be less interesting than mosquito larva in a jar) ... return item to Amazon in defeat and disappointment.

In the end, I'm actually glad the unit didn't work because I probably would have just kept it. At least it forced me to send it back and get a refund.

review_body: Don't waste your time or money...the price should have been an indicator, you really do get what you pay for in this case. When it is charged the red light will go out.  You then need to turn it off and then back on, and press the middle button (that is play and pause) for it to play.  The sideways buttons are for volume.  I am still only giving 3 stars because it is somewhat confusing (nothing like the shuffle) to operate and the lack of instructions is ridiculous.

product_title: Sony HT-CT370 2.1 Channel 300W Sound Bar with Wireless Subwoofer, Bluetooth, and NFC
review_body: Yes, this sound bar can be mounted. However, it's as if the mounting options were included as an afterthought. This is a major flaw in the system, in my opinion.    To explain, cables from anything below the soundbar have to travel up and behind the soundbar, then make a 180-degree turn downward to fit the HDMI ports located at the top of the unit. This not only puts constant tension on the connectors, it leaves you with ugly loops of cable visible above the soundbar. Not intuitive at all. This is especially true if you want to take advantage of the handy ARC feature by running several HDMI cables from different sources to the soundbar. Just imagine what it would look like from the side!    Also, the mounting hardware is an issue. It comes with mounting brackets and screws for attaching the brackets to the unit. But It does NOT include screws for mounting the unit to the wall. The mounting brackets use a keyhole system, which is very specific to what size screw it will accept.    Like I said, afterthought.    Because of these issues, I decided to use the soundbar as it was clearly designed to be used -- resting on my entertainment center. I must say I'm actually very pleased with this setup. The unit sounds and works great. The ARC feature is particularly awesome. There isn't a cable in sight. Even if the mounting issues were somehow fixed, I'd probably keep it how it is. So, in the end, it turned out to be a happy accident.    Still, I'd definitely advise looking elsewhere if you plan to mount.

product_title: HIFIMAN HM700 32G Portable Player plus RE400 In-Ear Monitors/IEMs
review_body: The HiFiMan HM-700 was my first venture into lossless audio.  I did a fair amount of research before purchasing the player and had high expectations based on favorable reviews at Amazon and other sites.  When I received the unit I was impressed with the packaging and the nice RE-400 IEMs that came with the unit but my favorable impressions began to quickly change when I started listening to the player through my car audio system and the RE-400 IEMs.  When listening to the player through my car audio system I found that the player did not provide significant improvement over my old mp3 player when comparing CD ripped FLAC music files to the same files converted to 320 bps quality mp3s.  I do not have a high end audio system in my car so initially I thought that maybe I needed a better amp and speakers in my car to hear the difference.  However, as I note later, I did hear improved performance when I tried another lossless player through my car system.  I also expected to be impressed with the IEMs since they are matched to the HM-700 but I did not find them to be better than other IEMs that I tried with the player.  The bass response is poor and the overall sound is too tinny for my taste through the IEMs.  A major issue that I have with the HM-700 is the expected battery life.  My experience falls far short of the advertised 16 hour battery life.  I generally only see 5 to 6 hours of operation before needing a recharge.  The user interface is poor as well.  The controls are flush on the face which gives the unit a sleeker appearance, however, in poor lighting conditions or sun glare it is hard to find the buttons to use the player.  After playing the HiFiMan HM-700 for 4 months I finally became so unhappy with it that I purchased a Fiio X3 music player.  The Fiio X3 performance is what I had expected to hear when I made the upgrade to lossless audio.  FLAC files sound noticeably better on the X3 through my car audio system, battery life is at the 16 hour mark, plusit will play 24 bit files whereas the HM-700 will not.  The Fiio X3 player costs a little more than the HM-700 but I think it provides noticeably superior performance.  Overall, I am disappointed with my HiFiMan HM-700 purchase and cannot recommend it.  I wish I had tried the Fiio X3 first.

product_title: Micca MB42 Bookshelf Speakers With 4-Inch Carbon Fiber Woofer and Silk Dome Tweeter
review_headline: Decent speakers on a low budget
review_body:
I've had these burned in for around 80-100 hours so far, and to me they're really just "ok' speakers. They're not bad, but they don't really seem to really excel at anything either. Maybe expectations were just too high because of the very high rating they received here.

The main thing they seem to have had going for them was the price, though it seems they went up to $120 now at the time I'm writing this review. The prices on speakers seem to fluctuate pretty heavily, and these are the cheapest 2.0 speakers I currently own. I wouldn't pay or recommend paying $120 for these, but they may be a decent choice at like $80. TBH I haven't tested many speakers at that price range.

At first listen, It seems like Micca aimed for a more monitor type sound with these, as opposed to the the more normal bookshelf speakers. However, the clarity really falls short for monitors. They simply don't sound very clean compared to the other monitors I have (M-Audio BX5a and Yamaha HS5m), and the separation is lacking from a monitor standpoint as well. They do however have a clean sound and overall better separation compared to regular 2.0 desktop speakers I have/had (Simple Audio Listen and AudioEngine A2). They may very well be comparable to lower end monitors, though I don't own any to compare with.

As bookshelf speakers PB42X are severely lacking in bass. I don't mind the lack of low bass and sub bass since I always connect my 2.0 speakers to a sub anyways. However mid bass is severely lacking, and almost feels hollow especially for 4" drivers. Before going to watch Furious 7, I re-watched the other 6 Fast and Furious movies while switching though different speakers and headphones, and couldn't help but notice that these were absolutely terrible for any sort of action scenes because there's just no impact. The other smaller 3" driver speakers I have/had did significantly better at both mid bass and lower bass.

As a final note, The PB42X isn't especially compact either, but I did like the simple clean looks and magnetic grilles. It's just hard to recommend these when the Monoprice clone of the M-Audio BX5 was recently on sale for $100, and those speakers are much better sounding.

product_title: Tripp Lite HDMI Extender Equalizer, Active Repeater for Video and Audio 1920x1200,1080p at 24Hz (HDMI F/F)(B122-000)
review_headline: Does not work for PC to TV connection.
review_body: First of all, this is not necessarily a bad review of this unit.  It may work as intended, for extending the HDMI run for AV equipment.  I needed an extended HDMI run from a PC (actually a recent model Asus I7 notebook with native 1080P panel with HDMI port) to a TV (specifically a Vizio P series 55 inch TV).  The current run is a 50 foot HDMI cable terminating to wall panels on both ends, then 6 footer HDMI cables are used to connect to source (notebook) and display (Vizio TV). The current setup works sporadically, and needed a signal boost.  I know this unit is meant for AV source like blue ray players or cable boxes and isn't meant for a PC which refreshes at 60 hz (if supported by TV) instead of 24hz.  But I was tempted to try after seeing other reviews that seemed to suggest it works for a PC setup.  It did not work for my setup.  Once the repeater is connected to the TV side, the TV never showed images (while the original cable runs would show at 50% of tries). Further the TV started acting strange in rebooting itself and refusing to respond to remote control commands.  I have tried HDMI1 and 2 ports on the TV to the same results.  Once the repeater is removed, the TV behaved normally.  I even tried the repeater on the source side which is the wrong place to use this repeater (Notebook) to see if I am lucky.  Same negative results.  Again, this is a use case clearly not supported by the description of the product (24hz), so please do not take it as a negative for its intended use.  I am returning this unit and getting the other Tripp Lite HDMI repeater that clearly states for 60hz use to try again.  Wish me luck.

review_headline: These are good AAA batteries but at a high price
review_body: These are good AAA batteries but at a high price! :-( I did extensive testing with sophisticated chargers (both PowerEx MC-C9000 and La Cross BC-1000 chargers) and these batteries are high quality but you don't get that much bang for your buck. The actual capacity I get with a modest load of 200 ma is about 811 mAh, which is slightly above the rated capacity of 800 mAh. Now you could be happy about them being 1% better than the rated capacity EXCEPT FOR THE HIGH PRICE! This battery is NOT a good value. I compared cost versus ACTUAL capacity on 5 types of batteries and these Amazon High Capacity batteries have a good capacity but a high cost per mAh.    Name  Rated mAh  Actual mAh  Purchase  Count  Cost Per  Cost Per Amp  EBL  1100  1023  $24.99  20  $1.25  $1.22  <-- EXCELLENT! :-)  SunLabz  1000  931  $11.49  8  $1.44  $1.54  Very good  Amazon HiCap  850  875  $17.99  8  $2.25  $2.57  Pricey  Amazon Green  800  811  $18.57  12  $1.55  $1.91  Somewhat Expensive  Eneloop  850  850  $11.54  4  $2.89  $3.39  <--- RIP-OFF!  :-(    Note that even though the Amazon and Eneloop batteries are expensive, they are high quality batteries that might hold up better over the long haul. I'm not sure, time will tell. But at least they are good batteries that meet or exceed their rated capacities. Too bad they are so $$$.    I noticed that the actual delivered capacity does NOT hold up well with higher discharge rates of 400 ma and 500 ma, where I get about 710 mAh, which is 10% less than the rated capacity. It's normal for all batteries to deliver less energy at higher discharge rates. But there wasn't anything special about this battery's ability to do unusually well in high demand applications- it's just a normal NiMH battery.    I haven't done long term testing for low self-discharge but based on the charging and discharging profiles, these do not seem to be similar to Eneloop batteries. They act like normal batteries to me. They were delivered with about a 70% charge.

product_title: NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Black/Blue)
review_headline: Only If You Need a Speaker For Your Bike
review_body:
OVERALL ASSESSMENT: Only buy this speaker if you actually plan to strap it to your bike. If that's what you're looking for, then there's probably not a better option. If you just want a portable speaker to set on a table or countertop, there are better options. Especially if the price starts creeping up towards the MSRP.

PROs:

The speaker is light--only about three quarters of a pound.

The speaker comes with clips that allow you to attach it to bicycle handles, or perhaps a stroller. A stroller seems the more likely option. These clips seem designed more for leisureliness than intense workouts.

The speaker has multiple connection options. You can connect a device via 3.5mm cable, USB cable, or bluetooth. An added bonus is that when you connect via USB cable, the speaker will charge your device (although the speaker's battery won't last as long).

CONs:

The sound quality is a little thin--lows are noticeably lacking. It's better than cheap earbuds or the built-in speaker on your phone (though not much). Its main virtue is that it can get louder than your phone's built-in speaker.

When I compared this speaker to the [[ASIN:B00N32I2Q6 Bose SoundLink Color Bluetooth Speaker (Black)]], the Bose blew this speaker away. However, the Bose is more expensive. At the time of this writing the NYNE sells for $69.95 on Amazon with a MSRP of $99.97, while the Bose sells for $129.

product_title: Beats Solo HD On-Ear Headphones
review_headline: Headphones broke after a month; the sound quality is good, but the build quality is terrible.
review_body:
Positives: The sound quality of these headphones was pretty good, great bass response for sure. The highs and mids could use some work, but overall I was totally satisfied with the sound quality.

Negatives: The build quality of the headphones is severely lacking. The headphones do look good, but the rigid plastic used in the design is not good for the constant expanding and contracting that takes place when putting the headphones on and taking them off.

Here is my story behind that:
Well I had my $150+ headphones for roughly one month before the headband cracked. So I thought, "No problem, they are covered by a warranty". So, I contacted the warranty department and was given an RMA number. I returned the headphones with all information that was requested and waited. I would like to note that I took great care of these headphones; I would put them back in their case after every time that I used them and coil up the headphone cord and place it in the case as well.

Finally after a few weeks I contacted the RMA department to ask for a status. They informed me that my headphones were being shipped back to me without being repaired because they were deemed un-authentic. So I asked for additional information on how they came to that conclusion only to receive a response of "They are fake".

I am 100% sure that the headphones I have are not fake. They were purchased brand new, came in the original sealed packaging and how no signs of being a counterfeit product.

I have since contact the RMA department twice for additional information in regards to why my claim was denied and was told I would receive a response within 1-3 business days; both time I have received no response.

To summarize:
- The $150+ dollar headphone broke after a month of use
- The RMA department did not contact me at all regarding my claim before returning the product to me unrepaired
- The RMA departmentfailed to provide information backing their claim
- The Customer Service is unresponsive in general and does not respond to customers in a reasonable amount of time, or at all.

So if you are looking to spend a good chunk of money on headphones that will break and then receive terrible customer service, these seem like the right choice. I would love to be contacted by Beats customer service to resolve my issue, but I am unsure that they will ever see this review.

product_title: iFrogz  Audio Tadpole
review_headline: It Works As Promissed, Just Not For Me
review_body:
I have a number of bluetooth speakers, and this is certainly the smallest. It is a little bigger than the key fob for my Jeep, but is within the window of what I could tolerate on my key chain.

=== The Good Stuff ===

* The unit paired with my iPhone with little drama, once I figured out how to use the control button. The bluetooth connection as reasonably strong-I got well past the 30-foot mark without a loss of signal.

* The sound quality is, well, what you would expect from a 1" speaker mounted in a plastic enclosure. There is, of course, very minimal base, sort of a muddy midrange, and not a lot of clear crisp treble. In a side-by-side test, I could convince myself it was better than my iPhone speaker, but no where near car audio or even a cheap boom-box. It could fill up a small room (a vehicle or small garage) with music without too much distortion.

* The unit does seem well constructed and while it lists itself as being water-resistant, I don't think it would survive being submerged or even used in a downpour.

=== The Not-So-Good Stuff ===

* The part of my memory that is used for remembering how to use "one-button" controllers has evidently been used for something else-I suspect old phone numbers. The single button has numerous functions depending upon how long you hold it down for. I hate this, although I will admit it did work as it was described.

* The obvious comparison for this speaker is just what comes out of the iPhone speaker. It had a superior sound quality...the problem is just that it was not all that superior. I am pretty picky about sound quality, and both this speaker and my iPhone rate somewhere near "barely tolerable". So for me, the added fidelity of this over the iPhone just wasn't worth the effort. Obviously I was a bit more willing to use this in hazardous areas, but that is just not something I need on a regular basis.

=== Summary ===

If you want an additional small speaker for your phone, this works as well as anything you will find. It is certainly lightweight and relatively easy to use, and I got an honest 2-3 hours of use out of a battery charge. For my own situation, it just wasn't a good fit for any real need that I have, but obviously your mileage may vary.==

review_headline: Fun little boombox, but how well it works depends on your specific needs.
review_body: It's a fun unit that meets my needs, which was for a small boombox into which I could stick a microSD card filled with MP3s and have them shuffle played. Of course, there are good and bad aspects, which will likely change how well it will work for you. There are also loads of features in which I'm not interested, so I didn't review those. Other folks have, though, so check other reviews!    The Good:    It sounds pretty good, for a player this size. Not great, but perfectly acceptable for casual listening. I use it when I'm exercising indoors, doing yard work, or working in the garage. It's plenty loud for these uses. You're not going to be using this for a party, though.    It supports files in folders. You don't have to cram everything into the root directory.    It supports random play, which is frustratingly hard to find on small cheap MP3 players. It appears to randomly play songs within a folder, but not across folders. That's fine with me. However, switching between folders can be frustrating. (See below on this.)    The display is tiny, but clear and easy to read. It's packed with info.    It's cheap, at less than thirty bucks, with Prime shipping, no less. I looked pretty hard for a cheaper player that supported folders and random play, with no luck. If this meets your needs, it's a steal.    The Bad:    The random play seems to barely work. It seems to play one set sequence of songs, not more than a dozen or so long. The bad controls don't help as I'm not really sure when I'm switching random on and off.    It doesn't play in stereo. I know, the description says it does and some reviews have claimed it does. It doesn't. It mixes stereo down to a single mono signal. There's one clearly visible speaker. The other is either a deeper-set speaker or some sort of bass port. Listening with it right up to my ear, I'd say it's just a port. I actually made a short audio file that bounced the sound between L & R to verify this.    The documentation is sparse and doesn't explain much.    The controls are touchy. The difference between a short press and a long press is tricky, yet crucial for navigating the menus. I just set it for random and let it play, so it's not a big deal for me. If you want to utilize many of its features, though, you'll find the experience frustrating.

product_title: TVPower USB Cable for Powering Roku 3
review_body:
My Roku 3's power brick says 12VDC @ 1.0A.
USB is 5VDC at 0.5A
That's 1/4 of the power.

This will run the internal filter caps at half power, which increases ripple, increases crashes, heats the caps, and causes the caps to fail early.

Also, if you're doing something that takes more CPU, such as YouTube, it may not be enough power to run.

If your TV has a USB 3.0 port, then you *may* be able to get 0.9A, which is better, but really, this is designed for something that runs on 5V, and not a Roku 3.

Now, for what it does, it does it well. It's a fine, quality USB to mini-barrel cable.

The product reviewed was provided as a free sample.
