product_title: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphone
review_headline: A compromise between features and looks
review_body:
Pros:
-Stylish. There's not much else on the market that has this color selection
-Comfortable. After ~2hrs of wearing they still feel comfortable (my opinion)
-A hard-shell case is included
-Sound quality is decent
-I've walked across the house from my device and was mostly interruption-free while listening to music. In my experience the range has been pretty good.

Cons:
-Expensive given the included features and sound quality. You're paying mostly for the stylish looks and the name.
-Only 16 increments from min to max volume. This may seem like a lot, but it really isn't. Often I find that one click is too high, and the next one down is too low. The volume adjustments via the headphone buttons are very "coarse".
-Power on indicators are very poor. When powering on while wearing the headphones, you get no indication whatsoever except for some noise canceling that occurs. No voice saying (like my plantronics earpiece does) "Power on, xx hours remaining", no power on chime. For the price, you'd expect better features in this regard.
-Pairing/connected indicators are poor. My Bose Soundlink Color actually tells me in a computerized voice the name of the device that has connected to it. These headphones only give you a jumble of tones/beeps when a device has connected, and a similar sound when a device has disconnected. It's very confusing when changing devices to figure out what the beeps mean that you just heard. Also, to enter pairing mode you press the power button and look for led's to blink on the outside of the headset, but to hear the audible indicator when connected you need to be wearing them.
-No dedicated track forward/reverse buttons. To change/pause a track or manage devices, you have to press (depending on what you want to do) the "b" button either 1x, 1x and hold, 2x, 2x and hold the second press, 3x, or 3x and hold on the third press. Not kidding. Confusing? You betcha.
-The noise canceling "hisses" more than other noise-canceling headphones I've owned
-The advanced noise canceling mode (which doesn't allow music to be played) gives no audible indicator, often making me wonder if it's in that mode or just powered on and not connected to a device.

Maybe at some point in the future we'll have more manufacturers making wireless/noise-canceling headphones that aren't all black or make you look like you're piloting an aircraft of some sort, but for now this is about as good as it gets, which still leaves a bit to be desired.

product_title: Mohu Leaf 50 TV Antenna Amplified 50 Mile Range MH-110584
review_body:
I live 4-14 miles from Baltimore, MD area tv stations. I get all those stations w/ absolutely no problems. Once I found a place where the stations had good signal strength, I didn't have to move it again. It worked and the picture was flawless.

I also live 20-25 miles from Washington, DC area tv stations (12 main stations w/ whatever "sub" stations are available). I get a total of 5 stations out of this one... a 20 mile, 22 mile, 24 mile, and two 25 mile stations. I get no signal whatsoever from the 5 other 25 mile away stations that's in the exact same direction (by degrees from my home as stated by AntennaWeb) as the two 25 mile away stations that I do get signal from.

What I actually did was used the 25 mile away station to "tune" my antenna. My TV shows signal strength of the station. I move the leaf around until I get the highest possible strength I can find for that station. Strangely enough, when I put it at the window the strength is gawdawful. I don't know if it's due to my aluminum window blinds but when I just put it against one area of my wall the signal strength is good. Also strangely enough, if I move the leaf just a quarter inch in any direction, it changes the signal strength drastically. But once I found an ok signal strength against the wall, I just use the tacks that come w/ the leaf to attach it to the wall. I even tried using extremely long (50 ft) coaxial cable and extremely short (6 inch) coaxial cable along w/ the included cable. It didn't make a difference as far as signal was concerned.

In conclusion: it's advertised as a 50 mile leaf but it barely got me 2 stations that were 25 miles away. But under 15 miles from a station, it worked great.

BTW, I tried the leaf w/o the amplifier and got ZERO stations. So yeah, I think the amplifier works.

product_title: JLab Epic Bluetooth 4.0 Wireless Sports Earbuds with 10 Hour Battery and IPX4 Waterproof Rating, Black
review_headline: Very good quality product that works as advertised at a good price. Lack of Siri support is big drawback to be aware of.
review_body:
I got these headphones based on a recommendation from Wirecutter. I've recently increased my fitness activity level to include a couple 5km runs a week and the odd hike. I also XC bike every week.

The headphones sound great with good range, clear vocals and good bass. Fitting them was quite straightforward and the memory wire helps keep them in place with all 3 activities I've used them for. Sweat hasn't interfered with the fit or use and not having to worry about them getting wet is very nice.

Pairing was very straightforward. Hold the power button to turn it on and put it in pairing mode and you get audio and visual cue it's in pairing mode. Connected to my iPhone 6 and iPad mini 2 without a problem. Battery life is good and as claimed. I've charged it twice since getting them and have easily used it 10+ hrs per charge.

Biggest drawback - and quite frankly it's almost become a deal killer for continued use - is the lack of support to initiate Siri from the headphones. If you *scan* their product page as I did, it sounds like they say they support Siri when in fact they're saying it'll work once you start Siri from the phone. That was a key requirement of mine and I should have read their statement more carefully, so my fault. I have my phone sometimes on an armband so for those instances it's annoying but still functional. What doesn't work is when I'm hiking or biking and phone is in the backpack. For a newly released product this is table stakes today and if they don't put out a firmware update to address it they will lose me and likely others as customers.

Overall product has worked quite well and as advertised, but the lack of Siri has dampened my enthusiasm on it and the usefulness.

product_title: BT-C3400 Universal Battery Charger Analyzer Tester for Li-ion NiMH NiCd rechargeable batteries
review_body: Has 2 major flaws, The item I received was version 2.1. The Discharge Refresh mode does not report the discharge capacity of the battery as specified. Instead it accumulates and reports the charge applied to the battery which is quite different and frankly not particularly useful. I monitored this over the 3 Charge discharge cycles, and in each case the charge cycle showed an incrementing mah reading during the charge cycle and showed a fixed reading during the discharge cycle which was the previous cycle accumulated charge applied. I wondered why my batteries (NiMH) were showing a 20% plus increase in capacity compared to my other chargers! The second flaw is that the charger is set to 4.2v for Lithium Ion batteries, which is fine for Lithium Ion but way to high for LiFepo4 batteries. There is nothing in the instructions to indicate this. I understand there is a switch inside the case to switch between 4.35/4.2/3.6volts, but opening the case to switch voltage for each lithium Ion battery type seams a little impractical. Beware if you charge LiFePo4 Batteries you are going to overcook them. All other functions seemed to work fine. I am returning my charger to Amazon due to these shortcomings.

product_title: 2 MXJO IMR 18500 15A 1000mAh 3.7v Rechargeable Flat Top Batteries
review_headline: Solid batteries, but not for high drain applications.
review_body:
They say High Drain but unfortunately that doesn't seem to be the case. In my case I draw about 7amps off these batteries. They get to about 75% charge and the voltage sags badly. On the battery it says they are rated to 15 amps. This seems to be a problem with all 18500 size batteries however. I did find a home for them though and at lower power draw they seem nice. Being IMR's they are also a little abusable regarding discharging and charging. Even when I was drawing 7amps they only got slightly warm, and only very slightly. If these batteries didn't say 15 Amp High Drain batteries I would honestly give them 5 stars as the batteries are simply not capable of 15Amps except maybe for a few seconds when they are fully charged.

To the other reviewer that gave these batteries 1 star because the shrink wrap pulled off the casing. If you got them from Expo, please talk to them. I had a shipping issue with my order that was entirely the faust of our United States Postal Service. :D Expo took care of me, was a pleasure to work with and made things right. If you haven't contacted them yet I recommend it. They'll take care of you.

Thanks for reading.

review_headline: Circuit was not designed to connect directly to a headphone... line out only...
review_body:
I bought this receiver in hopes that due to the apt-X codec, it would have a better sound quality than other Bluetooth receivers. While that may be true in theory, due to the way the amplification circuit was designed, it generates a lot of noise when connected directly to a headphone. Just by connecting this directly to a headphone, and letting it idle, you can hear a lot of noise coming from it.
I connected it to a FiiO E17 (high quality headphone amp) and the noise disappeared, which seems to suggest that their circuit was designed to be used as a line out only, and not directly connected to a headphone. This contradicts what they publicly advertised in a question where another customer was asking if he could connect his Beats headphone directly to it.
The lack of volume control is also something that hurts the audio quality, since you'll have to reduce the volume using a software mixer in your transmitter, effectively reducing the bit depth. My quest for a high quality Bluetooth headphone receiver continues...

product_title: Polk Omni S2 Rechargeable Compact Wireless Music Streaming Speaker with WiFi
review_body:
Just received this unit. Did the setup - a few hiccups, but it got the network and then took a few tries to download the update. Once the update came through was able to play music via pandora with no problem. The sound is good and, yes, I would put it a notch higher than SONOS Play 1. The fact that it's rechargeable battery and can moved with no interruption is awesome.

Here is where it falls flat. The iOS or iPhone, iPad software is nice, but not cutting edge. The SONOS app is a bit better, but that's OK as you don't look at the app all that much and the Polk app works. Where it falls short is that SONOS is on it's own mesh network (which is basically inconsequential to the end user) - where it does matter is you can start music on songs and then leave. If your device that started the session leaves or the app is shut off the WiFi network (let's say you went to work) on a SONOS the music keeps playing. With Polk it stops. Furthermore, any device that has SONOS installed can change the music, skip a track, change the station, change the volume - it can be me, my wife or my daughter. They can do this at anytime. With Polk you are limited to only the device that started streaming the music - so if I start music, my wife or daughter or whomever can't do anything on their polk app (turn down the volume or change the music). Furthermore, the polk app is mobile only apps (e.g., iOS or Android). While working on my mac laptop I can't access anything on Polk - whereas I can with SONOS their app is mobile and computer. The result with SONOS we have music playing about 16 hours a day. We leave and come back to music - we change it through the day, a station that someone started at 9am is changed at 3pm possibly by someone else - even though the originator of the station left hours ago. With Polk it has to start and stop - and can be done only through mobile devices (given a choice mobile devices are better than full computer apps, but it should be both). SONOS also has a pause/play button - with this button we pause the music when we turn in for the night and close down the house and then hit the same button when we wake up - no need to access the app.

I understand that Play-Fi is an open standard so that the people making good speakers, like Polk, can make a wireless music system. But for now, the SONOS mesh network is much better. And, just so it's clear - Play-Fi is way, way better than Apple's AirPlay (drops all the time) and Bluetooth (low quality sound).

Polk did good and I like that we paid a sale price for this item and I like the ability to just move it, but at full retail I would be hard pressed to suggest this item. product_title: Supersonic SC1081 4 Band AM/FM/SW1-2 Portable Radio
review_headline: Works Kinda Battery Problem/Danger 4 Band AM/FM/SW1-2 Portable Radio by Supersonic
review_body: UPDATED REVIEW FOR PEOPLE WHO OWN OR ARE THINKING OF BUYING THIS RADIO    I recently purchased this radio and wrote a review about it this update includes an overview of the original review and testing and suggestions for anyone who owns this radio.    What you need to know about this radio is the engineers who designed it wanted to throw in every option they could. If it was designed correctly it would be an amazing radio unfortunately the charging and power system is the problem.    The radio includes both USB and SD Card adapters so you can play MP3's. The MP3s are played in order of their alphabetical file names You can store the MP3s in directories but they will still play in order of file names. The Fast Forward is actually a Skip to the next Song File so you an not fast forward on full album MP3's. MP3's play well but there is no shuffle feature which would be great so you're not listening to an hour of the same artist.    The Radio has AM FM SW1 SW2 the AM for me plays like its an FM Station with no distortion and very strong signal I am 60 miles from 3 major cities Right in the center and I get real good AM Signals Better than my car. The other bands also work well.      OK so lets get to the problem    The radio can be powered in three ways.    D Cell Batteries it takes 4 of them 1.5v each for a total of 6VOLTS     DC 6 Volt Power Supply connector .. you buy your own power supply 6v @300mw works    AC Plug.. THIS IS THE PROBLEM   The AC Plug is not designed to power the radio It is used to charge an internal Rechargeable Battery.     The AC Cord connects to an internal Transformer which only puts out 1.2volts which then charges the rechargeable battery but unfortunately the rechargeable battery is only 4.2volts and the MP3 Player requires a minimum of 5 volts to run.    With the Rechargeable Battery fully charged and brand new D Cell Batteries installed the radio will run for a long time since it only takes a small amount of power. THE MP3 PLAYER TAKES MUCH MORE POWER. If you have the rechargeable and D Cell Batteries installed the MP3 Player will draw down both sets of batteries and then you will need to recharge the rechargeable batteries to bring it back up to 5volts total for minimal MP3 Playing.    This is where it gets fun The Power Supply that charges the rechargeable battery is hooked to the rechargeable which is in turn connected to the D Cell Battery Bank .. Which is then attached to the Circuit Board. Whenever you charge the internal Battery you are sending power to the D Cell Batteries.    WHEN EVER THE RECHARGEABLE BATTERY HAS JUICE IN IT.. IT WILL DRAIN INTO THE D CELL BATTERIES AND OVERCHARGE / DESTROY THEM.    Your D Cell Batteries are not rechargeable unless you install Rechargeable Batteries. Normal Alkaline batteries will take a charge but they are not suppose to be charged so you end up destroying your regular brand batteries.    The AC Power Cord that you plug into the Radio...   There is a tiny switch in the hole where the power cord goes When the AC Cord is plugged in it shuts off power to the Radio and to the MP3 Player so only the battery is being charged. Remember the MP3 Player requires 5 volts to run and the internal transformer only puts out 1.2 volts so it could never run the MP3 Player but it can run the radio.    Ok so what about the 6volt power supply .. ?    When the 6 volt is powering the radio and MP3 Player it works great.  However it passes voltage across the circuit board into the batteries it will pass into the D Cells and then into the Rechargeable Batteries.    So .. basically you have one option to defeat their horrible design.. because they wanted to add everything to this radio a rechargeable .. DC Power Supply and Removable Batteries...     You have to open the radio 4 screws .. do not remove the screws near the antenna!    Cut the wires to the square rechargeable battery and remove the battery.    Then Use a DC Power Supply to power the Radio. A 6 volt @300ma is workingwell for me but one with slightly more power might also work better say 6v@500ma    THEN IMPORTANT.. BECAUSE THE POWER SUPPLY WILL OVERCHARGE YOUR D CELL BATTERIES    you need to do what they do when they send out items with batteries in them ...    You need to place a piece of tape over the end of one of the batteries so it will not complete the circuit.. Then if you want to take the radio outside you pull that piece of tape out and disconnect the 6volt power supply and it will run off the D Cell Batteries ONLY.. then when you come back in put the tape back on before you connect the power supply.    This will allow you to power the MP3 Player and the radio with the 6v Power Supply  AND  Power the Radio only when you are outside.  If you try to power the MP3 Player on just the D Cell Batteries it will suck the life out of them in 3 or so songs.  However the radio will keep working on less power.    So if you have one thats the deal.. if you want one then you will have to do this before you use it.    Use either the DC Power Supply or the D Cell Batteries.. Not both at the same time.     If you don't understand the tape thing on the batteries then just pull them out before you attach the 6volt power supply.    If I didn't have an extra Power supply around I would be pretty mad about this.    The engineers went overboard and it came out bad.    Should you buy this radio... Unfortunately I have to say no until they fix the power system.    Should you throw this radio away... NO at the very least you can open it up remove their battery and use a 6volt power supply or D Cell Batteries .. Remember not both at the same time.. and the radio will work.    WOW CRAZY REVIEW HERE .. but i don't want people who bought this and cant return it now to think there is nothing they can do.

product_title: Onkyo TX-NR545 7.2-Channel Network A/V Receiver
review_headline: Nice Features, Great for Shallow Cabinets, Outdated UI
review_body:
I was looking for a mid-line receiver that would fit my entertainment center. The features of the 545 are quite attractive. HDCP 2.2 on 3 inputs (necessary for 4K support in the future), 384kHz/32 bit DAC chips, support for the DSD format, Apple Airplay, Bluetooth support, and discrete NON-DIGITAL power amplifiers all caught my attention.

The 545 measures about 13" deep, which includes the volume knob in the front and the speaker jacks in the back. The depth on my entertainment center is 15" so the 545 is an easy fit. There is a generous 2" clearance for the speaker cable and about 2.5" for HDMI cables. I'm sure others are in a similar predicament. (The 646 has a similar depth.)

Its hard to compare the power rating of the 545 to other receivers. The specs say 65 W/ch at (a rather high) 0.7% THD when driving 2 channels. I usually ignore the published power figures and go straight to the unit's weight which is 19 pounds. That is comparable to the Marantz slimline series of receivers rated at 50 W/ch. For my setup 50 W/ch is good enough. All of the speakers powered by the receiver are crossed over at 80 Hz. I can crank it up more than loud enough for movies and game play. If I was running full range front speakers I would have opted for the 646 for the extra headroom.

The auto speaker calibration is not as sophisticated as the Audyssey system. Only one measurement position is used so it cannot average out different seating positions. The test procedure determined that my front speakers should be crossed over at 160 Hz. I repeated the test a second time, got the same result. I built the front speakers myself, so I know the response is flat to 75 Hz. Fortunately, its easy to change this setting. The overall sound was definitely different from my previous receiver's Audyssey calibration. The 545 calibration is brighter, and the bass is not as well integrated between the front speakers and the subwoofer.I'll be playing around with it to see if I can get better integration.

The user interface is just text, sparse, and not completely intuitive. This unit replaces a five year old Marantz which also has a text user interface, and back when the Marantz came out a text interface was considered old school ! I am also disappointed that the results of the speaker auto calibration are not presented. I like to see these results in case they are a little strange so I can rerun the calibration, maybe try a different microphone location.

It's good enough that I am keeping it in the home theatre for the moment. But, I see myself upgrading this sooner rather than later.

product_title: Creative Airwave HD Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with NFC
review_headline: Great Speaker....... If you require a speaker with a 20 minute lifespan
review_body:
I purchased this speaker from an online retailer here in Australia during a post Christmas sale so I scored it for a very nice price and was very happy with my purchase..... that was until the item actually showed up! I unboxed the speaker and set it up to charge and later on and paired it with my phone and started listening to music and it sounded pretty good too, It have a nice full sound for a speaker of its size, a decent amount of bass and a good amount of clairty too, I was thinking hey! this is the bargain of the year......

Then it all turned sour very quickly - About 20-30 minutes into my listening session just as I was switching songs I hear a loud pop or click type sound and from that point onwards the speaker was silent, I tried it with bluetooth and an aux cable but still no sound... The speaker didn't even make the sounds that it used to when powered on or when put into pairing mode. I tried a master reset which I found described on the creative site which made no difference to the problem. I contacted Creative customer support about a warranty claim and they told me that its most likely a flat battery.... which could have been possible If I had disconnected the speaker from the wall adapter and ran it off the battery which I hadn't and I had also left the speaker to charge for about 8 hours before the first use too, and then they tell me that they don't handle warranty claims or repairs and that I have to deal with the place of purchase which I thought was quite poor service!!! Luckily I contacted the store I purchased from and they gave me an instant refund because they dont do replacements and told me to keep the speaker - most likely because of how cheap they were selling for it wasn't worth the cost of return for them (and by the time I got my refund the price of the speaker had gone up to 3x the price I paid).

So after that I kept fiddling with the speaker to try and get it working and after about 20 minutes of pairing and unpairing my phone trying to get it to work the problems got even worse, I couldn't even get the speaker to stay on for more than a minute or so before it switched itself off. So by this point I'd had enough, I had got my money back and I had nothing left to lose really so I opened the speaker up to see if I could spot the problem inside and potentially repair it. Upon opening it I found one of the main connectors that had become disconnected from the main board completely which wasn't surprising seeing as after I inspected the main board closer I saw just how poorly the joints on the board were soldered. They were soldered with a very minimal amount of solder and were very weak and flimsy joints and parts moved around with the slightest touch, Honestly I must say I have seen better quality soldering in cheap $2 chinese electronics!

Overall I must say I am very disappointed with the speaker - the sound quality was good.. but the build quality was terrible, Especially for a device that can sell for $150+ at stores here in Australia!!!! I'll definitely think twice or maybe even 3 times before I even consider buying another Creative item again.

product_title: Sony CFDS50 Portable CD
review_headline: Based on the "#1 best seller" in the super great "boombox" category on Amazon
review_body:
If 2 two stars was acceptable rather than "do not like" I would give this 2 stars. Based on the "#1 best seller" in the super great "boombox" category on Amazon, I was thinking it was reasonable that the $30 difference between this Sony stereo and the ZSS3IPBLACKN was a result of the more expensive technology for the lightning connection on the ZSS3IPBLACKN. Not correct. Though the the sound quality is enjoyable and relatively reasonable quality for the price, there is a significantly noticeable difference between the ZSS3IPBLACKN that I already have and the real interesting CFDS50. The lesser quality sound issues encompass the following:
(1) probably at least 20% more distortion (playing CDs or MP3s from the Audio in jack) than the almost distortionless ZS3,
(2) weak clarity and separation of secondary music elements (as opposed to the primary elements, usually vocals, guitar, lead synthesizer, lead drum) that muffles and tangles those secondary elements, at least 33% worse than the ZS3,
(3) fewer options for genuinely incremental loudness in volume (too big a difference in loudness between 11 & 13),
(4) significant loss of sound quality if the listener's ears are to the side or significantly above the stereo (i.e. it is used on a waist level counter or table), and
(5) The CD player seems cheaper and weaker and at greater risk at burning out after 2 years or less of moderate use.

This situation is the perfect example of the problem that arises from the loss of quantitative sound performance information for stereos
priced below $100. If the sound performance information for this stereo was available for comparison shopping prior to the purchase,
I definitely would have purchased another ZS3. I got the CFDS50 to back up the ZS3 and to use as a good, though not optimal, speaker system
for Mac Book\PC audio activities that feature music. Not that many years ago and to an extent even now, sound performance information was\is available for earbuds and earphones below $50 to allow shoppers to comparison shop the quality\price combination alternatives and make informed choices that relate to quality and price combination alternatives. This information should be available for stereos systems below $100, too.

If you can afford the extra $30 bucks and the relatively easy means to copy your cassettes to blank CDs,
get the ZS3. If you need a cassette player, the CFDS50 is a worthy preserver of access to cassette music.

Not only does it only work on 2.4GHz frequency, there is zero feedback on why the hub doesn't connect. Sometimes the iOS app reports a weak wifi signal however in the network list (and for the phone itself) the signal is showing strongly. 802.11g devices out of the room and on other floors all connect to the same router without issue.

After several hours of hunting and reading about wifi issues on the forums, I'm attempting to contact support by phone. After creating accounts on myharmony.com it was annoying to create yet another account on the support site. I'm expecting to have to return this product to Amazon soon but am hopeful that a firmware fix or other resolution is provided by Logitech.

product_title: Audio-Technica ATH-ANC7B QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling Closed-Back Headphones
review_body:
Generally, I like Audio-Technica equipment. These worked for a while, but ultimately failed and do have some drawbacks.

Noise Cancellation - These do a reasonably good job of canceling droning sounds like an aircraft. They are not perfect, but are a noticeable improvement over passive-only attenuation.

Battery Life - Reasonable. However, there is not an auto-shutoff feature. If you fail to turn off the cancelation, you will return to a dead set of batteries. Always keep a spare set in the carrying case.

Music Reproduction - Not bad. They are significantly better than cheaper headphones and earbuds. However, they are not at the top tier level.

Comfort - I found them to be reasonably comfortable for short periods of time (less than 1 hour.) Longer times tended to become uncomfortable due to the way the pressure exerts to keep the muffs in place.

Problem - A week after the warranty expired (one year), the left channel went out on these. I can tap the muff and it will sometimes come on, but overall, they are of little use in the current condition.

Overall - If the left channel had not died, I would recommend these without hesitation. However, since I don't know if mine was a fluke or indicative of larger QC problems, I suggest caution. A good pair will likely satisfy most people.

product_title: Sony XL-5200 Replacement lamp for the Grand WEGA A-Series TVs
review_headline: PLEASE DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT!!!
review_body:
I hated this product from the second I opened the box. First, the lamp practically fell apart in my hands as soon as I opened it up. I tightened down all of the screws, hoping that it just slipped past their quality assurance department (which clearly doesn't exist). I removed the old lamp from my television. The old lamp hadn't died, it was just nearing the end of its life. I installed the new lamp, crossed my fingers, and turned on the television. To my surprise, it lit up nice and vibrant. I set the television's settings so that it knew I replaced the lamp, and turned it off. Five minutes later, I turned the television back on and heard a terrible arcing noise. I pulled the lamp out, and sure enough the (fishing) wire they used to secure the bulb to the electrical connection had melted apart. I thought I had made a critical error, but to be sure, I installed the old (still functional) lamp. The television came on no problem... It's clear to me that whatever company makes this lamp assumes that the consumer's original lamp has blown, and can't be tested to make sure that the bulb they sent you is bad.

P.S. I have the KDS-60A2000 model projection television, and unless they completely falsified the advertisement for this lamp, it says it will work. It's set up the exact same way as the original lamp, but with way cheaper parts.

product_title: Pyle Home  Mini Power Amplifier with LED Display
review_body:
Poor Quality and Design. The blue LED bar-graph relative audio power "meter might have been a good idea, BUT . . they are blindingly bright even in a brightly sunlit room; in a dark rook when watching TV and using this for the TV sound with external speakers . . .well they are so blindingly bright that they totally distract from the show.

Tested this amplifier with a Hewlett-Packard function generator, General Radio Audio power and distortion meter, and looked at output waveforms on a Tektronix oscilloscope. It puts out only about 30% of it's rated "75 watts" when you look at it in honest RMS wattage; and that's with the volume turned all the way up, and it's distorting really badly then.

Constant low background hum in the speakers when the amplifier has no signal input, regardless of where the volume control is set - you have to be over 8 feet away from the speakers to not notice the hum (in a quiet room). When given a clean input signal and when it's driving efficient speakers (like 95db/w/1M) and when tthe volume is set low enough to not be in it's distortion range, then and only then is this amplifier even "listenable".

Also it gets HOT after it's been on for a while. Oh, and the IR remote control doesn't work from across my tiny 8" x 10" living room - I'd have to get up and be within 4 feet of the amplifier to make the remote work (and then only if it's carefully aimed) so by them I might as well take one step more forward and adjust the thing by hand.

Overall I was VERY sorry I wasted my money on this, it's total garbage. I had trouble selling it in a yard sale for $25; finally on the 3rd and last day of the sale I "gave it away" for $10 and quite honestly I felt bad for the person I "ripped off" by selling it to him for the $10.

review_headline: Good for price, but nothing exceptional
review_body:
I not usually listen to such cheap headphones, so my experience may be not relevant, but yeah, I was not expecting such quality from a 10$ headphones.

Here is comparison to KOSS porta pro (the closest competitor I could find):
JVC has more harsh and dirty highs. KOSS is much softer on highs, one would even say that KOSS lacks highs, but I would prefer absence of highs than garbage on highs (dirty highs cause tiredness).
JVC lacks mids. Actually, that may be due to overemphasis on highs and lows.
JVC has poorly articulated bass comparing to KOSS. Attack is softer, bass is rendered with more overtones.
Stereo base is worse than in KOSS also.

And JVC is several times cheaper than KOSS.

For the price, you have bass that is quite loud and, I would say, deep. Highs, though dirty, are also sufficiently loud.

Would recommend as a cheap headphones. Wouldn't recommend even as portable headphones if you're used to something more expensive.

review_headline: Only if the random feature could be utilized

I bought it again through an Amazon fulfilled seller to alleviate any return issues. This one charges and recharges but the random/shuffle feature does not activate. For a $17.99 discontinued product the touchscreen works well but not great. It has an external speaker but it isn't loud enough to be a selling feature. I don't plan to use the video playback feature very much since you have to customize the format to play on the player. I will only use the video camera/still camera if I need to record something unexpected since the specs are not high quality. I bought this to play at the office during lunch so the size and battery life is not a big concern, only the lack of being able to use the random feature on a low priced item knocked down the rating.

Cobyusa website is no longer up so do not expect technical support on this product. It has a lot of features I may never use but it has them if someone likes to play our with a 8Gb MP3 audio, video, text, and picture player.

This MP3 player is not as good as Sansa 200, Samsung Muse, or Philips Raga, but better than RCA branded MP3 players.

This sound bar power connection box is a great idea, but its length required that I cut off both ends of the wall cover flange flush with the edge of the mounting screw holes in order for the box to fit between the mounting bracket for my LG 37" sound bar and the wall standoff pad on the power cord end of the sound bar. My recommendation would be that this power connection box is best for sound bars of at least 40" or greater.

Another engineering flaw in the design of this power connection box is that the power cables enter and leave the box on the top and bottom of the box which means the cutout hole in the wall has to allow for these cables when inserting the box into the wall. A better design would have these cables entering/leaving through the back of the box.

product_title: Bravo Audio V1 Tube Driven Headphone Amplifier
review_headline: Overall I really like this amp
review_body: *******Update #2******* I've returned this item.  *******Update******* I had to knock a star off of my original 4 star review.  I'd actually like to give it 3.5 stars, but Amazon won't let me do that.  The issue I'm hitting now is that randomly there will be a clicking noise that will suddenly pop in.  Adjusting the volume knob does nothing to fix the issue.  I have to remove the audio jack and then re-insert it, but even that's only occasionally effective.  Sometimes all I have to do is touch and hold the output jack.  This leads me to believe that it's some sort of static build up.  This isn't too much of a problem when I listen to music at louder volumes, but it is a problem when listening even at just medium levels.  It's annoying and frequent enough for me to revise my review and knock off a star which is unfortunate.  Otherwise, I really do like this amp.  *******Original review******* Overall I really like this amp.  It looks pretty cool and really drives my new V-MODA Crossfade M-100 headphones.  The amp itself is a lot larger than I had thought it would be.  For some reason the pictures make it look a lot smaller than it is.  It's a little larger than the palm of my hand.  The size is a good thing though since I like to display this amp on my desk.  I will say that the one downside is the signal noise that this generates.  I found the position that produces no noise by turning off my music source while keeping the amp on.  As others have stated; right around the 9 o'clock position on the dial will produce no noise.  However, at this position the amp does not push my M-100 headphones as much as I like.  These are bass heavy headphones and at this position I have to really turn up the volume in order to get the bass response I'm looking for.  However, this has the unfortunate side effect of turning up the mids and highs to the point of discomfort.  If I turn the knob on the amp to about the 11 o'clock position I get the bass response I'm looking for without having to turn up my source's volume which means no boosting of the mids and highs.  Naturally this means that I have to deal with a bit of noise in between songs or when I turn off the music.  Since I'm using this setup in a work environment I sometimes like to just turn off the music while keeping the headphones on to isolate a bit of the office din and white noise.  I've learned to just turn the amp off during these occasions to eliminate the noise and also accept the warm-up time when I'm ready to listen to music again.  The warm-up doesn't take long at all, so this is a compromise I'm willing to make.  I would definitely recommend this amp to anyone looking to push their high impedance headphones, but I do wish that it had a bass boost feature.  I may try out a FiiO E10K amp at some point down the road, but for now this amp is pretty sweet.  I'm sure that I'll be able to sell it for close to what I paid should I want to make a switch in the future.

product_title: BT-1000 On-Ear Bluetooth Headphones Wireless + Wired Technology Headset Stereo Built-in Mic for Hands Free Calling
review_body:
I have to say that I am largely disappointed with these headphones. I've been using them for a few months and I'm firmly ready to throw them away. Here's why:

Pros:
+ The audio quality is decent. These aren't top of the line headphones, but I'm not listening to top of the line audio either. When the audio is playing from video games and Youtube/Netflix, I haven't had too many complaints. (caveat in cons section)
+ Battery life is acceptable. When listening to audio, I haven't had them cut out yet.

Cons:
- There is no support from the manufacturer for these headphones. Driver support is non-existant. I use these headhpones with the price bundled SoundBot SB340 BT adapter on a Win 7 Pro computer. The above mentioned caveat is that, roughly 70% of the time, my system is unable to correctly identify or use the headphones. Stereo and Mono audio are for some reason two different drivers for this headphone system, and Windows is frequently confused about what is available and what isn't.
- The headphone charges via a 3.5 mm barrel jack (product provides USB to 3.5 mm barrel cord). In the current world, I can find usb to usb cords very easily, but usb to barrel jack is uncommon in your average store. This means that, if you lose the cord for some reason, it'll take extra time to find a new charger cord. This is phenomenally inconvenient and should have been included in the product description so I could decide if I actually wanted to keep track of another cord type.
- On Windows, none of the audio playback controls work. This is probably because, again, the drivers are generic windows drivers that the headset doesn't actually work with.

Bottom Line:
I hate these things as computer headphones. Maybe they'd work better if used with a cell phone or other portable device, but I'm not willing to screw around with them anymore. If feel like headphones should have all the simplicity of "plug and play", I don'trecommend these. If you're willing to fiddle with settings to figure out the optimal way to get these to work, then please write a blog post and upload any necessary software to the web. I've done my best to look and I can't find anything online at this point.

product_title: APC Smart-UPS 750VA UPS Battery Backup with Pure Sine Wave Output (SMT750)
review_headline: Pure Sine Wave but Different HW Versions and Constant Annoying Hum/Whine
review_body:
Due to shipping issues that I will not go into, I ended up buying my APC units in person at a retail supply store.

I have some important feedback regarding these units for anyone considering purchasing one.

I bought a new desktop computer with a PSU that requires pure sine wave input and all of my existing APC units (CS, BK, etc.) output an approximated step wave when running on battery. The SMC series is the cheapest APC product line that I could actually find in stock anywhere that outputs pure sine wave when running on battery. (Note: there are other manufacturers that make backups that output pure sine wave when on battery and these units are cheaper than APC ones but I did not test any of them.) I notified a dealer that's about a 2 hour drive for me to let me know when they received new units. That way, I could come and test it out in the store. I did this because I had read a lot of negative feedback about both the SMC and SMT series of backups.

The two SMC units I tried (SMC1000 and SMC1500) were very loud compared to all of my other old units. All other APC backups that I've purchased in stores (probably 20+ units over the years) are virtually 100% silent when operating normally (fan does not run at all and there is NO noise) and when on battery, you hear only a little bit of noise from the fan. You have to literally put your ear 1 inch away from these units to hear anything when they're running on AC. However, for the SMC units, the fan runs constantly and you can hear the units across the room. More importantly, the SMC units emit some kind of constant hum or whine. It is very annoying and I could not stand it. It also drove my dog crazy. I brought the SMC1500 home for a few days and the whine was very noticeable at the base of my stairs, with the unit installed upstairs between the wall and a cabinet. When the battery kicks on, the fan really speeds up and the whine also gets a louder. This whine noise is emitted as soon as you power the unit on--not a single device plugged into it, so it has nothing to do with what's plugged into the unit. Due to this annoying whine, I took the unit back.

In several places, I read that the pricier SMT series were quieter so I decided to try one of those--SMT1500. The constant whine/buzz is still present but it is not as loud as on the SMC units I examined. Also, the fan ran much slower when not on battery. I decided that this was acceptable so I purchased and APC 9630 network management card for it (more on that in a moment). This SMT was manufactured in May 2015. When I decided to pick up a second SMT1500, I was disappointed because its fan was much louder when operating on AC power. This unit was manufactured in March of 2015 so I wondered if it was a hardware change. The fan was so much louder that I took the unit back. Later I purchased another SMT1500 and this one was manufactured in July of 2015 and it exhibited behavior like my first (the May 2015) one. So right out of the box, new from the manufacturer, some of these units exhibit different hardware characteristics. I should mention that on all three of the SMT1500 units, the factory firmware version was the same--9.2 ID 18.

So then I ordred another 9630 card for this second unit. Meanwhile, I installed a 9630 in my first SMT1500 unit. It is very straight forward and I did not have any problems. If you search on YouTube, APC has a video with a step by step guide on installing and configuring the network card. I will provide my details below, for reference:
-Power down unit and disconnect battery
-Remove rear Smart card cover
-Insert card and tighten screws
-Connect battery and plug in unit (no need to power on)
-Connect one end of the serial cable supplied with the card to the Console port on the card and connect the other to your computer. The other end is a standard DB9 serial connector and I did not have any puters old enough to have a serial port so I used a serial to USB adapter.
-The APC instructional video that I mentioned uses the old HyperTerminal application (that got removed in Win7) to configure the card. To get HyperTerminal on my Win8 machine, I copied the Hyper* files from the I386 folder on an old WinXP CD that I had lying around. Those files end with .XY_ and all you have to do is use the EXPAND command to uncompress them. Then just run the .exe. This gets you HyperTerminal. The video explains step by step how to do the rest.

Next, I hit the IP I specified for the unit in my browser and I was able to login to the web interface with no problems. I had downloaded the 9.3 ID 18 ENC firmware file from APC's site. I selected the Update firmware option, uploaded the file, and let the process run. About 8 minutes later, it finished and the firmware update was successful--VERY EASY.

So later when my second network card arrived, I repeated the install process in my other SMT1500--that went fine. But when I hit the web interface and tried to upgrade the firmware using the same file I had used for my other unit, it failed--it said something like XMODEM disconnected. This left my unit running but not turned on and the fan was running at full speed. I could toggle through the menu options but the power button did not respond. I had to pull the power cord and disconnect the battery and turn it back on. I tried two more times, thinking it was just a fluke, but I got the same results. Then I started asking myself what was different about this time compared to the first? Then I remembered that I had used Chrome the first time and this time, kind of by accident, I had used IE 11. So I opened Chrome, logged into the web UI, uploaded the file, and let it go. It finished successfully, without any problems. So keep this in mind--the upgrade process can be quirky. However, I was very happy to see that upgrading the firmware did not affect the idle fan speed because I was hoping that it wouldn't cause the fan to run faster. My fans barely turn when the unit is on AC power--if you put your hand beside the fan vents, you can feel a very, very small amount of air flow coming out.

So overall, I would like to stress that if you have always been used to store-bought APC backups, like the CS, BK, ES, etc., models, and you think that you will just plop one of these SMC or SMT models in the floor beside your desk or wherever and everything will be same, THING AGAIN. This was a real wake up call for me. I had always taken for granted the fact that APC battery backups are totally silent except for when running on battery. Keep in mind that the SMC and SMT units will emit a hum/whine and the fan will run constantly (the speed, it seems, will vary depending on the hardware configuration). And I'm not just being picky. I promise you that you will notice this hum/whine/squeal noise even when standing across the room away from the unit. I guess that consumers must rarely purchase either one of these product lines because otherwise, I can't imagine APC not doing something about the annoying whine noise. But when these things are sitting in server rooms in the mix of a lot of other noisy fans and equipment, you would never hear them.

I highly recommend getting a 9630 card. It is very nice being able to sit down at your computer and login to the web interface for the backup because you can see and managed all of the settings without having to fiddle around with the buttons and menu system on the front of the unit. You can also configure settings via the web interface that you cannot get access to via the control panel on the front of the unit.ers old enough to have a serial port so I used a serial to USB adapter.

product_title: Altec Lansing BX1521 12W 2.1 Speaker System with Subwoofer
review_headline: Poor balance between sub and satellites
review_body:
I don't consider myself an audiophile, but, after 10+ years with a substantial set of Boston Accoustics and a SONOS system in the house, I am a bit picky. Unfortunately, the BA speakers have finally bit the dust and I'm on the hunt for a replacement. These are not it.

The build quality is... okay. The satellites are housed in a decently sturdy silver metallic plastic, while the sub is constructed of a moderately thick, laminated MDF. Neither are as hefty as I would prefer, and are quite a bit lighter than I expected.

As to the audio quality, I am disappointed. A previous computer came with a set of Altecs years ago, and they were a well-balanced set of speakers. These -- not as much. The highs and mids are very clear, very crisp, even at high volumes; the acoustic guitar work I was listening to sounds pretty darn good. I only wish the subwoofer were up to the challenge! It seems underpowered, given the strength and clarity of the satellites. So, songs from the Tron: Legacy soundtrack (for example) felt a bit top heavy, and lacked the strong bassline that is the backbone for the album, even with the sub cranked to full.

For this price, I know not to expect the same quality as my BA speakers. At the same time, I don't use the PC speakers as often, so a greater expenditure is hard to justify. I still hoped for something a little better from Altec for the money. These are going back to the brick and mortar I purchased them from. Time to keep looking...

(It's ok if I de-ground the laptop, but there's still a tiny bit of radio noise at higher volumes when I pause my music.) Even just plugging in my premium shielded patch cable from Monoprice creates interference (and loud hum, of course, if I touch the tip). I tried using the grounding wire, but that didn't seem to help much.

TIPS:
-put you device's volume at 100% and use the iHome's (flaky) control to control volume. This reduces overall volume and noise.
- tweaking the selected radio station won't help; the patch cable (and power cable?) is acting as an antenna, and the interfering station is whatever happens to pick up.

review_body: I bought two of these in a row and they both had exactly the same defect, the sockets would not receive a plug.  This of course would defeat the whole purpose of a smart plug, being unable to plug anything into it.  The first one I returned because I thought it might be a one-off glitch, however, exactly the same thing happened with the second one.  I finally figured out what the deal was with the second one.  Right out of the box, I tested to make sure it would receive a plug and it did.  After I went through the set-up process and got it connected to my router and recognized by the app, it no longer would receive a plug.  That made me think there was some mechanical switch, so I tried forcing it.  Which ended up, I inadvertently popped the plug open.  I don't recommend doing this on purpose, however, because it exposed all these chips and circuits and it might void the warranty.  But sure enough, I was able to eyeball the obstruction.  Some kind of janky spring mechanism that theoretically would slide away if you inserted a plug.  Guess what Amcrest, it fails easily.  Anyways I removed the mechanism and my plug went easily into the socket.  I have no idea what purpose if any this mechanism serves other than causing the whole device to fail.  And the way it is put together, it would seem to have a high rate of failure.  What is the use of a clever smart plug if it doesn't do the basic thing, i.e., receive a plug??????

review_body: I ordered and received the black cables, and I'm very disappointed with the quality. They are simply too brittle--right out of the box, without any exposure to extreme temperatures or UV. Normally cable ties can bend around uneven surfaces and be pulled quite tight without breaking, and I've often given the loose ends of cable ties an extra pull with some pliers to make them more snug...and I've only had them break if I apply a great deal of force. These can break when they are hand-tightened, and they cannot tolerate an abrupt bend at all. Just to make sure I wasn't judging them unfairly, and got out some of my other cable ties and tried bending them back on themselves, pinching them near the bend with my fingers, and they didn't break. I did the same with one of these, it was remarkably easy to reduce the entire cable tie to a pile of tiny pieces. That might be fine if you plan to use them in very light-duty applications, and don't need small radius loops or a truly snug fit, but I'll be returning mine.

product_title: Sennheiser PX-200 II Headphones Precision On-Ear Sealed PX200-II
review_headline: Decent above-average headphones for the price
review_body:
Overall: Decent headphones for the cost, but I wouldn't buy them again or recommend them to a friend.

Positive: The sound quality is decent after they're burned in, they're loud, very lightweight and very portable, good build quality, they probably won't break easily. Again, for only being $60 you get what you pay for and they're noticeably not "just some cheap headphones".

Negative: They aren't comfortable. The reason I wanted to go with small, on-ear headphones is because my supra-aural headphones hurt after several hours of wearing them due to the weight. Unfortunately, these headphones clamp too tightly and they hurt my ears after 2-3 hours of listening. It doesn't really work for long bus/train rides or all-day listening because of this, it just gets too uncomfortable and I need to take them off for a break. Also I know they're supposed to be portable, but the cord is a little short. Would prefer if it had another foot or two. It's hard to use them with a computer because of it unless you have an extension

About the sound quality / texture: In general is sounds like a slightly above average, modern, closed-ear headphone, which isn't really my favorite but I don't hate it either. The highs and mids are very "smooth" sounding and have pretty good separation. The bass is loud but it's not that clear, the separation isn't very good in the lower ranges, but you can definitely feel it. I'm not really a fan of this because I think if the headphone is going to be oriented towards the lower frequencies, it should at least have great clarity in those frequencies, and I don't think the PX-200 II achieves that. EQing down the lower frequences makes them somewhat more listenable for me.

review_body: First of all this is a very cool idea and I really wanted this device to work.  However, I could never get the device to work properly while connected to a USB 3.0 port.  The advertised product clearly states that USB 3.0 at 5 gbps is supported, but from my experience it doesn't.  Connected to a USB 3.0 port (which I know works fine with other USB 3.0 devices and hard drives), I tried both a 2.5 inch laptop spinning drive and an SSD drive.  Neither could keep a stable connection long enough to be formatted.  They would disconnect and reconnect over and over.  After several attempts, I did finally manage to get one of the drives formatted.  I then tried to copy a 5 GB file to it.  The speed was in the range of 10 MBs to 20 MBs and then the connection dropped after a couple of seconds.  I tried to copy the file several more times, but the same thing happened.  Then I plugged it into a an USB 2.0 port and was able to format and copy files with no problem.  The speed when copying the 5 GB file on the USB 2.0 port averaged around 23 MBs.  So, yes it works, but not as advertised and it is not stable when connected to a USB 3.0 port.  I would not recommend this device unless you are happy with USB 2.0 speeds.  I bought this hoping to be able to use it at USB 3.0 speeds and so that I wouldn't have to take drives in and out of my external hard drive enclosures all the time.  But this device isn't stable enough to do that.

Again the problem is mainly from the their software, User Interface. It again and again had trouble to update the media library after the ALAC lossless files were transferred to its MicroSD card successfully. The media library updating process either freezes when reading certain file or simply shows a white screen with no button can push to get out except the reset button.
The support from the forum is no support at all. I have to register twice with different Username and Passcode to stay in the forum cause it locked me out even with my correct information. I posted two times with different question and problems of the unit. The posts were never replied by tech support except asking me to down one ALAC file for texting. After I further explained the problem is not signal files but reading bunch of files. My case was left with no reply at all.
Now, I would like to tell Fiio that the very MicroSD card formatted as X3, with over 1400 songs is playing flawlessly in iBasso DX50. The ALAC files from iTunes don't have any problem. The Fiio X3ii has problem!
With the easiness of setup and control with touch screen instead of rotary wheel, user replaceable battery (Sumsung S3) and sound quality, iBasso DX50 is the clear winer!

review_headline: There is literally no way this cable performs better than any other HDMI cable that is not falling ...
review_body:
A digital signal is a digital signal. The sent data is checked on receipt by the computer/TV. There is literally no way this cable performs better than any other HDMI cable that is not falling apart. It merely sends zeros and ones. Not one damned thing more. There was a time when the cable quality actually meant something (analog signals from/to analog devices), but these cables aren't sending the music/video any more... they are just sending zeros and ones which are then checked and decoded by the processor on the other end. Anything that can send a digital signal... that is literally just not falling apart... will work flawlessly for any application.

This is an insanely overpriced item and the top raters are either magnificently misinformed, lying, or in need of mental help...

review_headline: Only $49.95 - Good for the Price but Keep Expectations In Check

Good for the price, but keep your expectations in check.

However the button layout is seriously frustrating. the locations of the volume buttons aren't intuitive, and I can never remember where they are relative to the center button - same is true for the next track/previous track buttons. They're organized in a circle without logic.

The phone button/media start button is easy enough to use. Not sure why there has to be a big light on the side, very annoying to see that blinking light out of the corner of my eye when I'm outside in the early morning hours.

Ultimately, I would buy this again. Unless of course a better device appears on the market.

product_title: Bluedio BS-2 (Camel) Mini Bluetooth Speakers Portable Wireless Speakers 3D Surround System (Champagne Gold)
review_headline: It was in good condition. Took out the unit from the box ...
review_body:
First of all, I just want to say the delivery was extra fast with Amazon Prime and I was able to receive the unit on Sunday in my location.

Now on with the review. I received the unit on Sunday and checked the packaging. It was in good condition.Took out the unit from the box and charged it for a couple of hours. Take out the user manual which was tiny and I basically had to take a magnify glass just to read the instructions.

I followed the instruction to pair the unit to my iPhone 6 Plus by pressing the power button until the blue and orange LED lights were alternating. It was easy peazy, lemon squeezy. Played a couple of songs to test the lows, middle and high frequencies. For a unit its size, it produced enough music power. I believe maybe in the 85dB range. Don't quote me as I did not measure the dB. It's just my guess. It was loud and good enough for my 600 square feet living room. The only drawbacks were that there were no bass and/or middle frequencies. It sounds tiny and was hurting my ears with all the high frequencies.

I wasn't expecting much from $24.99, but definitely this unit cannot compare to a JBL Charge (I got for $79.99) or the JAMBOX. And definitely it will not compare to a Bose Mini @ $299.99.

So I wanted to know why this speaker cannot compare to the competitors. For one, it does not have a passive radiator or port that the JBL, JAMBOX or Bose all have. So it's not going to be "All About the Bass". I decided to hook it up to my Laptop to find out the frequencies response. Eureka! It can do 50Hz-20kHz, but whoever tuned this speaker made it about the high frequencies that the low and middle were totally GONE!!!

Now why would any sound engineer do that!!! Using my EQ, I lowered the 6kHz, 12kHz, 14kHz and 16kHz to -10dB and increase the 60Hz, 170Hz, 310Hz, 600Hz, and 1kHz to +10dB. I also increase the gain to about +3dB. Now it was comparable to JBL Charge that has an audio output of 5W x 2 and I can finally hear the bass and mid frequencies. I wish I have a way to write this to the unit, but I can't.

Conclusion: for the price it's OK. I like the hands-free calling. I like the Bluetooth 4.1 which I was able to have my iPhone upstairs and still can connect to the speaker downstairs. I like the design and the AUX input, but I do NOT like that the sound engineer did not tune this speaker to its potential! It could have competed at the $79.99 price range!

product_title: Pioneer SC-81 7.2 Channel Networked Class D3 AV Receiver with HDMI 2.0 (Black)
review_body: SEE UPDATE AT THE BOTTOM OF THIS REVIEW  In the tradition of Elite Pioneer A/V Receivers, the SC-87 is a great product. Setup was very easy and the sound is crystal clear. Just hook everything up, place the included microphone in the seating position and let the receiver calibrate itself. Couldn't be simpler. If you still want to tweak things, you can go into the menus and adjust multi-band equalizers and level adjustments for each channel.  For me, this is an upgrade from the Pioneer SC-55. I wanted 4K pass through and Dolby Atmos. I went ahead and purchased 4 Onkyo Dolby Atmos speakers (the ones that reflect sound from the ceiling) and so far they are working great with this receiver. Dolby Atmos sounds awesome. Free Dolby Atmos demo material can be streamed from Vudu and there are some Dolby Atmos movies available on Blu-Ray.  Now some of the cons. Switching between video sources can be very slow sometimes taking up to 10 seconds. This is normal. HDMI handshaking is always tricky and for some reason, this particular model takes more time than any other receiver I've owned. Not a deal breaker, you just need to be patient. Another minor item to mention is how long the receiver takes when you turn it on. It takes about 5 seconds. Some universal remotes (like the Harmony remotes) start sending commands before 5 seconds so you will need to program a delay into the remote. Take note, this receiver is limited to 9 channels. Dolby Atmos is limited to 5.2.4 (5 surround, 2 subwoofers and 4 ceiling speakers). You can NOT do 7.1.4 or 7.2.4. If you really want those back surround speakers, you need to go to another brand.  I would highly recommend using the iControlAV5 app for your mobile device. You can control the functions of the SC-87 more easily instead of using the onscreen menus built into the receiver. You can also easily switch between surround modes.  Speaking of surround modes, this receiver will upconvert any stereo audio signal to Atmos. While watching a 5.1 movie, simply switch the receiver to "Dolby Surround" and you will get audio from all speakers (up to 9 channels).  Overall, great receiver. You can find this product at great prices (well below the retail price) so look around a bit. Well worth the money and will elevate you to the latest and greatest home theater sound.  UPDATE:  At first I gave this receiver a glowing review. Well, after owning this receiver for the past 7 months I have decided to upgrade to this year's model due to lack of HDCP 2.2. Also, I was having HDMI switching issues which caused the receiver to lock up. I don't think it's the receiver itself, but more that my components just don't play nice with it. Still would recommend if you don't care about using future 4K devices. The Dolby Atmos is quite amazing!

product_title: Winegard FL-55YR FlatWave Amplified Razor Thin HDTV Indoor Antenna (Certified Refurbished)
review_body:
It's an antenna, so its operation is going to be governed by the laws of physics. It's pretty large (a bit bigger than a US Letter piece of paper), but has a white side and a black side so you can try to make it blend in with your house.

I found that it worked best in a window oriented towards the signal in the way you'd expect (vertically). The instructions also indicate that it can receive signals placed perpendicular to (i.e. "slicing") the direction of the TV transmitter, but had no luck this way.

It picks up the channels that various antenna websites say a 30-mile antenna should at my place. Channels right on the border (25-30 miles) don't come in reliably in all conditions. In my experience the range rating is honest but don't expect some kind of beyond-specifications magic.

Mine was refurbished and came with 2 3M mounting tape strips. These were sufficient to attach the antenna but as it's floppy 4 would have been nicer.

review_headline: Mediocre isolation, choppy connection, average quality sound
review_body:
Not sure where these overwhelmingly positive reviews are coming from. Received and fully charged them last night, wore them on my subway commute this morning. Note that I haven't owned a pair of BT headphones before, so perhaps these perform well in comparison, and for $150 maybe I'm expecting too much, but these comments are made compared to my (then) $225 Sennheiser Adidas HD 25s and $25 Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones with Mic and Nylon Cable (Red):

1. Sound isolation is 5/10, even by passive standards.
2. They get hot. 30 minutes of wear and my ears were sweating.
3. Sound quality is 7/10. I don't have experience with bluetooth headphones before, but I was surprised at how low the volume was when the speakers started to max out.
4. Most importantly: choppy connection. Moderately windy with light rain (under an umbrella), to get a clear connection I had to take the phone (iPhone 5s) out of my pocket. Even under ideal conditions, streaming from Spotify was choppy (though in the same conditions using the Music app was not) For a product that allegedly has a 150-ft range, I was surprised that it was so sensitive to environmental conditions.

I'll give it another day or so and update this review if things change, but right now it's looking like a return.

review_headline: They pop out easily so need to put in the ear clips on ...
review_body:
This is my first wireless headphones. Well to say I am not very much impressed with it. But its just 35$ so frankly i should not be expecting too much. Few things which I have noticed using it for few days.
1. It won't stay into your ears constantly if ear hooks/clips are not attached when you are running or jogging. They pop out easily so need to put in the ear clips on the buds.
2. The length of the cable is not long enough so when I keep the cord on behind my neck while running it tries to pull by the right side where the volume up and down and other control switch box and hence you have to all the time keep on adjusting the ear buds back into the ear or keep throwing the switch box back over the neck which is annoying. Well you can solve this my keeping the cord in front of your neck but that something you have to live with.
3 Bluetooth connection is not that awesome. When i walk in different rooms when my phone lies in one it just goes away. Its okay not awesome connection.

It will behave like a 35$ headphone donot expect too much. It is good for starters. If you specifically looking for running then this is not for you. I had never got a wireless headphones so was skeptical about getting over 100$ plus headphones but now after buying these I would go for a better one. If you are just looking for a regular use it works great. It connects with the phone, when turned on I haven't had any issue. The blue blinking light is annoying when you are laying at night with all lights turned off listening to music when going to sleep it is too annoying. I just keep in under my shirt to keep it from hitting my eye.

In all an okay product if you are looking for less than 50 bucks then its ok, not a work out headphones for sure. One thing I have learned over the period of years, quality never comes cheap and this one proves that.

review_headline: This product is the Leader of the Bluetooth Speakers of Mediocrity.
review_body:
Over View at bottom
The Magicbox did not reach all my expectations, I've had it for about a week and here are some quick pros and cons.
Pros-
Easy connect: I didn't read any documentation and I was hooked up after I turned the speaker on within two minutes.
Acceptable Sound Quality: For it's size and price it sounds okay to me,But this is not totally a pro, The sound DOES sound like it is coming from a very small source, which the speaker is quite small.
Battery Life: I haven't had a problem with battery life, however I don't use it all day, I charge it at night and it hasn't run out of batteries yet.
Portability: Very Small, Very Portable.
Cons-
Range: I know Bluetooth is short range but this is ridiculous, If your phone is on the other end of a short table the sound quality starts going out, If you are 5 feet away you disconnect. This product works well within about 0-2 feet.
Delay: There is quite a delay that you won't really notice if all you do is play music. If you navigate through menus that have sound effects, or if you play a game using this speaker, you will notice a good 1-2 second delay.

-----Over View-----
overall the magicbox has sound quality that is just acceptable(I'm not a sound snob), is very portable, and has an acceptable battery life. While I find the range and the delay slightly annoying. Given the price, I don't regret the purchase.

review_headline: Mine might be defective, or are they all this way?

It disconnects when audio stops mostly, or when a streaming audio service takes some time to load the next track, but sometimes it will disconnect at random. Half of the time it does so with a constant shrieking tone that forces me to turn the speaker off and back on again. I'd say for a full battery charge I need to reconnect it 3-4 times because it loses connection.

Also it seems to only work in close proximity to the source of the audio. I get more than 10 feet from it and it starts to get choppy.

Other than these obvious problems it would be a worthwhile purchase. Sound quality is decent enough and much better/louder than my phone/ipad2/macbook built in speaker (good thing right?). I've taken it to the park, worked fine. I've used it for a small fire spinning party/practice (4 people) and we could at least hear the music over the fire (when you spin fire poi etc., the fire can easily be too loud to hear your music and mess up your flow).

I considered that it could be just the battery needs to be charged, and when the battery is low it DOES disconnect much more, but even with a full charge it acts up. If only it would not cut out and have a better range I'd give it 5 stars

review_headline: The speaker that I received was junk and so was it's replacement!!!!!
review_body: I was set on purchasing another speaker when I came across the Polaris.  I really liked the fact that the Polaris accepted a mini SD card and that the battery could be replaced.  After a couple of days of careful consideration I decided to go with the Polaris.  Unfortunately, I now wish I would have went with my 1st choice.  The first thing that I noticed was that the unit I received is slightly different than the one pictured.  Mine doesn't have the Polaris logo on the front (was I shipped an older model? I think this is called \\"bait and switch\\") and the speaker grill is the same color red as the rest of the unit and not a slightly contrasting color like in the photo.  I think it looks \\"cheap\\" in person.  As far as the grill goes I will take a little of the blame because I didn't look at the other photos that show a closer likeness to the actual product, but the main photo is deceiving.  I don't care at what angle I look at the speaker I doesn't look like the photo.  Before purchasing the Polaris I auditioned three other bluetooth speakers and the Polaris was the only one that had substantial lag.  It was out of sync enough when watching videos (I tried many different video sources) that I just couldn't take it.  I suppose that if you are only going to listen to music that the Polaris might work for you, but if you don't need a replaceable battery or SD slot I would go with something else.    *Doesn't read any of my micro SD cards? Also doesn't lock SD card into place except my new 32g micro SD Card which I had to use tweezers to extract from the \\"socket\\".  Drops blue tooth connection (the 2 other speakers I've used didn't do this) from only 2 feet.    I am a bit miffed about this. I purchased it mainly for use with my laptop for an online class that starts tomorrow. I also wanted to take advantage of the SD card feature and purchased a new micro SD card specifically for this unit which got a bit scratched up while trying to remove it from the unit before I sent itback.    REVIEW OF REPLACEMENT SPEAKER (SPEAKER #2):    I had to laugh!    I sent my 1st unit back because it was different than the one pictured, the micro SD slot was messed up and didn't work, and it would drop the Bluetooth signal and had a horrible lag.  Guess what?  The replacement unit showed up in a box that had previously been open (broken seal) and I found the unit itself covered in black marks (like it had been used), marks and a dent on the gill, and what seems to be sand!  The highest concentration of the sand like substance is on the bottom of the unit's feet.  The good things are that they sent the same item as is shown in the photo this time, the micro SD slot works, and it has less off a \\"lag\\" than the last one.  I want to try it out a little to see if it performs any better than the last which will determine if I will exchange it one more time or just get a refund and find something else.

product_title: Beats Studio Wireless Over-Ear Headphones
review_body: The Beats Studio headphones sound good, are extremely comfortable, have solid battery life, and come with a bunch of accessories. But the active noise canceling (ANC) feature needs some tuning. To keep this review simple, two major revisions would make this feature great. The first would be it actually working! The level of ANC (and the white noise hiss that comes with it) does not adjust, ever. This stays true regardless of the type of music you listen to, or the level of outside noise. So their is no "automatic" change Beats claims. The second revision would be a companion app (like the Parrot headphones) that allows users to adjust the level of ANC manually. Letting users control the level of ANC to match the environment (home vs. on a plane) would be great! If it were't for the ANC issue, I would give these a solid 4/5 stars. Maybe even higher at the discounted price Amazon is offering on the matte black. I should note that if you only plan to use these in noisy environments, the ANC noise may not be as intrusive.

review_headline: Good noise cancellation, okay sound quality, garbage craftsmanship
review_body: these headphones should only be purchased for their noise canceling abilities.  The sound quality is otherwise nothing special.  The craftsmanship sucks.  Literally it is garbage. Having one stop working is aggravating, having two go smacks of incompetent design and craftsmanship.  Not what one expects with a $299 product which is at the top of the price range for consumer headphones (with maybe one or two exceptions), and definitely not what you'd expect from a company that appears to pride itself on quality and performance.  I'd be wary and wouldn't buy them again after having two break.  If you do get them, be sure to register the purchase with Bose, so you can take advantage of the warranty and get them replaced for free if they stop working. I sent it back and just brought home the new TDK a360 which is only $179.00 at bestbuy (why $280 on amazon I have no idea) .... the TDK sounds AWESOME, and comes with handy treble and bass controls, but we will see in a few days how the battery life holds up.

[[VIDEOID:20a928123a746e60c7737a7e542bc9b2]] I was looking to replace my old Jambox that was on its last breath and was looking for a new speaker that is durable, LOUD, has decent-ish sound, and all at a good value (no big deal if lost or damaged).

Durability - 4 STARS.
This thing is very durable and would probably stand up to anything other than prolonged dunking underwater. That said it's a bit clunky but not overly so.

Loudness - 5 STARS
Delivers on volume BIG TIME. Check the video. This thing at 70% absolutely blows away the Jambox at 100%. Not even close. Big time volume here.

Sound - 2 STARS
Despite its size and wattage the sound is pretty subpar. This thing basically has no bass and very little dynamic range. It's all mids and highs and pretty tinny, although serviceable if you're just looking to bring something along to the beach or to leave on a porch or in the backyard. You can hear how much richer the sound from the Jambox is in the video, although so so quiet. At this price compared to $100+ for the Jambox sound compromise is expected...was just hoping not to have to compromise THIS much.

Value - 4 STARS
Despite its \\"meh\\" sound it's durable, loud, and only about $35. I'd say you get a pretty good value here.

Overall - 3.5 STARS

I like this guy but I'm going to keep looking. I'd be willing to spend $15 more to get better sound. But I'm going to hold on to it for the time being just in case my search proves fruitless.
