product_title: Yubi Power Universal Power Strip 2 Outlets for 110v-250v Worldwide
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:2468300e1cc05196f00615a1ff3f1a24]]I like the idea of a compact travel adapter like this Yubi Power Strip a lot, but the product has several major design flaws keeping it from being a first-rate product. First, to eliminate any confusion, it is intended primarily for use by travellers coming to the US, not for US travellers going abroad. The 3-prong plug is a standard plug used in North America and is known by its NEMA designation as \\"5-15\\". NEMA 5-15 receptacles are the most common sockets found found in homes, businesses, and public places in North America. If you are traveling abroad, you will need something else, like a socket adapter kit.

That having been said, this power strip will fit most devices from other countries, with 2 USB ports at the end (one 1 A, one 2.4 A). Make sure you verify the voltage needed on your device before plugging it into the electrical socket though, to prevent damage. The shortcomings? Let's start with the cord. The product description is completely wrong. It is not 2 feet. It's 15\\", and just short enough to be inconvenient in most places. The power strip does not touch the floor and hangs on one end on most of my wall sockets. This makes the power strip useful only when the socket is very close to a surface, like a kitchen counter or desk. There's no nail hole on the back of the strip to mount it to a wall like other power strips have. The plug rotation is not adjustable and unfortunately, my sideways receptacles are oriented with the grounding pin on the right side, so the plug points up when plugged in. I checked my extension cords and other right angled power strip plugs. The round grounding pin is always aligned so it's closest to the wire, not rotated like this. I don't know why Yubi Power designed it this way. My other plugs fit sideways or hang down, not point up like the Yubi.

Lastly, a minor point is the lack of an ON/OFF switch. Overall, a good idea hampered by too short of a cord and non-standard grounding pin orientation. Manufacturer provided evaluation unit.

UPDATE: 3/5/15 - Yubi Power has corrected the cord length in the product description to 15\\" instead of 2 ft. However, my assessment still stands. The cord is too short and the orientation of the grounding pin is a major inconvenience.

product_title: Logitech Harmony Ultimate Home [Discontinued by Manufacturer]
review_headline: Capable Replacement for my Harmony 900 that had recharging "issues"
review_body: This purchase was a replacement for my very-capable Harmony 900 that no longer would recharge (even with a new OEM battery), and the 900 was a replacement for my favorite-Harmony-of-all-time Harmony One which also had to be retired because of a recharging issue and couldn't be used anymore. (See a theme here?). So why would I continue to purchase another Harmony remote?  Because when a Harmony works, it very capably combines/substitutes for my six OEM "universal" remotes (Sony BluRay, Sony VHS, Roku, Onkyo Receiver, Sony flat screen LCD, Cisco/Verizon STB) all of which seem to only be semi-universal in spite of what their operator manuals proclaim.  This beastie continues along the path that every succeeding generation Logitech Harmony remote's setup is at least double the complexity and frustration of the previous generation. Very limited setup instructions included in the box with this unit. You must setup using the mandatory iPhone/Android/PC app, which, at best, is confusing and limited.  This Harmony Ultimate Home remote's layout is a bit of a setback from the Harmony One/900 layout, although the hard buttons seem to function well and they're easy to locate in the dark. The soft buttons on the screen are really useless if you only use your thumb while you hold the remote. I find I have to use two hands, one to hold the remote, and the other to actually get the direct-channel-number soft buttons to recognize a touch. This deficiency is almost enough to get me to return the Harmony Ultimate Home. I'll continue to try to figure out another way to do direct-channel-number input for the next 30 days before my amazon return period expires.  It also appears you can't change the order of the soft button "Activities" once they've been added with the set-up app. You can change the Activities order with the Android app on your smart phone, sync with the hub, then sync your remote with the hub, but the Activities ordering doesn't get modified/saved on the remote. Maybe there's a way to change the order on the remote, but since there's very little help available, it may take awhile to figure out if there's a way to do this on the remote.  I have no clue how the IR magic of the "hub" works, as there's really no line-of-sight for the IR which apparently shoots through the perimeter plexiglass of the hub to actually "see" all of my media components. I placed the hub on top of my media base cabinet under my flat screen, and somehow the BluRay, STB, receiver, and VHS communicate okay from behind the glass doors inside the media cabinet below the hub. Go figure. The only function that doesn't seem to reliably work solely with the remote/hub is volume up/down for the receiver. It'll work sometimes, but not without fiddling. I changed the location of the hub in relation to the receiver, but the volume up/down was still flaky. I ended up placing one of the IR blasters inside the base cabinet directly in front of the receiver, and that seems to have eliminated the issue with the volume up/down issue.  I'll update my review here after I've used my new Harmony Ultimate Home for a few weeks.  JULY 21, 2015 UPDATE: With the help of a comment to my review here, I was able to easily re-order the soft buttons' Activities. I also ended up installing the second IR blaster so all of my components in my TV base cabinet respond flawlessly with the control puck using both IR blasters. I still don't like the remote's hard buttons layout (I frequently/accidentally hit the mute button when I'm really only trying to reduce volume, but the buttons are so closely co-located mute happens more often than volume-down). Overall, though, a really terrific universal remote system.

review_headline: Okay, but there are other options
review_body:
I just started looking for bookshelf speakers and after reading rave reviews, the Zensor 1's were on my short list to audition.

I had high expectations but I found the speakers to be veiled in the midrange, adversely affecting vocals. The bass was muddy and the soundstage was small. Perhaps my expectations were too high for a $400 speaker. The same day I auditioned the Wharfedale Diamond 220's. They were $50 less and sounded better, but still had a veiled midrange. However, for $350, they are a good deal.

I have no horse in this race and I do not work for any of these speaker companies. Audio has been a hobby of mine, on and off for 30 + years. My recommendation to anyone looking to purchase is to audition these for yourself as well as some more expensive speakers to see how they differ. That will also reveal areas of weakness. Then, you will be able to determine what is important to you and how much you will need to pay to find something you enjoy.

product_title: Sylvania SCR1053 Jumbo Digit Dual Alarm Clock Radio with Blue LED
review_headline: If all you need is a clock...
review_body: If it was more expensive, I'd send it back. I needed to replace my clock radio after the dangly antenna wire from my other one was the victim of a tragic canister vac-related incident and I could no longer get FM. Not that I minded AM until one of my neighbors acquired some sort of device that causes my radio to make regularly spaced chirps around the time I wake up. Let me start off by saying I'm one of those people who doesn't usually read the manual. In fact, stupidly, I recycled it before realizing I'd need it. Though after finding it online, I can say it's nearly no help at all. The instructions skip important steps and don't actually work as written (what exactly is this magical standby mode and how does one get there? part of the problem is not knowing if the radio is on or off...see my comments on reception below). I mean, are buttons really so expensive that each button has to encode 12 different functions to be cost effective? And given that this is a clock with giant numbers for the very nearsighted and/or seniors, are you sure your target audience is going to figure this out at all? Hello? Marketing? And excellent reception my aunt Sally, my clock whose dangling wire antenna was lost to my overzealous canister hoovering currently gets better reception sans antenna. And unfortunately, this clock filters out static, so it's not actually clear when it's on or off. I have yet to locate a gradual wake function as advertised. I set it for tomorrow, not sure if for the radio or not since the instructions (which incidentally, appear to have been translated using babelfish circa 1998) don't actually cover that. I'm not sure it's even set at all, so I'm setting my iPad as backup.

review_body:
There are many features with this surge protector that would make it a valuable piece of protective equipment but unfortunately it hasn't performed very well at all. One plus is that the design is great and it allows for the best use of space for electrical plugs. I do not really know how well this unit performs as far as protection but I have found that it fails in allowing the full and proper transmission of signals with the coaxial and ethernet sections.

I was having problems with my phone modem working properly for a long time and had tried just about everything to fix it when I realized that I had forgotten about having routed my ethernet through this surge protector. I first tried different ethernet cords but the problem persisted, Finally I just bypassed the surge protector and plugged my ethernet directly into the phone modem and the problem was solved and has never returned. The second issue I had was with the coaxial ports. I installed an antenna on my roof and I did not want to plug the cable directly into my TV for fear of electrical surges and the possibility of damaging an expensive television. I thought this surge protector would be a perfect fix and I installed my cable and routed the other port into my television. The reception on my television immediately began to fail. At times I had large lines across the screen but it mainly decreased my signal strength significantly. It consistently dropped my reception by 20-25 percentage points. I tried numerous cable cords but the results were always the same. As I mentioned before I do not know how this unit performs as far as protecting against surges but the fact that it failed so significantly in two areas does not give me any confidence in having protection I can count on.

The bolts were stripping the drill bit when we tried to just drill them into the wall, so it took two of us taking turns and painstakingly twisting the bolts a half-turn at a time to get it secured to the wall. Hanging the TV also proved quite harrowing, and despite following the instructions and tightening, we were not able to get it to stop tilting forward to some degree. product_title: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Headphones|Earbuds|Earphones with Microphone
review_headline: Totally worth it - if they work longer than 6 months!
review_body:
Sad to give it such low rating but please continue reading.

Nowadays its very difficult to find quality earbuds for a good price and unfortunately this holds true for these as well.
After failing to find a few good earphones on the lower price scale I decide to try mid-range. I found these and did some research on the company. In the end I moved forward and decided to buy them. The main factors where previous rating, company, aesthetics (the wood housing of the ear piece itself) and the nylon around (since I do a lot of sports and heavy duty line is a must). Seemed all to fit a good buy.

Now initially my hypothesis held true. They were nice, the sound was above average. I really did like them. The company did "harass" me right of the bat for quite some time in order to leave a positive feedback. I told them I would try the product in good faith and first put it to the test. Well here you go - results are in.

Again, the product started out meeting my expectations (nothing above or below). Then I noticed the remote does not work with Android phone(s). It was 100% worthless and then I tried it on my Apple products, pretty much same results. To be honest the remote factor was not a buying factor (at all). But briefly staying on the Apple factor, they don't (fully) align with the 3.5mm jack in the iPad all the way. You need to wiggle and play around a bit to receive full sound and even then it might change since its not a snug fit. Not optimal for iPads.

But it seems the remote started to cause more trouble by not only not working. When I jogged for a long period of time and sweat started to accumulate and pour down it seems it leaked into/through the remote causing it to trigger commands. My phone would do the weirdest things and music would just stop. I had to forfeit all operations once this happened. I solved this issue by hiding the remote/lines between layers of shirts (between undershirt and t-shirt). This reduced the exposure to sweat.

After solving this problem the headphones lasted only a few more months. In total I had them about 6 months. I would say I am an above average use in terms of quantity. Volume is always moderate. One day, out of the blue only one side worked. Now this was on the iPad and I thought (as mentioned above) its because of the disproportion of the 3.5mm connection. I wiggled and unplugged only to plug back in and see if it finally works. Unfortunately with no luck. I checked the remote since I knew it had caused trouble in the past and that didn't do anything either but I noticed that wiggling the remote go the sound back. Through a bit of experimenting I found the spot that caused troubles. It was right where the remote was connected. Piece of line was either broken or the remote was causing it to hang up - not fully sure there. Fact is, that it only worked sporadically. A few days later it fully died. I was left with one side that worked pretty much fine while the other (remote side) wasn't at all.

I contacted Amazon since I don't think I received full value from 6 months worth of use. Initially I wanted a replacement but Amazon, which out investigating or questioning anything issued a partial refund. I am OK with that since I did use them and for the majority of the time they did work fine but I would have wanted a replacement, preferably one without a remote.

Hope you can draw some conclusion or value of this review, happy to answer any outstanding questions.

review_headline: In my opinion the bass response should have been much better. and the charge aux input cable system wasn't ...
review_body: This is a well constructed speaker that is indeed loud. I did return it though for a cople of reasons. In my opinion the bass response should have been much better. and the charge aux input cable system wasn't what I had expected. I have an UrgeBasics Soundbrick that I've used for 2 years. It produces only 5 watts of output, so isobviously not as loud as the 15 watt Skiva, but the UrgeBasics has a superior low end bass. Also the Skivia has one combination charge/audio input cord with a mini use connector for the speaker, and both the standard ubs and 3.5 mini plug for aux audio input. You cannot use both at the same time, and Skiva recomments having the speaker in the off position while charging. My UrgeBasics is plugged in charging, while listining to streaming audio. The UrgeBasics also has an output plug, giving it the ability to be used on much larger speaker system, something the Skiva just isn't able to do. For these reasons I decided not to keep the Skiva, and returned it, no quetions asked, for a prompt refund. As I said, it is a well made speaker, with good customer satisfaction service, but just wasn't for me. It may be just what you are looking for if a high powered speaker at a very reasonable price fits your needs.

review_body: So far not good.    Pros: They look nice. I've never been one to care about style over substance so this being the only pro at the moment is not a real pro.    Cons: I bought these wednesday, received them yesterday and charged it for maybe 3 hours between last night and this morning. That in mind maybe these headphones need to charge for 15 hrs the first time so it can play for that long as Skullcandy claims. Last night I played a video on a tablet with the headphones and it seemed fine. Bluetooth? Fine. This morning just as one reviewer said I hook up the phone with the headphones and make my way to the train station, sound cuts in and out. Just like a cheap pair of earbuds or headphones after long use. Bluetooth? Nothing. After several tries the light would flash purple for a second but it never connected with my phone. The songs also cut in and out when using bluetooth. If i can't get music from the short distance of my hip to my head then i don't want this.    I used these headphones all day today and the bluetooth connection got even worse. Everything i've listened to sounds like a scratched cd. This (bluetooth and headphone wire for listening) not working out of the box? Not cool. Maybe i didn't charge it long enough but the wire not working is unacceptable. I had never given Skullcandy a second thought before b/c the products looked nothing more than style and no substance. I hope i'm wrong.    This experience makes me wonder why i have a lifetime warranty for this but it seems i'll have to go in that direction. There aren't many reviews for these headphones and that means it's either really new or something is up. Very disappointed as i need headphones for work. I can only hope i don't have a back and forth for 6 months trying to get a refund. I've had ear buds and headphones bought in the train station that last longer with no problems than this.    I'll be returning these to b&h on sunday and getting another pair. I hope i'm wrong but Skullcandy, We are not off to a good start.    UPDATE: I used these headphones that weekend and had no problem returning them to the store. This probably doesn't happen with everyone but i did get a headache after a few hours of use. I'm not well versed in audio terminology but if you listen to a lot of bass, these probably aren't for you. I've heard people describe bass as muddy with their headphones. It's disappointing the negatives remain the same. I must've purchased a lemon. I doubt i'll buy anything from this company again.

review_headline: Blurry and double image....may work better on different televisions
review_body: After researching about the best way to output old composite devices to HDMI, I decided to give this box a try.  I was hoping to get my old NES/SNES/N64 to work on my ultra HD television.  The instruction manual lacks detail, but I played around with the buttons and settings until I figured it out.  I could only get an image on the 2160p @ 30Hz setting. At first the image was severely doubled and blurry.  After some more tweaking, I got the image to be less blurry but still it was difficult to watch.  I switched to a S-video input and that cleaned up the image somewhat, but there were definitely still some artifacts, esp with motion.  I switched from the SNES to the N64 and the image was blurry again and no settings could be found that cleaned it up.  I decided to return it to Amazon.

product_title: Mount-It! MI-2065L Full Motion Swivel Articulating Arm LCD, LED 4K TV Wall Mount Bracket for 23-55 inch Screen Size, Compatible with VESA 400x400, 66 lbs Capacity, Tilt, Swivel, and Rotation Motion
review_headline: HORRIBLE PAIN to hold them in with your fingers or ...
review_body: I don't take the time very often to write reviews but wanted to let others know about some of the issues we had that resulted in us returning the two we purchased.  It's important to note that we have a 50" TV which the description says we should have not problem using this mount.  This was NOT the case at all.  However, our first issue was connecting the extension pieces to the vesa mount.  The extensions require 2 bolts each with a flat rounded head so the mount will fit close to the back of the TV and each of them have a square on the underside of the head to keep from spinning when tightening.  HORRIBLE PAIN to hold them in with your fingers or vise grips (which scratch) to tighten!!!  Remember there are 2 each which makes 8 fun times till finished.  After this painstaking time you move to attaching it to the back of your TV and the wall.  The single mount bracket works like any other as far as attaching it to the wall with lag bolts but the arm IS one piece as others have mentioned.  It isn't that difficult to take it apart at the junction of the two pieces extending from the wall and the one that extends BUT what is the absolute worse design I've ever seen is where the swivel hold the TV from dropping down.  You can see the front of the 'ball" dead center of the vesa mount in the pictures.  There are three bolts with springs on them that are supposed to simultaneously tighten to hold the TV from moving.  My son and I tightened them OFF of the arm angling as far up as possible to attempt to mount and keep the TV facing up vs. pointing toward the floor.  It did NOT work at all due to the weight of our TV.  Those were the painful parts of this product.  The best part of the process (other than the wasted time) was that I was able to ship them both back free and already received my refund.  We even sent one back with the extension piece bent over as we couldn't get it off no matter how hard we tried.  It had the square headed bolts that I described above.My final assessment is that this mount could most definitely be improved to make it easier for the consumer to assemble but most importantly change the type of "swivel ball" that hold the TV adjustment.  Also, change the description to reflect the proper size.  This is NOT sturdy enough for a 50" TV at all!!!  I hope this review helps others and the company making these mounts.

product_title: Cable Matters 5-Pack, Gold Plated Right Angle F-Type Coaxial RG6 Adapter
review_headline: Flimsy, but do their job done on the cheap
review_body:
Works as designed, but I am sure glad these came in a 5-pack.

The rotating screw cuff is very flimsy, if tightened too hard (read: barely at all) the threaded cuff pops right off. The cuff can be pushed back on but the fitting is noticeably looser and thus useless unless you get some sort of childish glee out of moving an entire bookcase to check connections every time the internet goes out...

I wasted two adapters by accidentally popping the cuff off while trying to finger-tighten them onto my wall-plate. I was able to find a balance with the third one, I securely tightened it to the wall plate but then immediately popped the cuff off again when I moved the coaxial cable too close to the wall during cable routing.

The fourth one was the charm, the cabling was already secured in place and I used one of the broken adapters as a brace between the wall and cable so it couldn't move. This has held up so far 3 months after installation, but as I mentioned earlier it is virtually impossible for anything to mess with the connection as it is securely behind 200lbs+ of hardcover books.

Overall I can't be overly upset, these adapters were inexpensive and they do get the job done. However, they did waste 45 minutes of my otherwise efficient network installation, so that does count for something.

product_title: Onkyo IE-FC30
review_headline: Don't buy these unless you're a quadripelegic!
review_body:
I'm seriously wondering if the other reviewers are writing about the same product as I have.

I received the Onkyo IE-FC300(V) ear buds about a month ago, and have been using them since. The sound quality is very good, much better than the Sony Fontopias they were meant to replace. Much higher efficiency, too--I've had to turn my Cowan J3 volume down 3 notches from the setting for the Fontopias. Two stars for the sound.

But... unless your idea of activity is sitting very, very still, not moving your head at all, these are not for you. I've tried every ear cuff supplied, and the danged things WILL NOT stay in my ears. I have to snug them up every few minutes when typing on the computer, and trying to do my job, requiring moderate mobility, well, they're useless. There is no way I could run, hike, or ski while wearing these. Maybe my ears are really weird, but I've never had a pair of buds fit so badly. No stars for wear-ability.

The flat "tangle-proof" cables would better be called "comfort proof". They're about 3/16" (5mm) wide, made of very springy silicone-feeling rubber. They go where they want to, which isn't where I want them. This also contributes to the buds falling out of my ears, as the cables are sprung out where they snag on any- and every-thing. I'd much prefer to untangle thin, round, limp cables. So what if they're replaceable--if I needed the cables to match my outfit, this might matter. But for the $50 or so to replace them, I can buy some comfortable, practical ear buds. No stars for the cables.

product_title: Aether Cone
review_headline: Price is on the high side. Missing the important bluetooth connection function.
review_body:
This Aether Cone is basically a wi-fi connected speaker box. It differentiates itself against other products with its unique user interface...it takes your voice instructions.

Build: The hardware build quality is good, the design is elegant and it does not look cheap. Even package cardboard box is also very well designed...or I should say impressive.

Connection: There is only one port for connecting the charging cord. There is no aux in and no USB port, or ethernet port. You need to have another wi-fi connected device (smartphone, table, notebook, chromebook, or wi-fi connected desktop) in order to setup the cone over wi-fi...first time to see a device need to be setup this way. Too bad, bluetooth connection is not supported. So, I can not use it as a bluetooth speaker.

Conents: To play music from this cone, you need to access the Rdio radio stations to either use their free service (with commercials), or pay $10/month to get the premium service. Without the bluetooth connection, I can not play my own music with this cone.

Battery: The built-in battery provides up to 8 hours of playing. And the battery recharges fast. But, they use proprietary power cord. They should join the main stream to use USB port for charging.

Portability: Though it's a portable device, I have to hold the cone with both hands. I hope there is some sort of handle bar with this cone, so I can easily grab it with one hand.

Sound Quality: With such a small size, I am surprised with its nice sound quality...especially the bass and vocals. However, for $400 price tag, I would expect something more to justify this premium price for a mobile speaker. This is especially true since blue-tooth based wireless speakers are more like commodities these days.

User Interface: The cone takes your voice instructions to select song, artist, or album for playing. Unfortunately, the voice recognition has limitations as it gets about 70% right. There is no display screen to show what the cone has heard from me, I have to wait till the music is played to know if it gets my word correctly or not.

This cone is highly welcomed when I bring it to parties, as each person will speak a song, or a band, or a signer. And cone will play it (again, around 70% correct). However, with $400 price tag, the $10/month subscription fee and the missing bluetooth function, I have hard time to recommend it to my friends.

product_title: Channel Master CM-7500TB1 Dual-tuner DVR with program guide, 1TB
review_body: I am seriously disappointed in Channel Master.  I bought one of these (from another website - Amazon did not offer the stand alone at the time) and use the optical cable to deliver audio to my receiver, while using the HDMI to deliver video to my TV.  Out of the box, the optical port was dead.  I used different cables and ports on my receiver (which had worked fine with 3 different satellite receivers over the past 6 years) and checked all settings on the receiver and the DVR+, but nothing worked.  The documents that come with the product all state to contact Channel Master and not the retailer for tech support, so I sent an email off to their support regarding this issue.  I got zero response in a matter of 4 business days (their automated response says that someone will respond within 24 hours).  So, I called their support line.  The woman (Courtney) who I talked to was a little curt and needed to put me on hold after every question.  She told me, quite frankly, that the only support that they can offer is for me to work with the settings on my receiver.  That's it.  Luckily, the other retailer immediately offered to replace the unit and will refund me 100% if the replacement does not work. Other than this issue, the receiver is ok.  It works as stated and I may be more excited once I can get the full experience.  You must sign-up for their service in order to use the internet functions on this, including guide info further out.  It's basically Vudu, Pandora, and a bunch of internet TV channels that stream for free already (news, religious, and hunting channels are what I have seen so far).  In the days where all TVs are internet ready and come pre-installed with apps from Netflix, Amazon, Hulu, etc, it's hard to understand why this unit does not come with these.  They claim that there is more content to be added, but this is a pretty steep price for a unit that isn't even wifi ready (you must purchase a separate wifi USB for $40 if you can't run an ethernet cableto the unit). EDIT:  The second unit came from the other retailer in less than 48 hours.  Optical port is good and I now have a fully functioning unit.  As there are not many reviews of this product, I thought that I would elaborate a little more and add a couple more points.  The U/I is actually very nice (after an initial FW update - sort of clunky and slow out of the box).  Guide info is a little lacking, if you are coming from cable/satellite, and internet channels have no guide info at all - just the channel name.  Clicking onto a channel from the guide is a two step process, as once you click on the channel you would like to jump to, the software brings up a secondary pop-up window to ask if you want to watch the program, record it, or record the series.  This is slightly annoying for every channel change, but I understand why it is as it is.  DVR recording and playback works well and the series recording function has the option of recording all or just new episodes.  The skip buttons on this unit are 10 seconds ahead and behind and the playback FF and REW has several seeking speeds that make it fairly easy to get around a recording.  The tuner itself is very good - with RG6 to my attic antenna, I am able to view channels from the next market over.  Overall, I do like this unit and it has the potential to be great if they decided to ADD NETFLIX, AMAZON, HULU, ETC!!!!!!!!  I have given the unit another star to represent this.

review_headline: but it doesn't make it worse, either
review_body:
I purchased this to convert my older S-Video device outputs to HDMI, mostly because my new TV and A/V receiver have no S-Video ports. Since this product only makes the conversion for one device, I used an S-Video multiple input selection device that I already had on hand.

This product does a decent job of making the conversion from S-Video to HDMI. It does not noticeably upscale or improve picture quality, but it doesn't make it worse, either. My reason for giving it 3 stars is the high price relative to the basic function performed and the fact that this device has no RCA style audio input jacks, only a 3.5mm headphone style jack. That might be OK for gamers, but not for those wishing to convert A/V devices. There are far less expensive S-Video to HDMI converters out there that include the RCA style audio input jacks, but I bought this one on a third party recommendation before I realized that. I was able to work around the issue by plugging the RCA style audio inputs into my new A/V receiver and mapping them to the HDMI input from this device, but not everyone would necessarily have that option.

Overall, the product seems to work OK but it would be much better if more audio inputs were included so sound and video could run together in the HDMI output.

product_title: NZXT Digital Controller Cooling Fan with Grid AC-GRIDP-M1
review_headline: The Best WORST Product that NZXT has EVER made.
review_body:
1) You can not control individual fans, they are all controlled as if it were one single fan. This was a problem as i had high airflow fans and lower airflow fans that i wanted to stay at 100% all the time.
2) Fan adjustments are locked to either CPU or GPU Temperature
3) CPU Temperature comes from the phantom zone and was never remotely close what what my system what, it went from 50c to 95c and everything in between. I checked 4 other separate programs including PCMETER, CORETEMP, MSI Command Center, and SpeedFan, they all were within 2-3c of each other likely due to polling. The CAM software was no where close.
4) Some sort of overlay called CAM FPS, caused pretty much every game I, DOTA, LoL, Elder Scrolls Online, World of Tanks, World of Warships, Blade and Soul CN, Tera, Tomb Raider (2013), Alien Isolation, have to crash, corrupted the screen windows in windows itself. Overwrote all the hot keys for other programs but wouldn't actually work itself. Even when i disabled this feature it was still running in the background.
5) Completely incompatible with Windows 10, caused complete system lock ups when the fans turned on and even worse screen corruption.
6) Fan curves was a good idea but bad in practice, if the fans went from a very low or off state to full power, it would crash the system. Not a PSU issue at all, this was all the software.
7) No independent temperature monitors other than locked CPU (broken) and GPU.

How to fix this, NZXT needs to fire who ever made this software. Completely re-design it with individual fan controls with customization Temperature inputs including an on-board temperature probe. Don't add unrelated bloatware, (fps overlay crap).

In the meantime, i found a workaround. I had an old windows laptop, i ran an usb cord (software interface uses a micro-usb cord) out of my case and into the laptop. The Laptop has one job, to control the fan software so my 2k Gaming Rig isn't destroyed by bad software. Just in case you are doubtful, attached are pics of a standard micro-usb cable running out of my case to my laptop with one job!destroyed by bad software. I have setup this type of speaker/amp systems since the mid 1980's using different speaker setups, but the speakers were a much larger size type. Also, I noted a few of the reviews that I came across did mention the muted sound from the center channel and the weak bass from the sub, so you can add me to that group of reviewers.

As of today, I decided to order a Polk Audio TL2 center channel to replace my Energy center channel speaker, so I will update this review after I receive it from Amazon. Also, the Energy sub is a bottom-type facing speaker, instead of the older Energy sub I previously owned, which might be causing a weak bass because it is facing a carpeted floor. I plan on setting it on a piece of wood or some other material to find out if that is the main problem. I wished I would of purchased a different setup, but I still have about a week to send it back to Amazon, which I hate to do because they are a sleek looking set.

product_title: Sennheiser Headphones Black
review_headline: Not what I expected based on previous Sennheiser purchases
review_body:
I am a Sennheiser fan as the brand is dependable and the products tend to be reliable. However, I was very disappointed with this particular set of headphones. While they were not as much as I have paid for other Sennheiser headphones in the past, I purchased this product based on the reviews and upon using them, they fell very short of my expectations.

I had a pair of Pioneer headphones and though they were uncomfortably tight on the ears which began to hurt after a couple hours of wear and broke within a year of purchase, they sound quality was excellent! They were also less expensive most Sennheiser headphones. But sound quality of these particular Sennheiser's were not good. While the headphones were much more comfortable, the sound was not as high quality as I am used to from this maker - nor as good as the sound from the Pioneer's. I believe it is due to the earcups being padded with foam which make them comfortable, but permit sound to leak (not an expert on headphones, but I see the distinct difference in the type of materials used in the earcups).

Unfortunately, I have opened them, so I'm not able to return them, but I wish I had known about this and would have used the $50 to purchase a different set of Seinnheiser's since, as I've said, I've had better luck with them in past purchases. I love music and the theater surround sound of movies, so this is why I was not happy with the product. If all you want is a comfortable pair of headphones to hear sound, this set of headphones will suit your needs. Otherwise, I recommend looking elsewhere.

product_title: Pioneer SC-81 7.2 Channel Networked Class D3 AV Receiver with HDMI 2.0 (Black)
review_body:
So I was looking to replace my very old but still functioning Onkyo from 2008. It never gave me any issues but it just never wowed me either. So I purchased this SC-81 receiver. It has a very solid feature set, new HDMI, streaming capabilities, good power, lots of inputs. But I ended up returning it and here's why:

1. The menu is incredibly difficult to navigate, I found, and it lacked a lot of features I had on my almost 10 year old Onkyo. It doesn't have individual speaker cutoffs, only one "all or nothing" cutoff, so if you have a mix of large and small speakers, you're kinda out of luck (like I was).
2. The sound separation, especially in Dolby digital just underwhelmed me. I ended up getting a Denon x4000 and the surround effects just blow me away. For some reason the SC-81 just didn't sound good no matter how many times I tried to change the settings or try different surround effects.
3. The MCAAC calibration just isn't that intuitive, and it seems like it goes over my head. I've always had Audyssey, and it just works. This one, after reading forum after forum, everyone always seemed to have different ways of tweaking the MCAAC with various menu options and fancy graph options, it shouldn't be so difficult to get good auto-calibration.
4. It doesn't have video-throughput when listening to audio. FOr instance, I love watching sports while listening to music. This receiver just doesn't have this feature which was just about a deal breaker for me. The denon has this and it's so awesome.
5. It only has front pre-outs, I really like having a center pre-out for a small sub to bring out more bass.

Now the good things: this runs extremely cool, and the Class D amps are really awesome -- I could shut the doors to my entertainment center and it wouldn't even get warm, even after hours of watching. My other receivers get really hot. For music, I felt this receiver also did very well, I was not disappointed. But for movies and TV I just didn't like it enough to keep it. The Denon just excels here

product_title: uxcell S-360-24 Aluminum Housing Output DC 24V 15A 360W LED Power Supply
review_headline: Came a bit battered and needed repairs
review_body:
This arrived in really bad shape, the main inductor had almost broken free of the PC board and several other capacitors and a resistor had cracked solderjoints due to vibration. The original manufacturer did not glue the big parts down to the board and left a lot of excess lead length so the parts could vibrate and break the solder joints. I ended up completely disassembling the PSU and resoldering the inductor and all the big capacitors. It worked after that, but given the size of the internal components and their ratings, I don't think this PSU could run 100% rated load for long.
Given the sub-$20 price, it's an OK value, not everyone could fix it though.

product_title: CyberPower BRG1500AVRLCD UPS Outlets AVR LCD USB Ports Mini Tower
review_body:
I decided to order this UPS since I own the older model 1000. I like the small form factor even though you may end up not being able to use one or two plugs on the back since they are a bit close together. In short, my old one has been working for a long time now and eventually the lcd seems to have gone out and I can only see half the numbers on it. I contacted cyberpower and all they said after they got my information was that mine had been manufactured in like 2008, and that it was out of warranty so that was it. I couldn't get any help getting that fixed even though I didn't have it when it was manufactured. But, I still like the one battery form factor so I thought I give them another shot. Unfortunately amazon was taking their sweet time and after the third day, I happended to be at costco. Well it turns out they had the 1300 which I guess it's and oddball retail version and it cost less than this one. The only reason I didn't want anything bigger was due to the physical size and the fact that anything larger than the 1000 uses two batteries. However it was a no brainer since it cost less and I got a bit more. So far it's working as well as my old one but has the more subtle white lighted button and lcd which I like. I don't have anything that needs a pure sineware so that's why I went with the model that has the two usb ports in the front. In short even though now I know their support won't be there after the warranty exprires, at least I know the UPS itself is pretty good, so this is the reason I went with the same brand again. Plus I figured costco has better support if I need it. So it only gets three starts because amazon didn't have it and because of the no support I got from them. Otherwise the actual UPS works fine so far.

Update July 17, 2017
Apparently the one I bought first was the 1300 with the 3 year warranty. Today I received this specific model with 12 outlets. I needed one more item to plug and I figured I get this new one withthe 5 year warranty. I got mine from out of state though. The one thing I didn't realized on the new one is that they moved the two cable ports on the back from the middle to the side. The 1300 has both of those in the middle which lets me use the outlet for one of those weird sideway plugs. I can't use that top one on the left with one of those wall warts now since the two connectors get in the way right above it which sucks since it takes yet another outlet.

review_headline: Right now I like it...Loving it may come later
review_body: I researched HDMI switches for a couple of weeks to find the exact features I wanted/needed and the Panlong came closest to what I wanted.  It was easy to hook-up, less than 10 minutes (cable box, ps3, soundbar system --> TV).  One big thing I overlooked when buying was that this is not an "auto switch", it is manual.  Meaning you do have to use the remote, or the box itself to switch to the source you want.  It was my mistake for not looking closer at the description.  I have only had the switch for a week, but already it has froze once requiring me to shut all devices down and resetting the switch, worked fine, just an inconvenience.  If it happens again and I can trace the source, I will update my review.  I am using all "Blue Rigger" cabling, heavy gauge, gold tipped, 3', no crazy cable routing or kinking.  The switch and the cables support HDMI 1.4.  It seems the resolution, currently set to 1080p for both the cable box and PS3 are not displaying properly, there is graniness and streaking images on some of the Blu Ray discs and HD Channels.  I will ensure my TV is setup properly before knocking the switch for that.  Right now I'm giving it 3 stars because I think its just OK.  I bypassed the optical audio on the switch and instead went direct from soundbar to TV.  Problem with that is there is no shut off for TV speakers so there is an echo (different discussion for a different time).  I do like having the feature though.  One last positive comment - it is smaller than you think and the LED lighting is not blinding - good design.

product_title: Bose CineMate 130 Home Theater System
review_body:
All right, so I am writing this review as sort of a chronicling of my experience with this product, and I plan on adding more things as time goes on.

I don't claim to know the ins and outs of audiophile lingo, or really even their concepts. I suspect that I am the sort of person that is preyed upon the most by Bose. I really looked more and more into Bose after I bought this product, and I agree that certain things are quite concerning; they do not publish specific information about their construction methods or composition of their speakers, and urge the listener to move past such things and trust their ear. Hearing, of course, is highly subjective, and those without trained ears may be more likely to let the reputation of a company color their listening.

All I know for sure is that coming from a Polk IHT 5000 Surroundbar, I had eventually gotten fed up with its muddy and indistinct vocals / center mix and extremely bass-heavy sound, as well as a host of other issues. I originally wanted a Yamaha YSP-2500 as an upgrade, and at the store, was urged to get Bose instead, because hey, it's Bose. That was pretty much the entire sales pitch. I decided to do it and really get into the whys and wherefores of Bose and whether or not you should buy their products.

So far it's been a mixed bag. Interestingly, all the reviews I've seen laud Bose on its packaging. It's true, they do have very intuitive and well-packed boxes. The construction of the soundbar itself seems quite nice, it feels heavy and substantial, but it also has quite a slim profile. The "Acoustimass" module (AKA a subwoofer but don't call it a subwoofer) also seems well-made. This product also comes with what is basically a control console, to which you will be hooking up all your cables. I couldn't shake the feeling that control console looks and feels like a low-end cable box.

I like that the control console has 4 HDMI inputs and an output for the TV / ARC. However, I think that there are numerous HDCP issues. I have noticed odd screen-tearing with my TV, which must be shut off and turned back on for the tearing to subside. This never happened prior to the usage of the Bose product. I also did my homework on the ARC, and thought hey, it's probably easier to leave all my devices hooked up to my TV and just hook one HDMI cable up to the Bose control console to make use of the ARC. This worked great for about 15 minutes. After this, no matter in what order the control console / device / TV were turned on, if the control console was powered on, the picture and sound would cease for about 5 seconds, then come back for 5 seconds, looping constantly. My only thought is that this is some sort of HDCP issue. There appears to be very little ownership of the Cinemate 130 by anyone who is remotely technically savvy, or at least nobody who is experiencing the same issue so I can't do much research on this.

I did like that the Cinemate 130 was immediately recognized by my TV, and I can use my TV remote to control the volume, and have a visual representation on the screen.

With respect to the sound quality, I will be commenting more on this as time goes on. The first movie I decided to try on this was Avengers, which sounded good initially, but I also felt that certain elements, such as the car chase near the beginning, sounded a little anemic. As I said, I am coming from a very bass-heavy product, so perhaps this representation is more accurate, it's hard to really tell at this point.

There is some directionality, maybe not true 5.1 level, but enough to get a sense of things happening around you, which I liked a lot. I'm going to go out on a limb and use an audiophile term, so bear with me; I feel like it does project a nice "soundstage" as opposed to the Polk IHT 5000, which kind of just made everything louder. The mids did sound very crisp and clear, and I will be keeping an ear out for more of the lows. One of my go-to LFE tests is the opening scene of Sauron's defeat from Fellowship of the Ring.

Update: 11/5/16. After more than 2 years with this system, I have come to understand some of its limitations and its strengths. As previously noted, the soundstage is excellent. It sounds very open. Contratry to my initial thoughts, bass is not anemic, and does a great job with shaking the room even at about 50% volume. Mids above 60% volume are subject to some distortion; however, given how loud the system is, if you're in a small to mid-sized room, even 45% volume is more than sufficient.

My biggest quibble is that if there is a low sustained sound, that low sound will cut out periodically for about a quarter of a second. It happens maybe every minute or so. It's not a pop or anything else, it's just an absence of that sound. It is not all audio, just the low sustained sound, so voices, other noises, etc, are unaffected. It happens across different devices and media types (movies, music, games) which means that it is either a system flaw or a defect in just my system. You normally don't notice things like that, but when you hear it, you start to focus on it, and sounds like those are actually surprisingly common when you focus on it.

Given how much I paid for this thing, I'm not sure I would move forward with this purchase again, knowing that flaw. product_title: Bluedio Turbine T2s Wireless Bluetooth Headphones with Mic, 57mm Drivers/Rotary Folding
review_headline: I so wanted to keep these!
review_body:
These headphones are a good value for what they are, but they have a few flaws and one that is a deal killer for me.

Pros:
+ They have good sound for the money. They are muddy out of the box, but can be tuned with a good equalizer.
+ They have the best control system I have every run across. Very simple and intuitive. I wish all headphones used this control scheme.
+ They look cool! Subjective I know, but I like them.
+ They pair easily and just work.

Cons:
- They are made entirely of plastic. Not surprising at this price point, but they feel cheap.
- The controls that I love are made with VERY cheap plastic. They feel as if they would break at any moment and that is a shame.
- They are muddy with boomy base. I was able to correct most of this, but not all.
- THE KILLER FLAW. They are very painful for me to wear over any period of time. The earcups are very adjustable in the horizontal plane and this is good. They cannot be adjusted in the vertical plane and this means they absolutely will not work for me. The bottoms are angled in and these dig into the bottom of my ears. No matter how I adjust them, they hurt after 10 minutes or so. I have tried to remedy this problem, but it doesn't work. So, sadly, I am sending these back.

I really do like these headphones and I tried everything possible to keep them, but causing pain makes them a no go. The design is odd and may work for some, but not me. If they fit you, I am certain that you will be pleased. Very good value for an inexpensive pair of cans.

product_title: Clip Plus 4 GB MP3 Player (Black)
review_body:
I plugged it in and after a couple of hours all I could see on the screen was an image of a headphone and a battery indicator, which lit up when turned on. When pressing buttons I could see some light flickering around the very edges of the screen. I could not figure out how to get to the navigation menu since the view on the screen never changed. The only sound I could get out of it was static. When hooked up to the pc, I could navigate through the file structure without issue. I was able to drap/drop a couple of mp3's.

After fiddling with it for some time with no success, I filed a return for replacement. Shortly afterward we figured out the problem.

It's embarrassing to say, but the "problem" turned out to be a sticker on the screen that blocked the view of the actual screen. It took two of us with glasses and close scrutiny to determine that, yes, it actually was just a damned sticker. They made the sticker to look like the screen and it lit up when the unit was turned on. It even has a fake battery indicator. To shorten the story, I eventually forced the edge of the sticker up and peeled it off, revealing the real screen. It did not come off easily at all. This was not the typical translucent vinyl we've become accustomed to seeing, rather it was black paper with very strong glue. Further, the instructions that came with it are absolutely minimal bordering on worthless. The static I was getting was because it was on radio and signals have always been weak at my house.

I have to pull out the instructions every time I want to change the time or the alarm, or really, make any change at all. It's much easier to just plop your iPod in to update the time. The radio is so-so, but our reception is pretty bad in the entire house. I haven't really learned to use my iPod as an alarm, so perhaps this would be much easier to use if I just programmed it that way!

Weirdly, even with the universal time update systems, it's always 1 minute different from my husband's alarm clock (he has a Chumby.) I don't know which one of us is off, but it drives us both crazy. He doesn't buy my 'slightly different time zone' theory. ;-)

review_headline: The size is perfect and they went on easily
review_body: I bought these for $8.99 (free shipping) for my JVC HA-NC250s. The size is perfect and they went on easily. But I'm right on the fence of whether or not I should have gone with the OEMs direct from JVC for $16.85 (http://store.jvc.com/product.asp?Model=J34899-001). Here's why: These just aren't as soft and supple as the originals. That goes for the vinyl covering as well as the foam itself. Does it matter? The difference in comfort is only marginal. However, the originals conform to the ear. They seat right down and create more of a seal. These rest on the ear without that seating. I know, they are "on-ear" headphones. But there is a difference and I can't help but wonder if that difference affects sound quality and noise reduction quality. Also, the inner diameter of the hole on these is a bit smaller than on the originals. I'm guessing that doesn't make a difference in sound quality, but what do I know. Any sound engineers out there? So even if JVC charged shipping, it would be about $21 for the real deal or $9 for these. You decide. But every time I put these one (which is pretty much every day), it's going to bug me. One paragraph later, I'm no longer on the fence. I wish I'd bought the JVCs.

product_title: NG 283220 AC Adapter Power Supply for HP Pavilion dv1000 dv4000 dv5000 dv6000
review_headline: Spend a little more and get something that lasts longer than 2 days
review_body:
Do NOT buy this product. I guess I should have known that a $7 adapter wasn't going to last long - but this thing only lasted a couple of days before the wire coating cracked. As you'll see in the photo, the black outer coating cracked, leaving the inner wires exposed. I am gentle with my electronics, and I unplug wires correctly (not yanking on the cord). There is no good reason to explain this happening TWICE in a row.

Now if this only happened once, I would dismiss it as a one-time flaw. Unfortunately, that doesn't seem to be the case. The first adapter I received lasted exactly two days before developing an identical crack in the wire coating (though at the other end of the cable). After contacting Amazon, they were kind enough to send a replacement for the first adapter. Now, another few days have passed, and the second cable has cracked as well.

While this doesn't immediately affect the performance of the adapter, it's a pretty serious design flaw. I'm not going to go through the hassle of getting another replacement. Right now, I've just swaddled the entire end of the cable in electrical tape, and I'm hoping that it lasts for a few months.

DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. Spend a little more and avoid the frustration of faulty, inferior products.

product_title: Phiaton Bluetooth 3.0 Active Noise Cancelling Stereo Earphones with Mic
review_headline: Good solution in gneral, but not for people with hearing problems like hyperacusis
review_body:
I'm not a traveler trying to reducing airplane cabin noise, although I'm sure these earbuds would be satisfactory for that use. I have Meniere's Disease with hyperacusis. (See my webpage if you're not sure what this is: http://www.c--h--s.com/index.php/menieres/ .) I need protection from popping, cracking sounds (you know those horrible people who just can't help but squeeze their plastic water bottles to express their nervous energy). I have previously used Bose QC15 headphones with success, but they tend to knock down all sound, not just sounds in the painful range. These Phiaton PS 210s do indeed block/cancel some sound, however, the amount and nature of sounds cancelled is in question.

I'll contrast two situation which reveal the 210s competencies. #1) I was recently at a Bluegrass concert at which the sound level was consistently in the 80db range (as measured by an app on my phone). The 210s knocked out a lot of ambient sound and left a nice stream of music coming through. However, consistent with this genre of music, there were some vocal yelps and instrumental zingers that passed through the 210s with ease and caused me pain. I finally got out my Etymotic ER20s (baffled silicone earplugs) and, although the sound was more muddled, the level was tolerable. Phiaton fail. (I report similar experience in restaurants which tend to have both roar (ambient noise) and sharp peaks (reckless busboys slamming plates, babies crying, drunk hussies cackling incessantly, etc etc). In restaurants, the 210s were minimally effective. The sharp, loud sounds were just simply not "cancelled".)

#2) I have weekly staff meetings that are much like any staff meeting you can imagine - lot's of paper shuffling and crackling, water bottles cracking, pens clicking, and lots of sidebar conversations that create an overall sonic storm, but not extremely loud. I wore my 210s to two recent staff meetings and was pleased with the result. Annoying sounds were tamped down, yet I could still hear each speaker (mostly female) very clearly. Last staff meeting I left the 210s at home and had to protect myself with the Etymotic ER20s (I carry them on my keychain). Speech was much more muddled and I did not hear all speakers clearly. In this situation, the Phiaton PS 210s were clear winners.

The noise-canceling function and Bluetooth audio function work independently of one another which is quite nice. I'm not an audiophile, but I feel like the sound quality is excellent. Phone calls are crisp and clear. I have a feeling that the Bose QC20 earplugs would provide superior noise canceling and sound quality, but they are not Bluetooth - a solution I prefer.

My overall assessment is that Phiaton PS 210s do not live up to the45db sound reduction suggested by one Amazon reviewer. The overall reduction is probably in the 15-20db range, which is very helpful in many situations. For people with hearing problems such as I have, the elimination of "roaring" ambient sound it very welcome relief. However, if you have a feeling that you need more in the direction of hearing protection than noise reduction, these are not the plugs I would recommend.

review_headline: Good if you have really small ears...
review_body:
I was looking for a pair of over-the-ear noise canceling Bluetooth headphones to replace a Sony headset that broke after a few years of ownership, and I was sold by the description of the features on the MM550-X. I was especially interested in the Talk-Through feature and the noise cancellation.

The biggest disappointment was that they just didn't fit over my ears. I didn't think I had big ears, but within moments of opening the box and trying them on, I knew that I would be returning them. The ear cups are WAY smaller than they look in the photo. You could probably fit a medium sized lime in the ear cup, but definitely not a small lemon. When I tried it on, they sat on my ear and I had to squish my ear into the cavity. With bigger ear cups, these definitely would have been a keeper.

The sound quality was great, and the noise cancellation seemed effective (I turned on our noisy microwave vent). While a lot of other reviewers didn't seem to like the SRS feature, I thought that music sounded better with it on... I guess with these headphones, it all comes down to your ears.

product_title: Sony MDRAS800 Active Sports Headsets
review_body:
I'm surprised at the poor design. It feels like Sony rushed to get this product out.

Pro's: Sound is good, fairly flat, not an overly saturated bass like Dr. Beats or over-clipped highes. The earbud are comfortable and stay in for general use (didn't keep them long enough to try them working out). The earbuds really seal the ear and reducing outside noise. I had no problems pairing with my LG G2 and Ipad. (It has NFC but I couldn't get it to work) They are very light and you don't notice them when they are on.

Con's: The single "multipurpose" button is a huge joke. It uses something similar to morse code, 2 short click and one long to do something, 1 short click to do something else. Seriously, if I have to memorize some set of codes to use the thing.......... Remember this is to be used with your phone, right? Well, Sony decided we didn't need the ability to answer or dial a phone call using the headphone. Just to make them even harder to use, I couldn't figure out how to turn them on/off. So with them on all the time when they were fairly close to me, I couldn't talk on my phone without finding the headphones. So after getting so frustrated with them, I ended up disconnecting them from the bluetooth of my phone so I could start using my phone again. The battery doesn't last long enough to use them for a single day.

At ~$150, there are much better products out there.

Found a dinky piece of paper in the box that looked as if you are supposed to push the top of yellow cable with more force into the power station. No writing on it, no explanation as to what may be the issues that you should try to avoid or overcome. For heaven's sake, my husband is a mechanical engineer with two master's degrees and has always been able to figure out how to connect electronic units to anything and everything. Absolutely this is going back and we intend to express our profound disappointment that a formerly great company like Sennheiser has so poorly designed or allowed this unit to be so poorly manufactured.

product_title: MEElectronics Sport-Fi M6 Noise Isolating In-Ear Headphones with Memory Wire
review_body:
Overall, these are so-so. I disagree with most reviewers and found that the sound quality on these is pretty terrible. I suppose they're nice if you're replacing factory apple earbuds or something similar, but compared to other in-ear headphones in the <$20 price range, these don't stack up.

Pros:
-Memory wire is successful at stopping them from being pulled out at the gym or while running.
-insulated wires don't transfer much movement noise, unlike many others I've tried
-Included case and clothing clip is very useful.

Cons:
-Poor sound. Bass is lacking. Highs sound tinny. Occasional distortion with heavier music. These aren't terrible and work okay if you're just out for a run, but they definitely don't stack up to a lot of other <$20 offerings. I've probably had close to a dozen different in-ear headphones over the past 8 years, and yes, I know how to fit them in my ear.

product_title: SanDisk  Clip Jam MP3 Player
review_body:
I have been getting these SanDisk Clips since about 2008. So, I have seen the evolution and improvements. The reason I got these is that I like to make playlists by breaking up podcasts and inserting music as breaks or interstitials. It WAS very easy to use Windows Media Player to create a playlist and sync it with the Clip. Now, there is a complicated process involving five steps that have to do with creating a folder, then creating a playlist in the M3U format, then saving to a folder on the Clip and copying from who knows where, and it goes on. No longer is it an easy process to make a playlist.

Also, it used to be that when you hit the back button (the arrow not the "|<<" symbol) it would take you one level up the "tree". Now it is more like the home button. So now instead of going back to the album (if you were looking up just one song) it takes you back to the Music/Books/Radio/etc level. This is unnecessarily complicated because sometimes the arrow works like pushing a "home" button and sometimes the |<< symbol goes to the previous track or up one level on the tree.

The one thing they finally got right is that the music counter/timer is back on. Now, if I were to pause a 15 minute segment, I would know where I left off. So, "morning win" on that one.

The size is good, the display is good. But, it no longer does what I need it to do and that is to be a simple device for replaying my customized playlists.

There was a time in 2011 when I wasn't satisfied with the Clips and started shopping around for better products. But, I came back to them because they were the best at making the playlists that I needed. I guess now I have to stick with refurbs or find a new manufacturer.

product_title: Timex Decorative XBBU Dual Alarm Clock
review_headline: Gets the job done. I do not recommend this if you keep multiple things on your bedside table.
review_body:
I have a love-hate relationship with this alarm clock. I like all of the features, such as the night light, adjustable brightness, and the alarm itself. The alarm is just loud enough to wake me up without making me grumpy or startling me. The night light also makes it easy to see in the night. The USB charger makes it easy to plug in my phone on my nightstand, where I have easy access to it if I need to check something while I'm laying down in bed.

However, I recommend not to underestimate the top-heaviness of the clock. As a whole, the clock is extremely lightweight with most of the weight being in the top; whenever I lean over to show my husband something, or roll over on my side to look at my phone, I often yank the clock off the table on accident if my phone is plugged in. This is due to the clock being so lightweight, with no weight on the bottom to keep it solid on the nightstand. If there were weights on the bottom, or if the whole clock just sat directly on a surface, I wouldn't have any issues. I read other reviews saying this and thought it couldn't be that bad, but it is! It's so annoying, especially if I'm groggy or if it happens in the middle of the night. I've almost knocked glasses of water and other normal nightstand items off as a result.

Just be cautious with this item and trust what the reviewers say. The features are nice, but I would probably search for another alarm clock if I had to buy one again.

product_title: Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote, Programmable Remote (Silver)
review_headline: This brand is on its way downhill
review_body:
Avoid the 650. Previously, we had the Harmony 550. That remote was the best remote I've ever owned. Unfortunately, after about 3+ years of perfect functionality, it died (I believe my toddler had something to do with it if I recall). We could not find the 550 at our local retailer, so we opted for the new base model, the 650. Immediately, we saw there were problems.

For the "newer and improved" remote, Logitech opted for less devices to be controlled. They added a fancy new color screen that provides no additional benefit; in fact, the user experience is worse as the menus are harder to use than the 550. I can't recall, but I think the 650 takes more batteries too (I think fewer AAA vs more AA or similar - I forget). Having had such a great experience with the 550, we decided to live with it. That was a mistake. Despite several attempts at programming the remote, we can't get it to change the tv input to the correct input prior to turning off all the devices. When we use 'help' to get to the right input again, it refuses to recognize that "one click of input brings up a screen, and subsequent clicks move you through the list." The last two could maybe be fixed through the web interface, but I've tried many times and cannot get it set up properly.

The worst is that the remote constantly reboots itself. We've had buttons fall off. Aside from the web software, the remote's software and new screen eat batteries. On the 550, we changed batteries every few months as most, maybe two or three times a year. With the 650 it is at least once a month. This is a poorly engineered product (especially in comparison to the older 550 remote). This is not a quality product that you would expect for ~$100 price point. At this point, using multiple remotes to manage our entertainment center is a better experience. Heck, getting up and walking to our center is a better and more responsive experience. We can only use the 650 by knowing what inputs onthe tv and av receiver go with what activities due to the constant rebooting and it not going to the right input on the tv prior to turning off. We have to go through the help menu all the time. This is harder than just using two or four remotes. And, starting yesterday, the remote will only take in one command before rebooting (even on a fresh set of batteries).

I was a Harmony remote advocate and I thought a customer for life. I am no longer. Now, I actively recommend against the brand. They have sacrificed quality for poorly implemented features and the brand has suffered. Could I just have a more defective model? Perhaps. Am I willing to gamble more hundreds of dollars trying their other models? Heck no. To drive this home: I have a broken foot right now, and I would rather hop across the room and press buttons (even when I have to kneel down to get to some of them) than continue using this broken remote.

product_title: Phiaton Balanced Armature Earphones with Mic
review_body:
I'm comparing these to three other sets of earphones: original Apple earbuds, Apple EarPods, and Koss KSC75s.

Comfort: once I switched to one of the smaller sets of ear pads, I found the Phiatons to be acceptable, although I wouldn't exactly call them comfortable. I always knew they were there, and I couldn't tolerate having them in my ears for more than an hour. The other earphones are all more comfortable.

Staying in place: the Phiatons stayed inside my ears even when I moved my head and body. The Apple earbuds were only fair, and the Apple EarPods were poor (I couldn't get them to stay in my ears at all). The Koss KSC75s were the best in this regard.

Cord: the cord on the Phiaton earphones tangles less easily than the others, as advertised. It's shaped like a long piece of linguine pasta and has a finely ribbed texture. Even if I roll the earphones into a ball and stuff them into a pocket, it's easy to pull them out without finding them twisted into multiple knots. In this regard, the Phiatons beat the other earphones I compared them to. I did notice, however, that the Phiaton cord transmits more noise/vibration into my ears than the others.

Audio quality: The Phiatons were only fair when it came to audio quality. Treble was rolled off, with a noticeable sibilance on things like symbols and \\"S\\" vocals. Bass was not as bad as I expected it would be, but not great either. Mids were good, or at least they seemed good, perhaps because of the not-so-good treble and bass performance. I could never escape the feeling that I was listening to music through a tin can. The Apple earbuds and Apple EarPods were significantly better, and the Koss KSC75s were the best.

Ambient noise isolation: the Phiatons were pretty good in this regard, better than the two Apple products and much better than the Koss.

Overall: I would recommend these if your most important requirements are noise isolation, staying in place, and not getting tangled up. These would be great for working out, commuting on the train, etc. I do think they're a bit overpriced when you consider some of the other drawbacks. If you want the best audio quality and don't need noise isolation or an inline mic, the Koss KSC75s are a better solution and cost much less. Apple EarPods would be a good compromise between the Phiatons and the Koss IF they stay in your ears, but unfortunately this varies from person to person and you would need to buy them in order to find out.in place, and not getting tangled up. review_body: I purchased and LG Smart 3D TV and it came with one of this same magic remote.  It might be magic but very irritating -- it works like a pointer, or a mouse pointer.  You have to wiggle the remote all the time to get the scroll/mouse arrow -- that is, you have to point it at the screen and wiggle, wiggle, wiggle to get the arrow to appear and then you point the remote around and the arrow moves with your movement, then when over your target you press the center wheel down, it acts as a scrolling wheel as well as a command button, just like on a mouse wheel.  But, if you stop to read something on the screen, like an instruction or a discription of the program you want to choose the command arrow disappears and you are back to wiggle, wiggle, wiggle to get it back and then try to get back on to your target.  If you hit the button wheel, under certain situations and the arrow pops up it may activate the nearest target whether that is what you are after or not.  I hate the damned thing, and wish I could get it back to the conventional point and shot remote.  I know this is supposed to be designed to use like a mouse but it is slow in responding when you want it and it goes off in just a couple of seconds so if you are not constantly in motion you have to keep waking it up and this gets tedious when you are trying to navigate something like Amazon Video or Netflix.  Had I know this was part of the TV I purchased I would not have bought the TV,  It is in a spare room so I don't use it as much as my other Smart TV with the conventional remote, and love it, great 3D.  Don't know what I will do if the built in connection in the other smart TV for the magic remote ever fails?  This typs of remote does not use the external dongal, as it is connect wireless to the TV.  I would only buy this remote as a back up just in case the one I have gets broken by accidently bouncing off the wall.  Peace, Dan

review_headline: Just didn't meet our needs but it also has some significant draw backs and issues
review_body:
Retuned the radio becasue it simply did not meet our needs for a back up car radio.

I bought this for my wife who is forever driving the kids around to various practices and then having to wait for them. So she wanted a raido to listen to while waiting, without having to drain the van battery or run the engine.

Reasons for returning:
a) While this radio has a speaker it does not sound good at all - at least to us.
b) she wanted a digital radio with presets which this radio has. However, you only get one preset that is actually memorized where you press a button and the station comes up. The other 19 presets are stored in memory but you need to cycle through them all to find the one you are looking for.
c) For what ever reason they gave the radio an oval base, so it does not stand up on its own reliably. I can't understand why it doesnt have a flat bottom so that you can stand it up but it does not. Also when I laid it down on its sides it made a crackling sound - not sure what this was about or why.
d) If you want to use the speaker then you need to hang a cord off of it to get reception which given the state of the van will last all of about a day before it gets lost. You can use a set of headphones but my wife doesnt carry them, just uses the speaker on the iphone. I tried it without a cord or headset in it to act as an antenna and the reception sucked.
e) It comes with headphones which we never tried but look really cheap. So if you buy this and want to use headphones you need to pay for a pair.
f) It does not come with batteries in the box. This is not a huge deal but for $43 I would think they would include at least a set of cheap generic batteries to you started.

We never really got past the poor sound from the speaker or the goofy way the presets worked to really test reception. So I gave 2 stars on the hope that it does have good reception with the use of a cord or headset acting as anantenna.

review_body: My SanDisk Clip 4GB MP3 Player lasted less than 6 months. This device was first used on 26 Dec 2014. At this time it will not power up. Multiple chargers have been used but the SanDisk player does not respond. The SanDisk was used to play music for sleeping and kept indoors on a night table.This represents a low stress life for a portable digital player. The whole thing has to be thrown away, just more plastic and electronic material in the landfill.When the device worked it performed as described. I conclude that this device and any SanDisk products using this design have a short life cycle and the consumer will be better served with a different product.  I suggest that we should all consider how long portable electronic devices last. Small electronic devices like this one are hard to recycle because of the labor to disassemble them and the resulting payback is low. These small electronic devices just don't compost, so this one will be around for generations but will have only been useful for less than six months. The only people who win in this game is SanDisk who will sell you another one.
