product_title: NAD D 7050 Direct Digital Network Amplifier
review_headline: I set up a NAD D 7050!
review_body:
Sound quality from the NAD D 7050 is excellent, and Airplay has never dropped out. Setup took several hours. Some functions have cut out and returned on their own.

Instructions for Airplay setup are neither complete nor entirely correct. Wifi connectivity during setup was inconsistent, requiring repeated attempts. The unit arrived requiring a firmware update, which I discovered only after searching online for why the iPhone app did not work. Several tries to install the firmware update via Wifi only confirmed that the unit's Airplay setup menu simply lacked the option for firmware update which the instructions clearly showed it should have. NAD Support responded to a help request within 12 hours, and the update was then installed successfully via USB thumb drive. But then the D 7050 setup menu would no longer allow use of the network password, and I had to figure out how to do a dhcp login. Having completed the setup on the NAD D 7050, I feel as though there ought to be a badge.

Initial performance of the D 7050 was accompanied by a distinct background hiss which went away on its own during the first 5 minutes of use; just barely in time to save it from being stuffed back in its box and returned. Background is now silent, and I couldn't be happier with the sound quality.

After several weeks of use, the volume control and the on/off switch both stopped working and I could control both only via the iPhone app. Function returned on its own after several hours, again in time to avoid a return. But between the user-hostile set up and the sporadic problems, this product is no longer deserving of four stars.

product_title: Vertical Universal Cpu Holder
review_headline: Eye-Crossing Assembly Guide, Very Snug Fit For Wide/Older CPU's!
review_body:
I got this to mount my re-furbed G5 Dual Core Tower on my cubby-hole music-studio wall. The assembly guide sheets are very confusing at first, second, and third glance, until you realize you'll have to take your time to look at it very carefully, to figure out the exact mounting setup you need to go by. While I can see that they were created in a way to live up to the "Universal" status, more detailed instructions would have helped, whether by words, or by diagrams.

With this being mounted right over the end of my studio's twin bed, I took advantage of every, single screw-hole available on the mounting plate, though I had to buy the extra screws and anchors for this purpose. Even extending the mounting plates as far as they go, I barely had enough room to squeeze-in my 55 lb tower, which being a re-furb already had quite a few dents and scratches; but this was actually quite the workout to do, and NOT something I would even TRY doing with a brand new CPU, that was the same size.

So though I made it work to suit my purpose, with 2 extra purchased shelf-brackets supporting it for my own sense of security, it was no easy task, and this CPU holder was clearly NOT made for older, or customized CPU's that would be wider by design.

So I'm giving this product 3 stars, since they stand for "it's okay", which is my exact opinion, though I should add that I would make it 2 and a half stars, IF that option was available, here.

product_title: JBL Cinema SB350 Home Cinema 2.1 Soundbar with Wireless Subwoofer
review_body: UPDATE: When I first reviewed this unit, I was watching video on my computer and letting the speaker system play the audio. However, now that I have set it up with my TV, I am noticing a few milliseconds of lag with the video.  If you are just playing music through this, it doesn't matter.  But when you are watching people talking in a movie, and the sound is delayed just a bit after the video, it can get annoying.  I even tried using the optical cable, but the delay was still present.  Even when I hooked this system up to my music keyboard, there was a slight delay using the aux in.  I now have it hooked up to my laptop for playing music while I use the computer and for watching YouTube videos, and it is fabulous for that.  The volume is impressive, and the bass is tight, accurate and controllable via the remote.  I have reduced my score to 3 stars.  This system likes being pushed and sounds better at a decent volume.  This unit will fill a room with sound (specs say 320 watts). While listening to action movies, jazz, rock, and classical music, at no time did I hear distortion. Stereo separation is good on this unit.  The soundbar paired easily with both its subwoofer and my tablet.  The overall sound level is controllable via remote, and the amount of bass is separately controllable.  The selection of inputs is excellent, with HDMI, mini phone, optical, and bluetooth available.  The 6.5" ported subwoofer is impressive and tight, however only the lowest bass is shunted to this unit.  The rest of the sound is handled by the soundbar's 2.25" speakers (2 per side) and 1.25" dome tweeters.  The low mid-range is downplayed with this set up (it is difficult for 2" speakers to accurately handle low mid-range) with the high end consequently being overly present.  This is not a problem with movies, but is not ideal for critical music listening (which, admittedly, few people do anymore).  I found the best listening was to acoustic guitar, fusion jazz, and classic rock and roll.  Summary: good unit for casual listening to streaming music/mp3's, video on computer, etc.

product_title: Eton Scorpion Multifunction Radio
review_body: Pros: water/splash proof, can use as auxiliary speaker, clips to Molle and bags well, VERY LOUD, light is bright, has bottle opener.  Cons: takes FOREVER to charge in the sun, antenna is humorously short, stations do not come through very well most times, build quality is a little better than "ok", does not "dump charge" meaning you have to crank constantly to charge anything, buttons are mushy and almost feel on the end of breaking when pushing hard. Needs can opener not bottle opener.  I bought another kind of these emergency radios a while back and it didn't have everything I wanted (mainly the fact that it wasn't water/splash proof). The Eton Scorpion is a much better version but it still has flaws. For instance the clip on the end on mine is slightly off center and requires that I nudge it over so it sits flush. But that just might be mine and that not my main complaint. My main use for this was supposed to be to charge my iPhone when it died and I was away from plugs. I take the bus a lot so I'm in the sun quite a bit. The Scorpion keeps charge very well if it is in the sun a lot, but when trying to charge a phone you have to constantly be cranking the arm, EVEN WHEN IT IS FULLY CHARGED. Which is not quiet and also very tiring. It takes several minutes just to get 1 or 2% of battery life. The iPhone also throws hissy fits if it doesn't get the correct voltage of input, Androids may suffer the same issue but I don't have a current gen Android. Since crank charging fluctuates in voltage it often doesn't work at all on iPhones. I've solved this by charging an external battery phone charger, and then plugging that into my iPhone. Works much better. The bottle opener is awkwardly placed but works fine (needs to be parallel w/ the frame no perpendicular). The antenna is very fragile. If you pull too hard i feel that it could easily come completely out. And is also a short 8inches. It works retracted just as good as it does deployed so I don't ever even pull it out. The Scorpion needs to have "dump charge" capabilities and then I'll give it a 4. Better antenna? 4.5. Add a can opener instead of of bottle opener and its a 5.

I do think this a great device, even with the very very poor battery life but as a result it is not worth $99. With the low battery life it wouldn't even be worth half that. review_body: In my quest for a great Bluetooth speaker, I have purchased (and subsequently) returned or sold the following in order: a UE mini Boom, JBL Flip 2, UE Boom, Creative SoundBlaster Roar, Bose Soundlink Mini, and a UE Megaboom.  As you can tell, my price point kept going up (out of necessity for the quest).  The Bose and the Megaboom were the best of the bunch, but neither good enough that I still wasn't constantly trying to tweak them with an EQ or move around to find the perfect location.  I kept wanting more.  I guess I am an audiophile, although I never received a certificate stating as such!  What I want from a speaker is to hear layers, separation, clarity AND feeling...it needs to breathe.  Am I asking too much??  If you're like me then the reviews on this Riva Audio speaker probably peaked your interest too.  Sad to say....didn't work for me.  I always try to preface a bad review by saying perhaps I got a bad one.  But while this Riva did sound very good, I'd put it in the class of the last two above.  Definitely brighter and clearer mids than the Bose but with less bass, and balanced like the Megaboom but neither was ultra clear to my ears.  This Riva was good, just not great.  Definitely NOT Audiophile grade to me.  Sigh.  On the PLUS side though, I do think my search is over.  Having upped my price range this high I was willing to go up to the Peachtree Audio Deepblue2 and all I have to say is......OH MY GOSH!!  You do sacrifice some portablility since it is bigger and needs an AC outlet, but if you are looking for the things I am in a Bluetooth speaker I haven't found THIS sound in anything else for less or in a smaller/rechargeable offering.  Hope this helps someone.

product_title: Harman Kardon SB16 Soundbar and Wireless 100 Watt Subwoofer (Black)
review_body:
Five star sound with a 1 star computer inside.

So the sound is incredible HOWEVER, be prepared for the remote control nightmare.

The remote fuctionality is easy enough to program in. If you happen to have a smart remote though and want to use it to control this sound bar you may be out of luck. For me I use the volume control on my Samsung ir remote. This is fine with the tizen os but for the 2014 and earlier os this means dealing with a huge external speaker message box everytime you change the sound. Because the Samsung smart remote doesn't use ir unless configured as universal remote this isn't possible. Mainly because Harmon Karon has no default remote codes for this device so it can't be added. The optical out is glitch and the reason is that the bar will not accept and downconvert signals other than 2.1 or stereo. So if you send 5.1 with optical it will cut out the audio. This may be a problem if you have a TV or receiver that won't downconvert before sending. 2014 and previous Samsung do not down convert 2015 tizen os fixes this too.

If you are having audio cut out on quiet scenes or animated series it likely due to 5.1 being sent through optical. You can easy fix if your TV or receiver can't down convert by switching to rca for audio since that channel is incapable of more than stereo.

Harman Karon has good support but don't lose the wall bracket in case you ever want to wall mount. They are just a couple metal j hooks but they won't sell them to you if lost.

I've been using this sound bar for over 3 years now and as side from the base randomly losing connection, the remote glitches, and the down sampling problems it's been great. The bass is probably more than anybody needs.

review_body:
This product works well for its price. I have it set up for a mobile FPV rig that I can strap to just about any plane and it gets decent range. I have not done any real long range stuff, but I have never had a problem with signal loss while flying. I absolutely recommend using CP antennas or better with this unit. I dont even bother with the stock antennas anymore. I have a CP on the transmitter and a homemade 10 turn helical on the receiver. There are a couple of things you need to know about this before you purchase.

When it says that this is fatshark compatible it should really say that it is partly fatshark compatible. The receiver works well with my attitude sd v2 goggles when it is in the 40 range of channels. The receiver will not pick up any of my three fatshark transmitters, but it does work with all 4 of my other transmitters of varying brand.

This one is really my fault for not checking, but it is still something that is useful to know in the beginning. The transmitter is a passthrough for the power to the camera so it will output whatever voltage you put in. I found this out the hard way after seeing one of my fatshark pilotHDs go up in smoke after connecting a 3s battery to the transmitter. like I said, this is not the fault of the transmitter, but I do blame the lack of adequate instructions for part of my problem.

product_title: Harman Kardon AVR 2650 7.1 Channel 95-Watt Audio/Video Receiver with HDMI v.1.4a, 3-D, Deep Color and Audio Return Channel (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
review_headline: Doesn't work with DirecTV Genie, and ridiculously horrible customer support
review_body: My year and a half battle with Harman Kardon has finally come to a close. I should have written this warning review sooner, but I'm finally taking the time to tell my cautionary tale. After having previously owned two other HK AV receivers, when I finally replaced my old non-HDMI rear projection TV with an HDMI flat panel, I decided to get a new HK AVR (the 2650) to go with it. After connecting the new unit up with our DirecTV Genie HDR, our AppleTV, and our Sony BluRay player, I ran the speaker calibration, and all seemed well. Unfortunately we soon discovered that about every 4th or 5th time we powered on our system to watch DirecTV, we would get no picture. When this happened, we had to try switching sources and power cycling multiple times to get the picture to show up. After calling tech support, and not getting much help, I decided to use HK's on-line warranty exchange process to get a new unit. I thought surely HK didn't have a design issue that would cause their AVRs to be incompatible with DirecTV's mainline receiver. I was sent a 3650-Z as a replacement. Unfortunately, the new unit exhibited the same problem as the original, and in addition would also take several seconds to start playing audio whenever we skipped backwards in the show we were watching. Annoying, since the usual reason for skipping backwards was to try to catch a bit of dialog we had missed! Thinking again that surely HK didn't have a design problem, I spent several months experimenting with new cables, changing the order and timing of powering on components, etc., all to no avail. I finally resorted to calling tech support again, and here's where things got truly frustrating. After spending almost two hours on hold, I was finally connected with a support person. After explaining my problem, he told me he was going to transfer me to his supervisor for assistance. After waiting on hold for another 10 minutes, the call was disconnected. When I tried to call back, I got a recording that their support center was closed, even thought it was still 5 minutes till the posted closing time. I tried using the on-line support form, where a response was promised within 2 business days, but didn't get any response for a week. I tried calling again two days later, and once again had my call dropped after being on hold for over half an hour. I called back in immediately, and this time decided to try leaving a message when the kind automated voice promised that they would get back to me within a day. No response. We finally called the main corporate number from the HK website to complain , and the nice receptionist promised us that she would have her customer service manager take care of us. Two days passed. Nothing. We called the receptionist again. She was very angry and promised us a call from someone who could help us. Finally late that day we got a call. I explained to the new support person the history of my situation, and told him I was done with HK and wanted my money back. He asked if we had bought from HK directly. I said, no, from Amazon. He said he couldn't refund our money then, but promised to send us their new, top-of-the-line 3700 model, which he assured me hadn't given them any problems. I reluctantly agreed to the switch. The unit arrived, I connected it up, and the only difference now was when the intermittent video loss on power up occurred, we didn't get a blank screen, but instead got a scrambled display. Upon contacting the support person again, I was asked to try a specific order of powering on the components. I did, but it didn't help. Once again, I requested a refund. Once again, I was told it wasn't possible. Another call to the corporate receptionist, and they finally agreed to refund our money after we returned the unit. I promptly returned the unit, and then had to wait over two months, with numerous e-mail exchanges encouraging them to send the promised check, before it finally arrived. I'm sorry to say, after being a loyal HK customerfor probably two decades, I will never touch one of their products with a ten foot pole, and I will strongly advise anyone I come in contact with to do the same. The end of the story is I went to a local store and bought an Onkyo AVR, which has worked flawlessly from day one with the same equipment.for probably two decades, I will never touch one of their products with a ten foot pole, and I will strongly advise anyone I come in contact with to do the same. The end of the story is I went to a local store and bought an Onkyo AVR, which has worked flawlessly from day one with the same equipment.

product_title: Audioengine D1 24-bit Digital-to-Analog Converter
review_headline: The USB probably works fine on Windows
review_body:
Both the USB and S/PDIF inputs are flaky in their own ways. The USB probably works fine on Windows, but in Linux I was having horrible stuttering/underrun issues whenever the CPU is even slightly busy. With S/PDIF it's perfect until the sample rate changes -- going from playing music to watching a video with a different sample rate, for example, I hear the internal relay "click" and then dead silence. Unplugging the optical cable and plugging it back in resets things and it's fine. I ended up configuring PulseAudio to resample everything to a fixed rate just so it wouldn't get stuck like this.

On the plus side, it sounds great and has a nice extruded enclosure. If your needs are simple it'll probably be fine, but for a main DAC on a Linux PC I can't really recommend it. When I bought this I thought I'd get some value from having a high sample rate and/or bit depth but after further research I think it's generally a waste of money for listening purposes, so if I had to buy something new I'd definitely get something cheaper.

product_title: Teac AH01 Stereo Amplifier with Digital to Analog Converter
review_headline: Wonderful sound diminished by serious usability issues
review_body:
Maybe I'm breaking the rules by not using this as a desktop amp with my computer.

Instead I wanted a small amp and some bookshelf speakers to connect to a Sharp LC-46LE700UN flat screen tv, which has shockingly bad built-in speakers. This would be used much of the time when I didn't want to fire up the big home theater amp and subwoofers etc., just to watch the news and mindless tv drivel.

This TEAK amp does deliver wonderful sound and drives a pair of Monitor Audio Radius 90 speakers effortlessly. This combination delivers satisfying base even without a sub, and delightfully precise upper end sound as well. It is more than enough for watching most movies as well as playing classical music through the home theater's laptop.

So what's my beef?

Since I'm sitting in a recliner and not right in front of the amp, I rely exclusively on the remote which Teak supplied with this amp. This remote is almost completely useless, so I frequently turn the stupid amp off and go back to the horrible Sharp speakers, which at least Sharp's remote will control.

The Teak remote has 2 major problems.

There is no on/off button for this amp on its remote. I guess Teak figured you'd be sitting right in front of the amp and would just reach out and turn it on or off. This is not my big issue, and considering my next complaint, an on/off button probably wouldn't work anyway.

The second issue is the keys on the remote need to be pressed incredibly hard before their functions activate. I mean you have to press them so hard that you are sure you are going to break the remote. If you just press a key with normal pressure as you do every other remote, nothing happens.

I hate loud commercials. And I hate the Teak remote because as soon as the commercial noise begins, I press \\"mute\\" and NOTHING HAPPENS. The noise blares on. Pounding on the mute button and threatening to shoot the remote eventually causes the amp to mute. Usually.

Then you must reverse the process to un-mute the amp when the commercial is over.

Plan B when a commercial comes on is to try reducing the volume with the volume up/down keys. The volume only changes if the up/down key is mashed about as hard as I can press it.

I've tried everything I can think of including putting fresh batteries in the remote, but it remains almost useless.

The bottom line is I'm delighted with this Teak sound and completely frustrated by its unusable remote. A relative is looking for a similar system, and I will NOT be recommending Teak for a solution!

product_title: HomeSpot NFC-Enabled Bluetooth Audio Receiver for Sound System
review_body:
My expectations were a bit higher than what this Bluetooth receiver was able to deliver. Maybe I should have taken the low cost as a warning sign. I'll shoot straight: it usually works, and when it does, the audio sounds like it should (for being translated through Bluetooth). And for most people, that'll be good enough.

What I didn't expect when I bought this, however, is that the manufacturer highly recommends a "line-of-sight" path between your phone/tablet/etc and the receiver itself. If this doesn't bother you, stop and consider the ramifications for a minute. Having to keep a clear, unobstructed path between your mobile device and this receiver [almost] defeats the purpose of Bluetooth.

The manufacturer doesn't try to bury this detail in the documentation, either. There's a special insert with the unit that calls your attention to this in big print--possibly the result of customer inquiries or complaints. I read that warning and thought, "Surely this company is a bit too concerned with connectivity problems," and I disregarded it.

Until I plugged in the receiver and made all the connections. After 2-3 minutes of use (and regularly thereafter), it was clear that this receiver cannot be tucked behind, covered up by, or placed against anything. Anything. It has to be out in the open to work well. The problem with that, though, is that the blue led is fairly bright. I was hoping to use this in our bedroom, and after the first night, had to give up on that hope.

Anyway, long story short: it does work pretty well as long as you keep the receiver out in the open where you can always have your eye on it (literally). I suppose a little duct tape or electrical tape will solve the LED annoyance, too.

I wouldn't recommend this one to a friend or family member, with a number of other options readily available. But if you know about these limitations up front, and don't mind them, the price is right. Happy shopping!py shopping!

product_title: PORTTA Auto-Switching 3-Port HDMI2
review_headline: Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't work with my cable box and Roku 3
review_body:
I have connected this to my cable box, DVD player and a Roku 3 and will sometimes have issues with the cable box being able to be watched (black screen and no sound). Sometimes I have to remove the device to get the cable box back in working order. I was aware that this may be an issue with a switch device prior to ordering since it is hit and miss when you have a device that is always on (Roku 3) with a cable box.

Update (5/9/15): The device is still connected to my Comcast Cable Box (port 1), DVD player (port 2) and Roku 3 (port 3) and I have not had ANY issues like I did when I first got it. Nothing changed with the connection but it is working great, not sure why though...

product_title: Vamery 2Pcs 18650 3.7V-4.2V 5000MAH Li-ion Rechargeable Efficient Battery Blue
review_headline: If you buy these batteries....it's your OWN fault!!
review_body:
FAKE, FAKE, FAKE.

THERE IS NO SUCH THING AS A 5000 MAH 18650 BATTERY!!

In most cases, these are LESS than 1000mAh. What does that mean???

It means they WON'T last long at all in a device that needs over 2 amps to power. They will need charging after LESS than 1 hours use!!

They are dangerous.
They are old.
They are recycled.
They are rejects.
They are NO good!

Anyone here who has given them a good grade hasn't used them under a heavy enough load to know their limitations.

The more you charge them, the WEAKER they will get.

Trust me, I know a lot about lithium batteries!
